n00002.summary: When Abu Taalib was dying, the Quraysh complained to him about the Prophet's preaching, and the Prophet offered them the single statement Laa Ilaaha Illallaah, which they refused.

n00018.summary: Amr bin al-Aas asks Umar what to do about a man who repeatedly left Islaam and returned to it, and Umar rules that he should be invited to Islaam again, then freed if he accepts or otherwise executed.

n00020.summary: Abu Bakr, a close friend of the Prophet, accepts Islaam immediately when the Prophet calls him, and several leading Companions then follow him.

n00049.summary: The Prophet calls Abul Haysim and some young men of the Banu Abdil Ash'hal to Islaam, and Iyaas bin Muaadh accepts and dies reciting the Kalimah.

n00064.summary: The Prophet asks the Banu Shaybaan to protect the Deen, Nu'maan bin Shareek pledges support, and Ali relates the Prophet's foretold victory over the Persians at Quraqir, after which the Banu Rabee'ah became Muslims.

n00068.summary: Taariq bin Abdillaah sees the Prophet calling people to say Laa Ilaaha Illallaah in the Dhul Majaaz market while Abu Lahab follows him and Abu Jahal throws sand at him, and a second narrator describes the Prophet's appearance.

n00103.summary: Jaabir narrates that shortly before his death the Prophet sent letters to the emperors of Persia and Rome and to other rulers.

n00108.summary: Ibn Abbaas narrates that the Prophet sent a letter to Kisra through the governor of Bahrain, that Kisra tore it up, and that the Prophet cursed him, as relayed by Ibn Musayyib.

n00116.summary: Witnesses to the Najraan treaty carry the Prophet's letter back to Najraan, where Basheer (Abu Alqama) accepts Islaam after cursing the Prophet in a fall, the monk Ibn Abi Shimr goes to meet the Prophet, and the Prophet's letter of protection for the priests of Najraan is written by Mughiera.

n00124.summary: Ma'mar, relaying from Ayyoob, Ikrimah and Zuhri, reports the Hudaybiyyah negotiations: Suhayl bin Amr objects to the opening formula and to the clauses, and the Prophet accepts his terms.

n00164.summary: Aslam relates that Umar made wudhu with water from an old Christian woman's house, invited her to Islaam, and when she said she was about to die, called on Allaah to witness.

n00174.summary: Amr bin Umayyah relates that Umayr bin Wahb, after accepting Islaam, invited Safwaan bin Umayyah to Islaam at the Hateem, and Safwaan stayed silent.

n00192.summary: Ziyaad bin Haarith Sudaa'ee accepts Islaam and his people follow; when the Prophet appoints him their leader and he asks for a share of zakaah, he withdraws the request after the Prophet's warnings, and the Prophet appoints another man from the delegation.

n00209.summary: Yazeed bin Abi Habeeb relates Umar's letter to Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas ordering that enemies be invited to Islaam for three days before fighting, with the booty rules for those who accept before or after battle.

n00212.summary: Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas sends leading Companions to invite Rustam to Islaam at Qaadisiyyah; they tell him they are sure of victory, and Rustam recounts a dream in which the Persian weapons were handed to the Prophet and then to Umar.

n00245.summary: Ubaadah bin Saamit relates that eleven men made the first Aqaba pledge, promising not to associate partners with Allaah, steal, commit adultery, slander, kill their children, or disobey the Prophet in good, and that the same men returned the next year.

n00249.summary: Ka'b bin Maalik describes the Ansaar gathering at Aqaba with the Prophet and Abbaas, who asks them to guarantee his protection; Baraa bin Ma'roor pledges to protect him as they protect their families, and Abul Haytham bin Tayyihaan asks about the Jews and whether the Prophet will return to his people, and the Prophet answers that he shares their fate.

n00263.summary: Uqayla bint Ateeq describes her and her mother Qareera's pledge to the Prophet, which he took without touching their hands, and Umaymah bint Ruqayqah describes the women's pledge, which the Prophet confirmed by speech alone.

n00268.summary: Aa'isha relates that Hind bint Utba was told to go and dye her hands with henna before pledging, that she pledged to avoid shirk, theft, adultery and killing children, and that the Prophet called her gold bangles coals of Jahannam if their zakaah was not paid.

n00270.summary: Usayd bin Abi Usayd Barraad relates from one of the women who pledged that the Prophet required them not to disobey him in good, scratch their faces, dishevel their hair, tear their collars or pray for destruction.

n00275.summary: Ibn Afeef recounts that Abu Bakr took allegiance from the Companions to obey Allaah, His Book and the Ameer, and that Ibn Afeef later came to pledge on the same terms and was accepted.

n00278.summary: Umayr bin Atiyya Laythi asks Umar to raise his hand so he can pledge to him as the Prophet's pledge was taken, and Umar says the pledge gives rights on both sides; Abdullaah bin Ukaym adds that he pledged to Umar with these hands.

n00284.summary: Aqeel bin Abi Taalib relates that the Quraysh complained to Abu Taalib about the Prophet's preaching, and when Abu Taalib asked him to stop, the Prophet said he could not abandon his mission; Abu Taalib then assured the Quraysh that his nephew never lies.

n00301.summary: Urwa bin Zubayr relates the Prophet's journey to Taa'if after Abu Taalib's death, where three Thaqeef chiefs reject him, the crowd pelts him with stones, and Addaas, a Christian slave of Utba and Shayba, shows reverence after the Prophet speaks to him about Yunus.

n00327.summary: Uthmaan relates that while walking with the Prophet in Bat'haa they saw Ammaar and his parents tortured in the sun, Yaasir cried out, and the Prophet told the family to be patient and prayed for their forgiveness.

n00357.summary: Nu'maan relates that Umar, when great wealth came in during his caliphate, recalled that the Prophet had been restless all day because he could not find even poor-quality dates to fill his stomach.

n00359.summary: Aa'isha relates that a goat's leg sent by Abu Bakr's family was cut by her and the Prophet together, without a lantern.

n00369.summary: Anas relates that until his death the Prophet never ate from a table or ate bread made of finely ground flour, and another narration says he never even saw a roasted kid.

n00377.summary: Aa'isha says that the first calamity to befall this Ummah after its Nabi is overeating, because it makes bodies obese, hearts weak and carnal desires uncontrollable.

n00390.summary: Abu Hurayrah says that the only food he ate with the Prophet was dates and water, that they never saw wheat, and that their only clothing was the rough woollen shawls of the Bedouins.

n00399.summary: A narrator whose name is lost in the OCR relates that during the digging of the trench the Prophet went down with a stone tied to his stomach, after three days without food.

n00438.summary: Urwa bin Zubayr relates the Prophet's arrival at Madinah: Zubayr met him with white clothing, the people welcomed him at Harra, he stayed with Banu Amr bin Awf, and he founded the Masjid on land bought from two orphans, carrying bricks himself.

n00474.summary: Saalih bin Basheer relates that his grandfather Fudayk asked whether a man who does not migrate is lost, and the Prophet told him that establishing salaah and paying zakaah while avoiding evil makes him a migrant; Ataa relates Aa'isha's view that compulsory hijrah had ended, though jihaad and intention remain.

n00493.summary: Jaabir relates that the Ansaar gave the Muhaajireen the larger share of their harvests, and after Khaybar the Ansaar, having fulfilled their duty, asked the Prophet for Jannah in return, which he granted.

n00506.summary: Anas relates that the Aws and Khazraj boasted of their Companions: the Aws named Handhala, Sa'd bin Mu'aadh, Aasim and Khuzayma, and the Khazraj named the four who memorised the whole Qur'aan, Zaid bin Thaabit, Ubay bin Ka'b, Mu'aadh bin Jabal and Abu Zaid.

n00507.summary: Abdullaah bin Rabaah relates Abu Hurayrah's account of the conquest of Makkah: the Prophet had the Ansaar clear the Quraysh resisters, Abu Sufyaan asked whether the Quraysh would be wiped out, the Prophet promised safety to those who closed their doors or entered Abu Sufyaan's house, broke the idol at the Kabah, and told the Ansaar he had made hijrah towards Allaah and towards them.

n00515.summary: Anas relates that during the Prophet's final illness Abu Talha visited him, and the Prophet sent his salaam to the Ansaar, praising them as extremely chaste and patient.

n00533.summary: Anas relates that when the Prophet consulted the Companions about marching to Badr, Abu Bakr and Umar spoke first, and then an Ansaar man pledged to follow the Prophet even to a distant city, refusing to say what the Banu Israa'eel said to Moosa.

n00549.summary: Abu Hurayrah says that no one would worship Allaah had Abu Bakr not become Khalifah, and that after the Prophet's death, when tribes renounced Islaam, Abu Bakr refused to recall Usaama bin Zaid's army of seven hundred, which went out, defeated the Romans and returned, and the wavering tribes stayed Muslim.

n00577.summary: Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas addresses the Muslims before Qaadisiyyah, reminding them of Allaah's promise to give them the land, of the Persian army of about two hundred thousand, and warning that losing courage would cost them their Aakhirah.

n00596.summary: Miqdaad bin Aswad refused to sit out jihaad because of his weight, citing the Qur'anic command to march out light or heavy, as Jubayr bin Nufayr reports.

n00618.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports that Umar, overhearing a woman's lament at night, asked his daughter Hafsa how long a woman can be without her husband, then resolved not to keep an army away from home beyond that period.

n00647.summary: Abdullaah bin Amr reports the du'aa the Prophet made as he set out for Badr with 315 men, asking Allaah to provide transport, clothing and food for his Companions, and how Allaah granted this after the victory.

n00650.summary: Abu Sa'eed Khudri reports the du'aa the Prophet taught the Companions during the Battle of Khandaq, after which Allaah sent a powerful wind against the enemy.

n00662.summary: Mu'aadh bin Jabal relates the Prophet's words on the reward of dhikr and spending in jihaad, and explains that spending while out on an expedition earns far more than spending from home.

n00666.summary: Aasim bin Amr bin Qataadah tells how Quzmaan, whom the Prophet called a man of Jahannam, fought fiercely at Uhud only for his people's honour and then killed himself when his wound became unbearable.

n00673.summary: Maalik bin Aws reports Umar's teaching that the reward of those who fall in an army depends on their intention, and that true martyrs are those who fight with perseverance seeking Allaah's reward.

n00678.summary: Mu'aadh Juhani reports the Prophet's ruling that whoever crowds the camp or blocks a road earns no reward for jihaad, and a separate narration adds that the Companions stayed close together on campaign.

n00684.summary: Abu Sa'eed Khudri reports that Ubay bin Ka'b asked Allaah for a fever that would stay with him until death without preventing Hajj, Umrah, jihaad or congregational salaah, and it did.

n00689.summary: Anas bin Maalik tells how his uncle Anas bin Nadhar, who missed Badr, fought at Uhud with over eighty wounds until he was martyred, and how a verse of the Qur'aan was understood to refer to men like him.

n00717.summary: Qaasim bin Abdur Rahmaan reports that Anas bin Nadhar rebuked men who had lost heart after the report of the Prophet's martyrdom, then fought on until he was killed.

n00723.summary: Jaabir reports that at Uhud, when only eleven Ansaar and Talha remained with the Prophet, Talha repeatedly volunteered to hold back the enemy, and the Prophet told him that saying Bismillaah would have lifted him to heaven.

n00759.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas reports that after Uhud Ali brought his sword to Faatima, and the Prophet said that Sahal bin Hunayf and Abu Dujaana Simaak bin Harasha had also fought well.

n00760.summary: Ubaydullaah bin Ka'b reports that at Khandaq Ali invited Amr bin Abd Wadd to Allaah, His Rasool and Islaam, and when Amr refused and taunted him, Ali fought and killed him in single combat.

n00778.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood says that at Badr Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas fought alongside the Prophet both as cavalry and as infantry.

n00831.summary: Jaabir Ru'ayni reports that Abu Bakr, seeing an army off, said that those who help prepare it, send it off and make du'aa for it share in the reward of going out in the path of Allaah.

n00836.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas reports that the Prophet set out in Ramadhaan to conquer Makkah and kept fasting until he reached Kudayd.

n00852.summary: Ummu Atiyya, who went on seven expeditions with the Prophet's army, describes how she cooked, nursed the wounded and tended the sick in the camp.

n00861.summary: Anas reports that Ummu Sulaym kept a dagger with her at Hunayn to deal with any Mushrik who came near her, and that the Prophet smiled at her answer.

n00872.summary: Qataada reports that Uthmaan began praying four rakaahs at Mina, and that Abdullaah bin Mas'ood, though he recited Innaa lillaah, prayed four behind him, saying that causing division was worse.

n00900.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas describes Umar's sigh and the qualities Umar named for a khalifah: strong without harshness, lenient without weakness, generous without extravagance, and careful with money without miserliness.

n00902.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas recounts his questioning of Umar, who said that Ali had merits but that a khalifah must not compromise principles and must judge fairly even against his own people.

n00904.summary: Salmaan testifies that Umar is a khalifah and not a king, and Ka'b, citing scripture, says the prophecy he found describes Umar as a khalifah in the pattern of prophethood before kingship.

n00909.summary: Sha'bi reports that Umar kept certain Quraysh confined to Madinah to protect the seat of khilaafah, that Uthmaan released them and they scattered, and the text then records Umar's and others' counsel to the Prophet on the caravan of Abu Sufyaan and on the Badr prisoners, including the revelation on ransom.

n00912.summary: Abu Hurayrah reports that when Haarith of the Banu Ghitfaan demanded half the produce of Madinah, the Prophet consulted four leading Sa'ds, and Haarith's party answered with an accusation of betrayal.

n00973.summary: Abu Khuzayma bin Thaabit reports that Umar set conditions for his governors on appointment, forbidding Turkish horses, fine flour, fine clothing and locked doors to the needy, and reminded them they were sent to establish salaah, share the spoils and judge justly.

n01013.summary: Abu Salama reports Umar's oath that he would have executed anyone who killed a Mushrik after pointing to him as a sign of safety and then surrendering to him.

n01014.summary: Anas bin Maalik says that Hurmuzaan, who surrendered at Tustar, was spared by Umar after Anas gave testimony that Hurmuzaan had been promised amnesty, and Hurmuzaan then accepted Islaam and received an allowance.

n01020.summary: Abul Furaat reports that Uthmaan asked his slave to twist his ear in retribution, and when the slave did so gently Uthmaan told him to twist harder, praising the delight of retribution in this world.

n01070.summary: The text traces Abu Bakr's life as khalifah: he gave up trade for a fixed allowance, returned public money on his deathbed, and on his Umrah visit to Makkah was greeted by its leaders while his father Abu Quhaafa wept with joy.

n01106.summary: On the Prophet's advice, Abu Talha divided his beloved orchard at Bir Haa among his relatives and nephews.

n01114.summary: Abu Hurayrah reports that a hungry Ansaari guest was hosted by an Ansaari man and his wife, who put out their lamp and pretended to eat so the guest could eat, and Allaah praised their conduct and revealed the verse about preferring others.

n01147.summary: Uthmaan reports that the blind Haaritha bin Numaan gave charity to beggars with his own hand, guided by a string, because the Prophet had said that giving to the poor personally saves one from a gruesome death.

n01187.summary: Urwa reports that Sa'd bin Ubaadah would announce from his house an open invitation to anyone wanting meat or fat, that his son did the same after him, and that Abdullaah bin Umar confirmed no one was as generous as that father and son.

n01203.summary: Jahjaa Ghifaari, who came to accept Islaam, recounts how the Prophet hosted him and his group, and the Prophet explained that a believer eats to fill one intestine while a disbeliever eats to fill seven.

n01215.summary: Anas reports that when dates were brought to the Prophet, he shared them with the Companions while eating quickly, apparently because he was about to leave.

n01226.summary: Jaabir reports that Qais bin Sa'd bin Ubaadah slaughtered seven camels to feed his hungry expedition, and that on the shore they then found a giant fish which fed them for three days.

n01267.summary: Ja'far bin Burqaan reports that Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf freed thirty families of slaves, after an opening saying of the Prophet about who will show compassion to his people after his death.

n01338.summary: Ibraheem bin Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf reports that when the treasures of Kisra were brought to Umar, Umar wept, saying that Allaah sets enmity between a nation when it is given such wealth, while Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf tried to comfort him.

n01342.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports that when Umar was given a gold-laden table cloth to distribute, he wept, fearing it was a test rather than a blessing.

n01360.summary: Umar finds Rasulullah lying on a coarse mat that had marked his side, and Rasulullah says his luxuries are postponed to the Aakhirah while this world is like a traveller's brief shade.

n01362.summary: Anas reports that Rasulullah wore woollen clothing and patched shoes and ate coarse barley, and Hasan explains what Bashi was.

n01380.summary: Humayd bin Hilaal reports that Hafs bin Abul Aas would not eat Umar's plain food, and Umar explains that he avoids luxury out of fear it would reduce his good deeds on the Day of Qiyaamah.

n01383.summary: Utba bin Farqad brings Umar a basket of sweetmeats, which Umar refuses after asking whether every Muslim has one, and then they share a plain meal of coarse bread and tough meat.

n01391.summary: Shurahbeel bin Muslim says that Uthmaan served rich meals to guests but ate only vinegar and olive oil at home.

n01433.summary: Yahya bin Sa'eed reports that Umar rebuked Jaabir bin Abdullaah for buying meat for his family, quoting the verse about using up one's good things in worldly life, and a second report has Jaabir describing how Umar kept repeating his excuse.

n01446.summary: Salmaan asks Abu Bakr for advice, and Abu Bakr tells him to fear Allaah, take from conquests only what he needs, and never break the protection given by Allaah.

n01488.summary: Abbaas claims land in Bahrain that Rasulullah granted him, Umar does not rule in his favour despite Mughiera's testimony, and Umar then says he was happier at Abbaas's acceptance of Islaam than he would have been at his own father's.

n01493.summary: Usaama bin Shareek says that when he came to Rasulullah, his companions sat around him so still that it seemed birds were perched on their backs.

n01525.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas reports that when Rasulullah heard the Ansaar weeping for fear of his death, he spoke from the pulpit, foretelling that the Ansaar would dwindle to little more than salt in food and advising that their good be accepted and their faults overlooked.

n01544.summary: After Rasulullah passed away, Abu Bakr and Umar visit Ummu Ayman, who weeps because revelation from the heavens has ended, and a second report says she wept bitterly for the same reason.

n01547.summary: Anas reports Faatima's grief when Rasulullah fell ill and after his death, including her words about Jibra'eel informing them and her question to Anas about throwing sand over him.

n01587.summary: Aa'isha reports that Rasulullah prayed at night in a room made of mats during Ramadhaan, and told the Sahabah to take on only the deeds they can keep up, since the most beloved deeds to Allaah are the consistent ones.

n01595.summary: Abu Bakr vows that he will not recall the army Rasulullah sent out under Usaama bin Zaid nor untie a flag Rasulullah tied, and in a second report says he would send it even if he were the only one left in Madinah.

n01603.summary: Bakr bin Abdullaah reports that Abdullaah bin Abbaas told a Bedouin why his family serves nabeedh on Hajj, recalling that Rasulullah came to them with Usaama bin Zaid, drank it and praised it.

n01610.summary: Aa'isha says that no one followed the footsteps of Rasulullah on his journeys, at every stop, as closely as Abdullaah bin Umar did.

n01648.summary: Usaama bin Zaid reports that on a raid he killed a man who had recited the Kalimah, and Rasulullah rebuked him until he wished he had only become Muslim that day.

n01663.summary: Abu Umaamah reports that Uthmaan, while under siege, said he had been threatened with death although Rasulullah said blood is lawful to shed only for three reasons, none of which applied to him.

n01669.summary: Zaid bin Thaabit tells Uthmaan that the Ansaar at his door offer to help him, and Uthmaan refuses them permission to fight if they intend to fight.

n01717.summary: Aa'isha reports that Rasulullah told her to spit out a piece of meat after she remarked on a woman's long hem, and Zaid bin Aslam reports that in his final illness Rasulullah rebuked his wives for winking at Safiyya's sincere wish to share his suffering.

n01726.summary: Abdur Rahmaan bin Awf reports that on a night patrol he and Umar came to a house where people were drinking wine, and Umar, recalling the Quranic ban on spying, went away and turned a blind eye.

n01732.summary: Sha'bi reports that a man asked Umar how to treat his daughter, who had been buried alive in ignorance, then rescued, converted and repented, and Umar told him to keep her past hidden and marry her as he would any chaste Muslim woman.

n01746.summary: Abdullaah bin Amr asks Sa'd how he has earned his reward, and Sa'd replies that he never sleeps with ill-feeling towards any Muslim, which Abdullaah says is beyond what he can manage.

n01756.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports that Abu Bakr asked Umar's forgiveness after a heated exchange, Umar refused, and Rasulullah praised Abu Bakr and ordered every door to the Masjid sealed except his.

n01764.summary: Thumaamah ibn Hazan reports that Umar stopped on his donkey to listen to a woman who spoke to him harshly, justifying this by the Quranic verse that Allaah heard a woman who complained to Him about her husband.

n01779.summary: Abu Hurayrah reports that when the room was full, Rasulullah threw his garment to Jareer bin Abdullaah to sit on, and told his Companions to honour a prominent person who comes to them.

n01782.summary: Abu Raashid reports that he went to Rasulullah with a hundred men of his tribe, was taught the Muslim greeting, accepted Islaam, and was honoured with a seat beside Rasulullah and gifts of the Prophet's shawl, shoes and staff.

n01784.summary: Someone asks why Rasulullah gave Uyaynah and Aqra a hundred camels each and not Ju'ayl, and Rasulullah replies that Ju'ayl is better but that he gives to win the hearts of the others, entrusting Ju'ayl to his Imaan.

n01807.summary: Abu Abdullaah Jadali reports that Ummu Salamah rebuked those who reviled Ali, asking how Rasulullah could be reviled when Ali, whom he loved, was reviled.

n01832.summary: Abul Bakhtari reports that Ali was asked whether those who fought him at the Battle of Jamal were mushrikeen or munaafiqeen, and Ali replied that they were simply brothers who had rebelled against them.

n01841.summary: Hasan reports that Umar angrily summoned people who claimed Umar was better than Abu Bakr, and told them that he wished he could reach a place in Jannah from where he could see Abu Bakr at the furthest point of his sight.

n01866.summary: Anas reports that when Umar's consultative assembly met after his death, Abu Talha warned that each of them seemed to want the Khilaafah for himself or to pass it on, and said that every Muslim home had suffered by Umar's death.

n01890.summary: Zubayr reports that Rasulullah stayed in sajdah while Hasan bin Ali climbed on his back, did not make him get down until he got down himself, and sometimes parted his legs so the child could pass through.

n01893.summary: Abu Qataadah reports that Rasulullah carried his granddaughter Umaamah bint Abil Aas on his shoulders while praying, setting her down for ruku and lifting her again when he stood.

n01913.summary: Anas reports that when a tree came between them during a journey with Rasulullah, they would greet each other with Salaam as soon as they were back together.

n01930.summary: Aa'isha reports that when Zaid bin Haaritha arrived in Madinah, Rasulullah rushed out in excitement, embraced him and kissed him.

n01932.summary: Hasan reports that Umar would sigh through the night when he thought of a companion, and after Fajr would hurry to embrace that companion as soon as he met him.

n01938.summary: Ka'b bin Maalik reports that after the verses confirming his forgiveness for staying behind from the Tabook expedition were revealed, he went to Rasulullah and kissed his hands.

n01954.summary: Abu Mijlaz reports that when Mu'aawiya came out while Abdullaah bin Zubayr stayed seated and Abdullaah bin Aamir stood, Mu'aawiya quoted Rasulullah that whoever likes people to stand for him should prepare a house in Jahannam.

n01969.summary: Salmaan Faarsi advises that a gift or meal from a friend, neighbour or relative who works for the state should be accepted, since any sin in unlawful earnings falls on the giver.

n01976.summary: Anas and Abu Hurayrah report that the Prophet answered the sneeze of the one who said Alhamdu Lillaah and did not answer the one who did not, explaining that the first had remembered Allaah.

n02015.summary: Umar sent Abu Moosa away after three requests to enter went unanswered, and only when Abu Moosa brought Abu Sa'eed and the Ansaar as witnesses to the Prophet's rule on seeking permission did Umar accept it.

n02025.summary: Amr bin al-Aas reports that when asked whom the Prophet loved most, he named Aa'isha, then Abu Bakr, then Abu Ubaydah.

n02064.summary: Abu Dardaa asked Aa'isha about the Prophet's character, and she said his character was the Qur'aan: he was pleased with what Allaah is pleased with and disliked what Allaah dislikes.

n02072.summary: Abu Hurayrah and Anas describe how the Prophet never withdrew his hand from anyone who took it, even a child of Madinah, and gave his full attention to whoever spoke to him.

n02095.summary: After Hunayn the Prophet gave extra booty to Aqra bin Haabis and Uyaynah bin Hisn, and when Abdullaah bin Mas'ood reported a complaint about it, the Prophet pointed to Musa's patience under abuse and asked who would be just if Allaah and His Rasool were not.

n02105.summary: A Jewish woman served the Prophet poisoned goat meat to test whether he was a true Rasul; he warned the Companions, questioned her, and took no action against her.

n02133.summary: An added narration says the Prophet also visited the sick and attended funerals.

n02138.summary: Abu Umaamah reports that when an immoral woman mocked the Prophet for eating like a slave, he gave her food from his own hand and mouth, and afterwards she never again flirted with a man.

n02145.summary: Urwa and Amrah each report asking Aa'isha whether the Prophet did household chores, and she said he mended his shoes and clothes and milked his goat himself.

n02157.summary: Umar says he once had no source of livelihood apart from a few handfuls of raisins given to him for carrying water, and that he told this to humble himself after feeling pride.

n02178.summary: Ibn Seereen reports that Hudhayfah arrived at Madaa'in riding on a carriage on his donkey and eating bread with meat, and Talha bin Musarrif adds that his legs hung down by the donkey's side.

n02192.summary: Anas reports that the Prophet, seeing the camel-driver Anjasha hurrying the camels while Umm Sulaym and the wives were travelling with him, told him to go easy with the crystals, and Abu Qilaabah gives a similar remark.

n02203.summary: Jaabir, and Abu Sa'eed citing a longer hadith from Abdullaah bin Abi Bakr, each say that the Prophet never refused anything he was asked for.

n02225.summary: Anas saw the Prophet weep as his son Ibraheem died; Makhool reports Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf asking why he wept, and the Prophet explained that tears of mercy are natural but wailing and praising the dead are not.

n02231.summary: Ummu Haaritha says she will be patient if her son is in Jannah, and the Prophet tells her there are many levels of Jannah and her son is in Firdous, the highest.

n02237.summary: Abu Bakr tells two grieving people that the good Allaah grants is vast for both of them.

n02244.summary: Usayd bin Hudhayr says he has every right to weep, since he heard the Prophet say that the pillars of the Arsh shook at the death of Sa'd bin Muaadh.

n02250.summary: Sufyaan reports that Ali consoled Ash'ath bin Qais on the death of his son, saying that patience is rewarded and that impatience brings sin.

n02269.summary: Ali says every bounty is followed by gratitude, which brings an increase, and Muhammad bin Ka'b Qurazi reports Ali's further teaching that the doors of du'aa, repentance and forgiveness are never closed while Allaah's Book is recited, citing verses.

n02323.summary: Qataadah reports that Abu Ubaydah bin Jarrah wished he were a sheep his owners would slaughter and eat, and that Imraan bin Husayn wished he were sand the wind would blow away.

n02328.summary: Tawoos reports that Mu'aadh bin Jabal refused a masjid built from rocks and trees for fear of carrying it on his back on the Day of Qiyaamah; Naafi reports Abdullaah bin Umar weeping in sajdah in the Ka'bah; and Abu Haazim reports Abdullaah bin Umar's remark about a man who fell unconscious when the Qur'aan was recited.

n02336.summary: Ubayd bin Umayr reports that Umar wept while leading Fajr when he reached the verse about Ya'qoob's eyes turning white with grief, and then went into ruku.

n02395.summary: Aa'isha confesses her jealousy: after the Prophet married Ummu Salamah she thought her more beautiful than people said, Hafsah told her she was not, and on a second look Aa'isha agreed it had been her own possessiveness that made her see it that way.

n02427.summary: Hudhayfah says he wishes he had someone to manage his affairs so he could lock his door and meet no one until he met Allaah, and Ibn Abbaas says that he would go where he had no friends if Shaytaan's whisperings did not hold him back, because people corrupt people.

n02446.summary: Anas describes the wedding meal of Zaynab bint Jahash: after the guests left and three men stayed talking, the Prophet went to Aa'isha's room and then returned to Zaynab's, and the verse of hijaab was revealed as he dropped the curtain.

n02474.summary: Umar asked Ali for Ummu Kulthoom in marriage; Ali said he had reserved his daughters for the sons of Ja'far, Umar pleaded and Ali agreed, and Umar told the Muhaajireen he now wished to be the Prophet's relative; Ataa Khuraasaani adds that Umar gave a dowry of forty thousand dirhams.

n02480.summary: Umar admits that everyone understands more than he does, returns to the pulpit, and withdraws his limit of four hundred dirhams on dowries, so people may give what they wish.

n02496.summary: Ibn Abbaas reports Aa'isha's account of the choice the Prophet offered his wives under the verses of Surah Ahzaab, that she and the others chose Allaah, His Rasool and the Aakhirah, and that this was not counted as a divorce.

n02499.summary: Ibn Abbaas describes staying the night at his aunt Maymoona's house, where the Prophet rose for night prayer, made wudu, prayed thirteen rakaahs, and at Bilaal's call prayed two rakaahs before the iqaamah.

n02507.summary: Abu Sa'eed Khudri relates that the Companions took turns serving the Prophet, and that when they were discussing the Dajjaal the Prophet came out and asked why they were whispering, reminding them he had forbidden private whispered discussion.

n02514.summary: Abdullaah bin Ja'far recalls being a child on the Prophet's mount, where the Prophet took him first and then Quthm, sons of Abbaas being the other children, and prayed that Allaah be a successor to Ja'far for his children.

n02537.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports that Umar and Zubayr raced twice; each won one race, and each called out that he had won by the Rabb of the Kabah.

n02554.summary: Aa'isha reports that while the Prophet ate with six others, a Bedouin ate all the food in two morsels, and the Prophet said the food would have sufficed for them all had he said Bismillaah, and taught that one should say it before eating.

n02563.summary: Abu Uthmaan Nahdi reports that Salmaan Faarsi said he loved to eat from the work of his own hands.

n02564.summary: Abu Hurayrah says he had fifteen dates, broke his fast with five, ate Sehri with five and kept five to break his fast with later.

n02581.summary: Hishaam bin Khaalid saw Umar tie his waist-wrap above his navel, and Aamir bin Ubaydah Baahili reports Anas saying he wished khazz had never been created, since all the Sahabah except Umar and his son wore it.

n02596.summary: Abu Is'haaq reports seeing Abdullaah bin Umar wear his waist-wrap halfway down his calves, and seeing Usaamah bin Zaid, Zaid bin Arqam and Baraa bin Aazib dressed the same way.

n02617.summary: Abu Dardaa says that freeing a hundred slaves from one man's wealth is a great deed, but better is imaan that stays in the heart day and night, with the tongue kept moist with the dhikr of Allaah.

n02644.summary: Anas reports that the Prophet met a young Ansaari, Haarith, and asked how he felt that morning; Haarith said he felt like a true believer, the Prophet advised him to weigh his words, and Haarith said he had turned his eyes away from this world.

n02645.summary: The Prophet asks how a person substantiates his imaan, since every statement requires proof.

n02652.summary: Abu Dharr warns his people that on the Day of Qiyaamah mankind will be resurrected in three groups, and that a calamity will destroy all riding animals.

n02655.summary: A man told the Prophet ﷺ 'what Allaah wills and what you will', and the Prophet rebuked him for equating him with Allaah.

n02669.summary: On his deathbed Salmaan asks for musk to be sprinkled around him, because angels who smell fragrance but do not eat are coming to him.

n02679.summary: Umar used to recite couplets from the pulpit saying that the outcome of all matters is in Allaah's hand.

n02688.summary: Abu Bakr said that the clothing of the dead will only be given over to body fluids and decay.

n02721.summary: Ali consoled Umar, who was weeping after being stabbed, with the glad tidings of Jannah that Ali had heard from the Prophet.

n02751.summary: Abu Bakr asks how anyone can be safe from punishment for every sin, and the Prophet says the hardships of this world are the retribution for sins.

n02776.summary: On his deathbed the Prophet stressed salaah and the treatment of slaves more than anything else, until he could no longer speak.

n02782.summary: Abdullaah bin Amr said that the ground on which a Muslim prays will testify for him on the day he meets Allaah.

n02788.summary: Abu Moosa Ash'ari said that the Fardh salaah compensates for the sins a person commits between one prayer and the next.

n02790.summary: Jibra'eel told the Prophet that salaah had been made beloved to him, so he should take from it as much as he pleases.

n02794.summary: Aa'isha and Anas describe how the Prophet stood so long in night salaah that his feet ruptured, and said he should be a grateful servant.

n02795.summary: Anas describes how the Prophet's night salaah, sleep and fasting varied, so that his Companions could not predict them.

n02808.summary: Uthmaan once stood by the Maqaam Ibraheem at night and recited the entire Qur'aan in a single rakaah.

n02809.summary: After leading the people in salaah, Uthmaan would stand behind the Maqaam Ibraheem and recite the entire Qur'aan in one rakaah of witr.

n02810.summary: Muhammad bin Seereen would stand in salaah all night, completing the entire Qur'aan in a single rakaah.

n02815.summary: Ibn Mas'ood was not very regular with Duha salaah, and he explained that he fasted less often because fasting weakened him for salaah.

n02819.summary: Abu Uthmaan Nahdi stayed seven days with Abu Hurayrah, whose household took turns worshipping through a third of each night.

n02843.summary: The Prophet explains that his reason for walking to the masjid with short steps is to increase the steps he takes for salaah.

n02860.summary: Ataa reports that the Companion Ya'la bin Umayyah would sit in the masjid, even for a moment, with the intention of i'tikaaf.

n02865.summary: The Prophet drank fadeekh in a masjid, which is why it was named Masjidul Fadeekh; the rest is the author's cross-reference to other narrations about the masjid.

n02870.summary: Jaabir said swords should not be drawn in the masjid, and the Prophet told a man carrying arrows through it to hold their heads firmly.

n02873.summary: Ubay bin Ka'b rebuked a man who called out for a lost item in the masjid, saying they had been commanded to do so.

n02889.summary: Ibn Mas'ood disapproves of appointing blind men or Qur'aan teachers to call the adhaan.

n02898.summary: The Prophet says a person keeps receiving the angels' prayers for his forgiveness for as long as salaah keeps him waiting in his place.

n02899.summary: Abu Hurayrah relates that a person keeps receiving the angels' prayers while he waits in his place of salaah, and that wudhu breaks when wind is passed.

n02905.summary: Ibn Mas'ood says that people who pray at home and leave the masjids forsake the Sunnah of the Prophet.

n02910.summary: Ibn Umar, whenever he missed a congregational salaah, would keep praying until the next salaah.

n02926.summary: Anas says the Prophet stood up with a Bedouin who held his clothing and demanded his due, and only then returned to lead salaah.

n02947.summary: Adi bin Haatim criticised an imam who prolonged the salaah, then led briefly himself; Anas refused to follow such imams until Umar bin Abdul Azeez ended the practice.

n02963.summary: Bilaal reports that the Prophet came out late for Fajr because he was praying his two sunnah rakaahs, which he would perform properly even if the sky were brighter.

n02965.summary: Ali reports that the Prophet prayed four rakaahs before Zuhr and two after it.

n02976.summary: Ibn Mas'ood says the four rakaahs before Zuhr are the only daytime salaah equal to night salaah, since they are regarded as on par with Tahajjud.

n02978.summary: Naafi reports that Ibn Umar prayed eight rakaahs before Zuhr and four after it.

n02980.summary: Ali called the salaahs between Maghrib and Isha 'Salaatul Chaflah' and warned people they had become negligent, and Ibn Umar said that whoever prays four rakaahs after Maghrib is like a fighter in battle after battle.

n02998.summary: Ibn Abbaas prayed Duha once every ten days, and Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas prayed eight rakaahs of Duha, as reported by his daughter.

n03025.summary: On the Suffa, the Prophet said that learning or teaching two verses of the Qur'aan in the masjid is better than two camels, and more verses are better than as many camels.

n03030.summary: Ibn Mas'ood urges people to seek knowledge of the Deen before it is taken away, warns against hair-splitting, and tells them to follow the practice of the Sahabah.

n03063.summary: Ibn Abbaas rebukes people for asking the Ahlul Kitaab, since the Qur'aan they have is unaltered and the Ahlul Kitaab altered their own scriptures for worldly gain.

n03066.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar wept after hearing from Abdullaah bin Amr a hadith warning that anyone with pride the size of a mustard seed in his heart will be thrown headlong into the fire.

n03076.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood said they would not learn the next ten verses of the Qur'aan until they had put the first ten into practice; asked whether this meant practising first, Shareek confirmed it.

n03088.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports that Abu Bakr used to teach the Tashahhud to the people from the pulpit, as children are taught at school.

n03089.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas reports that Umar bin Khattaab took his hand and taught him the Tashahhud, which Umar had himself been taught by the Prophet; a second report from Abdur Rahmaan al-Qaari of Umar teaching it from the pulpit follows, and the text is cut off.

n03114.summary: Zaid bin Thaabit says the Prophet asked him to learn the Syriac (or Hebrew) language because letters were coming to him, and he learnt it in seventeen days.

n03139.summary: Ubaydullaah bin Adi says he asked Ali about a hadith and Ali related it on condition that he tell no one else; Ibn Mas'ood's saying about travelling far for knowledge of the Book is introduced.

n03140.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood says that if a camel could carry him to someone with more knowledge of what was revealed to Muhammad ﷺ than he has, he would go to them to increase his own knowledge.

n03142.summary: Abu Tha'laba says he went to Abu Ubaydah bin Jarraah, who was talking with Basheer bin Sa'd, and Abu Ubaydah then related the Prophet's words that after prophethood would come a khilaafah on its pattern, followed by monarchy and tyranny.

n03180.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar says a man can only be a respected scholar if he is free of envy, does not look down on those beneath him, and does not sell his knowledge.

n03194.summary: Umar bin Khattaab said dowries should not exceed forty awqiya; a woman stood up and corrected him from Surah Nisaa verse 20, and Umar accepted that she was right.

n03195.summary: Muhammad bin Ka'b Qurazi reports that a man corrected Ali's answer to a question; Ali admitted he was wrong and recited the verse that above every knowledgeable person is one more knowledgeable.

n03196.summary: Sa'eed bin Musayyib says Umar and Uthmaan would debate a question so fiercely that onlookers thought they could never be reconciled, yet they always parted most amicably.

n03204.summary: Ali tells people to rehearse the ahadith among themselves so they do not forget them, and adds that they should keep visiting each other.

n03217.summary: Ummu Sulaym asks the Prophet whether a woman must bathe after dreaming of intercourse; he says yes if she finds semen, and tells Ummu Salamah, who objected, that women are offshoots of men.

n03224.summary: Aamir reports that when Ammaar was asked about a matter, he asked whether it had actually happened, and when told it had not, said to leave it until it does.

n03227.summary: Anas reports that Abu Talha came to the Masjid and found the Prophet teaching the men of Suffa, with a stone tied to his belly against hunger.

n03229.summary: Anas reports that Umar asked about Abu Moosa Ash'ari, who was teaching the Qur'aan in Basrah; Abu Rajaa then says Abu Moosa taught him Surah Alaq, the first surah revealed to the Prophet.

n03241.summary: Umar tells the Sahabah not to occupy people with ahadith in a way that stops them mastering the Qur'aan; a second report has Umar explaining why he walked with them, and that report is abridged.

n03243.summary: Sulaymaan bin Yasaar relates that Sabeegh bin Isl kept questioning the mutashaabih verses of the Qur'aan, so Umar beat him with date-palm branches until his head bled; Sabeegh then said that his doubt had gone.

n03249.summary: Tufayl bin Amr gave Ubay bin Ka'b a bow after Ubay taught him the Qur'aan; the Prophet asked Ubay why he wore it, called it a spark from Jahannam, and explained that food prepared for others may be eaten but food prepared specially for the teacher eats from his share in the Aakhirah.

n03258.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood advises that a man of the Qur'aan should be known by his night prayers, fasting, sorrow, weeping and humility, and should be a good listener; another report gives further advice to listen and heed Allah's commands.

n03265.summary: Abdur Rahmaan bin Haatib says he has not seen any Companion narrate hadith as well and thoroughly as Uthmaan, though Uthmaan was very reluctant to narrate.

n03269.summary: Masrooq reports that when Ibn Mas'ood began a hadith with 'The Prophet said', he shook so much that his clothes trembled, and then added that the Prophet said something to that effect.

n03272.summary: Abu Ja'far Muhammad bin Ali says that no Companion of the Prophet was more careful than Abdullaah bin Umar about adding to or omitting anything from the Prophet's ahadith.

n03287.summary: Abdullaah bin Ukaym quotes Ibn Mas'ood that on the Day of Judgement each person will be asked whether he acted on his knowledge; Adi bin Adi relates Ibn Mas'ood's warning that the one who has knowledge but does not practise is destroyed.

n03288.summary: Ibn Mas'ood says everyone has fine words but only those whose deeds match their words will succeed, and that people need the scholar who acts on his knowledge and the one absorbed in Allaah.

n03292.summary: Anas says that knowledge brings no reward until it is practised, and that true scholars seek to remember and act on it while foolish people seek only to relate it to others.

n03310.summary: Umar says the Sunnah is what Allaah and His Rasool have determined, and that one should not let one's own opinion take its place; Amr bin Dinaar reports Umar disclaiming that Allaah guided his judgements, as that was a speciality of the Prophet.

n03325.summary: Abu Husayn says that people now issue fatwas on matters which, had they been put to Umar, he would have referred to the veterans of Badr before answering.

n03337.summary: The Prophet tells Faatima that he has married her to the first of his Ummah to accept Islaam, the most knowledgeable and most tolerant man.

n03347.summary: Aamir, son of Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas, reports his father's praise of Abdullaah bin Abbaas for his wit and knowledge, and that Umar would call him for complicated problems and accept his opinion even in front of the Badr veterans.

n03348.summary: Abu Zinaad reports that Umar visited the ill Abdullaah bin Abbaas and that Talha praised his understanding; Muhammad bin Ubay bin Ka'b reports that Ubay foretold Ibn Abbaas would become the most learned scholar of the Ummah, since the Prophet had prayed for his understanding of Deen.

n03351.summary: Ibn Abbaas relates that Umar asked him a question that Ya'la bin Umayyah had sent from Yemen; after the answer, Umar testified that Ibn Abbaas was the most eligible to speak on behalf of the Prophet's household.

n03352.summary: Ataa says people came to Ibn Abbaas to ask about poetry, lineage and the battles and history of the Arabs, and he gave each group a full answer.

n03354.summary: Ibn Abbaas says he stayed close to the senior Muhaajireen and Ansaar to learn about the battles and the revelations concerning them; Ubay bin Ka'b told him that twenty-seven Surahs were revealed at Madinah and the rest at Makkah.

n03365.summary: Urwa says he has not seen a woman as knowledgeable in medicine, fiqh and poetry as Aa'isha.

n03366.summary: Urwa asks his aunt Aa'isha how she came to know fiqh, Arab history, lineage, poetry and medicine; she says she learnt medicine from the remedies that physicians sent when the Prophet's illness worsened.

n03367.summary: Aa'isha says that by using these remedies to treat the Prophet she learnt all about them.

n03370.summary: Ibn Mas'ood says that scholars who hand their knowledge to worldly people for a share of the world fall in the eyes of the people, and quotes the Prophet that whoever makes the Aakhirah his only worry, Allaah will take care of his other worries.

n03371.summary: Sufyaan bin Uyaynah reports Ibn Abbaas saying that scholars who uphold knowledge properly are loved by Allaah, His angels and the pious and held in awe by people, while those who seek worldly wealth with it are detested by Allaah and lose their standing.

n03380.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood warns that frequenting the doors of rulers brings tribulation and that the Deen is lost in exchange for their wealth.

n03397.summary: Asked which jihaad carries most reward, the Prophet said it is the jihaad of those who engage most in dhikr, and a man is told to keep his tongue moist with the dhikr of Allaah.

n03401.summary: Umar says to engage in the dhikr of Allaah because it is a cure, and to avoid discussing people because it is a disease.

n03402.summary: Uthmaan says that had their hearts been pure they would never tire of the dhikr of Allaah.

n03420.summary: Mu'aadh bin Jabal says he prefers the dhikr of Allaah from morning to night over providing thoroughbred horses for jihaad.

n03434.summary: Abu Barzah reports the words the Prophet recited at the end of every gathering, which he said are an expiation for the sins of that gathering.

n03452.summary: Aa'isha reports that the Prophet would not sleep until he had recited Surah Zumar and Surah Bani Israa'eel.

n03456.summary: Umar says that whoever recites Surah Baqarah, Aal Imraan and Nisaa in a single night is recorded among the obedient.

n03457.summary: Jubayr bin Mut'im reports that the Prophet taught him to recite the last five surahs on journeys, after which he always had the best position and the most provisions.

n03470.summary: Zaid bin Arqam reports that whoever recites the Kalimah with sincerity enters Jannah, and Abu Sa'eed Khudri reports Allaah's answer to Musa that the Kalimah outweighs the seven heavens and earths.

n03473.summary: The Prophet says that if the heavens, the earth and everything in them were made into a ring with the Kalimah placed on top, it would shatter them all.

n03499.summary: Ibn Kawwaa asks Ali about the phrase Subhaanallaah, and Ali explains it is a phrase Allaah chose for Himself to proclaim His purity from all evil.

n03500.summary: Umar eases the lashing of one of two men he had flogged, because that man was saying tasbeeh, which can only find a place in the heart of a believer.

n03501.summary: Ibn Mas'ood explains that when a person recites the tasbeeh and dhikr words an angel carries them up to the heavens, and he cites the verse that the pure word rises to Allaah.

n03519.summary: Abu Qilaabah reports that two men who met in the marketplace sought Allaah's forgiveness together, and one later saw the other in a dream and learned that they had been forgiven.

n03523.summary: Abu Tameemah Hujaymi reports that the Prophet taught a rider behind him on a stumbling animal to say Bismillaah, which humiliates Shaytaan.

n03525.summary: Anas reports that whenever the Sahabah reached a destination they recited Subhaanallaah until they had unloaded their carriages.

n03531.summary: Ka'b bin Ujrah reports that the Prophet said Aameen on each step of the pulpit after Jibra'eel's curses on the person who misses forgiveness in Ramadhaan, who fails to send salutations on him, and who fails his aged parents.

n03540.summary: Ibn Abbaas says that it is not appropriate to send salutations upon anyone other than the Ambiyaa.

n03581.summary: Aa'isha says the Prophet raised his hands in du'aa for so long that she would grow tired watching.

n03591.summary: Abu Umaamah Baahili reports that when the Prophet was asked for du'aa he prayed for forgiveness, mercy, acceptance, Jannah and protection from Jahannam for them, and said he had included all their affairs.

n03594.summary: The Prophet tells people who meet Uwais Qarni to ask him to seek forgiveness on their behalf.

n03602.summary: Abu Ayaash adds that the Prophet's du'aa also asked Allaah for Jannah and for protection from Jahannam.

n03605.summary: Salamah and Anas report that the Prophet began every du'aa with a praise and always included the request for the best of this world and the Aakhirah and protection from the Fire.

n03614.summary: Ibn Mas'ood reports the Prophet's du'aa, 'O Allaah! Assist Islaam through Umar.'

n03616.summary: Abu Sa'eed Khudri reports that the Prophet three times said he was pleased with Uthmaan and asked Allaah to be pleased with him too.

n03617.summary: Ibn Mas'ood reports the Prophet's du'aa asking Allaah to forgive all of Uthmaan's past and future sins, public and private.

n03622.summary: Ibn Abbaas reports the Prophet's du'aa for Ali: 'O Allaah! Guide him in passing judgement.'

n03627.summary: Ali reports that the Prophet drew a shawl over himself, Faatimah, Hasan and Husayn and prayed that Allaah be pleased with them as he was.

n03630.summary: Usaama reports the Prophet added that he loves whoever loves Hasan and Husayn, and Abu Hurayrah reports that he added that he detests whoever detests them; the Prophet called them his children.

n03631.summary: Abu Hurayrah, Sa'eed bin Zaid and Aa'isha report the Prophet's du'aa 'I love Hasan, so love him too', and Muhammad bin Seereen reports his du'aa that Hasan be kept safe and keep others safe through him.

n03632.summary: Baraa reports seeing the Prophet carry Husayn on his shoulders and pray, 'O Allaah! I love him, so You love him too.'

n03636.summary: Abu Usayd Saa'idi reports the Prophet gathering Abbaas and his household under a shawl and praying that Allaah shelter them from Jahannam; Ibn Abbaas reports the Prophet's du'aa for his understanding of the Deen and the Qur'aan.

n03638.summary: Ibn Umar reports the Prophet's du'aa, 'O Allaah! Bless him and spread the Deen through him.'

n03648.summary: Jareer reports that after the Prophet placed his hand on Jareer's chest and prayed that he be steady and rightly guided, he never fell from a horse again.

n03649.summary: Jareer reports the Prophet asking him to relieve him of Dhu Khalasa, the Khath'am idol-house, and Jareer repeats that he cannot stay steady on a horse.

n03650.summary: Abdullaah bin Busr reports that the Prophet ate at his family's door and prayed for blessings on them, after which they always saw abundant sustenance.

n03660.summary: The Prophet prays after rising from a Fajr rakah for the release of Waleed bin Waleed, Salamah bin Hishaam, Ayaash bin Abu Rabee'ah and the other oppressed Muslims in Makkah, and against Mudhar; the text then breaks into a farewell du'aa.

n03702.summary: Umar reports the Prophet's words seeking Allaah's complete protection for Hasan and Husayn from every Shaytaan, harmful creature and evil eye.

n03707.summary: Khaalid bin Waleed often woke frightened from sleep, and the Prophet taught him to say Bismillaah on waking and then the du'aa to dispel what he saw in his dreams.

n03708.summary: Waleed bin Waleed told Rasulullaah that he often felt fearful, and Rasulullaah advised him to recite the du'aa when going to bed.

n03719.summary: Abu Raafi reports that Abdullaah bin Ja'far, under duress, married his daughter to Hajjaaj bin Yusuf and taught her a du'aa from Rasulullaah that kept Hajjaaj from getting close to her.

n03722.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood teaches a du'aa to say when fearing a tyrannical ruler, asking Allaah for protection from him, from the jinn and from mankind.

n03734.summary: Jaabir reports Rasulullaah's sermon urging repentance, dhikr and sadaqah, and stating that the Jumu'ah salaah is compulsory until the Day of Qiyaamah, with a warning against neglecting it.

n03744.summary: Raafi bin Amr Muzani saw Rasulullaah deliver a sermon at Mina on a brown mule, with Ali repeating his words for the crowd.

n03745.summary: Abu Hurra Raqaashi reports Rasulullaah's sermon on the days of Tashreeq during Hajj: the sanctity of life, property and honour, the waiving of interest and of Jahiliyyah blood-feuds, the rights of husbands and wives, and the command to convey the message. Humayd and Abdullaah bin Umar add further reports.

n03764.summary: Anas bin Maalik reports Rasulullaah warning in a sermon that interest is a grave sin, and Abu Moosa Ash'ari reports his warning against Shirk together with the du'aa for protection from it.

n03779.summary: Abu Hurayrah reports Rasulullaah urging people to think well of the Lord of the universe, because Allaah treats His servants according to their expectation of Him.

n03781.summary: Tha'laba reports Rasulullaah ordering Sadaqatul Fitr of a saa of dates or a saa of barley for every person, whether minor or adult, free or slave.

n03789.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas reports that during his final illness Rasulullaah came out with his head bound and gave his last sermon, which also included advice about the Ansaar.

n03791.summary: Another narration confirms that this was the last sermon Rasulullaah ever delivered.

n03797.summary: Hasan (al-Basri) reports Abu Bakr's speech on taking up the khilaafah: he is not the best of them, he dislikes the post, and he asks to be watched and corrected if he strays.

n03835.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas reports Umar's lecture defending stoning (Rajm) as a penalty ordained by Allaah, carried out by Rasulullaah and afterwards, and warning of people who will deny Rajm, Dajjaal, intercession, punishment in the grave and release from Jahannam.

n03842.summary: Qabeesah reports that Umar said from the pulpit that whoever shows no mercy will receive none, and whoever does not forgive, repent or abstain from sin will not be forgiven, accepted or saved.

n03843.summary: Urwa reports Umar's saying that greed leads to poverty and losing hope leads to independence; Abdullaah bin Khiraash reports Umar's du'aa asking Allaah to hold them with His rope and keep them steadfast on the Deen.

n03846.summary: Abdullaah bin Zubayr reports Umar's warning that men who wear silk in this world will not be given silk in the Aakhirah; Abu Ubayd, freed slave of Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf, reports Umar leading the Eid salaah without adhaan or iqaamah, then forbidding fasting on the two Eid days.

n03847.summary: Alqama bin Waqqaas Laythi reports Umar's lecture quoting Rasulullaah that actions are judged by intention; Sulaymaan bin Yasaar reports Umar's address in a drought, calling the people to pray with him for relief.

n03855.summary: Qutaybah bin Muslim reports Hajjaaj's sermon on the grave, which he backs with a chain: Abdul Malik and Marwaan report that Uthmaan said Rasulullaah always wept whenever he saw a grave or spoke of one.

n03857.summary: Hasan (al-Basri) reports that Uthmaan instructed from the pulpit that dangerous dogs should be killed and pigeons kept for sport should be slaughtered.

n03864.summary: Asbagh bin Nabaatah reports Ali's sermon on death and the coming day, when even the young will turn white and people will look intoxicated from the severity of Allaah's punishment; Ali and those around him wept.

n03884.summary: Abdullaah bin Sabt reports that Ali foretold his own death at the hand of an assassin, forbade his followers from killing anyone but the assassin, and refused to name a successor, preferring to leave the Ummah as Rasulullaah had left it.

n03886.summary: Umayr bin Abdul Malik reports Ali's sermon from Kufa, in which Ali says Rasulullaah told him, quoting Allaah, that Allaah turns His punishment away from those who turn from disobedience to obedience and turns His wrath towards those who turn from obedience to disobedience.

n03888.summary: Abu Tufayl reports Hasan bin Ali's address after his father's death: he names his lineage, recites Qur'anic verses on the Prophet's family, and says Rasulullaah handed the flag to Ali while Jibra'eel fought beside him.

n03894.summary: Umayr bin Haani reports Mu'aawiya bin Abi Sufyaan quoting Rasulullaah that this Ummah will stay steadfast on the Deen until the Day of Qiyaamah and will dominate others; Maalik bin Yakhaamir says he heard Mu'aadh bin Jabal identify these people as the people of Shaam.

n03899.summary: Ataa bin Abi Rabaah reports Abdullaah bin Zubayr quoting Rasulullaah that one salaah in the Masjid of Madinah is better than a thousand elsewhere, except the Masjidul Haraam; Ibn Zubayr explained that the whole Haram counts as a Masjid.

n03907.summary: Abu Waa'il reports that after Umar's death Abdullaah bin Mas'ood travelled from Madinah to Kufa and told the people to pledge allegiance to Uthmaan, as the Companions had done.

n03918.summary: Uqba bin Abul Ayraaz reports Husayn bin Ali's address at Bayda to the army of Hurr bin Yazeed, quoting Rasulullaah on the tyrant, rebuking the ruling party, and calling on the people of Kufa to keep their pledge, reminding them how they had treated his father, brother and cousin Muslim bin Aqeel.

n03938.summary: Sufyaan Thowri reports that Umar wrote to Abu Moosa Ash'ari that wisdom is a gift from Allaah rather than something that comes with age, and told him to stay away from shameful acts and evil character.

n03941.summary: Ali tells Umar that to meet his two companions, Rasulullaah and Abu Bakr, he should curb his hopes, eat less than his fill, shorten his loincloth, and patch and mend his garments and shoes.

n03949.summary: Amr bin Maymoon Awdi reports Mu'aadh bin Jabal telling the Banu Awd that everyone will return to Allaah and go to Jannah or Jahannam, to live there forever.

n03951.summary: Abdullaah bin Salamah reports Mu'aadh bin Jabal's advice to a man who asked to be taught: fast only at times, pray at night and also sleep, earn without sinning, die as a Muslim, and beware the curse of the oppressed.

n03955.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood says that the best of this world has passed on, leaving only waste, so death is a gift for every Muslim.

n03959.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood says that each person is a guest and his wealth is borrowed: the guest must leave one day, and the borrowed item must be returned to its owner.

n03962.summary: Mundhir reports that when non-Arab chiefs visited Abdullaah bin Mas'ood, he told the people that a healthy-bodied kaafir may have a sick heart and a sick-bodied Muslim a healthy heart; he also taught that comfort lies only in meeting Allaah, that no one should follow others blindly in faith, and that Allaah conceals a person's faults in this world and will do so in the Aakhirah.

n03964.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood says that whoever does things to be seen in this world will have his faults shown on the Day of Qiyaamah, that whoever seeks to be heard will have his faults made known, and that Allaah humiliates the proud and raises the humble.

n03971.summary: Abu Dardaa advises worshipping Allaah as if seeing Him, counting oneself among the dead, being content with little, and remembering that good deeds never age and sins are never forgotten; he adds that goodness lies in knowledge, forbearance and excelling in worship, and that one should praise Allaah when doing well and seek His forgiveness when doing wrong.

n03973.summary: Abu Dardaa says the apex of Imaan is steadfastly fulfilling Allaah's orders, being content with His decree, trusting Him and surrendering to Him; he warns against being consumed by wealth, and addresses the people of Damascus about storing and building beyond their needs and the ruin of earlier nations.

n03977.summary: Shurahbeel reports that whenever Abu Dardaa saw a funeral he would say that the living follow the dead, that death is a powerful advice, and that only the senseless remain unheedful.

n03979.summary: Abu Dardaa says that a person who often thinks of death will show off less and be less jealous.

n03981.summary: Abdullaah bin Jubayr bin Nufayr reports that a man asked Abu Dardaa for something that would benefit him, and Abu Dardaa advised eating, earning and bringing home only what is pure, seeking daily sustenance from Allaah, counting oneself among the dead, entrusting one's honour to Allaah, and seeking forgiveness after sin.

n03982.summary: Abu Dardaa says a person stays youthful in his love for this world even in old age, and gives three rules: never complain of calamities, never speak of your illness, never claim spiritual purity.

n03985.summary: Abu Dardaa writes to a companion that only what one sends ahead for the Aakhirah is truly one's own, so one should spend for oneself rather than hoard for heirs; he also writes to Maslamah that Allaah makes all creation love the person whose actions conform to His commands.

n03989.summary: Abu Dharr says people are born to die and buildings are built to fall, that people chase what ends while neglecting what lasts, and that death and poverty are the two things people dislike.

n03990.summary: Hibbaan bin Abi Jabalah reports that Abu Dharr and Abu Dardaa both said people are born to die and build to ruin, chase what ends while neglecting what lasts, and dislike three things: death, illness and poverty.

n03994.summary: Hudhayfah warns against the trials of temptation, which sweep away anyone who tries to stand against them alone, and says that when such trials come one should stay at home, break one's swords and cut one's bowstrings.

n03995.summary: Hudhayfah says the trials of life have periods of calm and periods of upheaval, and that if one can choose to die during the calm, one should do so.

n03997.summary: Several sayings of Hudhayfah: trials wear a person down more than pure wine does; in the time of trial only one who calls on Allaah like a drowning man is safe; and the best person takes from both this world and the Aakhirah, as reported by A'mash.

n04007.summary: Wahab bin Kaysaan reports Abdullaah bin Zubayr's letter of advice: the people of taqwa show patience in adversity, contentment with Allaah's decree, gratitude for blessings and submission to the Qur'aan; and a ruler attracts whatever is popular with him, truth or falsehood.

n04015.summary: Abdullaah bin Busr says the people of taqwa are simple, the scholars are leaders, sitting in their company is worship, time shortens life while deeds are recorded, so one should prepare provisions for the return to Allaah.

n04018.summary: Ibn Abbaas says the angels at Badr wore white turbans and only added to the Muslims' strength; Abu Raafi, freed slave of the Prophet, tells how Abu Lahab, who sent a substitute to Badr, struck him when news of the defeat arrived, how Ummu Fadhl hit Abu Lahab with a tent pole, and how Abu Lahab died of a plague within seven days.

n04034.summary: Haarith bin Simma says the Prophet told him the angels were fighting beside Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf at Badr; Abdur Rahmaan, standing among seven fallen enemies, said he had killed only two of them himself.

n04045.summary: Anas says Ubay bin Ka'b resolved to praise Allaah in the Masjid, then heard an unseen voice behind him saying words of praise and repentance, and reported it to the Prophet, who said it was Jibra'eel.

n04054.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports the Prophet saying that seventy thousand angels came down for the funeral of Sa'd bin Muaadh, and that if anyone could be saved from the squeezing of the grave it would have been Sa'd.

n04055.summary: Sa'd bin Ibraheem reports that some hypocrites mocked how light Sa'd bin Muaadh's bier was, and the Prophet said seventy thousand angels had come down for his funeral.

n04072.summary: Naafi bin Aasim says that the man who injured the Prophet's face was Abdullaah bin Qami'ah, and Allaah sent a ram that gored him to death.

n04077.summary: Abu Bakr bin Muhammad bin Amr bin Hazam reports that Sa'eed bin Zaid called on Allaah against a woman named Arwa who falsely claimed he had wronged her; a flood then showed the boundary in his favour, and within a month Arwa went blind and fell into her well.

n04081.summary: Mahmood bin Labeed reports from Qataadah that his eye was knocked out at Uhud and fell onto his cheek, and the Prophet put it back in its socket, after which it became the better of his two eyes.

n04086.summary: Habeeb bin Fuwayk reports that his father's eyes turned completely white after his leg fell on a snake's egg, and that when the Prophet applied saliva to the eyes his father could see at once.

n04094.summary: Ali tells people not to question Umar for calling out 'O Saariyah' in his sermon, since Umar always has a valid reason; Umar says the idea of using the mountain for defence came to his heart and he spoke hoping one of Allaah's servants would convey it to the army.

n04107.summary: A narration from Baraa says that Sawaad bin Qaarib was in India when a Jinn came to him; Muhammad bin Ka'b reports that Sawaad, having heard the call of Islaam, went to Madinah after the Prophet had migrated, recited verses to the Prophet, who smiled and called him successful.

n04141.summary: Zaid bin Khaarija's corpse speaks after death: it praises the one in the middle of three rulers as one who never feared blame, says Uthmaan will be Ameer and that strife will follow, urges obedience to the ruler, calls for Abdullaah bin Rawaaha, asks after his father Khaarija, and recites a verse on Jahannam.

n04144.summary: Another narration identifies the old, blind woman in the story as Ummu Saa'ib.

n04157.summary: Dahhaak reports that the Prophet sent Miqdaad and Zubayr to take Khubayb bin Adi's body down from the pole; the body was still fresh, Zubayr had to leave it when the Mushrikeen closed in, and the ground took it in, which is why Khubayb was called the one the ground took in.

n04159.summary: Abu Hurayrah reports that the Companions buried Alaa bin Hadhrami in soft sand, went back to protect the body from wild animals and could not find it, then dug a grave without a recess and could not find that grave again.

n04165.summary: Safeenah says that after a shipwreck he and his companions lost their way, and a lion walked ahead of him to the main road, then nudged him as if to bid them farewell.

n04176.summary: Abu Bakr sent Alaa bin Hadhrami to fight the apostates in Bahrain; the lost camels came back with their loads, Allaah provided a pond of water, and Alaa led the army on foot across the gulf to defeat the enemy and return, all within a single day.

n04179.summary: Abu Uthmaan Nahdi tells how Gharqadah slipped from his horse while the Muslims crossed the Tigris and was pulled out by Qa'qaa bin Amr, and how a lost cup was returned; Umayr Saa'idi reports that Sa'd led the army across in pairs with mounds appearing to rest on; and Qais bin Abu Haazim says the deepest part reached only a horseman's reins.

n04180.summary: Habeeb bin Suhbaan reports that Hujr bin Adi asked what kept the Muslims from crossing the Tigris, recited a verse on the fixed time of death, plunged in on his horse, and the others followed until the enemy fled calling them madmen.

n04181.summary: Habeeb bin Suhbaan reports that when the Persians saw the Muslims crossing the Tigris on the day Madaa'in was conquered, they called them mad devils and said they were fighting Jinn, and so they were defeated.

n04192.summary: Hamzah bin Amr says that when hypocrites made the Prophet's camel bolt at Tabook and his luggage fell, all five of his fingers lit up so he could pick up the whip, rope and other items.

n04200.summary: Maalik Daar reports that in Umar's time of drought a man went to the Prophet's grave, saw him in a dream saying rain would soon come and Umar should keep using his judgement; when told, Umar wept and said he was doing all he could.

n04208.summary: Baraa bin Aazib says that the fourteen hundred people at Hudaybiyyah drew all the water from its well, then the Prophet sat on the rim, made du'aa, gargled and spat into the well, and soon there was enough water for all of them and their animals.

n04209.summary: Jaabir bin Abdullaah reports that during Hudaybiyyah the Companions had no water except what was in the Prophet's leather bag; when he put his hand in it, water flowed between his fingers, and Baraa said it would have been enough for a hundred thousand.

n04218.summary: Abu Hurayrah and Abu Sa'eed Khudri report that during the hunger of Tabook the Companions asked to slaughter their water camels for food and oil; the Prophet permitted it, Umar intervened, and the narration then breaks off.

n04224.summary: Waathila bin Asqa tells how, when the men of Suffa were hungry, the Prophet asked Aa'isha for her bread, made thareed with his own hands so that it multiplied, and fed groups of ten until all were full with the plate still full; a second narration gives twenty men and says bread and milk were served.

n04227.summary: Yahya bin Sa'eed reports that Ummu Shareek Dowsiyyah, fasting and thirsty on her migration after a Jewish couple refused her a drink, found a bucket of water in the night and drank from it; she had a small container of butter, and the narration goes on to describe its blessings.

n04237.summary: Anas says his mother Ummu Sulaym asked the Prophet to pray for him; the Prophet prayed for his wealth and children and for blessing in them, and Anas says he has buried a hundred and twenty-five children and his orchards bear fruit twice a year.

n04249.summary: A narration says that someone asked the Prophet whether he received food from Jannah.

n04254.summary: A narration of a Sahabi and his wife: she prays for provision for what they can grind, knead and bake, the bowl fills with bread and the grindstone grinds by itself; when her husband stops it, the Prophet says had he left it, it would have gone on grinding until the Day of Qiyaamah.

n04255.summary: Abu Hurayrah reports that a poor Ansaari's wife, with no food in the house, ground grain and lit the oven so the neighbours would think they had food; on the husband's return they found the grindstone turning, flour everywhere and the oven full of bread, and the Prophet said had the husband left it, it would have gone on grinding for his whole life.

n04279.summary: Khaalid bin Waleed drank poison that Amr bin Buqayla carried, after reciting a du'aa, and it did him no harm.

n04281.summary: Ali says that after the Prophet applied his saliva to Ali's painful eyes before Khaybar, he never again felt heat or cold.

n04292.summary: Ubay bin Ka'b made du'aa during a thunderstorm and the rain was averted from him and Ibn Abbaas, while the others on the journey were soaked.

n04306.summary: Two reports say that the men who took part in the killing of Husayn, and the man who defecated on his grave, were struck with misfortune in this world.

n04313.summary: Ma'roof Mowsili heard a voice reciting couplets lamenting the death of Umar when he was martyred.

n04314.summary: Aa'isha heard an unseen voice lamenting Umar at night, reciting couplets in his praise and grief.

n04335.summary: Abdullaah bin Salaam says that Salmaan appeared to him in a dream after his death and advised him to hold fast to Tawakkul.

n04350.summary: Jaabir bin Abdullaah swears that the army at Qaadisiyyah sought the Aakhirah, and names three men whom they had doubted but who proved trustworthy and abstinent.

n04361.summary: Khaalid bin Waleed kept a hat containing hairs of the Prophet and said he was always granted victory when he faced an enemy wearing it.

n00001.summary: Ibn Abbaas narrates that the Prophet was greatly concerned for all of mankind to accept Imaan, and Allaah revealed verses telling him that guidance and misguidance are decreed.

n00003.summary: Quraysh leaders ask Abu Taalib to mediate; the Prophet offers them one statement, Laa Ilaaha Illallaah, and they refuse and leave.

n00004.summary: Sa'eed bin Musayyab reports that Abu Taalib died under pressure from Abu Jahal and Abdullaah bin Abi Umayyah, and that the Prophet was then told not to seek forgiveness for the Mushrikeen.

n00005.summary: Another report says Abu Taalib died without reciting the Kalimah while Abu Jahal and Abdullaah bin Abi Umayyah repeated their objections, and that the two verses were revealed afterwards.

n00006.summary: Abu Hurayrah narrates that the Prophet asked Abu Taalib on his death-bed to say Laa Ilaaha Illallaah, and Abu Taalib refused for fear of Quraysh ridicule; the verse Qasas 56 was revealed on that occasion.

n00007.summary: Aqeel bin Abi Taalib narrates that Abu Taalib asked the Prophet to stop saying things that hurt the Quraysh, and the Prophet refused, saying he could not stop what he was sent to do.

n00008.summary: Abu Taalib asks the Prophet to stop, and the Prophet refuses even if the sun and moon were placed in his hands; Jaabir then narrates how Utba bin Rabee'ah failed to bargain the Prophet off and was moved by his recitation of Surah Sajdah.

n00009.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar narrates that Utba bin Rabee'ah offered the Prophet wealth, position and leadership to stop his preaching; after the Prophet recited Surah Sajdah, Utba told the Quraysh to leave him alone.

n00010.summary: Miswar and Marwaan report that Budayl bin Waraqa told the Prophet that the Quraysh were ready to fight, and the Prophet replied that he came only for Umrah and offered a treaty, vowing to fight if they refused Islaam.

n00011.summary: The Tabraani version, also from Miswar and Marwaan, has the Prophet declare that he will fight the Quraysh for the Deen until victory or his death if they refuse Islaam and still fight.

n00012.summary: Sahal bin Sa'd narrates that at Khaybar the Prophet gave the flag to Ali, who was cured of eye pain by the Prophet's saliva, and that Ali was told to invite the people to Islaam before fighting.

n00013.summary: Miqdaad bin Amr narrates that he took Hakam bin Kaysaan prisoner, Umar wanted him executed, and the Prophet kept inviting Hakam until he accepted Islaam.

n00014.summary: Ibn Abbaas narrates that Wahshi bin Harb, who killed Hamza, asked whether he could be forgiven; after a series of verses that answered each objection, he accepted Islaam.

n00015.summary: Ibn Abbaas narrates verses revealed for murderers and adulterers who asked about expiation; a second report from Abu Tha'laba Khushani describes Faatima weeping at the Prophet's pale, tired appearance after a journey.

n00016.summary: Tameem Daari narrates the Prophet's saying that Islaam will reach every home, bringing honour to Muslims and disgrace to the disbelievers, and says he saw this come true in his own family.

n00017.summary: Anas narrates Umar's wish to win back six apostates from Bakr bin Waa'il by inviting them back before any execution; a second report from Abdur Rahmaan Al Qaari gives Umar's ruling on a man who reverted, and a third has Amr bin Al Aas asking how to treat a man who reverted repeatedly.

n00019.summary: Abu Imraan Jowni narrates that Umar wept on seeing a Christian monk worn out by worship, because the Qur'aan says such labour still ends in the Fire.

n00021.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood narrates that the Prophet prayed that Islaam be strengthened through Umar or Abu Jahal, and Allaah answered the prayer in Umar's favour.

n00022.summary: Thowbaan's report, promised for a later chapter, is summarised here: Umar, after leaving his sister's house, came to the Prophet, who shook him and asked what he wanted, and Umar accepted Islaam on the spot.

n00023.summary: Aslam narrates Umar's own account of how the Prophet seized his collar and called him to Islaam, and Umar testified to the Kalimah on the spot.

n00024.summary: Amr bin Uthmaan reports Uthmaan's account of meeting the Prophet at his aunt Arwa's house; after the Prophet recited Surah Dhaariyaat on the Hereafter, Uthmaan followed him out and accepted Islaam.
