n00025.summary: Ibn Is'haaq reports Ali's acceptance of Islaam after he found the Prophet and Khadeeja praying; Ali later recalls his father Abu Taalib's remark on seeing them pray, and Habba Urani reports seeing Ali laugh at it.

n00026.summary: Shaddaad bin Abdillaah reports Amr bin Abasa's account of meeting the Prophet in Makkah, accepting Islaam there, and being told to go home until the Prophet became dominant.

n00027.summary: Amr bin Abasa reports the Prophet's message of joining family ties, preserving life and roads, and worshipping one Allaah; a second account has Khaalid bin Sa'eed beaten and cast out by his father Sa'eed bin Al Aas for following the Prophet.

n00028.summary: Khaalid bin Sa'eed accepted Islaam after a dream, was beaten and cut off by his father for it, and then stayed constantly with the Prophet.

n00029.summary: Ibn Abbaas narrates Dimaad's conversion: he came to cure the Prophet, heard the Prophet's sermon and pledged Islaam; he later refused Abu Jahal's mockery, and Ali returned camels taken from his people.

n00030.summary: The Quraysh send Husayn to speak to the Prophet, who asks how many gods he worships; Husayn accepts Islaam on the Prophet's advice, and his son Imraan kisses his head, hands and feet.

n00031.summary: Abu Tameema Hujaymi narrates from a man of his tribe, who came to the Prophet, heard about Allaah, accepted Islaam immediately, and was then advised not to swear oaths.

n00032.summary: Mu'aawiya bin Haydah narrates that he came to the Prophet, asked what Islaam is, and was told about surrender to Allaah, salaah, zakaah and the brotherhood of Muslims.

n00033.summary: Adi bin Haatim narrates that he first fled from the Prophet, then came to him and accepted Islaam after the Prophet addressed his objections, and was told of the coming conquest of Kisra's treasures and safe travel from Heera.

n00034.summary: Adi bin Haatim narrates that his captured aunt was freed by the Prophet, who then spoke to Adi; Adi accepted Islaam, and the Prophet urged charity even of a date and foretold wealth and safety.

n00035.summary: Dhul Jowshin Dhababi narrates that after Badr he refused the Prophet's invitation to Islaam, and later regretted it when he heard the Prophet had taken control of the Kabah; the Prophet had Bilaal fill his satchel with dates.

n00036.summary: Basheer bin Khasaasiyah narrates that after accepting Islaam he was renamed Basheer and placed in Ahl us-Suffa, and that he followed the Prophet to the graveyard, where the Prophet greeted the dead.

n00037.summary: A man from the Baladawiyyah tribe, reporting from his grandfather, describes the Prophet, whom he saw trading, teaching leniency in buying and selling; he later accepted Islaam. Anas then narrates a separate story about inviting an uncle of the Banu Najjaar.

n00038.summary: Anas narrates that the Prophet visited a sick Jewish boy who served him, asked him to accept Islaam, and the boy did so with his father's consent.

n00039.summary: Anas narrates that the Prophet told a man to accept Islaam and he would be at peace; the man said he disliked it, and the Prophet replied, 'Even though you dislike it.'

n00040.summary: Asmaa bint Abi Bakr reports that on the day Makkah was conquered, the Prophet told Abu Quhaafa to accept Islaam and remain in peace.

n00041.summary: Asmaa reports that when the Prophet entered Makkah, Abu Bakr brought his father Abu Quhaafa to him; the Prophet had him sit before him, he accepted Islaam, and the Prophet advised him on his white hair.

n00042.summary: Mughiera bin Shu'ba narrates that the Prophet invited Abu Jahal to Islaam in a Makkah alley, and Abu Jahal refused, saying that the Bani Qusay had taken each office in turn and he would never accept a Nabi from among them.

n00043.summary: Abu Jahal persuades Waleed bin Mughiera to dismiss the Qur'aan he had been moved by, calling it magic.

n00044.summary: The Prophet warns Abu Sufyaan and Hind of death and the Hereafter and recites the Qur'aan to them, and Abu Sufyaan vouches for him against Hind's accusation.

n00045.summary: Uthmaan and Talha follow Zubayr to the Prophet and accept Islaam, and Uthmaan then reports a vision he had on his way back from Shaam.

n00046.summary: Ammaar bin Yaasir and Suhayb meet at Arqam's house, hear the Prophet and accept Islaam, then leave secretly in the evening.

n00047.summary: Sa'd bin Zurarah and Dhakwaan bin Abd Qais go to Makkah to settle a dispute, accept Islaam from the Prophet, and become the first from Madinah to do so.

n00048.summary: The Quraysh leaders offer the Prophet wealth, honour and kingship, then demand miracles; he refuses them all, and Abdullaah bin Abi Umayyah walks out unconvinced.

n00050.summary: As Surah Shu'araa is revealed, the Prophet climbs Marwah and calls the Quraysh tribes to Islaam, and Abu Lahab rejects him, prompting the revelation of Surah Lahab.

n00051.summary: The Prophet calls the family of Abdul Muttalib and others from Safa to hear a warning, and Abu Lahab rejects him, leading to the revelation of Surah Lahab.

n00052.summary: Abdullaah bin Ka'b describes the years of secret and open da'wah in Makkah and the approaches at Hajj; Maysara later recounts the Jewish description of the Prophet and his own acceptance of Islaam.

n00053.summary: Waabisa reports how the Prophet invited the Banu Abs to Islaam near Mina, and how Maysara bin Masrooq later accepted Islaam after the Jews described the Prophet.

n00054.summary: The Prophet calls the Kindah tribe at their camp near Ukaaz; they hesitate and withdraw, and a Jew later tells them they had missed a golden opportunity.

n00055.summary: The Prophet asks the Banu Aamir for protection to convey his message; an old man named Bujra Qushayri says his claim to prophethood is true, but the tribe refuses to accept it.

n00056.summary: Zuhri reports that the Prophet invited the Banu Aamir and then the Kindah tribe, and both refused; Bajeera bin Firaas objected that kingship would go to others, and an old man of the Banu Aamir later said the Prophet's claim was true.

n00057.summary: The Prophet invites a family of the Banu Kalb to Allaah and asks them to accept Islaam and assist him, and they reject his message.

n00058.summary: The Prophet calls the Banu Haneefah to Allaah and asks them to assist him, and they reject him more harshly than any other Arab tribe.

n00059.summary: Abbaas shows the Prophet the camps of the Arab tribes at Hajj; the Kindah and Banu Bakr refuse his call, and Abu Lahab tells the people that the Prophet is insane.

n00060.summary: Rabee'ah bin Ibaad, as a boy with his father at Mina, hears the Prophet call the tribes to Allaah while his uncle Abu Lahab follows him and denounces him.

n00061.summary: Mudrik asks his father about a gathering at Mina and sees the Prophet telling the people to say La Ilaaha Illallaah.

n00062.summary: Haarith sees the Prophet calling people at Mina, and Hassaan bin Thaabit reports Umar torturing slave women before he became a Muslim.

n00063.summary: The Prophet, Abu Bakr and Ali call the Banu Shaybaan to Islaam; they decline but pledge support, and the Prophet later announces the Banu Rabee'ah victory over the Persians.

n00065.summary: Ali praises the Ansaar for nurturing Islaam, and Umm Sa'd bint Sa'd describes the first Aqaba pledge made by six or seven men of Madinah.

n00066.summary: Aqeel and Zuhri report that the Prophet asked Abbaas to take him to the tribes at Ukaaz, and six men of Aws and Khazraj accept Islaam at Aqaba after hearing Surah Ibraheem.

n00067.summary: Rabee'ah bin Ibaad, Taariq bin Abdillaah and another man report the Prophet calling people to Laa Ilaaha Illallaah in the Dhul Majaaz market, while Abu Lahab and Abu Jahal oppose him.

n00069.summary: The Prophet gathers his close relatives and tells his daughter Faatima and his aunt Safiyya that he cannot help them against Allaah's punishment.

n00070.summary: Ali reports a meal the Prophet gave for the family of Abdul Muttalib, where he asked who would settle his debts and become his successor, and Ali volunteered.

n00071.summary: Ali reports a third meal for the Banu Haashim, where the Prophet repeated his request for someone to settle his debts; Ali accepted while Abbaas stayed silent.

n00072.summary: Sa'd Aslami guides the Prophet through the Rakoobah valley, where two thieves of Aslam accept Islaam, and the Prophet tells them to join him in Madinah.

n00073.summary: A villager on a journey is invited to Islaam, and the Prophet calls a tree to bear witness to his message before the villager says he will come to him.

n00074.summary: Buraydah bin Khusayb and about eighty families accept Islaam at Ghameem during the hijrah, and the Prophet leads them in the Isha salaah.

n00075.summary: After Abu Taalib's death the Prophet walks to Taa'if to invite its people, is rejected, and on the return journey makes a du'aa under a tree.

n00076.summary: Ibn Abbaas and Abdur Rahmaan bin Aa'idh report that the Prophet never fought a nation before inviting it to Islaam, and he told his battalions to win people's confidence first.

n00077.summary: Buraydah reports the Prophet's instructions to his commanders: invite enemies to Islaam, then to migrate, then to pay jizya, and fight only if they refuse all three.

n00078.summary: Anas bin Maalik and Ibn Raahway report that the Prophet sent Ali out with the order not to fight an enemy until he had invited them to Islaam.

n00079.summary: Ali reports the Prophet's instruction never to fight a nation before inviting them to Islaam, and his saying that guiding one person is better than red camels.

n00080.summary: Farwa Ghutayfi asks to fight those of his people who refused Islaam, and the Prophet tells him to invite them first and not to be hasty with those who refuse.

n00081.summary: Farwa Ghutayfi asks again about fighting and is told to invite before fighting, and then asks about Saba, which the Prophet explains is a man with ten sons.

n00082.summary: The Prophet tells Khaalid bin Sa'eed, sent to Yemen, to leave a nation alone if he hears the adhaan there, and to invite it to Islaam if he does not.

n00083.summary: Captives from Laat and Uzza are freed because their captors never invited them to Islaam, and the Prophet recites Qur'aan verses on his mission as a warner.

n00084.summary: A battalion that attacked an Arab tribe near Laat and Uzza without inviting it to Islaam is told by the Prophet to free the captives and invite them first.

n00085.summary: The Ansaar accept Islaam and ask for a teacher, so the Prophet sends Mus'ab bin Umayr to Madinah, where he teaches and most homes come to Islaam.

n00086.summary: Abu Umaamah is sent to his Baahilah tribe, is refused water after they reject him, and after a dream of a drink the whole tribe accepts Islaam.

n00087.summary: Ahnaf bin Qais, who once dismissed a man's invitation to Islaam, was reminded of it later and of the Prophet's prayer for his forgiveness, which he valued above his good deeds.

n00088.summary: The Prophet sent a Companion to a powerful Jahiliyyah leader who mocked the message, and the leader was struck by lightning, after which a verse of Surah Ra'd was revealed.

n00089.summary: A Bazzaar report says the leader was a tyrant, worse than Fir'oun, and was killed by lightning while still being invited to Islaam, followed by editorial cross-references to Khaalid bin Sa'eed and Amr bin Murra.

n00090.summary: The Prophet sent Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf with a group to Dowmatul Jandal, where the Christian chief Asbagh bin Amr Kalbi accepted Islaam, and the Prophet then directed Abdur Rahmaan to marry Asbagh's daughter.

n00091.summary: The Prophet sent Amr bin Al Aas to the Banu Baliy to call the Arabs to Islaam, and when he sensed danger at Salaasil he asked for reinforcements, so a battalion under Abu Ubaydah was sent.

n00092.summary: Baraa bin Aazib recounts the Yemen mission under Khaalid bin Waleed, which won no one until Ali was sent to relieve him, after which the whole Hamdaan tribe accepted Islaam and the Prophet prayed peace upon them.

n00093.summary: Ibn Is'haaq reports that the Prophet sent Khaalid bin Waleed to Najraan to invite the Banu Haarith bin Ka'b for three days before fighting, and they all accepted Islaam; the report breaks off at the start of Khaalid's letter.

n00094.summary: Khaalid bin Waleed writes to the Prophet to report that the Banu Haarith bin Ka'b accepted Islaam without a fight and that he is teaching them the injunctions of Islaam.

n00095.summary: The Prophet replies to Khaalid, welcoming the Banu Haarith's acceptance of Islaam, telling him to give them good news of Jannah and warn them against Jahannam, and asking him to return with a delegation.

n00096.summary: The Banu Haarith delegation comes to Madinah; the Prophet praises their acceptance, Yazeed bin Abdil Madaan answers for them, and the Prophet appoints Qais bin Husayn as their leader.

n00097.summary: Jareer bin Abdillaah comes to accept Islaam, the Prophet teaches him the Shahaadah, Imaan, salaah and zakaah, and the Prophet honours him, always smiling when he saw him.

n00098.summary: The Prophet instructs Mu'aadh bin Jabal before he goes to Yemen: first invite the People of the Book to Tawheed and the Prophethood, then salaah and zakaah, and avoid taking their best wealth.

n00099.summary: Howshab Dhi Dhulaym relates that Abd Sharr came with a letter and forty horsemen, pledged to the Prophet on salaah, zakaah and enjoining good, was renamed Abd Khayr, and that Howshab then also accepted Imaan.

n00100.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas relates that the Prophet welcomed the Abd Qais delegation and commanded them to believe in Allaah, pray, pay zakaah, fast in Ramadhaan and pay one third of the spoils, and forbade four kinds of drinking vessels.

n00101.summary: Alqama describes how he and six others came to the Prophet and listed the attributes of their Imaan, and the entry then runs into a second report about the Prophet sending Companions to distant kings and rulers.

n00102.summary: Anas reports that shortly before his death the Prophet sent letters to the emperors of Persia and Rome and to every oppressive ruler, inviting them to Allaah.

n00104.summary: The Prophet writes to Najaashi, King of Abyssinia, inviting him to Islaam and affirming Isa's true status, and sends his cousin Ja'far and the Muslims in Abyssinia with Amr bin Umayyah Dhamri as the letter's bearer.

n00105.summary: Najaashi As'ham replies to the Prophet, affirming Isa as he was described, testifying that Muhammad is the true Rasul, saying he accepted Islaam at Ja'far's hands, sending his son Areeha, and offering to come in person.

n00106.summary: Dihya Kalbi delivers the Prophet's letter to Heraclius, who consults his high priest and Abu Sufyaan, recognises the signs of prophethood but refuses to give up his kingship, and the high priest is later killed after publicly testifying to Islaam.

n00107.summary: Abu Sufyaan recounts being questioned by Heraclius at Ilyia about the Prophet's lineage, followers and treaties, whose answers Heraclius took as signs of prophethood, and then the court's reaction to the Prophet's letter.

n00109.summary: Abdur Rahmaan bin Abd Qaari and Abu Salam report that Shujaa bin Wahab delivered the Prophet's letter to Kisra, who tore it; Kisra then ordered Baadhaan to bring the Prophet to him, the Prophet foretold Kisra's death, and Baadhaan accepted Islaam after Sherway killed Kisra.

n00110.summary: Zaid bin Abi Habeeb reports the letter Abdullah bin Hudhaafa carried to Kisra, which Kisra tore up, and the Prophet's reply to two envoys with shaven beards that his Rabb had commanded him to grow his own beard.

n00111.summary: Abu Bakrah reports that Kisra ordered Baadaam, his governor over Yemen, to stop the Prophet, and that the Prophet told Baadaam's envoy his Rabb had killed Kisra and Caesar, which the envoy found had come true.

n00112.summary: Dihya Kalbi reports the letter to Caesar, then the envoys of the San'aa governor, who were told that the Prophet's Rabb had killed Kisra that very night, which was later confirmed.

n00113.summary: Abdullah bin Abd Qaari reports that Haatib bin Abi Balta'ah took the Prophet's letter to Maqoqis of Alexandria, who received him well and sent gifts, including the slave woman Maariya, mother of Ibraheem, and another woman given to Muhammad bin Qais Abdi.

n00114.summary: Haatib bin Abi Balta'ah narrates his debate with Maqoqis over the Prophet's status and why he did not curse his people, after which Maqoqis sent gifts, including a slave woman who became the mother of Ibraheem, and the Prophet gave another woman to Hassaan bin Thaabit.

n00115.summary: The grandfather of Abd Yasoo reports the Prophet's letter to the people of Najraan and the mubaahala challenge, which they declined in favour of a treaty; the Prophet then wrote a letter guaranteeing the protection of their priests and property.

n00117.summary: Marthad bin Dhabiyaan reports that a letter from the Prophet was read out to the Bakr bin Waa'il tribe, calling them to accept Islaam and live in peace.

n00118.summary: Ma'bad Judhaami reports that the Prophet wrote a letter to Rifaa'ah bin Zaid Judhaami to invite his people to Allaah and His Rasool, and that they all accepted Imaan when he reached them.

n00119.summary: Abdullaah bin Salaam reports how the Jewish rabbi Zaid bin Su'na tested the Prophet's patience and was rebuked by Umar, then accepted Islaam and vowed to give half his wealth as charity to part of the Ummah.

n00120.summary: Miswar bin Makhrama reports that on the way to Hudaybiyyah, the Prophet's camel Qaswa halted, the Prophet declared he would grant the Kuffaar any request that respects what Allaah has made sacred, and water gushed from a spring after he had an arrow placed in it.

n00121.summary: Budayl bin Warqa warns the Prophet that the Quraysh's tribes are ready to fight, the Prophet says he came only for Umrah and offers a treaty, and Budayl relays this to the Quraysh.

n00122.summary: Urwa bin Mas'ood addresses the Quraysh and then negotiates with the Prophet, but Abu Bakr rebukes him and Mughiera bin Shu'ba strikes his hand from the Prophet's beard, and Urwa returns to say the Sahabah honour the Prophet more than any ruler's followers.

n00123.summary: A man of the Kinaana tribe, then Mikraz bin Hafs, go to the Prophet, and Mikraz begins negotiating before the report breaks off at the arrival of a man named only 'bin Amr'.

n00125.summary: Abu Jandal arrives in chains and Suhayl insists on his return under the treaty; Umar and Abu Bakr reassure each other that the Prophet will reach the Kabah, the Prophet's companions follow his example of sacrifice, and verses on women migrants are revealed, after which Umar divorces two wives who remained mushrik.

n00126.summary: Abu Baseer is handed back to two men sent under the treaty, kills one of them on the road, and after the Prophet's remark that he was a warmonger, he leaves Madinah for the coast.

n00127.summary: Abu Jandal escapes from the Quraysh and joins Abu Baseer, and their growing group attacks Quraysh caravans until the Quraysh ask the Prophet to call them to Madinah, after which verses of Surah Fath (24-26) are revealed.

n00128.summary: During the stay at Hudaybiyyah, Umar suggests and Rasulullaah ﷺ sends Uthmaan to Makkah with a message of peace; Uthmaan gives the Quraysh da'wah and is guaranteed safe passage.

n00129.summary: Umar says Rasulullaah ﷺ made concessions in the treaty of Hudaybiyyah and that he would have obeyed any Ameer who acted as the Prophet did.

n00130.summary: Abu Bakr says Hudaybiyyah was the greatest victory in Islaam, and recounts how Suhayl bin Amr, who had refused the title Rasool at the treaty, later honoured the Prophet at the Farewell Hajj and was guided to Islaam.

n00131.summary: Amr bin Al Aas plots against the Prophet's envoys, then goes to Najaashi and accepts Islaam; he travels with Khaalid bin Waleed and Uthmaan bin Talha to Madinah and pledges allegiance to the Prophet.

n00132.summary: Khaalid bin Waleed recounts how he came to Islaam after the treaty of Hudaybiyyah, after reading his brother Waleed's letter, dreaming, and meeting Safwaan, Ikrama, Uthmaan bin Talha and Amr bin Al Aas on the way to Madinah, where the Prophet prayed for his forgiveness.

n00133.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ left Madinah for Makkah on the tenth of Ramadhaan with ten thousand Sahabah, appointing Abu Ruhm Kulthoom as Ameer of Madinah, and camped at Marruz Zahraan.

n00134.summary: Abu Sufyaan, Hakeem bin Hizaam and Budayl set out to spy on the Muslims; Abu Sufyaan bin Haarith and Abdullaah bin Abi Umayyah, the Prophet's cousins, are admitted after Umm Salma interceded and both accept Islaam.

n00135.summary: Abbaas tells the Quraysh that they are doomed unless they seek amnesty before the Muslims enter Makkah by force, and rides the Prophet's white mule out to find someone to warn them.

n00136.summary: Abbaas meets Abu Sufyaan by night and brings him to the Prophet on the mule; Umar protests, and the Prophet grants Abu Sufyaan safe passage through Abbaas.

n00137.summary: Abu Sufyaan testifies to Tawheed and then to the Prophet's Risaalah after Abbaas urges him to accept Islaam before he is executed.

n00138.summary: Abbaas asks for honour to be given to Abu Sufyaan, the Prophet grants safety to whoever enters Abu Sufyaan's house, locks his door or enters the Masjid, and Abu Sufyaan warns Makkah as the tribes pass by.

n00139.summary: As the Muslims enter Makkah, Abu Sufyaan watches the tribal battalions pass with Abbaas, including those led by Khaalid, Zubayr, Abu Dharr and Sa'd bin Ubaadah, and the Prophet has Sa'd's flag handed to his son Qais.

n00140.summary: Abu Layla reports that Abu Sufyaan was captured by the Sahabah at Araak and brought to the Prophet, who offers him Islaam and safety, and Abu Sufyaan remarks on the greatness of the Prophet's kingdom as the Ansaar pass by.

n00141.summary: Urwa reports that Abu Sufyaan and Hakeem bin Hizaam were captured on their way to the Prophet, that Abbaas protected Abu Sufyaan, who accepted Islaam, and that the Prophet sent Abbaas to announce amnesty for Makkah while Hind attacked her husband.

n00142.summary: Suhayl bin Amr locks his house at the conquest, his son secures amnesty for him, the Prophet ﷺ praises him, and Suhayl later accepts Islaam at Ji'irraanah and is given a hundred camels.

n00143.summary: Umar reports that the Prophet ﷺ, after the conquest, compared his own treatment of the Quraysh with Yusuf and his brothers and pardoned Safwaan, Abu Sufyaan and Haarith, and Umar was embarrassed at his own eagerness for revenge.

n00144.summary: Ibn Abi Husayn and Abu Hurayrah report the Prophet ﷺ at the door of the Kabah pardoning the Quraysh with Yusuf's words, after which the people accept Islaam, and a version from Bayhaqi is added.

n00145.summary: Ummu Hakeem accepts Islaam on the day of the conquest and secures amnesty for her husband Ikrama, who had fled to Yemen; she follows him to bring him back, and Ikrama kills the Roman slave who had tried to seduce her.

n00146.summary: Ikrama comes to the Prophet ﷺ as a Muhaajir, is granted amnesty and wife, and accepts Islaam by testifying to the kalimah after the Prophet ﷺ tells the Sahabah not to curse his dead father.

n00147.summary: Ikrama asks the Prophet ﷺ to pray for forgiveness for his past enmity and vows to spend double and fight double in the path of Allaah, while Suhayl bin Amr mocks his past opposition at Hunayn.

n00148.summary: Abdullaah bin Zubayr and Urwa bin Zubayr each give a shorter account of Ikrama's acceptance of Islaam, the Prophet's du'aa for his forgiveness, and Ikrama's vow to spend and fight double in the path of Allaah.

n00149.summary: Ikrama is martyred in the Battle of Ajnaadeen during Abu Bakr's caliphate, having been appointed by the Prophet ﷺ to collect the zakaah of Hawaazin in the year of the farewell Hajj.

n00150.summary: Safwaan bin Umayyah flees Makkah; his wife Baghoom accepts Islaam, and Umayr bin Wahab goes to Safwaan to tell him that the Prophet ﷺ has granted him amnesty.

n00151.summary: Safwaan asks for a sign of the amnesty, Umayr brings the Prophet's turban, and after the Prophet grants him a four-month grace period Safwaan returns and dismounts to meet him.

n00152.summary: Safwaan lends a hundred coats of armour for the Battle of Hunayn, and when the Prophet ﷺ gives him a valley of camels and shepherds at Ji'irraanah, Safwaan accepts Islaam on the spot.

n00153.summary: Another narration of Safwaan's loan of armour: some of the coats are destroyed, the Prophet offers to pay for the damage, and Safwaan declines compensation because he wants to accept Islaam.

n00154.summary: Mundhir bin Jahm reports that Huwaytib, terrified after the conquest, is persuaded by Abu Dharr to come to the Prophet ﷺ and accepts Islaam, and the Prophet ﷺ then grants him a loan and a share of the Hunayn booty.

n00155.summary: Abdullaah bin Ikrama reports that Ummu Haani granted protection to Haarith bin Hishaam and Abdullaah bin Abi Rabee'ah, that Ali tried to attack them and was stopped, that the Prophet ﷺ upheld her protection, and that Haarith then accepted Islaam.

n00156.summary: Nudhayr bin Haarith, one of the most learned of the Quraysh, is made steadfast by the Prophet's du'aa, accepts Islaam, and then receives a gift of a hundred camels from the Prophet ﷺ which he shares with a man of the Banu Duwal.

n00157.summary: Urwa bin Mas'ood follows the Prophet ﷺ after he leaves Thaqeef, accepts Islaam, and asks to go back to his people, despite the Prophet warning that they would kill him.

n00158.summary: Urwa bin Mas'ood invites his people to Islaam from his house balcony, is struck by arrows and martyred, and the Prophet ﷺ compares his example among his people to the man in Surah Yaaseen.

n00159.summary: The Thaqeef send a delegation to the Prophet ﷺ, Mughiera bin Shu'ba meets them, and their conditions are negotiated, including the Prophet refusing to exempt them from salaah, while Abu Sufyaan and Mughiera are sent to destroy their idol.

n00160.summary: Wahab asks Jaabir about the Thaqeef's conditions, and Jaabir says the Prophet ﷺ accepted them while predicting that they would later pay zakaah and wage jihaad without being told.

n00161.summary: Aws bin Hudhayfa, who came with the Banu Maalik delegates, describes the Prophet ﷺ addressing them standing each night after Isha, and explains once that he came late because he had not finished his daily Qur'aan recitation.

n00162.summary: Ibn Ishaaq reports that Abu Bakr gave da'wah to the people who confided in him, and that Zubayr, Uthmaan, Talha, Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas and Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf accepted Islaam through him and then met the Prophet ﷺ.

n00163.summary: Asbaq, a Christian slave of Umar, is invited to Islaam and is freed on Umar's deathbed; Aslam reports Umar inviting an old Christian woman to Islaam after making wudhu with her water.

n00165.summary: As'ad bin Zuraarah brings Mus'ab bin Umayr to the Banu Abdil Ash'hal, Usayd bin Hudhayr is sent to confront them, and Usayd listens, accepts Islaam and sends Sa'd bin Mu'aadh to them.

n00166.summary: Mus'ab gives da'wah to Sa'd bin Mu'aadh, who first reproaches As'ad, then listens to the Qur'aan recited by Mus'ab, and accepts Islaam after bathing, cleansing his clothes and praying two rakaahs.

n00167.summary: Sa'd bin Mu'aadh tells the Banu Abdil Ash'hal that he will not speak to them until they believe, and the whole clan accepts Islaam by evening, after which Mus'ab continues his da'wah among the Ansaar.

n00168.summary: Tulayb bin Umayr accepts Islaam in the house of Arqam and persuades his mother Arwa bint Abdil Muttalib, who testifies to the kalimah and keeps encouraging him to support the Prophet ﷺ.

n00169.summary: Umayr bin Wahab sets out to kill the Prophet with a poisoned sword after plotting with Safwaan bin Umayyah, and Umar sees him at the Masjid and raises the alarm.

n00170.summary: Umar drags Umayr bin Wahab to the Prophet, who reveals the secret plot and then forgives him.

n00171.summary: Umayr bin Wahab accepts Islaam, asks leave to go to Makkah to call people to it, and Safwaan bin Umayyah swears never to speak to him again.

n00172.summary: Umayr bin Wahab invites people to Islaam in Makkah, and a large number accept at his hands.

n00173.summary: Umar says he now loves Umayr more than some of his own children, and Umayr confronts Safwaan in the Hateem, who stays silent.

n00175.summary: Abu Hurayrah invites his mother to Islaam, the Prophet prays for her guidance, and she accepts Islaam.

n00176.summary: Ummu Sulaym makes Islaam the condition for marrying Abu Talha, who accepts Islaam, and Anas bin Maalik performs the nikaah.

n00177.summary: Dimaam bin Tha'laba comes to Madinah as the representative of Banu Sa'd bin Bakr, questions the Prophet about the basics of Islaam, and accepts it.

n00178.summary: Dimaam bin Tha'laba returns to his tribe, rejects the idols, and the people present with him accept Islaam by that evening.

n00179.summary: Amr bin Murrah Juhani dreams in Makkah of a light and voices announcing the sealing of the Prophets and the destruction of idols, and tells his people.

n00180.summary: Amr bin Murrah Juhani accepts Islaam from the Prophet, is sent back to call his tribe, and a man among them answers with verses of abuse, and Amr's curse on him is fulfilled.

n00181.summary: Amr bin Murrah Juhani brings the members of his tribe who accepted Islaam to the Prophet, who welcomes them and has a letter of terms written, which Qais bin Shammaas scribes.

n00182.summary: Urwa bin Mas'ood, newly Muslim, asks the Prophet's leave to return to his people of Thaqeef to call them to Islaam, and they kill him.

n00183.summary: Mortally wounded by an arrow, Urwa bin Mas'ood forbids his people to take revenge for him, welcomes martyrdom and asks to be buried with the martyred Sahabah.

n00184.summary: The Quraysh warn Tufayl bin Amr Dowsi against the Prophet, and he resolves not to listen to him and stops his ears with wool.

n00185.summary: Tufayl bin Amr Dowsi hears the Prophet recite at the Ka'bah, follows him home, and accepts Islaam after the Qur'aan is recited to him.

n00186.summary: Tufayl bin Amr Dowsi's prayer moves a light from between his eyes to the top of his whip, and it serves as a sign to his people as he approaches them.

n00187.summary: Tufayl bin Amr Dowsi invites his father and his wife to Islaam, and both accept, while the rest of his tribe is slow to respond.

n00188.summary: Tufayl bin Amr Dowsi asks the Prophet to curse the Dows tribe, but the Prophet prays for their guidance, and Tufayl later brings them to Madinah.

n00189.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas recounts Tufayl bin Amr Dowsi's Islaam, and adds that the Prophet sent him to burn an idol before he was martyred at Yamaamah.

n00190.summary: Another account of Tufayl bin Amr Dowsi's Islaam, then of Jundub bin Amr and seventy-five Dows accepting Islaam at the Prophet's hand.

n00191.summary: During Abu Bakr's caliphate, Hishaam bin Al Aas Umawi and companions go to Jabala bin Ayham in Damascus with the invitation to Islaam, and predict the conquest of his kingdom.

n00193.summary: Bujayr bin Zuhayr accepts Islaam and writes to his brother Ka'b bin Zuhayr, who, after the Prophet orders his execution, comes to Madinah and accepts Islaam.

n00194.summary: Ka'b bin Zuhayr recites his poem Baanat Su'aad in the Prophet's Masjid, the Prophet signals the Sahabah to listen, and Bujayr's letter urging Ka'b to Islaam is also quoted.

n00195.summary: Khaalid bin Waleed writes to the Persian leadership, Rustam and Mahraan, inviting them to Islaam and offering the Jizya as the alternative to war.

n00196.summary: Khaalid bin Waleed's letter to the Persian leadership at Madaa'in, offering Islaam, the Jizya or war, is read to Sha'bi and alarms the Persians in 12 AH.

n00197.summary: Khaalid bin Waleed sends letters to the Persian commander Hurmuz and to the Persian royal family, offering Islaam, protection for the Jizya or war, and two envoys carry them.

n00198.summary: Haarith bin Muslim Tameemi gets a town to say Laa Ilaaha Illallaah, and the Prophet rewards him with a sealed letter that Abu Bakr, Umar and Uthmaan each honour.

n00199.summary: Ka'b bin Umayr Ghifaari is sent with fifteen men to invite people at Dhaat Itlaa in Shaam, and after they are refused, all but one are martyred.

n00200.summary: Ibn Abil Awjaa Sulami invites a large enemy force to Islaam, which they refuse, and most of his fifty men are martyred before the survivors return to Madinah.

n00201.summary: When Abu Bakr sends armies to Shaam, he walks with the commanders to see them off and gives them instructions to invite the enemy to Islaam, then to the Jizya, before fighting, and forbids harming women, children and the monks.

n00202.summary: Abu Bakr instructs Khaalid bin Waleed, sent against the apostates, to invite them back to Islaam, to accept any who return, and to fight only those who refuse.

n00203.summary: Khaalid bin Waleed invites the nobles of Heera, led by Qabeesa and Haani, to Islaam, and when they refuse war they agree to pay seventy thousand Dirhams as Jizya.

n00204.summary: Before the Battle of Yarmook, Abu Ubaydah and four other Sahabah go to meet Tadhaaruk, Heraclius' brother, and invite him to Islaam, but the treaty does not materialise and the battle is fought.

n00205.summary: During the Battle of Yarmook, the Roman commander Jarja asks to meet Khaalid bin Waleed and questions him about the Prophet and the sword he was given.

n00206.summary: Khaalid explains that the Prophet called him a sword of Allaah and that the Muslims call people to testify that there is none worthy of worship but Allaah and that Muhammad is His servant and Rasul, and Jarja asks what they call people to.

n00207.summary: Khaalid answers Jarja on the Jizya, the equal standing of all believers and the reward of later converts, then Jarja accepts Islaam, prays two rakaahs and dies of wounds in the battle that day.

n00208.summary: Khaalid urges the Muslims to leave Arabia for the fertile lands of the non-Arabs and fight for them, even apart from the obligation of jihaad and da'wah.

n00210.summary: Salmaan Faarsi invited the Persians of a besieged fortress to Islaam for three days before his army attacked.

n00211.summary: Salmaan Faarsi was appointed to invite the people of Bahursher and Qasrul Abyadh to Islaam, giving each three days, as Atiyya reports.

n00213.summary: Mughiera bin Shu'ba explained Islaam to Rustam, the Persian commander, before the Battle of Qaadisiyyah, and Rustam asked questions about it.

n00214.summary: Rib'ee bin Aamir, sent by Sa'd, invited Rustam to Islaam in his court and refused his request for more than three days to decide.

n00215.summary: On the second and third days Hudhayfa bin Mihsin and Mughiera bin Shu'ba presented Islaam to Rustam, who answered with a parable and threatened to kill them all.

n00216.summary: Before the Battle of Qaadisiyyah Mughiera bin Shu'ba went to Rustam, mocked the Persians' taunts, and presented Islaam and Jizya, and the Muslims then defeated the Persians at the river crossing.

n00217.summary: Mughiera bin Shu'ba was sent to the Persian leader before Qaadisiyyah and told him the Muslims had come to call to Islaam and to fight, not for food.

n00218.summary: Sa'd's envoys, led by Nu'maan bin Muqarrin and Mughiera bin Shu'ba, invited the Persian king Yazdajird to Islaam before the battle, and Mughiera answered his threats.

n00219.summary: Abdullaah bin Mu'tam invited the Arab tribes of Taghlib, Iyaad and Namir to testify to the Kalimah and accept what the Prophet brought, and they accepted Islaam.

n00220.summary: Amr bin Al Aas offered the Egyptian priests Islaam or Jizya before the battle for Egypt, and after a night attack the Egyptians came out to negotiate at Aynush Shams.

n00221.summary: Umar appointed Salama bin Qais Ash'jaee as commander of a regiment and told him to offer the enemy Islaam, then Jizya, and only then fight.

n00222.summary: Abu Moosa Ash'ari invited the people of Isfahan to Islaam and then offered Jizya, but they broke the night's agreement and attacked, and the Muslims were given victory.

n00223.summary: Amr bin Jamooh, who kept an idol, was won over when the young Muslims of Banu Salma repeatedly disgraced it, and he then accepted Islaam.

n00224.summary: Amr bin Jamooh's son recited the opening verses of the Qur'aan to his father, who consulted his idol, broke it, and accepted Islaam.

n00225.summary: Abdullaah bin Rawwaaha smashed Abu Dardaa's idol, and Abu Dardaa, seeing that it could not defend itself, went to the Prophet and accepted Islaam.

n00226.summary: Umar's letter to Amr bin Al Aas set the terms for Alexandria's Jizya and for the prisoners, who were to be offered Islaam or their own religion.

n00227.summary: After the prisoners of Alexandria were each offered Islaam or Christianity, Abdullaah bin Abdur Rahmaan, known as Abu Maryam, accepted Islaam despite his family's opposition.

n00228.summary: Ali's armour was found with a Christian, and when the judge Shuray ruled that Ali needed proof, the Christian accepted Islaam and Ali gave him the armour.

n00229.summary: Ali's armour was found with a Jew, the judge Shuray refused Ali's son Hasan's testimony, and the Jew, persuaded by Ali's honesty, accepted Islaam and was given the armour with money.

n00230.summary: Jareer reports the conditions the male Sahabah pledged to the Prophet, which matched those the women pledged, with the promise of Jannah for keeping them.

n00231.summary: Aswad saw people pledge to Islaam and the Shahaadah on the day of the Conquest of Makkah, and his teacher explained what the Shahaadah required.

n00232.summary: Bayhaqi reports that people of every age and both sexes pledged to Islaam and the Shahaadah at the Prophet's hands.

n00233.summary: Mujaashi bin Mas'ood asked to pledge to Hijrah after the conquest, and the Prophet instead took his pledge to Islaam and Jihaad, since Hijrah had ended.

n00234.summary: After Mughiera bin Shu'ba died, Jareer bin Abdillaah urged the people to fear Allaah and wish well for every Muslim, and Ziyaad bin Haarith Sudaa'ee's pledge to Islaam is also recorded.

n00235.summary: Basheer bin Khasaasiyah asked, when pledging, to keep the conditions only as far as he was able, and this concession was allowed for everyone after him.

n00236.summary: Jareer bin Abdullaah pledged to the Prophet to establish salaah, pay zakaah and wish well for every Muslim.

n00237.summary: Jareer asked the Prophet to state the conditions of the pledge, and he set out worship of Allaah alone, salaah, zakaah, wishing well for Muslims and rejecting shirk.

n00238.summary: When Jareer came to pledge, the Prophet asked him to commit to surrendering to Allaah and wishing well for every Muslim, and Jareer accepted as far as he was able.

n00239.summary: Awf bin Maalik Ash'ja'ee and his companions pledged to worship Allaah alone, pray the five salaahs and never ask anyone for anything.

n00240.summary: Thowbaan pledged to the Prophet never to ask anyone for anything, and Abu Umaamah reports him dismounting to pick up his own fallen whip, as Abu Bakr also did.

n00241.summary: Abu Dharr reports the pledges he gave the Prophet: to fear no critic for Allaah's sake, never to ask anyone for anything, and never to accept a trust.

n00242.summary: Sahl bin Sa'd reports that Abu Dharr, Ubaadah bin Saamit, Abu Sa'eed Khudri, Muhammad bin Maslama and a sixth Sahabi pledged never to be swayed by critics in Allaah's cause, and the Prophet released the sixth when he asked.

n00243.summary: Ubaadah bin Saamit reports the pledge taken from Madinah's leaders: no shirk, theft, fornication, unlawful killing, plunder or disobedience, with Jannah promised for keeping it.

n00244.summary: Ubaadah bin Saamit relays the Prophet's pledge against shirk, theft and fornication, and says that a sinner's fate is then left to Allaah's forgiveness or punishment.

n00246.summary: Ya'la bin Munyah asked to pledge his father to Hijrah after the conquest of Makkah, and the Prophet instead took a pledge of Jihaad because Hijrah had ended.

n00247.summary: During the Battle of Khandaq the Prophet declined a Hijrah pledge from outside Madinah and praised the Ansaar, saying whoever loves them will be loved by Allaah.

n00248.summary: Jaabir describes how the Prophet sought asylum at the Hajj markets, how the Ansaar of Yathrib offered it, and how seventy of them pledged at Aqaba to protect him.

n00250.summary: Ka'b bin Maalik reports that the Prophet asked the Ansaar for twelve leaders to head their people, and they chose nine from Khazraj and three from Aws.

n00251.summary: Urwa reports that Abul Haytham bin Tayyihaan was among the first to pledge, and after asking whether his people would help the Prophet, they all followed him.

n00252.summary: Abbaas bin Ubaadah warned the Ansaar of the cost of the pledge before they took it for Jannah, and when he offered to attack Mina the Prophet said he had not been commanded to fight.

n00253.summary: Before the Battle of Ahzaab the Prophet ﷺ prayed for the Muhaajireen and Ansaar digging the trench in cold and hunger, and they pledged to wage jihaad as long as they lived; similar pledges by Basheer, Ya'la and Mujaashi are cited.

n00254.summary: After pledging allegiance under a tree, Salama bin Akwa was asked by the Prophet ﷺ to pledge again, and the pledge he gave was to death.

n00255.summary: During the Battle of Harra, Abdullaah bin Zaid said that no one may pledge to die after the demise of the Prophet ﷺ, when people were pledging to die against Ibn Handhala.

n00256.summary: Ubaadah bin Saamit, having torn open a shipment of wine, recounted the terms of his pledge to the Prophet ﷺ: to listen and obey, to spend in hardship and ease, to speak the truth and to protect the Prophet ﷺ, in exchange for Jannah. A second version of his words follows.

n00257.summary: Jareer bin Abdillaah pledged to listen, obey and wish well for all Muslims; the Prophet ﷺ told him to pledge only to the best of his ability. Jareer's custom in trade of letting the other party decide is also recorded.

n00258.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports that when the Sahabah pledged to listen and obey, the Prophet ﷺ told them to add the clause 'to the best of my ability'.

n00259.summary: Utba bin Abd narrates that he pledged allegiance to the Prophet ﷺ seven times, five of them pledges of obedience and two of love.

n00260.summary: Anas says that with his own hands he pledged allegiance to the Prophet ﷺ to listen and obey to the best of his ability.

n00261.summary: Ummu Atiyya relates how the Prophet ﷺ sent Umar to the women of the Ansaar and took their pledge not to associate partners with Allaah, steal, commit adultery, kill their children, slander or disobey him in good. Umar then gave instructions on the Eid salaah, funerals and Jumu'ah for women.

n00262.summary: Salma bint Qais, the Prophet's maternal aunt, pledged with the Ansaar women. Uqayla bint Ateeq and Umaymah bint Ruqayqah each give their own pledges, and the Prophet ﷺ says his pledge to women is confirmed by speech, not by handshake.

n00264.summary: Abdullaah bin Amr relates how Umayma bint Ruqayqa came to pledge to Islaam, and the Prophet ﷺ set out the clauses: no shirk, theft, adultery, killing children, slander, wailing, or display like the women of the Period of Ignorance.

n00265.summary: Aa'isha relates that Faatima bint Utba came to pledge; the Prophet ﷺ asked her to pledge the clauses of the Qur'aanic verse, and she accepted after Aa'isha confirmed that all the women had agreed to them.

n00266.summary: Azza bint Khaabil pledged not to commit adultery, steal or bury her children alive, and explains her understanding that burying them alive in secret means spoiling them.

n00267.summary: Faatima bint Utba and her sister Hind bint Utba come with Abu Hudhayfa to pledge. Hind is permitted by her husband Abu Sufyaan to take food from his house, and her gold bangles are described as coals of Jahannam if zakaah is not paid. The Prophet ﷺ says no one has true Imaan until he is more beloved to them than their children and parents.

n00269.summary: Further accounts of Hind bint Utba's pledge: she goes with Umar to the Prophet ﷺ after Abu Sufyaan's remark, and Abu Sufyaan pardons her past taking of his wealth. The Prophet ﷺ recognises her, takes her pledge and recites its clauses, including the prohibition of wailing.

n00271.summary: Muhammad bin Ali bin Husayn relates that the Prophet ﷺ accepted the pledge of Hasan, Husayn, Abdullaah bin Abbaas and Abdullaah bin Ja'far while they were still young boys, and accepted pledges from no other children except those of his household.

n00272.summary: Abdullaah bin Zubayr and Abdullaah bin Ja'far say they went to pledge to the Prophet ﷺ at the age of seven. He smiled, stretched out his hands and accepted their pledges.

n00273.summary: Hirmaas bin Ziyaad recounts that as a child he stretched out his hand to pledge to the Prophet ﷺ, but the pledge was not accepted from him.

n00274.summary: Muntashir relates the terms on which the Sahabah pledged to the Prophet ﷺ, and Abu Bakr's condition that they obey him only while he obeys Allaah. Ibn Afeef describes Abu Bakr taking pledges after the Prophet's demise, to obey Allaah, His Book and the Ameer.

n00276.summary: Abu Safar relates that whenever Abu Bakr sent an army to Shaam he made the soldiers pledge to fight with spears if needed and to stay steadfast in a plague.

n00277.summary: Anas went to Madinah after Abu Bakr's death and asked Umar to let him pledge as he had to Abu Bakr. Umayr bin Atiyya and Abdullaah bin Ukaym also pledged to Umar, who said the pledge gives each side rights over the other.

n00279.summary: Saleem Abu Aamir relates that a delegation from Hamraa pledged to Uthmaan not to associate partners with Allaah, to establish salaah, pay zakaah, fast in Ramadhaan and give up the festivities of the fire-worshippers. Uthmaan accepted their pledge only after they agreed to all of these.

n00280.summary: Miswar bin Makhrama relates how the six Sahabah appointed by Umar consulted, and Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf took their choice. After private talks with Ali and Uthmaan he pledged to Uthmaan, and the Muhaajireen, Ansaar, army leaders and the public followed.

n00281.summary: Nufayr relates that Miqdaad bin Aswad rebuked a man who wished he had lived in the Prophet's time. He reminded him of the darkness before Islaam, of the Qur'aan separating truth from falsehood even between father and son, and of the hardships believers bore, citing Surah Furqaan 74.

n00282.summary: A man from Kufa asks Hudhayfa what life was like with the Prophet ﷺ. Hudhayfa describes the fear, hunger and bitter cold of the Battle of the Trench and tells him not to wish for such a time.

n00283.summary: Anas reports the Prophet ﷺ saying that he was harassed and threatened for Allaah's sake more than anyone, and that for thirty days and nights he and Bilaal had almost no food.

n00285.summary: Abu Taalib asks the Prophet to stop, and the Prophet refuses even if the sun and moon were placed in his hands; Jaabir then narrates how Utba bin Rabee'ah failed to bargain the Prophet off and was moved by his recitation of Surah Sajdah.

n00286.summary: Abdullaah bin Ja'far relates that after Abu Taalib died a foolish man of the Quraysh threw sand at the Prophet ﷺ. His daughter wiped it away and wept, and he told her that Allaah would protect her father. He also said the Quraysh had not dared harm him while Abu Taalib lived.

n00287.summary: Abu Hurayrah relates that after Abu Taalib died the Quraysh treated the Prophet ﷺ very harshly, and the Prophet ﷺ said he was quickly feeling his uncle's loss.

n00288.summary: Haarith bin Haarith recounts seeing the Prophet ﷺ calling people to Tawheed and Imaan and being harmed, until a girl, Zaynab, brought him water and a cloth. Muneeb Azdi describes the Prophet ﷺ calling people to La ilaaha illallaah while being abused, and the same girl bringing him water.

n00289.summary: Abul Aas describes the worst thing the mushrikeen did to the Prophet ﷺ: Uqba bin Abi Mu'eet throttled him with a cloth while he prayed at the Hateem, until Abu Bakr pushed Uqba away and recited Surah Mu'min 28.

n00290.summary: Amr bin Al Aas recounts the one time he saw the Quraysh try to kill the Prophet ﷺ: Uqba bin Abi Mu'eet throttled him while he prayed near the Maqaam of Ibraheem, and Abu Bakr rescued him. The Prophet ﷺ then warned the Quraysh that he had been sent to slaughter them, and Abu Jahal replied to him.

n00291.summary: Urwa bin Zubayr asks Abdullaah bin Amr about the worst Quraysh treatment of the Prophet ﷺ. Abdullaah describes their mockery and their final confrontation with the Prophet ﷺ, when Abu Bakr defended him. Asmaa bint Abi Bakr adds her own account of the attack and of her father being beaten.

n00292.summary: Anas relates that the mushrikeen beat the Prophet ﷺ until he was unconscious, and Abu Bakr protested that they were killing a man for saying Allaah is his Rabb. Another report says the attackers then turned on Abu Bakr.

n00293.summary: Ali asks the people who is most courageous and answers Abu Bakr: at Badr he stood guard by the Prophet ﷺ with a drawn sword, and when the Quraysh seized the Prophet ﷺ he alone defended him. Ali says a moment of Abu Bakr's life is better than the believer of Fir'oun's court, who hid his Imaan, since Abu Bakr made his Imaan public.

n00294.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood relates that Hamza, angered on learning what Abu Jahal had done to the Prophet ﷺ at the Ka'bah, struck Abu Jahal with his bow and then accepted Islaam. Muhammad bin Ka'b Qurazi gives a second version in which Hamza struck Abu Jahal's head with his bow near Safa and Marwa.

n00295.summary: Abu Jahal harassed the Prophet at Safa, and Hamza, angered on hearing of it, struck Abu Jahal with his bow in the Masjidul Haraam and then accepted Islaam, which strengthened the Muslims.

n00296.summary: Abbaas relates that Abu Jahal vowed to trample the Prophet ﷺ's neck if he saw him in sajdah. The Prophet ﷺ went to the Masjid in anger, recited Surah Alaq and prostrated, and Abu Jahal said the horizons had closed in on him.

n00297.summary: Barra bint Abi Tajra relates that Tulayb bin Umayr struck Abu Jahal's head when Abu Jahal harmed the Prophet ﷺ, and Abu Lahab stood up to defend Tulayb. Arwa, Tulayb's mother, called it his best day. Later Arwa accepted Islaam, and when Abu Lahab reproached her she told him to defend his nephew, the Prophet ﷺ.

n00298.summary: Qataada relates that Abu Lahab's sons Utayba and Utba divorced the Prophet ﷺ's daughters after Surah Lahab was revealed. Utayba rejected the Prophet ﷺ's religion, assaulted him, and was killed by a lion on a trade journey, as the Prophet ﷺ had said. Uthmaan later married Ummu Kulthoom.

n00299.summary: Rabee'ah bin Ubayd Deeli says the Prophet ﷺ's house lay between those of Abu Lahab and Uqba bin Abi Mu'eet, and filth and entrails were hung on his door. The Prophet ﷺ cleared them away with his bow and said the two were terrible neighbours.

n00300.summary: Aa'isha asks whether the Prophet ever had a harder day than Uhud, and he recounts the rejection at Taa'if, after which Addaas, a Christian slave of Utba and Shayba, recognised his words and honoured him.

n00302.summary: The people of Taa'if lined the road and stoned the Prophet until he bled, and he sheltered in the orchard of Utba and Shayba before returning to Makkah.

n00303.summary: Once safe from the Taa'if mob, the Prophet made a du'aa confessing his weakness and asking Allaah for protection from His anger.

n00304.summary: Utba and Shayba send grapes by their Christian slave Addaas, who recognises the Prophet's words, learns of Yunus from him, and kisses his head, hands and feet, and his masters rebuke him.

n00305.summary: Addaas says he testifies that the Prophet is Allaah's servant and messenger, and Aa'isha relays her father Abu Bakr's account of the climb to the cave of Thowr, when the Prophet's feet were bleeding.

n00306.summary: At Uhud the Prophet's canine tooth was broken and his head injured, and he asked how a nation could prosper after this; Maalik bin Sinaan then wiped and swallowed his blood.

n00307.summary: Aa'isha relays Abu Bakr's account of Uhud: Talha defended the Prophet, Abu Ubaydah pulled the helmet links from his face at the cost of two front teeth, and they then nursed Talha's many wounds.

n00308.summary: Abu Bakr openly preached at the Ka'bah and was beaten almost to death, his tribe carried him home, Ummul Khayr and Ummu Jameel tended him, and after the Prophet prayed for her, his mother accepted Islaam.

n00309.summary: Umar accepts Islaam after the Prophet's du'aa, openly declares it at the Ka'bah, and drives off anyone who tries to attack him, while Abu Jahal and the Quraysh look on.

n00310.summary: Aa'isha says her parents followed only Islaam, and Abu Bakr planned to emigrate to Abyssinia until Ibnud Daghina took him under protection on condition he worship at home; when he built a courtyard prayer place, the Quraysh asked Ibnud Daghina to withdraw the protection.

n00311.summary: In Ibn Is'haaq's version, Ibnud Daghina brings Abu Bakr back to Makkah under his protection, then withdraws it when Abu Bakr's public worship annoys the Quraysh, and Abu Bakr releases him from it.

n00312.summary: After Abu Bakr gave up Ibnud Daghina's protection, a Quraysh man threw dust on his head and he was beaten; Asmaa recalls her father's words as the mob turned on him.

n00313.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar describes his father Umar accepting Islaam and going to Jameel bin Ma'mar to announce it, after which the Quraysh mobbed Umar until an old man of Banu Adi sent them away; a second report gives Aas bin Waa'il's protection of Umar.

n00314.summary: Hakam bin Abil Aas bound his nephew Uthmaan in ropes after he accepted Islaam, and released him when he saw Uthmaan would not give up his new faith.

n00315.summary: Mas'ood bin Khiraash saw Talha bin Ubaydillaah, who had accepted Islaam, walking between Safa and Marwa with his arm in a sling while his mother Sa'ba cursed him.

n00316.summary: Talha recounts a monk at the Busra fair asking whether the Prophet Ahmad had appeared yet, which drove him back to Makkah, where he learned that Muhammad had appeared; the text breaks off there.

n00317.summary: Zubayr bin Awwaam accepted Islaam at eight years old, and his uncle hung him over smoke and urged him to return to kufr, which he refused.

n00318.summary: Hafs bin Khaalid reports an old man from Mosul who saw Zubayr's body covered in sword scars, each received alongside the Prophet in the path of Allaah.

n00319.summary: Zubayr told Ali bin Zaid that his chest bore scars shaped like eyes, made by arrows and spears.

n00320.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood names the first seven to make their Islaam public, and says that those without tribal protection were tortured, with Bilaal dragged through Makkah repeating 'Ahad! Ahad!'.

n00321.summary: Mujaahid reports that the other Muslims were left in steel armour under the sun, and Abu Jahal came at night with his spear to taunt and threaten them.

n00322.summary: Mujaahid reports that the Mushrikeen led Bilaal through the two mountains of Makkah with a rope around his neck.

n00323.summary: Urwa bin Zubayr reports that Umayyah tortured Bilaal on the sand until Abu Bakr bought and freed him, after Waraqa bin Naufal had promised to make the grave of Bilaal a place of blessing if he were killed.

n00324.summary: Umayyah threw Bilaal onto the burning sand with a heavy rock on his chest, demanding he reject Muhammad and worship Laat and Uzza, and Bilaal kept saying 'Ahad! Ahad!'; the item then introduces Ammaar reciting couplets about Abu Bakr's freeing of the slaves.

n00325.summary: Ammaar's verses praise Abu Bakr for freeing Bilaal, condemn Abu Jahal and Faakih for torturing him, and affirm Bilaal's stand on the Oneness of Allaah, citing the prophets Ibraheem, Yunus, Moosa and Isa.

n00326.summary: Jaabir reports the Prophet telling the family of Yaasir to be patient, as Jannah is their promised home, and Uthmaan reports the same scene while Ammaar and his parents were tortured in the sun, with the Prophet praying for their forgiveness.

n00328.summary: Abdullaah bin Ja'far reports the Prophet's words to the family of Yaasir, and Kalbi adds that Sumayya was killed when Abu Jahal thrust a spear into her, Yaasir died under torture, and Abdullaah bin Yaasir was shot dead by an arrow.

n00329.summary: Mujaahid states that Sumayya, the mother of Ammaar, was the first martyr in Islaam, killed when Abu Jahal thrust a spear into her.

n00330.summary: Ammaar, tortured until he spoke against the Prophet and praised the Mushrikeen's gods, tells the Prophet his heart still held Imaan, and the Prophet allows him to say it again if the torture recurs.

n00331.summary: Muhammad bin Ammaar reports the Prophet wiping Ammaar's tears and saying he may repeat the forced words, and Ameerul Mu'mineen bin Maymoon reports the Prophet's prayer over Ammaar while he was being burned, and the Prophet's word that rebels would kill him.

n00332.summary: Sha'bi reports that when Khabbaab came to Umar's gathering, Umar gave him the cushion of honour, saying only Bilaal deserved it more, and Khabbaab showed the back that had been burned.

n00333.summary: Sha'bi reports Umar asking Khabbaab about his torture, and Khabbaab shows his back and says only the fat on it put out the fire the Mushrikeen had lit under him.

n00334.summary: Abu Layla Kindi reports that Umar had Khabbaab brought to the front, calling Ammaar bin Yaasir the only man more deserving of that place, and Khabbaab showed him the scars left by the Mushrikeen.

n00335.summary: Khabbaab, a blacksmith, says Aas bin Waa'il refused to repay his debt unless he rejected Muhammad, and Khabbaab refused; the Qur'aan verses on Aas's claim to wealth and children in the Aakhirah are then quoted.

n00336.summary: Khabbaab asks the Prophet to pray for relief from the persecution, and the Prophet replies that earlier believers endured worse, and that Allaah will complete this Deen until a lone rider travels safely from Sa'aa to Hadramaut.

n00337.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas reports that Abu Dharr sent his brother to Makkah to find the man claiming to be a Rasul, and the brother returned describing good character and words that were not poetry, which did not satisfy Abu Dharr.

n00338.summary: Ali takes Abu Dharr home for three nights until he leads him to the Prophet, who tells him to return to his people; Abu Dharr then proclaims the testimony at the Masjidul Haraam, is beaten, and is shielded by Abbaas.

n00339.summary: In Muslim's account, Abu Dharr is stoned in Makkah after his brother's visit, hides near the Ka'bah for fifteen days, then meets the Prophet and Abu Bakr, and is the first to greet him with the greeting of Islaam.

n00340.summary: Abu Dharr declared his Islaam openly in the Masjidul Haraam, was beaten until he looked like a red idol, and was told by the Prophet to return to his people until he heard of victory.

n00341.summary: Qais reports that Sa'eed bin Zaid, speaking in the mosque of Kufa, recalled being tied with ropes by Umar after he accepted Islaam, and began the complete account.

n00342.summary: Sa'eed bin Zaid says that Umar bound him in ropes before Umar became a Muslim, because he had accepted Islaam.

n00343.summary: Anas reports that Umar set out to kill the Prophet, was turned back by the recitation of Surah Taa-Haa in his sister's and brother-in-law's house, and after reading it himself went to the Prophet, who prayed for him, and Umar accepted Islaam.

n00344.summary: Thowbaan reports the Prophet's du'aa for Umar; Umar beat his sister after hearing her recite Surah Alaq, then went to the Prophet's door, where Bilaal let him in, and he accepted Islaam when asked to testify.

n00345.summary: Umar recounts how, angered to hear that his sister had accepted Islaam, he struck her and then took the manuscript she was reading.

n00346.summary: Uthmaan bin Madh'oon gives up Waleed bin Mughiera's protection, then is slapped in the eye for disputing a poet's couplets with the Quraysh.

n00347.summary: A poem lamenting those who struck Uthmaan bin Madh'oon and warning that Allaah will punish them.

n00348.summary: Waleed asks Uthmaan bin Madh'oon to return under his protection, and Uthmaan refuses.

n00349.summary: Mus'ab bin Umayr, once Makkah's most pampered youth, accepts Islaam in secret, is jailed by his family, and endures hardship after returning from Abyssinia.

n00350.summary: Abdullaah bin Hudhaafa refuses to leave Islaam under torture by the Roman emperor, and Umar kisses his head after he is freed.

n00351.summary: Ibn Abbaas tells Sa'eed bin Jubayr how severely the Mushrikeen tortured Muslims, to the point that some said words of disbelief to save their lives.

n00352.summary: After the Hijrah to Madinah the Muslims faced attacks from the Arabs, and Allaah revealed Surah Noor verse 55 promising them succession and peace.

n00353.summary: A second report from Ubay bin Ka'b gives the same occasion for Surah Noor verse 55: the Arab attacks on the Muslims after the Hijrah.

n00354.summary: Abu Moosa Ash'ari recounts the scarcity on the Dhaatur Riqaa expedition, when his feet were cut and his nails fell off, and the expedition was named after the bandages.

n00355.summary: Abu Burda relays that Abu Moosa disliked telling the Dhaatur Riqaa story because it made his good deeds known, and said Allaah would reward it.

n00356.summary: Nu'maan bin Basheer and Umar describe how the Prophet often could not find even poor dates to fill his stomach.

n00358.summary: Abu Hurayra finds the Prophet praying seated from hunger, and the Prophet tells him that a hungry person who endures it for reward will not face strict reckoning on the Day of Qiyaamah.

n00360.summary: Asked whether the meat was cut by lantern light, Aa'isha says they had no oil for a lantern and would have eaten the oil rather than burn it.

n00361.summary: Abu Hurayra says the Prophet's wives went months without a lantern or fire, rubbing any oil on their bodies rather than burning it.

n00362.summary: Abu Hurayra says two months passed without a fire in the Prophet's house, and they lived on dates and water, with milk sent by Ansaar neighbours.

n00363.summary: Urwa relays Aa'isha's account of two months without a fire in the Prophet's rooms, living on dates and water, with the milk from Ansaar neighbours that the Prophet gave them to drink.

n00364.summary: Aa'isha says the Prophet's house sometimes went forty days without fire, living on dates and water when they could find them.

n00365.summary: Aa'isha weeps when she eats her fill, remembering that the Prophet never ate bread or meat to his fill twice in one day.

n00366.summary: Aa'isha says the Prophet never ate barley bread to his fill for three days, or wheat bread for two days, and at his death he could not fill himself even with dates and water.

n00367.summary: Aa'isha says the Prophet never filled himself for three days in a row, though they could have, because he preferred to give to others.

n00368.summary: Hasan and Anas describe the Prophet patching his own clothes, going three days without both lunch and dinner, and never eating from a table or fine bread.

n00370.summary: Ibn Abbaas narrates that the Prophet's family often went hungry at night, and that their most common bread was made of barley.

n00371.summary: Abu Hurayra refuses an invitation to a roasted goat, saying the Prophet left the world without eating his fill of even barley bread.

n00372.summary: Anas narrates that Faatima gave the Prophet a piece of barley bread, which he said was the first food he had eaten in three days.

n00373.summary: Abu Hurayra reports that when hot food was brought to the Prophet, he praised Allaah, saying he had not eaten hot food for a long time.

n00374.summary: Sahl bin Sa'd says that from the start of the Prophet's mission until his death the Prophet never saw fine white flour or a sift, so they ate barley that had been blown clean rather than sifted.

n00375.summary: Aa'isha says no barley bread was ever left on the Prophet's tablecloth, and another narration says no food was left when it was lifted.

n00376.summary: Abu Talha says the Companions showed the Prophet their stomachs with stones tied to them from hunger, and the Prophet showed his own two stones; Ibn Bujayr adds the Prophet's warning about the Day of Qiyaamah.

n00378.summary: Ibn Abbaas narrates how the Prophet, Abu Bakr and Umar, all hungry, were fed by Abu Ayyoob, and how the Prophet later gave Abu Ayyoob a slave woman, whom he freed.

n00379.summary: Umar tells how the Prophet met him and Abu Bakr, both hungry, and took them to the house of the Ansaari Abul Haytham bin Tayyihaan.

n00380.summary: Faatima recounts that the family had no food, and the Prophet found her sons out with Ali; Ali relates finding a lost dinar that bought bread, and that he later paid far more zakaah.

n00381.summary: Ummu Sulaym relates that the Prophet told her to be patient, since his household had gone seven days without food and three days without fire, though he could ask Allaah to turn the mountains of Tihaama into gold.

n00382.summary: Sa'd recounts that he and the Prophet in Makkah endured hard times patiently, and that he survived three days by drinking water after grinding and toasting a piece of camel leather.

n00383.summary: Sa'd describes how, in battles with the Prophet, the Companions had only acacia and lotus leaves to eat, and he was the first Arab to shoot an arrow in Allaah's path.

n00384.summary: Miqdaad relates that, starving, he drank the Prophet's share of milk, and after the Prophet prayed for them he found the goats full again and milked them for the Prophet.

n00385.summary: Mujaahid relays how Abu Hurayra, starving, was invited home by the Prophet, who sent him to call the people of Suffa, served them milk, and told him to drink what remained.

n00386.summary: Abu Hurayra says he went three days without eating, and the Prophet fed him from the leftovers shared with the people of Suffa until he was full.

n00387.summary: Abu Hurayra, wiping his nose with a fine cloth, recalls how he once collapsed from extreme hunger by the Prophet's pulpit and was taken for insane.

n00388.summary: Abu Hurayra recalls serving Uthmaan and Bujra for food and a mount, and his gratitude when Allaah gave him Bujra in marriage.

n00389.summary: Abu Hurayra describes the bare food and clothing of the early days, and Ibn Mas'ood reports the Prophet telling the Sahabah they were better off then than they would be with plenty.

n00391.summary: Asmaa bint Abi Bakr recounts how, hungry and expecting a child, she asked a Jewish neighbour for fire and was finally sent a plate of food by the neighbour's husband.

n00392.summary: A Sahabi tells his son about the Battle of Khandaq, when hunger and cold stopped anyone volunteering until the Prophet called on Hudhayfa, and Abdullaah bin Mas'ood reports the Prophet promising that each person would soon have a dish morning and evening.

n00393.summary: Muhammad bin Seereen reports that a Companion would go three days without food, eating toasted leather or binding a stone to his stomach.

n00394.summary: Fudhaala bin Ubayd reports that men of Suffa collapsed from hunger during the Prophet's salaah, and the Prophet told them of the reward for their hardship.

n00395.summary: Anas reports that seven Companions survived on a single date and fallen leaves until their mouths were sore.

n00396.summary: Abu Hurayra reports that the Prophet gave seven dates to seven Companions suffering hunger, one for each.

n00397.summary: Abu Hurayra reports Companions leaving home in hunger and the Prophet giving them dates, and Aamir recalls a single date shared on an expedition.

n00398.summary: Before the Battle of Ahzaab the Prophet ﷺ prayed for the Muhaajireen and Ansaar digging the trench in cold and hunger, and they pledged to wage jihaad as long as they lived; similar pledges by Basheer, Ya'la and Mujaashi are cited.

n00400.summary: Ibn Abbaas reports that the Sahabah dug the trench with stones tied to their stomachs from hunger, and Aamir recalls how a single date was shared out on an expedition.

n00401.summary: Jaabir bin Abdillaah recalls that the Prophet sent a small force under Abu Ubaydah with one bag of dates, given out a single date each.

n00402.summary: Jaabir bin Abdillaah tells a student that once the dates ran out they missed even that one date.

n00403.summary: Abu Khunays Ghifaari recounts how, on the Tihaama expedition, the Prophet gathered the Sahabah's leftover provisions at Umar's advice, made du'aa, and every satchel was filled.

n00404.summary: Umar recounts how the Prophet blessed a small pile of leftover food on an expedition so that everyone was filled, then taught the Kalimah and its reward.

n00405.summary: Sahl bin Sa'd recalls a woman of his tribe who served the Companions a simple beetroot and barley dish every Friday.

n00406.summary: Abdullaah bin Abi Awfa reports that during seven battles with the Prophet they ate locusts.

n00407.summary: Abu Barzah reports that on an expedition they ate wheat bread from the enemy's ovens and checked their sides for fat, believing wheat bread made people fat.

n00408.summary: An unnamed Companion says that at Khaybar, while with the Prophet, they drove the enemy off the fine wheat bread they had baked.

n00409.summary: Abu Hurayra recounts that after Khaybar they drove Jewish bakers away from their wheat bread and shared it, and he checked his sides for fat.

n00410.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas reports Umar's account of the thirst on the Tabook expedition, and how Abu Bakr asked the Prophet for du'aa and rain then fell.

n00411.summary: At Yarmook, three mortally wounded Companions each passed the water to another, and all died before drinking it.

n00412.summary: Muhammad bin Hanafiyyah reports that Abu Amr Ansaari, weak with thirst while fasting, kept firing arrows in Allaah's path after hearing the Prophet's words on their reward, and was martyred before sunset.

n00413.summary: Abu Rayhaana recounts volunteering for a night guard in the cold, when the Prophet made du'aa for him and said the fire of Jahannam is forbidden to the eye that guards in Allaah's path.

n00414.summary: Khabbaab bin Arat recounts Hamza's burial, when there was only one small shawl to shroud him.

n00415.summary: Shafaa bint Abdillaah reports that she rebuked the Prophet for having nothing to give her, then found her son-in-law Shurahbeel without a decent garment for the Masjid because the Prophet had borrowed his only cloth.

n00416.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports that Jibra'eel asked, through the Prophet, whether Abu Bakr was pleased with Allaah in his poverty, and Abu Bakr affirmed that he was.

n00417.summary: Ali recounts that when he married Faatima, their only bedding was a sheepskin and they had no servant.

n00418.summary: Abu Burda relays his father Abu Moosa Ash'ari's account of wearing sheepskin and living on dates and water, so that the Companions smelled like sheep when caught in the rain.

n00419.summary: Abu Hurayra reports seeing seventy men of Suffa, none with a large shawl, who held their garments together so they would not be exposed.

n00420.summary: Waathila bin Asqa says the men of Suffa had no complete clothing, and Aa'isha contrasts her slave-woman's plain shirt with the shirt she once had, which Madinah women borrowed for weddings.

n00421.summary: Hudhayfa recounts a freezing night at the Battle of Ahzaab, when the Prophet sent him to gather news of the enemy, prayed for his protection, and covered him with his shawl on his return.

n00422.summary: Yazeed Taymi reports that Hudhayfa, asked by a man who wished he had fought beside the Prophet, described the night of Ahzaab and the shawl the Prophet put over him when he returned cold.

n00423.summary: The Prophet asks who will go to gather news of the enemy, promising the volunteer companionship in Jannah, but no one stands up from fear, hunger and cold.

n00424.summary: Abu Saa'ib relays a report from a man of Banu Abdul Ash'hal who, wounded at Uhud, marched after the Prophet's caller with his brother, carrying him in turn.

n00425.summary: Abdullaah bin Sahl and his brother Raafi bin Sahl went to Hamraa'ul Asad despite their wounds, with no transport, each carrying the other in turn.

n00426.summary: Several elders of Banu Salma report that the crippled Amr bin Jamooh asked to march to Uhud, the Prophet excused him from jihaad, yet he went and was martyred.

n00427.summary: Abu Qataadah reports that Amr bin Jamooh asked the Prophet whether he would walk in Jannah with a healthy leg if martyred, and the Prophet said he could see him doing so after his death.

n00428.summary: Yahya bin Abdul Hameed reports that Raafi bin Khadeej, struck by an arrow, chose to have only the shaft removed so the Prophet could bear witness to his martyrdom, and that he died later under Mu'aawiya.

n00429.summary: Urwa reports that the Quraysh plotted to seize, kill or exile the Prophet, that Allaah revealed the plan to him, and that he was warned of a plot to kill him in his sleep on the day he went to Abu Bakr's house.

n00430.summary: Ali sleeps in the Prophet's bed while the Prophet and Abu Bakr hide in the cave of Thowr, where Allaah sends tranquillity when the Mushrikeen reach it; Aamir bin Fuhayra and Abdullaah bin Abi Bakr look after them.

n00431.summary: Aa'isha recounts how the Prophet told Abu Bakr at midday that he was permitted to migrate, Abu Bakr asked to accompany him, and Abu Bakr had camels ready; a second report says the Prophet insisted on buying one.

n00432.summary: Asmaa bint Abi Bakr recounts preparing provisions for the Hijrah and tying them with her belt, and how the Prophet and Abu Bakr hid in the cave while the Quraysh searched for them.

n00433.summary: Rasulullaah and Abu Bakr travel along the coast toward Madinah, and Suraaqa bin Maalik sets out after them when told of two riders.

n00434.summary: Umar praises Abu Bakr's devotion, recalling how Abu Bakr walked ahead and behind the Prophet and cleaned the cave before him.

n00435.summary: In the cave, Abu Bakr fears for the Prophet when the Quraysh come searching, and the Prophet tells him that Allaah is with them.

n00436.summary: Abu Bakr tells Anas that in the cave he warned the Prophet that a pursuer looking down would see them, and the Prophet asked what he thought of two whose third is Allaah.

n00437.summary: Baraa bin Aazib reports that Abu Bakr bought a saddle from his father and asked that the Banu Najjaar be honoured, and that the Prophet stayed where he was commanded the next morning.

n00439.summary: Anas bin Maalik, as a child, describes the crowds in Madinah who came out to welcome the Prophet and Abu Bakr on their arrival.

n00440.summary: Aa'isha reports that the women and children sang a welcoming verse when the Prophet arrived in Madinah.

n00441.summary: Baraa bin Aazib says the first emigrants to reach Madinah were Mus'ab bin Umayr and Ibn Ummu Maktoom, followed by Ammaar, Bilaal, Sa'd and Umar, and that the people of Madinah were overjoyed.

n00442.summary: A variant report by Baraa names Mus'ab bin Umayr, Ibn Ummu Maktoom and Umar as the first emigrants to reach Madinah, and says the Prophet and Abu Bakr arrived after them.

n00443.summary: Umar recounts how Abu Jahal and Haarith bin Hishaam tricked their cousin Ayaash bin Abi Rabee'ah back to Makkah and made him forsake Islaam, and how Hishaam bin Aas, also held back, later received the verses of Surah Zumar that gave him hope.

n00444.summary: Uthmaan bin Affaan becomes the first to emigrate with his family for Allaah's pleasure, travelling to Abyssinia with his wife Ruqayya, and the Prophet prays for them.

n00445.summary: A variant adds that the Prophet went out to wait for news of the emigrants until a woman brought him word about them.

n00446.summary: Ali recounts that the Prophet left him in Makkah to return the trusts people had deposited with him, and that Ali followed three days later and stayed at Kulthoom bin Hidm's house in Quba.

n00447.summary: Muhammad bin Haatib reports the Prophet's dream of a land of dates, after which Haatib and Ja'far sailed to Abyssinia, and Ja'far asked leave to worship Allaah without fear.

n00448.summary: Ummu Salama recounts that the Prophet sent the Muslims to Abyssinia to escape persecution, and that the Quraysh sent Amr bin Al Aas and Abdullaah bin Abi Rabee'ah with gifts to have them returned.

n00449.summary: At Najaashi's court, Ja'far explains the Muslims' faith and recites about Isa and Maryam, Najaashi refuses the Quraysh's demand, and the report also tells of Zubayr's news of Najaashi's victory and the Muslims who returned to the Prophet.

n00450.summary: Abu Moosa Ash'ari reports the same account, adding that Najaashi said he would have gone to the Prophet and kissed his feet, and then let the Muslims stay wherever they liked.

n00451.summary: Ja'far reports that Amr bin Al Aas and Umaarah bin Waleed, sent with gifts from Abu Sufyaan, demanded the Muslims be handed over; Najaashi heard them out, questioned the Muslims about Isa, and set a penalty for harming them that he doubled.

n00452.summary: Ja'far reports that Najaashi, having testified to the Prophet's Risaalat and asked for his forgiveness, sent the Muslims back to Madinah with provisions, and the Prophet prayed for Najaashi's forgiveness.

n00453.summary: Ummu Abdillaah bint Abi Hathma recounts that Umar, still a Mushrik, showed unusual gentleness when they left for Abyssinia, and her husband Aamir doubted he would ever accept Islaam.

n00454.summary: Khaalid bin Sa'eed and his brother Amr return from Abyssinia after Badr, and the Prophet tells them they made two Hijrahs.

n00455.summary: Abu Moosa Ash'ari recounts his migration from Yemen with his brothers and about fifty others by ship to Abyssinia and then to Madinah, Umar's remark to Asmaa bint Umays, and the Prophet's praise of the Ash'ariyyeen.

n00456.summary: Asmaa bint Umays asks the Prophet about people who boast that they came first, and he tells her that she and those with her made two Hijrahs.

n00457.summary: Ummu Salama recounts how the Banu Mughiera kept her from her husband Abu Salma and son, how they were reunited after a year, and how Uthmaan bin Talha escorted her alone to Quba.

n00458.summary: Suhayb reports that the Prophet told him of the land of migration, that youngsters of Quraysh held him back until he paid them gold, and that on reaching Quba the Prophet said his transaction had been profitable.

n00459.summary: Sa'eed bin Musayyib reports that Suhayb, pursued while migrating, emptied his quiver and offered to show the pursuers his wealth in Makkah if they left him alone, and that Surah Baqarah 207 was revealed about him.

n00460.summary: Ikrama reports that the pursued Suhayb emptied a quiver of forty arrows and offered the pursuers Abdullaah bin Umar's two slave women in Makkah if they let him go.

n00461.summary: Anas gives a similar account of Suhayb's encounter with the Quraysh and adds that Surah Baqarah 207 was revealed on that occasion.

n00462.summary: Suhayb reports that the Quraysh let him leave Makkah only after he gave them all his wealth, and the Prophet told him he had earned a grand profit.
