n00463.summary: Muhammad bin Zaid reports that Abdullaah bin Umar would close his eyes and not look at or stop at the house in Makkah he had left when he migrated.

n00464.summary: Another report says Abdullaah bin Umar wept whenever he spoke of the Prophet and closed his eyes when passing his former house in Makkah.

n00465.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas reports that Abd bin Jahash left Makkah secretly for the Prophet in Madinah against his wife's wishes, Abu Sufyaan became angry, and a poem about the migration follows.

n00466.summary: Verses of Surah Nisaa on Hijrah are revealed, and Dhamra bin Abil Ees, a blind and wealthy man, sets out to migrate despite illness and dies at Tan'eem, which prompts a further verse.

n00467.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas reports that Dhamra bin Jundub died on the way to the Prophet, and that Surah Nisaa 100 was then revealed about one who dies while making Hijrah.

n00468.summary: Waathila bin Asqa reports that he joined the Prophet's prayer at the back, was asked whether his Hijrah would be Baadi or Baati, and pledged obedience as far as he is able.

n00469.summary: Salama bin Akwa reports that the Prophet advised the epidemic-stricken Banu Sulaym to live outside the town, and told them they would be counted as Muhaajireen wherever they were.

n00470.summary: Junaadah bin Abi Umayyah asks the Prophet whether Hijrah has ended, and the Prophet says it continues as long as Jihaad is waged against the disbelievers.

n00471.summary: Abdullaah bin Sa'di reports that he asked the Prophet about the claim that Hijrah had ended, and was told that his need was better than theirs because Hijrah continues while Jihaad is waged.

n00472.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas reports that Safwaan bin Umayyah came to Madinah because he had heard that the one who makes no Hijrah has no Deen, and the Prophet told him Hijrah had ended with the conquest of Makkah, so he should return home and answer calls to Jihaad.

n00473.summary: Safwaan bin Umayyah asks whether the one who does not make Hijrah is destroyed, and the Prophet replies that Hijrah ended after the conquest of Makkah but Jihaad and its intention remain.

n00475.summary: Aa'isha recounts how the Prophet sent Zaid bin Haaritha and Abu Raafi to bring his family from Makkah, and how her own family travelled to Madinah with Abu Bakr's arrangements.

n00476.summary: Aa'isha recounts her camel bolting on the journey of Hijrah and how it stopped when someone told her to throw down its reins.

n00477.summary: Zaynab, daughter of the Prophet, recounts how Hind bint Utba tried to dissuade her from Hijrah, and how Kinaana then escorted her out of Makkah and was confronted by Abu Sufyaan at Dhu Tuwa.

n00478.summary: Urwa bin Zubayr reports that Zaynab was attacked by Quraysh men on her Hijrah, miscarried, and died later from the injury, and so was regarded as a martyr.

n00479.summary: Aa'isha describes how Habbaar bin Aswad injured Zaynab on her Hijrah and how she was cared for in Makkah, and the Prophet then sent Zaid bin Haaritha to bring her to Madinah.

n00480.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar, Abu Hurayrah and Ammaar bin Yaasir report that Durra bint Abu Lahab was insulted by Banu Zurayq women after her Hijrah, and that the Prophet consoled her and spoke of interceding for his family.

n00481.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas recounts how, as a child of eight, he and his brother Fadl lost their way on the road from Makkah and reached the Prophet at the trench during the Battle of Ahzaab.

n00482.summary: The author introduces the chapter on how the Sahabah valued assisting the Deen above worldly honour and sacrificed for it.

n00483.summary: Aa'isha reports that the Prophet presented his message to the Arab tribes each year, offering Jannah, until Allaah brought the Ansaar to grant him a place to migrate to.

n00484.summary: Umar recounts that the Prophet presented himself to every Arab tribe during the Hajj season until Allaah brought the Ansaar, who gave him sanctuary and help.

n00485.summary: Umar says that the Muhaajireen failed to keep their pledge to the Ansaar, and that if he lived a year every governor would be from the Ansaar.

n00486.summary: Jaabir bin Abdillaah relates that the Prophet sought support from people during the Hajj season, and that a man from Hamdaan and then a delegation of the Ansaar came to him.

n00487.summary: Urwa reports that a group of Ansaar on Hajj, including Mu'aadh bin Afraa and As'ad bin Zuraarah, accepted the Prophet's message and promised to return and invite their people, after which many Ansaar homes had Muslims.

n00488.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas learns couplets from Sirmah bin Qais that praise how the Ansaar welcomed the Prophet and supported the Muhaajireen with their wealth and lives.

n00489.summary: Anas recounts that the Prophet made Abdur Rahmaan bin Awf a brother to Sa'd bin Rabee, that Abdur Rahmaan then traded and married, and that the Prophet advised him to host a waleema.

n00490.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas explains that the early practice of inheritance between Muhaajireen and Ansaar brothers, made by the Prophet, was abrogated first by the verse on relatives in Surah Anfaal and then fully by Surah Ahzaab.

n00491.summary: Abu Hurayrah and Abdur Rahmaan bin Zaid bin Aslam report that the Ansaar offered to share their date plantations with the Muhaajireen, and the Prophet suggested they let the Muhaajireen work them and share the dates.

n00492.summary: Anas and Jaabir report the generosity of the Ansaar toward the Muhaajireen, including the harvest-sharing trick and the offer to hand over their Khaybar shares, which the Prophet accepted.

n00494.summary: Anas reports that when the Prophet asked the Ansaar to share the land of Bahrain, they refused unless the Muhaajireen received an equal share, and the Prophet told them to be patient.

n00495.summary: On the Prophet's request, Muhammad bin Maslama and companions deceive and kill Ka'b bin Ashraf, who had harmed Islaam, and report back to the Prophet.

n00496.summary: Five men from the Khazraj kill Abu Raafi Sallaam bin Abul Huqayq at Khaybar at night, and when they report back the Prophet inspects their swords.

n00497.summary: Baraa and Abdullaah bin Ateek describe how the Ansaar, sent by the Prophet, entered a fortress at Khaybar and killed Abu Raafi, and the Prophet healed Abdullaah's injured leg.

n00498.summary: Muhayyisa kills the Jewish trader Ibn Shayba on the Prophet's permission, and his brother Huwayyisa, angered at first, accepts Islaam after hearing that Muhayyisa would have killed him if the Prophet had commanded it.

n00499.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas recounts how the Prophet called the Jews of Madinah to Islaam after Badr, how they boasted of their strength, and how verses about Badr were revealed in reply.

n00500.summary: The Jews taunt the Prophet about Badr, and Ubaadah bin Saamit renounces his Jewish friends while Abdullaah bin Ubay insists on keeping them, after which verses forbidding taking Jews and Christians as friends are revealed.

n00501.summary: When the Banu Qaynuqah turned hostile to the Prophet, Ubaadah bin Saamit renounced his alliance with them, while Abdullaah bin Ubay bin Salool stood by them, and verses on not taking Jews and Christians as friends were revealed.

n00502.summary: Before Badr the Quraysh try to turn Abdullaah bin Ubay against the Muslims, and after Badr the Banu Nadheer plot against the Prophet, are besieged, and are expelled to Shaam.

n00503.summary: Ibn Abbaas describes the terms on which the Prophet besieged the Banu Nadheer and expelled them, allowing one camel and water bag per three people, with a variant that Muhammad bin Maslama gave them ten days to leave.

n00504.summary: Aa'isha reports the Battle of Khandaq: Sa'd bin Mu'aadh was struck by an arrow and prayed to live until the fate of Banu Qurayzah, then after their surrender chose execution of the warriors, and Sa'd died, and the Prophet and Sahabah wept for him.

n00505.summary: Another narration states that the Prophet's tears flowed onto his beard as he returned from the burial of Sa'd bin Mu'aadh.

n00508.summary: At Hunayn, when the Muslim army fled and the Prophet was left alone, he called the Ansaar, who answered that they were with him, and he reassured them, and the Ansaar wept and accepted his distribution.

n00509.summary: After the Battle of Hunayn the Ansaar felt hurt at the distribution of booty, and the Prophet gathered them, reminded them of Allaah's favour, and told them he would return home with them rather than with the goats and camels.

n00510.summary: After Hunayn the Prophet explains to the Ansaar, who were upset that he gave booty to the Quraysh and others, that he did so to win hearts, and the Ansaar weep with him.

n00511.summary: Anas reports that after Hunayn the Prophet gave booty to newer Muslims, that some Ansaar complained, and that the Prophet told them to be patient and to return home with him.

n00512.summary: Anas reports that the Prophet told the Ansaar they were close to him like under-clothing while others were like outer garments, and that he would walk the valley of the Ansaar.

n00513.summary: Anas reports the Prophet's words to the Muhaajireen and Ansaar after wealth came from Bahrain: the Ansaar turn out in large numbers in hazards but in small numbers when something is distributed.

n00514.summary: Anas and then a second narration report that the Prophet sent greetings to the Ansaar through Abu Talha, describing them as extremely chaste and patient, including during the Prophet's final illness.

n00516.summary: Abdullaah bin Shaddaad reports that the Prophet visited Sa'd bin Mu'aadh on his deathbed and told him that he had fulfilled his pledge to Allaah and that Allaah would fulfil His pledge to him.

n00517.summary: Aa'isha (RA) reports the Prophet's words on the Ansaar, and his question about a set of clothing he had given to a veteran of Badr, Uhud and Aqaba, which a Quraysh youth then bought.

n00518.summary: Usayd bin Hudhayr asked the Prophet to remember needy Ansaar families, who received a share of the Khaybar barley and dates; later Umar gave Usayd a garment, and Usayd recalled the Prophet's warning that others would be preferred over the Ansaar.

n00519.summary: Muhammad bin Maslama (RA) reports that Umar (RA) questioned him after he called takbeer in the Masjid, because he had seen Quraysh men and an Ansaari wearing clothes that Umar had given; Umar wept and vowed never again to favour the Quraysh over the Ansaar.

n00520.summary: Zaid bin Thaabit (RA) reports that the Prophet honoured Sa'd bin Ubaadah (RA) and his son, welcomed the Ansaar, told them others would be preferred over them after his death, and urged patience until they meet him at the Pond of Kawthar.

n00521.summary: Anas (RA) reports that Jareer (RA) served him greatly on a journey, because Jareer had seen the Ansaar serve the Prophet and so served every Ansaari he met.

n00522.summary: Habeeb bin Abi Thaabit reports that Abu Ayyoob Ansaari (RA), refused the financial help he asked for from Mu'aawiya (RA), recalled the Prophet's words that the Ansaar would be outranked later and was told to be patient; he then stayed with Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) in Basra, who gave him his household and generous provision.

n00523.summary: A variant report says Abu Ayyoob Ansaari (RA) went to Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) in Basra, who had been appointed governor by Ali (RA), and Ibn Abbaas gave him his household's furnishings and five times the grant he had asked for, plus forty slaves.

n00524.summary: Hassaan bin Thaabit (RA) reports that Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) pressed the Ansaar's request before the Ameerul Mu'mineen, arguing until it was granted, and that Hassaan then praised him in verse.

n00525.summary: Hassaan bin Thaabit (RA)'s verse praising Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) is continued, and the Ameerul Mu'mineen says that the word 'inefficient' in it was aimed at him.

n00526.summary: Anas bin Maalik (RA) reports that the Ansaar asked the Prophet to pray for their forgiveness, and he prayed for the Ansaar, their children and grandchildren, and by variant reports their spouses and neighbours.

n00527.summary: A variant report has the Prophet praying for the Ansaar, their children and their friends; Uthmaan bin Affaan (RA) then reports the Prophet's saying that imaan belongs to Yemen, and his prayer to honour the Ansaar, who gave him shelter, support and undaunted loyalty.

n00528.summary: A narrator reports Abu Bakr (RA) relating the bond between the Muhaajireen and the Ansaar in a sermon, quoting verses of poetry in praise of the Ansaar who stood by them in hardship.

n00529.summary: Humayd bin Abdur Rahmaan Himyari reports that when the Prophet died, Abu Bakr (RA) and Umar (RA) went to the Ansaar who were gathered over the Khilaafah, and Abu Bakr cited the Prophet's words that the Quraysh are the successors; Sa'd bin Ubaadah (RA) accepted this.

n00530.summary: Abu Sa'eed Khudri (RA) reports the debate in the Banu Saa'idah hall over the Khilaafah, where Zaid bin Thaabit (RA) argued that the leader should be from the Muhaajireen, Abu Bakr (RA) answered, and Zaid then took his hand and pledged allegiance to him.

n00531.summary: Qaasim bin Muhammad reports the pledge at the Banu Saa'idah hall: Hubaab bin Mundhir (RA) raised the Ansaar's concern, Umar and Abu Bakr (RA) answered, Basheer bin Sa'd (RA) pledged first, and Abu Bakr would not take back a share he had sent an old woman of the Banu Adi bin Najaar, who refused it because she would not be bribed from her Deen.

n00532.summary: Abu Ayyoob Ansaari (RA) and Anas (RA) report the Prophet's consultation before the march to Badr: Miqdaad (RA) said the Muslims would not fail to fight, Abu Bakr and Umar gave their views, and the Ansaar pledged to follow him even to the distant city of Barkul Ghimaad, after which a verse was revealed.

n00534.summary: Anas (RA) reports that the Prophet consulted about marching on Abu Sufyaan's caravan; he turned away from the views of Abu Bakr (RA) and Umar (RA), then Sa'd bin Ubaadah (RA) said the Ansaar would follow him wherever he went, and the Prophet gave the order to march.

n00535.summary: Alqama bin Waqqaas Laythi (RA) reports the Prophet's consultation at Rowhaa after leaving for Badr: Abu Bakr and Umar gave their views, Sa'd bin Mu'aadh (RA) pledged that the Ansaar would follow him anywhere, and a verse was revealed in praise of this; a further report and Ibn Is'haaq add Sa'd's words and the Prophet's promise of victory over one of two groups.

n00536.summary: Anas (RA) reports that the Prophet sent Basbas (RA) to spy on Abu Sufyaan's caravan and marched to Badr; he promised the Sahabah Jannah, which Umayr bin Hamaam (RA) took up, throwing down his dates and fighting until he was martyred. Ibn Is'haaq and Ibn Jareer report the same encouragement.

n00537.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) reports the Tabook expedition: the Prophet urged spending, Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf (RA) and Umar (RA) gave large sums, Aasim Ansaari and Abu Aqeel gave dates, the hypocrites mocked the small gifts, Jadd bin Qais asked to be excused, Khaalid bin Waleed captured a ruler, and Uthmaan (RA) provided two hundred camels; a verse of Surah Baraa'ah was revealed on the hypocrites.

n00538.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) reports that the Prophet asked Jadd bin Qais to march to Tabook, and Jadd asked to be excused for fear of the Roman women, after which a verse was revealed about him.

n00539.summary: Ibn Asaakir reports that the Prophet sent Sahabah to Makkah and to various tribes to recruit people for jihaad, including Buraydah bin Husayb (RA) to Banu Aslam, Raafi bin Makeeth (RA) and Jund bin Makeeth (RA) to Juhayna, Nu'aym bin Mas'ood (RA) to Ash'ja, and Budayl bin Waraqa (RA) among those sent to Banu Ka'b bin Amr.

n00540.summary: Abu Bakr (RA) gives all he owns and Umar (RA) half, Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf (RA), Talha (RA) and others give large sums, and Uthmaan (RA) equips a third of the army; women send jewellery, and the army camps at Thaniyyatul Wadaa. The Prophet insists that the army of Usaama (RA) be sent even while ill, despite Ummu Ayman's request to keep him back.

n00541.summary: The Prophet appointed Usaama bin Zaid to lead an army against Ubna, rebuked those who objected to the young commander, and insisted the army leave even while he was ill.

n00542.summary: Usaama (RA) turns back from Jurf on news from Ummu Ayman that the Prophet is dying, reaches Madinah with Umar and Abu Ubaydah after the Prophet's passing on Monday, and Buraydah bin Husayb (RA) plants Usaama's flag at the Prophet's door, which Abu Bakr then orders to be kept there until Usaama leads the army.

n00543.summary: After news of the Prophet's death, Abu Bakr (RA) insisted on sending Usaama's army despite objections from senior Sahabah, asked that Umar stay behind, required all who had marched before to go, and sent Usaama off from Jurf with three thousand men and a thousand horses; Hurayth was sent ahead as a spy to find the enemy.

n00544.summary: Hasan bin Abil Hasan reports that Usaama asked Umar to seek permission to bring the army back to Madinah, since the Prophet had died and he had the leading Sahabah with him; some Ansaar asked for an older commander, but Abu Bakr refused to reverse the appointment and seized Umar by the beard.

n00545.summary: Abu Bakr (RA) walks beside Usaama's mount as the army sets off, refuses to ride or let Usaama dismount, and asks for Umar to stay, which Usaama grants.

n00546.summary: Urwa (RA) reports that Abu Bakr (RA) refused to recall Usaama's army despite objections from Muhaajireen and Ansaar, saying he would not hold back an army he had dispatched and that the tribes refusing zakaah must be fought; he then appointed Khaalid bin Waleed (RA) to lead the force against the Murtaddeen.

n00547.summary: Urwa (RA) reports that after the pledge the Ansaar united, and when people asked Abu Bakr to hold back Usaama's army amid the wave of apostasy and hypocrisy, he refused, saying he would not hold back an army he had dispatched.

n00548.summary: Aa'isha (RA) describes how after the Prophet's death all the tribes apostatised and hypocrisy rose, and Abu Bakr alone held the affairs together; Abu Hurayrah (RA) reports that Usaama's army was sent to Dhi Khushub, that Abu Bakr refused to recall it, and that it returned victorious.

n00550.summary: Sayf reports that after Khaalid bin Waleed left for Shaam, Abu Bakr (RA) fell ill and appointed Umar (RA) as successor, telling him to send Muthanna (RA) and the people to Shaam at once and never let any hurdle prevent the matters of the Deen.

n00551.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) reports that after the Prophet's death Abu Bakr (RA) consulted the Muhaajireen and Ansaar about the tribes refusing zakaah; Umar, Uthmaan and Ali (RA) first advised leniency, Abu Bakr refused, and vowed to fight anyone who separated salaah from zakaah.

n00552.summary: Saalih bin Kaysaan (RA) reports Abu Bakr's sermon as the tribes left Islaam, recalling that the Prophet's few companions were made into the best nation, quoting Aal-Imraan 144 and Noor 55, and vowing to fight those who refused zakaah.

n00553.summary: Umar (RA) reports that when the tribes left Islaam, the Muhaajireen with him asked Abu Bakr to leave those who prayed without zakaah alone, but Abu Bakr refused, and Umar says that day of Abu Bakr's resolve outweighed the deeds of Umar's whole family.

n00554.summary: Umar (RA) reports that when the tribes left Islaam, he counselled Abu Bakr to show mercy towards those who refused zakaah, but Abu Bakr refused, saying he would fight them while his hand could hold a sword, and Umar found him the more capable of the two.

n00555.summary: Dabba bin Mihsin Anzi (RA) reports asking Umar whether he was better than Abu Bakr; Umar wept and recounted Abu Bakr's night of following the Prophet out of Makkah in the Hijrah and his day of standing firm when the tribes apostatised, with Umar's counsel.

n00556.summary: Abu Hurayrah (RA) reports that when the tribes left Islaam, Umar (RA) asked how they could be fought given the Prophet's words to fight people until they say La ilaaha illallaah; Abu Bakr replied that he would fight whoever separates salaah from zakaah, and Umar then accepted this.

n00557.summary: Qaasim bin Mahmood (RA) reports a sermon of Abu Bakr (RA): every matter has its principles, deeds without imaan or niyyah earn nothing, and the rewards for jihaad are a trade pointed to by Allaah that brings honour in both worlds.

n00558.summary: Ibn Is'haaq bin Yasaar reports, from Khaalid bin Waleed (RA), a letter from Abu Bakr (RA) after the battle of Yamaamah ordering Khaalid and the Muhaajireen and Ansaar to march to Iraq, urging jihaad for the sake of Allaah and promising Allaah's reward.

n00559.summary: Abdullaah bin Abi Awfa (RA) reports that Abu Bakr (RA) consulted senior Sahabah, including Ali, Umar, Uthmaan, Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf, Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas, Sa'eed bin Zaid and Abu Ubaydah, about marching against the Romans in Shaam to elevate the Kalimah, and said his view was only his own opinion.

n00560.summary: Umar (RA) answers Abu Bakr's proposal to march against the Romans by praising Abu Bakr's precedence in every good, and advises dispatching cavalry and infantry in succession so that Allaah assists the Deen.

n00561.summary: Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf advises raiding the Romans' borders with cavalry several times and gathering the tribes of Yemen before a full attack.

n00562.summary: Uthmaan backs Abu Bakr's plan for the Shaam campaign, and the leading Muhaajireen and Ansaar, including Talha, Zubayr and Sa'd, pledge to support him.

n00563.summary: Ali tells Abu Bakr that Allaah will grant victory, Abu Bakr is glad, and he then urges the people to march against the Romans in Shaam.

n00564.summary: Umar rebukes the Sahabah for their silence, Amr bin Sa'eed and Khaalid bin Sa'eed answer, and Abu Bakr orders the army for Shaam and writes to Yemen.

n00565.summary: Abu Bakr's letter calls the people of Yemen to jihaad against the Romans, promising martyrdom or victory and booty, and Anas bin Maalik carries it.

n00566.summary: Abu Bakr advises the army leaving for Shaam not to be proud and to keep ten rules, starting with not killing a helpless old man.

n00567.summary: Muthanna bin Haaritha urges a march on Persia, Umar answers that Abu Ubayd bin Mas'ood should lead, and Umar gives him advice on warfare.

n00568.summary: Umar says the Sahabah who volunteered first deserve command, and he appoints Abu Ubayd bin Mas'ood.

n00569.summary: After Abu Ubayd's martyrdom, Umar consults the Sahabah about marching on Persia, Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf argues against it, and Sa'd bin Maalik is chosen as commander.

n00570.summary: Uthmaan tells the people from the pulpit a Hadith that a day guarding the borders for Allaah's pleasure is better than a thousand days elsewhere.

n00571.summary: Uthmaan repeats the same Hadith from the pulpit, adding that guarding the borders is better than a thousand days of salaah and fasting.

n00572.summary: Ali praises Allaah, tells the people that tomorrow they face the enemy, and urges them to pray at night, recite Qur'aan and seek help from Allaah.

n00573.summary: At Siffeen, Ali urges the Muslims to trade Imaan and jihaad for forgiveness and Jannah, and to stand in straight, firm rows.

n00574.summary: Ali, having lost hope in the Khawaarij, warns that those who abandon jihaad face ruin and tells the army to prepare to march against them.

n00575.summary: After the Battle of Nahrwaan, Ali rebukes the people for refusing to march and sets out the mutual rights between ruler and people.

n00576.summary: During Siffeen, Howshab Himyari calls on Ali to leave the fighting so that Muslim blood is spared, and Ali refuses to compromise the Deen.

n00578.summary: At Qaadisiyyah, Aasim bin Amr tells the army that victory depends on steadfastness with the sword and spear, and that they must seek the Aakhirah.

n00579.summary: Abu Umaamah stays home with his mother instead of going to Badr, as his uncle Abu Burda advised, and later leads the funeral prayer for her.

n00580.summary: Umar says he would have preferred to meet Allaah except for three things: walking in the path of Allaah, prostrating to Allaah, and sitting with people who choose their words as the best dates are selected.

n00581.summary: Umar tells the people to perform Hajj, which Allaah has commanded, but says Jihaad is even more virtuous.

n00582.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar says he was refused for Badr as too young and wept all night until he was accepted the next year, and he admits the Muslims turned their backs at Uhud but that Allaah forgave them.

n00583.summary: Anas reports that Umar gave a man who wanted to go on Jihaad a mount and provisions, and the man, refusing the gold and silver in the treasury, prayed for Umar's reward.

n00584.summary: Umar asks who deserves the greatest reward, then names a man guarding Madinah from the Shaam side as better than the Ameerul Mu'mineen.

n00585.summary: Umar regrets that Mu'aadh bin Jabal left for Shaam and was not kept in Madinah, and Abu Bakr refused to hold him back.

n00586.summary: Umar moves Haarith bin Hishaam and Suhayl bin Amr aside for the early Muhaajireen, and he tells them the way to gain status is Jihaad on the Roman border.

n00587.summary: Suhayl bin Amr tells the Quraysh leaders that they cannot match those who accepted Islaam early, and that they should go out for jihaad, and then leaves for Shaam.

n00588.summary: Suhayl bin Amr quotes the Prophet that a moment standing in Allaah's path is better than a lifetime of deeds, and he stays at the border until he dies in the plague of Amwaas.

n00589.summary: Haarith bin Hishaam leaves Makkah for Jihaad despite the grief of the people, saying that the early Muslims excelled them and that he hopes to equal them in the Aakhirah, and he is later martyred.

n00590.summary: On his deathbed Khaalid bin Waleed says he loves a freezing night on a Jihaad expedition more than a wedding night, and that his Jihaad left him little time to learn the Qur'aan.

n00591.summary: On his deathbed Khaalid bin Waleed says he hoped for martyrdom and wanted his weapons and horse given in Allaah's path, and Umar says the family may weep but must not tear clothes or wail.

n00592.summary: Bilaal asks Abu Bakr for permission to guard the borders until he dies, Abu Bakr asks him to stay, and after Abu Bakr's death Umar appoints Sa'd to call the Adhaan in his place.

n00593.summary: After the Prophet's burial, Bilaal calls the Adhaan and the people weep. Abu Bakr then releases him to go to Shaam for jihaad, and Bilaal dies there.

n00594.summary: Miqdaad and Abu Ayyoob hold that Surah Taubah's command to proceed in jihaad 'when light or heavy' applies in all conditions.

n00595.summary: Miqdaad keeps planning to join a jihaad expedition despite his weight, quoting Surah Taubah's verse 'when light or heavy', and Abu Raashid and Jubayr bin Nufayr report his answers.

n00597.summary: Abu Talha, reciting the verse calling believers to march light or heavy, insisted on joining the naval expedition despite his age, and his body was found undecayed when buried on an island after seven days at sea.

n00598.summary: Abu Ayyoob Ansaari, who missed only one campaign after Badr, asked Yazeed bin Mu'aawiya to carry his body as far into enemy land as possible and bury him there.

n00599.summary: Abu Dhabyaan reports that in Mu'aawiya's time Abu Ayyoob asked his companions to bury him in front of the enemy lines on campaign, and the report continues.

n00600.summary: On a campaign under Yazeed bin Mu'aawiya, Abu Ayyoob asks to be buried beneath the feet of the army where it meets the enemy, and says whoever dies without shirk enters Jannah.

n00601.summary: Abu Khaythama, having missed the march to Tabook, hurries after the army in the heat, and the Prophet commends him and prays for him when he arrives.

n00602.summary: Ibn Yaameen Nasri gives Abu Layla and Abdullaah bin Mughaffal a camel and provisions so they can join the Prophet on jihaad, and Ulba bin Zaid gives Sadaqah in the night, which the Prophet praises as accepted.

n00603.summary: Ulba bin Zaid, with nothing to give in Sadaqah, gives up his honour for the Muslims in the night, and the Prophet tells him his Sadaqah is accepted.

n00604.summary: The Prophet sends an army to Mu'ta under Zaid bin Haaritha, with Ja'far and Ibn Rawaaha as successors, and rebukes Ibn Rawaaha for staying behind to pray Jumu'ah.

n00605.summary: On a Jumu'ah day the Prophet sends Abdullaah bin Rawaaha with an army, he stays to pray Jumu'ah first, and the Prophet tells him no deeds can match the morning of the army's march.

n00606.summary: The Prophet rebukes a Companion who stayed behind to pray with him and say farewell to his family, saying the companions who left are far ahead in virtue.

n00607.summary: The Prophet orders a battalion to leave, and when they ask whether to leave that night or in the morning, he asks if they would not like to spend the night in a garden of Jannah.

n00608.summary: Umar scolds Mu'aadh bin Jabal for delaying his departure to jihaad after the army had already left, citing the virtue of one morning or evening in the path of Allaah.

n00609.summary: Ka'b bin Maalik tells how he stayed behind from Tabook without excuse, was boycotted for fifty days, and was forgiven after he chose to speak the truth; the Qur'aan revealed his case.

n00610.summary: Abu Imraan reports from Constantinople that Abu Ayyoob Ansaari explained the verse 'do not throw yourselves into destruction' as a warning against staying home to tend fields instead of fighting; a second report repeats the same warning.

n00611.summary: Abu Imraan reports that Abu Ayyoob Ansaari answered those who called a Muhaajir's solo charge self-destruction, explaining that the verse referred to Ansaar who wanted to stay with their families and wealth instead of fighting.

n00612.summary: Umar takes land away from Abdullaah bin Harr Anasi after he started farming in Shaam instead of jihaad, and gives it to someone else.

n00613.summary: Abdullaah bin Amr bin Al Aas tells Yemeni visitors that the man who takes over a non-Muslim farmer's land in Shaam, with its jizya, and stops jihaad has turned back, not the man who returns to serve his parents.

n00614.summary: Jaabir reports that a quarrel between a Muhaajir and an Ansaari on an expedition was defused by the Prophet, who called their tribal shouting the calls of the Period of Ignorance; Umar offered to kill Abdullaah bin Ubay, which the Prophet refused.

n00615.summary: Urwa bin Zubayr and Amr bin Thaabit report that on the Muraysee expedition the Prophet had Khaalid bin Waleed destroy the idol Manaat; Abdullaah bin Ubay's remark led Umar and Usayd bin Hudhayr to offer to kill him, which the Prophet refused, and Surah Munaafiqoon was revealed.

n00616.summary: Umar rebukes a man who had guarded the borders for thirty days, asking why he did not complete forty.

n00617.summary: Umar, patrolling Madinah, hears a woman lamenting her long-absent husband and rules that no army may be kept away from home for more than four months, after consulting his daughter Hafsa; a second chain gives the same account from Abdullaah bin Umar.

n00619.summary: Rabee bin Zaid reports that the Prophet told a Quraysh youth who avoided walking in the dust that the dust of the path of Allaah is a fragrance from Jannah.

n00620.summary: Abul Musabbih reports that Maalik bin Abdullaah Khath'ami urged Jaabir bin Abdullaah to ride; Jaabir replied loudly that he had heard the Prophet say Jahannam is forbidden for feet that become dusty in Allaah's path, and everyone dismounted.

n00621.summary: Anas reports that on a journey the fasting Companions collapsed in the heat while those not fasting pitched tents and watered the animals, and the Prophet said those not fasting had taken all the reward.

n00622.summary: A narration cited as Bukhari says the Prophet praised those not fasting on an expedition who served the fasting Companions, giving them all the reward.

n00623.summary: Abu Qilaaba reports that the Companions praised a man who recited the Qur'aan and prayed on every journey, and the Prophet said those who served his travelling needs had gained all his reward.

n00624.summary: Ahmar, the freed slave of Umm Salama, ferried people across a stream on an expedition, and the Prophet remarked that he was a ship that day.

n00625.summary: Mujaahid recounts that Abdullaah bin Umar held his stirrup and straightened his clothes on journeys, and when Mujaahid objected, Ibn Umar called him straitened in personality.

n00626.summary: Abu Dardaa says that on journeys with the Prophet in extreme heat, only the Prophet and Abdullaah bin Rawaaha fasted.

n00627.summary: Abu Sa'eed Khudri reports that on expeditions in Ramadhaan, those who fasted and those who did not each accepted the other's choice without resentment.

n00628.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports that during the Battle of Yamaamah, Abdullaah bin Makhrama, lying on the ground and fasting, asked for water to break his fast, but had died before Abdullaah bin Umar returned with it.

n00629.summary: Mudrik bin Awf reports Umar's answer to a rumour that his uncle Awf bin Abi Hayya had thrown himself into destruction: Umar said Awf had bought the Aakhirah with this world; Awf kept fasting while wounded until he died.

n00630.summary: Muhammad bin Hanafiyyah reports that Abu Amr Ansaari, fasting and parched in battle, fired three arrows after recalling the Prophet's saying that an arrow fired in Allaah's path is a light on the Day of Qiyaamah, and was martyred before sunset.

n00631.summary: Ali reports that on the night before Badr every Muslim slept except the Prophet, who prayed under a tree and wept until dawn, and that Miqdaad was the only horseman among them.

n00632.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas reports that at Usfaan the Mushrikeen under Khaalid bin Waleed failed to attack while the Prophet led the Zuhr prayer, and that the Salaatul Khawf verses were revealed between Zuhr and Asr.

n00633.summary: Jaabir reports that the Mushrikeen said a prayer was soon coming that the Muslims loved more than their children.

n00634.summary: Jaabir reports that on the expedition of Dhaatur Riqaa the Prophet appointed Ammaar bin Yaasir and Abbaad bin Bishr to guard the camp; a Mushrik shot Abbaad three times while he prayed, and Abbaad finished his prayer before waking Ammaar.

n00635.summary: Three items: Abbaad bin Bishr keeps praying while Ammaar sleeps; Heraclius asks why the Romans are being defeated and is told the Muslims pray at night and fast by day; and Hind tells Abu Sufyaan that the night worship in the Masjid was unlike anything she had seen.

n00636.summary: The Prophet sent Abdullaah bin Unays to kill Khaalid bin Sufyaan, who was mustering forces against him; Abdullaah prayed Asr while walking to him, killed him, and was given a staff as a token for the Day of Qiyaamah.

n00637.summary: Urwa reports that the Muslims at Yarmook were known for night worship and day fighting, and Hind bint Utba, once hostile, admits she had never seen Allaah worshipped as the Muslims worshipped that night.

n00638.summary: Sa'eed bin Musayyib reports that after the conquest of Makkah the Muslims recited takbeer and tahleel and made tawaaf until dawn; the Prophet repeated to Abu Sufyaan what he had said privately to Hind, and Abu Sufyaan testified to his prophethood.

n00639.summary: Abu Moosa Ash'ari reports that on the way to Khaybar the Prophet stopped the Companions from shouting takbeer in a valley, and taught him 'there is no power or might except with Allaah' as a treasure of Jannah.

n00640.summary: Jaabir reports that the Companions on the journey said takbeer when climbing an incline and tasbeeh when descending.

n00641.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar describes two kinds of people on an expedition: those who stay conscious of Allaah and spend generously, and those who lack dhikr, avoid the fighting, boast, and misappropriate the booty, and so have no share of the reward.

n00642.summary: Section heading only: 'Making Du'aa when leaving a place', with no narration.

n00643.summary: Ibn Is'haaq reports the du'aa the Prophet made when leaving Makkah for Madinah, asking Allaah for protection, companionship and steadfastness.

n00644.summary: The grandfather of Abu Marwaan Aslami reports the du'aa the Prophet made on seeing Khaybar, asking for the good of the town and protection from its evil, then ordering the Companions to advance in Allaah's name.

n00645.summary: A narration cited as Tabraani says the Prophet made this same du'aa each time he entered a town.

n00646.summary: Umar reports that at Badr the Prophet, facing many more enemies, prayed towards the Qiblah until his upper garment fell off; Abu Bakr put it back and reminded him of Allaah's promise, and Surah Anfaal 9 was revealed.

n00648.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood reports that the Prophet's du'aa at Badr, pleading on Allaah's promise, was the most persistent he had heard, and that the Prophet then said he could see where the dead Mushrikeen would fall by nightfall.

n00649.summary: Two reports: Anas says the Prophet repeatedly prayed for help at Uhud, and Abu Sa'eed Khudri says that at the Battle of the Trench the Prophet taught the Companions a du'aa after which Allaah sent a powerful wind against the enemy.

n00651.summary: Jaabir reports that at Masjid Ahzaab the Prophet stood and cursed the Mushrikeen without prayer the first time, then cursed them again and prayed two rakaahs.

n00652.summary: Three narrations: the Prophet cursed the confederate forces attacking Madinah, asking Allaah to defeat and shake them; another du'aa asks for victory; and Abu Hurayrah relates a du'aa praising Allaah as the one who alone defeated the coalition.

n00653.summary: Ali reports that during Badr he went to check on the Prophet, who was in sajdah repeatedly saying 'Yaa Hayyu, Yaa Qayyoom' and kept doing so until Allaah granted victory.

n00654.summary: Ali reports that on the night before Badr the Prophet prayed through the night for the destruction of that group, and that rain fell, making the ground firm for the Muslims and muddy for the enemy.

n00655.summary: Ali reports that although the Prophet was a traveller, he spent the whole night before Badr in worship until morning.

n00656.summary: Rifaa'ah Zuraqi relates the Prophet's long du'aa of praise after Uhud as the Sahabah stood in rows, and Abdullaah bin Abbaas explains that some should stay behind on jihaad to learn Deen.

n00657.summary: Ahwas bin Hakeem bin Umayr Absi relates Umar's letter to the army commanders urging them to gain a deep understanding of Deen.

n00658.summary: Hitaan bin Abdullaah Raqaashi relates that Abu Moosa Ash'ari stopped people from renewing their wudu without need on the march and warned that knowledge would vanish and ignorance spread.

n00659.summary: Abu Mas'ood Ansaari relates that a man donated a reined camel in the path of Allaah, and the Prophet promised him seven hundred camels in return on the Day of Qiyaamah.

n00660.summary: Abdullaah bin Saamit relates how Abu Dharr spent his whole allowance in the path of Allaah, and the Prophet's warning that unspent gold and silver becomes live coal is quoted.

n00661.summary: Qais bin Sala Ansaari says his brothers complained that he gave away too much wealth, and the Prophet told him to keep spending so that Allaah would spend on him.

n00663.summary: Several Companions relay that spending while staying at home earns seven hundred times its reward and spending on an expedition seven hundred thousand times, and the Prophet recites Surah Baqara verse 261.

n00664.summary: Abu Hurayrah relates that when a man asked about a fighter who seeks worldly gain, the Prophet said he receives no reward, and repeated this each time he was asked, three times in all.

n00665.summary: Abu Umaamah relates that the Prophet said a man who fights for fame and fortune gets nothing, and that Allaah accepts only deeds done solely for His pleasure.

n00667.summary: Abu Hurayrah names Usayram as the man who entered Jannah without a single salaah, and Mahmood bin Labeed relates how he accepted Islaam on the day of Uhud and was martyred.

n00668.summary: Abu Hurayrah relates that Amr bin Uqaysh put off Islaam until his interest-bearing loans were repaid, then fought fiercely at Uhud, and when asked by Sa'd bin Mu'aadh's messenger he said he fought for Allaah and His Rasool.

n00669.summary: Shaddaad ibnul Haad relates that a Bedouin who had followed the Prophet hoping for martyrdom was struck in the throat by an arrow exactly where he had pointed, and the Prophet led his janaazah.

n00670.summary: Anas bin Maalik relates that a dark-skinned man who asked whether fighting would take him to Jannah was martyred, and the Prophet saw two wide-eyed damsels of Jannah disputing over his body.

n00671.summary: Amr bin Al Aas says he accepted Islaam for love of Islaam and not for wealth, when the Prophet offered to send him in command of an army, and the Prophet replies that good wealth is a fine thing for a good man.

n00672.summary: Umar rebukes men who called their martyred comrades martyrs, saying every fighter is raised according to the intention he died with, and Maalik bin Aws relates the same teaching from Umar.

n00674.summary: Umar asks who the martyrs are, and when told they are those killed in battle, explains that the true martyr gives his life hoping for Allaah's reward, and defines the true Muhaajir and the true Muslim.

n00675.summary: Asmaa tells her son Abdullaah bin Zubayr that if he fights to revive the Book and Sunnah he should die upon the truth, but if he seeks worldly gain there is no good in him, alive or dead.

n00676.summary: Abu Maalik Ash'ari relates that a man left the camp without the Ameer's permission, and Abu Moosa Ash'ari rebukes him and tells him to start afresh to undo his sin.

n00677.summary: Abu Tha'laba Khushani relates that the Prophet called it Shaytaan's work when Muslims camped separately in valleys on expedition, and after that they always stayed together.

n00679.summary: Sahl bin Handhaliyya relates that at Hunayn the Prophet asked for a night guard, Anas bin Abi Marthad Ghanawi volunteered and kept watch at the ravine, and the Prophet told him he had made Jannah compulsory for himself.

n00680.summary: Abu Atiyya relates that when the Prophet was told a man had died, he asked whether anyone had seen good in him, and a Sahabi said he had stood guard with him, so the Prophet led the janaazah and testified that he was of Jannah.

n00681.summary: Abu Atiyya and Abu Aa'idh relate that when some Companions asked the Prophet not to lead a janaazah, he asked whether anyone had seen any good deed by the dead man, and Umar objected that the man was sinful.

n00682.summary: Abu Rayhaana relates that the Prophet prayed for the volunteers who guarded the camp at night and said the eye that stands guard in the path of Allaah is safe from Jahannam, and Jaabir adds that Ammaar bin Yaasir and Abbaad bin Bishr guarded the mouth of the valley.

n00683.summary: Abu Sa'eed Khudri relates that the Prophet said illness annuls sins, and Ubay bin Ka'b prayed for a fever that would never stop him from worship, and it stayed with him until his death.

n00685.summary: Jundub bin Sufyaan relates that when the Prophet's finger bled from a fall, he said it was only a finger that bled and whatever it suffered was in the path of Allaah; Anas adds the injuries the Prophet took at Uhud.

n00686.summary: Aa'isha relays Abu Bakr's account of Uhud: the Prophet told them to tend to Talha, who had over seventy wounds, and Abu Bakr said every credit for that day went to Talha.

n00687.summary: Ibraheem bin Sa'd reports that Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf sustained twenty-one wounds at Uhud, and an injury to his leg left him limping.

n00688.summary: Anas bin Maalik relates how his uncle Anas bin Nadhar, who had missed Badr, fought at Uhud until he was martyred with over eighty wounds, and how the verse of Surah Ahzaab about men like him was revealed.

n00690.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar relates that the Prophet named Zaid bin Haaritha commander at Mu'ta with Ja'far and Abdullaah bin Rawaaha as successors, and that Ja'far's body had over ninety wounds, none on his back.

n00691.summary: Amr bin Shurahbeel relates that when Sa'd bin Mu'aadh was struck by an arrow at the Battle of the Trench and his blood spilled onto the Prophet, Abu Bakr and Umar cried out in shock.

n00692.summary: Sa'eed bin Ubayd Thaqafi relates that he shot Abu Sufyaan bin Harb in the eye at Taa'if, and when Abu Sufyaan offered it as an injury in Allaah's path, the Prophet offered to pray for its return or give him Jannah, and he chose Jannah.

n00693.summary: Qataadah bin Nu'maan relates that his eye was injured at Badr, and Rifaa'ah bin Raafi relates that an arrow ruptured his eye, which the Prophet treated with his saliva and prayer, leaving no pain.

n00694.summary: Raafi bin Khadeej asks the Prophet to remove an arrow from his chest, and separately a man from Banu Abdul Ash'hal and his wounded brother join the pursuit after Uhud, with the man carrying his brother at times.

n00695.summary: Anas relates that during the battle against Musaylama, Baraa bin Maalik scaled an orchard wall and opened its gate, suffering over eighty wounds, and that Khaalid bin Waleed nursed him for a month.

n00696.summary: Is'haaq bin Abdullaah bin Abu Talha relates that when Anas was being pulled up by a burning hook at an enemy fortress in Hareeq, Baraa bin Maalik held the chain until the rope gave way, burning his hand to the bone, and Allaah saved Anas.

n00697.summary: Another narration says the hooks caught Anas and lifted him off the ground, and Baraa ran, jumped onto the wall and tugged the chain until the rope gave way, his hands burnt to the bone.

n00698.summary: Abu Hurayrah relates that the Prophet swore he would have joined every expedition if not for men he could not provide transport for, and wished to be killed in the path of Allaah and given life again, repeatedly.

n00699.summary: Abu Hurayrah narrates the Prophet's promise of reward for whoever goes out in Allaah's path, and his wish to be martyred and brought back to life again and again.

n00700.summary: Qais bin Abi Haazim narrates Umar's sermon on the palace in Jannah for prophets and siddeeqs, and Umar's wish for martyrdom.

n00701.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood says that Allaah granted Umar martyrdom at the hands of a slave of Mughiera, but the report is cut off before the rest.

n00702.summary: Aslam, a freed slave of Umar, narrates Umar's du'aa for martyrdom in Allaah's path and for his death in the city of the Prophet.

n00703.summary: Hafsa narrates Umar's prayer to be killed in Allaah's path and to die in the city of the Prophet, and his answer when she asked how that could happen.

n00704.summary: Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas narrates the du'aas he and Abdullaah bin Jahash made before Uhud, and how Abdullaah's prayer for martyrdom was answered.

n00705.summary: Sa'eed bin Musayyib narrates Abdullaah bin Jahash's prayer to meet an enemy who would kill him and mutilate him, and says he hopes Allaah will also grant the rest of that prayer.

n00706.summary: Anas reports the Prophet's words about Baraa bin Maalik, who, when the Muslims were losing at Tustar and asked him to make a vow, prayed for the enemy's shoulders and was then martyred.

n00707.summary: Baraa bin Maalik made vows at two battles, asking Allaah for the enemy's shoulders; the Muslims won at the first, and after the second, at the bridge of Sus, he was martyred.

n00708.summary: Humayd bin Abdur Rahmaan reports that Humama, who prayed to Allaah for martyrdom or death in His path, died at Isfahan in Umar's caliphate, and Abu Moosa testified that he was a martyr.

n00709.summary: A narration cited to Imaam Ahmad adds Humama's prayer and says he died of a stomach illness at Isfahan, and Abu Moosa declared him a martyr on what he had heard from the Nabi.

n00710.summary: Ma'qal bin Yasaar narrates that Umar consulted Hurmuzaan on the Persian campaign, appointed Nu'maan bin Muqarrin to lead at Isfahan, and that Nu'maan prayed for martyrdom and was the first to fall.

n00711.summary: Jubayr narrates Nu'maan bin Muqarrin's words at the Battle of Nahaawind, in which he prayed for victory for Islaam and then for martyrdom.

n00712.summary: Sulaymaan bin Bilaal narrates that Sa'd bin Khaythama and his father both wanted to go to Badr, lots sent Sa'd, and Sa'd was later martyred by Amr bin Abd Wadd.

n00713.summary: Muhammad bin Ali bin Husayn describes the single combats at Badr: Ali killed Waleed bin Utba, Hamza killed Shayba, and Ubaydah bin Haarith was mortally wounded by Utba, after which the Prophet laid his head on his lap and Ubaydah asked whether he was a martyr.

n00714.summary: Zuhri gives a second account of the Badr duels, in which Ubaydah and Utba wounded each other, Ali and Hamza finished Utba, and they brought Ubaydah to the Prophet.

n00715.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar narrates that before Uhud Umar asked his brother Zaid to take his armour, Zaid said he wanted martyrdom as much as Umar did, and the two of them left the armour behind.

n00716.summary: Sa'eed bin Mansoor reports Ali's account of searching the dead after Uhud, failing to find the Prophet, resolving to fight until he was killed, and then seeing the Prophet among the enemy.

n00718.summary: Abdullaah bin Ammaar Khatmi reports that Thaabit bin Dahdaaha called the Ansaar back at Uhud, reminding them that Allaah is living, and that he was martyred by a spear thrown by Khaalid bin Waleed.

n00719.summary: Abu Najeeh reports that a wounded Ansaari told a Muhaajir that the Prophet had delivered his message and the believers must keep fighting, and that the verse of Aal Imraan 144 was then revealed.

n00720.summary: Zaid bin Thaabit narrates that after Uhud the Prophet sent him to look for Sa'd bin Rabee, and that Sa'd, dying, sent salaams and said he could smell the fragrance of Jannah.

n00721.summary: Abdur Rahmaan bin Abu Sa'sa'a narrates that the Prophet asked who would find out about Sa'd bin Rabee, and that Sa'd sent back a message of thanks to the Prophet on behalf of himself and the Ummah.

n00722.summary: Anas bin Maalik and Jaabir describe how the Ansaar defended the Prophet at Uhud one by one until they were martyred, and how Talha alone remained at his side to hold back the enemy.

n00724.summary: Mahmood bin Labeed narrates that two elderly men, Yamaan and Thaabit bin Qais, joined the Muslim army at Uhud in secret; Thaabit was killed by the Mushrikeen and Yamaan by Muslims who did not recognise him, and Hudhayfa forgave the blood money, which raised his standing with the Prophet.

n00725.summary: A second report adds that the two old men slipped into the Muslim army to seek martyrdom, and that Hudhayfa's forgiveness of the blood money raised his standing in the eyes of the Prophet.

n00726.summary: Abu Hurayrah reports how Aasim bin Thaabit's spying party was surrounded by the Banu Lihyaan and killed, with Khubayb bin Adi and Zaid bin Dathana taken and sold in Makkah; Aasim bin Umar bin Qataadah then reports how the envoys sent to Rajee were betrayed to the Hudhayl.

n00727.summary: Aasim bin Thaabit recites couplets as he fights and is martyred; the Hudhayl then try to take his head for Sulaafa, but wasps guard his body until a flood carries it away, and Umar says Allaah protects His servant in death as in life.

n00728.summary: After the Rajee betrayal, Abdullaah bin Taariq is stoned to death at Zahraan, and Zaid bin Dathana is executed at Tan'eem, where Abu Sufyaan asks whether he would rather have the Prophet in his place and Zaid says he would not let a thorn prick the Prophet.

n00729.summary: Ibn Is'haaq narrates through Maariya and Aasim bin Umar bin Qataadah how Khubayb bin Adi was held in Makkah and then executed at Tan'eem after a last prayer; Mu'aawiya recalls his father's fear of the curse, and Moosa bin Uqba relates that the Prophet announced the martyrdom of Khubayb and Zaid bin Dathana.

n00730.summary: Urwa bin Zubayr narrates that the sons of Mushrikeen killed at Badr executed Khubayb bin Adi, who refused to swear that he would prefer the Prophet to be in his place, and recited couplets while on the cross.

n00731.summary: Further couplets of Khubayb bin Adi, given as additions to the previous report, express his fear of the fire and his readiness to die as a Muslim for Allaah's sake.

n00732.summary: Mughiera bin Abdur Rahmaan and others narrate that Abu Baraa asked the Prophet to send teachers to Najd, that Mundhir bin Amr led about seventy Sahabah there, and that Aamir bin Tufayl's men killed them at Bir Ma'oona, with only Ka'b bin Zaid surviving and Amr bin Umayyah Dhamri spared.

n00733.summary: Anas bin Maalik narrates that Haraam bin Milhaan, sent with the Prophet's letter to Aamir bin Tufayl, was stabbed from behind as he spoke to the enemy under a promise of safety, and cried out that he was successful; the Prophet then cursed the tribes responsible for thirty mornings.

n00734.summary: Another report names the man who killed Haraam bin Milhaan as Jabbaar bin Salma Kilaabi, who accepted Islaam when told that Haraam's cry meant his entry into Jannah.

n00735.summary: Urwa bin Zubayr reports that the Prophet appointed Zaid bin Haaritha, then Ja'far and then Abdullaah bin Rawaaha as commanders for Mu'ta, and that Abdullaah wept at the departure and recited couplets, fearing the crossing over Jahannam.

n00736.summary: Abdullaah bin Rawaaha recites couplets of farewell to the Prophet as the Prophet turns back after seeing off the army.

n00737.summary: At Ma'aan the Muslims learn of Heraclius's army and resolve to press on, Abdullaah bin Rawaaha urges them to fight for victory or martyrdom, and at Mu'ta Zaid bin Haaritha and then Ja'far are martyred.

n00738.summary: Urwa narrates that after Zaid's martyrdom Ja'far took up the flag, hamstrung his red horse, fought until he was martyred, and became the first Muslim to disable his mount.

n00739.summary: Zaid bin Arqam recounts that, as an orphan in Abdullaah bin Rawaaha's care on the Mu'ta journey, he wept at the couplets about dying in Shaam and was struck with a whip for it.

n00740.summary: Abbaad bin Abdullaah bin Zubayr reports, through his foster father of Banu Murrah, that Abdullaah bin Rawaaha took up the flag after Ja'far was martyred, dismounted, recited couplets, and fought on until he was martyred after throwing down the meat he was eating.

n00741.summary: Abbaad bin Abdullaah bin Zubayr reports his foster father's account of Ja'far hamstringing his red horse and fighting on while reciting couplets about Jannah.

n00742.summary: Abdur Rahmaan bin Zaid bin Khattaab narrates that his father Zaid bin Khattaab carried the flag at Yamaamah, rebuked the fleeing Muslims and fought on until he was martyred, after which Saalim, freed slave of Abu Hudhayfa, took up the flag.

n00743.summary: During the Battle of Yamaamah, Thaabit bin Qais and Saalim dug a foxhole, refused to flee and fought until they were martyred.

n00744.summary: Abbaad bin Bishr told Abu Sa'eed Khudri of his dream of martyrdom, then led four hundred Ansaar in the attack at Yamaamah and was martyred.

n00745.summary: At Yamaamah, the mortally wounded Abu Aqeel answered Ma'n bin Adi's call to the Ansaar, fought, and died after learning that Musaylama had been killed.

n00746.summary: Before the Battle of Yamaamah, Thaabit bin Qais perfumed himself for battle, refused to join the flight and was killed fighting.

n00747.summary: At Yamaamah, Thaabit bin Qais cursed the enemy and the retreating Muslims, killed a man standing on a wall and was martyred.

n00748.summary: At the Battle of Yarmook, Ikrama bin Abu Jahal dismounted and walked into the fighting against Khaalid bin Waleed's advice, and was martyred.

n00749.summary: At Yarmook, Ikrama bin Abu Jahal and about four hundred Muslims pledged to fight to the death in front of Khaalid's tent, and many of them, including Diraar, were martyred.

n00750.summary: After Yarmook, Khaalid bin Waleed tended the badly wounded Ikrama and his son Amr, and said that Allaah had blessed the Muslims with martyrs although Umar had said they would not be martyred.

n00751.summary: At Siffeen, Ammaar bin Yaasir asked Ali why he had not yet been martyred, drank the milk he had been told would be his last drink, and fought until he was martyred.

n00752.summary: Abu Sinaan Duwali saw Ammaar bin Yaasir ask for milk, drink it, and say he would soon meet the Prophet and his companions.

n00753.summary: At Siffeen, Ibraheem bin Abdur Rahmaan heard Ammaar bin Yaasir say he would meet Allaah and the damsels of Jannah, and recalled the Prophet's words that the milk would be his last provision.

n00754.summary: Anas describes his brother Baraa bin Maalik's courage, and how Baraa led a counter-attack in Persia after the Muslims retreated and was martyred there.

n00755.summary: Umar bin Khattaab said he had thought less of Uthmaan bin Madh'oon for dying a natural death, until he realised that even the best of people die naturally.

n00756.summary: Ali said that Abu Bakr was the bravest of people, having stood guard over the Prophet with a drawn sword during the Battle of Badr.

n00757.summary: Ali said that Umar bin Khattaab alone made Hijrah openly, with sword on his neck and bow on his shoulder, daring the Quraysh to stop him.

n00758.summary: After Uhud, Ali asked Faatima to take his sword and recited verses; the Prophet praised Sahal bin Hunayf, Abu Dujaana and Ibn Simma for their fighting, and Jibra'eel said Ali was from him.

n00761.summary: Amr bin Abd Wadd challenged the Muslims three times; Ali accepted despite the Prophet's caution, and after a fierce exchange killed him.

n00762.summary: After killing Amr bin Abd Wadd, Ali recited verses, returned to the Prophet, and explained to Umar why he had not taken Amr's armour.

n00763.summary: Salama bin Akwa tells of the Khaybar expedition, where Aamir was killed in a fall of his own sword, and of Marhab coming out with a challenge.

n00764.summary: Aamir accidentally wounded himself fatally with his own sword in his duel with Marhab; the Prophet gave the flag to Ali, cured his eyes with saliva, and Ali killed Marhab.

n00765.summary: Abu Raafi, in Ali's party at Khaybar, describes Ali tearing a fortress door off to use as a shield, a door that a group of eight could not turn over afterwards.

n00766.summary: Jaabir reports that Ali lifted a fortress door at Khaybar so the Muslims could climb the walls, and that later forty men could not lift it back.

n00767.summary: Three reports: Ali lifted the Khaybar door, Jaabir bin Samura gave a variant of it, and Talha recited verses at Uhud praising Zubayr's sword and defending the Prophet.

n00768.summary: Sa'eed bin Musayyib reports that Zubayr bin Awwaam was the first to draw a sword for Allaah, going out in Makkah with it when he heard the Prophet had been killed, and the Prophet prayed for him.

n00769.summary: Urwa reports that as a boy of twelve, Zubayr heard a rumour that the Prophet had been captured, drew his sword and went to find him in Makkah; the Prophet prayed for him and his sword.

n00770.summary: At Uhud, Zubayr accepted Talha Abdari's challenge, leapt onto his camel, killed him with his own sword, and was praised by the Prophet.

n00771.summary: During the Battle of Khandaq, Zubayr answered Naufal Makhzoomi's challenge and split him in two with one blow, then returned reciting verses that defend the Nabi.

n00772.summary: Asmaa bint Abu Bakr reports that at the Prophet's word Zubayr took on a mushrik who had challenged from a height, and killed him after he fell into the ditch.

n00773.summary: At Khandaq, Abdullaah bin Zubayr, a boy kept with the women and children in a fortress, describes watching his father Zubayr fight, and his father's reply.

n00774.summary: At Yarmook, Zubayr broke through the enemy alone, was wounded on both sides of his old Badr wound, and left his ten-year-old son Abdullaah in the care of a companion.

n00775.summary: When the Sahabah asked Zubayr a second time to lead an attack, he complied as he had the first time.

n00776.summary: At Raabigh, Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas defended the Muslims with arrows and was the first to shoot an arrow in the path of Allaah, recalling it in verse.

n00777.summary: Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas killed three men with one returned arrow at Uhud, and at Badr fought as effectively as a cavalryman while on foot.

n00779.summary: Hamza bin Abdil Muttalib wore ostrich feathers at Badr, and the Mushrikeen said he had carried out all the major offensives against them.

n00780.summary: Umayyah bin Khalaf asked Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf who had marked himself with ostrich feathers at Badr, and on hearing it was Hamza, said Hamza had carried out all the major offensives against them.

n00781.summary: After Uhud, the Prophet searched for Hamza, wept over his mutilated body, had a cloth laid over it, and declared him the leader of the martyrs on the Day of Qiyaamah.

n00782.summary: Wahshi tells how he killed Hamza at Uhud to win his freedom, later came to the Prophet in Madinah to accept Islaam, and at Yamaamah killed Musaylama with the same spear.

n00783.summary: A variant report of Wahshi's account: Sibaa stepped forward to challenge the Muslims, and Hamza answered and killed him.

n00784.summary: At Taa'if, Handhala bin Rabee was captured by the people of Taa'if, and Abbaas bin Abdil Muttalib, answering the Prophet's call, snatched him back despite a barrage of stones.

n00785.summary: At Badr, two young Ansaar asked Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf to point out Abu Jahal, killed him, and the Prophet gave his possessions to Mu'aadh bin Amr bin Jamooh, whose arm had been cut off in the fight.

n00786.summary: Abu Dujaana takes the Prophet's sword at Uhud on condition of fulfilling its rights and fights bravely with it, as reported by Anas and then Zubayr.

n00787.summary: Zubayr describes Abu Dujaana receiving the sword with its rights at Uhud, and how he wore a red bandanna and destroyed the enemy with the sword.

n00788.summary: Zubayr, disappointed at not getting the sword, follows Abu Dujaana, watches him kill many enemies, and sees him turn the sword away from Hind.

n00789.summary: Umar and Zubayr ask for the sword and are refused, Abu Dujaana receives it and fulfils its rights, and Ka'b bin Maalik describes him killing a Mushrik in one blow.

n00790.summary: Qataadah bin Nu'maan loses an eye shielding the Prophet's face with his own at Uhud, and the Prophet prays that the injured eye see better than the other.

n00791.summary: Qataadah bin Nu'maan reports standing in front of the Prophet at Uhud to shield his face, while Abu Dujaana shielded his back with arrows in his body.

n00792.summary: Salama bin Akwa pursues a raiding party that had taken the Prophet's camels, kills and wounds several of them, recovers the camels, and then races an Ansaari to Madinah.

n00793.summary: Abu Hadrad asks the Prophet for help with his dowry, is sent with two others to spy on the Jusham leader, kills him, and brings back the booty and the head, which pay his dowry.

n00794.summary: Khaalid bin Waleed reports that nine swords broke in his hand during the Battle of Mu'ta until only a Yemeni sword remained.

n00795.summary: Khaalid kills Hurmuz in a duel at Kaadhima, and Abu Bakr gives Khaalid Hurmuz's belongings, including a crown valued at a hundred thousand Dirhams.

n00796.summary: Abu Zinaad reports Khaalid weeping on his deathbed over his wounds, and Anas reports Baraa bin Maalik at the Battle of Yamaamah defeating Muhakkam and taking his sword.

n00797.summary: Baraa bin Maalik describes fighting Musaylama's army at Yamaamah, cutting down a large warrior and breaking his sword.

n00798.summary: At the Battle of Yamaamah, Baraa bin Maalik had himself thrown over the orchard wall, opened the gate for the Muslims, and they then killed Musaylama.

n00799.summary: Muhammad bin Seereen reports that Umar decreed Baraa bin Maalik should never be made commander of an expedition, because his fearlessness would lead others into needless danger.

n00800.summary: Abu Mihjin Thaqafi fights fiercely at Qaadisiyyah and is set free by Sa'd. In a second report from Sayf, Ammaar and Haashim are martyred fighting for Ali's army against the people of Shaam.

n00801.summary: Fragment: only the word 'Yaasir' remains, so no narration can be tagged.

n00802.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports that at the Battle of Yamaamah, Ammaar bin Yaasir called out to the Muslims not to flee from Jannah, and fought fiercely even with his ear cut.

n00803.summary: At Siffeen beside Ali, Abu Abdur Rahmaan Sulami reports Ali's raids and Ammaar's call to fight for Jannah, and that Haashim bin Utba took up the banner and fought in the valley.

n00804.summary: In another narration, Abu Abdur Rahmaan Sulami says Ammaar followed Haashim bin Utba into the valleys of Siffeen, both were martyred in the attack, and Ali's army then charged as one man.

n00805.summary: Maalik bin Abdullaah reports that at Yarmook Amr bin Ma'dikarib killed challenger after challenger, then chased the fleeing enemy and fed the people gathered in his tent.

n00806.summary: Several reports on Amr bin Ma'dikarib at Qaadisiyyah, Umar's reinforcements, and Nahaawand, where he turned defeat into victory until an injury took him at Rowdha.

n00807.summary: Abdullaah bin Zubayr refuses to submit to Yazeed, is attacked in Makkah by Hajjaaj's forces, and is martyred after refusing his mother Asmaa's advice to compromise on his Deen.

n00808.summary: Umm Salama asks why Salama bin Hishaam no longer attends the prayer with the Prophet, and learns he is shamed at home for having fled at Mu'ta.

n00809.summary: Abu Hurayrah is taunted by his cousin for having fled at Mu'ta and has no answer to give.

n00810.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar and his companions who fled at Mu'ta return to Madinah and approach the Prophet, who tells them they are those who return to fight again and that he is their base.

n00811.summary: A second report of Abdullaah bin Umar and the fleeing men, in which the Prophet reassures them that he is their base, with an added line from the narration of Aswad.

n00812.summary: A third version of the same encounter, in which the men admit they had planned to sail to a foreign land, and the Prophet tells them not to do so.

n00813.summary: Umar, hearing from Abdullaah bin Zaid of the defeat at the Bridge, reassures the fleeing Muhaajireen and Ansaar that he is their base to return to.

n00814.summary: Mu'aadh Qaari weeps over a verse on fleeing the battlefield, and Umar tells him he is the base to which he can retreat and regroup.

n00815.summary: Umar offers Sa'd bin Ubayd Qaari the chance to redeem his flight by going to Shaam, but Sa'd returns to the battlefield he fled from at Qaadisiyyah, where he is martyred.

n00816.summary: When the Prophet is not himself fighting, he hands his weapons to Usaama or to Ali to take into battle.

n00817.summary: A youth from Banu Aslam asks the Prophet for means to join Jihaad, and the Prophet sends him to an Ansaari who had prepared but fallen ill, and who gives him all he had prepared.

n00818.summary: A man whose animal died asks the Prophet for transport; the Prophet has none, and a Sahabi refers the man to someone who can help, and the Prophet says the one who points to good has the same reward.

n00819.summary: The Prophet asks the Muhaajireen and Ansaar to take on two or three poor brothers each for an expedition, and Jaabir describes sharing his mount with the men he took on.

n00820.summary: Waathila bin Asqa hires an old Ansaari's help to reach the Tabook march in exchange for his share of booty, and the Ansaari returns the camels, wanting only the reward.

n00821.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood says that providing a rope for someone going out in Allaah's path is more beloved to him than Hajj after Hajj.

n00822.summary: Awf bin Maalik hires a volunteer for an expedition for a fixed payment of three Dinaars on condition of a share of booty, and the account breaks off as he asks the Prophet about the booty.

n00823.summary: Ya'la bin Munya hired a man for an expedition for a fixed three dinaars, and the Prophet ruled that these three dinaars were all the hired man would receive.

n00824.summary: Maymoona bint Sa'd asked the Prophet whether the reward goes to the one who funds jihaad or to the one who goes out, and he said the funder is rewarded for his wealth and the one who goes out for his intention.

n00825.summary: A man brought his son to Ali bin Abi Taalib to send on an expedition in his place, and Ali said he preferred the judgement of an adult to the fighting of a youngster.

n00826.summary: Umar hires out a youth who begged for money to go on Jihaad to an Ansaari for work, and later gives him his savings and leaves the choice of going or staying to him.

n00827.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood relays the Prophet's saying that horses carry good until the Day of Qiyaamah, and that one may buy and borrow for Jihaad with trust in Allaah, paying from the booty.

n00828.summary: The Prophet walks with an expedition to Baqee Gharqad and prays for them, and Abdullaah bin Yazeed reports the words of the Prophet's farewell prayer.

n00829.summary: Hasan reports that Abu Bakr walks beside Usaama's army as it departs, refusing to let Usaama dismount, and asks that Umar be left behind with him in Madinah.

n00830.summary: Abu Bakr walks with Yazeed bin Abi Sufyaan as he sees off an army for Shaam, saying that walking in the path counts for them, and Jaabir Ru'ayni reports the same custom.

n00832.summary: Mujaahid recalls that Abdullaah bin Umar came to see off men going out in Jihaad and entrusted them to Allaah, quoting the Prophet's saying that what is entrusted to Allaah is protected.

n00833.summary: Saa'ib bin Yazeed, as a boy, went out with the people of Madinah to Thaniyyatul Wadaa to welcome the Prophet back from Tabook.

n00834.summary: Umar says the Prophet marched to Badr and to the conquest of Makkah during Ramadhaan.

n00835.summary: Umar and Ibn Abbaas report the numbers at Badr, that the Sahabah did not fast on those two Ramadhaan campaigns, and that the Prophet left Madinah on the tenth of Ramadhaan with Abu Ruhm Kulthoom as deputy.

n00837.summary: On the march to Makkah during Ramadhaan the Prophet drank water in full view at midday so that the thirsty Sahabah would follow him in breaking their fast.

n00838.summary: Ibn Abbaas reports the Prophet's ruling that a non-Mahram man and woman must not be alone together and a woman must not travel without a Mahram, and that he told a Sahabi whose wife had gone for Hajj to perform Hajj with her instead of joining an expedition.

n00839.summary: Ka'b reports that on returning from a journey in the morning the Prophet would first enter the Masjid and pray two rak'ahs.

n00840.summary: Jaabir reports that when he returned with the Prophet from a journey, the Prophet told him to enter the Masjid and pray two rak'ahs.

n00841.summary: Jaabir reports that the Prophet had a cow slaughtered for the Sahabah on the way back, and on reaching Madinah sent him to pray two rak'ahs before paying him the price of his camel.

n00842.summary: Aa'isha recounts how she was left behind on the Banu Mustaliq expedition, was brought back by Safwaan bin Mu'attal, and how slander spread through the army and Madinah, with the Prophet hearing of it and consulting Ali, Usaama and Bareerah.

n00843.summary: Aa'isha describes the revelation that confirmed her innocence, the Prophet wiping sweat from his face and giving her the good news, and his order that Mistah, Hassaan and Hamna be given the prescribed punishment.

n00844.summary: Aa'isha reports that she refused her mother's urging to thank the Prophet, that Abu Bakr stopped supporting Mistah until the verse of forgiveness was revealed, and that he then resumed his support.

n00845.summary: A woman of Banu Ghifaar went out with the Prophet to Khaybar to nurse the wounded; after she first menstruated he told her how to clean the saddle, and after the victory he gave her a necklace that she kept until her death.

n00846.summary: Humayd bin Hilaal reports that the Prophet described a woman who lost a goat and her needle on a journey, prayed to Allaah, and had both restored by the next morning.

n00847.summary: Anas reports that the Prophet dreamt of his Ummah sailing the sea in the path of Allaah, and that Ummu Haraam was promised a place in the first group; she later went on a naval expedition and died after a fall from her animal.

n00848.summary: Ummu Sulaym reports that women of the Ansaar marched with the Prophet on expeditions to give water to the sick and treat the wounded.

n00849.summary: Anas reports that Ummu Sulaym and other women of the Ansaar marched with the Prophet on expeditions to provide water and tend the wounded.

n00850.summary: Rubayyi bint Mu'awwidh reports that when women were with the Prophet on expeditions they gave water to the soldiers, treated the wounded and brought back the dead.

n00851.summary: Rubayyi bint Mu'awwidh, quoted by Bukhari, describes women fetching water and bringing back the dead and wounded, and Ummu Atiyya says she went on seven expeditions cooking and nursing.

n00853.summary: Layla Ghifaariyya reports that she went on expeditions with the Prophet to nurse the wounded.

n00854.summary: Anas saw Aa'isha and Ummu Sulaym carrying water to the wounded at Uhud; Tha'laba reports that Umar gave a cloth to Ummu Saleet, who had sewn water-skins at Uhud, rather than to Ummu Kulthoom.

n00855.summary: A grandmother of Hashraj bin Ziyaad reports that women went with the Prophet to Khaybar to weave ropes, nurse the wounded and give barley porridge, and Zuhri adds that women gave water to the fighters.

n00856.summary: Ummu Sa'd reports from Ummu Ammaara that at Uhud, when the Muslims were losing, she fought close to the Prophet, took many wounds, and struck Ibn Qami'a, who had wounded her, with her sword.

n00857.summary: Umaarah bint Ghaziyyah reports that at Uhud Ummu Ammaara killed a Mushrik horseman; Umar reports the Prophet saying he saw her fighting in his defence on every side, and Umar sends her a valuable shawl over Safiyya bint Ubayd.

n00858.summary: Hishaam, reporting from his father, says that when the Muslims were losing at Uhud Safiyya came with a spear to drive them back, and the Prophet told Zubayr to look after his mother.

n00859.summary: Safiyya bint Abdul Muttalib reports that during the Battle of the Trench she killed a Jewish man who was circling the fort where the women and children were, because Hassaan would not do it.

n00860.summary: Anas reports that at Hunayn Ummu Sulaym kept a dagger ready to stab any Mushrik who came near her, and the Prophet asked her about it and smiled, while Abu Talha laughed about it.

n00862.summary: Muhaajir reports that Asmaa bint Yazeed killed nine Romans with a tent peg at the Battle of Yarmook.

n00863.summary: Ummu Kabsha asked the Prophet for permission to join an expedition to nurse the wounded and give water; he refused, saying he feared it would become a regular practice, and told her to stay at home.

n00864.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas reports a woman's question to the Prophet about women's reward compared with men's jihaad, and his answer that obedience to a husband and fulfilling his rights equals it.

n00865.summary: Sha'bi reports that a woman gave her young son a sword to fight at Uhud, the Prophet directed the boy's attacks, and when the boy was wounded the Prophet asked if he was frightened.

n00866.summary: Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas reports that the Prophet sent his brother Umayr back from Badr as too young, that Umayr wept until he was allowed to go, and that Sa'd tied knots in Umayr's sword belt to fit him.

n00867.summary: Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas reports that his brother Umayr hid to avoid being sent back from Badr, was allowed to go after weeping, and was martyred at sixteen.

n00868.summary: Ibn Is'haaq reports Abu Bakr's sermon at the orchard of the Banu Saa'idah that two leaders for the Muslims leads to dissension, the abandonment of the Sunnah and the rise of bid'ah.

n00869.summary: Umar says two swords cannot share one sheath, and Abu Dharr, after criticising Uthmaan's four rak'ahs, quotes the Prophet's warning against disgracing rulers and the three duties owed to them.

n00870.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood urged the people to hold to unity, described coming poverty and the signs before the Last Day, and reported that the earth will bring forth its hidden treasures.

n00871.summary: Abu Dharr criticised Uthmaan for praying four rakaahs at Mina, then rebuked a man who reported it to him, saying that causing division is worse, and quoted the Prophet on not disgracing rulers.

n00873.summary: Ali says he dislikes disunity and advises people to keep the practice of the earlier caliphs; he tells Ibnul Kawwaa that the Sunnah is the Prophet's way and unity is the consensus of the truth, and Ibn Seereen says narrations from extreme groups attributed to Ali are false.

n00874.summary: Urwa bin Zubayr reports that Abu Bakr came after the Prophet's death, uncovered his face, kissed him, rejected Umar's claim that he had not died, and gave a sermon quoting the verse that Muhammad is only a Messenger.

n00875.summary: Umar exclaims that he had forgotten the Quranic verse about the Prophet's death, and Abu Bakr recites verses stating that all will die and only Allaah remains.

n00876.summary: Abu Bakr tells the people that the Prophet completed his mission, that whoever worshipped Allaah should know Allaah lives, that whoever worshipped Muhammad should know he has died, and that the Qur'aan is a light and a cure.

n00877.summary: Anas reports Umar's sermon the day after the Prophet's death urging the people to pledge to Abu Bakr, and Abu Ubaydah saying he will not step ahead of the one the Prophet made imam of salaah; a second statement by Abu Ubaydah calls Abu Bakr the second of the two in the cave.

n00878.summary: Imaam Zuhri relates from Anas that the day after the pledge in the orchard, Umar told the people he had been wrong to deny the Prophet's death, and Abu Bakr then addressed the people, asking them to obey him only while he obeys Allaah and His Rasool.

n00879.summary: Ibn Abbaas relates Umar's warning at Mina and Madinah against anyone who calls the pledge to Abu Bakr a hasty affair, and then the events of the Saqifah: the Ansaar gathered around Sa'd bin Ubaadah, Abu Bakr spoke for the Quraysh, and Umar gave his hand to Abu Bakr first, after which the people followed.

n00880.summary: Umar relates what happened at the Saqifah: the Ansaar gathered with Sa'd bin Ubaadah, Umar and Abu Bakr went to them, Abu Bakr named Umar and Abu Ubaydah, Umar gave his hand to Abu Bakr, and later reports tell of Abu Ubaydah refusing to step ahead of Abu Bakr.

n00881.summary: Uthmaan bin Affaan says Abu Bakr is the most worthy of the Khilaafah, being the second of the two and the Prophet's close companion.

n00882.summary: Abu Bakr at first declines the Khilaafah, Ali and Zubayr object to being excluded from consultation, and Umar and Khaalid bin Sa'eed dispute the pledge to Abu Bakr.
