n00883.summary: Ibn Abjar reports that after the pledge to Abu Bakr, Abu Sufyaan went to Ali and offered to fill Madinah with cavalry and infantry against him, and Ali replied that Abu Bakr was the most worthy.

n00884.summary: Murra bin Tayyib reports that Abu Sufyaan offered to fill Madinah against Abu Bakr and Ali refused, and Sakhar relates how Umar tore up the silk cloak of Khaalid bin Sa'eed and argued with him about the Khilaafah.

n00885.summary: Ummu Khaalid reports that her father Khaalid bin Sa'eed delayed his pledge to Abu Bakr for three months, then pledged, and later prayed for Umar.

n00886.summary: Aa'isha reports that Abu Bakr drew his sword to ride out to Dhu Qassah alone, and Ali stopped him by recalling the Prophet's words at Uhud.

n00887.summary: Abu Bakr tells the people he never sought the Khilaafah for ambition, returns the allegiance to them, and asks them to give it to whoever is just.

n00888.summary: After the pledge, Abu Bakr tells the people to withdraw it and choose the best of them, they affirm he is best, and he counsels them on honest income and correction of leaders.

n00889.summary: Abul Jahhaaf reports that Abu Bakr locked his door for three days after the pledge and then complained to Umar that judging was a burden, and Umar cites the Prophet's reward for a judge who errs after striving.

n00890.summary: Raafi ibn Abu Raafi relates that after the people appointed Abu Bakr as Khalifah, he confronted him about his earlier advice never to lead even two people, and Abu Bakr explained that he accepted the post to protect the Deen.

n00891.summary: A man of the family of Rabee'ah reports that Abu Bakr sat at home grieving after becoming Khalifah and blamed Umar for forcing him into it, and Umar answered with the hadith that a judge who strives earns a double reward if right and a single reward if wrong.

n00892.summary: On his deathbed Abu Bakr tells Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf his regrets, including not appointing Abu Ubaydah or Umar and not asking the Prophet about the succession.

n00893.summary: On his deathbed Abu Bakr consults Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf and Uthmaan about Umar, then has Uthmaan write Umar's name as successor.

n00894.summary: Abu Bakr dictated his will appointing Umar as successor, Uthmaan wrote and sealed it, the people pledged to Umar, and Abu Bakr prayed for them; Hasan reports that Abu Bakr first asked the people to choose and then named Umar through Uthmaan's advice.

n00895.summary: Uthmaan bin Ubaydullaah reports that Uthmaan bin Affaan named Umar in Abu Bakr's will, and Talha objects, to which Abu Bakr replies that he fears Allaah's questioning.

n00896.summary: Aa'isha reports that Abu Bakr named Umar as his successor, and when Ali and Talha question him he replies that he knows Umar best and will answer to Allaah.

n00897.summary: Zaid bin Haarith reports that Abu Bakr wanted to appoint Umar, some people objected that Umar is harsh, and Abu Bakr replies that he fears Allaah.

n00898.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports Umar's assassination by Abu Lu'lu'ah, Umar's consultation with Ibn Abbaas, his naming of six men to choose the next Khalifah, and his qualities for leadership.

n00899.summary: Ibn Sa'd reports Umar's instructions about settling his debts, his request to Aisha to be buried beside the Prophet and Abu Bakr, his six-man consultative assembly and the roles he set for his son, and Abu Bakr's last sermon naming Umar as the best to succeed him.

n00901.summary: Ibn Abbaas recounts how Umar sighed and asked whom to choose as Khalifah, mentioned Ali as a candidate and the objection that he enjoys jest, and listed the qualities a Khalifah needs.

n00903.summary: Umar asks whether he is a Khalifah or a king, and Salmaan, Ka'b and Ibn Abil Awjaa's report affirm he is a Khalifah who takes and spends rightfully.

n00905.summary: Sa'eed bin Musayyib reports Umar's first address as Khalifah, in which Umar explained his sternness as service to the Prophet and Abu Bakr and asked the people to advise and help him.

n00906.summary: Muhammad bin Zaid reports that Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf was asked by Ali, Uthmaan, Zubayr, Talha and Sa'd to speak to Umar about being more lenient, and Umar explained his fear of Allaah both for leniency and for sternness.

n00907.summary: Sha'bi reports Umar's saying that for Allaah's sake his heart had become softer than butter, and at other times harder than a stone.

n00908.summary: Ibn Abbaas reports that when Umar became Khalifah he was told some people had tried to block him because he was too harsh, and Umar praised Allaah for filling his heart with mercy for them and theirs with awe of him.

n00910.summary: Under the pressure of the Battle of the Confederates, the Prophet offers the Ghatafaan leaders a third of Madinah's produce and consults Sa'd bin Mu'aadh and Sa'd bin Ubaadah, who refuse.

n00911.summary: Abu Hurayrah reports Haarith's demand for half of Madinah's produce, the Prophet's consultation with the Sa'ds and others who refuse, and a separate report from Musaddad on Umar.

n00913.summary: Qaasim reports that Abu Bakr consulted a group of senior Muhaajireen and Ansaar on matters, and that they issued rulings in his time and in Umar's.

n00914.summary: Uyayna bin Hisn and Aqra bin Haabis ask Abu Bakr for a barren piece of land, and Umar objects that it is public property and tears up the deed.

n00915.summary: Aqra and Zabarqaan ask Abu Bakr for the kharaaj of Bahrain in return for a guarantee against apostasy, Umar refuses to witness and tears up the deed, and Talha is angered.

n00916.summary: Abdullaah bin Amr reports that Abu Bakr wrote to Amr bin al-Aas to consult people in matters of war, as the Prophet used to do, and the text cross-refers to an earlier narration about Abu Bakr consulting men of knowledge before fighting the Romans.

n00917.summary: Abu Ja'far relates that Umar asked Ali for his daughter Ummu Kulthoom in marriage, Ali agreed, and Umar told the Muhaajireen in the Masjid that he wished to become the Prophet's relative as well as his companion.

n00918.summary: Umar and Uthmaan consult Ibn Abbaas on difficult matters, and Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas and Umar praise his intelligence, while Umar also consulted women when needed.

n00919.summary: At Siraar Umar consults the Muhaajireen, Ansaar and army leaders, and they agree to send another companion as commander while Umar stays in Madinah to send reinforcements.

n00920.summary: Umar writes to Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas reinforcing him with Amr bin Ma'diyakrib and Tulayha, who are to be consulted in military matters but not given command.

n00921.summary: Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas recounts the first expedition in Islaam under Abdullaah bin Jahash, whose men attacked a Quraysh caravan against the Prophet's wishes, and the Prophet's rebuke over disunity.

n00922.summary: Shihaab Ambari reports that he set fire to the gates of Tustar when Ash'ari was struck by an arrow, and was then made Ameer over ten men of his tribe after the conquest.

n00923.summary: Umar says that when three people travel they should appoint one of them as Ameer, as the Prophet commanded.

n00924.summary: Abu Hurayrah reports that the Prophet asked each member of a large expedition to recite what Qur'aan they knew, and a young man named several surahs including Baqara.

n00925.summary: Uthmaan relates that the Prophet sent an expedition to Yemen under its youngest man, who was healed of a leg problem when the Prophet recited over him, and that the Prophet described the Qur'aan as like a bag filled with musk.

n00926.summary: Someone asked Abu Bakr why he did not give command to the veterans of Badr, and he replied that he honours them but does not want to taint them with worldly authority.

n00927.summary: Imraan bin Abdullaah reports that Ubay bin Ka'b asked Umar why he was not given command, and Umar replied that he did not want to taint his Deen.

n00928.summary: Umar writes to a group of Muslims appointing Ammaar as Ameer and Abdullaah bin Mas'ood as teacher and minister, and sends Uthmaan bin Hunayf and Hudhayfa to survey Iraq's rural areas.

n00929.summary: Sha'bi reports that Umar sought a man for a public post, passed over Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf, and agreed on Rabee bin Ziyaad Haarithi.

n00930.summary: Bishr bin Aasim, who failed to collect Zakaah for Umar, cites the Prophet's warning about public office, and Umar is alarmed until Abu Dharr confirms the warning.

n00931.summary: Anas reports that the Prophet made Miqdaad an Ameer of cavalry and asked him about command after him, and Miqdaad would accept it only from Abu Bakr; Abu Bakr refused to force Abaan bin Sa'eed and sent Alaa bin Hadhrami to Bahrain.

n00932.summary: Miqdaad bin Aswad says that after an expedition he felt others were his servants and vowed never again to command even two people, and a second report tells of an unnamed commander who said the same, and the Prophet said leaders stand at the door of oppression.

n00933.summary: Raafi Taa'i relates Abu Bakr's advice on an expedition: keep the prayers, zakaah, fasting and Hajj, and never seek command, since leaders face the longest reckoning, and Hijrah and jihaad are excellent virtues.

n00934.summary: Raafi relates that Abu Bakr and Umar were with Amr bin al-Aas's expedition to Dhaatus Salaasil, that Raafi guided them, and that Abu Bakr later told him never to lead even two people; a year later, when Abu Bakr was Khalifah, Raafi reminded him, and Abu Bakr said the Khalifah must enforce the Book of Allaah.

n00935.summary: Sa'eed bin Amr bin Sa'eed bin al-Aas says that his uncles Khaalid, Abaan and Amr refused command after the Prophet and were martyred in Shaam; Abdur Rahmaan bin Sa'eed bin Yarboo reports that Umar was angry with Abaan for returning without leave, and that Abu Bakr chose Alaa bin Hadhrami for Bahrain.

n00936.summary: Umar offers Abu Hurayrah a governorship, he refuses for fear of erring in judgement, and Umar cites Yusuf as someone who sought a post.

n00937.summary: Uthmaan asks Abdullaah bin Umar to judge between people, and Abdullaah refuses, citing a saying of the Prophet, but the report breaks off mid-quote.

n00938.summary: Uthmaan wanted Abdullaah bin Umar to act as judge and excused him from it, and Abdullaah refused, quoting the Prophet that of three kinds of judges only one reaches salvation.

n00939.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar recalls the day Ali and Mu'aawiya met at Dowmatul Jandal, when his sister Hafsa urged him to join, and Mu'aawiya asked who would risk his neck for the Khilaafah; Abdullaah chose Jannah instead.

n00940.summary: Abu Husayn reports that Mu'aawiya asked who was more worthy of the Khilaafah, and Abdullaah bin Umar began a reply about the man who struck their necks but held back for fear of losing Jannah's bounties.

n00941.summary: Ibn Shihaab reports that when Hasan bin Ali and Mu'aawiya met, Mu'aawiya asked who was worthy of the Khilaafah, and Abdullaah bin Umar held back his reply for fear of being thought ambitious.

n00942.summary: Several reports under one heading: Imraan bin Husayn refuses Khurasan and Hakam bin Amr is sent in his place, Abu Bakrah rebukes a man who mocked the Ameer, Ali relates the Prophet's ruling on obeying a commander who orders disobedience, and Umar and Alqama discuss obedience to the Ameer.

n00943.summary: Ibn Abbaas recounts how Khaalid bin Waleed and Ammaar bin Yaasir quarrelled after Ammaar granted safety to a man who had accepted Islaam, and the Prophet upheld Ammaar's amnesty but forbade granting it without the Ameer's permission.

n00944.summary: Awf bin Maalik says that after the Battle of Mu'ta a Yemeni took the spoils of a Roman he had killed, Khaalid bin Waleed kept them, and when Awf complained the Prophet ordered them returned and rebuked Khaalid for disrespecting his commanders.

n00945.summary: Raashid bin Sa'd reports that Umar raised his whip at Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas for pushing through the crowd, and Abdullaah bin Yazeed reports that Abu Bakr stopped Umar from objecting when Amr bin al-Aas forbade fires on campaign.

n00946.summary: Jubayr bin Nufayr reports that Hishaam bin Hakeem rebuked Ayaadh bin Ghanam for harshly punishing the governor of Daaraa, and Ayaadh replied that advice to a leader should be given privately, quoting the Prophet on the matter.

n00947.summary: Zaid bin Wahab reports that Hudhayfah refused to be drawn into opposing his Ameer, and Ziyaad bin Kusayb reports that Abu Bakrah rebuked Mirdaas Abu Bilaal for mocking Abdullaah bin Aamir's dress; Ali reports a commander who ordered his men into a fire, and the Prophet said obedience is only in matters of good.

n00948.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports the Prophet's teaching that obeying him is obeying Allaah, that obeying the leaders is obeying him, and that the people should pray seated if their leaders pray seated.

n00949.summary: Asmaa bint Yazeed reports that the Prophet found Abu Dharr sleeping in the Masjid and told him to follow his leaders wherever they lead, and Abu Dharr adds that he obeyed an Abyssinian slave of Uthmaan who led the prayer at Rabdha.

n00950.summary: At Rabdha, Abu Dharr found an Abyssinian slave of Uthmaan calling the adhaan who asked him to lead the prayer, and when Abu Dharr declined, saying the Prophet told him to obey even an Abyssinian slave, he prayed behind the slave.

n00951.summary: Umar says that a believer must obey a ruler even if he is an Abyssinian slave with mutilated limbs, bear his wrongs patiently, refuse any attempt to diminish the Deen, and stay with the Jamaah.

n00952.summary: Hasan reports that Alqama bin Ulaatha met Umar at night, mistook him for Khaalid bin Waleed and complained that Umar had dismissed Khaalid; the next morning Umar asked Khaalid about it, and Alqama said obedience to leaders is owed in every condition.

n00953.summary: Ibn Abi Mulaykah reports that Umar told a leprous woman to stay away from Tawaaf, and after Umar died she still refused to come out, saying it was not fitting to obey him alive and disobey him dead.

n00954.summary: Shamar reports from a former governor under Ali that Ali ordered his men to obey, warning that otherwise the Jews and Christians would overpower them.

n00955.summary: Urwa bin Zubayr relates that Umar asked Abdullaah bin Umar about sitting with rulers and then speaking differently outside, and Abdullaah says the Companions regarded this as hypocrisy in the Prophet's time.

n00956.summary: Umar tells the people that a ruler's tolerance and compassion towards his subjects is the most beloved thing to Allaah, and that a ruler's foolishness and harshness is the most detested.

n00957.summary: Anas bin Maalik relates that the senior Companions of the Prophet warned them never to speak ill of their leaders, betray them or disobey them.

n00958.summary: Urwa asks Abdullaah bin Umar about flattering leaders who rule unjustly, and Abdullaah replies that in the Prophet's time they regarded such behaviour as hypocrisy; further reports repeat the same view.

n00959.summary: Sha'bi reports that people told Abdullaah bin Umar they flatter their rulers in person and speak differently outside, and he says the Companions regarded this as hypocrisy in the Prophet's time.

n00960.summary: Alqama bin Waqqaas narrates how a man who made governors laugh was warned, with Bilaal bin Haarith's hadith on the weight of a single word.

n00961.summary: Hudhayfa warns against the doors of rulers, where a person confirms their lies and praises them falsely.

n00962.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas relates his father Abbaas's three pieces of advice on serving the ruler: fear Allaah, never lie to him, never disclose his secrets, never backbite in his presence.

n00963.summary: Sha'bi reports Abbaas's advice to his son Abdullaah about Umar: never lie to him, never disclose his secrets, never backbite about anyone in his presence.

n00964.summary: Hasan narrates that Umar refused a verse from Ubay bin Ka'b, and when Ubay said he had heard it from the Prophet, Umar admitted the truth and said there is no good in a ruler in whose presence the truth cannot be spoken.

n00965.summary: Abu Mijlaz reports that Umar accused Ubay of lying about a verse, Ubay answered that Umar's lie was worse, and then Umar confirmed Ubay had spoken the truth.

n00966.summary: Nu'maan bin Basheer reports that when Umar asked a gathering what they would do if he became permissive, Basheer bin Sa'd promised to set him straight like an arrow.

n00967.summary: Moosa bin Abu Isa reports that Muhammad bin Maslama told Umar that if he strayed they would straighten him, and Umar praised Allaah for placing him among such people.

n00968.summary: Abu Qabeel reports that Mu'aawiya declared from the pulpit that the wealth was theirs to give or withhold, and a man objected three Jumu'ahs running; Mu'aawiya then recalled the Prophet's warning about rulers who speak wrongly and were thankful to the man for waking him.

n00969.summary: Khaalid bin Hakeem bin Hizaam reports that Khaalid bin Waleed rebuked Abu Ubaydah for harshly punishing non-Muslims over the jizya, citing the Prophet's warning about the severest punishment on the Day of Qiyaamah.

n00970.summary: Hasan reports that when Ziyaad appointed Hakam bin Amr governor of Khurasan, Hakam refused Mu'aawiya's order to withhold the gold and silver and distributed the booty, and Mu'aawiya had him arrested so he died in shackles.

n00971.summary: Ataa reports that Imraan bin Husayn, sent to collect zakaah, distributed it to the needy instead of bringing it back, and Abu Khuzayma bin Thaabit reports Umar's custom of appointing governors before witnesses and holding them to account.

n00972.summary: Aswad bin Yazeed reports that Umar asked every delegation about its governor, and dismissed the governor if any answer was negative.

n00974.summary: Abdur Rahmaan bin Saabit reports that Umar appointed Sa'eed bin Aamir Jumhi to lead a regiment for jihaad, telling him it was not to whip or humiliate them but to fight and share the booty.

n00975.summary: Abu Moosa Ash'ari tells the people that Umar sent him to teach them the Book of their Lord and the Sunnah of their Nabi and to administer municipal affairs.

n00976.summary: Abu Saalih Ghifaari reports that Amr bin Al Aas offered Umar a house in Egypt, and Umar refused and turned the plot into a marketplace for the Muslims.

n00977.summary: Tameem Jayshani reports that Umar wrote to Amr bin Al Aas ordering him to demolish a pulpit from which he rose above the people's necks.

n00978.summary: Abu Uthmaan reports that Umar wrote to Utba bin Farqad that his position and wealth were not his own efforts, telling him to feed the people as he feeds himself and avoid luxury, silk and imitating the mushrikeen.

n00979.summary: Urwa bin Ruwaym reports that Umar had the lofty residence of the governor of Hims burned and made him fetch water for the camels, then told him that his short time in this world did not justify such a building.

n00980.summary: Attaab bin Rifaa'ah reports that Umar sent Muhammad bin Maslama to bring Sa'd to account for his mansion, and Abu Moosa reports that Abu Ubaydah, having been ordered to move his people away from a plague, died of it himself.

n00981.summary: Umar goes round the governors of Shaam in disguise with his slave Yarfa, finds Yazeed bin Abi Sufyaan, Amr bin Al Aas and Abu Moosa Ash'ari living in luxury and strikes each with his whip, then finds Abu Dardaa living in poverty, and the two of them remind each other of the Prophet's words in tears.

n00982.summary: Abu Saalih Ghifaari relates that Umar used to visit a blind old woman on the outskirts of Madinah at night to fetch her water and do her chores, and that he always found someone had already done it, until he caught Abu Bakr doing it.

n00983.summary: Awzaa'ee relates that Talha saw Umar going at night into houses to help a blind, crippled old woman, and Talha, on learning this, rebuked himself for having looked for faults in Umar.

n00984.summary: Abdullaah bin Utba bin Masood quotes Umar saying that after revelation ended people are judged by their outward actions, and that Allaah alone judges their inner state.

n00985.summary: Hasan reports Umar's first sermon as Khalifah, in which Umar says he is tested through the people and they through him, and promises to deal directly with those present and to appoint capable, trustworthy agents over those absent.

n00986.summary: Tawoos relates that Umar said that appointing the best man and ordering him to be just does not discharge a ruler's duty, which also requires inspecting whether the appointee actually does what he was commanded.

n00987.summary: Abdullaah bin Ka'b relates that an Ansaari regiment rebuked Umar for failing to relieve it on time, and Abu Moosa reports that Umar ordered Abu Ubaydah to leave the plague-hit land of Shaam, that Abu Ubaydah refused and then died of the plague himself.

n00988.summary: Abu Ubaydah replies to Umar's letter that he will not leave the army to save his own life, and asks to be released from his command so he can stay with his soldiers.

n00989.summary: Abu Ja'far reports that the Prophet asked Abu Usayd whether he had sold a weeping captive woman's son, and Muhammad bin Sallaam reports that Umar removed an official who had lost his mercy, saying those without mercy for their own children cannot show it to the masses.

n00990.summary: Buraydah relates that when Umar heard a girl screaming because her mother was being sold as a slave, Umar gathered the Muhaajireen and Ansaar and then ordered that the mother of no free woman be sold, because it severs family ties.

n00991.summary: Abu Uthmaan Nahdi relates that Umar dismissed a governor from Banu Asad who said he had never kissed a child, telling him that someone without mercy for his own children would show none to the public; Muhammad bin Sallaam gives a similar account.

n00992.summary: Urwa reports that when the Makhzoomiyyah woman's penalty for theft was to be waived through Usaama, the Prophet refused and had her hand cut off, saying even Faatima would be punished if she stole, and afterwards she repented and married.

n00993.summary: Abu Qataadah relates that after Hunayn he killed a mushrik and claimed the dead man's possessions, the Prophet confirmed his right to them, and he bought an orchard with them, his first wealth as a Muslim.

n00994.summary: Abdullaah bin Abu Hadrad reports that he sold his shawl and turban to a Jew to pay a four-dirham debt when the Prophet ordered him to pay, and an old woman gave him a shawl.

n00995.summary: Ummu Salama reports that the Prophet refused to judge in favour of the stronger claimant in an inheritance dispute between two Ansaar men, warning that it would be a yoke of Jahannam, and told them to divide the right and draw lots.

n00996.summary: Abu Sa'eed reports that a Bedouin harshly demanded a debt from the Prophet, and the Prophet borrowed dates from Khowia bint Qais to repay him with extra, saying a nation whose weak cannot claim their rights without hesitation has no good in it.

n00997.summary: Khowla bint Qais reports that the Prophet owed dates to a man from Banu Saa'idah, and when an Ansaari paid him inferior dates he refused, and the Prophet wept, said the nation whose weak cannot claim their rights is not blessed, and ordered the debt settled.

n00998.summary: Abdullaah bin Amr reports that Abu Bakr struck a man who entered the Zakaah camels without permission, then gave him the rein to take revenge, and when Umar intervened Abu Bakr compensated him with a camel, a carriage, a blanket and five dinaars.

n00999.summary: Sha'bi reports that Umar and Ubay bin Ka'b took a dispute to Zaid bin Thaabit, who seated Umar at the head of the bedding, which Umar rejected, and Umar then took the oath as a common Muslim would; the Ibn Asaakir version gives a date-harvest dispute.

n01000.summary: Zaid bin Aslam reports that Umar asked Abbaas to sell or give his house by the Prophet's Masjid for the expansion, and when Abbaas refused, Ubay bin Ka'b ruled that no one may be removed from his house without consent, citing the Prophet's account of Sulaymaan.

n01001.summary: Sa'eed bin Musayyib reports that Ubay bin Ka'b decided in Abbaas's favour, telling the story of Sulaymaan buying land at a price he had to accept, and Abbaas then gave the house as sadaqah for the Muslims.

n01002.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports that his brother Abdur Rahmaan and Abu Saroo'ah drank wine in Egypt, were punished by Amr bin Al Aas at his own request, and Umar later punished Abdur Rahmaan further, who died a month later from an unrelated cause.

n01003.summary: Hasan narrates that Umar sent for a woman whose husband had gone missing, and she was so frightened that she went into labour; Umar then rebuked the one responsible for the killing.

n01004.summary: Zaid bin Wahab reports that Umar was grieved when a governor's men drowned an old man who was forced into a cold river, and Umar ordered the governor to pay the blood money and leave, saying one Muslim was worth more than all his conquests.

n01005.summary: Jareer reports that Abu Moosa Ash'ari gave a man twenty lashes and shaved his head over a dispute about his share of booty, and Umar ordered that the revenge be taken in the same way, but the man forgave him for the pleasure of Allaah.

n01006.summary: Hirmaazi reports that Umar summoned Fayrooz Daylami, who slapped a Qurayshi youth in a dispute over entry, and when Umar cited the Prophet's words about Fayrooz killing the false prophet Aswad Anasi, the youth forgave him and Fayrooz gave him his sword, horse and thirty thousand.

n01007.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas reports that a slave woman whose master burned her private parts on a false accusation of fornication was freed by Umar, who lashed the master a hundred times and cited the Prophet's ruling that no retribution is taken from a master for his slave, and that anyone burned is freed.

n01008.summary: Makhool reports that Ubaadah bin Saamit struck a non-Arab Christian labourer who refused to hold his animal, and Umar ruled that Ubaadah should pay compensation instead of allowing retaliation, after Zaid bin Thaabit objected to retaliation against Umar's brother.

n01009.summary: Suwayd bin Ghafala reports that Umar, on hearing a dhimmi had been beaten by a Muslim, had Awf bin Maalik punished after learning that Awf had struck a man who raped a Muslim woman, and crucified the rapist, saying there would be no protection for such a dhimmi.

n01010.summary: Abdul Malik bin Ya'la reports that Bakr bin Shaddaah confessed to killing a Jew who had insulted a Muslim's wife, and Umar acquitted him because of the Prophet's prayer that his speech be truthful.

n01011.summary: Abu Ubaydah referred the case of a Muslim who killed a Dhimmi in Shaam to Umar, who ruled that the man be executed if killing Dhimmis was his habit, but otherwise pay four thousand Dirhams.

n01012.summary: Umar wrote to a commander forbidding his men to kill Mushrikeen who had surrendered under a promise of safety, and warned that he would punish anyone who did.

n01015.summary: Abdullaah bin Abi Hadrad Aslami reports that Umar found an old, poor Dhimmi begging, excused him from jizya and fixed an allowance for him from the treasury.

n01016.summary: Umar tells an old Dhimmi begging at the Masaajid that the state has not treated him fairly, and has an adequate allowance given to him from the public treasury.

n01017.summary: Yazeed bin Abi Maalik reports that when a Dhimmi complained that his vineyard had been ransacked, Umar found a Sahabi carrying grapes on a shield, let him go, and ordered the owner paid from the treasury.

n01018.summary: Sa'eed bin Musayyib reports that Umar ruled in favour of a Jew against a Muslim, and when the Jew praised the verdict, Umar whipped him and asked how he knew, and the Jew explained what the Torah says about judges who rule by the truth.

n01019.summary: Iyaas bin Salama relates that his father Salama, struck lightly by Umar in the marketplace, was given six hundred Dirhams by Umar for his Hajj as compensation.

n01021.summary: Naafi bin Abdul Haarith relates how Umar chased a pigeon from his shawl in a room in Makkah, the pigeon was then killed by a snake, and Umar, after asking Uthmaan and Naafi for a verdict, had a three-year-old white goat paid as compensation.

n01022.summary: Kulayb reports that Ali, dividing the booty won at Isfahan into seven shares, placed a piece of a single loaf on each share and had the commanders draw lots to decide who received their share first.

n01023.summary: The narrator, the grandfather of Isa bin Abdullaah Haashimi, reports that Ali gave an Arab woman and her freed slave equal shares of grain and forty Dirhams, and when the Arab woman protested, Ali said the Book of Allaah gives the Arabs no preference over the freed slave.

n01024.summary: Ali bin Rabee'ah reports that Ja'dah bin Hubayrah urged Ali to rule for the one dearer to him, and Ali refused, saying he judges only to please Allaah, and lightly struck Ja'dah's chest.

n01025.summary: Asbagh bin Nabaatah reports that Ali, seeing traders in the marketplace encroach on their spaces, ruled that the Muslim market is like a place of salaah and that whoever arrives first has his place for the day.

n01026.summary: In a lengthy report about Khaybar, Abdullaah bin Umar says that Abdullaah bin Rawwaaha estimated the Khaybar crop fairly each year despite Jewish complaints and bribes, telling them that his love for the Prophet and his hatred of them would not make him unjust.

n01027.summary: Haarith bin Suwayd relates that Miqdaad bin Aswad, seeing a man beaten by the Ameer for grazing his animal against orders, brought the man before the Ameer with his sword around his neck, secured the man's right to retribution, and then said he hoped to die while Islaam is dominant.

n01028.summary: Dahhaak reports that Abu Bakr, seeing a bird on a tree, wished he were a bird that eats fruit and flies off without any reckoning, and wished he had never been a human facing reckoning.

n01029.summary: Dahhaak bin Muzaahim reports that Abu Bakr envied a sparrow and a sheep, and said he wished he had been a hair on the body of a Mu'min rather than a human facing reckoning.

n01030.summary: Dahhaak reports that Umar wished he were a sheep that a family fattens and then slaughters and eats, and wished he had never been a human.

n01031.summary: Aamir bin Rabee'ah reports seeing Umar pick up a twig and wish that he had been that twig, or had never been created or been born.

n01032.summary: Umar says that if a caller from the heavens announced that everyone would enter Jannah except one person, he would fear that person was himself, and if the caller announced that everyone would enter Jahannam except one, he would wish to be that one.

n01033.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports that Umar asked Abu Moosa Ash'ari whether he would want his deeds after the Prophet's time cancelled out so that he got neither reward nor punishment; Abu Moosa declined, and Umar said he wanted only his deeds from the Prophet's time.

n01034.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas reports that after Umar was stabbed, he congratulated him on his leadership and its benefits, and Umar replied that he wished to leave office with neither reward nor sin.

n01035.summary: Another report has Ibn Abbaas tell Umar that the glad tidings of Jannah are his, given his long companionship with the Prophet and his leadership, and Umar answers that he would ransom himself with the world from the terror ahead and wishes his leadership had neither reward nor punishment.

n01036.summary: Abdullaah bin Ubayd bin Umayr reports that Umar, propped up, asked Ibn Abbaas to repeat his words and then asked him to testify to them before Allaah, and Umar was very pleased with the answer.

n01037.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar relates that Umar, in his final illness, asked to have his head placed on the ground and said he and his mother would be ruined if his Rabb did not show mercy; Miswar reports that when Umar was stabbed he said he would ransom himself from Allaah's punishment with all the gold on earth.

n01038.summary: Saa'ib bin Yazid reports that someone asked Umar whether it is better not to fear criticism or to examine oneself, and Umar replied that officials must not fear criticism in matters done for Allaah, while others should reform themselves and advise the officials.

n01039.summary: Aghar, from the Banu Maalik, reports that when Abu Bakr decided to appoint Umar as successor, he advised him to fear Allaah, to remember that his leadership will be presented before Allaah, and to keep the people's blood, wealth and honour safe.

n01040.summary: Saalim bin Abdullaah bin Umar reports Abu Bakr's parting advice on his deathbed: he had appointed Umar as successor, and he told Umar to fear Allaah, that deeds are weighed by truth and falsehood, and to beware of his own self and of people's envy.

n01041.summary: Abdur Rahmaan bin Saabit, Zaid bin Zubayd bin Haarith and Mujaahid report Abu Bakr's last advice to Umar: fear Allaah, hope in His mercy and fear His punishment, and never be deceived about deeds or give up hope in Allaah's mercy.

n01042.summary: Abdullaah bin Abu Bakr bin Muhammad bin Amr bin Hazm reports that Abu Bakr, seeing Amr bin Al Aas off to Shaam, walked beside his mount and advised him to fear Allaah, be a father to the people, guard the booty and be steadfast in battle, and keep his speech brief.

n01043.summary: Qaasim bin Muhammad reports that Abu Bakr wrote to Amr bin Al Aas and Waleed bin Uqaba, who were collecting half the Zakaah of the Qudaa'ah tribe, urging them to fear Allaah in private and in public.

n01044.summary: Muttalib bin Saa'ib bin Abu Wadaa'ah reports Abu Bakr's letter to Amr bin Al Aas about Khaalid bin Waleed, who was to reinforce him: treat him well, do not assert authority over him, and consult the others without opposing their views.

n01045.summary: Abdul Hameed bin Ja'far reports that Abu Bakr appointed Amr bin Al Aas over the Baliy, Udhra, Qudaa'ah and other Arab tribes, and told him to encourage them to wage jihaad, provide for them, and treat each tribe according to its status.

n01046.summary: Muhammad bin Ibraheem bin Haarith Taymi reports that Abu Bakr, relieving Khaalid bin Sa'eed of his post, advised Shurahbeel bin Hasanah to honour Khaalid's status and to consult Abu Ubaydah, Mu'aadh bin Jabal and Khaalid before deciding anything.

n01047.summary: Haarith bin Fadhl reports that Abu Bakr gave the flag to Yazeed bin Abu Sufyaan and appointed him over the army in Khaalid bin Sa'eed's place, then told him to honour Abu Ubaydah and Mu'aadh bin Jabal, quoting the Prophet's praise of both, and never to decide without them.

n01048.summary: Yazeed bin Abu Sufyaan reports that Abu Bakr warned him not to favour his relatives in appointments, quoting the Prophet's warning that whoever appoints someone out of love for them, or gives a brother's wealth to another out of love, incurs Allaah's curse.

n01049.summary: Umar, as parting advice to his successor, urges him to honour the early Muhaajireen, recognise the good Ansaar, treat the people of other cities and the Bedouins well, take from them only their surplus, and protect the Dhimmis.

n01050.summary: Qaasim bin Muhammad reports that Umar told his successor that many would seek to take the Khilaafah from him, that Umar himself had to struggle to hold off challengers, and that he would rather be executed than be appointed if someone stronger were known.

n01051.summary: Saalih bin Kaysaan reports that the first letter Umar wrote as Khalifah gave Abu Ubaydah command of Khaalid bin Waleed's army, with instructions to fear Allaah, not to send Muslims to destruction for booty, to scout each camp, and not to be drawn to the world.

n01052.summary: Umar sends for Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas, appoints him commander of the Iraq offensive and gives him detailed advice on sincerity, equality before Allaah and the Prophet's example.

n01053.summary: Abdul Malik bin Umayr relates Umar's advice to Utba bin Ghazwaan, sent as governor of Basrah: to fear Allaah, call people to Islaam, avoid pride, and seek only Allaah's pleasure, with Alaa bin Hadhrami and Arjafa to support him.

n01054.summary: Sha'bi relates Umar's letter to Alaa bin Hadhrami, who was to take over Bahrain from Utba bin Ghazwaan, telling him that appointments are in Allaah's hands and urging him to focus on the Aakhirah.

n01055.summary: Dabba bin Mihsin relates Umar's letter to Abu Moosa Ash'ari, warning him against luxury in clothing, food and transport, telling him to enforce the Shari'ah penalties and stay accessible to the Muslims, and warning that a corrupt governor corrupts those beneath him.

n01056.summary: Umar writes to Abu Moosa Ash'ari that leaders must not postpone their duties, should prefer the Aakhirah to this world, and should fear Allaah and study the Qur'aan.

n01057.summary: After Uthmaan was martyred, a locked box yielded his parting advice, which affirms tawheed, the Prophet's messengership and the reality of the Hereafter, followed by verses on patience.

n01058.summary: During the siege of Uthmaan's house, Ali and his supporters drive off the rebels, Ali offers to fight them, and Uthmaan refuses to let blood be shed on his account.

n01059.summary: During the siege, Abu Qataadah and a companion ask Uthmaan whom to follow, Uthmaan tells them to stay with the majority, and when Hasan and Ibn Umar offer to act for him he refuses to let blood be spilt.

n01060.summary: Abu Hurayrah says that while he was under siege with Uthmaan, a man was killed, and Uthmaan ordered him to throw down his sword, which he did.

n01061.summary: Ali's letter to his governors warns them not to stay away from the people, because distance breeds ignorance and injustice, and tells them to stay accessible and fair.

n01062.summary: Ali writes to some governors asking them to remember their own death and the Day when their actions will be shown to them.

n01063.summary: Ali appoints a man of the Thaqeef tribe as governor of Ukbara and tells him not to oppress the local people when collecting what is due, taking only what is extra.

n01064.summary: Ali tells the governor of Ukbara not to sell the people's grain or animals and not to make them stand in the sun to extract payment, since only what exceeds their needs is to be taken.

n01065.summary: Sa'eed bin Aamir advises Umar to fear Allaah, to keep his words and deeds consistent, and to judge fairly for all the Muslims under his rule.

n01066.summary: Umar tests three men who are asked to speak before a delegation; the third, Rabee bin Ziyaad, gives frank advice, and Umar appoints him under an Ash'ari commander to be watched and reported on.

n01067.summary: Abu Ubaydah and Mu'aadh write to Umar warning him about justice and about a time when people will look friendly outwardly while being enemies inside, and the letter is shown to Muhammad bin Sooqa.

n01068.summary: Umar replies to Abu Ubaydah and Mu'aadh that he cannot manage justice without Allaah's help, that the times they warn of are not theirs, and that he always wants their counsel.

n01069.summary: Abu Ubaydah, dying of the plague in Jordan, advises the Muslims to keep the salaah, fast in Ramadhaan, pay zakaah, perform Hajj and Umrah, and prepare for death; Mu'aadh leads the prayer and then addresses the people after Abu Ubaydah's death.

n01071.summary: Umar suspects his governor of Hims, Umayr bin Sa'd, of keeping public wealth and recalls him, but Umayr shows he gave the money away to the poor and lived in great poverty, so Umar wishes for more men like him.

n01072.summary: Umar asks the people of Hims about their governor Sa'eed bin Aamir, hears their complaints and his replies, and sends him a thousand dinaars, which Sa'eed gives to those in need; he explains his fainting by recalling Khubayb Ansaari's martyrdom.

n01073.summary: Tha'laba bin Abu Maalik Qurazi recounts that Abu Hurayrah, then governor of Madinah for Marwaan, joked with him in the marketplace while carrying a bundle of wood, and Tha'laba answered him.

n01074.summary: When tribesmen of Mudar arrive in poverty, the Prophet urges the people to give charity and recites Qur'aanic verses, and a generous Ansaari's gift starts a flood of giving, which the Prophet praises as a good practice.

n01075.summary: The Prophet reminds the Ansaar of their generosity in the Period of Ignorance and urges them not to hold back their wealth now that they are Muslims, and they respond by opening their orchards to all.

n01076.summary: Anas reports the Prophet's first sermon, in which he urges generosity and good character, describing generosity as a tree of Jannah and miserliness as a tree of Jahannam.

n01077.summary: A man asks the Prophet for something he cannot give; Umar objects, and an Ansaari urges the Prophet to keep giving without fear of loss, which pleases the Prophet.

n01078.summary: Jaabir reports that Umar objected when the Prophet had nothing to give, and Abdullaah bin Hudhaafa told the Prophet to keep spending; in a second report Ibn Mas'ood says the Prophet asked Bilaal why he was storing dates.

n01079.summary: Anas reports that the Prophet gave a bird to his servant, and when she kept it until the next day, he reminded her that Allaah provides each day's sustenance.

n01080.summary: When Umar asks what to do with surplus funds, Ali argues from an earlier incident, involving Abbaas's refusal to pay Zakaah and the Prophet's Sadaqah, that Umar should not change a firm conviction into a mere assumption.

n01081.summary: Umar distributes wealth and asks the people what to do with the surplus; Ali says it should be distributed as the Qur'aan prescribes, the Prophet's distribution is recalled, and Ali completes the distribution, with Talha's share being 800 dirhams.

n01082.summary: Ummu Salama and Sahl bin Sa'd report that in the Prophet's last illness he was troubled by seven dinaars he had not yet given away, and had Aa'isha send them to Ali, who gave them in charity.

n01083.summary: Aa'isha reports that during his illness the Prophet told her to give some gold in charity, and when it was still in the house he said he did not want to meet Allaah with it.

n01084.summary: Abu Dharr tells Ubaydullaah bin Abbaas that the Prophet said he would not want to die with even a qiraat of wealth left, because the Prophet desired the Aakhirah rather than this world.

n01085.summary: Abu Dharr rebukes Ka'b Ahbaar with his staff for saying that paying zakaah leaves no further duty on wealth, quoting Qur'aanic verses on giving beyond it, and Uthmaan confirms he heard the Prophet's warning about wealth.

n01086.summary: Umar recounts that when the Prophet called for charity he brought half his wealth, but Abu Bakr brought all he had, saying he left Allaah and His Rasool for his family.

n01087.summary: A man tells Uthmaan that the wealthy have outdone the poor in good deeds, and Uthmaan replies that a dirham given in hardship is better than ten thousand given in plenty.

n01088.summary: A man brings the Prophet a young she-camel beyond the one-year camel that was due from him as Zakaah, and the Prophet accepts it and prays for the man's wealth.

n01089.summary: Ubay bin Kab relates that when he was sent to collect Zakaah, a man offered a larger she-camel in place of the one-year-old male due, and the Prophet accepted it as extra charity and prayed for the man's wealth.

n01090.summary: Abdullaah bin Zubayr says that Aa'isha and Asmaa were both generous, Aa'isha by gathering things before distributing them and Asmaa by never keeping anything for the next day.

n01091.summary: Abdur Rahmaan bin Ka'b reports that Mu'aadh bin Jabal was so generous that he fell into debt, the Prophet had his property sold to repay creditors, and on his return from Yemen with wealth from Zakaah funds, Umar wanted it taken, but Abu Bakr refused and gave it to him as a gift.

n01092.summary: A second report, from an unnamed son of Ka'b bin Maalik, describes Mu'aadh bin Jabal's generosity and debts, and refers the reader back to the account already given.

n01093.summary: Jaabir reports that Mu'aadh bin Jabal's creditors demanded payment; the Prophet had his possessions handed over, the creditors recovered only part of the debt, and Mu'aadh was later sent to Yemen and met Umar in Makkah, where Umar noticed his slaves.

n01094.summary: Ibn Mas'ood reports that after the Prophet's death, Umar met Mu'aadh in Makkah; Mu'aadh had slaves from Yemen, Umar advised giving them to Abu Bakr, and Mu'aadh gave them to Abu Bakr and then freed them all.

n01095.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports that Umar was given land in Khaybar, and on the Prophet's advice made it an endowment whose proceeds go to the poor, relatives, freed slaves, the path of Allaah and guests.

n01096.summary: Umar asked Abu Moosa to buy him a slave woman, then freed her after reciting the verse on spending what one loves.

n01097.summary: Umar then frees the slave woman.

n01098.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar freed a slave woman he loved, married her to one of his freed slaves, and later kissed the son she bore.

n01099.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar freed his most beloved possession, his Roman slave woman Marjaana, after hearing the verse on spending what one loves.

n01100.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar had the freed woman married to Naafi, and she bore Naafi a child.

n01101.summary: Naafi reports that Abdullaah bin Umar gave away whatever he loved most, freed slaves who showed good deeds, and marked a beloved camel for sacrifice.

n01102.summary: Naafi reports Abdullaah bin Umar giving away a beloved camel and large sums, and freeing Naafi after Ibn Aamir's gifts troubled him.

n01103.summary: When Abdullaah bin Umar was ill at Juhfa and had only one fish, he told a poor man who came to the house to take it.

n01104.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar rejects his wife's suggestion to give a dirham to the poor man instead and insists his own wish be carried out.

n01105.summary: On the Prophet's advice, Abu Talha gave his beloved orchard of Bir Haa in charity and divided it among his relatives.

n01107.summary: Zaid bin Haaritha gave his most prized horse Shibla as charity; the Prophet gave it to Zaid's son Usaama and reassured Zaid.

n01108.summary: Abu Dharr says wealth has three partners, and sends his most beloved camel ahead to the Aakhirah as charity.

n01109.summary: A woman gave the Prophet a shawl; he wore it, and when a Sahabi asked for it he gave it, the Sahabi saying he hoped for its blessing.

n01110.summary: Sahl bin Sa'd reports that the Prophet gave away a new striped garment to a Bedouin who asked for it, and died before a replacement was finished.

n01111.summary: Abu Aqeel earned two saa of dates by a night of labour, gave one to charity, and was mocked by the hypocrites, which led to a verse being revealed.

n01112.summary: Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf gave half his wealth and an Ansaari gave the produce of a night's labour; the hypocrites mocked both until a verse was revealed.

n01113.summary: Abdullaah bin Zaid gave his orchard to the Prophet as charity; the Prophet returned it to his parents, who had depended on it, and it passed to their son after they died.

n01115.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports that a goat's head went round seven houses because each household preferred the others to itself.

n01116.summary: A man wanted another's date palm to repair his wall; Abu Dahdaa bought it with his orchard and gave it to the Prophet, who promised him palms in Jannah.

n01117.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood reports that Abu Dahdaa lent his orchard of six hundred palms to Allaah when the verse on good loans was revealed, and told his wife to leave it.

n01118.summary: Anas reports that the Prophet readily gave a man goats to draw him to Islaam, and the man urged his people to accept Islaam.

n01119.summary: Zaid bin Thaabit reports that an Arab received a written grant of land from the Prophet, accepted Islaam, and urged his tribe to do the same.

n01120.summary: Safwaan bin Umayyah accepted Islaam on the spot when the Prophet gave him the valley of livestock he had been gazing at.

n01121.summary: Asmaa tells how she calmed her blind grandfather Abu Quhaafa about her father Abu Bakr's departure for Hijrah by showing him stones under a cloth, which he took to be the money.

n01122.summary: Uthmaan pledged a hundred camels with their saddles for the Tabook expedition, then a second hundred when the Prophet urged again, and the Prophet said he need do no more optional deeds.

n01123.summary: Uthmaan pledged three hundred camels for Tabook after the Prophet urged three times, and the Prophet said no sin would harm him after that day.

n01124.summary: Abdur Rahmaan bin Samura reports that Uthmaan emptied a thousand dinaars into the Prophet's bag, and the Prophet said no later deed of Uthmaan would harm him.

n01125.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports that the Prophet asked that Uthmaan's deed not be forgotten and that Uthmaan need do no more optional deeds.

n01126.summary: Hudhayfa bin Yamaan reports that Uthmaan sent ten thousand dinaars for the expedition, and the Prophet prayed for his forgiveness and released him from optional deeds.

n01127.summary: Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf says he was present when Uthmaan brought seven hundred awqiya of gold to the Prophet for the expedition.

n01128.summary: Qataadah and Hasan report the numbers of camels and horses that Uthmaan gave for the Tabook expedition.

n01129.summary: Aa'isha heard the noise of Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf's caravan of seven hundred camels, recalled the Prophet's words about him entering Jannah, and he gave the whole caravan away.

n01130.summary: Imaam Zuhri reports Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf's large donations of money, horses and camels during the Prophet's lifetime.

n01131.summary: Another report from Zuhri says Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf donated five hundred camels in the path of Allaah.

n01132.summary: Imaam Zuhri reports Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf's large donations of money, horses and camels during the Prophet's lifetime.

n01133.summary: Abu Hizaam relates that Hakeem bin Hizaam, the most generous provider of transport for those going out in the path of Allaah, mended satchels with rags and bought two pregnant camels with supplies and money for two Bedouins who came asking for transport.

n01134.summary: Hakeem bin Hizaam sells his house to Mu'aawiya for sixty thousand Dirhams, saying he had bought it in the Period of Ignorance for a bag of wine and was giving the price away for the poor and for freeing slaves; another report gives a price of a hundred thousand.

n01135.summary: Naafi reports that Abdullaah bin Umar sold a property for two hundred camels, gave a hundred in charity, and made the riders promise not to sell them before Waadi Qura.

n01136.summary: A translator's note recalls earlier donations for Tabook by Umar, Aasim, Abbaas, Talha, Sa'd bin Ubaadah, Muhammad bin Maslama and Qais bin Sala.

n01137.summary: Aa'isha reports that the Prophet's remark about long arms meant giving in charity, and that Zaynab bint Jahash had the longest arms because she gave away what she made by hand.

n01138.summary: Aa'isha reports that Zaynab bint Jahash wove cloth for those going to battle, and that the women's jewellery filled a cloth laid before the Prophet for Tabook.

n01139.summary: Umar, resting at midday, hears a poor Bedouin woman with two children complain that the Zakaah collector Muhammad bin Maslama gave her nothing; Umar sends for him, then gives her a camel with flour and oil, and two more camels at Khaybar.

n01140.summary: Aslam reports that Umar met a young widow, daughter of Khufaaf bin Eema Ghifaari, and gave her a loaded camel with food, money and clothing, because her father had been at Hudaybiyyah and her brother had shared in the booty of a conquest.

n01141.summary: After Umar sends Sa'eed bin Aamir to replace Mu'aawiya as governor of Shaam, and then sends a thousand dinaars, Sa'eed spends it on the poor rather than on his family, and when his wife complains he stays out of the house during the day.

n01142.summary: Abdur Rahmaan bin Saabit Jumhi reports that Sa'eed bin Aamir gave his salary away in charity, told his wife the rest was a loan, and rejected a warning about his family's rights, citing the Prophet's words that the poor believers will enter Jannah seventy years before others.

n01143.summary: Naafi reports that when Abdullaah bin Umar was ill and a bunch of grapes was bought for him, he gave it to a poor man, and the grapes were bought back and given to the beggar three times before Abdullaah could eat them.

n01144.summary: Naafi tells the same grapes incident in his own words: after the beggar's third or fourth return he rebuked him, bought the grapes back himself, and Abdullaah finally ate them.

n01145.summary: After Abu Nadhra wished aloud that he could afford a sheep for Eid, Uthmaan bin Abul Aas sent him a bag of fifty Dirhams, having first asked a passer-by what he had paid for his sheep.

n01146.summary: Imaam Maalik reports that Aa'isha, fasting with only one piece of bread at home, gave it to a beggar, and that evening was sent cooked meat; a second report says she gave a single grape to a beggar and explained the Qur'aan's teaching that an atom's weight of good is seen.

n01148.summary: Amr Laythi reports that Waathila bin Asqa handed a beggar a piece of bread with a coin on it himself, and explained that walking to give forgives sins and placing the gift in the hand forgives more.

n01149.summary: Naafi says Abdullaah bin Umar had his whole household eat from one platter each night, and when a poor man called he gave away his share; if nothing was left over he went without food the next morning.

n01150.summary: Anas reports that a Bedouin pulled the Prophet's Najraan shawl so hard it marked his neck and demanded some of Allaah's wealth; the Prophet smiled and told the Sahabah to give him something.

n01151.summary: Abu Hurayrah reports that a Bedouin demanding two camels pulled the Prophet's shawl until it marked his neck; the Prophet forgave him and ordered two camels given, one loaded with barley and one with dates.

n01152.summary: Nu'maan bin Muqarrin reports that four hundred Muzaynah travellers with no provisions were fed by Umar from a room of dates that did not visibly diminish, as the Prophet had ordered.

n01153.summary: Dhukayn bin Sa'eed reports that four hundred and forty people asked the Prophet for food; Umar objected that his dates would last only his family through the summer, then obeyed the Prophet's repeated order and fed them from a heap of dates that seemed undiminished.

n01154.summary: Dhukayn reports the same dates incident, this time with four hundred people; Umar first objects, Abu Bakr tells him to listen and obey, and Umar replies that he hears and obeys.

n01155.summary: Aflah bin Katheer says Abdullaah bin Umar never refused a beggar, and that even a leper with blood-dripping fingers ate from the same plate as him.

n01156.summary: Hasan Basri reports that Abu Bakr gave his sadaqah secretly and Umar gave openly, and the Prophet said the difference between their gifts was like the difference between their words, Abu Bakr's intention being the purer.

n01157.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports that the Prophet asked who would buy the well of Roomah for the Muslim public as a sadaqah, and Uthmaan bought it and donated it.

n01158.summary: Basheer Aslami reports that the Muhaajireen disliked the water of Madinah, and that after a Ghifaari owner declined the Prophet's offer of a fountain in Jannah for his well, Uthmaan bought it, asked whether he too would receive that fountain, and donated the well.

n01159.summary: Su'daa, wife of Talha, reports that Talha gave away a hundred thousand Dirhams in one day, and that he was late to the Masjid because she had to stitch together his only garment.

n01160.summary: A cross-reference to an earlier narration: Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf gave half his wealth (four thousand Dirhams), then forty thousand Dirhams and forty thousand Dinaars in the path of Allaah.

n01161.summary: Saa'ib reports from his father Abu Lubaabah that after Allaah forgave him, Abu Lubaabah offered to give all his wealth in charity, and the Prophet said a third would suffice, which he gave.

n01162.summary: Nu'maan bin Humayd, visiting Salmaan Faarsi, sees him earn his living by buying palm leaves and making goods to sell, putting one part back into more leaves, one on his family and one in charity, and vows to continue even if Umar stops him.

n01163.summary: Abu Mas'ood reports that during a hard expedition Uthmaan bought fourteen loaded camels and sent nine to the Prophet, who raised his hands in a long prayer for him.

n01164.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas says that providing for a Muslim family's needs for a while is dearer to him than hajj after hajj, and that giving his brother a small utensil as a gift for Allaah's pleasure is dearer than spending a Dinaar in the path of Allaah.

n01165.summary: Ali says that gathering a few friends to share a Saa of food is dearer to him than going to the market to buy a slave and free him.

n01166.summary: Abdul Waahid bin Ayman reports from his father that Jaabir served his guests bread and vinegar, quoting the Prophet that vinegar is an excellent gravy and that those who look down on what is offered are destroyed.

n01167.summary: Humayd Taweel reports that when guests visited the ill Anas, he told his slave to bring something for them even if only bread, quoting the Prophet that good character leads to Jannah.

n01168.summary: Shaqeeq bin Salama reports that Salmaan Faarsi, with only bread and salt for his guests, pawned his jug to buy mint, and told a guest who had wished for mint that contentment with what Allaah provides would have saved the jug.

n01169.summary: Hamza bin Suhayb reports that Umar told Suhayb he fed too many people and was being extravagant, and Suhayb replied that the Prophet said the best people feed others and return greetings.

n01170.summary: Jaabir says the Prophet took him by the hand to one of his wives' rooms, where they shared three pieces of bread, and that the Prophet called the vinegar an excellent gravy.

n01171.summary: Abdullaah bin Salaam reports that the Prophet had Uthmaan's camel-load of flour, butter and honey cooked in a stone pot and shared it with the Sahabah, calling it khabees.

n01172.summary: Abdullaah bin Busr says the Prophet's large plate, carried by four men, was brought out after the Duha prayer; the Prophet sat squatting, calling himself a generous slave and not an arrogant tyrant, and told them to eat from the sides.

n01173.summary: Abdur Rahmaan, son of Abu Bakr, reports that when guests came, Abu Bakr sent portions of camel meat to the Prophet's wives and then fed the rest to the Muhaajireen and Ansaar.

n01174.summary: Aslam relates that Umar ordered a blind Jizya camel slaughtered, sent portions of the meat to the Prophet's wives with Hafsah's share last, and then invited the Muhaajireen and Ansaar to eat the rest.

n01175.summary: Salama bin Akwa reports that when Talha bought a well at the foot of a mountain and invited people to a meal, the Prophet called him Fayyaadh, an extremely generous man.

n01176.summary: Abu Hurayrah says Ja'far bin Abi Taalib did more for the poor than anyone, taking them home to feed them and breaking open his butter container so they could lick what remained.

n01177.summary: Suhayb reports that he prepared food for the Prophet and invited him; when the Prophet asked whether the others could come too, Suhayb agreed, and everyone ate and food was left over.

n01178.summary: Muhammad bin Qais reports that Abdullaah bin Umar never ate without a poor person with him, until his health suffered and his wife gave him a date drink; a second report in the same entry says he ate only when an orphan was at the table.

n01179.summary: Hasan reports that Abdullaah bin Umar invited an orphan to every lunch or dinner and gave an orphan the cup from his hand; Maymoon bin Mahraan reports that Ibn Umar's wife, to keep the poor from waiting on the road, sent them food with instructions, so he had no dinner that night.

n01180.summary: Abu Ja'far Qaari, serving Abdullaah bin Umar on a journey, describes how Ibn Umar invited local people to share each meal and made room for a poor black boy beside him at Juhfa.

n01181.summary: Abu Ja'far Qaari describes how Ibn Umar's travelling meals fed everyone who came to his large dish, and Ma'n reports that Ibn Umar invited the poor but not the well-off.

n01182.summary: Section title only, naming Abdullaah bin Amr bin Al Aas as one who fed people; no narration follows.

n01183.summary: Sulaymaan bin Rabee'ah reports that in Mu'aawiya's caliphate a group of Basrah Qurraa found Abdullaah bin Amr in Makkah with three hundred camels, one hundred to carry his brothers and two hundred loaded for his guests and travellers, and then met him at the Kabah.

n01184.summary: Sa'd bin Ubaadah brings the Prophet a large dish of camel brains, saying he has slaughtered forty camels to feed him, and the Prophet eats and prays for him.

n01185.summary: Anas reports that Sa'd bin Ubaadah served the Prophet dates, bread and milk, and that the Prophet then prayed for the righteous, fasting people and angels to bless Sa'd's household.

n01186.summary: Anas gives a second, brief account in which Sa'd served sesame seeds and dates to the Prophet.

n01188.summary: Abu Mas'ood Ansaari reports that Abu Shu'ayb invited the Prophet and four others to a meal, and when a fifth man came along, the Prophet let Abu Shu'ayb decide, and he welcomed him.

n01189.summary: Another narration says Abu Shu'ayb noticed the Prophet's hunger and told his slave to cook for five people.

n01190.summary: Anas reports that a tailor served the Prophet barley bread and pumpkin gravy, that the Prophet searched the plate for the pumpkin pieces, and that Anas loved pumpkin from that day on.

n01191.summary: During the digging of the Trench, Jaabir's wife cooked one saa of barley and a kid goat, and at the Prophet's word the food and bread multiplied until all the Sahabah were fed with plenty left over.

n01192.summary: Jaabir reports that when his mother cooked and asked him to invite the Prophet, the Prophet had about fifty men come in ten at a time, and all ate their fill while food remained.

n01193.summary: Anas reports that Abu Talha and Ummu Sulaym fed the Prophet and some seventy or eighty men from a few loaves of barley bread and a little butter, in batches of ten.

n01194.summary: Qais bin Abu Haazim reports that after Ash'ath returned to Islaam, Abu Bakr released his shackles and married him to his sister, and Ash'ath then slaughtered camels in the market and told the people to eat them as his waleema.

n01195.summary: Hasan bin Hakeem reports, from his mother, that Abu Barzah kept a large dish of thareed ready each morning and evening for widows, orphans and the poor.

n01196.summary: Talha bin Amr, one of the men of the Suffa, reports that after the men complained of hunger and dates burning their stomachs, the Prophet spoke of his own hardships, and that he once told a man sleeping face-down in the Masjid that this was Shaytaan's way of lying.

n01197.summary: Fudaalah Laythi relates that visitors to Madinah stayed with acquaintances or on the Suffa, and that when Companions complained about eating dates, the Prophet told them a time would come when large platters of food would be served morning and evening.

n01198.summary: Salama bin Akwa relates that after leading salaah the Prophet told the Companions each to take home as many guests as they could host, and that he himself took those who remained.

n01199.summary: Muhammad bin Seereen reports that each evening the Prophet distributed the men of the Suffa among the Companions, and that Sa'd bin Ubaadah took eighty of them home every night.

n01200.summary: Abu Hurayrah relates that the Prophet sent him to invite all the men of the Suffa, who had neither wealth nor family, and that the Prophet gave them all the Sadaqah he received and shared any gifts with them.

n01201.summary: Abu Dharr relates that each evening the men of the Suffa were taken in as guests in turn, and that when he was lying face down in the Masjid the Prophet nudged him with his foot and said that this is how Shaytaan lies.

n01202.summary: Tughfah bin Qais recounts being taken with four other men to Aa'isha, who served them meat, dates and milk, and then being nudged awake in the Masjid by the Prophet.

n01204.summary: An unnamed man of the Suffa reports that on two evenings of Ramadhaan no one came to take the group to eat, so the Prophet prayed for Allaah's grace and mercy, and a roasted goat and bread then arrived.

n01205.summary: Abdur Rahmaan bin Abu Bakr reports that his father's guests would not eat until Abu Bakr came home, that Abu Bakr scolded him and then ate with them, and that the food multiplied until all were full and more remained.

n01206.summary: Yahya bin Abdul Azeez reports that when Sa'd bin Ubaadah was away on jihaad and many guests came to the Prophet, Sa'd told his slave Nistaas that his son Qais would take provisions from the storehouse, and Qais did so, striking Nistaas and bringing a hundred wasaq.

n01207.summary: Maymoona bint Haarith reports that during a drought a Bedouin ate all the Prophet's little food, and that after he accepted Islaam he ate only a little, so the Prophet said a Kaafir eats to fill seven intestines and a Mu'min only one.

n01208.summary: Aslam reports that in the Year of Ashes Umar appointed four men to distribute food to the Bedouins camped around Madinah, counted his nightly guests as they grew to fifty thousand, and had the Bedouins sent home with transport and provisions after the rains.

n01209.summary: Firaas Daylami reports that Umar had twenty camels, sent by Amr bin Al Aas from Egypt, slaughtered each day for his table to feed those hit by the drought.

n01210.summary: Aslam reports that Umar found a woman whose hungry children were crying over a pot of water, fetched flour, fat, dates, clothing and money from the treasury, carried it to her home himself, and cooked for the family until they were full.

n01211.summary: Another report from Aslam says he went with Umar at night towards Saraar, found a woman with her children by a fire, and that the rest matches the account above.

n01212.summary: Anas reports that Ukaydir, ruler of Dowmatul Jandal, sent the Prophet a bag of sweetmeats, which he shared around, and that when Jaabir had already had a piece, the Prophet gave him another for his sisters.

n01213.summary: Hasan reports that when Ukaydir's bag of sweets came, the Prophet's household had little food, so the Prophet had it passed around the Sahabah, and told Khaalid bin Waleed, who had taken from it twice, to eat and feed his family.

n01214.summary: Abu Hurayrah reports that the Prophet gave each Companion seven dates, and that one of his own seven had no seed and was the best of them, being firm and slow to chew.

n01216.summary: Layth bin Sa'd reports that in the Year of Ashes Umar wrote to Amr bin Al Aas in Egypt for help, and Amr replied that a train of camels was on its way.

n01217.summary: Amr bin Al Aas sends so many camels that the first reaches Madinah as the last leaves Egypt, and Umar has Abdur Rahmaan bin Awf, Zubayr and Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas give every household a camel with its provisions.

n01218.summary: Aslam reports that Umar asked Zubayr to take the first camel to Najd and bring back families, and when Zubayr excused himself and another man did too, Abu Ubaydah bin Jarraah took the task and accepted a thousand dinaars from Umar only after insistence.

n01219.summary: After a captive named Jaz accepted Islaam, the Prophet sent him to Aa'isha for two shawls, and she gave him two of her own, with the narrator noting that Arab women did not expose themselves because of hijaab.

n01220.summary: Ja'far bin Muhammad reports that Umar distributed new clothing, but was distressed when Hasan and Husayn came without any because the garments were too large for them, so he had two sets sent from Yemen for them.

n01221.summary: Shafaa bint Abdullaah reports that when Umar gave Aatika bint Usayd a better shawl than hers, she objected that she had come to Islaam first and was Umar's cousin, and Umar explained he preferred Aatika as closer kin to the Prophet.

n01222.summary: Asbagh bin Nubaata reports that Ali, to spare a destitute man the humiliation of begging, had him write his request in the dirt, then gave him a set of clothing and a hundred gold coins, quoting the Prophet's saying to treat people according to their status.

n01223.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas asks a beggar whether he testifies to Allaah's oneness and fasts in Ramadhaan, then gives him a garment, quoting the Prophet that a Muslim who clothes another stays under Allaah's protection as long as a rag of it remains on him.

n01224.summary: Jaabir reports that when Qais bin Sa'd's army went hungry on an expedition, Qais slaughtered nine riding animals to feed them, and the Prophet said generosity was the hallmark of that family.

n01225.summary: Raafi bin Khadeej relates that Abu Ubaydah and Umar pleaded with Qais bin Sa'd not to slaughter more camels, but he did so to feed the army during the Expedition of Leaves, and the Prophet praised him as being from the house of generosity.

n01227.summary: Qais bin Abu Haazim reports that when Umar reached Shaam, Bilaal rebuked him that the commanders ate well while the Muslims under them were ill fed, and Umar made each commander guarantee provision for every Muslim under his command.

n01228.summary: Abdullaah Howzini relates Bilaal's account of the Prophet's finances: Bilaal borrowed on his behalf to help the destitute, a creditor pressed him, and four camels sent as a gift from Fidak let him settle every debt; the Prophet then gave away what remained rather than die with wealth in his possession.

n01229.summary: Ummu Salama describes how a bag of eight hundred dirhams reached the Prophet at night, and how he kept breaking off his salaah to think about it until he had distributed all of it at dawn.

n01230.summary: Abu Moosa relates that Alaa bin Hadhrami sent eighty thousand from Bahrain; the Prophet gave it out on a mat without counting, and when Abbaas, who had paid his own and Aqeel's ransom after Badr, asked for a share, the Prophet let him take as much as he could carry.

n01231.summary: Sahl bin Abi Hathma reports that Abu Bakr kept the public treasury unguarded because it had a lock, distributed all of it, and after his death Umar's trusted men found only a single dirham in it.

n01232.summary: Ismaa'eel bin Muhammad reports that Abu Bakr gave everyone equal shares; when Umar objected about the Badr veterans, Abu Bakr said worldly provision should be equal and the Badr veterans' superiority would show in their reward in the Aakhirah.

n01233.summary: Three further reports show Abu Bakr refusing to favour any group in distribution: virtue is rewarded by Allaah in the Aakhirah and equality suits worldly life, and he asked whether he should buy the Muhaajireen's precedence from them, while Umar's objections are recorded.

n01234.summary: Umar bin Abdullaah, freed slave of Ghafra, reports that after the Prophet's death wealth came from Bahrain; Abu Bakr paid Jaabir the handfuls the Prophet had promised him, then gave every person ten dirhams, and twenty the following year, refusing to favour the early Muhaajireen and Ansaar.

n01235.summary: Umar, as Khalifah, sets the allowances by precedence in Islaam and closeness to the Prophet, giving Badr veterans and their sons more, and answers the objections of Safiyya, Juwayriyya, Talha, Muhammad bin Abdullaah bin Jahash and his own son Abdullaah.

n01236.summary: Anas bin Maalik and Sa'eed bin Musayyib report that Umar's allowances were five thousand for the Muhaajireen, four thousand for the Ansaar and four thousand for the sons of Muhaajireen who missed Badr, and that Abdullaah bin Umar refused a share he had no right to.

n01237.summary: Zaid bin Aslam relates that Umar gave Abdullaah, son of Handhala, two thousand, more than Talha's Muhaajir cousin, because of his father Handhala's courage at Uhud; the report breaks off mid-sentence.

n01238.summary: Naashira bin Sumay Yazani reports Umar's lecture at Jaabiya: he gave the Muhaajireen of Badr the most, the Ansaar of Badr less and the Uhud fighters three thousand, gave all the Prophet's wives an equal amount after Aa'isha pointed out the Prophet treated them equally, and defended removing Khaalid bin Waleed from command, which Abu Amr bin Hafs disputed.

n01239.summary: Abu Hurayrah reports bringing Umar eight hundred thousand dirhams from Abu Moosa; Umar checked that it was lawful and stayed awake all night, then consulted the Sahabah and had a register drawn up, starting with the Prophet's family and the Banu Haashim.

n01240.summary: Jubayr bin Huwayrith reports that Umar consulted on keeping a register; after Uthmaan and Waleed bin Hishaam urged it, Umar had Aqeel, Makhrama bin Naufal and Jubayr bin Mut'im record people by status, starting with the Prophet and his kin, and then Abu Bakr's tribe and his own.

n01241.summary: Aslam reports that when Umar put his own tribe after Abu Bakr's, the Banu Adi called him the successor of Rasulullaah; Umar corrected them that he succeeded Abu Bakr, and said honour comes only through the Prophet and reward only through deeds, not lineage.

n01242.summary: Umar bin Abdullaah, freed slave of Ghafra, repeats the report of wealth from Bahrain after the Prophet's death, and Umar's Jumu'ah address answers rumours of a quick pledge after his death: he would switch to Abu Bakr's equal distribution if he lived.

n01243.summary: Hasan reports that after Umar had distributed the money, some remained, and Abbaas argued that as the uncle of the Prophet he deserved it more than the uncle of Musa, so Umar gave the rest to Abbaas.

n01244.summary: Aa'isha relates that Umar sent her a perfume container, asking permission because of the Prophet's love for her; she remarked on how many conquests Umar had made after the Prophet and prayed not to live to see his next gift.

n01245.summary: Anas bin Maalik relates that Abu Bakr had sent him to collect zakaah, Abu Bakr died before he returned, and Umar let him keep the four thousand collected, making him the richest person in Madinah.

n01246.summary: Abdullaah bin Ubayd bin Umayr relates that Umar gave a wounded man four thousand dirhams in four instalments; when the man left embarrassed, Umar said he would have kept giving until nothing was left, because of the scar from his wound in the path of Allaah.

n01247.summary: Ali distributes the wealth from Isfahaan three times a year and, announcing that he is not their treasurer, gives away everything, even the ropes that held the animals.

n01248.summary: Sa'eed narrates that Umar ordered the treasurer Abdullaah bin Arqam to distribute the Baytul Maal monthly, then weekly, then daily, and rejected a suggestion to keep a reserve as Shaytaan speaking, saying he would follow the Prophet's preparation of obedience to Allaah and His Rasool.

n01249.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports that when wealth from Iraq arrived, Umar refused a suggestion to hold a reserve for future emergencies, saying he would not disobey Allaah today for tomorrow's dangers and would prepare for the Muslims as the Prophet had.

n01250.summary: Salamah bin Sa'eed reports that when Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf urged keeping a reserve, Umar said the idea came from Shaytaan, quoted the verse promising a way out for the one who has taqwa, and warned that Shaytaan's words would become a test for later generations.

n01251.summary: Hasan narrates that Umar wrote to Abu Moosa Ash'ari that he wished a day would come when the Baytul Maal was empty, so that Allaah would know he had given every person his right.

n01252.summary: Hasan reports that Umar wrote to Hudhayfah to pay everyone his dues; Hudhayfah replied that a large sum still remained, and Umar ordered it distributed, saying it was the people's property and belonged neither to him nor his family.

n01253.summary: Ali bin Rabee'ah Waalibi reports that when Ibn Nabbaaj told Ali the Baytul Maal was full of gold and silver, Ali distributed all of it to the people of Kufa and then prayed two rakaahs in the emptied treasury; Mujamma Taymi adds that Ali swept it and prayed there, hoping it would testify for him.

n01254.summary: Mu'aadh bin Alaa reports that Ali had received only one date container as his share and distributed the whole Baytul Maal; Antara Shaybaani reports Ali collecting from artisans and refusing to keep anything overnight; Abu Ubayd, through Antara, reports Qambar's hidden gold dish, which Ali weighed out and gave away.

n01255.summary: Aslam reports Umar's consultation on who should receive the wealth, quoting the Qur'anic verses on the booty of the villages and the rights of the Muhaajireen and Ansaar.

n01256.summary: Umar says the wealth belongs to more than those first named, including those who come after, citing the verse of prayer for the brothers who preceded them in Imaan.

n01257.summary: Umar says there is no Muslim, even a shepherd in Aden, who has no right to the wealth.

n01258.summary: Maalik bin Aws bin Hadathaan reports that Umar recited the verses on the recipients of zakaah and on the one-fifth share of spoils, and concluded that zakaah is reserved for those groups.

n01259.summary: Umar recites the verses on the booty of the villages and on the Muhaajireen and Ansaar, and says the verse covers every Muslim, so each will receive his right even if he is a shepherd in the upper reaches of Yemen.

n01260.summary: Su'da relates that Talha was distressed by wealth he did not know what to do with, so she advised him to give it to his family and tribe, and his treasurer later said the sum came to four hundred thousand.

n01261.summary: Hasan reports that Talha sold a piece of land for seven hundred thousand, stayed awake all night for fear of dying before giving it away, and distributed all of it at dawn.

n01262.summary: Su'da reports again that Talha was distressed over the accumulated wealth, distributed four hundred thousand to his family and tribe on her advice, and was given the title Talha Fayyaadh, the Very Generous.

n01263.summary: Sa'eed bin Abdul Azeez reports that Zubayr had a thousand slaves who earned for him, and he gave the earnings away every night so that nothing was left when he returned home.

n01264.summary: Mugheeth bin Sumay reports that although Zubayr's thousand slaves earned for him, not one dirham of their earnings entered his house, because he gave all of it to the needy.

n01265.summary: Zubayr asked his son Abdullaah to sell his property to clear his debts, and Abdullaah repaid them by selling land at Ghaabah before distributing the inheritance after four Hajj seasons of announcements.

n01266.summary: Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf sold a property for forty thousand Dinaars and gave the money away, and when Aa'isha heard of it she recalled the Prophet's words about his wives.

n01268.summary: Umar sent four hundred Dinaars first to Abu Ubaydah and then to Mu'aadh bin Jabal to see what they would do with it, and both gave the whole sum to the needy.

n01269.summary: Umar wished for men like Abu Ubaydah, Mu'aadh and Hudhayfah to employ in Allaah's service, and when he tested them with money, each gave all of it away.
