n01270.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar gave away twenty thousand Dinaars during one gathering, and also spent a hundred thousand sent to him by Mu'aawiya within a single year.

n01271.summary: After receiving large sums, Abdullaah bin Umar had given it all away, and a visitor saw him buying fodder on credit for one Dirham, which his slave confirmed.

n01272.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar gave away about twenty thousand the moment he received it, borrowed to pay a latecomer, and was defended against the charge that he was a miser.

n01273.summary: After returning from Makkah, Ash'ath bin Qais gave every person at his mosque clothing, shoes and five hundred Dirhams, and a man from outside the locality also received a gift.

n01274.summary: Aa'isha gave away a hundred thousand that was brought to her while she was fasting, and when reminded she could have bought meat to break her fast, she said she would have if she had been told.

n01275.summary: Umar sent a bag of Dirhams to Sauda, who asked what they were and then gave the whole amount to the poor.

n01276.summary: Umar sent Zaynab her share of surplus wealth, and after she objected that he gave allowances only to weaned children, he fixed an allowance for every Muslim child at birth.

n01277.summary: Muhammad bin Ka'b relates that Zaynab bint Jahash, given a surplus share of twelve thousand, gave it all to her family and to the needy, and that Umar sent her another thousand, which she also gave away.

n01278.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar relates that Umar, on night watch with Abdur Rahmaan bin Awf, rebuked a mother whose crying baby kept him awake, learned the child was not yet weaned, and then ordered allowances for every Muslim child born so that mothers would not hurry weaning.

n01279.summary: Umar said he treated public funds as the wealth of orphans, taking from it only when he had to and only as much as he spent from his own earnings.

n01280.summary: Umar borrowed from the public treasurer when short of money and repaid it from his share of the surplus, even when the treasurer had to press him for payment.

n01281.summary: Umar, while trading as Khalifah, refused Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf's suggestion that he borrow from the public treasury and preferred a private loan, so that it could be repaid from his estate if he died.

n01282.summary: When Umar was ill and prescribed honey kept in the public treasury, he asked the people's permission to use it, saying it would otherwise be forbidden to him, and they gave it.

n01283.summary: Umar refused his daughter Hafsah's request that relatives receive a share of public money, saying his relatives had a right only in his own wealth.

n01284.summary: Abdullaah bin Arqam asked Umar to review jewels and silver from Jaloola, and Umar prayed against the pull of worldly wealth before refusing his young son Abdur Rahmaan's request for a ring.

n01285.summary: When musk and ambergris arrived from Bahrain, Umar declined his wife Aatika's offer to weigh it for distribution, fearing she might take a share for herself.

n01286.summary: Umar saw a weak little girl and, on learning she was Abdullaah's daughter, told him he must earn to provide for his children, since he did not spend on her.

n01287.summary: After Umar had supported his newly married son Aasim from the public treasury for a month, he stopped and told him to sell produce from his orchard and go into partnership with a trader instead.

n01288.summary: A Roman empress sent Umar's wife a bottle filled with gems in return for perfume, and Umar sold the gems, gave his wife one Dinaar and deposited the rest in the public treasury.

n01289.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar bought a camel and pastured it with public funds, and when Umar saw it fattened for sale he told him to return the profit to the Baytul Maal and keep only his capital.

n01290.summary: When an in-law of Umar asked for money from the public treasury, Umar rebuked him, and later gave him ten thousand Dirhams from his own money.

n01291.summary: Ali, shivering in a shawl at Khowrnaq, refused to take anything from the state's wealth and said he had brought the shawl from his house in Madinah.

n01292.summary: Allaah offered the Prophet the choice of being a prophet-king or a prophet-servant, and after Jibra'eel signalled humility he chose to be a servant and never ate reclining again until his death.

n01293.summary: On Mount Safa the Prophet said his family had had no food that evening, and when offered treasures and mountains of gold he again chose to be a servant-prophet out of humility.

n01294.summary: The Prophet declined his Lord's offer to turn the rocky plains of Makkah into gold, preferring to eat one day and be hungry the next so that he could be humble, thankful and remember Allaah.

n01295.summary: Ali reports that the Prophet declined an offer from his Lord to turn the plains of Makkah into gold, preferring to eat one day and be hungry the next so that he could thank and beg from Allaah.

n01296.summary: After a Mushrik was killed at the Battle of Ahzaab, the Mushrikeen offered payment for his body, and the Prophet refused the money, saying both the body and the money were worthless.

n01297.summary: Hakeem bin Hizaam bought a suit of Dhu Yazan's clothing in Yemen and presented it to the Prophet, who refused it because he does not accept gifts from Mushrikeen.

n01298.summary: Hakeem bin Hizaam relates that he bought Dhu Yazan's clothing to give to the Prophet, who refused it as a gift but accepted to pay for it, and the Prophet then gave it to Usaama bin Zaid, who wore it.

n01299.summary: Aamir bin Tufayl relates that Aamir bin Maalik, the Spear Juggler, sent the Prophet a horse with a request for a remedy; the Prophet declined the horse, sent him honey, and refused a gift from a mushrik who would not accept Islaam.

n01300.summary: Ayaadh bin Himaar presented a camel to the Prophet as a gift, and when the Prophet found he was not a Muslim he refused it, saying he had been forbidden to accept gifts from Mushrikeen.

n01301.summary: Abu Bakr, who feared his Khilaafah allowance might not be permissible, accepted one fixed by consultation, and on his deathbed had the eight thousand Dirhams he used returned to the Baytul Maal.

n01302.summary: On his deathbed Abu Bakr asked Aa'isha to return an orchard he had given her to his estate and to send his few belongings to Umar, and Umar refused to return them even when Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf advised it.

n01303.summary: Ataa bin Yasaar reports that Umar returned a gift the Prophet had sent him, and the report breaks off as the Prophet asks why.

n01304.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar relates that Abu Moosa sent a silk mat as a gift to Aatika bint Zaid, Umar's wife, and that Umar struck her over the head with it when she showed it to him, then had Abu Moosa brought and struck him with the mat, saying they had no need of gifts sent to his wives.

n01305.summary: Layth bin Sa'd relates that Maqoqis offered Amr bin Al Aas seventy thousand Dinaars for the foot of Muqattam hill, and that Umar forbade the sale because a tree of Jannah is reserved for the believers there, so Muslims should be buried there.

n01306.summary: In the Year of Ashes Umar sent Abu Ubaydah a thousand Dinaars for his work, and when Abu Ubaydah refused, Umar cited the Prophet's instruction not to refuse such payment, and he accepted.

n01307.summary: Umar offered Sa'eed bin Aamir a thousand Dinaars, which he refused, and Umar explained the Prophet's teaching to accept wealth that comes without asking or craving, so Sa'eed accepted it.

n01308.summary: Umar offered Sa'eed bin Aamir bin Hudhaym, a governor in Shaam, ten thousand Dirhams, which he refused because he had enough wealth and wanted to serve the Muslims freely.

n01309.summary: Abdullaah bin Sa'di refused pay for his public services, and Umar explained that the Prophet had taught him to keep or give away what came without asking, so he urged Abdullaah to take payment.

n01310.summary: After the Battle of Hunayn the Prophet told Hakeem bin Hizaam that wealth taken with a generous heart is blessed, and Hakeem then refused all payment from anyone, including Abu Bakr and Umar, until his death.

n01311.summary: Hakeem bin Hizaam refused the money and gifts offered by Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthmaan and Mu'aawiya, each until that ruler's death.

n01312.summary: Section heading only: Aamir bin Rabee'ah refuses land.

n01313.summary: Aamir bin Rabee'ah refuses a valley of land offered by an Arab guest, citing the revealed verse about the Day of Qiyaamah drawing near.

n01314.summary: Abu Dharr asks Uthmaan's leave to live in Rabdha and refuses the zakaah animals offered him, then rebukes Ka'b for praising a rich man's spending; a second report has him refuse money sent for his needs.

n01315.summary: Habeeb bin Maslamah sends Abu Dharr three hundred dinars, and Abu Dharr sends them back, saying he fears owning anything beyond his needs.

n01316.summary: A Quraysh man living in Shaam sends Abu Dharr three hundred dinars, and Abu Dharr refuses, quoting the Prophet on begging.

n01317.summary: The Prophet warns Abu Raafi not to give all his wealth away and to keep some for his son; later, poor, Abu Raafi refuses charity, and once wealthy he regrets his riches.

n01318.summary: Mu'aawiya sends a hundred thousand dirhams to Abdur Rahmaan bin Abu Bakr after he refused to pledge allegiance to Yazeed; he refuses the money and dies in Makkah.

n01319.summary: Mu'aawiya asks Amr bin Al Aas to find out whether Abdullaah bin Umar would fight over the Khilaafah; Amr offers him land and wealth for his allegiance, and Abdullaah refuses, saying his Deen is not for worldly wealth.

n01320.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar, who had agreed a kitaabah contract with his slave, refuses money the slave had earned by begging and frees him for Allaah's pleasure, letting him keep the money.

n01321.summary: A chief in Iraq asks Abdullaah bin Ja'far to intercede with Ali for a need; after Ali grants it, the chief sends forty thousand dirhams, which Abdullaah returns, saying they do not sell their good deeds.

n01322.summary: Uthmaan appoints Abdullaah bin Arqam treasurer of the Baytul Maal and pays him a large remuneration, which he refuses, saying he did the work for Allaah's pleasure.

n01323.summary: During Ramadhaan, Amr bin Nu'maan bin Muqarrin refuses a bag of dirhams sent by Mus'ab bin Zubayr, saying he does not recite the Qur'aan for worldly profit, and sends it back.

n01324.summary: Asmaa bint Abi Bakr refuses gifts from her non-Muslim mother until Allaah revealed the verse permitting kind dealings with such relatives; the Prophet told her to accept the gifts and welcome her mother.

n01325.summary: Aa'isha refuses a poor woman's gift out of pity, and the Prophet tells her to accept it, return something in exchange, and humble herself.

n01326.summary: Abu Sa'eed Khudri, in poverty, is sent by his wife to ask the Prophet for help; the Prophet says Allaah grants independence to whoever asks Him for it, so he returns without asking, and the world later comes to them.

n01327.summary: Abu Sa'eed Khudri, starving with a stone tied to his belly, goes to the Prophet on another's advice; the Prophet says he prefers those who do not depend on others, so Abu Sa'eed returns without asking and Allaah later provides abundantly.

n01328.summary: Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf gives up asking the Prophet for a promised share; Thowbaan pledges to ask no one for anything, and Abu Umaamah reports how Thowbaan would not even ask for his fallen whip.

n01329.summary: Abu Bakr would strike his camel to make it kneel so he could pick up its fallen rein himself, because the Prophet had told him never to ask people for anything.

n01330.summary: Eight years after Uhud, the Prophet bade farewell to the living and the dead from the pulpit, said he could see the Fountain of Kowthar, and feared the Ummah would compete for worldly things rather than revert to shirk.

n01331.summary: Uqba bin Aamir relates a second version: the Prophet prayed the janaazah for the Uhud martyrs, said he could see his fountain and had been given the keys to the treasures of the earth, and feared worldly competition more than shirk.

n01332.summary: The Prophet, pleased that Abu Ubaydah has returned from Bahrain with wealth, tells the Ansaar he fears the world will be spread before them and destroy them as it did earlier peoples.

n01333.summary: Abu Dharr reports that when a Bedouin complained of drought, the Prophet said he feared the worldly wealth that would be poured on his Ummah, and wished they would not wear gold.

n01334.summary: Abu Sa'eed Khudri reports the Prophet, speaking from the pulpit, saying he feared the splendour and wealth the world would open up to them.

n01335.summary: Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas reports the Prophet's saying that he feared prosperity for them more than hardship, because the world is sweet and tempting.

n01336.summary: Awf bin Maalik reports the Prophet's warning that conquests over Rome and Persia will bring worldly wealth that diverts from the straight path.

n01337.summary: Umar weeps while inspecting the booty from Qaadisiyyah, saying such wealth brings enmity and hatred to a nation; Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf asks why, as it is a day of joy.

n01339.summary: Hasan Basri reports that Umar placed Kisra's crown and bracelets before the people, gave the bracelets to Suraaqa bin Maalik, and prayed that this wealth would not be a trap for him.

n01340.summary: Abu Sinaan Duwali finds Umar weeping over a ring his son had taken into his mouth, because he heard the Prophet say that worldly wealth opened to a nation brings enmity until the Day of Qiyaamah.

n01341.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports that Umar, after finding the public money stacked before him, asked Uthmaan and him to share it out, and wept, wishing to leave the Khilaafah with a clean record. A second report has Umar giving him gold to distribute and weeping at the test it represents.

n01343.summary: Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf finds Umar crying among stacked bags of money and consoles him; they agree to distribute the money, four thousand each to the Prophet's wives and two thousand to everyone else.

n01344.summary: Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf, served food after fasting, weeps because Mus'ab bin Umayr and Hamza were martyred and shrouded in cloth too small for them, while worldly wealth has now been spread before him.

n01345.summary: Naufal bin Ayaadh reports that Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf, served bread and meat at his home, wept because the Prophet and his family never filled their bellies even with barley bread.

n01346.summary: Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf asks Umm Salama whether his great wealth will destroy him; she tells him to spend it in charity, and when Umar asks whether he is among the companions the Prophet mentioned, she refuses to say.

n01347.summary: Some Sahabah visit Khabbaab during his illness and tell him he will meet Muhammad at the pond; he points to his house and asks how that is possible, given the Prophet's words that a person needs only a traveller's provisions.

n01348.summary: Sahabah visit the ill Khabbaab and say he will soon meet his brothers; he weeps, fearing that their rewards were kept for the Aakhirah while he has received worldly wealth.

n01349.summary: During his illness, after seven brandings, Khabbaab says he would wish for death if the Prophet had not forbidden it, but fears the forty thousand dirhams in his house will keep him from meeting the Prophet.

n01350.summary: Khabbaab recalls having no dirhams when he was with the Prophet and now having forty thousand beside his room; when his shroud is brought he weeps, noting that Hamza had only a small sheet.

n01351.summary: On his final illness Khabbaab weeps over eighty thousand dirhams, fearing his companions died poor while he has wealth, and says he wishes the world were like dung; other reports tell of Mus'ab's small shroud and the Prophet's instruction to cover the feet with idhkhir grass.

n01352.summary: Salmaan Faarsi tells a man of the Banu Abs that the treasures now in Muslim hands are a worry, recalling that in the Prophet's time the Sahabah began their mornings with nothing and the Prophet never filled his belly for three days.

n01353.summary: Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas visits the dying Salmaan Faarsi, who weeps and gives advice to fear Allaah in judgement, in distribution and in intentions.

n01354.summary: In Salmaan Faarsi's last illness Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas asks why he weeps; Salmaan says he fears he broke the Prophet's instruction to own only a traveller's provision, gives Sa'd advice, and leaves an estate of about twenty Dirhams.

n01355.summary: On his deathbed Salmaan Faarsi is uneasy because he had more than a traveller's provision; his estate is valued at about fifteen Dirhams, and the reports on its value differ.

n01356.summary: Mu'aawiya visits Abu Haashim bin Utba as he weeps on his deathbed; Abu Haashim says he failed to keep the Prophet's advice to own only a servant and a conveyance, and his estate is valued at thirty Dirhams.

n01357.summary: Abu Ubaydah bin Jarraah weeps, fearing that his house full of servants and animals means he cannot face the Prophet, who said the dearest person to him is the one who meets him in the state he left him.

n01358.summary: Heading only: the section title on the abstinence of the Prophet and the Sahabah. No narration follows.

n01359.summary: Umar tells Ibn Abbaas how he found the Prophet on a straw mat that had marked his side, with only a handful of barley and some leaves in the room; the Prophet consoles him that the others have the world and the Muslims have the Aakhirah.

n01361.summary: Aa'isha says the Prophet returned a woollen bedding that an Ansaari woman sent, saying that if he wished, Allaah would make mountains of gold and silver travel with him.

n01363.summary: Ummu Ayman makes the Prophet bread from refined flour; he asks her to put it back and knead the coarse flour he was used to.

n01364.summary: Salma, wife of Abu Raafi, serves Hasan bin Ali, Abdullaah bin Ja'far and Abdullaah bin Abbaas coarse barley bread with olive oil and chillies, the food the Prophet liked.

n01365.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports that the Prophet, four days without food, ate dates from the ground in an Ansaari orchard, and warns of a time when people will store provisions and their trust in Allaah will be weak; a verse about provision for animals is revealed.

n01366.summary: Aa'isha says the Prophet refused a cup of milk mixed with honey as excess, saying he fears being questioned about worldly luxury on the Day of Qiyaamah and that he humbles himself before Allaah.

n01367.summary: Zaid bin Arqam reports that Abu Bakr wept when offered honeyed water, because he had seen the Prophet repel the world, and feared that the world would take hold of him and that he might oppose the Prophet's way.

n01368.summary: A second version of the same incident: Abu Bakr weeps twice when offered honeyed water, and says the world told the Prophet that those after him would not escape it.

n01369.summary: Aa'isha says Abu Bakr left no dinar or dirham and gave all his money to the Baytul Maal; a second report says he deposited all his money on becoming Khalifah, since public affairs left him no time to trade.

n01370.summary: When Abu Bakr became Khalifah and went to the market, Umar stopped him, and Abu Ubaydah set his allowance from the Baytul Maal: the average of a Muhaajir's, a set of clothing for each season, and half a goat a day.

n01371.summary: Humayd bin Hilaal reports that the Sahabah agreed Abu Bakr should receive two shawls, a travelling animal and household expenses from the Baytul Maal as Khalifah, and he was happy with it.

n01372.summary: Umar finds Abu Bakr's allowance hard to live on; Zubayr suggests raising it, Uthmaan advises first asking Hafsa, who reports Umar's anger, and Umar explains that the Prophet's and Abu Bakr's frugality is his model.

n01373.summary: Hasan Basri reports a gathering in Basrah where Ahnaf bin Qais says Umar shunned them for wearing Persian cloth until they changed, then welcomed them and shared the booty; the Sahabah then asked Ali, Hafsa and Aa'isha to ask Umar to dress and eat better, and Umar answered with the Prophet's frugal life.

n01374.summary: Hafsa, Ibn Mutee and Abdullaah bin Umar urge Umar to eat good food for strength; he replies that he will keep to the route his two companions, the Prophet and Abu Bakr, took.

n01375.summary: Abu Umaamah bin Sahl reports that Umar took nothing from the Baytul Maal until poverty set in; he consults the Sahabah, Uthmaan and Sa'eed bin Zaid advise a sum that lets him feed others, and Ali advises enough for morning and evening meals, which Umar accepts.

n01376.summary: Qataadah reports Umar saying he could have the best food and clothing but prefers to keep his luxuries for the Aakhirah; on reaching Shaam and seeing rich food, Umar weeps for the poor Muslims who die hungry and are in Jannah.

n01377.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports Umar refusing to eat meat with butter at his house, because the Prophet ate only one and gave the other away; Abu Haazim reports Umar refusing Hafsa's two gravies, saying he will not eat them until he meets Allaah.

n01378.summary: Anas and Saa'ib bin Yazeed report that Umar as Khalifah ate inferior dates and dry bread and meat, wiping his hands on his feet; a report through Thaabit and Deenowri adds that Umar told Jaarood to wipe his hands on his sleeve.

n01379.summary: Abdur Rahmaan bin Abu Layla reports that Umar, seeing Iraqis eat little of his plain food, rebuked them with the Ahqaaf verse about luxuries used up in worldly life; Umar also rebuked Hafs bin Abul Aas, who would not eat the plain food, saying he could have refined meals made if he wished.

n01381.summary: Saalim bin Abdullaah reports Umar saying they could easily have refined food and drink but prefer to keep their luxuries for the Aakhirah, citing the Ahqaaf verse about good things used up in the world.

n01382.summary: Abu Moosa Ash'ari reports that Umar, when a Basrah delegation ate with him, rejected luxuries and quoted the Ahqaaf verse; when the delegates asked for food from the Baytul Maal, Umar granted two goats and two bags of flour a day, warning that a town which takes that daily will be ruined.

n01384.summary: Hasan reports that when Umar was thirsty and offered honey mixed in water, he refused it, fearing he would be questioned about it on the Day of Qiyaamah.

n01385.summary: Another report: Umar, offered water mixed with honey, calls it excellent but refuses it, citing the Ahqaaf verse about good things used up in worldly life.

n01386.summary: Urwa reports that when Umar's upper garment tore on a long journey, the priest mended it and made a new one; Umar gave the new one back and wore the mended garment, saying it better absorbs sweat.

n01387.summary: Qataadah reports that Umar as Khalifah wore a patched woollen robe with leather patches, carried a whip to correct people in the marketplace, and picked up stray thread and date stones to throw into people's yards.

n01388.summary: Hasan and Anas report Umar's clothing: he gave a lecture wearing a lower garment with twelve patches, and Anas saw a garment with three patches between the shoulders.

n01389.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports that Umar took from the Baytul Maal only what his family needed, plus one set of summer clothing, and patched rather than replaced; Muhammad bin Ibraheem reports that Umar's daily allowance was two Dirhams.

n01390.summary: Abdul Malik bin Shaddaad saw Uthmaan on the pulpit in a plain garment; Hasan says Uthmaan slept in the Masjid and got up with the mark of a straw mat on his side; Shurahbeel bin Muslim says Uthmaan fed guests royally but ate only vinegar and oil at home.

n01392.summary: A man of the Thaqeef tribe reports that Ali, when he appointed him governor of Ukbara, ate barley flour mixed with water from a sealed bag; A'mash reports that Ali fed guests well but ate only food brought from Madinah.

n01393.summary: Abdullaah bin Shareek reports from his grandfather that when Faalooda was served to Ali, Ali said he did not want to grow used to something he was not accustomed to.

n01394.summary: Zaid bin Wahab reports that Ali (RA) wore a plain lower garment tied with a strip of cloth to keep away pride, and said he had bought a coarse garment for five dirhams.

n01395.summary: Mujammi bin Sam'aan Taymi reports that Ali (RA) took his sword to the market to sell it, saying he would never sell it if he had four dirhams to buy a lower garment.

n01396.summary: Ali (RA) is reported riding a donkey and saying he holds the world in contempt, and separately the Prophet ﷺ wept on seeing Mus'ab bin Umayr wearing a patched shawl.

n01397.summary: Abdullaah bin Razeen relates that when they visited Ali on Eid al-Adha and Ali served them a dish of meat and bran, Ali said he heard the Prophet say a Khalifah may take only two dishes from public funds, one for himself and his family and one for guests.

n01398.summary: Urwa reports that Umar found Abu Ubaydah sleeping on a saddle blanket with his mount's satchel as a pillow, and Ma'mar reports that when Umar reached Shaam he embraced Abu Ubaydah and found nothing in his house but a sword, a shield and his mount.

n01399.summary: The text is only the word 'Umayr' from a split section heading about Mus'ab bin Umayr's abstinence, and contains no narration.

n01400.summary: Ali relates that, starving on a cold winter morning, he drew water from a Jew's well for dates, and that the Prophet wept on seeing Mus'ab bin Umayr in a patched shawl, telling the Companions they were better off than they would be in future times of plenty.

n01401.summary: Umar (RA) reports that the Prophet ﷺ praised Mus'ab bin Umayr, who came in a sheepskin after giving up a pampered life for the love of Allaah.

n01402.summary: Zubayr (RA) reports that the Prophet ﷺ praised Mus'ab bin Umayr for leaving a wealthy upbringing for Allaah, foretold wealth from conquests over Persia and Rome, and warned against being at ease with this world.

n01403.summary: Khabbaab (RA) reports that all Mus'ab bin Umayr left behind was a sheet too small to cover his whole body at burial, so the Prophet ﷺ had his head covered and his feet covered with Idhkhir grass.

n01404.summary: Ibn Shihaab reports that Uthmaan bin Madh'oon entered the Masjid in a shawl patched with leather, and the Prophet ﷺ wept and foretold a time of plenty, saying their present state was better.

n01405.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) reports that the Prophet ﷺ wept over the body of Uthmaan bin Madh'oon, told the Sahabah to stop weeping, and said he had left the world owning nothing from it.

n01406.summary: The Prophet ﷺ prays for Uthmaan bin Madh'oon, saying that he neither took from this world nor did the world take from him.

n01407.summary: No narration: the text is only the word 'Faarsi', a fragment of a heading about Hadhrat Salmaan Faarsi.

n01408.summary: Atiyya bin Aamir reports seeing Salmaan Faarsi (RA) refuse more food, quoting the Prophet ﷺ that the most full in this world will be the most hungry in the Aakhirah.

n01409.summary: Hasan reports that Salmaan Faarsi (RA), governor of about thirty thousand Muslims, gave away his whole allowance and earned his living by weaving palm-fibre baskets.

n01410.summary: A'mash reports that Hudhayfah offered to build Salmaan Faarsi a room just big enough to lie down and stand in, and Salmaan said it was as if Hudhayfah lived in his heart.

n01411.summary: Maalik bin Anas reports that Salmaan Faarsi (RA) sat in the shade, and when a man offered to build him a room, Salmaan approved the plan of a room the size of his body.

n01412.summary: No narration: the text is only the word 'Ghifaari', a fragment of a heading about Abu Dharr Ghifaari.

n01413.summary: Abu Asmaa reports that Abu Dharr (RA), living in Rabdha, refused advice to move to Iraq, because the Prophet ﷺ had said light loads cross the slippery Siraat bridge more easily.

n01414.summary: Abdullaah bin Khiraash reports that Abu Dharr (RA), sitting on coarse sackcloth with his wife, thanked Allaah for taking his children to the Aakhirah and preferred a humbling wife to a proud one.

n01415.summary: Abu Dharr and Abu Dardaa (RA) both give up worldly comfort for the Aakhirah: Abu Dardaa gives his guests' bedding away as charity, and Umar (RA) finds him sleeping on sand with a flimsy shawl.

n01416.summary: Abu Dardaa relates that he was a trader before the Prophet announced his mission, and that after the announcement he gave up trade because he could not combine it with worship.

n01417.summary: Abu Dardaa says he would not want a shop at the Masjid door that earns forty Dinaars, all of which he gives in charity, because he fears the intensity of the reckoning.

n01418.summary: Abu Dardaa says he would take no pleasure in trading at the Masjid door for three hundred Dinaars of profit, and three further reports show him giving his bedding away and telling his guests that they are heading for a permanent abode in the Aakhirah.

n01419.summary: This entry is a cross-reference that repeats, in abridged and garbled form, the earlier account of Umar finding Abu Dardaa's unlocked, dark room bare and the two of them reminding each other of the Prophet's words.

n01420.summary: Aflah reports that Umar (RA) sent Mu'aadh bin Afraa (RA) fine clothing, which he sold to buy and free five slaves, and when Umar sent plainer clothing instead, Mu'aadh asked again for the best Umar gave others.

n01421.summary: Jalaaj (RA) says that since accepting Islaam at the Prophet's ﷺ hands he has never filled his belly and eats only enough to sustain him; a report from Bayhaqi gives his lifespan as 120 years.

n01422.summary: Hamza bin Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) reports that Abdullaah bin Umar, though he had plenty of food, would not eat to his fill while anyone he had not yet invited was present, and told a visitor he had not eaten his fill for eighty years.

n01423.summary: Umar bin Hamza reports that his father Hamza asked about a conversation a man had with Abdullaah bin Umar, in which the man urged him to eat better and Abdullaah said he had not filled his belly for eighty years.

n01424.summary: Ubaydullaah bin Adi, a freed slave of Abdullaah bin Umar, reports bringing him a digestive preparation called Jawaarish, which Abdullaah refused because he had not filled his belly for forty years.

n01425.summary: Muhammad bin Seereen reports that when Abdullaah bin Umar was offered Jawaarish, he said he had not eaten his fill for four months, not for lack of food but because he lived as the Prophet ﷺ and the Sahabah did, sometimes eating and sometimes going hungry.

n01426.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) says that since the Prophet ﷺ was taken away he has never laid a brick on a brick or planted a single date palm.

n01427.summary: Jaabir (RA) and Suddi say that Abdullaah bin Umar alone kept the state the Prophet ﷺ left them in, and Hudhayfah (RA) says he would rather his family had no food than have worldly wealth, quoting the Prophet ﷺ that Allaah guards the believer from it.

n01428.summary: Aa'isha (RA) reports that the Prophet ﷺ rebuked her for eating two full meals in one day, asking whether she cared for nothing but her stomach and calling it extravagance.

n01429.summary: Aa'isha (RA) reports weeping at the Prophet's ﷺ deathbed, and he told her that to meet him in the Aakhirah she should live on a traveller's provisions and never mix with the affluent.

n01430.summary: Urwa (RA) reports that Aa'isha (RA) patched her clothes until the patches overlapped and gave away the eighty thousand dirhams Mu'aawiya (RA) sent her by evening, after the Prophet ﷺ had advised mending clothes before replacing them.

n01431.summary: Abu Juhayfah (RA) reports that the Prophet ﷺ told him not to belch in front of others after a heavy meal, warning that those who fill themselves most in this world will suffer most hunger on Qiyaamah, after which he never ate to fill again.

n01432.summary: Ja'da reports that the Prophet pointed at a man with a large stomach and said the food would have been better in a poor person's stomach.

n01434.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports that Umar saw a dirham in Jaabir's hand, asked what it was for, and rebuked him for buying meat out of craving.

n01435.summary: Hasan reports that Umar (RA) rebuked his son Abdullaah for eating meat merely because he craved it, saying that eating whatever one craves is enough to make a person extravagant.

n01436.summary: Sa'eed bin Jubayr reports that Umar (RA), told that Yazeed bin Abu Sufyaan ate many kinds of meat, went to his evening meal, ate beside him, and warned that opposing the Prophet's ﷺ way leads away from the highest Jannah.

n01437.summary: Hasan reports that Umar (RA), passing a rubbish dump while his companions recoiled from the smell, said this is the world people aspire to and rely upon.

n01438.summary: Salma bin Kulthoom reports that when Abu Dardaa (RA) built a tall building in Damascus, Umar (RA) wrote from Madinah rebuking him for building like the Persians and Romans, because the Companions must set an example to others.

n01439.summary: Raashid bin Sa'd reports that when Umar (RA) heard Abu Dardaa (RA) had built porches at house entrances in Hims, he wrote calling him a little builder and asking whether the decorations of the Romans and Persians were not enough for him.

n01440.summary: Umar (RA) adds to his letter that the decorations of the Romans and Persians should be enough and orders the recipient to move from Hims to Damascus at once, which Sufyaan says was a form of punishment.

n01441.summary: Yazeed bin Abi Habeeb reports that Umar (RA) ordered Amr bin Al Aas (RA) to demolish the double-storey house Khaarijah bin Hudhaafah built in Egypt, because it would let him spy on his neighbours.

n01442.summary: Abdullaah Roomi reports that Ummu Talq (RA) kept her roof low, citing Umar bin Khattaab's instruction to his governors not to build tall buildings, because the worst days come when people do.

n01443.summary: Sufyaan bin Uyayna reports that Umar (RA) told Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas, governor of Kufa, to build only what shields him from sun and rain because this world is only a place to make do with, and the report is cut off as Umar writes to Amr bin Al Aas.

n01444.summary: Umar rebukes a man who built with baked bricks, warning that people like Fir'oun could appear in this Ummah.

n01445.summary: Saalim bin Abdullaah bin Umar recounts how Abu Ayyoob rebuked his father Abdullaah for decorating the walls at Saalim's wedding, and refused to enter the house or eat there.

n01447.summary: Hasan reports that Salmaan Faarsi visited Abu Bakr on his deathbed for advice, and Abu Bakr said Allaah will open the world, so no one should take more than he needs.

n01448.summary: Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf visits the dying Abu Bakr, who warns that worldly wealth is coming and that being executed is better for a person than drowning in the intoxication of this world.

n01449.summary: Amr bin Al Aas rebukes his companions for craving the world the Prophet avoided, saying the Prophet never had more than he owed.

n01450.summary: Amr bin Al Aas says the Prophet never went three days without his debts exceeding his dues, and contrasts the Prophet's abstinence with the Companions' desire for the world.

n01451.summary: When his son asked for a new garment, Abdullaah bin Umar told him to cut off the torn part and wear the rest, and warned against living only for food and clothing.

n01452.summary: Abu Dharr rebukes Abu Dardaa for building a house, saying he is loading boulders onto people's necks, and says he would have preferred to see him tending his family's waste.

n01453.summary: Aa'isha wore a new garment and Abu Bakr warned that Allaah dislikes a servant who admires himself for worldly beauty, so she gave the garment away as sadaqah.

n01454.summary: Habeeb bin Hamzah reports that Abu Bakr's son kept looking at his pillow when dying, and that five or six dinars were found beneath it, which Abu Bakr said his skin could not withstand.

n01455.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood built a house, and Ammaar told him that a sturdy house with long hopes meant death was near.

n01456.summary: Ataa reports that Abu Sa'eed Khudri, invited to a waleema with many dishes, reminded the host that the Prophet did not combine a big morning meal with a big dinner.

n01457.summary: Abu Ubaydah bin Jarraah kills his father during the Battle of Badr after he kept confronting him, and Allaah reveals the verse that believers do not befriend those who oppose Allaah and His Rasool, even their fathers.

n01458.summary: Maalik bin Umayr reports two men who fought or left their fathers in battle, and the Prophet stayed silent; Abu Hurayrah reports that Abdullaah bin Ubay's son offered to bring his father's head, and the Prophet refused.

n01459.summary: Abdullaah, son of Abdullaah bin Ubay, asks the Prophet for permission to execute his father, and the Prophet refuses, choosing to be lenient with him while he remains among the Muslims.

n01460.summary: Usaama bin Zaid reports that Abdullaah, son of Abdullaah bin Ubay, drew his sword before his father and vowed not to sheathe it until his father called the Prophet honourable; the Prophet was pleased with his act.

n01461.summary: Urwa reports that Handhala, son of Abu Aamir, and Abdullaah, son of Abdullaah bin Ubay, both asked the Prophet to let them execute their fathers, and he refused.

n01462.summary: Abdur Rahmaan bin Abu Bakr tells his father he avoided him at Uhud, and Abu Bakr says he would have attacked him; later, when the still non-Muslim Abdur Rahmaan challenged for a duel, Abu Bakr stood up to accept and the Prophet held him back.

n01463.summary: Umar tells Sa'eed bin Al Aas that he did not kill Sa'eed's father, who was struck down by Ali after Umar turned away, and Sa'eed replies that his father was on falsehood; Umar is greatly pleased.

n01464.summary: Aa'isha reports that the Prophet spoke to the Mushrikeen dragged into a well after Badr, and Abu Hudhayfah grieved over his father Utba being dragged there; the Prophet made dua for him.

n01465.summary: Nubay bin Wahab reports the Prophet ordered Badr captives treated well; Abu Azeez, Mus'ab's captive brother, recounts that the Ansaar gave him bread, and that Mus'ab told his captor to bind him tightly because his mother would pay a ransom.

n01466.summary: Ayyoob bin Nu'maan reports the same episode: Mus'ab asked Muhriz to bind Abu Azeez tightly for ransom, Abu Azeez protested, and his mother then paid four thousand dirhams.

n01467.summary: Zuhri reports that Abu Sufyaan, before accepting Islaam, asked the Prophet to extend the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah and was refused; he then sat down on the Prophet's bedding, and his daughter Ummu Habeebah rolled it up.

n01468.summary: Ummu Habeebah adds that she did not want her father to sit on the Prophet's bedding.

n01469.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood says he would rather dust the sand from his sons' graves than see a sparrow's egg fall from its nest, and that he would rather his family die and he follow them than see the sparrow die.

n01470.summary: Umar, disagreeing with Abu Bakr about the Badr prisoners, asks that Aqeel be handed to Ali and Abbaas to Hamza for execution, so Allaah would know the Muslims have no love for the Mushrikeen; the passage ends with an author's note on the Ansaar.

n01471.summary: Abdullaah bin Abu Bakr reports that Sa'd bin Mu'aadh offered to build the Prophet a shelter at Badr so he could stay safe, and the Prophet praised him and prayed for him.

n01472.summary: Aa'isha reports a man who feared he would not see the Prophet in Jannah; Allaah revealed Nisaa verse 69, promising companionship with the prophets, the truthful, the martyrs and the righteous.

n01473.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas reports a man who loved the Prophet and feared he would be on a lower level in Jannah; Allaah revealed Nisaa verse 69, and the Prophet recited it to him.

n01474.summary: Anas reports that a man asked when Qiyaamah would come and said he had prepared only his love for Allaah and His Rasool; the Prophet told him he would be with those he loves, and Anas says he loves the Prophet, Abu Bakr and Umar.

n01475.summary: A man from the desert asks when Qiyaamah will come and says he loves Allaah and His Rasool; the Prophet tells him he will be with those he loves, and Anas says the Companions were overjoyed. A Tirmidhi report adds a similar exchange.

n01476.summary: Abu Dharr asks the Prophet about a man who loves a people but cannot do their deeds; the Prophet tells Abu Dharr he will be with those he loves, and Abu Dharr says he loves Allaah and His Rasool.

n01477.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas reports that Ali earned dates for the hungry Prophet by drawing water for a Jewish man; the Prophet told him that love for Allaah brings hardship. Talha then dies before the Prophet arrives, and the Prophet prays that he be smiling when he meets Allaah.

n01478.summary: Ka'b bin Ujrah, hungry and having earned dates by watering a Jew's camel, brings them to the Prophet, who tells him that poverty comes swiftly to one who loves him and that he should prepare patience for trials.

n01479.summary: Husayn bin Wahwah reports that Talha bin Baraa's love for the Prophet was so great that he was ready to obey even an order to kill his father, and that the Prophet prayed for Talha after his death.

n01480.summary: Talha bin Miskeen reports that Talha bin Baraa pledged to the Prophet only after being told Islaam does not require severing ties with parents; Talha later fell ill and died, and the Prophet prayed for him.

n01481.summary: Zuhri reports that someone complained to the Prophet about Abdullaah bin Hudhaafa's jokes and useless talk, and the Prophet told them to leave him because his heart loves Allaah and His Rasool.

n01482.summary: Adra reports that a man reciting Qur'aan loudly at night was called a show-off, and the Prophet said he was Abdullaah bin Dhul Bijaadayn; after his burial the Prophet widened the grave, and mourned him because of his love for Allaah and His Rasool.

n01483.summary: Abdur Rahmaan bin Sa'd reports that Abdullaah bin Umar's cramp eased when he named the Prophet, and recalls Zaid bin Dathana and Khubayb bin Adi refusing to let the Prophet be harmed even to save their own lives.

n01484.summary: Anas and Abdullaah bin Umar report that Abu Bakr wept when his father Abu Quhaafah came to pledge to the Prophet, having hoped Abu Taalib would accept Islaam instead; Abu Bakr told the Prophet that his happiness is all he wishes for.

n01485.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports Umar offering to free the captive Abbaas from the Ansaar, who refused; the Prophet was troubled, so the Companions began informing him only after a death, and later carried biers to his house. Umar bin Muhammad explains the place Mowda'ul Janaa'iz is named after this practice.

n01486.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas reports that Umar urged Abbaas to accept Islaam, because the Prophet would have liked him to be among the first to do so.

n01487.summary: Sha'bi reports an exchange in which Umar honours Abbaas as the Prophet's uncle and, in a dispute over Bahrain land, refuses to rule for Abbaas on the testimony of Mughiera bin Shu'ba, after which Abbaas speaks harshly and Umar reminds him that his acceptance of Islaam pleased the Prophet more.

n01489.summary: Abu Sa'eed Khudri describes how the Companions first informed the Prophet of deaths in Madinah, then changed the practice to spare him inconvenience by bringing the bier to his house; Umar bin Muhammad adds that the place became known as Mowda'ul Janaa'iz.

n01490.summary: Aslam reports that Umar went to Faatima, the Prophet's daughter, and told her that after her father none was dearer to him.

n01491.summary: Anas reports that the Companions did not raise their gaze before the Prophet, except Abu Bakr and Umar, who were close enough to smile and speak informally with him.

n01492.summary: Usaama bin Shareek describes the Companions sitting so still around the Prophet that it seemed birds were perched on their backs, and the Prophet said the most beloved servants of Allaah are those with the best character.

n01494.summary: Baraa bin Aazib says he delayed for two years before asking the Prophet a question, out of the awe he felt for him.

n01495.summary: Zuhri relays that the Sahabah raced to collect the Prophet's saliva and leftover wudhu water for blessing, and the Prophet told them that whoever loves to be loved by Allaah and His Messenger must speak the truth, return trusts and not harm his neighbour.

n01496.summary: Urwa bin Mas'ood, sent to negotiate at Hudaybiyyah, describes how closely the Sahabah honoured the Prophet, and tells his people he has never seen any ruler's followers so devoted to their leader.

n01497.summary: Abu Quraad Sulami says the Sahabah drank the water dripping from the Prophet's wudhu, and the Prophet told them that loving Allaah and His Messenger means keeping trusts, speaking truth and being kind to neighbours.

n01498.summary: Aamir reports that Abdullaah bin Zubayr drank the blood the Prophet had cupped out, and the Prophet foretold strife for him and for the people because of it; a separate note says popular opinion linked his great strength to that blood.

n01499.summary: Kaysaan reports that Salmaan saw Abdullaah bin Zubayr drinking from the Prophet's cupping blood, and the Prophet told him he would be spared the Fire except to pass over the Bridge, after foretelling strife for him.

n01500.summary: Safeenah says the Prophet asked him to bury his cupping blood out of sight, but he drank it instead; when he told the Prophet, the Prophet only laughed.

n01501.summary: Abu Sa'eed Khudri reports that his father Maalik bin Sinaan licked the Prophet's blood from his face after Uhud, and the Prophet said that once his blood had mixed with Maalik's, the Fire would never touch him.

n01502.summary: Hakeemah bint Umaymah reports that the Prophet kept a wooden cup for urine under his bed, and when a maidservant drank from it, the Prophet said she had built a solid barrier against the Fire.

n01503.summary: Abu Ayyoob reports that he hosted the Prophet on the lower storey and worried about standing above him, and that the Prophet taught him dhikr with great reward; a second part says the Prophet sent back food containing garlic or onion.

n01504.summary: Abu Ayyoob asks the Prophet to move to the upper storey, since it is not proper for him to be above the Prophet, and the Prophet has his small luggage moved.

n01505.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas reports that Umar had Abbaas's gutter removed after blood from it spoiled his clothes, and then told Abbaas to restore it exactly where the Prophet had placed it, even if he had to climb on Umar's back.

n01506.summary: Ibraheem bin Abdur Rahmaan reports that Abdullaah bin Umar touched the place where the Prophet sat on his pulpit and then his own face, and Yazeed bin Abdullaah reports Sahabah taking sand from beside the Prophet's grave to make du'aa.

n01507.summary: Abu Layla reports that Usayd bin Hudhayr, while joking with the Prophet, asked to be allowed retaliation for a poke, and when the Prophet lifted his garment, Usayd embraced him and kissed his sides.

n01508.summary: Habbaan bin Waasi reports that at Badr the Prophet nudged Sawaad bin Ghuzayyah's belly with an arrow shaft, and when Sawaad asked for retaliation and kissed the Prophet's belly, the Prophet made du'aa for him.

n01509.summary: Hasan reports that the Prophet jabbed a man wearing yellow dye with a date-palm branch, leaving a mark, and when the man asked for retaliation the Prophet bared his belly and the man kissed it, forgoing retribution on condition of the Prophet's intercession.

n01510.summary: Hasan reports that the Prophet prodded Sawaad bin Amr in the belly with a twig for wearing perfume, and the rest of the account is said to match the report above.

n01511.summary: Hasan reports that Sawaadah bin Amr wore so much Khalooq perfume that the Prophet shook it off his clothes, and after the Prophet lightly struck him with a twig he asked for retaliation, then kissed the Prophet, forgoing it on condition of intercession.

n01512.summary: This is a cross-reference saying that Talha bin Baraa embraced the Prophet and kissed his feet on meeting him, and that Abu Bakr's kiss on the Prophet's forehead at his death will be quoted later.

n01513.summary: Anas bin Maalik reports that when Madinah heard the Prophet had been martyred at Uhud, an Ansaari woman who had lost her father, son, husband and brother went looking for him, and on finding him safe said she no longer cared about her losses.

n01514.summary: Zubayr reports that on the day of Uhud, when the women of Madinah heard that the Prophet had been martyred, one woman set out on foot to see for herself how he was.

n01515.summary: Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas reports that a woman of Banu Dinaar, whose husband, brother and father had all died at Uhud, asked after the Prophet and said that after seeing him every calamity seemed trivial.

n01516.summary: Anas reports that during Uhud Abu Talha shielded the Prophet with his arrows and his own chest, asked him not to rise lest an arrow strike him, and offered to be sent on any task.

n01517.summary: Qataadah bin Nu'maan says that after his bow broke during Uhud, he stood in front of the Prophet and turned his own face to take each arrow aimed at the Prophet's face.

n01518.summary: Abu Sa'eed Khudri reports that in the Prophet's final illness he said he was standing at his Kowthar and that a servant of Allaah had chosen the Aakhirah over this world, and that only Abu Bakr understood and wept.

n01519.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas reports that after a revelation the Prophet told Faatima that his death was near, and she wept until he told her she would be the first of his family to join him, and then she laughed.

n01520.summary: Aa'isha reports that during his final illness the Prophet whispered to Faatima, first making her weep and then making her laugh when he told her she would be the first of his family to join him.

n01521.summary: Ummu Salamah reports that Faatima laughed because the Prophet had told her that she would lead the women of Jannah after Maryam, the daughter of Imraan.

n01522.summary: Alaa reports that as the Prophet was about to pass away, Faatima wept, and he told her to say Innaa Lillaahi wa Innaa Ilayhi Raaji'oon, since every calamity is rewarded, and she asked whether this applied even to losing him.

n01523.summary: Mu'aadh bin Jabal reports that as the Prophet walked beside him on his way to Yemen, the Prophet told him he might not see him again and that those closest to him are the people of taqwa, wherever they are; Mu'aadh wept at the parting.

n01524.summary: A short variant reports that the Prophet told Mu'aadh not to weep, because such weeping comes from Shaytaan.

n01526.summary: Ummul Fadhl bint Haarith reports that she wept during his final illness fearing how they would be treated after his death, and the Prophet replied that they would be in a weaker position once he had left.

n01527.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood reports the Prophet's final instructions: he would be bathed by his closest family, shrouded in his own clothes, prayed over first by the angels, and placed in the grave by the men of his family.

n01528.summary: Yazeed bin Baabnoos reports Aa'isha's account of the Prophet's last illness and death, Abu Bakr's kisses on his forehead and his speech that Muhammad had died while Allaah lives forever, and Umar then urging the people to pledge allegiance to Abu Bakr.

n01529.summary: Ali bin Abi Taalib reports the dispute over who would bury the Prophet, which Abu Bakr settled by saying that the family should decide who enters the room; a second report from Ali bin Husayn says the Ansaar also claimed the right.

n01530.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas reports that Ali stayed with the Prophet as he died, and that Ali then washed the body with Fadhl bin Abbaas and an Ansaari, guided by a voice from the house to bathe him in his clothes.

n01531.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas reports that after the Prophet's death, groups of men entered the room and prayed the Janaazah salaah individually, with no one leading them, followed by the women, children and slaves.

n01532.summary: Sahl bin Sa'd reports that once the Prophet was shrouded and placed on a bed in a corner of the room, people entered in groups to pray the Janaazah salaah, with no one leading them.

n01533.summary: Moosa bin Muhammad bin Ibraheem reports, from a book written by his father, that Abu Bakr and Umar greeted the Prophet and made du'aa at the front of the rows, with no one acting as imam.

n01534.summary: Ali (RA) narrates the janaazah salaah for the Prophet, which the people performed in groups without an imaam, and Ali's farewell supplication.

n01535.summary: Anas (RA) reports that Abu Bakr, on hearing of the Prophet's death, hurried in grief towards the Masjid.

n01536.summary: Ibn Abbaas reports Abu Bakr's address on the Prophet's death, his recitation of Aal Imraan 144, and Umar's collapse on hearing it; Uthmaan's own account of his grief follows in the same text.

n01537.summary: Abdur Rahmaan bin Sa'eed bin Yarboo reports that Ali was deeply grieved at the Prophet's death, and Abu Bakr replied that no one grieved more than he did.

n01538.summary: Ummu Salamah describes the wives' grief at the Prophet's death, the sound of grave-digging before dawn, and Bilaal's weeping when he called the Fajr adhaan.

n01539.summary: Abu Dhu'ayb Hudhali describes the wailing in Madinah when he arrived and learned that the Prophet had passed away.

n01540.summary: A narrator whose name is lost in the OCR reports that the governor of Makkah, Attaab bin Usayd, could not speak after the Prophet's death, so Suhayl bin Amr addressed the people in Makkah in his place.

n01541.summary: Abu Ja'far reports that Faatima never laughed after the Prophet's death and only smiled slightly.

n01542.summary: Is'haaq reports Abu Bakr's words on the Prophet's death that revelation and speech from Allaah had now been lost.

n01543.summary: Anas reports that Ummu Ayman wept because revelation had ended; Abu Bakr and Umar visited her to console her, and their own tears followed hers.

n01545.summary: Moosa bin Uqba quotes Ummu Ayman saying she wept because the news from the heavens, which had come to them daily, had ended.

n01546.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports that the people wept at the Prophet's death, and Ma'n bin Adi replied that he wished to believe in him after his death as he had in his life.

n01548.summary: Another narration gives Faatima's words to Anas after the Prophet was buried, and Hammaad reports that Thaabit wept as he related it.

n01549.summary: Urwa reports Safiyya's couplets in grief for the Prophet; a second set of her verses and a third narration from Muhammad bin Mi bin Husayn follow.

n01550.summary: Ghunaym bin Qais reports the couplets his father recited after the Prophet's departure.

n01551.summary: Zaid bin Aslam reports that Umar, on his night patrol, found an old woman grieving for the Prophet in her couplets, wept with her, and asked her to pray for him.

n01552.summary: Aasim bin Muhammad reports that his father said Abdullaah bin Umar's eyes always filled with tears whenever he mentioned the Prophet.

n01553.summary: Muthanna bin Sa'eed Daari reports that Anas said he saw the Prophet in a dream every night, and wept as he said it.

n01554.summary: Ka'b bin Alqama reports that Gharfa bin Haarith Kindi struck a Christian who reviled the Prophet, and that Amr bin Al Aas replied that a treaty applied, which Gharfa rejected.

n01555.summary: Gharfa bin Haarith reports his own case: he struck a Christian called Mundaqoon in Egypt for reviling the Prophet, and Amr bin Al Aas said that a treaty protected him.

n01556.summary: Another narration tells of Gharfa killing a man under a peace treaty after he reviled the Prophet, and Amr bin Al Aas objecting that the treaty protected him.

n01557.summary: Urwa bin Zubayr reports the expedition to Nakhla under Abdullaah bin Jahash, who followed the sealed instructions, the killing of Ibn Hadhrami in a sacred month and the verses revealed after it; Jundub bin Abdullaah gives a second report of Ubaydah bin Haarith's expedition, which Abdullaah bin Jahash took over.

n01558.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports the Prophet's order after the Battle of Ahzaab not to pray Asr until reaching Banu Qurayzah, and that he did not rebuke either group who differed on it.

n01559.summary: Ka'b bin Maalik reports the Prophet's order after the Battle of Ahzaab to march on Banu Qurayzah at once, and the two groups' different decisions on Asr; Duhaym adds a separate account of the same event.

n01560.summary: Jaabir reports that at Hunayn the Prophet had Abbaas call the Ansaar and the Bay'ah companions, and that Abu Sufyaan's requests to Abu Bakr, Umar and Faatima were refused.

n01561.summary: Ikrama reports that after the Quraysh breached the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah, Abu Sufyaan went to Madinah to ask Abu Bakr, Umar and Faatima to renew it, and was refused by each, so he returned with nothing achieved.

n01562.summary: Abu Azeez bin Umayr, a prisoner taken at Badr, recounts that the Ansaar gave him wheat bread and ate dates themselves, as the Prophet had commanded them to treat prisoners well.

n01563.summary: Abdur Rahmaan bin Abi Layla reports that Abdullaah bin Rawaaha sat down at once when the Prophet told him to during a sermon, and Aa'isha gives a second report of the same incident.

n01564.summary: Ataa reports that Abdullaah bin Mas'ood sat down at the door at once when the Prophet told the people to be seated during a sermon.

n01565.summary: Jaabir reports the same incident: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood sat at the Masjid door until the Prophet called him inside.

n01566.summary: Anas reports that the Prophet disliked an Ansaari's dome and turned away from its owner until he demolished it, and that the Prophet said every building is a curse on its owner except what is necessary.

n01567.summary: Abdullaah bin Amr bin Al Aas reports that when the Prophet disliked his red shawl, he threw it into the oven, and the Prophet told him he could have given it to the women of his household.

n01568.summary: Sahl bin Handhaliyya reports that the Prophet praised Khuraym Asadi except for his long hair and low garment, and Khuraym immediately cut his hair and raised his garment.

n01569.summary: Juthaama bin Musaahiq reports that as Umar's envoy to Heraclius he got off a gold throne he had been given, because he had heard the Prophet forbid such things.

n01570.summary: Raafi bin Khadeej relays his uncle's words that the Prophet had forbidden them something that had been beneficial, and that obedience to Allaah and His Rasool is even better.

n01571.summary: Muhammad bin Aslam bin Bujra reports that, in his old age, he would go back to Madinah to pray two rakahs in the Prophet's Masjid, having forgotten to do so on each visit, as the Prophet had instructed.

n01572.summary: Mughiera bin Shu'ba reports that, on the Prophet's advice, he looked at a woman from the Ansaar before marrying her; she allowed it only because the Prophet had told him to.

n01573.summary: Ma'roor bin Suwayd reports that Abu Dharr, who had insulted Bilaal over his mother, was rebuked by the Prophet, who told him that slaves are his brothers to be fed and clothed as he is.

n01574.summary: Another narration gives the Prophet's words to Abu Dharr that his slaves are his brothers, whom Allaah has put in his care, and should be fed and clothed as he is.

n01575.summary: Abu Salamah bin Abdur Rahmaan reports that Umar tore the silk garment worn by Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf's son Abu Salmah, saying the Prophet had allowed silk to Abdur Rahmaan only because of lice and not to others.

n01576.summary: Umar tears the silk garment worn by the son of Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf, and Abdur Rahmaan protests, pointing out that he himself wears silk.

n01577.summary: Umar challenges Khaalid bin Waleed for wearing a silk garment, and in a second report Umar orders the people to tear up the silk cloak of Khaalid bin Sa'eed.

n01578.summary: Umar cuts the silk buttons off a man's green garment after the man finishes his salaah.

n01579.summary: Sa'eed Qaari goes to Uthmaan about his brother's bequest wearing a silk-trimmed cloak, Ali pulls at the cloak to tear it, and Uthmaan gives a ruling on the bequest.

n01580.summary: Jaarood and Abu Hurayrah testify that Qudaamah bin Madh'oon, Umar's governor of Bahrain, drank wine, and Umar has him lashed, then later reconciles with him.

n01581.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood tells a man laughing at a funeral that he will never speak to him again.

n01582.summary: Abu Hudhayfah says he would kill Abbaas at Badr against the Prophet's order to spare the Banu Haashim, Umar asks to behead him, and Abu Hudhayfah lives in fear of his words until he is martyred at Yamaamah.

n01583.summary: During the siege of Banu Qurayzah, Abu Lubaabah gestures to them that they will be killed if they surrender, and then regrets it deeply.

n01584.summary: After his regret, Abu Lubaabah ties himself to a pillar of the Masjid, and the Prophet says he will not untie him until Allaah decides the matter.

n01585.summary: Thaabit bin Qais fears that raising his voice above the Prophet's has destroyed his deeds, and the Prophet gives him glad tidings that he will be among the people of Jannah.

n01586.summary: Thaabit bin Qais tells the Prophet he fears ruin because he loves praise, beauty and a loud voice, and the Prophet promises him a praiseworthy life, martyrdom and Jannah, which he later attains at the battle against Musaylama.

n01588.summary: Anas reports that the Prophet wore a silver ring for only one day, and when he discarded it the Sahabah also removed their rings.

n01589.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports that the Prophet wore a gold ring, then discarded it saying he would never wear it again, and the Sahabah removed their rings.

n01590.summary: Umar declines to carry the Prophet's message to the Muslim prisoners in Makkah, so Uthmaan goes instead, is escorted by his cousin Abaan, and the Sahabah pledge allegiance under the tree at Hudaybiyyah, with the Prophet pledging on Uthmaan's behalf.

n01591.summary: Abaan tells Uthmaan to let his garment fall and to perform Tawaaf, and Uthmaan replies that they follow the Prophet's example and do nothing before him.

n01592.summary: Abu Bakr and Umar persuade Zaid bin Thaabit to compile the Qur'aan into one manuscript, and Zaid finds the last verses of Surah Taubah with Khuzaymah bin Thaabit.

n01593.summary: Abu Bakr swears he would rather fall from the sky than leave unfought what the Prophet fought for, and then wages jihaad against the Arabs who renounced Islaam and refused zakaah.

n01594.summary: Abu Bakr vows to fight those who separate salaah from zakaah, even over a rope the Arabs once gave the Prophet.

n01596.summary: Abu Bakr tells Usaama to march as the Prophet commanded, saying he would rather have all the Arabs turn against him than hold back the army.

n01597.summary: Abu Bakr seizes Umar's beard and rebukes him for asking that Usaama be relieved of the command the Prophet gave him.

n01598.summary: Umar reminds his daughter Hafsah of the hard life the Prophet and Abu Bakr led, and says he will share their hardship so he may join them in ease in the Aakhirah.

n01599.summary: Umar recites the du'aa for a new garment, cites the Prophet's words on giving old clothes to the poor, and has the excess sleeves cut off without stitching the ends.

n01600.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports that Umar had the sleeves of a new garment cut to length, unevenly, because he had seen the Prophet do the same.

n01601.summary: Umar kisses the Black Stone only because the Prophet did, Abu Bakr does the same on his Hajj, and the Prophet is reported to have kissed it while saying it neither benefits nor harms.

n01602.summary: Ya'la bin Umayyah asks Uthmaan to touch the western pillar of the Kabah, and Uthmaan reminds him that the Prophet did not touch it and that the Prophet is the perfect example.

n01604.summary: Ja'far bin Tammaam reports Ibn Abbaas explaining that the Prophet praised the Nabeedh that Abbaas served him, and that he prefers not to replace it with milk and honey.

n01605.summary: Ibn Seereen reports that Abdullaah bin Umar stopped his animal at a narrow place near Ma'zamain to relieve himself, because the Prophet had done so there.

n01606.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar used to take his afternoon nap under a certain tree between Makkah and Madinah because the Prophet did the same.

n01607.summary: Naafi reports that Abdullaah bin Umar was very particular about following the Prophet's footsteps, marking every place he prayed on journeys and watering a tree under which the Prophet had dismounted.

n01608.summary: Mujaahid reports that Abdullaah bin Umar turned aside on a journey to follow the Prophet's footsteps, and the Prophet then declared each of the Ansaar, Muhaajireen and Banu Haashim equally beloved to him.

n01609.summary: Naafi says that Abdullaah bin Umar followed the Prophet's footsteps so closely that an observer would think him mad.

n01611.summary: Naafi says that Abdullaah bin Umar searched for the Prophet's footsteps as thoroughly as a camel searches for its lost young one.

n01612.summary: Abdur Rahmaan bin Umayyah asks Abdullaah bin Umar why the salaah of fear and the salaah of a resident are in the Qur'aan but not the traveller's salaah, and Abdullaah replies that they follow what the Prophet did.

n01613.summary: Umayyah bin Abdullaah asks Abdullaah bin Umar why the Qur'aan mentions shortening the salaah of fear but not the traveller's salaah, and Abdullaah says the Prophet did it and they copy him.

n01614.summary: Waarid bin Abu Aasim asks Abdullaah bin Umar about the salaah on a journey while in Mina, and Abdullaah rebukes him by citing the Prophet's practice of praying two rakaahs; Abu Muneed Jurashi adds a question about shortening salaah in safety.

n01615.summary: Zaid bin Aslam reports seeing Abdullaah bin Umar pray with his buttons open, and Abdullaah says he saw the Prophet do this.

n01616.summary: Qurra reports that he and a delegation of Banu Muzayna pledged allegiance to the Prophet and felt the seal of prophethood on his back through his open collar, and Urwa bin Abdullaah reports that Mu'aawiya bin Qurra and his son always prayed with their buttons open.

n01617.summary: Ka'b bin Ujrah reports a dispute among the Ansaar, Muhaajireen and Banu Haashim over who was closest to the Prophet, and the Prophet affirmed the claim of each group and said he was the brother of the Ansaar, one of the Muhaajireen, and from Banu Haashim.

n01618.summary: Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf complains about Khaalid bin Waleed, and the Prophet forbids anyone from hurting the veterans of Badr or Khaalid himself.

n01619.summary: Khaalid bin Waleed disputes superiority with Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf over the date of their acceptance of Islaam, and in a second report the Prophet's farewell words ask people to treat the Ansaar kindly and overlook their faults.

n01620.summary: Abu Hurayrah reports that a dispute arose between Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf and Khaalid bin Waleed, and the Prophet told them to leave his Companions alone because even spending Uhud's worth of gold cannot match the reward of a Badri's mudd.

n01621.summary: Jaabir reports the Prophet's saying that Allaah chose his Companions above all creation after the prophets, singling out Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthmaan and Ali, and that his Ummah's first four generations are chosen too.

n01622.summary: Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf reports the Prophet's final advice to be good to the early Muhaajireen and their children, warning that otherwise no deed will be accepted.

n01623.summary: The Prophet advises goodness towards the early Muhaajireen and their children, and Zaid bin Sa'd reports the Prophet's last sermon in which he asked people to treat the Ansaar well, accepting the good among them and overlooking their faults.

n01624.summary: Anas reports that the Prophet stopped people from accusing Maalik bin Dukhshun of hypocrisy, and Ibn Abbaas reports the Prophet cursing anyone who reviles his Companions.

n01625.summary: Aa'isha reports the Prophet's command never to revile his Companions and his curse on anyone who does.

n01626.summary: Sa'eed bin Zaid asks whether people are telling him to revile the Sahabah, and prays that Allaah shower His mercy on them and forgive them all.

n01627.summary: Sa'eed bin Jubayr reports that Ibn Abbaas advised a man to fear Allaah and not to speak ill of the Sahabah.

n01628.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports the Prophet's final words about his household, and Ummu Salamah reports the Prophet covering Faatima, Ali, Hasan and Husayn with his shawl and praying for them.

n01629.summary: The Prophet ﷺ prayed that the progeny of Abdul Muttalib be kept steadfast, educated and guided, warned that bearing enmity towards them leads to Jahannam, and promised to repay anyone who is not repaid in this world for a kindness shown to them.

n01630.summary: Jaabir (RA) reports Umar's remark, on marrying Ali's daughter, that this made him kin to the Prophet ﷺ; a second report has the Prophet warning against speaking ill of the Quraysh, whose status is high in Allaah's sight.

n01631.summary: Ali (RA) reports the Prophet's instruction to put the Quraysh first and never to go ahead of them, and his statement that he would otherwise have told them their high status in Allaah's sight.

n01632.summary: Aa'isha (RA) reports that the Prophet ﷺ told her he would have revealed the high status of the Quraysh had he not feared their pride.

n01633.summary: Abu Hurayrah reports the Prophet's praise of the trustworthiness of the Quraysh; Rifaa'ah bin Raafi reports that Umar was sent to gather the people, and that the Prophet told them only those with taqwa are Allaah's friends and warned against searching out the faults of the Quraysh.

n01634.summary: Ibn Abbaas reports the Prophet's warning that enmity towards Banu Haashim and the Ansaar leads to kufr, and that enmity towards the Arabs is a sign of hypocrisy.

n01635.summary: Aa'isha (RA) relates the Prophet's prophecy that the Quraysh would be the first of his Ummah to die and be envied, after which people would become like locusts devouring the weak until Qiyaamah; a second narration calls them the first to be destroyed.

n01636.summary: Umar (RA) reports that the Prophet ﷺ ranked the Imaan of those who believe in him without seeing him as the strongest of all, above the angels, the Ambiyaa and the martyrs.

n01637.summary: Amr (RA) reports that the Prophet ﷺ ranked those who believe in him unseen above the angels and the Ambiyaa; Abu Jumu'ah (RA) reports that when Abu Ubaydah asked whether anyone was superior to the Sahabah, the Prophet gave the same answer.

n01638.summary: Abu Umaamah (RA) reports the Prophet's glad tidings: a reward for those who believe in him after seeing him, and seven times that reward for those who believe in him without seeing him.

n01639.summary: Abu Hurayrah (RA) reports the Prophet's saying that people will come after him who would wish to sacrifice their families and wealth just to see him.

n01640.summary: Anas (RA) reports the Prophet's wish to see his brothers, who will believe in him without seeing him, and that when the Sahabah asked whether they were not his brothers, he said they were his companions and his brothers are those who believe unseen.

n01641.summary: Ammaar bin Yaasir (RA) reports the Prophet's comparison of his Ummah to rain, of which it cannot be said whether the first part or the last part is better.

n01642.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) reports that the Prophet ﷺ said angels convey the greetings of his Ummah to him, that his life is good for them because they ask him about Deen, and his death is good for them because their deeds are shown to him; he praises Allaah for good deeds and asks forgiveness for their sins.

n01643.summary: Abu Burdah (RA) reports that, while the heads of the Khawaarij were brought before Ibn Ziyaad and Abdullaah bin Yazeed, he declared each one headed for Jahannam, and Abdullaah rebuked him, quoting the Prophet that the punishment of this Ummah is in this world.

n01644.summary: A narration with no named narrator quotes the Prophet ﷺ that Allaah has made killing the punishment of this Ummah in this world.

n01645.summary: Abu Burdah (RA) reports that he left Ubaydullaah bin Ziyaad because of the harsh punishment he was giving the Khawaarij, and that a Sahabi told him the Prophet ﷺ had said this Ummah's punishment would be by the sword.

n01646.summary: Ibn Abbaas (RA) reports that after a man was killed in mysterious circumstances, the Prophet ﷺ addressed the people from the pulpit: if all the inhabitants of the heavens and the earth conspired to kill one Muslim, Allaah would punish them all.

n01647.summary: Abu Sa'eed (RA) reports that after an unknown person was killed, the Prophet ﷺ asked three times on the pulpit who had done it, then warned that conspiring to kill a Mu'min brings Jahannam, and that bearing enmity to his household does too.

n01649.summary: Usaama bin Zaid (RA) gives further reports of the Prophet ﷺ repeatedly asking who would defend him against La ilaaha illallaah, and of Usaama's pledge never to kill anyone who professes it; a third report names Mirdaas bin Nuhayk, killed after he professed the Kalimah.

n01650.summary: Bakr bin Haaritha (RA) reports that in battle he killed a man who had accepted Islaam to save himself; the Prophet ﷺ withdrew from him until Surah Nisaa verse 92 was revealed on the matter, after which he was pleased with him again and drew him close.

n01651.summary: Uqba bin Khaalid Laythi (RA) reports that a Muslim killed a fleeing man who had cried out that he was a Muslim; the Prophet ﷺ condemned it, and when the killer said the man had professed Islaam only to save himself, the Prophet kept turning away from him and rebuked him.

n01652.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas reports that Miqdaad killed a man who had said the Kalimah, and the Prophet rebuked him, after which the verse about verifying before judging a claim to Islaam was revealed.

n01653.summary: Abdullaah bin Abu Hadrad (RA) reports that Muhallim bin Jathaamah killed Aamir bin Athbat on an old grudge after Aamir greeted them with salaam, and that Surah Nisaa verse 94 was then revealed on the matter.

n01654.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) reports the same incident: Muhallim bin Jathaamah shot and killed Aamir bin Athbat; Uyaynah and Aqra debated before the Prophet ﷺ, who refused to forgive Muhallim, who died within seven days; the earth twice returned his body, so the Sahabah buried him under rocks, and Surah Nisaa verse 94 was then revealed.

n01655.summary: Qabeesah bin Dhuwayb (RA) reports that a Sahabi killed a defeated Mushrik who had recited the Kalimah, was distressed by it, and after he died the earth twice refused his body, so the Prophet ﷺ ordered it thrown into a crevasse in the mountains.

n01656.summary: Abu Ja'far Muhammad bin Ali reports that after Makkah was conquered Khaalid bin Waleed, sent to invite people to Islaam, killed many of the Banu Jadheema after they had laid down their arms; the Prophet ﷺ raised his hands to disown the act, sent Ali to compensate every loss, and praised what Ali did.

n01657.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) reports that Khaalid bin Waleed had the Banu Jadheema prisoners executed and that the Prophet ﷺ disowned the act; Ibn Is'haaq adds the quarrel between Khaalid and Abdur Rahmaan bin Awf, and the Prophet told Khaalid to leave his Badri companions alone.

n01658.summary: Sakhar (RA) reports that he held the Thaqeef under siege until they surrendered and sent them to the Prophet ﷺ; the Prophet then had him hand back the captured aunt of Mughiera bin Shu'ba, and return the oasis he had taken from the Banu Sulaym once they embraced Islaam again.

n01659.summary: Aws bin Aws Thaqafi (RA) reports that the Prophet ﷺ ordered a man executed after a whispered report, then recalled him, asked whether he had testified to Allaah's oneness and the Prophet's risaalah, and ordered his release, since blood and wealth are protected once people testify.

n01660.summary: Abdullaah bin Adi Ansaari (RA) reports that when the Prophet ﷺ was told of a hypocrite who had been killed, he asked whether the man had testified to Allaah's oneness and to his risaalah and prayed salaah, and said that such people were the ones he was forbidden to kill.

n01661.summary: Aa'isha (RA) reports that the Prophet ﷺ asked for one of his companions, and after Abu Bakr, Umar and Ali were named and declined, he called Uthmaan and whispered to him; when Uthmaan was besieged and his companions asked to fight, he refused, saying the Prophet had made him pledge to remain steadfast.

n01662.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) reports that Uthmaan, besieged in his house, asked the rebels why they wanted to kill him, quoted the three cases in which a person's blood is lawful, and denied that any of them applied to him.

n01664.summary: Abu Layla Kindi reports that Uthmaan, under siege, warned the rebels through a gap in the wall that killing him would divide the Muslims, quoting Shu'ayb's warning from Surah Hood, and that Uthmaan then asked Abdullaah bin Salaam, who advised restraint.

n01665.summary: Mughiera bin Shu'ba (RA) relates the three options he offered Uthmaan under siege (fight, leave for Makkah, or go to Shaam), and Uthmaan refused all three, quoting the Prophet's warning about a Quraysh man who would spread irreligiousness in Makkah, and saying he would never leave the place of Hijrah.

n01666.summary: Abu Hurayrah (RA) reports that he told Uthmaan under siege that fighting the rebels was now lawful, and Uthmaan answered that killing even one person is like killing all of mankind; Abu Hurayrah then left without fighting.

n01667.summary: Abdullaah bin Zubayr (RA) asks Uthmaan to let them fight the rebels, and Uthmaan refuses, pleading that no man should have his blood spilt for him or spill another's for him; a second narration gives the same request and refusal.

n01668.summary: Abdullaah bin Aamir (RA) reports that Uthmaan, under siege, said the one most useful to him is the man who restrains his hand and his weapon.

n01670.summary: Uthmaan forbade his men, who were ready to fight the rebels besieging him, from fighting, and Sa'eed bin Al Aas then went out to fight and was fatally wounded.

n01671.summary: Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas refused his son Aamir's urging to join the fighting unless he was given a sword that spares believers, and quoted the Prophet on loving the inconspicuous person who has taqwa.

n01672.summary: Asked why he did not take up arms though he was among the consultative assembly and more deserving of the Khilaafah, Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas said he would fight only with a sword that could tell a believer from an unbeliever.

n01673.summary: Usaama bin Zaid and Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas each said they would never fight anyone who recites the kalimah, and when challenged with the verse on fighting, they replied that they had fought until corruption ended.
