n01674.summary: Two men asked Abdullaah bin Umar why he did not join the fighting in Abdullaah bin Zubayr's time, and he answered that Allaah had made his brother's blood haraam to spill and that the fighters were spreading corruption.

n01675.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar explained to questioners why he did not fight, and gave his view of Uthmaan (forgiven by Allaah) and Ali (the Prophet's cousin and son-in-law).

n01676.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar told a questioner that the 'corruption' in the verse means fighting the Mushrikeen, unlike the fighting of his own day over land.

n01677.summary: Abdullaah bin Safwaan asked Abdullaah bin Umar why he would not pledge allegiance to Abdullaah bin Zubayr, and Ibn Umar replied that he would not pledge while the people's swords dripped with Muslim blood.

n01678.summary: Hasan says that when the Muslims were in turmoil and people urged Abdullaah bin Umar to take the pledge of allegiance, he refused, and he was never drawn into their aims until he died.

n01679.summary: Khaalid bin Sumayr reports that Abdullaah bin Umar, asked to take up the Khilaafah, said he would not accept it at the cost of even one life, since the unity of the Ummah matters more.

n01680.summary: Qatan reports that a man told Abdullaah bin Umar that no one had done more harm to the Ummah, and Abdullaah replied that he had not shed blood, divided unity or broken strength, and would not want the Khilaafah while people disagreed about him.

n01681.summary: Qaasim bin Abdur Rahmaan reports that when people urged Abdullaah bin Umar to fight during the first period of strife, he refused to fight people who say La ilaaha illallaah, and said he wanted to stay united with the Muslims.

n01682.summary: Asked why he prayed with factions who were killing one another, Abdullaah bin Umar said he answers the call to salaah and to success, but refuses a call to kill his Muslim brother.

n01683.summary: Abul Ghareef recounts that Hasan bin Ali's frontline forces were furious at his truce with Mu'aawiya, and that Hasan told a man who called him a humiliator of the Mu'mineen that he had only disliked killing them for land.

n01684.summary: Hasan bin Ali addressed the people after the truce with Mu'aawiya, saying he had given up his claim to rule to save the Ummah's lives, and Amr bin Al Aas remarked to Mu'aawiya that this was exactly what he wanted.

n01685.summary: Jubayr bin Nufayr asked Hasan bin Ali about the claim that he wanted the Khilaafah, and Hasan answered that he gave up the post for Allaah's pleasure to save the Ummah's blood.

n01686.summary: When Marwaan asked Ayman bin Khuraym Asadi to fight beside him against Dahhaak bin Qais, Ayman refused unless given a guarantee of freedom from Jahannam, and recited verses saying he would gain nothing from fighting another Muslim for no reason.

n01687.summary: A messenger from Ali asked Hakam bin Amr to help him in the matter of the Khilaafah, and Hakam replied that a friend had advised that in such times it is best to take up a wooden sword, which he had done.

n01688.summary: Abu Ash'ath San'aani reports that Yazeed bin Mu'aawiya sent him to Abdullaah bin Abi Awfa, who said the Prophet told him to break his sword and submit to being killed rather than fight Muslims.

n01689.summary: Muhammad bin Maslamah recounts the Prophet's command to break his sword and stay at home rather than fight when Muslims fight Muslims, and says he did so after Uthmaan was martyred.

n01690.summary: At Hudhayfah's funeral a man recalled his words that if Muslims fought one another he would go home and let any attacker take his sins along with his own.

n01691.summary: Waa'il bin Hujar recounts being welcomed by the Prophet, and later refusing to fight in the strife after Mu'aawiya summoned him, citing the Prophet's warning about tribulations and declining governorship.

n01692.summary: Abul Minhaal recounts how his father asked Abu Barzah Aslami about the conflict between Marwaan, Ibn Zubayr and the Qurraa in Basrah, and Abu Barzah condemned all sides as fighting for worldly gain and advised withdrawal.

n01693.summary: Thamar bin Attiyya reports that Hudhayfah told a man that if he killed the worst of sinners he would be an even worse sinner himself.

n01694.summary: Umar asked Anas how his men besieged cities, and when Anas said a shield-bearer would be killed by thrown rocks, Umar said he would never be pleased to take a city of four thousand warriors at the cost of one Muslim's life.

n01695.summary: Umar said that rescuing a single Muslim from the unbelievers is more precious to him than control of the whole Arabian peninsula.

n01696.summary: Abul Hasan, who fought at Badr, recounts that the Prophet asked how a Companion would answer for frightening a believer after another Companion hid the first one's shoes as a joke.

n01697.summary: Aamir bin Rabee'ah reports that when a Companion hid another's shoes in jest, the Prophet said that frightening a Muslim is a great injustice.

n01698.summary: Nu'maan bin Basheer and Layla each report that the Prophet rebuked Companions who startled a sleeping traveller on a journey, saying it is not permissible to frighten a Muslim.

n01699.summary: Sulaymaan bin Surad reports that the Prophet rebuked Companions who took away a Bedouin's rope during salaah, saying whoever believes in Allaah should never frighten a Muslim.

n01700.summary: Aa'isha reports that when Usaama bin Zaid fell and cut his head, the Prophet licked the blood from the wound himself, and said that had Usaama been a girl he would have adorned and married her off.

n01701.summary: Ataa bin Yasaar reports that the Prophet washed and kissed the smallpox-stricken Usaama bin Zaid, after which Aa'isha vowed never to distance him, while Urwa says the people of Yemen reverted to kufr because they looked down on Usaama.

n01702.summary: Urwa reports that after the Prophet's passing the people of Yemen reverted to kufr because they looked down on Usaama bin Zaid.

n01703.summary: Hasan reports that Umar rebuked Abu Moosa Ash'ari for giving gifts to the Arab Muslims but none to the non-Arab slaves, saying it is enough evil for a man to look down on his Muslim brother.

n01704.summary: Aa'idh bin Umar reports that Salmaan, Suhayb and Bilaal made a remark about Abu Sufyaan that angered Abu Bakr, and the Prophet warned that angering them would anger Allaah, so Abu Bakr went back to ask whether he had angered them.

n01705.summary: Suhayb reports that after he said a Mushrik prisoner's neck would make a perfect place for a sword, Abu Bakr was angry, and the Prophet told Abu Bakr that hurting Suhayb would have hurt Allaah and His Rasool.

n01706.summary: Umar reports that the Prophet forbade cursing a man called Abdullaah, nicknamed Himaar, who was lashed repeatedly for drinking wine, because he loves Allaah and His Rasool.

n01707.summary: Another report says that Himaar gave the Prophet butter and honey, and when the seller came to collect unpaid, the Prophet smiled and ordered him paid.

n01708.summary: Zaid bin Aslam reports that when someone cursed Ibn Nu'maan for repeated drinking and lashing, the Prophet told them not to curse him, because he loves Allaah and His Rasool.

n01709.summary: Abu Hurayrah reports that the Prophet stopped Companions from cursing a drinker they had lashed, and the same narration records Umar's vow to cut out his son Abdullaah's tongue for swearing Miqdaad.

n01710.summary: Aa'isha reports that a man asked the Prophet how to deal with slaves who lie, cheat and disobey him, and the Prophet explained that they will be recompensed on the Day of Qiyaamah; the man then asked to be separated from them.

n01711.summary: Abu Hurayrah reports that when someone abused Abu Bakr and he replied to some of it, the Prophet left, and explained that Shaytaan had come in; the Prophet also affirmed that forgiving injustice brings strength. Separately, Umar vowed to cut off his son Abdullaah's tongue for swearing Miqdaad, and Bahiy reports the same dispute.

n01712.summary: Anas reports that when someone spoke ill of another in the Prophet's presence, the Prophet told him to stand up and leave, because his testimony of faith was worthless and he had mocked the Qur'aan by doing what it forbids.

n01713.summary: Taariq bin Shihaab reports that when someone spoke ill of Khaalid bin Waleed to Sa'd, Sa'd told him to stop, saying their dispute should not spill into their Deen.

n01714.summary: Abu Hurayrah reports that the Prophet likened backbiting a Muslim who had been stoned for adultery to eating a dead animal, and Ibnul Murtkadir reports that the Prophet told someone who said a stoned woman's deeds were destroyed that the punishment had cleansed her, while he would be called to account for his words.

n01715.summary: Aa'isha reports that the Prophet rebuked her for remarking that Safiyya was short, saying such words would spoil the ocean, and also that he disliked her imitating someone even for great wealth.

n01716.summary: Safiyya's camel fell ill and the Prophet asked Zaynab to give her one, but Zaynab refused with an insult, so the Prophet stayed away from her for months.

n01718.summary: Abu Hurayrah reports that when some Sahabah called a companion who left a gathering feeble, the Prophet said they had backbitten him and eaten the flesh of their brother.

n01719.summary: Mu'aadh bin Jabal reports the same incident, with the Prophet explaining that mentioning a fault a person really has is backbiting, while mentioning one he does not have is slander.

n01720.summary: Abdullaah bin Amr reports that the Sahabah described a companion as lazy, and the Prophet said that mentioning a real fault in a brother is backbiting.

n01721.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood reports that after a companion left a gathering, someone spoke ill of him, and the Prophet told that man to repent for eating his brother's flesh.

n01722.summary: In a terse report the Prophet tells a man to pick his teeth, and the man asks why, since he has eaten no meat.

n01723.summary: Anas reports that the Prophet told two young women who had fasted all day, while backbiting, to vomit, and said that their backbiting had broken their fast and would have burned them in Jahannam.

n01724.summary: In another report the two women vomit blood and flesh, and the Prophet says they broke their lawful fast with the forbidden act of backbiting.

n01725.summary: Anas bin Maalik reports that when Abu Bakr and Umar mocked their sleeping servant, the Prophet told them they had eaten his flesh and advised them to ask the servant to forgive them.

n01727.summary: Sha'bi reports that Umar and Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf spied on a companion of Umar who was drinking in his house, and Abdur Rahmaan advised that the repentance for spying is to keep what was learned private and think well of him.

n01728.summary: Taa'oos reports that Umar, on night patrol, called out to a house where people were drinking, and when one of them reminded him that spying was forbidden, Umar left them alone.

n01729.summary: Thowr Kindi reports that Umar scaled a wall to confront a man singing in his house, and when the man rebuked him with the Qur'aanic prohibitions on spying and on entering without permission, Umar pardoned him.

n01730.summary: Suddi reports that after Umar caught an old man drinking and was rebuked for spying, Umar swore privately that he had told no one, and the old man said he had never repeated what he had done.

n01731.summary: Abu Qilaabah reports that Umar found Abu Mihjin Thaqafi drinking at his house and left him alone when Abu Mihjin reminded him that spying was forbidden, with Zaid bin Thaabit and Abdur Rahmaan bin Arqam agreeing.

n01733.summary: Sha'bi reports that when a woman's uncle asked Umar whether he must disclose her repented past before her marriage, Umar told him to marry her off as he would any righteous girl.

n01734.summary: Sha'bi reports that when Umar tried to identify a foundling's mother, one of the women rebuked him for trying to expose a woman Allaah had concealed, and Umar admitted he was wrong and told the nurse not to question the visitors.

n01735.summary: Saalih bin Karz reports that Anas bin Maalik persuaded him to take back his slave girl, who had committed fornication, instead of having her punished, urging him to fear Allaah and conceal her sin.

n01736.summary: Dukhayn, scribe to Uqba bin Aamir, reports Uqba's advice against reporting neighbours who drank wine; the text then runs into Haatib bin Abi Balta'ah's secret letter to Quraysh, which the Prophet forgave because Haatib had fought at Badr.

n01737.summary: Bilaal bin Sa'd Ash'ari reports that Mu'aawiya asked Abu Dardaa for a list of the criminals of Damascus, and Abu Dardaa refused, telling his son to begin with his own name.

n01738.summary: Sha'bi reports that Umar, smelling a fart in a room, ordered the person responsible to make wudhu, and Jareer bin Abdullaah suggested everyone should do so to spare him embarrassment, which Umar praised.

n01739.summary: Ali reports that the Prophet sent him, Zubayr and Miqdaad to a woman carrying a letter from Haatib bin Abi Balta'ah to the Mushrikeen of Makkah, and Haatib, a Badri, explained he had acted to protect his family, so the Prophet forgave him despite Umar's demand to kill him as a hypocrite.

n01740.summary: Abu Matar reports that Ali released a man who had confessed to theft once he retracted, and cites the Prophet's teaching that people should pardon one another's wrongs rather than demand punishment.

n01741.summary: Abu Maajid Hanafi reports that Ibn Mas'ood had a drunkard lightly flogged, and then quotes the Prophet's grief over a thief's hand being cut and his call to forgive rather than demand punishment.

n01742.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports that a man whom Abu Moosa Ash'ari had flogged and paraded for drinking came to Umar in despair, and Umar warned Abu Moosa that he would be disgraced the same way if he repeated it, and ordered the man to be accepted if he repents.

n01743.summary: Abu Own reports that Khaalid bin Waleed had Maalik bin Nuwayrah executed for apostasy despite testimony in his favour and then married his widow, and that Abu Bakr refused Umar's demands to punish Khaalid, saying he had erred in judgement.

n01744.summary: Abu Qilaabah reports Abu Dardaa's advice to hate a sinner's sin rather than the sinner, and Ibn Mas'ood's instruction not to help Shaytaan by cursing a brother who sins.

n01745.summary: Anas reports that Abdullaah bin Amr followed a man the Prophet had named as one of the people of Jannah, and stayed with him three days, learning that the man's secret was harbouring no envy or ill-feeling towards any Muslim.

n01747.summary: A variant names the companion as Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas, who says he harbours no ill-feeling towards any Muslim and never speaks ill of them, and Abdullaah bin Amr says he cannot match this.

n01748.summary: Zaid bin Aslam reports that Abu Dujaanah's face shone during his illness, which he credited to speaking only when necessary and keeping a clear heart towards all Muslims.

n01749.summary: Buraydah Aslami reports that when someone insulted Abdullaah bin Abbaas, he listed three things that made him happy: wishing all people shared his knowledge of the Qur'aan, joy at a just Muslim ruler, and joy at rain falling on Muslim cities.

n01750.summary: Aa'isha reports that the Prophet received a man he had called the worst of his tribe warmly, and that he explained the worst people are those whose abuse others must guard against.

n01751.summary: Safwaan bin Assaal reports that the Prophet welcomed a man he had called the worst of his tribe, saying he was a hypocrite and that he treated him kindly so that the man would not spoil the Prophet's name among others.

n01752.summary: Buraydah reports that the Prophet welcomed a wealthy Quraysh man as a close friend, then said that Allaah will not set up a scale of deeds for him on the Day of Qiyaamah because he has no good deeds.

n01753.summary: Abu Dardaa says that they may smile in the faces of some people while their hearts curse them.

n01754.summary: A variant adds Abu Dardaa's words that they also laugh with such people.

n01755.summary: Abu Dardaa reports that after Abu Bakr and Umar quarrelled, the Prophet asked the Companions to leave Abu Bakr alone, and Abdullaah bin Umar gives a parallel report that the Prophet urged Umar to forgive him.

n01757.summary: Aa'isha reports that Ummu Habeebah, on her deathbed, asked her forgiveness for the rivalries between co-wives, and then did the same with Ummu Salamah.

n01758.summary: Sha'bi reports that Abu Bakr asked Faatima's permission to visit her in her last illness, and calmed her by affirming his devotion to Allaah, His Rasool and her household until she was pleased.

n01759.summary: Sha'bi reports that when Umar disliked Abdullaah bin Amr, Abdullaah explained that his unbroken fasts and night worship had been corrected by the Prophet, who told him to alternate fasting with sleep and to obey his father.

n01760.summary: Rajaa bin Rabee'ah reports that Abdullaah bin Amr refused to greet Hasan bin Ali until after the Battle of Siffeen, when he sought his pardon, explaining he had fought only by following his father and had fasted and prayed through the nights, which the Prophet had told him to moderate.

n01761.summary: Abdullaah bin Amr (RA) asks Husayn bin Ali (RA) for forgiveness after a long estrangement, and Husayn accepts once Abu Sa'eed (RA) has arranged the meeting.

n01762.summary: Ali (RA) says that fulfilling a Muslim's need is more beloved to him than a earth full of gold and silver.

n01763.summary: Umar (RA) stands still and listens to an old woman, Khowlah, until she has stated her need, and explains that Allaah heard her complaint from above the seven heavens.

n01765.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas, while in I'tikaaf in the Prophet's Masjid, leaves it to help a man with a debt, recalling the Prophet's saying that walking to meet a Muslim's need is better than ten years of I'tikaaf.

n01766.summary: Abdullaah bin Qais reports that the Prophet often visited the Ansaar, both at home and in the Masjid; Anas reports that he once prayed on a mat at an Ansaari house and made du'aa for the household.

n01767.summary: Anas (RA) reports that the Prophet ﷺ forged a bond of brotherhood between every two Sahabah, so that each missed his brother terribly until they met.

n01768.summary: Companions of Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) tell him they still visit each other, and he says they will remain in good stead as long as they keep doing so.

n01769.summary: Ummu Dardaa (RA) reports that Salmaan (RA) walked all the way from Madaa'in to visit her husband Abu Dardaa in Shaam, and that Abu Dardaa wore only a short shawl.

n01770.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) reports that the Prophet ﷺ threw him a pillow stuffed with bark during a visit, which he did not sit on out of respect.

n01771.summary: Ummu Sa'd (RA), daughter of Sa'd bin Rabee (RA), is given a sheet to sit on by Abu Bakr (RA), who tells Umar (RA) that her father has already prepared his place in Jannah.

n01772.summary: Anas (RA) reports that Salmaan (RA) visited Umar (RA), who threw him a cushion, and Salmaan quoted the Prophet's words that a host who gives his guest a cushion has his sins forgiven.

n01773.summary: Anas (RA) reports that Umar (RA) threw a cushion to Salmaan (RA) and recited the hadith that a host who gives a cushion to his guest has his sins forgiven.

n01774.summary: Anas (RA) reports that Salmaan (RA) threw a cushion to Umar (RA), who asked what it meant, and Salmaan quoted the Prophet's hadith on the cushion of hospitality and honour.

n01775.summary: Ibraheem bin Nasheet reports that Abdullaah bin Haarith bin Jaz Zubaydi threw him the cushion he had been sitting on, and said that whoever is not hospitable to a visitor has no ties with Ahmad or Ibraheem.

n01776.summary: Sahal bin Sa'd (RA) reports that Abu Usayd Saa'idi (RA) invited the Prophet ﷺ to his wedding feast, where his new bride served him dates soaked overnight in a vessel.

n01777.summary: Two visitors decline a cushion from Abdullaah bin Haarith (RA), who warns that whoever is not hospitable to a visitor has no ties with the Prophet or Ibraheem.

n01778.summary: The Prophet ﷺ throws his shawl to Jareer bin Abdullaah (RA) so he can sit, and tells the people to honour a prominent person of a tribe who comes to them.

n01780.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas reports that when Uyaynah bin Hisn came to the Prophet, who was sitting with Abu Bakr and Umar on the bare ground, the Prophet had a duvet placed for him and said a prominent person of a tribe should be honoured.

n01781.summary: Adi bin Haatim reports that the Prophet gave him a cushion, which he declined in favour of sitting on the ground, and that after praising the Prophet's humility he accepted Islaam; the Prophet then said a prominent person of a tribe should be honoured.

n01783.summary: Abu Dharr (RA) judges Ju'ayl (RA) to be a poor man, but the Prophet ﷺ says Ju'ayl is better than a world full of leaders like him, and that he gives to Uyaynah and Aqra only to win their hearts to Islaam.

n01785.summary: Husayn bin Saburah and Amr bin Muslim ask Zaid bin Arqam (RA) about the Prophet's household, and Ibn Abbaas (RA) reports that Abu Bakr (RA) gave his seat to Abbaas (RA), after which the Prophet ﷺ foretold the future of Abbaas's descendants.

n01786.summary: Abu Bakr tells the Muslims to consider Muhammad ﷺ in how they treat the members of his household.

n01787.summary: Aa'isha relates that the Prophet lowered his voice when his uncle Abbaas came in, and Ibn Abbaas relates that Abu Bakr gave up his seat for Abbaas and the Prophet foretold Abbaas's descendants would be kings.

n01788.summary: Ja'far bin Muhammad reports the seating order around the Prophet ﷺ, and that Abu Bakr (RA) always gave his place to Abbaas (RA) when he came.

n01789.summary: Abbaas (RA) comes to the Prophet ﷺ in anger at how the Quraysh treat the Banu Haashim, and the Prophet says that faith is incomplete without loving the Banu Haashim for the sake of Allaah.

n01790.summary: Abbaas (RA) reports that he complained to the Prophet ﷺ that the Quraysh greet the Banu Haashim with strange faces, and the Prophet became very angry.

n01791.summary: Ismah narrates that Abbaas (RA) noticed resentment on people's faces in the Masjid, asked the Prophet ﷺ about it, and the Prophet told the people that they cannot be believers until they love Abbaas.

n01792.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) reports that the Prophet ﷺ sent Umar (RA) to collect zakaah, that Umar and Abbaas (RA) quarrelled over it, and that the Prophet approved Umar's conduct after Ali (RA) brought the matter to him.

n01793.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) reports that Abbaas (RA) slapped a man who insulted his father, and the Prophet ﷺ told the people that Abbaas is from him and that the dead should not be insulted to hurt the living.

n01794.summary: In another report, the people ask the Prophet ﷺ to seek Allaah's forgiveness on their behalf after the incident with Abbaas, and he agrees.

n01795.summary: Ibn Shihaab reports that Abu Bakr (RA) and Umar (RA), during their caliphates, dismounted and led Abbaas's animal on foot whenever they met him riding.

n01796.summary: Qaasim bin Muhammad reports that Uthmaan (RA) had a man lashed for ridiculing Abbaas (RA), reasoning that whoever allows such behaviour opposes the Prophet, and the Sahabah approved the ruling.

n01797.summary: Anas (RA) reports that Abu Bakr (RA) gave his place beside the Prophet ﷺ to Ali (RA), and the Prophet said that only people of virtue recognise virtue in others.

n01798.summary: Rabaah bin Haarith reports that a group of Ansaar greeted Ali (RA) as their Moula, citing the Prophet's words at the pond of Khum, and that Abu Ayyoob Ansaari (RA) was among them.

n01799.summary: Buraydah (RA) reports that after an expedition under Ali (RA) he complained about Ali, and the Prophet ﷺ's face turned red with anger as he said: for whoever I am a friend to, Ali is also their friend.

n01800.summary: Amr bin Shaas Aslami (RA) reports that he harboured anger against Ali (RA) for his harshness, and the Prophet ﷺ told him that whoever hurts Ali has hurt him.

n01801.summary: Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas (RA) reports that he and two others insulted Ali (RA) in the Masjid, and when the Prophet ﷺ came in angry, he said that whoever hurts Ali has hurt him.

n01802.summary: Umar (RA) rebukes a man who insulted Ali (RA) in his presence, reminding him that the Prophet ﷺ is in the grave and that hurting Ali hurts him.

n01803.summary: Abu Bakr bin Khaalid bin Urfuta asks Sa'd bin Maalik whether he has reviled Ali, and Sa'd says he would never revile him even if a saw were placed on his head.

n01804.summary: Mu'aawiya bin Abi Sufyaan asks Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas (RA) why he does not revile Ali, and Sa'd lists the virtues the Prophet ﷺ gave Ali: the rank like Haaroon and Moosa, the flag at Khaybar, and being called with his family.

n01805.summary: Abu Nujayh reports that Mu'aawiya bin Abi Sufyaan, during Hajj, spoke ill of Ali (RA) to Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas (RA), who rebuked him and walked out, quoting the Prophet's words about Ali.

n01806.summary: Abu Abdullaah Jadali reports that Ummu Salamah (RA) asked whether people revile the Prophet, and then quoted the Prophet that whoever reviles Ali has reviled him.

n01808.summary: Ali (RA) tells Abu Saadiq that his lineage and his deen are the same as the Prophet's, so whoever reviles him reviles the Prophet.

n01809.summary: Abdur Rahmaan bin Isbahaani reports that the young Hasan (RA) asked Abu Bakr (RA) to leave the Prophet's pulpit, that Abu Bakr lifted him onto his lap and wept, and that Ali (RA) said he had not instructed it.

n01810.summary: Urwa (RA) reports that Hasan (RA) climbed the Prophet's pulpit during Abu Bakr's sermon, and Ali (RA) said it was done without his consultation.

n01811.summary: Husayn tells Umar to step down from his grandfather's pulpit; Ali threatens Husayn, Umar intercedes, and Umar later welcomes Husayn into his home and blesses him.

n01812.summary: Uqba bin Haarith describes how the Prophet comforted Hasan and Husayn, who were crying of thirst, by giving them his tongue to suck until they were quiet.

n01813.summary: Abu Hurayrah asks Hasan to show him the part of his belly the Prophet used to kiss, and then kisses that spot himself.

n01814.summary: Abu Hurayrah greets Hasan as 'my leader', explaining he heard the Prophet call him a leader.

n01815.summary: Marwaan objects to Abu Hurayrah's love for Hasan and Husayn; Abu Hurayrah answers with an account of the Prophet quieting the two thirsty children on a journey.

n01816.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas holds the stirrup for Zaid bin Thaabit, who protests; Abdullaah says this is how scholars and elders are honoured, and Zaid kisses his hand in honour of the Prophet's family.

n01817.summary: Sha'bi reports the same stirrup incident: Zaid bin Thaabit is served by Abdullaah bin Abbaas, who says this is how scholars and elders are honoured.

n01818.summary: Another report says Abdullaah bin Abbaas, holding Zaid bin Thaabit's stirrup, explained that they had been commanded to hold the stirrups of their teachers and seniors.

n01819.summary: Abu Umaamah reports that when the Prophet passed a drink to Abu Ubaydah, the eldest, he insisted that Abu Ubaydah drink first, and said that blessings lie with elders.

n01820.summary: Two Ansaar reports: after Abdullaah bin Sahl was murdered at Khaybar, the Prophet let the eldest speak first, offered the case to the Jews by oath, and paid the blood money himself when the Ansaar refused the oath.

n01821.summary: Waa'il bin Hujar says that he left his kingdom in Hadhramaut to come to the Prophet, who welcomed him, seated him beside himself on the pulpit and praised his sincerity before the people.

n01822.summary: In a second report, the Prophet tells the people to be kind to Waa'il bin Hujar, who has just left his royal background, and promises to repay him double for what his family took from him.

n01823.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas reports that the Prophet embraced the dying Sa'd bin Mu'aadh and prayed for him, and that the Prophet overruled criticism of Sa'd's mother reciting a lament, saying poets other than her lie.

n01824.summary: Khaarijah bin Zaid reports that Umar invited Mu'ayqeet, a leprosy-stricken Companion, close to sit and eat with him; a second report says Umar urged him to eat from the dish in front of him.

n01825.summary: Abdul Waahid bin Aun Dowsi reports that Tufayl bin Amr was martyred at Yamaamah, that his son Amr, who had lost a hand there, was embarrassed to eat with others, and that Umar insisted he eat and would not eat until Amr did.

n01826.summary: Hasan reports that Umar wrote to Abu Moosa Ash'ari instructing him to admit the people of virtue, status and character first, before the rest.

n01827.summary: On his deathbed, Qais bin Aasim advises his sons to fear Allaah, give leadership to their seniors, earn and invest wealth, avoid begging, not wail over him, and bury him where the Banu Bakr cannot find his grave.

n01828.summary: Yahya bin Sa'eed reports that Ali ordered his army at Jamal not to start the fighting; Abul Bakhtari reports that Ali called the opponents his brothers who had rebelled, neither polytheists nor hypocrites.

n01829.summary: Before the Battle of Jamal, Ali prays and orders his men not to pursue fleeing enemies, not to kill the wounded, and not to take their possessions.

n01830.summary: Marwaan bin Hakam tells Ali bin Husayn that he never saw a man so noble in victory as Ali, who at Jamal ordered that no fleeing or wounded man be killed.

n01831.summary: Ali says the men who fought him at Jamal were his brothers who rebelled, that he pardoned them, and that they were neither mushrikeen nor munaafiqeen.

n01833.summary: Abu Habeebah, freed slave of Talha, reports that after Jamal Ali welcomed Talha's son Imraan, spoke warmly of Talha, quoted the verse about brothers in Paradise, returned Talha's lands and rents, and rebuked two men who had criticised Talha and Zubayr.

n01834.summary: Rib'ee bin Hiraash adds that Ali shouted that the critics could only mean Talha and himself; Ibraheem reports that Ali refused to see Ibn Jurmooz, the killer of Zubayr, and said that Talha, Zubayr and he were among those promised brotherhood in Paradise.

n01835.summary: Amr bin Ghaalib reports that Ammaar bin Yaasir rebuked a man who spoke ill of Aa'isha, saying she is the Prophet's wife in Paradise; a second report adds that Ammaar called him an insulter of the Prophet's beloved.

n01836.summary: Ammaar bin Yaasir says that Aa'isha is the Prophet's wife in this world and the next, and that Allaah used her to test whether the believers obey Him or her.

n01837.summary: Abu Waa'il reports that Ali sent Ammaar bin Yaasir and Hasan bin Ali to Kufa to rally people, and Ammaar told them that Aa'isha is the Prophet's wife in this world and the next, and that Allaah was testing whether they obeyed Him or her.

n01838.summary: Zaid bin Wahab reports that Abdullaah bin Mas'ood told him that Allaah assisted the Prophet when the disbelievers drove him out, and quoted the verse of the cave, where Abu Bakr was with him, to show Abu Bakr's rank.

n01839.summary: Umar seizes a man who mocked Abu Dardaa, brings him to the Prophet, and the verse about 'only joking' is revealed.

n01840.summary: Umar rebukes a group who said he was the best after the Prophet, insisting Abu Bakr was purer than musk and that Awf had told the truth.

n01842.summary: Umar declares that Abu Bakr is the best of this Ummah after its Nabi and that anyone who claims otherwise is a slanderer to be punished.

n01843.summary: Umar whips a man who said Umar was the best of this Ummah after its Nabi, insisting that Abu Bakr is better than him.

n01844.summary: Ali rebukes a man who asked why the Muhaajireen and Ansaar ranked Abu Bakr above him, and lists four virtues of Abu Bakr, quoting the verse about the cave.

n01845.summary: Mughierah bin Shu'bah reports that when a man from the Ansaar insulted Abu Bakr, the Khalifah, he struck him, and Abu Bakr refused to let the Ansaar take retribution, preferring exile to letting them harm a man who restrains others from evil.

n01846.summary: Abu Waa'il reports that Ibn Mas'ood told a man to lift his garment; when the man retorted that Ibn Mas'ood also wore his high, Ibn Mas'ood explained his thin calves. Umar then struck the man for insolence. Alaa reports that Umar threw a brick at a Quraysh man who suggested he hire someone to build for him, saying he did not want to dislike Ibn Mas'ood.

n01847.summary: Abu Waa'il reports that Umar had a man who swore an oath against Ummu Salamah, who owed him money, lashed thirty stripes.

n01848.summary: Ummu Moosa reports that when Ibn Saba claimed Ali was superior to Abu Bakr and Umar, Ali wanted him executed, but accepted a ruling that he should simply not be allowed to live in Ali's town.

n01849.summary: Ibraheem reports that Ali, on hearing that Abdullaah bin Aswad had belittled Abu Bakr and Umar, reached for a sword to execute him, but was persuaded to exile him to Shaam instead.

n01850.summary: Katheer reports that a man praised Ali as the best of people; Ali asked whether he had seen the Prophet, Abu Bakr or Umar, and said that a claim to have seen the Prophet deserves execution and a claim to have seen Abu Bakr or Umar deserves lashing.

n01851.summary: Alqamah reports Ali's lecture that the best after the Prophet is Abu Bakr, then Umar. A second report from Suwayd bin Ghaflah has Ali praising Abu Bakr and Umar, describing Abu Bakr's nomination to lead prayer and Umar's appointment by consultation, and warning against reviling them.

n01852.summary: Abu Is'haaq reports that a man called Uthmaan a sinner for introducing new practices, and Ali asked him whether Allaah had selected Uthmaan to marry the Prophet's daughters, then warned the man to say nothing else.

n01853.summary: Saalim reports that his father, Abdullaah bin Umar, rebuked a companion who complained about Uthmaan, reminding them that during the Prophet's time they named Abu Bakr, Umar and Uthmaan together, and that the complaint arose only when wealth became the priority.

n01854.summary: Aamir bin Sa'd reports that Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas warned a man against reviling Ali, Talha and Zubayr, then prayed that Allaah would show the man His power; a camel then trampled him, and the people hailed Sa'd's prayer as accepted.

n01855.summary: Mus'ab bin Sa'd reports that when a man reviled Ali, Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas cursed him, a camel killed the man, and Sa'd then freed a slave and vowed never to curse anyone again.

n01856.summary: Qais bin Abu Haazim reports that Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas, finding a man reviling Ali in the Madinah marketplace, listed Ali's virtues and prayed that the gathering be shown Allaah's power; the ground swallowed the man's mount and he died.

n01857.summary: Rabaah bin Haarith reports that Sa'eed bin Zaid objected to a Kufan who swore at Ali while sitting with Mughiera bin Shu'ba, and cited the Prophet's words that ten people, including Ali, would enter Paradise; a second report from Abdullaah bin Dhaalim says Sa'eed warned Mughiera's orators against reviling Ali.

n01858.summary: Ibn Seereen reports that Suhayb wept aloud over Umar's stabbing, and Umar reminded him of the Prophet's words that the person over whom people wail is punished. Abu Burdah reports the same. Miqdaam bin Ma'dikarib reports that Hafsa wailed, and Umar forbade her to wail over him.

n01859.summary: Abdul Malik bin Zaid reports that Sa'eed bin Zaid wept, saying Islaam had suffered a void at Umar's death that would never be filled. Abu Waa'il reports that Ibn Mas'ood wept more than ever at Umar's death and said even thorny trees were distressed by it.

n01860.summary: Abu Uthmaan reports that when Umar heard of Nu'maan bin Muqarrin's death, he put his hands on his head and wept.

n01861.summary: Abul Ash'ath San'aani reports that Thumaamah bin Adi, governor of San'aa, wept when he heard of Uthmaan's death, saying the caliphate on the pattern of prophethood had ended and that kingship and tyranny would follow.

n01862.summary: Three reports on the death of Uthmaan: Zaid bin Thaabit wept for him on the day he was martyred in his home; Abu Hurayrah wept whenever it was mentioned; Abu Humayd Saa'idi, a Badr veteran, vowed never to laugh again until he met Allaah.

n01863.summary: Abu Sa'eed Khudri says that they had hardly left the burial when they found a change in their hearts.

n01864.summary: Ubay bin Ka'b said that after the Prophet passed away, the Companions who had been united while with him began looking in different directions.

n01865.summary: Anas bin Maalik said Madinah turned dark on the day the Prophet passed away, and recalled that the day he entered Madinah was the brightest day and the day of his death the darkest.

n01867.summary: Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas said that when the Mushrikeen asked the Prophet to drive away the poor Sahabah, among them Bilaal and Ibn Mas'ood, Allaah revealed the verse forbidding him to do so.

n01868.summary: Ibn Mas'ood reports that when a group of the Quraysh asked the Prophet to drive away poor Muslims such as Suhayb, Bilaal, Khabbaab and Ammaar, Allaah revealed Surah An'aam verses 51 and 52.

n01869.summary: Anas and Aa'isha report that while the Prophet was inviting Ubay bin Khalaf to Islaam, the blind Ibn Umm Maktoom came to him, and that Surah Abasa was revealed; afterwards the Prophet always honoured Ibn Umm Maktoom.

n01870.summary: Khabbaab bin Arat relates that Aqra and Uyayna asked the Prophet to send away the poor Sahabah before the delegations saw them, and that Allaah revealed verses commanding him to stay with them, after which the Companions sat close to him.

n01871.summary: Salmaan reports that Uyayna and Aqra asked the Prophet to move the poor Muslims in woollen cloaks away from him so they could sit and learn with him, and that Allaah revealed Surah Kahf verses 27 and 28 forbidding him to obey such people.

n01872.summary: Abu Salma reports that Qais bin Mataatiyyah belittled Salmaan, Suhayb and Bilaal, and that Mu'aadh seized him and brought him to the Prophet, who told the people that all are of one Rabb, one father and one Deen, and that Arabic makes no one superior, and said to leave the man to the Fire.

n01873.summary: Buraydah reports that a man asked whether he had repaid his mother by carrying her on his neck across scorching sands, and the Prophet said it may have repaid only a single labour pain.

n01874.summary: Aa'isha reports that when a man came with his elderly father, the Prophet told him never to walk or sit before his father, never to call him by name, and never to make him the target of abuse.

n01875.summary: Abu Ghassaan Dhabi says that Abu Hurayrah met him walking with his father and advised him to walk behind or beside his father, not to let anyone come between them, not to walk on an unrailed roof, and not to eat meat his father was eyeing.

n01876.summary: Abdullaah bin Amr reports that when a man asked to join Jihaad, the Prophet asked whether his parents were alive and told him that his Jihaad was to be with them.

n01877.summary: Three reports say that men who wished to migrate or wage Jihaad were told to return to their parents and be good to them, and a man from Yemen was told he could fight only with his parents' permission.

n01878.summary: Anas reports that a man who wanted to march in Jihaad but lacked the means was told that serving his mother would bring him the reward of Hajj, Umrah and Jihaad.

n01879.summary: Abu Umaamah reports that when the Prophet called the Muslims to march on Khaybar, Abu Hurayrah stayed behind to care for his mother, and the Prophet told him that being with his parents and fulfilling their rights is also in the path of Allaah.

n01880.summary: Ibn Abbaas reports that a woman brought her son, who wanted to join Jihaad, to the Prophet at Siqaayah, and the Prophet told him to stay with his mother until she permitted him or died, as that would earn him greater reward.

n01881.summary: A narration states that a man wanting to fight in Jihaad, whose mother was against it, was told by the Prophet to stay close to her, as his reward with her would equal the reward of Jihaad.

n01882.summary: Talha bin Mu'aawiya Sulami reports that he asked the Prophet's permission to wage Jihaad, and was told to stay at his mother's feet because Jannah lies there.

n01883.summary: Jaahimah reports that when he came to the Prophet for advice about Jihaad, he was asked whether his parents were alive, and was told to stay with them because Jannah lies beneath their feet.

n01884.summary: Jaahimah recounts asking the Prophet about Jihaad, being told to stay with his mother because Jannah lies beneath her feet, and receiving the same answer on repeated asking.

n01885.summary: Nu'aym reports that Abdullaah bin Umar, sitting beneath a tree between Makkah and Madinah, recalled seeing a young man ask the Prophet to join Jihaad and being told to go back and be good to his parents.

n01886.summary: Hasan narrates that when Umar proposed for Ummu Kulthoom, Ali said she was too young; after Umar cited his kinship with the Prophet and Ali's sons objected, Ali told them to get the proposer married.

n01887.summary: Ibn Seereen reports that when a date palm's sap was prized at a thousand dirhams, Usaama bored into a palm and gave the sap to his mother because she had asked for it.

n01888.summary: Abdullaah bin Amr reports that the Prophet came down from the pulpit to lift Husayn after the child tripped on his cloth during the sermon, saying that children are a trial.

n01889.summary: Abu Sa'eed and Zubayr report that Hasan climbed onto the Prophet's back while he was in sajdah, and the Prophet did not rise or move him until the boy chose to get down.

n01891.summary: Bahiy reports that Ibn Zubayr described Hasan as the grandson most like the Prophet and most beloved to him, who would climb onto his back during salaah and be left there until he got down.

n01892.summary: Ibn Mas'ood and Anas report that Hasan and Husayn would climb onto the Prophet's back during sajdah, and that he prolonged the sajdah, saying he did not like to rise quickly while his grandsons were on him.

n01894.summary: Abu Hurayrah reports that the Prophet came out carrying Hasan on one shoulder and Husayn on the other, kissing each in turn, and said that whoever loves them loves him and whoever hates them hates him.

n01895.summary: Mu'aawiya reports that he saw the Prophet suck Hasan's tongue and said that a tongue or lips the Prophet had sucked could never suffer punishment.

n01896.summary: Saa'ib bin Yazeed reports that when the Prophet kissed Hasan, Aqra said he had ten children and had never kissed one of them, and the Prophet replied that Allaah does not show mercy to those who do not show mercy to people.

n01897.summary: Aswad bin Khalaf reports that the Prophet kissed Hasan and said that a child makes a man miserly, foolish and cowardly, because he fears for the child's welfare.

n01898.summary: Anas reports that the Prophet was the most compassionate towards his family and visited his son Ibraheem, who was nursed at a blacksmith's home, kissing and smelling the child.

n01899.summary: Anas reports that after Aa'isha told the Prophet how a mother split her last date between her two daughters, he said she would surely enter Jannah for that deed.

n01900.summary: Hasan bin Ali reports that the Prophet gave a mother's two sons one date each and that she split her own date between them, and he said Allaah would show her mercy; Abu Hurayrah then reports the Prophet asking a father whether he is merciful to his child.

n01901.summary: The Prophet rebukes a man who kissed his son and seated him on his lap but only seated his daughter in front of him, telling him to treat his children equally.

n01902.summary: Mu'aawiya bin Haydah asks the Prophet about the rights of neighbours and is told how to visit, help, congratulate and support a neighbour.

n01903.summary: A man complains to the Prophet about a troublesome neighbour; after advice to be patient, the Prophet tells him to put his belongings on the street and states the duties owed to neighbours and guests.

n01904.summary: The Prophet bars a man who had urinated against his neighbour's wall from joining a military expedition.

n01905.summary: Miqdaad reports that the Prophet asked the Sahabah about adultery and theft, and said that both are more serious when committed against one's neighbour than against others.

n01906.summary: Mutarrif reports Abu Dharr's hadith that Allaah loves three kinds of people, beginning with one who fights with steadfastness in the path of Allaah; the passage then gives Aa'isha's account of the Prophet's teaching to treat people according to their status.

n01907.summary: Rabaah bin Rabee recounts that on the Prophet's advice two Companions let him ride their camel and took turns walking, because a righteous travel companion should be treated well.

n01908.summary: Aa'isha explains that she invited a prominent man to eat with her but gave a passing beggar only bread, because the Prophet told them to treat people according to their status.

n01909.summary: Variant accounts of Aa'isha's practice of treating a rich man and a beggar differently, based on the Prophet's instruction; the text cross-refers to Ali's earlier similar act.

n01910.summary: Aghar reports that Abu Bakr greeted everyone he saw from afar with salaam before they could greet him, and Zuhrah bin Khameesa reports Abu Bakr saying people had outdone them in returning greetings.

n01911.summary: Umar reports riding behind Abu Bakr, who greeted every group they passed, and that the replies were fuller than the greeting, prompting Abu Bakr to remark that people had surpassed them greatly that day.

n01912.summary: Abu Umaamah urged patience and recalled how the Companions greeted each other with Salaam even when a tree separated them, as Anas reports.

n01914.summary: Tufayl bin Ubay reports that Abdullaah bin Umar greeted everyone he met in the marketplace and went there only for the sake of Salaam.

n01915.summary: Abu Umaamah greets everyone with Salaam and tells a Jew who beat him to it that the Prophet said Salaam is a greeting for the Ummah and a security for non-Muslims under Muslim rule.

n01916.summary: Muhammad bin Ziyaad reports that Abu Umaamah greeted every Muslim, Christian and child he passed and urged his nephew to spread Salaam among Muslims.

n01917.summary: Basheer bin Yasaar says that no one ever beat Abdullaah bin Umar to making Salaam.

n01918.summary: Salmaan reports that the Prophet answered a greeting in full and, when asked why he answered differently for later greeters, cited Surah Nisaa on returning a greeting in kind.

n01919.summary: The Prophet tells Aa'isha that Jibra'eel sends her Salaams, and Jibra'eel blesses the Ahlul Bayt.

n01920.summary: Anas and other Companions report that the Prophet sought permission at the door of Sa'd bin Ubaadah, who answered each Salaam softly and then served him olive oil and received his du'aa.

n01921.summary: Anas reports that the Prophet greeted the children of the Ansaar and, at Sa'd bin Ubaadah's door, greeted three times before leaving, and Sa'd ran after him as in the previous narration.

n01922.summary: Umar complains to Abu Bakr that Uthmaan did not return his greeting, and Uthmaan explains he was lost in thought about Shaytaan's whisperings, so Abu Bakr relates the Prophet's teaching that the Kalimah is the salvation of this Ummah.

n01923.summary: Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas says Uthmaan did not return his greeting; Uthmaan explains he was thinking of the Prophet's du'aa of Yunus, which the Prophet taught.

n01924.summary: Ash'ath bin Qais and Jareer bin Abdullaah visit Salmaan Faarsi with a message from Abu Dardaa; Salmaan refuses their offer of wealth and accepts only the greeting Abu Dardaa sent.

n01925.summary: Jundub reports that the Prophet never shook hands before first greeting, Abu Dharr says the Prophet always shook his hand, and Hasan reports Umar embracing his companions after Fajr.

n01926.summary: Hudhayfah turns away from the Prophet's handshake because he is in a state of impurity, and the Prophet says that sins fall away when Muslims shake hands.

n01927.summary: Anas reports the Companions asked whether they could bow, embrace or shake hands, and Aa'isha describes the Prophet rushing out to embrace Zaid bin Haaritha when he returned to Madinah.

n01928.summary: Anas reports that the Prophet forbade bowing and embracing a brother, but allowed shaking his hand.

n01929.summary: The Prophet allows embracing and kissing only after a journey, and Aa'isha describes him rushing to embrace Zaid bin Haaritha when Zaid arrived in Madinah.

n01931.summary: Anas says the Companions shook hands on meeting and embraced on returning from a journey, and Hasan relates how Umar hurried to embrace a companion after Fajr.

n01933.summary: Urwa reports that when Umar reached Shaam he dismounted and embraced Abu Ubaydah on his arrival.

n01934.summary: Sha'bi reports that the Prophet embraced Ja'far bin Abi Taalib and kissed him between the eyes on his return from Khaybar.

n01935.summary: Abdur Rahmaan bin Razeen reports that Salamah bin Akwa showed the hand he had pledged allegiance with, and the people kissed it without his stopping them.

n01936.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports that he kissed the Prophet's hands.

n01937.summary: Umar reports that he kissed the Prophet's hands.

n01939.summary: Zaari bin Aamir and Mazeedah Abdi report that visitors kissed the Prophet's hands, and that Ashaj kissed them too, and the Prophet told Ashaj that Allah and His Messenger love two of his qualities.

n01940.summary: Abu Rajaa saw Umar kissing Abu Bakr's head in Madinah for his stand against those who refused to pay zakaah.

n01941.summary: Tameem bin Salamah reports that Abu Ubaydah welcomed Umar in Shaam, shook his hand and kissed it, and that kissing the hand of pious people is Sunnah.

n01942.summary: Yahya bin Haarith asks Waathilah bin Asqa whether he pledged allegiance to the Prophet with those hands, and then kisses his hand.

n01943.summary: Yunus bin Maysarah reports that Yazeed bin Aswad, when ill, took Waathilah bin Asqa's hand and rubbed it on his face, and Waathilah told him the hadith that Allah treats His slaves according to their expectation of Him.

n01944.summary: Abdur Rahmaan bin Razeen reports that Salamah bin Akwa showed them his large hand, the one he pledged with, and they stood and kissed it.

n01945.summary: Abu Jad'aan reports that Thaabit Bunaani asked Anas whether he had touched the Prophet's hand, and when Anas said he had, Thaabit kissed his hand.

n01946.summary: Suhayb says he saw Ali kiss the hand and feet of Abbaas.

n01947.summary: Aa'isha describes how Faatima most resembled the Prophet in speech and manner, how he welcomed and kissed her, and what passed between them during his final illness.

n01948.summary: Hilaal reports that whenever the Prophet left a gathering, the Companions stood up for him and did not sit until he had entered his room.

n01949.summary: Abu Umaamah says that when the Prophet came out leaning on his staff and the Companions stood for him, the Prophet told them not to stand as non-Arabs stand for one another.

n01950.summary: When Abu Bakr urged the Companions to stand up for the Prophet against a hypocrite, the Prophet said none should stand, since only Allaah deserves that.

n01951.summary: Anas says the Companions loved seeing the Prophet more than anyone, yet did not stand up for him, because they knew he disliked it.

n01952.summary: Naafi reports that the Prophet forbade a man from making another stand up and then sit in his place, so Abdullaah bin Umar would not sit where someone had stood for him.

n01953.summary: Abu Khaalid Waalibi reports that Ali rebuked the Companions who stood waiting for him with their chests out like soldiers.

n01955.summary: Waathila bin Khattaab reports that the Prophet moved from his place in the Masjid for a man who entered, and Waathila bin Asqa reports the same and that Abu Bakr moved for Ali.

n01956.summary: Katheer bin Murra found Awf bin Maalik Ashja'ee folding in his outstretched legs in a gathering, saying he had stretched them out so that a pious person would come and sit there.

n01957.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas said that the person he respects most is the one sitting with him, and two chains report his words.

n01958.summary: Ali gave two visitors cushions and told the man sitting on the ground to take the cushion, since only a donkey refuses hospitality.

n01959.summary: Umar reports that Abu Bakr gave him no reply when he proposed Hafsah to him, because he had heard the Prophet mention a proposal and kept the secret, and then Umar married Hafsah to the Prophet.

n01960.summary: Anas refuses to tell his mother the Prophet's secret errand and tells Thaabit Bunaani that he would trust no one else with it.

n01961.summary: Abu Hurayrah reports that when a man complained of a hard heart, the Prophet told him to stroke an orphan's head and feed the poor.

n01962.summary: Abu Dardaa reports the Prophet's advice to a man with a hard heart: show mercy to an orphan, stroke his head and feed him, which will soften the heart and fulfil needs.

n01963.summary: Basheer bin Aqrabah reports that on the day of Uhud, after his father was martyred, the Prophet comforted him, stroked his head and offered to be his father and Aa'isha his mother.

n01964.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar gives his donkey and his turban to a Bedouin whose father had been a friend of Umar, citing the Prophet's teaching to keep ties with a father's friends.

n01965.summary: Another narration adds that when someone asked whether two dirhams would not suffice, Abdullaah bin Umar cited the Prophet's command to care for a father's associates.

n01966.summary: Abu Usayd Saa'idi reports the Prophet's advice on how to treat parents after their death: make du'aa and seek forgiveness for them, fulfil their promises, keep their ties and honour their friends.

n01967.summary: Ziyaad bin An'am reports that Abu Ayyoob Ansaari, while fasting, accepted an invitation to a meal because the Prophet said a Muslim owes six rights to his brother.

n01968.summary: Umar and Uthmaan accepted a meal invitation, but Umar wished he had not gone, fearing it was hosted for show; later Uthmaan accepted Mughiera bin Shu'ba's wedding invitation while fasting, to pray for blessings.

n01970.summary: Mu'aawiya bin Qurra says Ma'qal Muzani removed an obstacle from the road and told him, quoting the Prophet, that removing an obstacle from the Muslims' path earns a good deed and that whoever has a single good deed accepted enters Jannah.

n01971.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports that when the Prophet sneezed while sitting with the Sahabah and they answered Yarhamukallah, he prayed that Allaah guide them and set their affairs right.

n01972.summary: Aa'isha reports that a man who sneezed in the Prophet's presence asked what he should say, and the Prophet taught him the words for his own sneeze and for the reply to it.

n01973.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood says the Prophet taught the Sahabah to respond whenever someone sneezed.

n01974.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood describes the Prophet's teaching: the sneezer says Alhamdulillah, those present say Yarhamukallah, and the sneezer replies with a prayer for their guidance and the setting right of their affairs.

n01975.summary: Umm Salamah reports that the Prophet replied to a sneezer who said Alhamdulillah, and said that a second sneezer who gave a longer praise had surpassed the first by nineteen stages.

n01977.summary: Abu Burdah reports that his father Abu Moosa Ash'ari did not reply to his sneeze because he had not said Alhamdulillah, but did reply to a woman's sneeze that did, and his mother approved.

n01978.summary: Makhool Azdi reports that when someone sneezed in the Masjid, Abdullaah bin Umar said Yarhamukallah only if the sneezer had said Alhamdulillah.

n01979.summary: Naafi reports that whenever someone answered Abdullaah bin Umar's sneeze with Yarhamukallah, Abdullaah bin Umar replied with a prayer for their mercy and forgiveness.

n01980.summary: Naafi reports that Abdullaah bin Umar rebuked a man who said Alhamdulillah on sneezing for not sending salutations on the Prophet as well.

n01981.summary: Dahhaak bin Qais Yashkari reports that Abdullaah bin Umar asked a man who had said Alhamdulillah on sneezing why he had not completed it by sending salutations on the Prophet.

n01982.summary: Abu Jamara reports hearing Abdullaah bin Abbaas reply to someone's sneeze with a prayer for their mercy and forgiveness.

n01983.summary: Zaid bin Arqam says the Prophet visited him when he was suffering from an eye infection.

n01984.summary: Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas says that when he fell gravely ill in the year of the Farewell Hajj and wished to give away most of his wealth, the Prophet advised a third, and told him that what he spends for Allaah's pleasure is rewarded, even a morsel placed in his wife's mouth.

n01985.summary: Jaabir bin Abdillaah says that when he was unconscious from illness, the Prophet and Abu Bakr visited him, and he asked how to dispose of his wealth but got no answer until the verses of inheritance were revealed.

n01986.summary: Usaama bin Zaid recounts the Prophet riding to visit Sa'd bin Ubaadah past a gathering that included Abdullaah bin Ubay, and Abu Faakhita relates Abu Moosa visiting Hasan and Ali's hadith on the reward for visiting the sick.

n01987.summary: Ibn Abbaas relates that the Prophet visited a villager with fever and said it would cleanse his sins; the villager said it would kill him, and he died of it.

n01988.summary: Aa'isha describes the fever of Abu Bakr and Bilaal on arriving in Madinah, the couplets they recited, and the Prophet's du'aa that Madinah be made beloved and healthy.

n01989.summary: Abu Hurayrah reports that the Prophet asked who had fasted, visited a sick person, followed a funeral and fed a poor person that day, and Abu Bakr had done all four, so the Prophet said such a person enters Jannah.

n01990.summary: Abdullaah bin Naafi reports that Abu Moosa Ash'ari visited ailing Hasan bin Ali, and Ali relates the reward for visiting a sick Muslim morning or evening.

n01991.summary: Abu Musa Ash'ari visits the ailing Hasan, and Ali confirms the Prophet's saying on the reward of visiting a sick Muslim brother.

n01992.summary: Abdullaah bin Yasaar reports that Ali objected to Amr bin Hurayth visiting the ailing Hasan bin Ali when Amr's opinion opposed his, and then reminded Amr of the Prophet's hadith on the seventy thousand angels who pray for the one who visits the sick.

n01993.summary: Sa'eed reports that he was with Salmaan when they visited a sick man in Kindah, and Salmaan said a believer's illness brings forgiveness, while a sinner's is like a camel tied and released without knowing why.

n01994.summary: Sa'eed bin Wahab reports the same visit with Salmaan to a sick Kindah man, with the same comparison of a believer's illness to forgiveness and a sinner's to a released camel.

n01995.summary: Naafi reports that whenever Abdullaah bin Umar visited a sick person he asked how they were, and on leaving he only prayed that Allaah give them the best.

n01996.summary: Abdullaah bin Abu Hudhayl reports that Abdullaah bin Mas'ood rebuked a man who stared at a woman in the house of a sick person, saying it would be better for him if his eye burst.

n01997.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas reports that when the Prophet visited a sick person he sat by his head and recited a prayer seven times asking the Majestic Allaah to cure him, and the person recovered if his time had not yet come.

n01998.summary: Ali reports the prayer the Prophet said whenever he visited a sick person, asking the Lord of mankind to remove the difficulty and grant a cure that only He can give.

n01999.summary: Another narration adds words to the Prophet's prayer for the sick, asking for a cure that leaves no illness.

n02000.summary: Ali reports that when the Prophet visited a sick person he placed his right hand on the person's right cheek and prayed for a cure.

n02001.summary: Anas reports the prayer the Prophet said for a sick person, asking the Lord of mankind to remove the difficulty and grant a cure that leaves no illness.

n02002.summary: Aa'isha reports that when the Prophet visited a sick person he placed his hand on the part of the body that was in pain before saying a prayer.

n02003.summary: Salmaan says the Prophet visited him when he was ill and prayed that Allaah ease his difficulty, forgive his sins and grant him well-being in his Deen and body until death.

n02004.summary: Aa'isha reports that whenever the Prophet went to see a sick person, or a sick person was brought to him, he prayed for a cure in the same words.

n02005.summary: Aa'isha reports that she passed the Prophet's hand over his body with protective words as he lay dying, and he drew his hand away and asked Allaah to forgive him and let him meet the Highest Friend.

n02006.summary: Anas reports that when the Prophet gave Salaam to seek permission to enter a home he did so three times, and when he said something important he repeated it three times.

n02007.summary: Qais bin Sa'd narrates that when the Prophet visited his father's house and gave Salaam, his father Sa'd bin Ubaadah answered quietly so that he could hear more Salaams, then hosted him with food, a shawl and a donkey.

n02008.summary: Rib'ee bin Hiraash reports a man of Banu Aamir who asked permission to enter without first giving Salaam, and the Prophet had a slave girl teach him the greeting, after which he was admitted.

n02009.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas reports that Umar asked permission with Salaam to enter the Prophet's upper room, and Abu Hurayrah reports that the Companions asked permission when they came after being summoned.

n02010.summary: Safeenah reports that when Ali came to the Prophet's room and knocked very lightly, the Prophet had the door opened for him.

n02011.summary: Sa'd bin Ubaadah reports that the Prophet told him not to seek permission while standing directly in front of the door, because asking permission is meant to protect the sight.

n02012.summary: Anas bin Maalik reports that when a man peeped into one of the Prophet's rooms, the Prophet stood up with an arrowhead in his hand as if looking for a chance to strike him.

n02013.summary: Sahl bin Sa'd reports that the Prophet rebuked a man who peeped through the door of his room, saying that seeking permission exists to protect the sight.

n02014.summary: Abu Sa'eed Khudri describes how Abu Moosa, refused entry three times by Umar, left, and how Umar demanded a witness before Ubay bin Ka'b and Abu Sa'eed confirmed the Prophet's ruling.

n02016.summary: Aamir bin Abdullaah reports that Umar refused a slave girl entry and sent after her, and that Hudhayfah warned a man who asked whether he must seek permission even from his mother.

n02017.summary: Umar asks to see Zaid while a slave girl is combing Zaid's hair, and Zaid comes to him; separately Abdullaah bin Mas'ood veils his wife when people ask to see him.

n02018.summary: Musa bin Talha is struck by his father for entering without permission, and Hudhayfah warns a man who was peeping in before asking to enter.

n02019.summary: Suwayd Abdi reports that Abdullaah bin Umar questioned him about peeping into his room, and that when asked about Jihaad, Abdullaah answered that whoever wages Jihaad does so for his own benefit.

n02020.summary: Baraa bin Aazib reports that the Prophet named loving and hating for Allaah's sake as the strongest link of Imaan, and Abu Dharr reports the Prophet saying the same deed is the most beloved to Allaah.

n02021.summary: Aa'isha and Uthmaan bin Abil Aas report that the Prophet loved the people of taqwa, and that he held Abdullaah bin Mas'ood and Ammaar bin Yaasir dear until his death.

n02022.summary: Amr bin Al Aas says he cannot tell whether the Prophet appointed him out of real affection or only to ease his heart, and names Abdullaah bin Mas'ood and Ammaar bin Yaasir as the two men the Prophet loved most.

n02023.summary: Amr bin Al Aas is told that Ammaar, whom the Prophet loved, was killed at Siffeen by their side, and he admits it.

n02024.summary: Usaamah bin Zaid reports the Prophet naming Usaamah and then Ali as the family members he loved most, and Amr bin Al Aas reports the Prophet naming Aa'isha, Abu Bakr and Abu Ubaydah as the people he loved most.

n02026.summary: Anas reports that a Companion was told by the Prophet to tell a man he liked for Allaah's sake that he liked him, and that the man prayed for him in return.

n02027.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar tells how, on the Prophet's instruction, he told a man he liked him for Allaah's sake.

n02028.summary: Abdullaah bin Sarjas tells the Prophet he likes Abu Dharr, is told to tell him, does so, and the Prophet says that even mentioning it carries great reward.

n02029.summary: Mujaahid reports that Abdullaah bin Abbaas said a passing man liked him a lot, and explained that he liked the man in return.

n02030.summary: Mujaahid reports a Sahabi who told him he loved him for Allaah's sake and offered his daughter in marriage, and then reports Abdullaah bin Umar's saying that friendships and enmities must be for Allaah's sake.

n02031.summary: Auf bin Tufayl reports that Aa'isha vowed never to speak to Abdullaah bin Zubayr after he remarked on her charity, until Miswar and Abdur Rahmaan brought about reconciliation; Urwa bin Zubayr adds that she freed forty slaves as expiation.

n02032.summary: Sahl bin Sa'd reports that the people of Quba fell into a dispute that led to stone-throwing, and that the Prophet went to settle it; another report says the same of the Banu Amr bin Auf.

n02033.summary: Anas reports that Abdullaah bin Ubay insulted the Prophet's donkey, the two sides quarrelled and fought, and the Prophet calmed them; Anas says this is the occasion of the revelation on reconciling believers.

n02034.summary: Anas reports that the Aws and the Khazraj, who had been enemies, fought over a quarrel of poetry, and that the Prophet stopped them by reciting the verses on unity and the fear of Allaah.

n02035.summary: Haaroon bin Rabaab reports that Abdullaah bin Amr, on his deathbed, asked people to find a man to whom he had promised his daughter and married her to him, so as not to meet Allaah with a broken promise.

n02036.summary: Anas reports that a Sahabi disliked a passing man, and after questioning the man's neighbour and the Sahabi, the Prophet said the man was the better of the two.

n02037.summary: Ubaadah bin Saamit reports that a man from the Banu Layth asked the Prophet's permission three times, then recited a poem praising the Prophet, and the Prophet approved it.

n02038.summary: Khallaad bin Saa'ib reports that Usaamah bin Zaid praised him to his face, explaining that the Prophet said praise given to a believer's face increases his Imaan.

n02039.summary: The father of Mutarrif reports that a delegation from the Banu Aamir praised the Prophet, and he told them to speak more simply and not overstep the limits of praise.

n02040.summary: Another narration says the Prophet asked not to be raised above the rank Allaah gave him, describing himself as the servant of Allaah and His Rasul.

n02041.summary: Anas reports that someone called the Prophet the best of people and the son of the best, and the Prophet corrected him to say only what he was told and to keep to the limits Allaah set.

n02042.summary: Abu Bakrah reports that the Prophet rebuked a man who praised another in front of him, and taught that one should say only that he believes a person to be righteous, since only Allaah knows.

n02043.summary: Abu Moosa reports that the Prophet, hearing someone overstate his praise for another, told him that he had broken the man's back.

n02044.summary: Rajaa reports that Buraydah Aslami joked to Mihjin Aslami about the long prayer of Sabkah, and that the Prophet forbade Mihjin from praising the man in his hearing and said the best deed of the religion is the easiest.

n02045.summary: Another report from Rajaa says the Prophet told Mihjin to stop praising the worshipper, repeated that the best deed of the religion is the easiest, and said Allaah wants ease for this nation.

n02046.summary: Ibraheem Taymi reports that Umar rebuked a man who praised another to his face, saying he had slaughtered him and asking how one can praise a man's Deen to his face.

n02047.summary: Hasan reports that when someone praised Umar, Umar said the praiser was destroying both himself and Umar.

n02048.summary: Hasan reports that Umar struck Jaarood with a whip after a remark that Jaarood was the leader of the Rabee'ah, explaining that he wanted to remove any pride that might settle in Jaarood's heart.

n02049.summary: Hammaam reports that Miqdaad threw pebbles in the face of a man praising Uthmaan, quoting the Prophet's command to throw sand at those who praise for ulterior motives.

n02050.summary: Another narration says Miqdaad threw sand on the face of a man who was heaping praise on one of the Khalifahs, citing the Prophet's command.

n02051.summary: Ataa bin Abi Rabaah reports that Abdullaah bin Umar threw sand at the mouth of a man who praised another in his presence, quoting the Prophet's instruction.

n02052.summary: Ataa bin Abi Rabaah reports that Abdullaah bin Umar threw sand at the mouth of a man who praised Abdullaah himself, citing the Prophet's words.

n02053.summary: Naafi reports that when someone called Abdullaah bin Umar the best of people, Abdullaah replied that he was only a servant of Allaah, and that people keep praising a man until they destroy him.

n02054.summary: Taariq bin Shihaab reports that Abdullaah bin Umar warned that a man can leave home with his Deen intact and return without it after swearing praise of a powerless man in the hope of gain.

n02055.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas reports that during a famine before the Prophet's mission, the Prophet and Abbaas took in Ali and Ja'far, while Abu Taalib kept Aqeel.

n02056.summary: Jaabir reports that when Juwayriyyah wanted to free one of her slaves, the Prophet advised giving the slave to an uncle among the Bedouin instead, for a greater reward.

n02057.summary: Abu Sa'eed Khudri reports that when the verse on giving the relative his due was revealed, the Prophet told Faatima she could have his land at Fidak.

n02058.summary: Abu Hurayrah reports a man who complained that his relatives cut ties with him, and the Prophet told him that an angel stays with him as long as he keeps treating them well.

n02059.summary: Abdullaah bin Amr reports a man who complained that his relatives cut ties with him, and the Prophet told him to take the better course and keep up the bonds of kinship.

n02060.summary: Abu Hurayrah warns that the deeds of anyone who severs family ties are not accepted, and a young man who had been estranged from his aunt for two years goes to ask him why.

n02061.summary: A'mash reports that Abdullaah bin Mas'ood asked those who sever family ties to leave a gathering before he made du'aa, since the doors of heaven are closed to them.

n02062.summary: Sa'd bin Hishaam reports that when he asked Aa'isha about the Prophet's character, she replied that his character was the Qur'aan.

n02063.summary: Qataadah says the Qur'aan brought every noble trait, and Abu Dardaa reports that Aa'isha described the Prophet's character as the Qur'aan, being pleased with what Allaah is pleased with.

n02065.summary: Zaid bin Baabnoos reports that when people asked Aa'isha about the Prophet's character, she told them to read from Surah Mu'minoon and said that was his character.

n02066.summary: Aa'isha says there was none with better character than the Prophet, and the report goes on to a garbled account of his dealings with the Jews of Khaybar.

n02067.summary: Khaarijah bin Zaid reports that Zaid bin Thaabit described how the Prophet joined in every kind of conversation with his companions, whether about worldly matters, the Aakhirah or food.

n02068.summary: Safiyya bint Huyay says she never saw anyone with better character than the Prophet, recalling how he gently woke her on the journey back from Khaybar and later explained what he had been forced to do to the Jews of Khaybar.

n02069.summary: Anas reports that the Prophet was the most compassionate of people, never refusing a slave or child who brought him water, listening patiently to requests, and never withdrawing his hand before the other person did.

n02070.summary: Anas bin Maalik reports that the slaves of Madinah brought water to the Prophet after Fajr, and he dipped his hands into every vessel for blessing, even on very cold mornings.

n02071.summary: Anas reports that the Prophet never withdrew his hand or turned away from a person until that person did, and never moved his head from one whispering to him until the person moved away.

n02073.summary: Another narration says that even the slave girls of Madinah could take the Prophet by the hand and lead him wherever they needed him to go.

n02074.summary: Anas reports that a woman with a mental illness asked the Prophet for help, and he stepped aside with her into a street to hear her problem.

n02075.summary: Muhammad bin Maslamah says that when he returned from a journey, the Prophet took him by the hand and did not let go until he did.

n02076.summary: Aa'isha says the Prophet always chose the easier of two options when it involved no sin, and that he took revenge only for the sake of Allaah.

n02077.summary: Aa'isha reports that the Prophet never struck a servant or a woman, always took the easier option when it involved no sin, and punished only when Allaah's prohibitions were violated.

n02078.summary: Aa'isha and Abu Hurayrah describe how the Prophet was never rude, vulgar or noisy, and always forgave and overlooked.

n02079.summary: Anas says the Prophet never cursed people or was rude, and that the strongest thing he said when scolding was 'May sand fall on his forehead'.

n02080.summary: Abdullaah bin Amr reports that the Prophet was never rude or vulgar, and said the best of people is the one with the best character.

n02081.summary: Anas tells how Abu Talha brought him to the Prophet to serve him, and how the Prophet never reproached him for what he did or failed to do.

n02082.summary: Anas says the Prophet never scolded him for delayed or bungled tasks, and told his household to leave him alone when they scolded Anas.

n02083.summary: Anas says the Prophet never hit, cursed or frowned at him during ten years of service, and recounts how his mother offered him to the Prophet for service.

n02084.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar, Ali, Usaama and Abdullaah bin Ja'far report the Prophet's affection for Ja'far and Ali and his praise of their resemblance to himself.

n02085.summary: Hasan reports that the Prophet said he could find fault with each of his Companions' characters except Abu Ubaydah's.

n02086.summary: A narrator whose name is garbled in the text reports that the Prophet, visiting his daughter as she washed Uthmaan's head, told her to treat Uthmaan well because his character was closest to his own.

n02087.summary: Abu Hurayrah reports that Ruqayya, combing the Prophet's hair, said he had just asked how Uthmaan was, and then praised Uthmaan's character as closest to his own.

n02088.summary: Abdullaah bin Aslam reports that the Prophet told Ja'far he resembled him in looks and in character.

n02089.summary: Ali, Usaamah bin Zaid and Abdullaah bin Ja'far report the Prophet's words to Ja'far, Zaid and Ali, and Abdullaah says he would not trade them for red camels.

n02090.summary: Bahriyyah reports that when the Prophet's plate was stolen, Umar neither cursed the thief nor reproached him.

n02091.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas reports that Uyaynah insulted Umar to his face, Umar nearly struck him, and Ali praised Ibn Mas'ood's knowledge.

n02092.summary: Aamir bin Rabee'ah says Mus'ab bin Umayr was his close friend from the time Mus'ab accepted Islaam until his martyrdom at Uhud, and that he never saw a better character.

n02093.summary: Habba Urani reports that people praised Abdullaah bin Mas'ood in front of Ali, and Ali called on Allaah to witness that he agreed with their praise.

n02094.summary: Saalim and Zuhri report that Abdullaah bin Umar never cursed a slave, and that he once stopped himself partway through a curse.

n02096.summary: Abu Sa'eed Khudri reports that Dhu Khuwaysarah demanded justice from the Prophet, that Umar asked to behead him, and that the Prophet forbade it while describing the people who would come from him.

n02097.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports that when Abdullaah bin Ubay died, his son asked the Prophet for a shirt to shroud him and for the funeral prayer, and the Prophet prayed before the verse forbidding it was revealed.

n02098.summary: Umar recounts objecting when the Prophet was about to pray over Abdullaah bin Ubay, and how Allaah then revealed verses forbidding prayer for the hypocrites.

n02099.summary: Jaabir reports that the Prophet came to the funeral of Abdullaah bin Ubay, found him already buried, had him exhumed, blew on the body and shrouded it with his own garment.

n02100.summary: A narration says the Prophet had the body of Abdullaah bin Ubay taken out of the grave and shrouded it with his own garment.

n02101.summary: Zaid bin Arqam reports that the Prophet was ill for days from a Jew's spell, and that he never mentioned it to the Jew or showed anger.

n02102.summary: Aa'isha relates how the Prophet came to believe he had been with his wives when he had not, because of a spell, and how the location of the spell was revealed in a dream and he chose not to publicise it.

n02103.summary: Aa'isha adds that for six months the Prophet believed he had been with his wives when he had not, because of witchcraft, and that two angels then came to him.

n02104.summary: Anas and Abu Hurayrah report that a Jewish woman poisoned goat meat for the Prophet, and that he questioned her and did not punish her.

n02106.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas reports that the Prophet had cupping done whenever he felt the effect of the poison, including once while about to enter ihraam.

n02107.summary: Jaabir reports the poisoned roast goat, the woman's confession and the Prophet's forgiveness, and other reports say the Prophet had cupping done and that the woman was later executed.

n02108.summary: Marwaan bin Uthmaan reports that on his deathbed the Prophet told Ummu Bishr he could feel the poison from the meal he had eaten with her brother Bishr at Khaybar.

n02109.summary: Ja'da bin Khaalid reports that the Prophet rebuked a large-bellied man for overeating, and that when told of an assassination plot he said nothing could harm him without Allaah's permission.

n02110.summary: Anas and Abdullaah bin Mughaffal report the Makkan ambush of eighty and then thirty men during the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah, how the Prophet's prayer captured or blinded them, his forgiveness, and the revealed verse.

n02111.summary: Abu Hurayrah reports that Tufayl bin Amr asked the Prophet to curse the Daus tribe, and that the Prophet instead prayed for their guidance.
