n02112.summary: Abu Za'raa reports Ali's statement that he, his pure wives and his pious progeny had been the most tolerant in youth and the most learned as adults, and Sa'd's praise of Ibn Abbaas for his knowledge and tolerance.

n02113.summary: Anas reports that the Prophet shortened the salaah when he heard a child crying, because the crying would pain the child's mother.

n02114.summary: Anas reports that when a man asked about his father, who died as a mushrik, the Prophet said he was in the fire and then consoled the man by saying his own father was there too.

n02115.summary: Abu Hurayrah reports that when a Bedouin was rude about the gift he had received, the Prophet answered patiently and kindly, and told the Bedouin's story as a parable about a camel.

n02116.summary: Asma'ee reports that people asked Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf to ask Umar to be gentle with them, and Umar replied that his compassion for them would surprise them if they knew it.

n02117.summary: Abu Sa'eed Khudri says the Prophet was more modest than a virgin in her private chamber, and that his dislike showed on his face.

n02118.summary: Anas reports the Prophet's saying that modesty is goodness, and his words to Aa'isha that he should be shy before one before whom even the angels are shy.

n02119.summary: Aa'isha says that when news reached the Prophet of something someone had said, he never named that person, but spoke of people in general.

n02120.summary: Aa'isha says she never saw the private parts of the Prophet.

n02121.summary: Sa'eed bin Al Aas reports that the Prophet let Abu Bakr and Umar in as he lay covered, but sat up and covered himself for the bashful Uthmaan, and explains why when Aa'isha asks.

n02122.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports that while the Prophet sat with Aa'isha, Abu Bakr, Umar and others entered, and that he covered his knees when Uthmaan asked to enter because the angels are shy before Uthmaan.

n02123.summary: Hasan describes the extreme modesty of Uthmaan, who would bathe seated and not stand up straight even behind a locked door.

n02124.summary: Aa'isha reports Abu Bakr's saying that he covers his head out of modesty before Allaah, even when entering the toilet.

n02125.summary: Sa'd bin Mas'ood and Umaarah report that Uthmaan bin Madh'oon did not want his wife to see his private parts, and that the Prophet told him the spouses are each other's garments.

n02126.summary: Abu Mijlaz, Abu Qataadah and Anas report Abu Moosa Ash'ari's extreme modesty, including bathing in a dark room, bending over to get his clothes, and sleeping in clothing.

n02127.summary: Ubaadah bin Nusay reports that Abu Moosa Ash'ari said he would rather die and be raised again many times than do what people in the water were doing without their lower garments.

n02128.summary: Ashaj Abdul Qais reports that the Prophet told him that tolerance and modesty are two qualities Allaah loves, and that these were naturally instilled in him.

n02129.summary: Abu Hurayrah reports that an angel came to the Prophet offering him the choice of being a king-prophet or a slave-messenger, and that the Prophet chose to be a humble slave-messenger.

n02130.summary: Aa'isha reports that the Prophet never ate reclining and said he ate as a slave eats and sat as a slave sits.

n02131.summary: Abu Ghaalib asked Abu Umaamah for a Hadith, and Abu Umaamah described the Prophet's dhikr, brief talks, long salaah and humility.

n02132.summary: Anas describes the Prophet's dhikr, plain clothing and riding, his acceptance of slaves' invitations, and his donkey at Khaybar.

n02134.summary: Abu Moosa Ash'ari says the Prophet rode a donkey, wore woollen clothes, milked a goat himself and served guests personally.

n02135.summary: Ibn Abbaas says the Prophet sat and ate on the floor, milked a goat himself and accepted a slave's invitation to barley bread; another report adds that he accepted such an invitation in the middle of the night from a man of the upper part of Madinah.

n02136.summary: Anas says the Prophet accepted even plain food, and pawned his armour to a Jew, dying without the money to redeem it.

n02137.summary: Umar says that each of the three times a man called the Prophet, he answered 'Labbaik'.

n02139.summary: Jareer says the Prophet calmed a man who was trembling before him, telling him he was no king but the son of a Quraysh woman who ate dried meat.

n02140.summary: Ibn Mas'ood reports the same calming of a trembling man on the day Makkah was conquered, and Aamir bin Rabee'ah says the Prophet took his shoe and would not let him fix its strap, disliking preferential treatment.

n02141.summary: Abdullaah bin Jubayr says someone shaded the Prophet with a sheet, and he took it down, saying he was only a human being like them.

n02142.summary: Abbaas wonders how long the Prophet will remain with them and asks why he has no raised platform; the Prophet says he prefers to stay among the people.

n02143.summary: Ikramah reports Abbaas asking about the platform again, and concluding from the reply that the Prophet would be with them only a short while.

n02144.summary: Aswad asks Aa'isha what the Prophet did on entering the house, and she says he did household chores and went to salaah when the time came.

n02146.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas says the Prophet never gave anyone the job of preparing his wudu or distributing his charity, and attended to both himself.

n02147.summary: Jaabir says that when the Prophet came to visit him, he rode neither a mule nor a thoroughbred horse.

n02148.summary: Anas says the Prophet performed Hajj on an old carriage under a sheet worth about four Dirhams, and prayed for a Hajj free of show and boasting.

n02149.summary: Anas says that when the Prophet entered Makkah at the conquest, he lowered his head onto his carriage out of humility.

n02150.summary: An unnamed narrator says that at Dhu Tuwa the Prophet stood on his carriage and lowered his head in gratitude to Allaah until his beard touched the middle of the carriage.

n02151.summary: Abu Hurayrah says the Prophet bought trousers in the market and carried them himself, told the measurer to give the buyer the benefit, and pulled his hand away from a man who tried to kiss it.

n02152.summary: Aslam reports that when Umar rode a camel into Shaam, he rebuked people who looked at the mounts of unbelievers instead of those used by the Prophet and the Muslims.

n02153.summary: Hishaam says he saw Umar stop a woman making aseedah and show her how to make it with a wooden spoon.

n02154.summary: Hishaam bin Khaalid says he heard Umar teach women to add flour only once the water is hot, stirring gradually to avoid lumps.

n02155.summary: Zirr says he saw Umar walk barefoot to the Eid salaah.

n02156.summary: Umar Makhzoomi reports Umar's sermon recalling how he herded for his Banu Makhzoom aunts for a few dates; Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf criticised it, and Umar said he had felt pride and wished to humble himself.

n02158.summary: Hasan says that Umar, walking out on a hot day, asked a boy on a donkey for a ride and then rode behind him into Madinah.

n02159.summary: A boy recounts that Umar, with a lash, sent other boys scattering from the fallen dates, did not hit him when he saw the dates in his garment, and walked him home.

n02160.summary: Maalik's grandfather says he saw Umar and Uthmaan each carry a youngster on the ride into Madinah; the narrator explains this as humility and benefit to others, and criticises rulers who make youths walk behind them.

n02161.summary: Maymoon bin Mahraan says he saw Uthmaan, while Khalifah, ride a mule with his slave Naa'il riding behind him.

n02162.summary: Abdullaah Roomi says Uthmaan drew his own water for night wudu and never woke his household for Tahajjud; the grandmother of Zubayr bin Abdullaah, once his servant, adds that he fasted constantly.

n02163.summary: Hasan says he saw Uthmaan sleeping in the Masjid under a shawl with no one around him, though he was then Ameerul Mu'mineen.

n02164.summary: Unaysa says Abu Bakr milked goats for the girls of the locality, and kept doing so after he became Khalifah, asking them how they wanted the milk.

n02165.summary: Saalih, a blanket merchant, reports that his grandfather saw Ali buy dates for a Dirham and refuse help to carry them.

n02166.summary: Zaadhaan reports that Ali walked the market guiding lost people, announcing lost items and helping the weak, and recited a verse about the Hereafter, saying it was revealed about just and humble rulers.

n02167.summary: Jurmooz saw Ali leave his house in two reddish cloths, walk the market with a lash, and urge traders to fear Allaah, deal amiably and give full weight and measure.

n02168.summary: Abu Matar recounts Ali's episodes in the market: he warned against oaths in trade, made a date seller take back dates sold to a servant, banned dead fish, and refused a refund a cloth merchant's father tried to give him.

n02169.summary: Ataa reports that Faatima's plaits hit the bowl as she kneaded dough, and Mutallib bin Abdullaah says Ummu Salamah, who had married the Prophet that evening, was grinding flour later that night.

n02170.summary: Salaamah Ajali says he and his cousin Qudaamah went to see Salmaan Faarsi, and found him weaving palm baskets while in command of twenty thousand men; Salmaan prayed that Allaah love the cousin.

n02171.summary: Haarith bin Umayrah recounts visiting Salmaan Faarsi, who was scraping hide in his tannery, and Salmaan says that souls who came together for Allaah's pleasure become friends.

n02172.summary: Abu Qilaabah reports that Salmaan Faarsi, while making dough himself, received a man who had come to pass on greetings from someone else, and told him that the greeting was a trust that would have been left unfulfilled.

n02173.summary: Amr bin Abu Qurra Kindi reports that his father offered his sister in marriage to Salmaan Faarsi, who refused and married a freed slave woman; when Abu Qurra went to Salmaan after an argument with Hudhayfah, Salmaan received him in very simple surroundings.

n02174.summary: Three reports on Salmaan Faarsi's humility as a commander and governor: soldiers mocked him as he rode a donkey, the people of Madaa'in called him Gurg Aamad, and a witness saw him in short, shabby clothes; he said good and bad will be seen only in the Aakhirah.

n02175.summary: Thaabit reports that while Salmaan Faarsi was governor of Madaa'in he carried a stranger's load of figs to the man's house, saying he had intended to do it to please Allaah and could not put it down before he arrived.

n02176.summary: Abdullaah bin Buraydah reports that Salmaan Faarsi made things with his hands, sold them, and used the money to buy meat or fish to share with lepers.

n02177.summary: Muhammad bin Seereen reports that whenever Umar bin Khattaab appointed a governor he would write that the governor should greet first, be content with a lower seat, and dislike ostentation and boasting.

n02179.summary: Sulaym bin Abu Hudhayl says that when Jareer bin Abdullaah left his house and mounted his mule, he took his slave up behind him.

n02180.summary: Abdullaah bin Salaam carries a bundle of wood through the marketplace to guard against pride, quoting the Prophet that someone with even an atom of pride will not enter Jannah.

n02181.summary: Ali says the core of humility is to greet others first, to accept a lower place in a gathering, and to dislike ostentation and boasting.

n02182.summary: Abu Hurayrah reports that the Sahabah asked the Prophet whether he joked with them, and he said he joked but spoke only the truth.

n02183.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas describes a joke of the Prophet with one of his wives, whom he told to wear a large shawl and drag it along like a bride's.

n02184.summary: Anas describes the Prophet's gentleness with Abu Umayr, a young brother of his, asking after the child's pet bird, and then recounts the Prophet leading prayer on a mat at their home.

n02185.summary: Anas reports that the Prophet would ask his young brother Abu Umayr how his little bird, Nughayr, was doing.

n02186.summary: Anas reports that at the home of Abu Talha, the Prophet noticed Abu Umayr looking sad, learned that his bird had died, and affectionately asked how Nughayr was.

n02187.summary: Anas reports that a man asked the Prophet for transport, and the Prophet offered him a camel's young to ride, then asked whether every camel is not the child of another.

n02188.summary: Anas reports that the Prophet affectionately teased him by calling him 'O two-eared one'.

n02189.summary: Anas reports that the Prophet loved Zaahir, a countryman who brought him gifts, joked with him in the market, and told him that he was precious in Allaah's sight.

n02190.summary: Nu'maan bin Basheer reports that Abu Bakr, finding his daughter Aa'isha raising her voice before the Prophet, moved to slap her and was stopped by the Prophet; when Abu Bakr later found them reconciled he joked that they should let him into their peace as they had let him into their war, and the Prophet agreed.

n02191.summary: Aa'isha recounts how she beat the Prophet in a race when she was slim, and he beat her in a later race when she had gained weight, saying 'This is for that'; Anas and Abu Qilaabah report him telling the camel-driver Anjasha to go easy with the women.

n02193.summary: Hasan reports that an old woman asked the Prophet to pray that she enter Jannah; he told her old women will not enter it, and then sent word, citing the verse that Allaah created the women of Jannah especially.

n02194.summary: Awf bin Maalik Ashja'ee reports that during the Tabook expedition he jokingly asked the Prophet 'All of me?' when he was let into a very small tent, and Waleed explains the joke.

n02195.summary: Aa'isha joked with the Prophet ﷺ, and her mother's remark about the Kinaana tribe drew his reply that they are the subject of many of the Muslims' jokes.

n02196.summary: Abu Sufyaan joked with the Prophet ﷺ in the house of his daughter Ummu Habeebah, and the Prophet smiled at his remark.

n02197.summary: Bakr bin Abdullaah says the Sahabah played together, throwing melons, yet were the most resolute men when matters were serious.

n02198.summary: Qurra asked Ibn Seereen whether the Sahabah joked, and Ibn Seereen said they did, quoting Abdullaah bin Umar's couplet said in jest.

n02199.summary: Umm Salamah reports that Abu Bakr sent Nu'aymaan and Suwaybit bin Harmala on a trade journey, where Nu'aymaan tricked Suwaybit into being taken as a slave; Abu Bakr returned the ten camels paid for him and freed him, and the Prophet laughed about it for a year.

n02200.summary: Rabee'ah bin Uthmaan reports that Nu'aymaan bin Amr Ansaari, urged by some Sahabah, slaughtered a Bedouin's camel to eat it; when the Prophet found Nu'aymaan hiding in a house, Nu'aymaan blamed the Sahabah, and the Prophet compensated the Bedouin.

n02201.summary: Abdullaah bin Mus'ab reports that Makhramah bin Naufal, an old blind man, was led by Nu'aymaan to urinate in a corner of the Masjid; afterwards, on Nu'aymaan's word, Makhramah struck Uthmaan, who was praying, and Uthmaan forgave Nu'aymaan because he was a Badr veteran.

n02202.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas says the Prophet was the most generous of people, most of all in Ramadhaan when he met Jibra'eel every night, and more generous than the blowing wind.

n02204.summary: Ali reports that when asked for something, the Prophet said yes when he intended to do it and stayed silent when he did not, but never said no.

n02205.summary: Rubayyi bint Mu'awwidh reports that her father sent a Saa of fresh dates with cucumber to the Prophet, who in return filled her hand with jewels that had just come from Bahrain.

n02206.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports that a woman brought a garment for the most generous of the Arabs, and the Prophet directed it to Sa'eed bin Al Aas, after which such garments were called Sa'eediyyah.

n02207.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar says there was a time when the Muslims thought of each other above themselves, but now people love dinars and dirhams more than their brothers.

n02208.summary: Abu Sa'eed Khudri reports visiting the Prophet during a high fever and being told that the prophets suffer most, then the scholars, then the pious; Abu Ubaydah bin Hudhayfah reports, from his aunt Faatimah, that the Prophet lay under a dripping water bag in his fever and said the closest to the prophets suffer most.

n02209.summary: Aa'isha reports that the Prophet, in great pain, turned from side to side on his bed, and told her that every thorn or pain a believer suffers forgives a sin and raises his rank.

n02210.summary: Jaabir reports that fever asked permission to visit the Prophet and was sent to the people of Quba; when they complained, he offered to pray it away or let it stay as a purification from sin, and they chose to keep it.

n02211.summary: Salmaan reports that the Prophet sent fever to the people of Quba, who chose to keep it as a means of forgiveness; Abu Hurayrah reports that fever went to the Ansaar, the Prophet prayed and they were cured, and a woman of the Ansaar chose patience and Jannah over a cure.

n02212.summary: Aa'isha reports that when a regular attendee at the Prophet's gatherings was struck down by a high fever, the Prophet visited him and told him that fever is his Ummah's share of Jahannam in this world.

n02213.summary: Abu Safar reports that when people visited Abu Bakr during his illness and asked whether they should summon a physician, Abu Bakr said the physician had already seen him and that Allaah does as He pleases.

n02214.summary: Mu'aawiya bin Qurra reports that when friends visited Abu Dardaa in illness, he said his sickness was for his sins and that he wished for Jannah, and when they offered to summon a physician he said that it was Allaah who had laid him there.

n02215.summary: Abdur Rahmaan bin Ghanam reports that when the plague struck Shaam, Amr bin Al Aas told people to flee it and Shurahbeel bin Hasanah rejected that; Mu'aadh bin Jabal prayed for his family's full share of the plague, lost two daughters and then his son Abdur Rahmaan, was himself struck, and advised a weeping man to seek knowledge from four men.

n02216.summary: Shahr bin Howshab, reporting from Raaba, says that when the plague spread Abu Ubaydah prayed for his family's share and then died of it; Mu'aadh bin Jabal, after taking command, also lost his son and was struck himself; Amr bin Al Aas then told people to flee to the mountains, Abu Waathilah rebuked him, and Umar, hearing the matter, said Amr had not condemned it.

n02217.summary: Abu Qilaabah reports Mu'aadh bin Jabal's reply to Amr bin Al Aas, that the plague is martyrdom, a mercy and the Prophet's du'aa, and explains the du'aa: the Prophet asked that his Ummah not perish by drought, be overrun by an enemy, or split into factions; the last was refused, so he said 'let it be fever or a plague'.

n02218.summary: Urwa bin Zubayr reports that Abu Ubaydah and his family were spared the plague until a sore appeared on his little finger, and that he hoped Allaah would bless it, since Allaah makes a little thing much.

n02219.summary: Haarith bin Abu Umayrah Haarithi reports that Mu'aadh bin Jabal sent him to ask Abu Ubaydah how he was in the plague; Abu Ubaydah showed him a plague sore on his palm and swore he would not trade it even for red camels.

n02220.summary: Zaid bin Arqam says that when he developed a cataract the Prophet visited him and told him that if he lost his eye and bore it patiently for Allaah's reward, his reward would be Jannah.

n02221.summary: Anas accompanies the Prophet to visit Zaid bin Arqam during an eye ailment, and the Prophet tells Zaid that losing his sight with patience and hope of reward will bring him to Allaah without sin.

n02222.summary: Zaid bin Arqam relates that the Prophet visited him in illness and told him that if he lost his sight in old age and bore it patiently he would enter Jannah without reckoning.

n02223.summary: A variant report says Zaid bin Arqam went blind after the Prophet's death but Allaah restored his sight before Zaid died.

n02224.summary: Qaasim bin Muhammad reports that a blind Companion said he would not want his sight back now that the Prophet has passed away, since he wanted it only to see the Prophet.

n02226.summary: Usaama bin Zaid relates that when the Prophet's grandson was dying, the Prophet went with several Companions, and seeing the child's last moments he wept and explained that Allaah places mercy in the hearts of His servants.

n02227.summary: Abu Hurayrah and Ibn Abbaas report the Prophet's grief at the mutilated body of his uncle Hamza after Uhud, his vow to mutilate in return, the revelation of Surah Nahl verse 126 counselling patience over revenge, and his funeral prayer for Hamza and the other martyrs.

n02228.summary: Usaama bin Zaid relates that the Prophet wept when Usaama came to him after the martyrdom of Usaama's father Zaid bin Haaritha, and Khaalid bin Shumayr reports that the Prophet wept again when Zaid's daughter cried, calling it the longing a friend has for his friend.

n02229.summary: Aa'isha reports that the Prophet's eyes filled with tears when he kissed Uthmaan bin Madh'oon after his death, and said the reason was that he had been killed by the People of the Book.

n02230.summary: Haaritha bin Suraaqa was killed by a stray arrow at Badr, and his mother vowed patience if he was in Jannah; the Prophet ﷺ told her of Firdous, the highest level.

n02232.summary: In another narration from Anas, Ummu Haaritha says she will not grieve if her son is in Jannah, and the Prophet ﷺ tells her Haarith is in Firdous, so she rejoices.

n02233.summary: When Khallaad was martyred at Banu Qurayzah, his mother went to receive his body in her veil, saying she had lost Khallaad but not her modesty, and the Prophet ﷺ said he has the reward of two martyrs.

n02234.summary: Anas relates that Ummu Sulaym refused Abu Talha's proposal until he accepted Islaam, which she made her dowry, the Prophet married them on that basis, and after their son died she bore it patiently, so the Prophet promised them another child.

n02235.summary: Anas relates that Ummu Sulaym did not tell Abu Talha of their son's death until after the night, that the Prophet prayed for a blessing on that night, and that the newborn received tahneek from the Prophet with a date.

n02236.summary: Qaasim bin Muhammad relates that Abdullaah, son of Abu Bakr, was struck by an arrow at Taa'if and died when the wound reopened forty days after the Prophet's death, that Abu Bakr bore it with patience, and that he thanked Allaah for his son's martyrdom when he showed the arrow to the Thaqeef delegation and learned who had shot it.

n02238.summary: Amr bin Sa'eed relates that Uthmaan smelled each newborn while it was still wrapped so that he would feel more love and need more patience if it died, and that Abu Dharr thanked Allaah when told none of his children seemed to survive, since Allaah stores them as treasure for him in the Aakhirah.

n02239.summary: Umar bin Abdur Rahmaan relates that Umar bin Khattaab consoled himself with patience after his brother Zaid bin Khattaab's death, and told the man who killed Zaid that he thought of him every time the wind blew.

n02240.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas relates that Safiyyah came looking for Hamza after his death, that Ali and Zubayr did not tell her, that the Prophet calmed her with a hand on her chest and a du'aa, and that she accepted it saying 'To Allaah we belong'; the Prophet then prayed the funeral prayer for the martyrs one group at a time, leaving Hamza's body until last.

n02241.summary: Zubayr relates how the Prophet forbade women to see the bodies at Uhud, how his mother Safiyyah insisted on bringing two sheets for Hamza, and how lots were drawn between Hamza and an unnamed Ansaari for the sheets; a second report has Safiyyah bearing the news with patience and the Prophet letting her go to Hamza's body.

n02242.summary: Ummu Salamah relates that her husband Abu Salamah told her of the Prophet's promise that a Muslim who says 'To Allaah we belong' and the calamity du'aa will be given something better, that she recited it at his death, and that the Prophet later proposed marriage to her.

n02243.summary: Aa'isha relates that Usayd bin Hudhayr wept on hearing of his wife's death, and when she asked why, he said the Prophet had said the Arsh shook at the death of Sa'd bin Mu'aadh.

n02245.summary: Awn relates that Abdullaah bin Mas'ood wept at the news of his brother Utba's death, saying he would rather be left to hope for reward for his patience than die first.

n02246.summary: Khaytama relates that Abdullaah bin Mas'ood's eyes welled with tears at his brother Utba's death, and he said the weeping was a mercy Allaah placed in the heart.

n02247.summary: Abdullaah bin Abu Saleet relates that Abu Ahmad bin Jahash, who was blind, carried the bier of his sister Zaynab bint Jahash in tears, and when Umar asked him to step aside he said carrying her bier cooled his grief, so Umar told him to hold on tight.

n02248.summary: Ahnaf bin Qais relates that after Umar was stabbed he asked Suhayb to lead prayer for three days and had food served, and that the grieving people refused to eat until Abbaas bin Abdul Muttalib began, which showed Ahnaf what Umar meant when he said the Quraysh are leaders.

n02249.summary: Abu Uyaynah relates that Abu Bakr consoled a bereaved person by saying there is no calamity where there is patience, and that thinking of the loss of the Prophet makes one's own loss seem light.

n02251.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas relates that an Ansaari woman who suffered seizures chose to persevere for the reward of meeting Allaah without sin rather than be cured, and that after the Prophet prayed for her she would cling to the Kabah's shroud and the spirit would leave her.

n02252.summary: Ataa relates Abdullaah bin Abbaas's account of a black woman with epilepsy who chose patience for Jannah over a cure, asking only that her body not be exposed, which the Prophet prayed for; Ataa adds that she was called Ummu Zufar.

n02253.summary: Abdullaah bin Mughaffal relates that the Prophet told a man who struck his face on a wall after looking at a woman who had been a prostitute that Allaah intends good for him by hastening his punishment in this world; two further reports have Umar saying that anything a believer dislikes is a calamity, over a broken sandal strap and a broken shoe.

n02254.summary: Aslam relates that Abu Ubaydah wrote to Umar about the Romans' massive offensive, and Umar's reply urges steadfastness and patience, quoting the Qur'aanic command to persevere and fear Allaah.

n02255.summary: Mahdi says that Uthmaan had two virtues that Abu Bakr and Umar did not have: he persevered until his martyrdom, and he united the Muslims on one standard text of the Qur'aan.

n02256.summary: Abdur Rahmaan bin Awf relates that the Prophet prolonged his sajdah in his room until he feared he had died, and told him that Jibra'eel had brought word that Allaah sends mercy on whoever invokes blessings upon the Prophet, so he prostrated in gratitude.

n02257.summary: Mu'aadh bin Jabal relates that the Prophet stood in prayer until dawn and made a long sajdah, and explained that his Lord had asked about his Ummah and promised he would never be made to grieve over it, so he prostrated in thanks.

n02258.summary: Abdur Rahmaan bin Abu Bakr relates that the Prophet recited Surah Sajdah and prostrated so long that people gathered, explaining he did so in gratitude that seventy thousand of his Ummah would enter Jannah without reckoning, and Abu Bakr and Umar remarked on how great a gift that was.

n02259.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar relates that the Prophet dismounted and prostrated when he passed a man with a terminal illness, and that Abu Bakr and then Umar did the same.

n02260.summary: Ali relates that the Prophet prayed that if Allaah returned his family safely from an expedition he would thank Him as He deserves, and when they returned he thanked Allaah and told Ali that he had just done so.

n02261.summary: Anas relates that the Prophet gave a beggar a single date, which the beggar threw away, and that when a second beggar was delighted with a date he had the Prophet's instruction to have forty dirhams given to him through Ummu Salamah; a second report from Hasan has a beggar who was made wealthy after the Prophet told people to treat him well.

n02262.summary: Sulaymaan bin Yasaar relates that passing Dajnaan, Umar recalled herding animals there for his stern father Khattaab, thanked Allaah for making him the guide of the Ummah of Muhammad, and recited verses that worldly wealth and children are temporary while Allaah remains.

n02263.summary: Umar says that when he comes to the conveyance of gratitude or the conveyance of patience, he does not mind which of the two he rides.

n02264.summary: Ikramah relates that Umar, passing a leper who was also blind, deaf and dumb, asked his companions whether they saw any bounty in him, and pointed out that the man could urinate with ease, which is a great bounty.

n02265.summary: Ibraheem relates that Umar heard a man say he wished to spend his wealth and his life in Allaah's path, and rebuked the people for not staying silent, advising patience in difficulty and gratitude in prosperity instead.

n02266.summary: Umar asks a man who greeted him how he is, then writes to Abu Moosa Ash'ari urging him to be content with the provision Allaah gives and to be grateful for it.

n02267.summary: Umar says the grateful always receive more from Allaah, so one should ask Allaah for more, citing Surah Ibraheem verse 7.

n02268.summary: Uthmaan praises Allaah for not meeting a group of wrongdoers he was sent to deal with, and frees a slave as a sign of gratitude.

n02270.summary: Abu Dardaa calls a day without hardship a great bounty from Allaah, and says those who see Allaah's bounties only in food and drink have limited understanding.

n02271.summary: Aa'isha says gratitude is due even for plain water drunk without difficulty, and Asmaa bint Abi Bakr falls into sajdah of gratitude after finding a keepsake from the Prophet that she had lost following Abdullaah bin Zubayr's martyrdom.

n02272.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood reports that at Badr, when the Prophet's turn came to walk, Abu Lubaabah and a second companion offered to walk instead, and the Prophet refused, saying they were no less in need of reward than he was.

n02273.summary: Muttalib bin Abu Wadaa'ah reports that the Prophet said the salaah of one who prays seated is half the reward of standing, and the Sahabah then strove to pray standing.

n02274.summary: When the Muslims in Madinah were ill with fever and could pray only seated, the Prophet said seated prayer is half the reward, and the Sahabah then struggled to stand in prayer despite their weakness.

n02275.summary: Rabaa'ah bin Ka'b, who served the Prophet, asks for companionship in Jannah, and the Prophet tells him to help himself by making much sajdah.

n02276.summary: Abdul Jabbaar bin Haarith describes coming to the Prophet with a delegation, accepting Islaam and pledging allegiance, and refusing a worldly grant because he prefers to ask the Prophet for help in the Aakhirah.

n02277.summary: Amr bin Taghlib reports the Prophet praising him for trusting the independence Allaah placed in his heart when others were given gifts, and Amr says he would not trade those words for red camels.

n02278.summary: Ali and Umar see a Bedouin carrying his mother around the Tawaaf, and Ali urges Umar to go round again so that the mercy coming down on the Bedouin may reach them too, both reciting couplets.

n02279.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar frees a shepherd who had escaped with him from the captors of his camel, declines to reclaim the camel so as to keep the reward, and is urged by his sister Hafsah to marry so that his children either earn reward for patience or pray for him.

n02280.summary: Ammaar bin Yaasir, on the way to Siffeen, prays that he would gladly risk death for Allaah's pleasure and trusts that Allaah will never let him fail while he acts to please Him.

n02281.summary: Abdullaah bin Amr says a good deed done now is dearer to him than two liked deeds done in the Prophet's time, because the world has now come to the Sahabah while they were then focused on the Aakhirah.

n02282.summary: Alqama asks Aa'isha whether the Prophet set aside particular days for worship, and she replies that his deeds were constant, and that no one can do what he did.

n02283.summary: Mughiera bin Shu'ba reports that the Prophet stood in salaah until his feet split, and when asked why, given that Allaah had forgiven his past and future errors, he said he should be a grateful servant.

n02284.summary: Zubayr bin Abdullaah reports, through his grandmother Zuhaymah, that Uthmaan fasted continually and prayed through the night, sleeping only briefly at the start.

n02285.summary: Mujaahid says Abdullaah bin Zubayr's worship was unmatched, and that during a flood, when people could not perform Tawaaf, he went round the Ka'bah several times by swimming.

n02286.summary: Two chains report that Abdullaah bin Zubayr fasted seven days in a row until his insides dried, and that when very old he reduced it to three days.

n02287.summary: Anas describes the Prophet as the most handsome, generous and bravest of people, who rode Abu Talha's horse to investigate a night alarm in Madinah and reassured the people, and says the Sahabah sought refuge with him whenever battle grew fierce.

n02288.summary: An unnamed Companion says that at Badr they sheltered by the side of the Prophet, because he was the fiercest of fighters.

n02289.summary: Baraa bin Aazib says the Prophet did not desert at Hunayn, describing the Hawaazin archers and the Prophet remaining on his white mule, with Abu Sufyaan holding its reins, while declaring he is a Nabi without a lie.

n02290.summary: Baraa continues that the Prophet dismounted and prayed for help, and that in the battle only the bravest could fight beside him.

n02291.summary: Abdullaah bin Amr reports that the Prophet ate a date he found by his side, then stayed awake fearing it might have been one of the Sadaqah dates.

n02292.summary: Ibn Seereen says Abu Bakr alone forced himself to vomit food he had eaten, and Abdur Rahmaan bin Abu Layla recounts that the food came from Ibn Nu'aymaan's paid incantation, which Abu Bakr then vomited out on learning its source.

n02293.summary: Zaid bin Arqam reports that Abu Bakr's slave brought food from incantations he had performed for pay, and that Abu Bakr ate a morsel, then forced himself to vomit it out, fearing the Prophet's warning about a body fed by unlawful food.

n02294.summary: Zaid bin Aslam reports that Umar, finding the taste of some milk strange, learnt it came from zakaah camels and vomited it out.

n02295.summary: Miswar bin Makhrama recounts sticking close to Umar, and Sha'bi reports that Ali, learning that a householder was a money-changer, refused to drink from his well and to take shade under a tax collector's property, citing the Prophet.

n02296.summary: Yahya bin Sa'eed reports that Mu'aadh bin Jabal, who had two wives, treated them equally, and that when both died in the Shaam plague he drew lots to decide which would be placed first in their shared grave.

n02297.summary: Tawoos reports that Abdullaah bin Abbaas, asked when Umar left Arafaat, declined to say out of caution, which surprised the people.

n02298.summary: Not a narration: the text is only the phrase 'Rasulullaah ﷺ' under a section heading.

n02299.summary: Jaabir narrates that a Bedouin drew the Prophet's sword while he slept under a tree, and when the Prophet woke and asked who would save him, the Bedouin said Allaah, and the Prophet did not punish him.

n02300.summary: Jaabir narrates that at Nakhlah, Ghowrath bin Haarith stood over the sleeping Prophet with a sword, the sword fell from his hand, and the Prophet let him go after he pledged not to fight him or join those who did.

n02301.summary: Yahya bin Murrah narrates that Ali, when guarded at night, said that guarding does not help against what is decreed, that angels protect a person until his decreed time, and that no one tastes the sweetness of Imaan unless convinced of qadr.

n02302.summary: Qataadah reports that Ali was restless on his last night, that his family urged him not to go out, and that he said angels protect a person until destiny comes, then went to the Masjid and was assassinated.

n02303.summary: Abu Mijlaz reports that when a man warned Ali of a plot, Ali said a person's appointed term is his guard, and Yahya bin Katheer adds that Ali said the same when people offered to guard him.

n02304.summary: A narrator (name garbled in the OCR) reports that when Ali judged a dispute while sitting at the base of a wall, one man said the wall was about to fall, and Ali told him to continue because Allaah suffices, and the wall fell after Ali had left.

n02305.summary: Abu Dhabiyya reports that Uthmaan visited Abdullaah bin Mas'ood on his deathbed and offered a stipend for his daughters, and that Abdullaah declined, telling them to recite Surah Waaqi'ah nightly because the Prophet said poverty would never afflict its reciter.

n02306.summary: Umar says he does not mind whether his morning brings what he likes or what he dislikes, since he does not know where the good lies.

n02307.summary: Hasan reports that Ali was told Abu Dharr prefers poverty and illness; Ali replies that whoever relies on Allaah's choice never wishes for another state, and separately says that whoever is content with Allaah's decision is rewarded.

n02308.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood says that on the Day of Qiyaamah people will wish they had only enough food to live on, that daily conditions harm only a heart full of anger, and that it is better to burn oneself than to say 'if only' about what Allaah has decreed.

n02309.summary: Kumayl bin Ziyaad relates that at a graveyard Ali addressed the dead, told Kumayl that the best provision is taqwa, and wept, saying the grave is a box holding one's actions.

n02310.summary: Qais bin Abu Haazim reports Ali's advice to value the acceptance of one's deeds above taqwa itself.

n02311.summary: Another report gives Ali saying that a deed done with taqwa can never be undermined, so how can an accepted deed ever be undermined.

n02312.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood says that knowing Allaah has accepted even one of his deeds is dearer to him than earth full of gold.

n02313.summary: Abu Dardaa says the sleep of the intelligent and the little good done with taqwa and conviction are worth more than a mountain of worship by the negligent.

n02314.summary: Abu Dardaa says that knowing for certain that Allaah accepted one of his salaah is dearer to him than the whole world, citing the verse that Allaah accepts only from those with taqwa.

n02315.summary: Ubay bin Ka'b says that whoever gives up something for Allaah's pleasure is given something better from unexpected sources, while the careless who take without knowing the lawful source are afflicted.

n02316.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas reports that Abu Bakr and then Umar each noticed the Prophet's greying hair, and the Prophet said Surah Hood and the surahs with it had whitened it.

n02317.summary: Abu Sa'eed reports the Prophet's concern about the angel ready to blow the Trumpet and the words he taught the Sahabah in reply; Abdullaah bin Umar reports that the Prophet fainted on hearing a verse about the chains of Jahannam.

n02318.summary: Sahl bin Sa'd reports that a young Ansaari, overcome by fear of Jahannam, died in the Prophet's embrace, and the Prophet ordered him enshrouded because fear had ruptured his liver.

n02319.summary: Hudhayfah reports the same incident: the youth stood to embrace the Prophet and fell dead, and the Prophet said Allaah had saved him from the Fire and that whoever fears something will flee from it.

n02320.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas reports that when the verse about saving yourselves from the Fire was recited, a young Sahabi fainted; the Prophet told him to say Laa Ilaaha illallaah and gave him glad tidings of Jannah.

n02321.summary: Sa'eed bin Musayyib reports the Prophet's visit to the ill Umar, who said he had both hope and fear; Hasan reports Abu Bakr saying that Allaah pairs ease with hardship so the believer keeps both hope and fear.

n02322.summary: Abdullaah bin Roomi reports that Uthmaan said he would rather be turned to ashes than not know whether he is going to Jannah or Jahannam.

n02324.summary: Aamir bin Masrooq reports that Abdullaah bin Mas'ood, told that someone did not want to be among the As'haabul Yameen, said he himself wished not to be resurrected at all; Hasan reports Abdullaah saying he would rather be dust than be placed between Jannah and Jahannam.

n02325.summary: Abu Dharr says that if people knew what he knew they would neglect their wives and beds, and wishes Allaah had created him as a felled tree whose fruit is eaten.

n02326.summary: Hizaam bin Hakeem reports Abu Dardaa saying that if people knew what follows death they would take no pleasure in food or drink, and wishing to be a felled tree.

n02327.summary: Abu Dardaa wishes to be a sheep whose throat is cut to feed guests, and Abdullaah bin Umar wishes to be a pillar.

n02329.summary: Shaddaad bin Aws Ansaari, unable to sleep from fear of Jahannam, would cry out to Allaah and then stand in salaah until morning.

n02330.summary: Amr bin Salamah reports Aa'isha wishing she were a tree or sand, or had never been created; another report has Abdullaah bin Abbaas praising Aa'isha before her death, and she replies that she wishes only to be forgotten.

n02331.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood reports that the Prophet asked him to recite the Qur'aan, and that when he reached the verse about a witness from every nation the Prophet's eyes filled with tears and he said that was enough.

n02332.summary: Abu Hurayrah reports that the men of Suffa wept when a verse was revealed, the Prophet wept with them, and he said the one who weeps out of fear of Allaah will never enter Jahannam.

n02333.summary: Anas reports the Prophet describing the fire of Jahannam and an Abyssinian man weeping loudly before him; the Prophet praised him, and Allaah's message brought through Jibra'eel is that tears shed in fear of Him will be rewarded with laughter in Jannah.

n02334.summary: Qais bin Abu Haazim says that when he went to visit the Prophet he found Abu Bakr had already taken his place as Khalifah, and that Abu Bakr praised Allaah at length in his address and wept greatly.

n02335.summary: Hasan bin Muhammad bin Abi Taalib reports that Umar wept so much reciting Surah Takweer in the Friday sermon that his voice stopped, and that after reciting Surah Toor he fell ill and people visited him for twenty days.

n02337.summary: Abdullaah bin Shaddaad bin Haad says he could hear Umar sobbing in the Fajr prayer from the last rows, as Umar recited Surah Yusuf and stopped at the verse about complaining of sorrow to Allaah.

n02338.summary: Hishaam bin Hasan narrates that a verse sometimes choked Umar with emotion, so that he would fall down weeping and stay indoors while people visited him thinking he was ill.

n02339.summary: Haani, freed slave of Uthmaan, reports that Uthmaan wept at graveyards, quoting the Prophet that the grave is the first stage of the Aakhirah and the most frightening sight he had seen.

n02340.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports that Umar asked the weeping Mu'aadh bin Jabal why he wept, and Mu'aadh quoted the Prophet that even slight ostentation is shirk and that the people most beloved to Allaah are the hidden God-fearing.

n02341.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar wept so much reciting Surah Mutaffifeen that he fell down; Naafi reports he always wept at certain verses of Baqarah and Hadeed; Yusuf bin Maahak reports walking with Abdullaah bin Umar to ask about Abu Dharr's worship, which was meditation in solitude.

n02342.summary: When Ubayd bin Umayr recited the verse about the witness from every nation, Abdullaah bin Umar wept so much that his beard and collar were wet with tears.

n02343.summary: Ibn Abu Mulaykah reports that Abdullaah bin Abbaas stood in prayer half the night and wept while reciting Surah Qaaf, and Abu Rajaa describes the tear marks on his face.

n02344.summary: Uthmaan bin Abu Saudah saw Ubaadah bin Saamit weeping on the wall of the Masjid over a valley of Jahannam, and Ubaadah said the Prophet ﷺ had shown them that place.

n02345.summary: Ya'la bin Ataa reports that Abdullaah bin Amr wept so much that his eyes were affected, and Muslim bin Bishr reports Abu Hurayrah weeping in his final illness over the journey to Jannah or Jahannam.

n02346.summary: Dhamrah bin Habeeb reports from a freed slave of Abu Rayhaanah that Abu Rayhaanah stood in prayer all night after a campaign, lost in thought about the descriptions of Jannah, and did not hear the Adhaan until Fajr.

n02347.summary: Muhammad bin Waasi reports that a man came from Basrah to ask Ummu Dharr about Abu Dharr's worship, and she said he spent his whole days in solitary meditation.

n02348.summary: Aun bin Abdullaah bin Utba reports that Ummu Dardaa named meditation and heeding lessons as Abu Dardaa's best deed, and Abu Dardaa said meditation for a moment is better than standing in salaah all night.

n02349.summary: Abu Dardaa says some people are keys to good and locks to evil, who will be richly rewarded, while others are keys to evil and locks to good, who will be severely punished, and repeats that meditation for a moment is better than a night of salaah.

n02350.summary: Habeeb bin Abdullaah reports Abu Dardaa advising a man going to jihaad to remember Allaah in ease so that He remembers him in hardship; Saalim bin Abil Ja'd reports Abu Dardaa drawing a lesson from two bulls, one whipped for stopping and the other spared.

n02351.summary: A freed slave of Abu Bakr reports Abu Bakr saying that whoever opposes his own carnal self for Allaah's sake will be saved from Allaah's anger.

n02352.summary: Umar bin Khattaab urges people to weigh themselves before they are weighed, and Anas reports Umar's fear of Allaah while alone in an orchard.

n02353.summary: Jaabir bin Samurah tells Simaak that the Prophet was a man who often remained silent.

n02354.summary: Abu Maalik Ashja'ee reports that his father said the Companions never saw anyone as silent as the Prophet, who only smiled when others talked too much.

n02355.summary: Ubaadah bin Saamit reports that Mu'aadh bin Jabal asked what deeds to do after the Prophet, and the Prophet taught that remaining silent except for good speech is the greatest restraint on the self.

n02356.summary: Abu Hurayrah reports the Prophet telling a weeping woman not to call a slain man a martyr, and Anas reports the same about a Companion who died at Uhud.

n02357.summary: Khaalid bin Numayr reports that Ammaar bin Yaasir often stayed silent for long periods and seemed depressed, and when he did speak it was mostly to seek Allaah's protection from trials.

n02358.summary: Abu Idress Khowlani recounts seeing a quiet, respected man in the Masjid of Damascus and learning from him a du'aa for steadfastness, gratitude, a pure heart and a truthful tongue.

n02359.summary: Abu Waa'il reports that Ibn Mas'ood told a man to lift his garment; when the man retorted that Ibn Mas'ood also wore his high, Ibn Mas'ood explained his thin calves. Umar then struck the man for insolence. Alaa reports that Umar threw a brick at a Quraysh man who suggested he hire someone to build for him, saying he did not want to dislike Ibn Mas'ood.

n02360.summary: Sa'eed Jareeri reports that he saw Abdullaah bin Abbaas holding his tongue and warning that on the Day of Qiyaamah a person will be angriest with his tongue.

n02361.summary: Shaddaad bin Aws, after pledging allegiance to the Prophet ﷺ, said that since then every word he spoke was measured, and taught a du'aa for steadfastness and a pure heart.

n02362.summary: Shaddaad relays the Prophet's du'aa for steadfastness and forgiveness, which the Prophet advised people to fill their treasures with instead of gold and silver hoarding.

n02363.summary: Isa bin Uqba reports that Abdullaah bin Mas'ood swore nothing on earth deserves a long prison sentence more than the tongue.

n02364.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood warns to beware of futile speech and to say only what will get one's needs fulfilled.

n02365.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood says those guilty of the most sins on the Day of Qiyaamah will be those who engaged most in idle talk.

n02366.summary: Ali bin Abi Taalib gives several sayings on the tongue and silence: the tongue governs the whole body, keep a low profile, silence leads to Jannah, and a couplet on keeping secrets.

n02367.summary: Abu Dardaa advises learning silence as one learns speech, listening more than speaking, and not speaking or laughing about things that do not concern you.

n02368.summary: Abu Dardaa says the tongue is the limb a believer is loved for most, since it leads him to Jannah, and the limb a disbeliever is hated for most, since it leads him to Jahannam.

n02369.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar says a person most needs to purify his tongue, and Anas says no one attains Taqwa until he controls his tongue.

n02370.summary: Heading only, 'The Speech of Rasulullaah', with no narration under it.

n02371.summary: Aa'isha describes how clearly the Prophet spoke, so that his words could be counted, and tells how she missed a chance to rebuke a man who spoke loudly beside her room.

n02372.summary: Aa'isha says the Prophet's speech was so clear that everyone understood it and he never spoke continuously and quickly, and a Companion said each of his letters was distinctly pronounced.

n02373.summary: Anas reports that when the Prophet said something important he repeated it three times, and that he greeted a gathering three times.

n02374.summary: Thumamah bin Anas reports that Anas repeated important words three times, saying the Prophet did the same so that people would understand him.

n02375.summary: Abu Hurayrah reports the Prophet's words that he was given concise yet comprehensive speech and the keys to the treasures of the heavens and the earth, and Abdullaah bin Salaam reports that the Prophet looked to the sky when he sat to talk.

n02376.summary: Amr bin Al Aas says the Prophet gave his full attention to whoever he spoke with, and recounts asking whether he, Abu Bakr, Umar or Uthmaan was best, then regretting the questions.

n02377.summary: Aa'isha says she never saw the Prophet laugh so much that his uvula showed, and that he only smiled.

n02378.summary: Abdullaah bin Haarith bin Jaz says he never saw anyone smile as much as the Prophet, and that the Prophet never laughed but only smiled.

n02379.summary: Simaak bin Harb reports asking Jaabir bin Samurah whether he was often with the Prophet, and Jaabir describes the Prophet smiling while the Companions laughed about pre-Islamic matters.

n02380.summary: Simaak bin Harb reports that Jaabir bin Samurah described the Prophet as often silent and laughing very little, and only smiling when the Companions recited poetry and he said something that made them laugh.

n02381.summary: Husayn bin Yazeed Kalbi says he never saw the Prophet laugh, only smile, and that at times he had to tie a rock to his belly from hunger.

n02382.summary: Amrah asks Aa'isha how the Prophet behaved at home, and Aa'isha replies that he was the noblest and most compassionate of men and often laughed and smiled.

n02383.summary: Jaabir says that when revelation came or the Prophet was giving a lecture he looked like a warner, but otherwise he had the most smiling face, was the most jovial, and was the handsomest of men.

n02384.summary: Abu Umaamah says the Prophet ﷺ was one of the most jovial and best-natured of people.

n02385.summary: Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas told Aamir that during the Battle of Khandaq the Prophet ﷺ smiled broadly after Sa'd shot an enemy soldier who was taunting the archers.

n02386.summary: Abu Hurayrah reports a man who broke his fast in Ramadhaan by relations with his wife; the Prophet ﷺ told him to free a slave, fast, or feed the poor, and when he had nothing, gave him dates to spend on his family, and smiled.

n02387.summary: Abu Dharr reports the Prophet ﷺ describing a man whose minor sins are shown to him and whose major sins are hidden, and Abu Dharr saw the Prophet ﷺ smile widely.

n02388.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood reports the Prophet's account of the last person to leave Jahannam, who is granted Jannah and ten times what the world had to offer, and says the Prophet then smiled so widely his molars showed.

n02389.summary: Khaarijah bin Zaid says the Prophet was the most dignified person in his gatherings and never stretched his limbs out towards people while seated.

n02390.summary: Shahr bin Howshab and Abu Muslim Khowlaani describe how the Companions turned to Mu'aadh bin Jabal, who was quiet and dignified, for verification of hadith, and Mu'aadh identifies himself as the youthful man in the second account.

n02391.summary: Abu Barzah says he wanted to execute a man who spoke harshly to Abu Bakr, but Abu Bakr rebuked him, and Umar says no sip is better than a sip of anger held back.

n02392.summary: Ubay bin Ka'b says he would have killed a man seen visiting his father's wife, and the Prophet laughs and says he is more possessive than Ubay, and Allaah is more possessive than the Prophet.

n02393.summary: Mughierah reports that Sa'd bin Ubaadah said he would strike any man found with his wife, and the Prophet replied that he and Allaah are more possessive; Abu Hurayrah and Ibn Abbaas add the four-witness ruling and the Companions' plea for Sa'd.

n02394.summary: Aa'isha tells of her jealousy of Umm Salama, which she and Hafsah discussed, then the Qur'an verse on monasticism, and Mu'aadh bin Jabal's warning against forsaking enjoining good.

n02396.summary: Ali rebukes the people for letting their women crowd markets with unbelieving men, saying there is no good in one who has no sense of possessiveness, and that possessiveness is good only when it protects the family.

n02397.summary: Abdullaah bin Masood was told by the Prophet ﷺ that the best people do good deeds with deep understanding, and that the most learned see the truth in disputes; he then recounted the seventy-two groups and the tortured followers of Isa who opposed the kings.

n02398.summary: Mu'aadh bin Jabal narrates the Prophet ﷺ warning that love of the world and ignorance will lead people to stop enjoining good and forbidding evil.

n02399.summary: Yazeed Raqaashi reports from Anas that the Prophet described people who travel to advise others, and who become beloved to Allaah by making His servants beloved to Him through enjoining good and forbidding evil.

n02400.summary: Hudhayfah asks the Prophet when people will abandon enjoining good and forbidding evil, and the Prophet answers that it will be when the affliction of the Bani Israa'eel befalls them: leniency towards sinners, knowledge given to the worst, and leadership to the young.

n02401.summary: Qais bin Abu Haazim reports that when Abu Bakr became Khalifah he warned people against misreading the verse about looking after oneself, citing the Prophet's words that punishment reaches all when evil is seen and not changed.

n02402.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas reports Abu Bakr, on the day he became Khalifah, recounting the Prophet's explanation of the verse Take care of your own selves: when evil is tolerated in a community, Allaah will punish them all and their du'aas will not be accepted.

n02403.summary: Abu Bakr says that when people commit evil while stronger people who could stop them do not, Allaah will engulf them all in a calamity that will not be lifted.

n02404.summary: Umar asks the people why they do not oppose a fool who dishonours others, and warns that if they stay silent out of fear they will be unable to bear witness for the Ambiyaa on the Day of Qiyaamah.

n02405.summary: Uthmaan says to enjoin good and forbid evil before the worst among the people are given authority over them, since even the best will then have their du'aas rejected.

n02406.summary: Ali urges the people to enjoin good and forbid evil or the worst will rule them, and in a sermon warns that earlier nations were destroyed when their religious scholars failed to forbid their sins.

n02407.summary: Ali divides jihaad into three kinds, with the hand, the tongue and the heart, and says the jihaad of the hand will disappear first.

n02408.summary: Ali says the jihaad of the hands, then the tongue, then the heart will vanish, and a heart that cannot recognise good or reject evil will be turned upside down.

n02409.summary: Idrees Shaybaani tells Abdullaah bin Mas'ood that whoever does not enjoin good and forbid evil is destroyed, and Ibn Mas'ood replies that one whose heart does not recognise good and reject evil is already destroyed, then describes three types of people who do good.

n02410.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood says to wage jihaad against the hypocrites with the tongue, and if nothing else is possible, at least to frown at them.

n02411.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood says that disliking an evil you cannot change is enough for Allaah, that approving of an evil done in your absence is like witnessing it, and that many evils will come in the future.

n02412.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood says the righteous will die first, leaving behind doubtful people who can neither recognise good nor reject evil.

n02413.summary: Abur Ruqaad recalls a gathering addressed by Hudhayfah, who warned that unless people enjoin good and forbid evil, Allaah will set the worst over them and their du'aas will go unanswered, and who said a time will come when the best people are those who do neither.

n02414.summary: Adi bin Haatim says that what is good today will be called evil in times to come and the reverse, and that people stay on the right path only while they do not call good evil and scholars keep speaking the truth.

n02415.summary: Abu Dardaa says he advises people to do something he does not practise himself, hoping to be rewarded by Allaah for the advice.

n02416.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports that whenever Umar meant to forbid the people something, he first warned his own family that anyone of them who did it would receive double the punishment.

n02417.summary: Ibn Shihaab reports that Hishaam bin Hakeem and some men enjoined good and forbade evil together, and Umar used to say that evil would not happen while he and Hishaam were alive.

n02418.summary: Abu Ja'far Khatmi reports that his grandfather, the Sahabi Umayr bin Habeeb, advised his son to avoid foolish company and to be patient with the harm that comes from enjoining good and forbidding evil.

n02419.summary: Abdul Azeez reports that Abu Bakrah led the funeral prayer for his wife over her brothers' objections, fell when people pushed him at the grave, and told his children he feared living in a time when he could not enjoin good and forbid evil.

n02420.summary: Ali bin Zaid reports that Hajjaaj threatened Anas bin Maalik for supporting rival factions, and Anas answered calmly and left, saying he had held back only for the sake of his children.

n02421.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar says he held back from objecting to a speech by Hajjaaj, recalling the Prophet's saying that a Mu'min should not humiliate himself by taking on what he cannot bear.

n02422.summary: Umar says that keeping to oneself is a way to escape bad company, and another narration has him urging people to take their full share of keeping to themselves.

n02423.summary: Mu'aafaa bin Imraan reports that Umar, passing people who were following an arrested man, said there is no welcome for faces that appear only at times of evil.

n02424.summary: Adasah Taa'ee reports that when Abdullaah bin Mas'ood received a bird brought from a far-off place, he wished he could be somewhere he need not speak to anyone, and no one would speak to him, until he met Allaah.

n02425.summary: Qaasim reports that Abdullaah bin Mas'ood advised a man who asked for counsel to stay indoors, guard his tongue and weep over his sins.

n02426.summary: Ismaa'eel bin Abu Khaalid reports that Abdullaah bin Mas'ood advised his son Abu Ubaydah to keep taqwa, stay indoors and weep over his sins.

n02428.summary: Yahya bin Sa'eed reports that Abu Jahm bin Haarith did not mix with his fellow Ansaar, and when this was mentioned to him he said people are worse than solitude.

n02429.summary: Abu Dardaa says a Muslim's best place of seclusion is his home, where he keeps his self, eyes and private parts under control, and warns against marketplace gatherings that lead to negligence and idle talk.

n02430.summary: Abdullaah bin Amr finds Mu'aadh bin Jabal talking to himself at his door, and Mu'aadh explains that Shaytaan urges him to leave home, while the Prophet said those who go out for good causes, or who stay home without backbiting, are under Allaah's protection.

n02431.summary: Abdullaah bin Ubayd reports that Umar, seeing Ahnaf in a new garment bought for twelve dirhams, told him six would have been enough and the rest should go to a good cause.

n02432.summary: Hasan Basri reports that Umar wrote to Abu Moosa Ash'ari to be content with the provision he receives, since Allaah gives some people more and tests the wealthy by whether they are grateful.

n02433.summary: Abu Ja'far reports that Ali ate dry dates and drank water, then said that whoever's stomach leads them into the Fire is far from Allaah's mercy, and recited a couplet on the regret that follows indulging one's appetites.

n02434.summary: Sha'bi reports that Ali advised not to worry about the next day's food, since sustenance is assured, and warned that wealth beyond one's needs is held in trust for someone else.

n02435.summary: Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas advises his son that independence must be sought through contentment, because wealth without contentment never makes a person independent.

n02436.summary: Jaabir bin Samurah, or another Sahabi, reports that the young Prophet gave up goat-herding for trade with camels, that Khadeeja's sister praised his modesty and character, and that Khadeeja then sought to marry him and afterwards sent gifts.

n02437.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas reports that the Prophet described how Khadeeja got her father drunk and then persuaded him to marry her to the Prophet, and that when he sobered up and objected to marrying the orphan of Abu Taalib, she talked him round.

n02438.summary: Nafeesah reports that Khadeeja, a wealthy and noble woman, sent her to ask the Prophet whether he would marry, and that Khadeeja's uncle Amr bin Asad arranged the marriage when the Prophet was twenty-five and Khadeeja forty.

n02439.summary: Aa'isha reports that after Khadeeja died, Khowla bint Hakeem proposed to the Prophet on behalf of Aa'isha and Sauda, that Abu Bakr at first doubted the match, and that the Prophet's answer of Islamic brotherhood settled it and the marriage was arranged.

n02440.summary: Abu Bakr withdraws his promise of Aa'isha to Mut'im bin Adi's son after Mut'im's wife objects, and then marries her to the Prophet; Khowla then proposes Sauda bint Zam'ah, whose brother Abd bin Zam'ah later regrets his grief, and Aa'isha describes her wedding in Madinah.

n02441.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports that after Khunays bin Hudhaafah died, Umar offered Hafsah first to Uthmaan and then to Abu Bakr, both of whom held back, until the Prophet proposed to her himself and then gave his daughter to Uthmaan.

n02442.summary: Ummu Salamah declines Abu Bakr's proposal, then accepts the Prophet's proposal after his replies to her objections, and her son Umar brings the marriage about.

n02443.summary: Ummu Habeebah recounts that Najaashi's envoy Abraha brought the king's news that the Prophet wished to marry her, that Khaalid bin Sa'eed gave her in marriage, and that Najaashi paid the dowry and hosted a meal.

n02444.summary: Ummu Habeebah tells how her dream of her husband Ubaydullaah bin Jahash foretold his turn to Christianity and his death in drink, how her later dream made her expect marriage to the Prophet, and how Abraha returned her gifts.

n02445.summary: Anas relates how Zaid went to propose to Zaynab bint Jahash for the Prophet, how she referred the matter to her Lord and the marriage was then settled by revelation, and the walima and the Hijaab verses that followed.

n02447.summary: Anas relates that his mother Ummu Sulaym sent a dish after the Prophet's marriage to Zaynab, that the Prophet had about three hundred people fed from it, and that the Hijaab verses were revealed as the men left.

n02448.summary: Anas relates that after the Khaybar captives were gathered, Dihya asked for a slave woman and was sent to take another, and the Prophet freed Safiyya bint Huyay and married her.

n02449.summary: Anas relates the Prophet's marriage to Safiyya after Khaybar, the walima held near Sahbaa with food set on a leather cloth, and the Prophet's care in helping her onto his camel on the way back.

n02450.summary: Anas describes the walima for Safiyya, served on a leather cloth with dates, cheese and butter, and the Muslims' question about whether she was a wife or a slave woman; Jaabir reports the Prophet handing out dates after Safiyya entered his tent.

n02451.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports that the bluish marks around Safiyya's eyes came from her husband's slap after she told him of a dream, and Safiyya says her hatred for the Prophet left once he explained his position on her father and husband.

n02452.summary: Abu Hurayrah reports that Abu Ayyoob guarded the Prophet's tent after his marriage to Safiyya, and Ataa bin Yasaar reports that Aa'isha went to see Safiyya and the Prophet corrected her for calling Safiyya a Jewess, since she had accepted Islaam.

n02453.summary: Sa'eed bin Musayyab reports that on arriving in Madinah Safiyya gave her gold palm-leaf earrings to Faatima and some other ladies.

n02454.summary: Aa'isha reports that Juwayriyyah, a captive of the Banu Mustaliq under a kitaabah contract with Thaabit bin Qais, came to the Prophet for help, and that he paid her ransom and married her, after which the Muslims freed the tribe's captives.

n02455.summary: Urwa reports how a man asked the Prophet to marry Faatima to him, and was told to send back the armour, worth about four hundred dirhams, that the Prophet had given him, which became Faatima's dowry.

n02456.summary: After the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah, the Prophet ﷺ went for Umrah and sent Ja'far to propose to Maymoonah bint Haarith, whose affairs Abbaas arranged, and the marriage was consummated at Sarif.

n02457.summary: A second narration says that after the marriage the Prophet ﷺ stayed in Makkah three days, and when Huwaytib and the Quraysh told him to leave, he left for Madinah and consummated the marriage at Sarif.

n02458.summary: Ali narrates how he asked the Prophet ﷺ for Faatima's hand; he had no dowry except an armour, which the Prophet ﷺ accepted as her dowry.

n02459.summary: Buraydah reports that some Ansaar urged Ali to propose for Faatima, that the Prophet welcomed the proposal, and that Sa'd provided a sheep for the walima, and the Prophet prayed for the couple on their wedding night.

n02460.summary: A narration of the same wedding night adds that the Prophet called Ummu Ayman to fetch Ali, prayed for the couple, sprinkled water on Ali, and then sent for Faatima, who came flustered, and reassured her.

n02461.summary: Asmaa bint Umays describes Faatima's wedding night at Ali's house: the Prophet ﷺ made du'aa over Ali and Faatima, said Ali was his brother, and prayed for Asmaa.

n02462.summary: In another narration, Asmaa bint Umays describes the Prophet ﷺ coming the morning after the wedding, making du'aa for Ali and sprinkling water on him, and then telling Faatima he had married her to the family member he loved most.

n02463.summary: Ali narrates that after marrying him to Faatima the Prophet had water brought, gargled, and sprinkled it on Ali's chest and between his shoulders, and recited the protective surahs over him.

n02464.summary: Albaa bin Ahmar reports from Ali that Ali sold his armour and other goods for 480 dirhams to pay the dowry, that the Prophet had the money spent on perfume and clothing, and that the Prophet put something in Hasan's mouth that made him more knowledgeable than his brother.

n02465.summary: Jaabir reports attending the wedding of Ali and Faatima, which was simple: a matting stuffed with date-palm bark, raisins and dates served, and a sheepskin for her first night's bedding.

n02466.summary: Ali reports that when Faatima married, the Prophet gave her a blanket, a water-skin and a leather pillow stuffed with idhkhir grass.

n02467.summary: Abdullaah bin Amr reports the Prophet's gifts to Faatima and Ali, and a quarrel over a date palm between Abu Bakr and Rabee'ah, in which Rabee'ah refused to repeat Abu Bakr's words, and the Prophet told Rabee'ah to forgive Abu Bakr, so that Abu Bakr wept.

n02468.summary: Rabee'ah Aslami tells how the Prophet ﷺ sent him to marry into an Ansaar tribe, how he paid a dowry of gold, and how the Prophet ﷺ made a waleemah with a sheep, and then how the Prophet ﷺ settled a land dispute between him and Abu Bakr, who then wept.

n02469.summary: Abu Barzah reports the Prophet's request to an Ansaari for his daughter in marriage on Julaybeeb's behalf, and then an account of Salmaan Faarsi's wedding night, in which he rejects the luxuries of his house and advises his wife to obey Allaah.

n02470.summary: Salmaan Faarsi tells how, on his wedding night, he refused to let his companions in, removed the excess drapes and goods and servants, and advised his wife on obedience to Allaah, citing the Prophet's ﷺ advice to keep only what a traveller needs.

n02471.summary: Ibn Abbaas reports that Salmaan asked Umar to marry him to one of his daughters, and Umar's family asked him to drop it; Thaabit Bunaani reports that Abu Dardaa went with Salmaan to propose for a Banu Layth woman, then married her himself, and Salmaan regretted the mix-up.

n02472.summary: Thaabit Bunaani reports that Abu Dardaa refused Yazeed bin Mu'aawiya's proposal for his daughter Dardaa, married her instead to a poor Muslim, and explained that he wanted to protect her faith from the pull of wealth.

n02473.summary: Abu Ja'far reports that Umar proposed to Ali for Ummu Kulthoom, Ali first deferred because of his brother Ja'far's sons, then agreed, and Umar told the Muhaajireen he wished to be the Prophet's relative; Ataa Khuraasaani gives the dowry as forty thousand dirhams.

n02475.summary: Sha'bi reports that Amr bin Hurayth proposed for Adi bin Haatim's daughter on condition that he pay the 480-dirham dowry the Prophet gave Aa'isha, which Adi called the Sunnah; a second report gives Adi's reply in the same terms.

n02476.summary: Sha'bi reports that Bilaal and his brother, both freed from slavery, proposed to families in Yemen and were accepted; Maymoon reports that when Bilaal's brother, who claimed Arab descent, proposed to an Arab family, they required Bilaal to be present, and Bilaal's speech won the match.

n02477.summary: Urwa bin Ruwaym reports that Abdullaah bin Qurt Thumaali, appointed governor by Umar, whipped the people who lit fires at a wedding in Hims, then told them in a sermon that they had imitated the disbelievers, recalling how Abu Jandal had held his own wedding simply.

n02478.summary: Aa'isha reports that the Prophet's dowry to her was twelve awqiya and a nash, totalling five hundred dirhams.

n02479.summary: Masrooq reports that Umar forbade dowries above four hundred dirhams from the pulpit, then accepted a Quraysh woman's correction from the Qur'aan and withdrew the prohibition, saying everyone knows more than Umar.

n02481.summary: Sha'bi reports that Umar bin Khattaab once delivered a sermon, and the text stops there.

n02482.summary: Umar bin Khattaab withdrew his earlier limit on dowries, saying a man may give what he likes from his wealth, and admitted that everyone has more understanding than he does.

n02483.summary: Umar said that if exorbitant dowries brought status in the Aakhirah, the Prophet's ﷺ daughters and wives would have deserved them most.

n02484.summary: Ibn Seereen reports that Umar allowed dowries of two thousand Dirhams and Uthmaan allowed dowries of four thousand.

n02485.summary: Naafi reports that Abdullaah bin Umar married Safiyya for four hundred Dirhams, she called it too little, and he added two hundred more without his father Umar knowing.

n02486.summary: Ibn Seereen narrates that when Hasan bin Ali married a woman, he sent her a hundred slave women, each carrying a thousand Dirhams.

n02487.summary: Aa'isha relates how Sauda smeared her face with hareerah at the Prophet's urging, how Umar's approach sent them to wash, and Abu Bakr adds that the Prophet lowered his knee to let Sauda get back at Aa'isha.

n02488.summary: Razeenah reports that Sauda Yamaaniyyah visited Aa'isha while Hafsah was there, dressed to impress, and Hafsah teased her that the Prophet was coming and that the one-eyed Dajjaal had appeared, which Sauda, who was hard of hearing, took as true.

n02489.summary: Hafsah sends Sauda to hide in the tent; the Prophet finds her shivering, tells her the Dajjaal has not yet appeared, and dusts the dirt and cobwebs off her.

n02490.summary: Hafsah complains to Aa'isha that they look unkempt before the Prophet's visit, and Aa'isha recounts watching the Abyssinians' display with the Prophet, who remarks that the human and jinn devils flee from Umar when he appears.

n02491.summary: Aa'isha says the Prophet stood at her door and screened her with his shawl while she watched Abyssinians perform with spears in the masjid, and he stayed standing until she tired.

n02492.summary: Aa'isha relates how she, Sauda bint Zam'ah and Safiyya agreed to tell the Prophet that the honey he had taken at Hafsah's smelled of Maghaafeer; Sauda reports how she did it, and the Prophet later declined honey when Hafsah offered it.

n02493.summary: Ibn Abbaas reports how he asked Umar which two wives the Tahreem verse meant, and Umar then recounts going to the Prophet, who was reclining on a straw mat, to ask whether he had divorced his wives; after that Umar advised Hafsah and Aa'isha, and the Prophet vowed to stay away from his wives for a month.

n02494.summary: Ibn Abbaas reports Umar's account of hearing that the Prophet had divorced his wives, going to the Prophet who said no, then calling out in the masjid that the wives were not divorced, and the verse on checking rumours being revealed about this.

n02495.summary: Jaabir reports that Abu Bakr and Umar, refused entry at first, were let in when the Prophet sat silent among his wives; Umar's joke made the Prophet laugh, Abu Bakr and Umar rebuked their daughters, and the choice verses of Surah Ahzaab were revealed, with the Prophet offering Aa'isha the choice first.

n02497.summary: The Prophet tells Aa'isha he can tell when she is pleased or angry by how she swears, and she answers that she only leaves out his name while her love stays the same.

n02498.summary: Aa'isha tells of racing the Prophet ﷺ on a journey, and Ibn Abbaas describes staying the night with Maymoonah and watching the Prophet ﷺ pray thirteen rakaahs of tahajjud before Bilaal called the adhaan.

n02500.summary: Aa'isha reports that the Prophet ﷺ gave a warm welcome to an old woman, named Jathaamah Muzaniyyah, whom he called Hasaanah, because she used to visit when Khadeeja was alive, and maintaining old ties is part of Imaan.

n02501.summary: Aa'isha reports the Prophet ﷺ honouring an old woman who used to visit when Khadeeja was alive, and Abu Tufayl saw him spread his shawl for a woman who had nursed him as a baby.

n02502.summary: Umar found the Prophet's short Abyssinian servant rubbing his back, asked whether he had been hurt, and the Prophet said his camel had thrown him the night before.

n02503.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood carried the Prophet's shoes and staff, screened him when he bathed, woke him when he slept and walked with him when no one else was there.

n02504.summary: Anas says he was ten when the Prophet reached Madinah and twenty when he died, and that his mother and aunts urged him to serve the Prophet.

n02505.summary: Asked whether he was at Badr, Anas says he was there as a boy to serve the Prophet, and Jaabir reports the Prophet praising Hasan and Husayn as excellent riders when they climbed on his back.

n02506.summary: Anas says twenty young Ansaar always stayed close to the Prophet ﷺ and were sent on errands, and Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf says four or five Sahabah never left his side on journeys or at his door.

n02508.summary: Aasim bin Sufyaan reports that either Abu Dardaa or Abu Dharr told him the Prophet ﷺ allowed him to spend the night at the Prophet's door so that he could wake him for any need.

n02509.summary: Hudhayfah reports that after praying with the Prophet in Ramadhaan, the Prophet offered him the leftover bathing water, and when Hudhayfah bathed the Prophet screened him in return.

n02510.summary: Anas describes the Prophet's tenderness toward his son Ibraheem, whom he would kiss and hold on visits to the wet nurse's house. Amr reports the Prophet's words when Ibraheem died while still being suckled, promising him two nursing mothers in Jannah.

n02511.summary: Abdullaah bin Haarith reports that the Prophet lined up the children of Abbaas, promised a prize to whichever reached him first, and they raced to him, jumping onto his back and chest as he hugged and kissed them.

n02512.summary: Abdullaah bin Ja'far reports that when the Prophet returned from a journey he set Ja'far's son in front of him on the animal, then one of Faatimah's sons, Hasan or Husayn, behind, so three rode into Madinah together.

n02513.summary: Abdullaah bin Ja'far recounts that the Prophet lifted him and a son of Abbaas onto his animal while he was playing. In a second report, Ubaydullaah and Quthm, the sons of Abbaas, are taken up in turn, and the Prophet passes his hand over Ja'far's son's head and prays that Allaah be Ja'far's successor for his children.

n02515.summary: Umar bin Khattaab says he saw Hasan and Husayn riding on the Prophet's shoulders and remarked on what a fine mount they had. The Prophet replied that they were fine riders.

n02516.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas reports that the Prophet came out carrying Hasan on his shoulders, and when someone called the child a fine conveyance, the Prophet said he was also a mighty fine rider.

n02517.summary: Baraa bin Aazib reports that while the Prophet was in salaah, Hasan and Husayn climbed onto his back, and he held them gently when he finished. Jaabir adds that he once found the Prophet on all fours with the two children riding on him.

n02518.summary: Ummu Ayman reports that Hasan and Husayn were lost, and the Prophet finds them clinging together beside a snake, which slides away from him, then carries one on each shoulder while Salmaan praises the boys as excellent riders.

n02519.summary: Jaabir describes how, on the way to a meal, the Prophet ran to catch Husayn playing in the street, made him laugh, hugged and kissed him, and said Husayn is from him and he is from Husayn.
