n02520.summary: The wife of Uthmaan bin Madh'oon complained that he worshipped all night and fasted all day, the Prophet rebuked him, and she then dressed well again; at his deathbed she mourned him in verse.

n02521.summary: A variant names the wife as Khowla bint Hakeem and says she visited Aa'isha, and records the Prophet telling Uthmaan that monasticism is not prescribed for them and that he himself fears Allaah most.

n02522.summary: Abdullaah bin Amr neglected his new wife through his worship, his father Amr complained to the Prophet, and the Prophet had him reduce his fasting and Qur'aan recitation and fast on alternate days like Dawood.

n02523.summary: Abu Juhayfah reports that the Prophet made a bond of brotherhood between Salmaan and Abu Dardaa. When Salmaan visited, he made Abu Dardaa break his fast, urged him to sleep at night, and told him that each person has rights owed to their Rabb, their body and their wife. The Prophet confirmed that Salmaan was right.

n02524.summary: Asmaa bint Abi Bakr describes her hardships after marrying Zubayr, who owned only a horse. She carried date stones from land the Prophet had given him, felt too shy to ride with the Prophet when he offered her a ride, and was made to feel the weight of Zubayr's possessiveness, until her father sent a servant to take over the horse.

n02525.summary: Asmaa bint Abi Bakr complained to her father about Zubayr's strict nature, and Abu Bakr told her to be patient, since a woman with a pious husband who does not remarry after he dies will be reunited with him in Jannah.

n02526.summary: A woman complains to Umar that her husband Abu Salamah has grown harsh while his goodness has faded; Umar hears both, strikes her, gives her three garments and warns the husband, then quotes the Prophet on the best generations of the Ummah.

n02527.summary: A woman complains to Umar that her husband worships all night and fasts all day; Umar excuses her, and Ka'b bin Soor, asked to judge, cites the Qur'aan on multiple wives and advises a balance of fasting, prayer and the wife's rights, so Umar appoints him judge of Basrah.

n02528.summary: Aatika, bound by her late husband's condition over an orchard, is freed by Ali's ruling to remarry Umar, and at the wedding feast Ali recites her grief verses to her, making her weep.

n02529.summary: Qataadah reports that a woman complained to Umar that her husband stood in prayer all night and fasted all day. Umar questioned her, then, on the advice of Ka'b bin Soor, ordered the husband to spend one night in four with his wife and to skip one fast in four, since she has a right to him.

n02530.summary: Abu Gharzah led Ibn Arqam by the hand to his wife and asked her if she hated him, and she said yes. When Umar called them both, the wife said she had been made to swear and could not lie. Umar said that not every home is built on love, and that many are built on courtesy, social standing and Islaam.

n02531.summary: Abu Salamah bin Abdur Rahmaan recounts that Aatika bint Zaid, married to Abdullaah bin Abi Bakr, was left an orchard on condition she did not remarry. After his death at Taa'if she mourned him in verse. Umar later proposed, and Ali advised that she could remarry if she returned the orchard. At the wedding feast Ali recited her verse to her, and she wept loudly.

n02532.summary: Nadbah, sent by Maymoonah to Ibn Abbaas, sees two beds; Maymoonah finds his wife was menstruating and reproaches Ibn Abbaas, reminding him that the Prophet touched his wives during menstruation.

n02533.summary: Ikrimah reports that Ibn Abbaas rebuked a cousin who called a slave woman an adulteress, warning that such slander will be punished in the Aakhirah and that Allaah dislikes vulgar speech.

n02534.summary: Abu Imraan reports that Amr bin Al Aas rebuked his wife for falsely calling a slave woman an adulteress, warned her of the eighty lashes waiting on the Day of Judgement, and advised freeing the slave as compensation.

n02535.summary: Abu Hurayrah raised his whip over his slave woman, held back for fear of retaliation on the Day of Judgement, and then set her free, saying she was Allaah's.

n02536.summary: On Umar's arrival in Shaam, Abu Ubaydah persuaded him not to stop the sword-bearing entertainers of Adhri'aat, since that would look like breaking the treaty, and Umar agreed, placing his family under Abu Ubaydah's command.

n02538.summary: Saleem bin Handhalah says they walked with Ubay after a session of hadith, and Umar warned that being followed like that was a source of pride for the teacher and of shame for the students.

n02539.summary: Abul Bakhtari reports a traveller telling Salmaan that every host had treated him like a son of his own father, and Salmaan said this shows Imaan is fresh, like a newly loaded beast that carries its load quickly.

n02540.summary: Hayya bint Abu Hayya tells how a man came to her house at midday seeking shade and water, and when he named himself Abu Bakr she spoke of the old tribal wars and the love Islaam created, and he said the bond lasts while the leaders stay upright.

n02541.summary: Haarith bin Mu'aawiya reports that Umar asked about the people of Shaam and warned that mixing with the mushrikeen leads to eating and drinking with them, which would spoil their good state.

n02542.summary: Ayaadh reports that Umar ordered Abu Moosa Ash'ari to present his accounts as governor on one piece of leather, and when Umar was impressed by Abu Moosa's Christian clerk he had Abu Moosa dismiss him, reciting the verse forbidding taking Jews and Christians as confidantes.

n02543.summary: Abu Hurayrah reports that the Prophet never found fault with food, eating what he liked and leaving the rest without comment.

n02544.summary: Ali reports that the part of a goat the Prophet liked most was the foreleg.

n02545.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood reports that the Prophet liked the foreleg and that, when it was once poisoned, people blamed the Jews. Jaabir says the Prophet remarked that the family seemed to know he liked meat when they slaughtered a goat for him, and Anas says the Prophet loved bottle gourd and he picked it out for him.

n02546.summary: Anas reports that the Prophet licked his three fingers after eating.

n02547.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas says the Prophet was so humble that he ate on the floor, tied the legs of goats he was about to milk, and accepted slaves' invitations to plain barley bread.

n02548.summary: Yahyaa bin Abu Katheer reports that Sa'd bin Ubaadah sent the Prophet a plate of thareed every day, and it went with him to whichever wife's house he was in.

n02549.summary: Anas reports that after drinking goat's milk the Prophet rinsed his mouth, saying the milk left a sticky residue.

n02550.summary: Abu Bakr reports that when the Prophet stopped at a place, he milked the goats a boy brought, gave the first milk to the boy's mother, the second to Abu Bakr, and drank the third himself.

n02551.summary: Ibraheem reports that the Prophet kept his right hand for eating, drinking and wudhu, and his left for cleaning himself. Ja'far bin Abdullaah reports that his grandfather Hakam, seeing him eat from all over the plate, told him not to eat like Shaytaan does.

n02552.summary: Umar bin Abu Salamah says that while eating with the Prophet he kept reaching all over the dish, and the Prophet told him to eat from what was in front of him.

n02553.summary: Ummayyah bin Makhshi reports the Prophet's remark that Shaytaan ate with a man who did not say Bismillaah until he named Allaah. Hudhayfah reports the Prophet stopping a Bedouin and a girl from grabbing food without Bismillaah, since food becomes lawful for Shaytaan when Allaah's name is not taken.

n02555.summary: Abdullaah bin Busr reports that the Prophet was served a meal and drink by his father, tossed the date stones behind him, and when he mounted, his father held the reins and asked for du'aa; the Prophet asked Allaah to bless them in their sustenance and to forgive and have mercy on them.

n02556.summary: Abdullaah bin Busr reports that his father invited Rasulullaah ﷺ to a meal of thareed, and the Prophet ﷺ afterwards made du'aa for the household.

n02557.summary: Ibn A'bad reports that Ali taught him the words to say before eating and the words of thanks to say after.

n02558.summary: Umar warns against excessive eating and drinking, saying it harms the body, causes illness and dulls salaah, and that moderation is healthier.

n02559.summary: Abu Mah'dhoora reports that when Safwaan bin Umayyah brought a platter, Umar invited the poor and slaves to share it, and then rebuked those who will not let their slaves eat with them.

n02560.summary: Maalik bin Anas reports that Ibn Umar had his baker pour every dish into one plate, and that Ibn Aamir corrected the baker who mocked him by calling Ibn Umar his leader.

n02561.summary: Ja'far reports that Ibn Abbaas always ate pomegranate seeds because he had heard that every pomegranate grows from a seed from Jannah.

n02562.summary: Saalim reports that Zaid bin Sowhaan questioned Salmaan Faarsi for buying a large quantity of grain, and Salmaan said that securing one's sustenance frees the heart for worship; a second report has Salmaan saying he loves to eat from the work of his own hands.

n02565.summary: Muslim, freed slave of Ali, reports that when Ali asked for a drink, Ali refused the cup he had brought him and told him to drink it first.

n02566.summary: Abdur Rahmaan bin Abu Layla reports that Umar said he saw the Prophet ﷺ wearing a narrow-sleeved cloak made in Shaam.

n02567.summary: Jund bin Makeeth reports that the Prophet ﷺ wore his best clothing to receive delegations and that Abu Bakr and Umar dressed the same; Salamah bin Akwa reports that Uthmaan's loincloth reached halfway down his calves and that Uthmaan said it was the garment of the Prophet ﷺ.

n02568.summary: Ash'ath bin Sulaym reports that the Prophet ﷺ told a man in Madinah to lift his loincloth, and Abu Burdah reports that Aa'isha showed a patched shawl and a coarse loincloth, saying the Prophet's soul was taken in those two garments.

n02569.summary: Umm Salamah says the garment the Prophet ﷺ loved most was his qamees.

n02570.summary: Several short reports describe the Prophet's ﷺ clothing: sleeves reaching the wrists, a black turban on entering Makkah and when preaching, an oily bandage while ill, and turban tails hung between the shoulders, which Ibn Umar also did.

n02571.summary: Aa'isha says that when asked about the Prophet's ﷺ bedding, it was leather stuffed with the bark of a date palm.

n02572.summary: Aa'isha tells how a woman of the Ansaar saw the Prophet's ﷺ bedding, a double-folded cloak, and sent a wool-stuffed bedding; the Prophet ﷺ ordered it returned and said that had he willed, Allaah would have made mountains of gold and silver travel with him.

n02573.summary: Muhammad reports asking Aa'isha and then Hafsah about the Prophet's ﷺ bedding, and Hafsah's folded sheet was left as it was because its softness prevented the Prophet ﷺ from performing night salaah.

n02574.summary: Umar reports that when the Prophet ﷺ put on new clothing he recited the du'aa of thanks, and said that giving the old clothes to a poor person for Allaah's sake keeps the wearer under Allaah's protection.

n02575.summary: Ali reports that when a woman fell from her donkey and her trousers kept her covered, the Prophet ﷺ prayed for forgiveness for the women of his Ummah who wear trousers and told the men always to wear trousers to protect their women.

n02576.summary: Dihya Kalbi reports that after he was sent as an envoy to Heraclius, the Prophet ﷺ gave him fine Egyptian cloth to make a qamees and a scarf for his wife, and then told him to have her wear something underneath so the scarf was not revealing.

n02577.summary: Usaama bin Zaid says the Prophet ﷺ gave him the same white Egyptian cloth he had given Dihya, and when he gave it to his wife, told him to have her wear something underneath because the cloth showed the shape of her bones.

n02578.summary: Aa'isha says that when she wore a new garment and kept admiring herself in it, her father Abu Bakr told her that Allaah was not looking at her with favour.

n02579.summary: Aa'isha gives another account in which Abu Bakr told her that self-admiration over worldly beauty displeases Allaah, so she took the garment off and gave it away in charity.

n02580.summary: Several reports describe Umar's clothing: his qamees sleeves reached only his wrists, he went to Jumu'ah in a cloak from Sumbulaan and apologised for being late, he tied his loincloth above the navel, and Anas said that apart from Umar and his son, all the Sahabah wore khazz, which he disliked.

n02582.summary: Masrooq reports that Umar came out in cotton clothing, recited a couplet saying all wealth and children will perish, and said that compared with the Aakhirah this world is a fleeting thing.

n02583.summary: Abu Abdullaah, freed slave of Shaddaad bin Haad, says he saw Uthmaan on a Friday standing on the pulpit in a Kufa shawl and a coarse Aden loincloth worth four or five dirhams.

n02584.summary: Moosa bin Talha says that on Fridays Uthmaan leaned on a staff on his way to the Masjid and was one of the most handsome men, wearing a cream loincloth and shawl as he sat on the pulpit.

n02585.summary: Sulaym Abu Aamir says he saw Uthmaan wearing a Yemeni shawl worth a hundred dirhams.

n02586.summary: Muhammad bin Rabee'ah bin Haarith says the Sahabah spent generously on fine, modest clothing for their wives, and that Uthmaan wore a silk-edged shawl worth two hundred dirhams that he had given his wife Naa'ilah, wearing it only to please her.

n02587.summary: Zaid bin Wahab reports that a delegation from Basrah criticised the clothing of Ali, and Ali replied that his clothing was far from pride and a fitting example for people to follow.

n02588.summary: Amr bin Qais reports that when Ali was asked why he patched his qamees, he said the heart is humbled by it and the believer is able to follow the example.

n02589.summary: Ataa Abu Muhammad says he once saw Ali wearing an unwashed qamees of extremely coarse cloth.

n02590.summary: Abdullaah bin Abu Hudhayl reports that Ali's qamees from Ray had sleeves reaching his fingertips, and that Ali trimmed off the excess, saying sleeves should never extend beyond the hands.

n02591.summary: Abu Sa'eed Azdi says he saw Ali at the market looking for a qamees for three dirhams, and that Ali paid the price the trader named, though he thought the trader had lowered it because he was the Ameerul Mu'mineen; Ali then had the extra sleeve cut off.

n02592.summary: Sa'd bin Ibraheem saw Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf wearing a shawl or suit of clothing worth four or five hundred Dirhams.

n02593.summary: Qur'ah offered Abdullaah bin Umar soft cotton cloth from Khurasaan, since his own clothes were coarse. Ibn Umar checked that it was not silk and refused it, saying he feared becoming a boastful snob and that Allaah detests the boastful.

n02594.summary: Abdullaah bin Hubaysh saw Abdullaah bin Umar wearing two cloths made by the Ma'aafir, a tribe of Yemen, reaching halfway down his calves.

n02595.summary: Waqdaan reports that a man asked Abdullaah bin Umar what clothing he should wear. Ibn Umar advised clothing that neither fools would mock nor sensible people criticise for extravagance, which costs between five and ten Dirhams.

n02597.summary: Uthmaan bin Abu Sulaymaan reports that Abdullaah bin Abbaas once bought and wore a garment worth a thousand Dirhams.

n02598.summary: Katheer bin Ubayd says that when he visited Aa'isha she was stitching an old garment, and she told him that a person who does not wear old clothes does not deserve new ones and may not have them in the Aakhirah.

n02599.summary: Abu Sa'eed reports Aa'isha mending an old garment and saying that one who will not wear old clothes does not deserve new ones; then Asmaa bint Abi Bakr, already blind, sent back fine garments from Marw and Quw that her son Mundhir had brought, and accepted only plain ones.

n02600.summary: Anas reports that a woman came to Umar saying her upper garment was torn, and Umar gave her a fine garment and told her to wear the old one while baking and cooking.

n02601.summary: Kharasha bin Hurr reports that Umar saw a youth whose loincloth trailed below his ankles, asked him if he was menstruating, and then had the trailing end cut off with a knife.

n02602.summary: Abu Uthmaan Nahdi reports Umar's letter to the army under Utba bin Farqad in Azerbaijan, telling them to dress simply, avoid luxury and non-Arab attire, and not to wear silk, which the Prophet ﷺ forbade beyond the width indicated by his finger.

n02603.summary: Mu'aadh bin Muhammad reports a gathering discussing the rooms of the Prophet's ﷺ wives, which Waleed bin Abdil Malik had ordered included in the Masjid; Ataa Khuraasaani and Imraan bin Abu Anas describe their simplicity, Sa'eed bin Musayyib wished they had been left standing, and Abu Umaamah said the same so people would see how little the Prophet ﷺ needed.

n02604.summary: Abu Hurayrah searches for the Prophet ﷺ, who had stepped away from a group of Companions, and finds him in an orchard; the Prophet sends him with his shoes to give glad tidings of Jannah to anyone who sincerely testifies that there is none worthy of worship but Allaah, and Umar, fearing people would rely on it, persuades the Prophet to let them keep doing good deeds.

n02605.summary: Abu Dharr walks at night with the Prophet ﷺ, who tells him Jibra'eel brought the good news that whoever dies without shirk enters Jannah, even if he commits adultery or theft.

n02606.summary: An old Bedouin, Alqama bin Ulaatha, says he cannot learn the Qur'aan but testifies that there is none worthy of worship but Allaah and that Muhammad ﷺ is the servant and Rasool of Allaah, and the Prophet ﷺ praises his understanding.

n02607.summary: Uthmaan says he heard the Prophet ﷺ speak of a statement that keeps a sincere speaker from the Fire, and Umar explains that it is the testimony that there is none worthy of worship but Allaah, the statement the Prophet ﷺ urged his uncle Abu Taalib to recite at his death.

n02608.summary: Abu Shaddaad, reported by Ya'la bin Shaddaad with Ubaadah bin Saamit confirming, recounts how the Prophet ﷺ had the door shut and had the Companions raise their hands and say Laa Ilaaha Illallaah, then lowered his own hands praising Allaah and affirming the promise of Jannah for this Kalimah.

n02609.summary: Rufaa'ah Juhani reports that at Kudayd the Prophet ﷺ told those who had asked leave to go home that whoever sincerely testifies and walks the right path will enter Jannah, and that 70,000 of his Ummah will enter without reckoning.

n02610.summary: A variant clause says it was Abu Bakr who called anyone who sought leave after this a fool.

n02611.summary: Anas reports that when the Prophet ﷺ charged a man for a deed the man denied with an oath, the Prophet told him to atone by testifying that there is none worthy of worship but Allaah.

n02612.summary: Abdullaah bin Zubayr reports that the Prophet ﷺ said a man who swore falsely using the words of the Kalimah was forgiven because of those words.

n02613.summary: Abu Moosa Ash'ari reports the Prophet ﷺ saying that Muslims in Jahannam will be taken out after the unbelievers see them, and recites Surah Hijr verses 1-2; Anas reports that believers in Laa Ilaaha Illallaah will be removed from Jahannam by Allaah's mercy after idol-worshippers mock them.

n02614.summary: A narration reported via Tabraani adds that the believers will be called 'the people from Jahannam' because of blackness on their faces, until they bathe in a river in Jannah and the name is removed.

n02615.summary: Hudhayfah reports the Prophet ﷺ saying Islaam will fade until only a few old people remain who recite Laa Ilaaha Illallaah from following their forefathers, and that this Kalimah will save them from Jahannam, as Hudhayfah tells Sila when Sila keeps asking.

n02616.summary: Ali says the people closest to Allaah are those who most love and honour the believers in Laa Ilaaha Illallaah; Abu Dardaa, told that Abu Sa'd bin Munabbih freed a hundred slaves, says that keeping Imaan attached to the heart and the tongue moist with Dhikr is better.

n02618.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood says Allaah gives Imaan only to those He loves, and that whoever is too miserly to give Sadaqah, too afraid to fight in Jihaad, or too weak for night worship should recite Laa Ilaaha Illallaah, Allaahu Akbar, Al Hamdu Lillaah and Subhaanallaah abundantly.

n02619.summary: Anas reports that Abdullaah bin Rawaaha would invite Companions to believe for a moment by talking about Allaah, and the Prophet ﷺ forgave him after a man complained; Ataa bin Yasaar adds that Abdullaah said this to increase Imaan when a companion asked whether they were not already believers.

n02620.summary: Shurayh bin Abdullaah reports that Abdullaah bin Rawaaha would take hold of a Companion's hand and ask him to stand with him in a gathering of Dhikr to believe for a while.

n02621.summary: Abu Dardaa says Abdullaah bin Rawaaha took his hand and said to believe for a moment, because the heart overturns faster than a pot boiling at its pitch.

n02622.summary: Abu Dardaa says Abdullaah bin Rawaaha would call him to sit and discuss Imaan, likening it to a qamees that is taken off and put on again, and that the heart overturns faster than a boiling pot.

n02623.summary: Abu Dharr reports that Umar would take one or two Companions by the hand and ask them to stand with him to renew their Imaan, and they would talk about Allaah.

n02624.summary: Aswad bin Hilaal reports that while walking with them, Mu'aadh bin Jabal asked them to sit with him so they could believe for a moment.

n02625.summary: Abu Hurayrah reports that the Prophet ﷺ told people to renew their Imaan, and when asked how, said to recite Laa Ilaaha Illallaah abundantly.

n02626.summary: Abu Sa'eed Khudri reports that a man's brother had diarrhoea, honey made it worse twice, and the Prophet ﷺ told the man to try again, saying Allaah speaks the truth and the brother's belly is lying, until the brother was cured.

n02627.summary: Zaynab, wife of Abdullaah bin Mas'ood, reports that he cut a thread tied to her neck, calling incantations and amulets shirk, and told her to recite the Prophet's ﷺ supplication for cure instead.

n02628.summary: Ikrimah reports that Abdullaah bin Rawaaha was caught by his wife with a slave-woman; when she came with a knife he recited verses, and she said she believed in the Book of Allaah and rejected what her eyes had seen, and the Prophet ﷺ smiled broadly when told.

n02629.summary: Habeeb bin Abu Thaabit reports Abu Waa'il's account that at Siffeen Sahl bin Hunayf reminded them that at Hudaybiyyah they had accepted the treaty rather than fight, and that Umar questioned the treaty until the Prophet ﷺ and then Abu Bakr assured him.

n02630.summary: Sahl bin Hunayf and Umar recall the Hudaybiyyah treaty: Abu Jandal pleads not to be returned, the Prophet ﷺ says he cannot disobey Allaah, and both the Prophet and Abu Bakr assure Umar that he will perform Tawaaf at the Kabah, after which Umar makes amends.

n02631.summary: Anas reports that on the return from Hudaybiyyah the Prophet ﷺ received the verse of forgiveness and victory, which he said he loved more than everything on earth, and the Companions then received the verse promising Jannah to the believers.

n02632.summary: Anas and Mujammi bin Jaariya Ansaari report that after Hudaybiyyah the Prophet ﷺ recited the verses of clear victory, and when asked whether it was a victory he swore that it certainly was.

n02633.summary: Baraa says the 'victory' of Surah Fath is the pledge of Ridwaan at Hudaybiyyah rather than the conquest of Makkah, and Jaabir says it is nothing other than the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah.

n02634.summary: Qais bin Hajjaaj, reporting from his teacher, says Amr bin Al Aas stopped the Egyptian custom of throwing a virgin into the Nile, the river stopped flowing, and after Umar's note was thrown in it rose sixteen arm's lengths in a single night.

n02635.summary: Sahm bin Minjaab reports that on an expedition Alaa bin Hadhrami prayed at the island of Daarayn and led the army through the sea, where the water did not reach their saddle-cloths.

n02636.summary: Abu Hurayrah reports that Ibn Muka'bir, the Persian governor, seeing the Muslims cross the water, refused to fight such people and sailed back to Persia; the author then summarises a later account of Hujr bin Adi leading the crossing of the Tigris, with Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas.

n02637.summary: Mu'aawiya bin Harmal reports that Umar sent Tameem Daari to deal with a fire rising from Harra, and Tameem drove it back into its crevice with his bare hands; Umar then said one who has witnessed such a sign cannot be like one who has not.

n02638.summary: A Sahabi reports that when the Prophet ﷺ struck a boulder at the Khandaq with a spade, each strike sparked and showed him the palaces of Persia, Rome and Abyssinia, and he asked Allaah to grant them to the Muslims; Salmaan Faarsi watched and confirmed it.

n02639.summary: Amr bin Auf Muzani reports the same boulder event in which the spark lit up Madinah and the Prophet ﷺ promised Heera, Rome and San'aa; the Munaafiqeen mocked, and Surah Ahzaab verses were revealed; the author then previews Ibn Abbaas's fuller account.

n02640.summary: The author previews later narrations: the incident of poison having no effect on Khaalid bin Waleed, and the words of a Christian named Amr praising the Arabs while the Sahabah are with them.

n02641.summary: Thaabit bin Aqram tells Abu Hurayrah that numbers did not help at Badr; Khaalid says victory comes from Allaah and not numbers; Abu Bakr writes to Amr bin Al Aas that Allaah helped them with few, and refuses to hold back Usaamah's army; and Abdullaah bin Rawaaha urges the Muslims at Mu'ta to fight with trust in Allaah.

n02642.summary: Anas reports that the Prophet ﷺ found Haarith bin Maalik asleep in the Masjid and asked how he felt that morning; Haarith said he felt like a true Mu'min, describing how he turned from the world, fasted, prayed at night and seemed to see the Arsh and the people of Jannah and Jahannam, and the Prophet told him to remain steadfast.

n02643.summary: Another narration names the Sahabi as Haaritha bin Nu'maan, who asked the Prophet ﷺ to pray that he be martyred, and was the first to mount his horse when the call to Jihaad was made and the first to be martyred; Anas then reports a similar exchange with a young Ansaari, and another narration gives the same question about substantiating Imaan.

n02646.summary: Anas reports that Mu'aadh bin Jabal said he felt like a true believer that morning; when the Prophet ﷺ asked for proof, he described fearing death each morning and evening, seeing all nations kneeling for the Day of Qiyaamah, and the punishments of Jahannam and rewards of Jannah, and the Prophet told him to remain steadfast.

n02647.summary: Suwayd bin Haarith (RA) relates how a delegation of seven met the Prophet, who asked them the reality of their Imaan, and they listed its fifteen attributes.

n02648.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar relates how Harmalah bin Zaid Ansaari confessed that his heart held hypocrisy, and the Prophet prayed for him and left the obstinate hypocrites to Allaah.

n02649.summary: Aa'isha (RA) relates that an unnamed Sahabi who led prayers always ended with Surah Ikhlaas, and the Prophet said Allaah loves him for loving it.

n02650.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood relates the words of a Jewish scholar about Allaah's power over creation, which the Prophet confirmed with a smile and a verse of Surah Zumar.

n02651.summary: Anas bin Maalik relates the Prophet's answer about the disbelievers being raised on their faces, and Hudhayfah bin Usayd reports Abu Dharr's account of the three groups in which people will be resurrected and of the calamity that will destroy all riding animals.

n02653.summary: Tufayl bin Abdullaah (RA) relates his dream about Christians and Jews, after which the Prophet told the Sahabah not to say what Allaah and Muhammad wills but to say that the One Allaah wills.

n02654.summary: Hudhayfah relates a Muslim's dream about the Ahlul Kitaab and the Prophet's correction of the phrase what Allaah and Muhammad wills, and Abdullaah bin Abbaas reports the Prophet rebuking a man who equated him with Allaah.

n02656.summary: Awzaa'ee reports that a Jew asked the Prophet about free will, and each action was affirmed as Allaah's will, after which Jibra'eel said the Prophet had been inspired with the correct facts as Ibraheem was.

n02657.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood relates how the Prophet and the Sahabah overslept Fajr on the way back from Hudaybiyyah and the Prophet said Allaah had willed it as a lesson, and Abu Qataadah reports the Prophet saying Allaah takes souls in sleep when He wills.

n02658.summary: Taariq bin Shihaab relates that a Jew asked Umar where Jahannam is, given the verse about the vastness of Jannah, and Umar answered by comparing it to where the day goes at night, which the Jew said matched the Torah.

n02659.summary: Muhammad relates that Ali questioned a man who debated volition, asking whether Allaah creates, sickens, cures and moves people as He wills or as they will, and the narration breaks off mid-sentence.

n02660.summary: Anas bin Maalik relates that the Sahabah feared hypocrisy when they left the Prophet's company, and the Prophet said that Allaah being their Rabb in private and in public is not hypocrisy.

n02661.summary: Abu Hurayrah relates how a Bedouin asked who will call creation to account on the Day of Qiyaamah, and when told it is Allaah, the Bedouin said they were saved because the Magnanimous One forgives.

n02662.summary: Sa'eed bin Musayyib relates that Umar sent Mu'aadh bin Jabal to collect zakaah, and Mu'aadh gave it all to the poor and told his wife an inspector had gone with him, after which Umar laughed and gave her a gift.

n02663.summary: Aa'isha (RA) relates that Allaah hears everything, and that a verse was revealed about Khowla bint Tha'laba's debate with the Prophet over her husband, though Aa'isha could hear nothing from the corner of the room.

n02664.summary: Aa'isha (RA) relates Khowla bint Tha'laba's complaint to the Prophet about her husband, and that Jibra'eel brought the verse before she had stood up.

n02665.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports that the people wept at the Prophet's death, and Ma'n bin Adi replied that he wished to believe in him after his death as he had in his life.

n02666.summary: Alqamah reports from his mother that a woman who came to Aa'isha's room to pray near the Prophet's grave died while still in sajdah. Aa'isha took this as a lesson about death, and her doubt about the sudden death of her brother Abdur Rahmaan was removed.

n02667.summary: Ali (RA) explains that the water of the Flood and the wind that destroyed Aad were released by Allaah directly, without the angel who normally measures them, and cites the verses of Surah Haaqqah.

n02668.summary: Buqayrah (RA), the wife of Salmaan Faarsi, relates that on his deathbed Salmaan had the doors opened for expected visitors and musk sprinkled around his bed, and she found him dead as if asleep.

n02670.summary: Aa'isha (RA) remarks on a child of the Ansaar who died young, and the Prophet explains that Allaah created the people of Jannah and Jahannam with their destinies set while they were still in their fathers' backs.

n02671.summary: Waleed bin Ubaadah relates his father Ubaadah bin Saamit's deathbed advice that one cannot taste Imaan without believing in predestination, quoting the Prophet that the pen was the first thing Allaah created.

n02672.summary: Abu Nadhrah relates that Abu Abdullaah, a companion of the Prophet, wept on his deathbed because he did not know which of the two handfuls of souls Allaah had set aside for him.

n02673.summary: Muaadh bin Jabal (RA) weeps on his deathbed, saying he does not know which of the two handfuls of souls he will be placed in, as the Prophet had said.

n02674.summary: Muhammad bin Ubayd Makki relates that Ibn Abbaas, on hearing of a man who denied predestination, vowed to break his neck and bite off his nose, quoting the Prophet's warning that denying predestination would be the first Shirk in this Ummah.

n02675.summary: Ataa bin Abu Rabaah relates Ibn Abbaas's words about people who objected to predestination, whom he called the worst of this Ummah and whose sick he would not visit or whose dead he would not bury.

n02676.summary: Ibn Abbaas says he wishes he could trample the head of anyone who denied predestination, because the Lowhul Mahfoodh is written by Allaah's glances that create, give life, give death and honour as He pleases.

n02677.summary: Naafi relates that Abdullaah bin Umar cut off a correspondent in Shaam who objected to predestination, quoting the Prophet's warning that people in his Ummah would deny it.

n02678.summary: Nazzaal bin Sabrah relates that Ali corrected a claim that Allaah does not know something until it happens, explaining the verse about testing, and quotes his earlier saying that nothing happens on earth until it is decided in the heavens.

n02680.summary: Ibn Abbaas relates that when the verse about the trumpet was revealed, the Prophet said he could not live in ease with the trumpet-blower poised to blow, and taught the Sahabah to say that Allaah is sufficient for them.

n02681.summary: Another narration of the trumpet incident says that when the Sahabah heard the warning they were troubled, and the Prophet told them to recite that Allaah is sufficient for them.

n02682.summary: Hafsa (RA) tells Sauda Yamaaniyyah (RA) that the one-eyed Dajjaal has appeared, and Sauda hides in a tent until the Prophet comes, clarifies that he has not yet appeared, and dusts her off.

n02683.summary: Sa'eed bin Musayyib relates that Abu Bakr asked whether there is a place in Iraq called Khurasaan, from which Dajjaal would emerge, and Abu Bakr also stated that Dajjaal would come from the Jews of Marw.

n02684.summary: Ibn Abi Mulaykah relates that Ibn Abbaas stayed awake fearing the smoke sign of the Last Day after a tailed star appeared, and another report has him fearing that Dajjaal would appear.

n02685.summary: Ubaadah bin Nasi reports that Abu Bakr on his deathbed told Aa'isha to bury him in his two garments, since the dead will be either richly clothed or stripped in the grave.

n02686.summary: Aa'isha (RA) reports that when Abu Bakr was dying she recited a couplet on the uselessness of wealth, and he corrected her with a verse of Surah Qaaf and asked to be buried in his two garments, since the living need new clothing more than the dead.

n02687.summary: Aa'isha (RA) relates Abu Bakr's last days: he rebuked her weeping, asked which day the Prophet died, hoped to die that same night, and asked that his saffron-stained garment be washed and added to the Prophet's three-sheet shroud.

n02689.summary: Yahya bin Abu Raashid Nasri relates Umar's deathbed instructions to his son about washing, shrouding, the grave and the funeral, based on the hope of good with Allaah.

n02690.summary: Uthmaan (RA) wept whenever he stood at a grave, and when asked, said the Prophet called the grave the first stage of the Aakhirah and had never seen a sight more frightening.

n02691.summary: Hudhayfah, gravely ill, asked for a plain shroud, saying a good end would be exchanged for something better and otherwise the shroud would be quickly removed.

n02692.summary: Hudhayfah sent Sila and Abu Mas'ood to buy his shroud, rejected the striped sheet they bought, and asked for two plain white sheets instead.

n02693.summary: Hudhayfah told the men who bought his shroud that a righteous man's shroud would be exchanged, but a wicked man's would be thrown into the grave or used to strike his face on the Day of Qiyaamah.

n02694.summary: As death approached, Abu Moosa told his attendants to dig a wide grave, then described how the grave would either open onto Jannah or narrow onto Jahannam.

n02695.summary: Usayd bin Hudhayr said he would have no doubt of Jannah if he stayed in one of three states: reciting or hearing the Qur'aan, hearing the Prophet's sermon, or attending funerals.

n02696.summary: Abu Hurayrah reports that when the Sahabah asked about Jannah, the Prophet described its buildings and the three whose du'aa is never rejected.

n02697.summary: Faatima went to the Prophet for food for her hungry household, chose the words of dhikr he offered over five goats, and returned to Ali saying she had gained something of benefit for the Aakhirah.

n02698.summary: Anas bin Maalik reports that Abu Moosa, hearing people talk eloquently, asked why people neglect the Aakhirah, and answered that the world is before them while the Aakhirah is still to come.

n02699.summary: Imraan bin Husayn reports the Prophet explaining the verse about the earthquake of Qiyaamah, that nine hundred and ninety-nine in a thousand will go to Jahannam, and his hope that his Ummah will be a quarter, a third or half of Jannah's people.

n02700.summary: Abu Sa'eed Khudri relates the same teaching from the Prophet, in which Aadam is told to separate those for Jahannam, the Sahabah turn pale, and the Prophet again hopes his Ummah will be a quarter, a third or half of Jannah's people.

n02701.summary: Another report says the Sahabah were deeply grieved and worried when the Prophet said that nine hundred and ninety-nine in a thousand would enter Jahannam.

n02702.summary: Abdullaah bin Zubayr reports that when the verse about bringing cases before Allaah was revealed, Zubayr asked whether such cases would be brought against them, and on being told yes, called the matter a serious one.

n02703.summary: Zubayr asked what bounties people would be questioned about and whether disputes between people would be brought before Allaah, and the Prophet confirmed that every right will be repaid.

n02704.summary: Qais bin Abi Haazim reports that Abdullaah bin Rawaaha wept in his wife's lap, fearing he would not be rescued when crossing over Jahannam, and she wept with him.

n02705.summary: As death approached, Ubaadah bin Saamit asked everyone he had dealings with to claim any wrong from him, then told them not to weep, to pray and to ask forgiveness for him, and gave burial instructions.

n02706.summary: Umar, who had asked Abdur Rahmaan bin Awf for a loan of four thousand dirhams, was troubled at the idea of taking it from the public treasury, fearing he would be held to account on the Day of Qiyaamah.

n02707.summary: The author signposts two later narrations, one in which Abu Hurayrah collapsed and one in which Mu'aawiya wept, both on hearing a hadith about Allaah's accountability on the Day of Qiyaamah.

n02708.summary: Awf bin Maalik and his companions, searching for the Prophet at night, found him and learned he had chosen intercession over having half his Ummah enter Jannah, and he promised intercession for those who never commit Shirk.

n02709.summary: Abdur Rahmaan bin Abu Aqeel reports that when a Thaqeef delegation asked the Prophet for a kingdom like Sulaymaan's, he said Allaah had kept for him a special prayer, to be used for interceding for his Ummah on the Day of Qiyaamah.

n02710.summary: Ummu Salamah reports the Prophet saying that he is an excellent intercessor for the sinners of his Ummah, and that intercession will be denied to anyone who belittles his Companions.

n02711.summary: Ali bin Abi Taalib reports the Prophet's saying that he will keep interceding until his Rabb is satisfied, and then tells the people of Iraq that the verse giving the Prophet hope refers to the privilege of intercession.

n02712.summary: Ibn Buraydah reports that his father Buraydah told Mu'aawiya, who was being praised, that the Prophet expected to intercede for as many people as there are trees and stones, so Mu'aawiya should place his hope in that while Ali need not.

n02713.summary: Talq bin Habeeb and Yazeed Faqeer, who both had denied that believers will be brought out of Jahannam, were convinced by Jaabir bin Abdillaah's explanation of the Qur'aan and of the Prophet's words.

n02714.summary: Handhala, one of the Prophet's scribes, feared he had become a hypocrite because he forgot the vivid talk of Jannah when with his family, and the Prophet told him there are times for each.

n02715.summary: Ibn Mas'ood reports the Prophet's vision of the nations and the seventy thousand who enter Jannah without reckoning, described as those who do not brand themselves, use amulets or divine by birds, and trust only in their Rabb, and his hope that his Ummah will be a third or half of Jannah's people.

n02716.summary: Sulaym bin Aamir reports that a Bedouin asked about the thorny lotus of Jannah, and the Prophet explained that Allaah will remove its thorns and make each one a fruit with seventy-two flavours.

n02717.summary: Utba bin Abd as-Sulami reports that a Bedouin asked about the acacia tree in Jannah, and the Prophet said Allaah will replace its thorns with fruit, each with seventy-two flavours.

n02718.summary: Utba bin Abd as-Sulami reports a Bedouin's questions about Jannah, and the Prophet describes its pond, the tree Tooba, the walnut tree of Shaam, its grapes, and a grape as large as a waterskin bucket that could feed a whole family and tribe.

n02719.summary: Ibn Umar reports that an Abyssinian man asked whether he would be with the Prophet in Jannah, heard of its rewards, asked whether he would see what the Prophet sees, then wept until he died, and the Prophet himself lowered him into the grave.

n02720.summary: Ibn Zaid reports that when the Prophet recited the verses about Jannah to the Sahabah, an Abyssinian man sighed deeply and died, and the Prophet said that longing for Jannah had taken his soul.

n02722.summary: After a good meal was served, Umar wept at the thought that poor Muslims who died without filling themselves had been given Jannah, which he felt far surpassed his own share.

n02723.summary: Mus'ab bin Sa'd reports his dying father, Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas, telling him not to weep, since Allaah will never punish him and he will be among the people of Jannah, as the Prophet clearly stated.

n02724.summary: Several reports describe Amr bin Al Aas on his deathbed weeping over what follows death, recalling his past enmity, his conversion and his growing love for the Prophet, and giving instructions for his burial.

n02725.summary: The author cross-refers to earlier sayings in which Companions longed for Jannah in battle, at home, in illness and at the loss of a child, including Umayr bin Humaam, Anas bin Nadhr, Ammaar and Abu Dardaa.

n02726.summary: Aa'isha wept at the thought of Jahannam and asked whether anyone would think of family on the Day of Qiyaamah, and the Prophet described three moments when no one thinks of another: at the scales, at the handing out of the records, and at the bridge of Siraat.

n02727.summary: An elderly Companion fainted when the Prophet recited the verse on the fuel of Jahannam and was given glad tidings after saying the Kalimah; a young Ansaari who wept at mention of Jahannam died in the Prophet's arms.

n02728.summary: The author recalls two sayings: Shaddaad bin Aws said the fire of Jahannam had banished his sleep, and Abdullaah bin Rawaaha wept at Mu'ta, fearing the crossing over Jahannam.

n02729.summary: Nayyaar bin Mukram Aslami reports that when the revelation that the Romans would again prevail over the Persians came, Abu Bakr proclaimed it against the Quraysh, took their wager, and when the Romans won after the six-year limit many accepted Islaam.

n02730.summary: Baraa reports that Abu Bakr renewed the wager with the Quraysh on the Prophet's advice, and when the winnings came he was told to give them away in charity because they were unlawful.

n02731.summary: Ka'b bin Adi, returning from a delegation to the Prophet, has his doubts about the Prophet's death settled by a vision, and later tells Maqoqis of Allaah's promise that His Deen would dominate.

n02732.summary: Abu Bakr, Umar and Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas each urge the Muslims to wage Jihaad with trust in Allaah's promise, Sa'd reminding them of the army of Yazdgird they face.

n02733.summary: Umaarah bin Khuzaymah narrates how Khuzaymah bin Thaabit testified that the Prophet had bought a horse from a Bedouin, and the Prophet then accepted his single testimony as equal to that of two men.

n02734.summary: Two further versions of the horse testimony report that the Prophet asked Khuzaymah on what basis he testified, and that Khuzaymah's testimony was accepted because he believed the Prophet's news from the heavens.

n02735.summary: Aa'isha narrates that when the Prophet told of his night journey to Masjidul Aqsa and the heavens, some who had professed Imaan left Islaam, and Abu Bakr affirmed the report and received the title Siddeeq.

n02736.summary: Variant reports of the night journey account describe the test it posed to the people, and Abu Bakr's reply to those who came to him saying the Prophet had travelled a month's journey in one night.

n02737.summary: Jaabir bin Abdullaah reports that when locusts became scarce in Umar's caliphate and a rider brought a handful from Yemen, Umar recalled the Prophet's saying that locusts would be the first creatures to become extinct and the rest would follow.

n02738.summary: Fudhaala bin Abu Fudhaala Ansaari reports that his father urged the ill Ali to return to Madinah from Yamba, but Ali said the Prophet had told him he would not die until he became Khalifah and his beard was dyed with the blood from his forehead.

n02739.summary: Ali recounts that Abdullaah bin Salaam warned him, as he set out for Iraq, that a sword would strike him there, and Ali says he had already heard the same from the Prophet.

n02740.summary: Mu'aawiya bin Jareer narrates that when Ali caught Ibn Muljim giving a false name, Ali let him go after he gave his father's name, because the Prophet had said Ali's assassin would be a man from the Jews.

n02741.summary: Ubaydah reports the couplets Ali recited whenever he saw Ibn Muljim, and Abu Tufayl reports that Ali, after ordering his allowance paid, pointed to his beard and recited verses on facing death.

n02742.summary: Ummu Ammaar reports that Ammaar knew he would be killed in a battle between Muslim armies, and that at Siffeen he drank the milk he had been told would be his last drink before fighting until he was killed, and Khaalid bin Waleed relays Mu'aawiya's fear of being blamed for Ammaar's death.

n02743.summary: Ibraheem bin Ashtar reports that Abu Dharr, dying in the wilderness as the Prophet had foretold, had his wife watch the road until a group of travellers from Yemen, including a young Ansaari who gave his own shroud, came to bury him.

n02744.summary: Khuraym bin Aws reports that the Prophet foretold he would be given Shaymaa bint Buqaylah if Heera was conquered, and after the conquest he claimed her, as described, and sold her to her wealthy brother for a thousand Dirhams.

n02745.summary: Jubayr bin Hayya reports that Mughiera bin Shu'ba, sent to negotiate with the Persian commander Bandaarfaan, told him the Prophet had promised the Arabs victory and assistance, so they would never return to their former hardship.

n02746.summary: Jubayr bin Hayya reports a longer account of Mughiera bin Shu'ba, sent with Nu'maan bin Muqarrin's army to the people of Ahwaaz, explaining that the Prophet had ordered them to fight until the people worshipped Allaah alone or paid jizyah.

n02747.summary: Talq reports that Abu Dardaa stayed sure his house would not burn, because he recited the words the Prophet had taught him each morning for protection.

n02748.summary: The author gathers several remarks that confirm the Prophet's predictions: Adi's third prophecy, Hishaam bin Al Aas and others telling Jabala bin Ayham that they would take his kingdom, Ali assuring Abu Bakr the Deen would prevail, and a forward reference to Ibn Umar and a lion.

n02749.summary: Abu Asmaa reports that when the verse on an atom's weight of good and evil was revealed, Abu Bakr asked whether every evil would be requited, and the Prophet said worldly hardship is retribution while good deeds are rewarded in the Aakhirah.

n02750.summary: Abu Bakr reports that after the verse saying whoever does evil will be requited was revealed, the Prophet recited it to him, and when Abu Bakr asked who could be free of sin, the Prophet said believers are punished in this world so they meet Allaah without sin.

n02752.summary: Muhammad bin Muntashir reports that Umar struck a man who called a verse of the Qur'aan the harshest, then explained the next day that the verse had weighed on the Sahabah until Allaah revealed the verse promising forgiveness to those who seek it.

n02753.summary: Tha'laba reports that Amr bin Samurah confessed to theft and had his hand cut off, praising Allaah for cleansing him, and Hasan reports that the ill Imraan bin Husayn explained his suffering as the result of sins that Allaah had largely forgiven.

n02754.summary: Abu Bakr, finding dinars under his dying son's pillow, says he doubts his skin could bear the punishment for not giving them in charity, and the Prophet tells a slave-owner that his slaves' wrongs will be weighed against his punishment of them, after which the man frees them.

n02755.summary: Abu Hurayrah reports that the Sahabah were distressed by the verse on what is in the heart, and the Prophet taught them to say 'we hear and obey', after which Allaah abrogated the burden with the verse that He does not burden a soul beyond its capacity; Mujaahid reports Ibn Abbaas explaining this and Ibn Umar weeping over the verse.

n02756.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood reports that the Sahabah were distressed by the verse on not mixing Imaan with dhulm and asked who had not done wrong, and the Prophet explained from Luqmaan's advice to his son that dhulm here means shirk.

n02757.summary: A variant report says that when the verse on not mixing Imaan with dhulm was revealed, the Prophet said he had been told that he was among such people.

n02758.summary: Safiyya bint Shaybah reports Aa'isha's praise of the women of the Ansaar, who, when the verse on drawing scarves over the chest was revealed, covered themselves at once and came to salaah behind the Prophet looking like crows perched on their heads.

n02759.summary: Makhool reports that an extremely old, sinful man asked the Prophet whether repentance was possible, and on accepting Islaam was told that Allaah would forgive all his treachery and sins and turn his evils into good deeds.

n02760.summary: Abu Farwah reports that a man who had committed every sin asked whether he could repent, and the Prophet told him that doing good and abstaining from evil would turn all his past sins into good deeds, after which the man went off repeatedly saying Allaahu Akbar.

n02761.summary: Abu Hurayrah relates that a woman who had committed adultery and killed her child was told by him that she had no repentance, until the Prophet recited the verses of Surah Furqaan offering forgiveness, and another report says she freed her slave woman and repented sincerely.

n02762.summary: Abul Hasan, a freed slave of Tameem Daari, reports that when the verse saying only deviant people follow poets was revealed, Hassaan bin Thaabit, Abdullaah bin Rawaaha and Ka'b bin Maalik came weeping, and the Prophet recited the exception for believing poets who defend Islaam.

n02763.summary: Ataa bin Saa'ib describes the old Abdur Rahmaan bin Abu Layla explaining that a believer's longing to meet Allaah at death differs from the dread of the rejecter, quoting the Prophet's saying that whoever loves to meet Allaah, Allaah loves to meet him.

n02764.summary: Abdullaah bin Amr reports that Abu Bakr wept excessively when the Surah Zilzaal was revealed, and the Prophet told him that if people never erred, Allaah would create a nation that erred and sinned so that He could forgive them.

n02765.summary: Umar reports that the Prophet asked him how he would fare in the grave when Munkar and Nakeer examined him, and Umar, told he would be in full command of his senses, said he would be able to handle them.

n02766.summary: A variant of the grave examination account says the Prophet told Umar, on Jibra'eel's word, that he would answer the questioners with the articles of faith and that they would wonder whether they had been sent to question him or he to question them.

n02767.summary: Abul Bahriyya Kindi reports that Umar, coming out to a gathering where Uthmaan was present, said that among them was a man whose Imaan would suffice an entire army if it were divided among them.

n02768.summary: A set of cross-references gathers remarks already quoted elsewhere on the strength of Imaan: Ibn Umar on the Sahabah's hearts being firmer than mountains, Ammaar's contentment with Imaan, Abu Bakr and Umar's trust and taqwa, Ali's trust in Allaah over one's own hand, Aamir bin Rabee'ah's detachment from the world, and Aa'isha's account of Usayd bin Hudhayr.

n02769.summary: Haarith, a freed slave of Uthmaan, reports Uthmaan's wudhu and the Prophet's saying that sins between the prayers are forgiven, with the lasting good deeds being the tasbeeh, and Abu Uthmaan reports Salmaan Faarsi shaking a tree to show how sins fall away with wudhu and the five prayers.

n02770.summary: Aamir bin Sa'd reports, from his father Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas, that when told one of two brothers was the better, the Prophet pointed to the surviving brother's prayers and compared salaah to a river at the door that washes away dirt five times a day.

n02771.summary: Abu Hurayrah narrates that Talha dreamt that a man who died later entered Jannah before the martyr, and the Prophet explained it by the man's Ramadan fast and his extra salaah.

n02772.summary: Ali narrates that a man confessed a sin to the Prophet in the Masjid, and the Prophet told him that his salaah performed with proper wudhu was compensation for it.

n02773.summary: Abdullaah bin Amr narrates that the Prophet named salaah, then jihaad, then kindness to parents as the best deeds, and told a man who vowed to leave his parents for jihaad to judge whether they had others to care for them.

n02774.summary: Amr bin Murrah Juhani narrates that the Prophet told a man who asked his rank that the five salaahs, zakaah, Ramadan fasting and Nafl salaah in Ramadan would place him among the Siddeeqeen and the martyrs.

n02775.summary: Anas says that the Prophet's last emphasis on his deathbed was salaah and the treatment of slaves, which he repeated even when he could no longer speak clearly.

n02777.summary: Ali narrates that the Prophet asked for a writing so that his Ummah would never forget salaah, zakaah and the treatment of slaves, and Ali offered to memorise the words instead.

n02778.summary: Ali relates that the Prophet's last words, up to the departure of his soul, stressed salaah, zakaah, kindness to slaves and the Shahaadah, and that the Fire is forbidden to one who testifies to it.

n02779.summary: Abu Bakr says that a person secures Allaah's protection on earth by performing salaah.

n02780.summary: Abu Maleeh reports that Umar said from the pulpit that there can be no Islaam in a person who does not perform salaah.

n02781.summary: Zaid bin Thaabit, Hudhayfah, Abdullaah bin Umar and Abdullaah bin Amr each give a saying on salaah, including that the ground will testify for the one who prays on it on the day he meets Allaah.

n02783.summary: Abdullaah bin Amr narrates that a cyst on Aadam's neck moved down his body and finally left him each time he performed salaah.

n02784.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood says that while a person performs salaah he is knocking at the King's door, and the door opens to whoever knocks.

n02785.summary: Ibn Mas'ood and Salmaan Faarsi say that salaah compensates for sins committed between prayers, and Ibn Mas'ood tells how Aadam's cyst fell away with each salaah; Ibn Mas'ood also advises making du'aa after the Fardh salaahs.

n02786.summary: Salmaan Faarsi says that a person's sins gather above his head while he stands in salaah and fall away at each prostration, like leaves falling from a tree.

n02787.summary: Taariq bin Shihaab spent a night with Salmaan Faarsi, who advised guarding the Fardh salaahs and moderation in worship, and Abu Moosa Ash'ari said that salaah compensates for the sins that burn a person up.

n02789.summary: Anas narrates that the Prophet said perfume and women were made beloved to him and the coolness of his eyes was placed in salaah, and Ibn Abbaas narrates that Jibra'eel told the Prophet to take from salaah as much as he pleased.

n02791.summary: Ibn Abbaas narrates that the Prophet said every Nabi had a yearning, his being standing in Tahajjud salaah at night, and that his income is the Khums, which goes to the leaders after him.

n02792.summary: Anas narrates that the Prophet stood so long in Tahajjud salaah that his feet swelled, and when asked why, he said he should not then be a grateful servant.

n02793.summary: Abu Hurayrah, Ibn Mas'ood, Nu'maan bin Basheer, Aa'isha, Mughiera and Anas describe the Prophet's long Tahajjud standing until his feet swelled or cracked, and Anas, through Humayd, describes how his night prayer, sleep and fasting varied through the month.

n02796.summary: Ibn Mas'ood says he followed the Prophet in salaah and nearly sat down out of the length of his standing, and Abu Dharr narrates that the Prophet stood all night reciting one verse about Allaah's punishment and forgiveness.

n02797.summary: Anas narrates that after the Prophet was injured he still recited seven long Surahs in the night.

n02798.summary: Hudhayfah narrates praying behind the Prophet at night, when he recited Surah Baqarah, Nisaa and Aal Imraan unhurriedly, pausing to glorify, ask and seek refuge as he passed each relevant verse, with long ruku and sajdah.

n02799.summary: Hudhayfah narrates joining the Prophet's salaah from behind, when the Prophet prolonged four rakaahs, and that the Prophet said he would have shortened it had he known Hudhayfah was there.

n02800.summary: Aa'isha describes the Prophet's long night prayer and his final illness, when he asked Abu Bakr to lead the people in salaah despite her objections, and Ubaydullaah bin Abdullaah reports that the Prophet bathed repeatedly and fell unconscious each time he tried to go out to the people.

n02801.summary: Anas narrates that Abu Bakr led the people in salaah during the Prophet's final illness, and that when the Prophet lifted the curtain and looked at them, they almost broke their salaah with joy; the Prophet passed away that day.

n02802.summary: Anas narrates a second account of the Prophet lifting the curtain during Abu Bakr's leading of salaah on the Monday of his final illness, and indicating to them to complete the salaah.

n02803.summary: Miswar bin Makhramah narrates going to see Umar, who lay in a coma after being stabbed, and that Umar roused when told salaah was due, saying he must perform it, and then prayed with blood still flowing from his wound.

n02804.summary: Miswar narrates a second account in which Umar, after being stabbed, regained consciousness when told the time for salaah had set in, and said that there is no part in Islaam for one who does not perform it.

n02805.summary: Muhammad bin Miskeen narrates that Uthmaan's wife told the rebels surrounding his house that he spent whole nights reciting the entire Qur'aan in a single rakaah of salaah.

n02806.summary: Another narration reports that after Uthmaan bin Affaan was assassinated, his wife said he had spent whole nights reciting the entire Qur'aan in a single rakaah of salaah.

n02807.summary: Uthmaan bin Abdur Rahmaan Taymi relates that his father once saw Uthmaan recite the entire Qur'aan in one rakaah by the Maqaam Ibraheem, and Ataa bin Abi Rabaah and Muhammad bin Seereen are also reported to have spent nights reciting the whole Qur'aan in one rakaah.

n02811.summary: Musayyib bin Raafi narrates that Ibn Abbaas refused a treatment for his blindness that would have stopped his salaah for seven days, after the Sahabah asked what he would do with his salaah if he died in that time.

n02812.summary: Another narration says that when Ibn Abbaas lost his sight and was offered a treatment that required him to give up salaah for a few days, he refused, quoting the Prophet that whoever neglects salaah will meet Allaah in a state of His anger.

n02813.summary: Ali bin Abu Jameelah reports that Ibn Abbaas made sajdah a thousand times every day.

n02814.summary: Ibn Mas'ood fasted optional fasts rarely, saying he grew too weak to perform salaah when fasting and loved salaah more, so he fasted only three days a month; another report says he was irregular only in the Duhaa salaah.

n02816.summary: Abdur Rahmaan bin Yazeed reports that Ibn Mas'ood fasted optional fasts less than anyone he had seen, preferring salaah because fasting made him too weak to perform it.

n02817.summary: Aa'isha narrates that the Prophet praised Saalim, freed slave of Abu Hudhayfah, for his beautiful night recitation of the Qur'aan in the Masjid, saying Allaah had made such people amongst his Ummah.

n02818.summary: Masrooq describes Abu Moosa Ash'ari's night salaah and supplications on a journey, and Abu Uthmaan Nahdi says he was the guest of Abu Hurayrah for seven days, when the household took turns worshipping through a third of each night.

n02820.summary: Abdullaah bin Abu Bakr narrates that Abu Talha lost his focus in salaah on seeing a bird in his orchard, so he gave the orchard to the Prophet in charity; an unnamed Ansaari did the same with his orchard, which Uthmaan sold for 50,000 Dirhams.

n02821.summary: Asmaa narrates that her son Abdullaah bin Zubayr prayed through the nights and fasted through the days, and was therefore called the pigeon of the Masjid.

n02822.summary: Adi bin Haatim says that whenever the time for any salaah came, he was already prepared and full of eagerness for it.

n02823.summary: Abu Hurayrah helped carry bricks for the Prophet's Masjid, and when he offered to take a brick the Prophet was carrying, the Prophet told him to take another, reminding him there is no life other than the Aakhirah.

n02824.summary: Talq bin Ali says that while helping build the Masjid he was told by the Prophet to mix the mortar because he did it best, and the Prophet was pleased with the way he handled the spade.

n02825.summary: Abdullaah bin Abu Awfa says that when his wife died he asked the people to carry her bier with great fervour, because she and her slaves had carried rocks for the Masjid at night when the men could manage only two rocks at a time by day.

n02826.summary: Ubaadah bin Saamit relates that the Ansaar offered the Prophet money to renovate and beautify the Masjid, but he refused, wanting its ceiling to stay like the shelter of Moosa, and Hasan describes how high that shelter was.

n02827.summary: Ibn Shihaab reports that in the Prophet's time the Masjid had palm-trunk pillars and a roof of palm branches without plaster, so it became full of mud whenever it rained.

n02828.summary: Imaam Bukhaari reports from Abu Sa'eed Khudri that the Prophet, in a vision about Laylatul Qadr, saw himself prostrating in mud, and mud traces were later seen on his forehead after rain leaked through the palm roof during salaah.

n02829.summary: Khaalid bin Ma'daan narrates that Abdullaah bin Rawaaha and Abu Dardaa were measuring the Masjid with a stick to build it like the buildings of Shaam, and the Prophet threw the stick away and said it should be made of grass, sticks and a roof like the shelter of Moosa, because death is nearer than that.

n02830.summary: Naafi narrates that Umar extended the Masjid from the pillars up to the Maqsoorah, saying that he would never have done so had he not heard the Prophet say that the Masjid ought to be extended.

n02831.summary: Naafi reports from Abdullaah bin Umar that the Masjid in the Prophet's time was built of unbaked bricks with palm pillars and a palm roof, that Umar rebuilt it the same way without extending it, and that Uthmaan made a large extension in decorative stone and teakwood.

n02832.summary: Atiyya narrates that Abdullaah bin Umar said the Masjid's pillars were palm trunks in the Prophet's time, were rebuilt with palm trunks in Abu Bakr's Khilaafah, and were rebuilt by Uthmaan in baked brick, where they still stand.

n02833.summary: Mahmood bin Labeed reports that Uthmaan cited the Prophet's saying that whoever builds a Masjid for Allaah will have a house built for him in Jannah when he decided to rebuild the Masjid, and Muttalib bin Abdullaah reports that Uthmaan, after consulting the senior Sahabah, demolished and extended it over ten months, supervising the work himself.

n02834.summary: Jaabir bin Usaamah Juhani says he met the Prophet and his companions in the marketplace on their way to mark out a Masjid for his people, and by the time he arrived the Prophet had marked the site and fixed the Qibla with a stick.

n02835.summary: Uthmaan bin Ataa narrates that when Umar was conquering cities he wrote to the governors of Basrah, Kufa and Egypt to build one central Masjid for Jumu'ah with small tribal Masaajid, and told army commanders to set up bases in cities and build only one Masjid.

n02836.summary: Urwa bin Zubayr reports that one Sahabi said the Prophet instructed them to make places of salaah in their homes, build them well and keep them clean, and Aa'isha reports the same instruction.

n02837.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas narrates that the Sahabah buried a woman who used to clean the Masjid without telling the Prophet, and when he learned of it he prayed the Janaazah for her and said he had seen her in Jannah picking up dirt from the Masjid.

n02838.summary: Abdullaah bin Urhar (RA) reports that Umar used to burn incense in the Prophet's Masjid every Friday.

n02839.summary: Ubay bin Ka'b says that a man who lived furthest from the Masjid never missed salaah, and when told to buy a donkey he refused, wanting every step to be recorded for him, and the Prophet said Allaah has recorded it all for him.

n02840.summary: In another narration Ubay bin Ka'b says that a man from the Ansaar, whose house was furthest from the Masjid, refused a donkey because he hoped for reward in every step, and the Prophet told him he would have what he hoped for.

n02841.summary: Another narration states that the Prophet said the stages of the Ansaari man in Jannah are raised with every step he takes to the Masjid.

n02842.summary: Zaid bin Thaabit narrates that when he walked with the Prophet to salaah the Prophet took short steps, explaining that a person keeps the reward of salaah while he is making the effort toward it and that he did so to increase his steps toward salaah.

n02844.summary: Thaabit says he walked with Anas bin Maalik in Zaawiyah, and when Anas heard the Adhaan he shortened his steps until he entered the Masjid, explaining that this was so his steps in the effort of salaah would be increased.

n02845.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood hurried to the Masjid, and when someone objected he said he wanted to reach the first takbeer and that salaah is the most deserving thing to hurry toward, a reply Salamah bin Kuhayl also reports.

n02846.summary: Abu Qataadah narrates that while the Sahabah were praying behind the Prophet he heard noise from those at the back, and after salaah the Prophet forbade running to salaah and told them to pray what they caught and complete what they had missed.

n02847.summary: Anas narrates that when a Bedouin began urinating in the Masjid and the Sahabah shouted at him, the Prophet told them to leave him alone, then had a bucket of water poured over the spot and explained that Masjids are for the remembrance of Allaah, salaah and the Qur'aan, not for filth.

n02848.summary: Abu Sa'eed Khudri narrates that Mu'aawiya questioned a group sitting in the Masjid for dhikr and got their oath of sincerity, then related that the Prophet asked the same of his Sahabah and told them Jibra'eel had reported that Allaah boasts of them before the angels.

n02849.summary: Abu Waaqid Laythi narrates that the Prophet described three people who came to a gathering, one of whom found a place and was granted it, one of whom was shy and was treated kindly, and one of whom turned away and was turned away from, and Abul Qamraa relates that the Prophet sat with those learning and teaching the Qur'aan, saying he had been commanded to sit with that gathering.

n02850.summary: Kulayb bin Shihaab narrates that Ali, hearing loud Qur'aan recitation and teaching in the Masjid, said these were the people the Prophet loved most, and also reports Ali saying the same in the Masjid of Kufa.

n02851.summary: Hasan reports that Abu Hurayrah called out in the Madinah marketplace that the traders were missing the Prophet's inheritance, which was only people praying, reciting the Qur'aan and discussing halaal and haraam in the Masjid, and he rebuked them for it.

n02852.summary: Ibn Mu'aawiya Kindi reports that when he visited Umar in Shaam, Umar asked whether men sat in the Masjid only with their own tribe or acquaintances, and he replied that their Masjid had gatherings for learning and sharing good, so Umar said they would remain in good stead as long as they continued so.

n02853.summary: Abu Hurayrah narrates that the Prophet came out with the Sahabah and called the Jews to accept Islaam, and after they refused three times he told them the earth belongs to Allaah and His Rasool and that he wished to banish them, allowing them to sell their belongings first.

n02854.summary: Aa'isha narrates that Sa'd bin Mu'aadh was wounded at Khandaq and lodged in a tent in the Masjid, that Jibra'eel then directed the Prophet to Banu Qurayzah, where Sa'd ruled that their fighters be killed and their women and children enslaved, and that Sa'd's wound burst open and he died after praying for death if no further war with Quraysh remained.

n02855.summary: Yazeed bin Abdullaah bin Qusayt says that the men of the Suffa were homeless men of the Prophet's time who slept in the Masjid, and that the Prophet would call some of them at night to eat supper with him until Allaah made them independent.

n02856.summary: Asmaa bint Yazeed narrates that Abu Dharr served the Prophet and then lay down to sleep in the Masjid as his home, and when the Prophet found him lying there and nudged him with his foot, Abu Dharr sat up and asked where else he had to sleep.

n02857.summary: Abu Dharr says that after serving the Prophet he would lie down in the Masjid, Hasan says he saw Uthmaan take his siesta there during his Khilaafah, Abdullaah bin Umar says that as youths they spent nights in the Masjid and rested there after Jumu'ah, and Umar says lying on one's side is fine after sitting long in the Masjid.

n02858.summary: Khaleed bin Abu Is'haaq asked Abdullaah bin Abbaas about sleeping in the Masjid, and Ibn Abbaas replied that there is no harm in it when one sleeps to gain strength for salaah or Tawaaf.

n02859.summary: Jaabir says that when the wind blew fiercely at night the Prophet hurried to the Masjid and stayed until it calmed, and that he also hurried to salaah at eclipses, and Ataa reports that the Sahabi Ya'la bin Umayyah would sit in the Masjid even briefly with the intention of I'tikaaf.

n02861.summary: Atiyya bin Sufyaan bin Abdullaah narrates that when a delegation from Thaqeef came to the Prophet during Ramadhaan he pitched a tent for them in the Masjid, and once they accepted Islaam they began fasting with him.

n02862.summary: Uthmaan bin Abil Aas narrates that when the Thaqeef delegation came the Prophet housed them in the Masjid so that it would soften their hearts.

n02863.summary: Abdullaah bin Zubayr says that they once ate roasted meat with the Prophet in the Masjid, and when the Iqaamah was called they only wiped their hands on pebbles.

n02864.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports why the Masjid was called Masjidul Fadeekh, since the Prophet drank Fadeekh there, and the author lists other events that took place in the Masjid.

n02866.summary: Abu Sa'eed Khudri is with the Prophet when they enter the Masjid and see a man sitting with his fingers interlaced, which the Prophet forbids as prompted by Shaytaan.

n02867.summary: Abu Bakr reports that the Prophet barred anyone who had eaten garlic or onions from coming near the Masaajid, and Umar repeats this in a Jumu'ah lecture, advising that the smell be cooked out first.

n02868.summary: The Prophet forbids spitting in front of or to the right of a person praying, and Umar rebukes two men from Taa'if for raising their voices in the Masjid after Saa'ib brings them to him.

n02869.summary: Jaabir reports, through Banna Juhani, that the Prophet saw people passing naked swords to each other in the Masjid and cursed them, saying a sword must be sheathed before it is handed over. Sulaymaan bin Moosa reports that Jaabir said arrows carried through the Masjid must be held firmly by their heads.

n02871.summary: Muhammad bin Abdullaah was in the Masjid with Abu Sa'eed Khudri when a man turned an arrow round, and Abu Sa'eed reminded him that the Prophet forbade turning weapons around in the Masjid.

n02872.summary: Buraydah reports that the Prophet rebuked a man who announced a lost red camel in the Masjid, saying the Masaajid were built for their own purposes. Ibn Mas'ood silenced a similar announcer, and Ibn Seereen reports that Ubay bin Ka'b angrily rebuked a man for asking after a lost item in the Masjid.

n02874.summary: Saa'ib bin Yazeed was sleeping in the Masjid when Umar threw a pebble at him. Umar had two men from Taa'if brought to him and rebuked them for raising their voices in the Prophet's Masjid, saying he would have punished them had they been from Madinah.

n02875.summary: Sa'eed bin Ibraheem reports from his father that Umar told someone talking loudly in the Masjid to remember where they were, since Umar disliked loud speech there.

n02876.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar, Saalim and others report that Umar forbade noise, raised voices and futile talk in the Masjid, and had a platform built beside it for anyone who wanted to make noise.

n02877.summary: Taariq bin Shihaab reports that Umar had a man who was brought before him for a crime taken out of the Masjid before he was beaten.

n02878.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood sees people leaning against the Masjid wall facing the Qibla between the Adhaan and Iqaamah of Fajr and tells them not to block the angels' salaah.

n02879.summary: Abdullaah bin Aamir Alhaani reports that Haabis bin Sa'd Taa'ee, a Sahabi, told people praying at the front of the Masjid before dawn that they should be driven off because they were showing off.

n02880.summary: Murrah Hamdaani planned to pray behind every pillar in the Masjid of Kufa, and Abdullaah bin Mas'ood said that someone who knew Allaah was at the nearest pillar would not pass it without completing his salaah there.

n02881.summary: Abu Umayr bin Anas reports from his Ansaar uncles that the Prophet, troubled about calling people to salaah, rejected a flag, the trumpet and the bell, and that Abdullaah bin Zaid was then shown the Adhaan in a dream.

n02882.summary: Abu Sheikh reports Abdullaah bin Zaid's account of the Prophet's worry about calling people to salaah, the rejected bell and trumpet, and the Adhaan he saw in a dream, and Anas adds that someone once called out in the streets.

n02883.summary: Naafi bin Jubayr, Urwa bin Zaid bin Aslam and Sa'eed bin Musayyab report that before the Adhaan, the call 'As salaatu jaami'ah' was used to gather people for salaah and for important announcements.

n02884.summary: Sa'd Qaradh reports that when the Prophet came to Quba without Bilaal, Sa'd climbed a date palm and called the Adhaan to bring Muslims quickly, and the Prophet approved, telling him to call it whenever Bilaal was not with him.

n02885.summary: Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas, Abdullaah bin Mas'ood and Umar each praise the reward of the Mu'adhin, Umar quotes the Prophet praying for them, and Aa'isha links a Qur'aanic verse to the Mu'adhin.

n02886.summary: Umar says that if he were a Mu'adhin he would not mind missing Hajj or Umrah apart from the Fardh Hajj, because the angels would call the Adhaan themselves if they came down to earth.

n02887.summary: Qais bin Abi Haazim reports that when he went to Umar and was told their slaves called the Adhaan, Umar called this a grave deficiency and said he would rather be a Mu'adhin than Khalifah.

n02888.summary: Ali says he regrets not asking the Prophet to appoint Hasan and Husayn as Mu'adhins, and Abdullaah bin Mas'ood says he does not approve of appointing blind men or Qur'aan scholars to call the Adhaan.

n02890.summary: Yahya Bakkaa reports that Abdullaah bin Umar told a man who loved him for Allaah's sake that he disliked him for Allaah's sake, because the man sang the Adhaan and took payment for it.

n02891.summary: The Prophet sends Khaalid bin Sa'eed to Yemen with orders to take prisoner the people of any town where the Adhaan is not called, Amr bin Ma'dikarib gets Khaalid to release the Banu Zubayd, and Talha reports Abu Bakr's order to his commanders against the apostates.

n02892.summary: Zuhri reports that Abu Bakr, sending armies against the apostates, told them to hold off if they heard the Adhaan, because the Adhaan is a sign of Imaan.

n02893.summary: Ali reports that when the time for salaah came and the Prophet saw few people, he stayed seated and did not lead the salaah until a substantial gathering had come.

n02894.summary: Abdullaah bin Abi Awfa reports that the Prophet would wait until he heard the sound of people's shoes before he began the salaah.

n02895.summary: Umar reports that the Prophet, busy sending an army until about half the night had passed, came out to those still waiting for salaah and told them they were in salaah for as long as they were waiting.

n02896.summary: Abdullaah bin Amr reports that the Prophet told those who stayed seated after Maghrib that their Rabb boasts of them to the angels, and Abu Umaamah Thaqafi reports Mu'aawiya telling people to stay seated after Zuhr, citing the same saying of the Prophet.

n02897.summary: Anas and Abu Hurayrah report that the Prophet told people waiting for Isha that they are in salaah while they wait, and that the angels keep praying for them until they leave their place or break wudhu.

n02900.summary: Jaabir bin Abdullaah reports that the Prophet said making wudhu in difficult conditions, walking often to the Masjid and waiting from one salaah to the next wipe out sins and count as guarding the borders.

n02901.summary: Dawood bin Saalih reports Abu Salamah's explanation, citing Abu Hurayrah, that waiting for salaah one after another was how the Companions guarded the borders in the Prophet's time, when there was no war.

n02902.summary: Anas says that the verse about the sides parting from the beds refers to waiting for the Isha salaah.

n02903.summary: Ibn Ummu Maktoom asks the Prophet to let him pray at home because he is blind and far from the Masjid, and the Prophet tells him to come if he can hear the Adhaan or Iqaamah, and says he had considered burning the houses of those who do not come to salaah.
