n02904.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood says that a Muslim who wants to meet Allaah as a Muslim should pray the Fardh salaahs in congregation where the Adhaan is called, because missing them forsakes the Sunnah of the Prophet, and that in his time only hypocrites or the very sick missed congregational salaah.

n02906.summary: Mu'aadh bin Jabal says that the five Fardh salaahs should be prayed where the Adhaan is called, following the Prophet's practice, and that one should not claim a place at home for salaah, and the text breaks off into a footnote.

n02907.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar says that when a person was not seen at the Fajr and Isha salaahs, they became suspicious of him, because it is the hypocrites who skip those prayers.

n02908.summary: Umar did not see Sulaymaan bin Abu Hathma at the Fajr salaah, and his mother Shifaa explained that he had spent the night in prayer and sleep overtook him. Umar said he preferred attending Fajr in congregation to standing in prayer all night. In another report, Shifaa bint Abdullaah tells Umar that her husband and son slept after praying Fajr at home, and Umar again said he preferred Fajr in congregation to a night of Nafl.

n02909.summary: Ummu Dardaa reports that her husband Abu Dardaa came home angry because people were starting to pray apart from congregation, and Naafi reports that Abdullaah bin Umar, when he missed the Isha salaah in congregation, stayed in worship through the night.

n02911.summary: Ambasah bin Azhar reports that a newly married man usually stayed indoors for a few days and did not go out for Fajr, but when Haarith bin Hassaan went out for Fajr on his wedding night and was taunted, he said that a wife who kept him from congregational Fajr would be a terrible woman.

n02912.summary: Baraa bin Aazib narrates that the Prophet went along the rows straightening chests and shoulders, and warned that disorder in the rows brings disunity to the hearts, while Allaah shows special mercy to the first row.

n02913.summary: Baraa bin Aazib reports that the Prophet walked between the rows, touching chests and shoulders to straighten them, and said not to stand in disarray.

n02914.summary: Jaabir bin Samurah narrates that the Prophet asked the Sahabah why they did not form rows as the angels do, the angels completing the front rows first and standing close together.

n02915.summary: Jaabir bin Samurah narrates that the Prophet motioned them to sit during salaah and asked what prevented them from forming rows as the angels do.

n02916.summary: Nu'maan bin Basheer says that the Prophet straightened the rows as meticulously as an arrow, and on seeing one man's chest standing out he warned that Allaah would cast disunity between them unless they straightened their rows.

n02917.summary: Nu'maan bin Basheer adds that he then saw each man touch his shoulder, knee and ankle against the man beside him when the rows were straightened.

n02918.summary: Umar had the people straighten their rows and would not call the takbeer until he was told the rows were straight.

n02919.summary: Uthmaan had the people straighten their rows, calling them by name, and Abu Uthmaan also saw that Umar, before leading, looked at the shoulders and feet of those behind him.

n02920.summary: Abu Nadhar reports that Umar took people's names to move them forward or back to straighten the rows, saying Allaah wants them to follow the way of the angels' rows.

n02921.summary: Maalik recounts how Uthmaan, while Maalik was asking him for an allowance, straightened pebbles with his shoe and only then had the rows made straight before calling the takbeer, and that Ali told worshippers straight rows bring straight hearts.

n02922.summary: Ibn Mas'ood says the rows were always completed before salaah began and that those who advance to the first row earn Allaah's mercy, and a report of Aamir bin Mas'ood racing for the first row recalls the Prophet's saying about its value.

n02923.summary: Ibn Abbaas tells the people to always stand in the first row, on its right side, and not to form rows between pillars.

n02924.summary: Qais bin Ubaadah was pushed out of the first row in Madinah, by Umar in one account and by Ubay bin Ka'b in another, and each explained the Prophet's ruling that only the Muhaajireen and Ansaar should occupy it.

n02925.summary: Several reports describe the Prophet hearing people's needs even after the iqaamah had been called, and Anas says he was the most compassionate of people, staying with a Bedouin who held his clothes until the request was met.

n02927.summary: Abu Uthmaan Nahdi says people kept Umar talking about their needs even as salaah was about to begin, and Moosa bin Talha heard Uthmaan asking people about their conditions and market prices while the iqaamah was called.

n02928.summary: After accepting Islaam, Abu Sufyaan watched the Sahabah follow the Prophet in salaah with great discipline, and when he called it a kingdom, Abbaas replied that it was Nubuwwah.

n02929.summary: Maymoona relates that the Muslims competed for the water the Prophet had used for wudhu, and Abu Sufyaan called it a kingdom, which Abbaas corrected to Nubuwwah.

n02930.summary: Urwa relates that Abu Sufyaan saw the Sahabah hurrying to purify themselves and bowing and prostrating exactly as the Prophet did, and Abbaas said they would obey him even if told to give up food and drink.

n02931.summary: Umar began leading the salaah during the Prophet's final illness while Abu Bakr was absent, and when the Prophet learned this he had Abu Bakr lead, saying that neither Allaah nor the Muslims could accept otherwise.

n02932.summary: When the Prophet heard Umar's voice in salaah he angrily declared that only Abu Bakr should lead, and Abu Ubaydah, Ali and Zubayr later cited this to support Abu Bakr's leadership.

n02933.summary: After the Prophet's death the Ansaar proposed one Ameer from them and one from the Muhaajireen, but Umar reminded them that the Prophet had placed Abu Bakr forward in salaah, and they said they would never put themselves ahead of him.

n02934.summary: Ali says that because the Prophet chose Abu Bakr to lead the salaah while Ali was present and well, he is content to accept Abu Bakr as Khalifah for worldly affairs too.

n02935.summary: Salmaan Faarsi refused to lead Arab companions in salaah, saying non-Arabs could not lead Arabs, and when a man led four rakaahs on a journey, Salmaan said two would have been enough.

n02936.summary: Abu Sa'eed, a slave of the Banu Usayd, hosted a meal for Abu Dharr, Hudhayfah and Ibn Mas'ood, and when salaah began they confirmed the host's right to lead, so Abu Sa'eed, though a slave, led them.

n02937.summary: Naafi reports that Abdullaah bin Umar declined to lead in a Madinah masjid whose imam was a slave, and Abdullaah bin Handhala reports that Qais bin Sa'd had one of his slaves lead the salaah in his house, following the Prophet's ruling that the householder has the right to lead.

n02938.summary: Ibn Mas'ood and Abu Moosa each urged the other to lead the salaah at Abu Moosa's house, and Abu Moosa, who led, had taken off his shoes, which Ibn Mas'ood asked about.

n02939.summary: Ibn Mas'ood reminds Abu Moosa that the Sunnah is for the owner of the house to lead, but Abu Moosa refused until one of their slaves went forward.

n02940.summary: Furaat bin Hayyaan asked Handhala bin Rabee to lead the salaah in his masjid, and when Handhala refused, Furaat said the Prophet had praised Handhala after sending him as a spy to Taa'if, so Handhala led.

n02941.summary: Abdur Rahmaan bin Abi Layla reports that Umar objected when Naafi bin Alqama, governor of Makkah, appointed a man from among the slaves, Abdur Rahmaan bin Abzah, to lead the salaah, and was satisfied when Naafi explained he was the best reciter of the Qur'aan.

n02942.summary: At a Hajj gathering in Makkah, Miswar bin Makhrama pulled back a non-Arabic-speaking man of the Makhzoom family who was leading the salaah, because his unclear recitation could be copied by pilgrims, and Umar, after questioning him in Madinah, approved.

n02943.summary: Talha bin Ubaydullaah asked the congregation after leading the salaah whether they were pleased with it, recalling the Prophet's warning that the salaah of a leader whom the people dislike does not even pass his ears, let alone reach the heavens.

n02944.summary: Anas refused to pray behind Umar bin Abdul Azeez, and Abu Ayyoob Ansaari refused to pray behind Marwaan bin Hakam, each saying he would only follow an imam whose salaah matched the Prophet's.

n02945.summary: Abu Jaabir Waalidi asked Abu Hurayrah whether his salaah matched the Prophet's, and Abu Hurayrah said it did but was shorter, with the standing as brief as the time a muezzin takes to come down from the minaret.

n02946.summary: Anas says the Prophet's salaah was so brief that people would criticise anyone who copied it, and Adi bin Haatim, after an imam prolonged his sitting, led a brief salaah in the Prophet's manner; Anas refused to follow imams who prolonged it until Umar bin Abdul Azeez stopped the practice.

n02948.summary: Aa'isha says that after bathing, the Prophet would leave for salaah when Bilaal called the adhaan, and she would hear him weeping in salaah.

n02949.summary: Aa'isha describes a night when the Prophet wept in salaah until the ground around him was soaked, and when Bilaal asked why, he said he should be a grateful slave after a verse was revealed to him; Mutarraf's father heard the weeping like a grindstone in his chest.

n02950.summary: Abdullaah bin Shaddaad says he heard Umar weeping aloud in the Fajr salaah while reciting Surah Yusuf, when he reached the verse about complaining of sorrow to Allaah.

n02951.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar says that when he prayed behind Umar he could hear Umar's weeping from three rows back.

n02952.summary: Sahl bin Sa'd says that Abu Bakr could not be distracted while performing salaah.

n02953.summary: Mujaahid says that Abdullaah bin Zubayr stood as still as a stick in salaah, as Abu Bakr used to do, and that this is what devotion in salaah means.

n02954.summary: Mujaahid says that Abdullaah bin Zubayr stood as still as a stick in salaah, as Abu Bakr used to do, and that this is what devotion in salaah means.

n02955.summary: Several reports describe Abdullaah bin Zubayr standing motionless in salaah, and Abdullaah bin Umar walking to salaah so slowly, and facing the Qibla so carefully, that even his thumbs were turned towards it.

n02956.summary: Taa'oos says he had never seen anyone as careful to face the Qibla in salaah as Abdullaah bin Umar, whose face, palms and feet all faced it.

n02957.summary: Abu Burdah prayed beside Abdullaah bin Umar and heard him ask Allaah in sajdah to make Himself the most beloved and most feared to him, and heard him say he hoped each salaah would atone for his sins.

n02958.summary: A'mash says that when Abdullaah bin Mas'ood prayed he was so still that he looked like a discarded piece of cloth.

n02959.summary: Ummu Roomaan says Abu Bakr sternly reprimanded her for leaning in salaah, quoting the Prophet that one should stand at ease and not lean as the Jews do, since being at ease completes the salaah.

n02960.summary: Aa'isha lists the optional salaahs the Prophet performed: four rakaahs before Zuhr at home, two after Zuhr, Maghrib and Isha, nine at night including Witr, and two before Fajr.

n02961.summary: Aa'isha says the Prophet gave no optional salaah more importance than the two Rakaahs of Fajr.

n02962.summary: Aa'isha says the Prophet never omitted the Fajr and Zuhr sunnahs, and Bilaal reports that the Prophet came out late for Fajr because he was finishing the two Fajr Rakaahs and would not leave them even when the sky was bright.

n02964.summary: Qaaboos reports Aa'isha's answer that the optional salaah the Prophet kept most consistently was the four Rakaahs before Zuhr, and Abdullaah bin Saa'ib and Ali each report the Prophet's sunnah salaahs around Zuhr.

n02966.summary: Aa'isha says that if the Prophet could not pray the four Rakaahs before Zuhr he would make them up afterwards, and Abu Ayyoob reports the Prophet's regular practice of the four before Zuhr and his reason for it.

n02967.summary: Ali says the Prophet prayed four Rakaahs before Asr, giving salaam between each pair to the angels and the believers.

n02968.summary: Ali reports, in another narration, that the Prophet prayed two Rakaahs before Asr.

n02969.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas reports that the Prophet prayed two Rakaahs after Maghrib, reciting for so long that the people in the masjid had dispersed by the time he finished.

n02970.summary: Sa'eed bin Musayyib reports Umar saying that the two Rakaahs before Fajr are dearer to him than red camels.

n02971.summary: Abdur Rahmaan bin Abdullaah reports finding Umar praying before Zuhr, and Umar says the prayer counts as part of the night prayer.

n02972.summary: Abdullaah bin Utba says he prayed four Rakaahs with Umar in Umar's house before Zuhr.

n02973.summary: Hudhayfa bin Usayd reports seeing Ali pray four long Rakaahs after the sun passes its zenith, and Ali says he saw the Prophet pray the same salaah.

n02974.summary: Abdullaah bin Yazeed reports, from someone close to Ibn Mas'ood, that Ibn Mas'ood prayed four Rakaahs after noon reciting two long surahs, and then left for the masjid fully dressed when the adhaan was called.

n02975.summary: Aswad, Murra and Masrooq report Ibn Mas'ood saying that the four Rakaahs before Zuhr are the only daytime salaah equal to night prayer, because they have always been counted as equal to Tahajjud.

n02977.summary: Baraa and Abdullaah bin Umar are both reported to have prayed the Sunnah Rakaahs, and Naafi reports that Ibn Umar prayed eight Rakaahs before Zuhr and four after, while another account gives twelve before Zuhr.

n02979.summary: Ali says the Prophet urged him never to give up the four Rakaahs before Asr, Abu Faakhtah reports Ali calling the time between Maghrib and Isha 'salaah of negligence', and Ibn Umar begins to say that whoever prays four Rakaahs after Maghrib is like someone fighting battle after battle.

n02981.summary: Abdullaah bin Abul Qais reports Aa'isha telling him never to leave the Qiyaamul Layl, because the Prophet never left it, even when he was ill or very tired and then prayed it sitting.

n02982.summary: Jaabir says Qiyaamul Layl first became compulsory for the Companions with the revelation of Surah Muzammil, so long that their feet swelled, until Allaah granted a concession.

n02983.summary: Sa'eed bin Hishaam, after taking his wife back, asks Ibn Abbaas and then Aa'isha about the Prophet's night prayer and Witr, and Aa'isha describes the Prophet's Witr of eleven and then nine Rakaahs and his habit of making up missed Qiyaam.

n02984.summary: Ibn Abbaas reports that when the start of Surah Muzammil was revealed the Companions stood in prayer as long as they did in Ramadhaan, and a year passed between the first and last parts of the surah.

n02985.summary: Yahya bin Sa'eed reports that Abu Bakr prayed Witr at the start of the night and, when he rose for Tahajjud, prayed in units of two Rakaahs.

n02986.summary: Aslam reports that Umar prayed for a long time at night and, when half the night had passed, woke his family for prayer while reciting the verse that tells him to order his family to pray.

n02987.summary: Hasan reports that Uthmaan bin Abul Aas, who had married one of Umar's widows, asked her about Umar's night worship, and she described how Umar dipped his hand in water, made dhikr and dozed until it was time for Tahajjud.

n02988.summary: Sa'eed bin Musayyib reports that Umar loved to pray in the middle of the night.

n02989.summary: Naafi reports that Ibn Umar prayed for a long time at night, repeatedly asking Naafi whether the last part of the night had come, and then sat making istighfaar and du'aa until dawn.

n02990.summary: Muhammad reports that Ibn Umar began prayer whenever he woke in the night, and Abu Ghaalib reports Ibn Umar urging him to pray before dawn, saying that Surah Ikhlaas is equal to a third of the Qur'aan.

n02991.summary: Alqama bin Qais describes how Ibn Mas'ood prayed through the night, reciting steadily and finishing with Witr near dawn, and Taariq bin Shihaab reports Salmaan's advice to keep the five Fardh salaahs and to avoid haste in worship.

n02992.summary: Ummu Haani reports that when Makkah was conquered the Prophet bathed and then prayed eight Rakaahs of Duhaa, and Aa'isha says he usually prayed four but sometimes more.

n02993.summary: Anas reports seeing the Prophet pray six Rakaahs of Duhaa; the end of his sentence is garbled in the OCR.

n02994.summary: Ummu Haani states that the Prophet prayed six Rakaahs of Duhaa at her house when Makkah was conquered, and Abdullaah bin Abu Awfa says he prayed only two because the Prophet prayed two when he got news of a victory and when the head of Abu Jahal was brought to him.

n02995.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas says he came to understand the Qur'anic word 'Ishraaq' from Ummu Haani, who reported that the Prophet made wudhu and then prayed Duhaa, calling it the Ishraaq salaah.

n02996.summary: Abu Hurayrah reports the Prophet saying that a person who makes wudhu well, goes to the masjid for Fajr and then prays Duhaa returns sooner and with more reward than a returning army with booty.

n02997.summary: Ataa Abu Muhammad reports seeing Ali pray Duhaa in the masjid, Ikramah reports that Ibn Abbaas prayed Duhaa once every ten days, and Aa'isha bint Sa'd reports that her father Sa'd prayed eight Rakaahs of Duhaa.

n02999.summary: Sha'bi reports that Ibn Mas'ood did not pray Duhaa but prayed nawaafil between Zuhr and Asr alongside his long night worship.

n03000.summary: Naafi reports that Ibn Umar prayed nawaafil between Zuhr and Asr.

n03001.summary: Hudhayfah says he prayed Maghrib with the Prophet, and after that the Prophet kept on praying until Isha.

n03002.summary: Muhammad bin Ammaar reports seeing his father Ammaar pray six Rakaahs after Maghrib, and Ammaar says the Prophet promised that whoever prays them will have all sins forgiven, even as many as the foam on the oceans.

n03003.summary: Abdur Rahmaan bin Yazeed says he always found Ibn Mas'ood praying between Maghrib and Isha, and Ibn Mas'ood explains that it is a time of people's negligence of Allaah.

n03004.summary: Aswad bin Yazeed reports that Ibn Mas'ood called the time between Maghrib and Isha an excellent time, the time of negligence.

n03005.summary: Ibn Abbaas says that angels surround those who pray between Maghrib and Isha, which he calls Salaatul Awaabeen.

n03006.summary: Abdur Rahmaan bin Abu Layla reports that the widow of Abdullaah bin Rawaaha said he prayed two Rakaahs whenever he left the house and whenever he came back into it.

n03007.summary: Abu Hurayrah reports that the Prophet encouraged standing in Taraweeh during Ramadhaan without making it compulsory, promising forgiveness of past sins to whoever prays it in faith and hope of reward.

n03008.summary: Abu Hurayrah adds that the practice of Taraweeh stayed the same through the Khilaafah of Abu Bakr and the early part of Umar's Khilaafah.

n03009.summary: Abu Hurayrah reports that the Prophet saw Sahabah praying Taraweeh in congregation behind Ubay bin Ka'b in a corner of the Masjid, and approved of it.

n03010.summary: Abdur Rahmaan Al Qaari recounts how Umar gathered the people behind Ubay bin Ka'b for Taraweeh, calling it an excellent innovation while saying the latter part of the night is better for sleep.

n03011.summary: Naufal bin Iyaas Hudhali reports that Umar disliked people choosing Taraweeh leaders for their voices, and within three days had Ubay bin Ka'b lead the people.

n03012.summary: Abu Is'haaq Hamdaani reports that Ali, on entering the Masjid on the first night of Ramadhaan and finding lanterns lit and the Qur'aan recited, prayed for Umar's grave to be illuminated.

n03013.summary: Urwa reports that when Umar had all the people pray Taraweeh together, he placed the men behind Ubay bin Ka'b and the women behind Sulaymaan bin Abu Hathma.

n03014.summary: Umar bin Abdulaah Ansi reports that Ubay and Tameem Daari led the men and Sulaymaan led the women under Umar, and that under Uthmaan one Imaam led both, with the women leaving only after the men.

n03015.summary: Arjafa says that Ali had Taraweeh performed with one Imaam for the men and another for the women, and that she was the Imaam of the women.

n03016.summary: Jaabir reports that Ubay bin Ka'b led the women of his household in eight Rakaahs of Taraweeh and Witr, and the Prophet approved, so the practice is established as a Sunnah.

n03017.summary: Buraydah reports that the Prophet asked Bilaal how he had reached Jannah before him, and Bilaal explained that he prays two Rakaahs after each sin and two Rakaahs of Tahiyyatul wudhu after each broken wudhu.

n03018.summary: Thumaamah bin Abdullaah reports that in a drought Anas repeatedly prayed and made du'aa, sending the caretaker to look for clouds, until rain fell only on his own land.

n03019.summary: Ali relates that when he was in intense pain, the Prophet covered him with his shawl, prayed and made du'aa for him, and he was immediately cured.

n03020.summary: Anas narrates how Abu Mu'liq, threatened with death by a robber, prayed and made du'aa three times, and a rider with a spear, an angel from the fourth heaven, killed the robber.

n03021.summary: Safwaan bin Assaal reports that the Prophet welcomed him as a seeker of knowledge, and the Prophet told Qabeesah bin Mukhaariq that certain du'aas recited after Fajr would protect him from blindness, leprosy and paralysis.

n03022.summary: Sakhbarah reports that the Prophet told two men who were passing by that seeking knowledge atones for all of a person's past sins.

n03023.summary: Abu Umaamah reports the Prophet's words that the superiority of an Aalim over an ordinary worshipper is like his own superiority over the lowest of people, and that Allaah and all creation pray for the one who teaches good.

n03024.summary: Another narration gives the Prophet's words on the Aalim's superiority with a verse on those closest to the Prophets, and then Kumayl bin Ziyaad reports Ali's speech on knowledge being better than wealth and on the scarcity of true bearers of knowledge.

n03026.summary: Anas reports that in the Prophet's time one of two brothers worked while the other stayed with the Prophet to learn. When the working brother complained about him, the Prophet said that he may be receiving his sustenance because of his brother.

n03027.summary: Abu Tufayl reports Ali's saying that those closest to the prophets are those who act on what they brought, and he applies the verse about Ibraheem's followers to the Prophet's followers. Kumayl bin Ziyaad relates Ali's long discourse that knowledge is better than wealth, that scholars remain while the wealthy die, and that Ali longs to meet those few who can bear true knowledge.

n03028.summary: Mu'aadh bin Jabal lists the rewards of acquiring, studying, rehearsing, discussing and teaching knowledge, and how knowledge guides people in the halaal and haraam.

n03029.summary: Haaroon bin Rabaab and Zaid report Ibn Mas'ood urging people to begin each morning as an Aalim or a student of Deen, to acquire knowledge before it is lost with the departure of its bearers, and to follow the traditions of the Sahabah.

n03031.summary: Abul Ahwas narrates that Ibn Mas'ood said no person is born a scholar, and knowledge is gained only through study.

n03032.summary: Ibn Mas'ood says to begin each morning as an Aalim or student of Deen, and if that is not possible, at least to love the Ulema and never despise them.

n03033.summary: Hasan narrates Abu Dardaa's warning to be a scholar, a student, a lover of them or a follower of them, and never the fifth kind, which Hasan explains to Humayd is the one who innovates Bid'ah.

n03034.summary: Dahhaak reports Abu Dardaa's address to the people of Damascus, criticising neglect of learning and worldly building and hopes, and stating that teaching and learning bring equal reward.

n03035.summary: Hassaan reports Abu Dardaa rebuking the people of Damascus for neglecting remembrance of Allaah and for not seeking knowledge, and warning that earlier nations were destroyed by following their desires.

n03036.summary: Qurra reports Abu Dardaa saying to acquire knowledge before it is taken away, and Abdur Rahmaan bin Mas'ood Faraazi reports that going to the Masjid to learn or teach earns the reward of a Mujaahid.

n03037.summary: Ibn Abu Hudhayl reports Abu Dardaa saying that a person lacks intelligence if he thinks spending mornings and evenings in learning and teaching is not Jihaad.

n03038.summary: Rajaa bin Hayaat reports Abu Dardaa saying that knowledge is derived from study.

n03039.summary: Abu Dharr and Abu Hurayrah both say that learning one chapter of knowledge is more beloved to them than a thousand Nafl Rakaahs, and they narrate that the Prophet said whoever dies while studying the knowledge of Deen dies as a martyr.

n03040.summary: Another narration has Abu Dharr and Abu Hurayrah saying that learning a chapter of knowledge is better than a thousand Nafl Rakaahs whether or not it is practised upon.

n03041.summary: Ali Azdi reports that Ibn Abbaas said teaching the Qur'aan, Fiqh and the Sunnah in a Masjid is better than Jihaad.

n03042.summary: Ibn Abbaas says that everything, even the fish in the oceans, seeks forgiveness for the one who teaches people what is good.

n03043.summary: Zirr bin Hubaysh reports that Safwaan bin Assaal advised him to begin his mornings as an Aalim or student of Deen, and Safwaan also said the angels spread their wings for whoever leaves home seeking knowledge.

n03044.summary: On his deathbed, Mu'aadh bin Jabal asks whether dawn has broken, seeks refuge from a morning that leads to Jahannam, welcomes death, and says he loved this world only for fasting thirst, hardship and sitting with the Ulema.

n03045.summary: Abu Dardaa says that three things would make him wish to leave this world: prostrating to his Creator through the day and night, enduring thirst while fasting, and sitting with people who choose their speech as carefully as fruit.

n03046.summary: Ibn Abbaas recounts that after the Prophet's death he went to learn hadith from the Sahabah, waiting at their doors and asking them to let him come to them, despite the doubts of his Ansaari friend.

n03047.summary: Ibn Abbaas says that when the cities were being conquered and people turned to worldly affairs, he focused on learning from Umar, which is why most of his hadith come from Umar.

n03048.summary: Abu Hurayrah recounts that when he asked the Prophet to teach him, the Prophet narrated to him and he never forgot anything afterwards; he then explains why he narrates more hadith than others, citing the Qur'aanic warning against concealing knowledge.

n03049.summary: Abu Hurayrah describes the hunger he endured while staying with the Prophet, and how Ja'far bin Abi Taalib would take him and others home and feed them everything he had.

n03050.summary: Abu Moosa reports the Prophet's parable of the guidance and knowledge he was sent with as rain falling on different kinds of ground, showing the different ways people benefit from it.

n03051.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood relays the Prophet's warning that after earlier Nabis came people who did not practise, and that whoever resists them by hand, tongue or heart is a Mu'min.

n03052.summary: Abdullaah bin Amr relays the Prophet's saying that knowledge is of three kinds, the clear verses of the Qur'aan, authentic Ahadeeth and matching injunctions, and everything beyond these is extra.

n03053.summary: Amr bin Auf relays the Prophet's saying that he has left two things, the Book of Allaah and the Sunnah, and that holding fast to them keeps people from going astray.

n03054.summary: Abu Hurayrah reports that the Prophet called the learning of an Allaamah, a man who knows Arabic, poetry and the differences between Arab tribes, knowledge that does not benefit.

n03055.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar says that knowledge rests on three things: the Qur'aan, the constant Sunnah, and saying 'I do not know' when one does not know.

n03056.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas insists that knowledge comes only from the Book and the Sunnah, and corrects his students, who had ruled from their own opinion on a man troubled by a fluid after urinating, saying that wudhu is enough for him.

n03057.summary: Amr bin Yahya bin Ja'dah reports that the Prophet rebuked a man who brought him a scripture written on an animal's shoulder blade, and that the verse saying the Qur'aan is sufficient was then revealed.

n03058.summary: Khaalid bin Urfuta says Umar beat a man from the Abd Qais who had copied the scripture of Daaniyaal and ordered it erased, and Umar recalls the Prophet's anger when he once brought him a scripture from the People of the Book; Jaabir reports a similar rebuke.

n03059.summary: Abdullaah bin Thaabit reports that Umar brought the Prophet some quotations from the Torah, the Prophet's face reddened with anger, and the Prophet said that even Moosa could not be followed instead of him.

n03060.summary: Maymoon bin Mahraan reports that Umar whipped a man who had brought a scripture found in Madaa'in that did not match the Qur'aan, and said earlier nations were destroyed by turning to the books of their scholars.

n03061.summary: Hurayth bin Zuhayr reports that Abdullaah bin Mas'ood told people never to question the People of the Book, since they are misguided and may give them truth to reject or falsehood to believe.

n03062.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood and Abdullaah bin Abbaas each say that people should not ask the People of the Book, since they have Allaah's latest Book, which has not been altered.

n03064.summary: A variant report has Abdullaah bin Abbaas asking why people question the People of the Book when they have Allaah's latest Book, which is new and which they can read.

n03065.summary: Shufay Asbahi reports Abu Hurayrah's hadith that the reciter of the Qur'aan, the martyr and the wealthy man will be the first fuel for Jahannam because they acted for show; Mu'aawiya wept on hearing it. The report also has Abdullaah bin Umar weeping after hearing from Abdullaah bin Amr a hadith about pride.

n03067.summary: Abul Hasan reports that Abdullaah bin Rawaaha and Hassaan bin Thaabit came weeping to the Prophet when Surah Shu'araa was revealed, and he told them that the exception for poets who believe applies to them. A separate report by Abu Saalih has the people of Yemen weeping at the Qur'aan in Abu Bakr's time.

n03068.summary: Abzah Abu Abdur Rahmaan reports the Prophet's sermon rebuking tribes who neither teach Deen to their neighbours nor learn it, and the Ash'ar people who asked for a year's grace to teach theirs.

n03069.summary: Abdullaah bin Salamah reports that Mu'aadh bin Jabal told a weeping man at his bedside that whoever strives for knowledge and Imaan will be granted them, as Ibraheem was.

n03070.summary: Haarith bin Umayrah reports Mu'aadh bin Jabal's advice as he was dying: knowledge and Imaan remain until Qiyaamah, so seek them from Umar, Uthmaan, Ali and four men, and judge every claim by the Qur'aan and Sunnah.

n03071.summary: Yazeed bin Umayrah reports Mu'aadh bin Jabal's advice as he was dying: take knowledge from four named men, beware the blunders of a wise man and the words of a hypocrite, and take sound knowledge from wherever it comes.

n03072.summary: Amr bin Maymoon reports that Mu'aadh bin Jabal, who had come to Yemen as the Prophet's envoy, consoled him when he wept at Mu'aadh's death by saying that knowledge and Imaan will remain until Qiyaamah.

n03073.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar says that in the Prophet's time people learnt Imaan before the Qur'aan and then knew its commands; now people read the Qur'aan without knowing what it commands. Jundub bin Abdullaah says that learning Imaan first with the Prophet made their Imaan grow when they learnt the Qur'aan.

n03074.summary: Ali says each revelation in the Prophet's time strengthened the Mu'mineen's Imaan and that they abstained at once from any prohibition. Abu Abdur Rahmaan Sulami says the Sahabah did not go on to the next ten verses until they had learnt to practise the ones before.

n03075.summary: An unnamed Sahabi says the companions learnt the Qur'aan together with how to act on it. Abdullaah bin Mas'ood says they learnt ten verses from the Prophet before going on to the next ten, and Shareek confirms that this meant acting on them first.

n03077.summary: Hafs bin Umar Sa'di reports that Salmaan told Hudhayfah to learn only the Deen he needs, since knowledge is abundant and life short. Abul Bakhtari relates Salmaan's lesson with the sip of water from the Tigris: knowledge never decreases.

n03078.summary: Abu Qayla reports that when he asked Abdullaah bin Umar about knowledge, Ibn Umar replied in a letter that the most important thing is to meet Allaah with a tongue that did not dishonour a Muslim, with no Muslim's blood or wealth on one's hands, and united with the Muslims.

n03079.summary: Abu Rifaa'ah reports that he interrupted the Prophet during a sermon to say a stranger had come to learn his Deen, and the Prophet came down from the pulpit and sat to teach him.

n03080.summary: Jareer reports that a Bedouin asked the Prophet to teach him Islaam, and the Prophet listed the Shahaadah, salaah, zakaah, Ramadhaan, Hajj and loving for others what one loves for oneself. Muhammad bin Umaarah then says Farwah bin Musayk gave up Kindah's royalty to join the Prophet and learnt the Qur'aan and Shari'ah from Sa'd bin Ubaadah.

n03081.summary: Dubaa'ah bint Zubayr reports that a delegation of thirteen men from Bahraa came to Madinah, was hosted by Miqdaad bin Amr, accepted Islaam before the Prophet, learnt the Faraa'idh, and left with gifts after farewell.

n03082.summary: Ibn Seereen reports that Abu Bakr and Umar, when teaching Islaam, told people to worship Allaah alone, keep salaah on time, pay zakaah cheerfully, fast in Ramadhaan and obey their leaders.

n03083.summary: Hasan reports that a Bedouin asked Umar to teach him the Deen, and Umar listed the Shahaadah, salaah, zakaah, Hajj and fasting, and told him to judge only outward actions and not to probe people's private lives.

n03084.summary: Another narration adds that Umar told the same Bedouin to hold fast to this advice, and that when he meets Allaah he may tell Him whatever comes to mind.

n03085.summary: Hasan reports that a countryman asked Umar for a sure path to Jannah, and Umar advised him to worship Allaah alone, keep salaah, zakaah, Hajj, Umrah and obedience, and not to probe people's private lives; the man said he would tell his Rabb that Umar had instructed him.

n03086.summary: Abu Maalik Ashja'ee reports from his father that the Prophet taught salaah first to anyone who accepted Islaam.

n03087.summary: Hakam bin Umayr reports that the Prophet taught them that on standing for salaah they should say Allaahu Akbar, raise their hands without passing the ears, and recite the opening words of praise.

n03090.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas says the Prophet taught them the Tashahhud just as he taught them a Surah of the Qur'aan.

n03091.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood says the Prophet taught him the Tashahhud with his hand in the Prophet's hand, as he taught him a Surah. Aswad reports that Ibn Mas'ood taught them the Tashahhud the same way and corrected their small mistakes.

n03092.summary: Zaid bin Wahab reports that Hudhayfah saw a man pray for forty years without carrying out the salaah properly and told him he had not prayed at all, then taught him to perform ruku and sajdah correctly.

n03093.summary: Ali bin Abi Taalib reports that the Prophet offered him five phrases for his Deen and worldly life rather than five thousand goats, and taught him to ask for forgiveness, good character, lawful earnings, contentment and no craving for what is not decreed.

n03094.summary: Abdullaah bin Ja'far reports that Ali taught him words the Prophet used to recite in difficulty, and that Ali promised entry to Jannah for whoever recites them at death, with the Tasbeeh repeated three times each; the text breaks off in the middle of the list.

n03095.summary: Sa'd bin Junaadah relates how he came from Taa'if to accept Islaam in Makkah and how the Prophet then taught him the words called the Baaqiyaatus Saalihaat.

n03096.summary: Ubay bin Ka'b relates the morning and evening du'aa the Prophet taught the Companions, affirming the natural way of Islaam and the creed of Ibraheem.

n03097.summary: Sa'd and Naufal each report a du'aa the Prophet taught: one for protection from harm and one for a person who has passed away.

n03098.summary: Salaamah Kindi reports that Ali taught people a salutation to send to the Prophet, asking Allaah to bless Muhammad, the seal of the prophets, with the best of mercies, the highest house and the most complete light, and to accept his testimony.

n03099.summary: The Abdul Qais delegation arrives, and the Prophet welcomes their leader Mundhir bin Aa'idh (Ashaj), seats him beside himself and questions the delegation on what they have learnt.

n03100.summary: Abu Sa'eed Khudri relates how the Abdul Qais delegation came, was hosted and taught, and afterwards asked the Prophet about their local drinks.

n03101.summary: Jaabir relates the Prophet's journey for the Farewell Hajj, including the ihram instructions given to Asmaa bint Umays when her son was born at Dhul Hulayfah, and the talbiya recited on the road.

n03102.summary: Jaabir bin Azraq Ghaadiri recounts travelling from the far ends of Yemen to hear the Prophet at Mina, and the author then quotes Ibn Jareer's commentary on the verse about gaining understanding of Deen through jihaad.

n03103.summary: Abu Sa'eed Khudri says that the Sahabah left one or two men behind on campaigns to learn Hadith, who then reported the Prophet's words to the others on their return.

n03104.summary: Thaabit Bunaani reports Anas bin Maalik describing the Ansaar who learnt and taught the Qur'aan at night, and the martyrdom of Anas's uncle Haraam bin Milhaan and of the Qurra sent by the Prophet.

n03105.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas relates Umar's account of taking turns with an Ansaari neighbour to attend the Prophet's gatherings, and of his alarm when the neighbour brought word that the Prophet had divorced his wives, which proved untrue.

n03106.summary: Baraa says the Sahabah could not all sit to hear Hadith because of their property and work, so those who were present passed it on to those who were absent.

n03107.summary: Baraa adds that the Sahabah who were out grazing camels heard the Hadith from companions who had been with the Prophet.

n03108.summary: Abu Anas Maalik bin Abu Aamir Asbahi relates that Talha bin Ubaydullaah defended Abu Hurayrah against a man who doubted his many Hadith, explaining that Abu Hurayrah had always been with the Prophet while the others had homes and families.

n03109.summary: Umar bin Khattaab rules that no one may trade in the marketplace without first understanding the Deen that governs trade.

n03110.summary: Ali bin Abi Taalib explains the verse 'Save yourselves and your families from the Fire' as meaning to educate yourselves and your families in all that is good.

n03111.summary: Another narration gives Ali's explanation of the same verse as teaching one's family good manners.

n03112.summary: Maalik bin Huwayrith relates that after twenty days with the Prophet he and his companions were sent home to teach their families and to pray as they had seen the Prophet pray.

n03113.summary: Zaid bin Thaabit relates that the Prophet asked him to learn the Jewish language, or in other reports the Syriac or Hebrew, so that he could read and write the letters for him, and that he mastered it within about half a month or seventeen days depending on the report.

n03115.summary: Umar bin Qais describes how Abdullaah bin Zubayr spoke to each of his hundred slaves in their own language, and balanced worldly affairs with remembrance of the Aakhirah.

n03116.summary: Umar tells people to study astronomy only as far as it helps them navigate by land and sea in the dark, and then to stop.

n03117.summary: Another report has Umar telling people to study astronomy as far as it aids navigation and genealogy as far as it helps them keep family ties.

n03118.summary: Sa'sa'a bin Sowhaan relates that after a Bedouin challenged Ali's reading of a verse, Ali recited it correctly and had Abul Aswad Duwali add the vowel marks to the Qur'aan for the many non-Arabs entering Islaam.

n03119.summary: Urwa reports that when the Prophet left for Hunayn and later for Madinah, he appointed Mu'aadh bin Jabal over Makkah to teach the Qur'aan and develop understanding of Deen.

n03120.summary: Mujaahid reports that the Prophet appointed Mu'aadh bin Jabal over Makkah when he left for Hunayn, to teach the Qur'aan and develop understanding of Deen.

n03121.summary: Qaasim relates that Umar kept Zaid bin Thaabit in Madinah as his deputy and sent him out only for vital tasks, because the people of Madinah needed him, not because Umar thought less of him.

n03122.summary: Saalim bin Abdullaah relates that when Zaid bin Thaabit died, Abdullaah bin Umar called him a great scholar who gave rulings in Madinah while Umar sent others to the cities and forbade them to judge by their own opinion.

n03123.summary: Abu Abdur Rahmaan Sulami relates that Uthmaan told him to recite the Qur'aan to Zaid bin Thaabit, and Ka'b bin Maalik reports Umar's regret that Mu'aadh bin Jabal left for Shaam after Abu Bakr refused to keep him in Madinah.

n03124.summary: Aasim bin Umar bin Qataadah relates that after Uhud delegates from the Udhal and Qaara asked for teachers, and the Prophet sent six Sahabah under Marthad bin Abu Marthad.

n03125.summary: Ali relates that the Prophet sent him to Yemen to teach and judge between people, and that the Prophet's prayer for his heart to be guided and his tongue steadied kept his judgements sound.

n03126.summary: Anas relates that when people from Yemen asked for a teacher of the Qur'aan, the Prophet sent Abu Ubaydah bin Jarraah with them, calling him the most trustworthy person of this Ummah.

n03127.summary: Another narration says that the people of Yemen asked the Prophet for someone to teach them the Sunnah, but the text breaks off there.

n03128.summary: Abu Bakr bin Muhammad bin Amr bin Hazm quotes the letter the Prophet gave Amr bin Hazam on being sent to Yemen to teach, collect zakaah and urge taqwa, and Abu Moosa Ash'ari reports being sent there with Mu'aadh bin Jabal to teach the Qur'aan.

n03129.summary: Ammaar bin Yaasir relates that he was sent to teach a Qais clan and found them indifferent, and the Prophet said there are people even stranger, who know what these ignorant people do not and are just as indifferent.

n03130.summary: Haaritha bin Mudarrib reads Umar's letter to the people of Kufa, appointing Ammaar bin Yaasir as governor and Abdullaah bin Mas'ood as teacher and advisor, and praising them as among the choicest Companions.

n03131.summary: Abul Aswad Duwali relates that when he reached Basrah he found Imraan bin Husayn there, sent by Umar to teach Deen to the people.

n03132.summary: Muhammad bin Ka'b Qurazi relates that Yazeed bin Abu Sufyaan asked Umar for teachers for Shaam, and Umar sent Mu'aadh bin Jabal, Ubaadah bin Saamit and Abu Dardaa to Hims, Damascus and Palestine.

n03133.summary: Abdullaah bin Muhammad bin Aqeel reports that Jaabir rode for a month to Shaam to hear from Abdullaah bin Unays a Hadith of the Prophet on retribution on the Day of Qiyaamah.

n03134.summary: Jaabir bin Abdullaah relates travelling to Egypt to hear from Maslamah bin Mukhallad the Prophet's Hadith on concealing a Mu'min's faults, and Muneeb reports a similar journey by another Sahabi to hear the same Hadith.

n03135.summary: Ibn Jurayj relates that Abu Ayyoob Ansaari travelled to Egypt to hear from Uqba bin Aamir the Prophet's saying on concealing a Muslim's faults, and then narrated it in Madinah before dismounting.

n03136.summary: Makhool relates that Uqba bin Aamir went to Maslamah bin Mukhallad to confirm the Prophet's saying that whoever conceals a brother's sin will have his own sin concealed on the Day of Qiyaamah; Abdullaah bin Buraydah adds a one-line report of a Sahabi travelling to Egypt to see Fudhala bin Ubayd about a Hadith.

n03137.summary: Fudhaala bin Ubayd welcomes a visiting Companion who has come to ask whether he still remembers a Hadith they both heard from the Prophet.

n03138.summary: Ubaydullaah bin Adi travels to Iraq to hear a Hadith from Ali, who narrates it but asks him to keep it private; Abdullaah bin Mas'ood says he would travel to anyone with more knowledge of the Book.

n03141.summary: Abu Tha'laba asks the Prophet for a good teacher; the Prophet refers him to Abu Ubaydah bin Jarraah and praises him, and a Hadith about Khilaafah following Nubuwwat is begun.

n03143.summary: Anas asks the Prophet when people will stop enjoining good and forbidding evil, and the Prophet lists signs of the end including knowledge of Deen carried by the wretched.

n03144.summary: Abu Umayyah Jumhi reports that when the Companions asked the Prophet about the signs of Qiyaamah, he said knowledge would be sought from juniors.

n03145.summary: Abdullaah bin Ukaym reports Umar's saying that the truest words are Allaah's, the best way is that of Muhammad, the worst matters are fabrications in Deen, and people stay well only while they take knowledge from their seniors.

n03146.summary: Bilaal bin Yahya reports Umar's saying that people stay righteous while their knowledge comes from seniors, and degenerate when it comes from juniors.

n03147.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood says people stay steadfast while they take their knowledge of Deen from the Sahabah and their seniors, and are destroyed once it comes from juniors.

n03148.summary: Ibn Mas'ood says people do well while they take knowledge of Deen from their seniors, and that taking it from juniors and sinners will destroy them.

n03149.summary: Ibn Mas'ood says people are well guided while knowledge stays with their seniors, and that once it passes to juniors they will regard the seniors as fools.

n03150.summary: Mu'aawiya warns that the most effective way to mislead people is a man who recites the Qur'aan without understanding it and teaches it to children, slaves and women, who then argue with the scholars.

n03151.summary: Umar bin Khattaab says he does not fear for the Ummah a believer restrained by Imaan or an open sinner, but fears a man who learns the Qur'aan and interprets it in a way it should not be interpreted.

n03152.summary: On his deathbed Uqba bin Aamir tells his sons to accept Ahadeeth only from reliable people, not to borrow, and not to write poetry, which distracts the heart from the Qur'aan.

n03153.summary: Ibn Abbaas reports Umar's sermon at Jaabiya directing people with Qur'aan questions to Ubay bin Ka'b, inheritance questions to Zaid bin Thaabit, Fiqh questions to Mu'aadh bin Jabal, and sending those who need money to Umar.

n03154.summary: Safwaan bin Assaal says he came to the Prophet in the Masjid to seek knowledge, and the Prophet welcomed him as a seeker of knowledge, describing how angels encircle him with their wings.

n03155.summary: Abu Haaroon reports that whenever they visited Abu Sa'eed Khudri he welcomed them, quoting the Prophet's emphatic instruction to treat well the people who come to learn Deen.

n03156.summary: Abu Sa'eed Khudri quotes the Prophet that people will come from the East to learn and must be treated well; Abu Haaroon reports Abu Sa'eed's welcome to them.

n03157.summary: Several variant narrations record the Prophet's instruction to welcome, teach and accommodate students who come from far away, and Abu Sa'eed's own welcome and offer to explain whatever they do not understand.

n03158.summary: Hasan relates Abu Hurayrah's account of a large visit by students and the Prophet's instruction to welcome, greet and teach future seekers of knowledge, followed by a complaint about later teachers who were harsh to students.

n03159.summary: Ummu Dardaa says Abu Dardaa always smiled when narrating Ahadeeth, and he explained that the Prophet also smiled when he narrated.

n03160.summary: Ibn Abbaas reports that when the Prophet was asked which companions are best, he described one who reminds you of Allaah, whose speech adds to your knowledge, and whose deeds remind you of the Aakhirah.

n03161.summary: Qurra reports that when the Prophet sat in a gathering, the Companions sat in circles around him to learn and to ask him when they needed to.

n03162.summary: Yazeed Raqaashi reports that Anas, after narrating Ahadeeth, said the Companions used to sit in groups after Fajr to recite the Qur'aan and learn the compulsory and optional parts of Deen.

n03163.summary: Abu Sa'eed Khudri recounts sitting with poor Muhaajireen when the Prophet came and promised them perfect light on the Day of Qiyaamah and entry into Jannah half a day, five hundred years, before the rich.

n03164.summary: Abdullaah bin Amr reports that the Prophet passed two gatherings in the Masjid, one making du'aa and one learning and teaching Fiqh, and that he sat with the learning group, saying he had been sent as a teacher.

n03165.summary: Abu Bakr bin Abu Moosa reports that Abu Moosa went to Umar after Isha to discuss a matter of Fiqh, and that Umar, who had been occupied in salaah when he arrived, sat up and talked with him at length.

n03166.summary: Jundub bin Abdullaah Bajali travels to Madinah to seek knowledge and is put off by Ubay bin Ka'b's remark about Iraqis; Ubay apologises and promises to relate what he heard from the Prophet, and dies before Friday. Abu Moosa Ash'ari sighs when told of it.

n03167.summary: Hilaal bin Yasaaf says that on arriving in Basrah he saw Imraan bin Husayn narrating Ahadeeth to a group in the Masjid, and asked who he was.

n03168.summary: Abu Saalih describes the crowds at Abdullaah bin Abbaas's door and how Ibn Abbaas taught each group in turn about the Qur'aan and its Tafseer, Halaal and Haraam and Fiqh, inheritance, and Arabic poetry and rare words.

n03169.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood praises gatherings where wisdom is discussed, and says that people of Taqwa are the chiefs and that attending the gatherings of the jurists increases Imaan and knowledge.

n03170.summary: Abu Juhayfah tells people to sit with their seniors, associate with the Ulema and mingle with the wise, and Abu Dardaa says it is deep understanding that keeps a person in contact with men of knowledge.

n03171.summary: In another narration, Abu Dardaa adds that sitting in the gatherings of scholars is part of this advice.

n03172.summary: Abu Haazim reports that Sahl bin Sa'd Saa'idi became angry when some people talked among themselves during his teaching, and said he would leave and go out to fight in Jihaad to seek martyrdom.

n03173.summary: Abu Umaamah relates that a young man from Quraysh asked the Prophet for permission to commit fornication; the Prophet questioned him about his mother, daughter, sister and aunts, and then prayed for his forgiveness, purity and chastity.

n03174.summary: Abu Umaamah says that when the Prophet said something important he repeated it three times so that he would be understood.

n03175.summary: Sha'bi reports that Aa'isha told Ibn Abi Saa'ib, the teacher at Madinah, to keep three conditions when teaching: not to rhyme his du'aas, as the Prophet and Sahabah did not; to lecture once a week (at most thrice) so people do not tire of the Qur'aan; and not to interrupt people's discussions.

n03176.summary: Shaqeeq bin Salamah reports that Abdullaah bin Mas'ood did not lecture them daily so as not to tire them, following the Prophet's practice; A'mash reports Ibn Mas'ood telling a lecturer not to make people despair of Allaah's mercy.

n03177.summary: Ali describes a true scholar as one who neither makes people despair of Allaah's mercy nor licenses disobedience, nor lets them feel safe from Allaah's punishment, and says knowledge without understanding and worship without knowledge or contemplation have no value.

n03178.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports that the Prophet sent Mu'aadh bin Jabal and Abu Moosa to Yemen and told them to help each other and speak well to people, not to put them off; Mu'aadh then taught Islaam and understanding, and said a person is destined for Jannah when people speak well of him.

n03179.summary: Abu Sa'eed Khudri says the Companions' gatherings were always about Deen, and Abdullaah bin Umar says a man is respected as a scholar only if he is not jealous of his superiors, does not look down on those below him, and does not sell his knowledge.

n03181.summary: Umar advises people to acquire knowledge and teach it, to stay humble before their teachers and students, and never to be arrogant.

n03182.summary: Ali lists the rights a student owes a scholar, from not overburdening him with questions to honouring him in his absence.

n03183.summary: Jameela, a slave woman of Anas, reports that Anas had perfume brought for the hands of Thaabit Bunaani, who would not be satisfied until he kissed them.

n03184.summary: Ibn Abbaas recounts how, having held back for years from asking Umar about an incident, he finally asked who the two wives were who acted together against the Prophet, and Umar named Aa'isha and Hafsa.

n03185.summary: Sa'eed bin Musayyib asks Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas what the Prophet said to Ali when he appointed him deputy at Tabook, and Sa'd quotes the Prophet comparing Ali's status to that of Haaroon with Moosa.

n03186.summary: Uthmaan bin Abdullaah bin Mowhab reports that when Jubayr bin Mut'im was asked about inheritance, he said he had no knowledge and sent someone to ask Umar, who praised him for saying Allaah knows best.

n03187.summary: Mujaahid and Urwa each report that Abdullaah bin Umar, when asked about matters he did not know, simply said that he did not know.

n03188.summary: Uqba bin Muslim says he stayed with Abdullaah bin Umar for thirty-four months and that Ibn Umar often answered 'I do not know', warning that such questions would make their backs a bridge to Jahannam.

n03189.summary: Naafi reports that when a man asked Abdullaah bin Umar a question, Ibn Umar stayed silent for a long time, then rebuked him for thinking Allaah will not hold people to account for what they ask, and said he would answer only what he knew.

n03190.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood says a scholar should answer what he knows and otherwise say 'Allaah knows best', which is itself part of knowledge, and quotes the verse in which the Prophet is told to say he asks no payment and does not pretend.

n03191.summary: Abdullaah bin Basheer reports that when Ali was asked a question he said he had no knowledge of it, and then said it was a comfort that he had once admitted not knowing something he did know.

n03192.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas says that when an Aalim gives up saying 'I do not know', he has reached his ruin, and the same saying is given again in a second narration.

n03193.summary: Makhool reports that Umar gave people tree-planting to rest them from lessons; Abdullaah bin Mus'ab reports that Umar set a limit on dowries and conceded to a woman who quoted the Qur'aan against him; Muhammad bin Ka'b Qurazi reports that Ali conceded to a man who corrected him; and Sa'eed bin Musayyib says Umar and Uthmaan debated sharply but always parted amicably.

n03197.summary: Uqba bin Aamir tells how he took turns minding his tribe's camels so the others could hear the Prophet, and how Umar relayed the Prophet's words on wudhu and on dying without shirk, after which the Prophet asked whether he preferred one or twelve.

n03198.summary: Uthmaan bin Abul Aas, the youngest of a Thaqeef delegation, asked the Prophet to pray that he understand the Deen, and was made Ameer over his tribe; a second narration adds that the Prophet had a copy of the Qur'aan and gave it to him when he asked.

n03199.summary: Anas says that when the Prophet narrated Ahadeeth, as many as sixty Companions would sit with him, and when he left they rehearsed what they had heard among themselves.

n03200.summary: Abu Moosa Ash'ari says that after the Fajr salaah the Companions turned to the Prophet, and some asked him about the Qur'aan, others about inheritance and others about dreams.

n03201.summary: Fudhaala bin Ubayd tells his companions to learn and teach each other, rehearse what they have learnt, and add istighfaar to their discussions.

n03202.summary: Abu Nadhra says that when people asked Abu Sa'eed Khudri to write hadiths down, he refused, telling them to learn by memory as he had from the Prophet, and told them to rehearse hadiths among themselves because that reinforces memory.

n03203.summary: In another narration, Abu Sa'eed Khudri urges rehearsing hadiths, Ali says that without rehearsal they will be forgotten, and Ali adds that people should keep visiting one another.

n03205.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood says that rehearsing hadiths keeps them alive, and in another narration that rehearsing knowledge of the Deen earns the reward of nafl salaah.

n03206.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas says he prefers rehearsing the knowledge of Deen for part of the night to spending the night in worship.

n03207.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports that Umar put three questions to Ali, and Ali answered each with a saying of the Prophet about souls that either recognise or stay apart from one another, about clouds that pass over the heart so that a person forgets, and about true and false dreams; Umar said he was glad to have these answers before his death.

n03208.summary: Ibraheem Taymi reports that Umar, troubled that the Ummah differs although it has one Book, one Nabi and one Qiblah, asked Ibn Abbaas, who answered that differences arise when people recite the Qur'aan without knowing why its verses were revealed; Umar first rebuked him, then called him back and asked him to repeat it.

n03209.summary: Ibn Abbaas reports that when Umar asked what the orchard verse of Surah Baqarah meant and no one could say, Ibn Abbaas said it refers to deeds, and Umar agreed, explaining that a man most needs his deeds on the Day of Qiyaamah.

n03210.summary: Ibn Abbaas recounts that Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf objected to Umar letting him sit with the Badr veterans, and that when Umar asked about Surah Nasr Ibn Abbaas explained it as a sign of the Prophet's approaching death, which Umar confirmed.

n03211.summary: In another, abbreviated narration, Ibn Abbaas says Umar consulted him alongside the senior Companions and that Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf objected in the same way.

n03212.summary: Ibn Abbaas reports that Umar explained the Maa'idah verse against troublesome questions as relating to Muhaajireen doubts about lineage, then voiced fear that Ali might be carried away by conceit if he became Khaleefah, which Ibn Abbaas rejected by defending Ali and citing Aadam's lapse.

n03213.summary: Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas says Khabbaab told Ibn Umar that Abu Hurayrah reported a reward for attending funerals, so Ibn Umar sent Khabbaab to Aa'isha to verify it, and when she confirmed it Ibn Umar said they had lost many qiraats.

n03214.summary: Abu Hurayrah says the poor men of Suffa had no trade or farms to keep them from the Prophet, so he sought words to learn from him, and Ibn Umar tells him he knows more hadiths than they do because he stayed closer to the Prophet.

n03215.summary: Ibn Abbaas says the Companions asked the Prophet no more than thirteen questions, all of them matters of benefit that appear in the Qur'aan, and then adds that the angels were the first to circle the Ka'bah and that several prophets are buried between the Black Stone and the Yamani corner.

n03216.summary: Aa'isha says the Ansaari women were the best because modesty did not stop them asking about the Deen, and Ummu Sulaym asks the Prophet whether a woman must bathe after a dream of intercourse, to which he says yes if she finds semen, adding that women are offshoots of men.

n03218.summary: Sa'd (RA) says people used to question each other about things the Prophet mentioned, then questioned him so much that a matter which had been lawful became unlawful.

n03219.summary: Jaabir says the verses of Li'aan were revealed only because of the many questions asked; Ibn Mas'ood asks Haarith bin Qais why people ask so much, and Haarith says they want answers only to forget them, which Ibn Mas'ood affirms.

n03220.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar tells people never to ask about things that have not happened, because Umar used to curse those who did.

n03221.summary: Umar says it is not permissible to ask about things that have not yet happened, because Allaah has already decreed everything that is still to happen.

n03222.summary: Khaarijah bin Zaid reports that his father Zaid bin Thaabit would not give an opinion on a question until he had checked whether the matter had happened, and would answer only once it had.

n03223.summary: Masrooq says that when he asked Ubay bin Ka'b about a matter, Ubay asked whether it had happened, and on hearing it had not said they should rest until it did; a second narration adds that they would then find a solution.

n03225.summary: Abu Umaama says that when a man who had profited from trading a tribe's shares came to the Prophet, the Prophet told him that learning ten verses of the Qur'aan was more profitable, and the man went to learn them.

n03226.summary: Ubay bin Ka'b narrates that the Prophet taught him the virtue of Surah Faatiha as the seven often-repeated verses.

n03228.summary: Anas relates that Abu Moosa recited the Qur'aan at home, and that the Prophet, having heard him unseen, praised his recitation as one of the tunes of the family of Dawood.

n03230.summary: Ali says that after the Prophet passed away he vowed not to take off his shawl until he had memorised the whole Qur'aan.

n03231.summary: Maymoon reports that Abdullaah bin Umar took four years to learn Surah Baqara.

n03232.summary: Salmaan recites Surah Yusuf to a crowd in the Madaa'in masjid, and when most of them leave he rebukes those who prefer a lecture to the Book of Allaah.

n03233.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood teaches each verse of the Qur'aan to the people who come to his house each morning and tells them it is better than everything the sun rises upon.

n03234.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood tells the people to hold fast to the Qur'aan as Allaah's laden tablecloth, since knowledge is acquired only through study.

n03235.summary: Another narration has Abdullaah bin Mas'ood say that a house without the Book of Allaah is like a deserted house and that Shaytaan leaves a house where Surah Baqarah is recited.

n03236.summary: Umar tells a man who often came to his door to go and study the Book of Allaah, and the man later says the Book has made him independent of Umar's door.

n03237.summary: Umar says every Muslim man should learn six Surahs, two each for the Fajr, Maghrib and Isha salaah.

n03238.summary: Umar names the Surahs that should be learnt, citing Miswar bin Makhrama, a letter to governors reported by Haaritha bin Mudarrib, and a further narration on teaching Surah Noor to women.

n03239.summary: Abu Rayhaana complains that he finds the Qur'aan hard to learn, and the Prophet advises him not to take on more than he can manage and to pray much nafl salaah; Umayrah reports that he used to make much sajdah at Asqalaan.

n03240.summary: Qaradha bin Ka'b reports that Umar, on the journey to Iraq, asked the Sahabah to keep the people occupied with the Qur'aan and narrate few Ahadeeth, and Qaradha repeated that prohibition when asked to narrate in Iraq.

n03242.summary: A freed slave of Abdullaah bin Umar relates how Umar had Sabeegh, who questioned the mutashaabih verses, beaten with date-palm branches and ordered the people to shun him until Abu Moosa reported he had reformed; a second narration, from Sulaymaan bin Yasaar, gives an account of Sabeegh being beaten by Umar in Madinah until he said his doubts had gone.

n03244.summary: Abu Uthmaan says Umar wrote ordering the Muslims not to associate with Sabeegh, and another narration says Sabeegh was despised by his people after once being their leader.

n03245.summary: Some men from Egypt, who had questioned Abdullaah bin Umar about difficult Qur'aanic matters, are examined by Umar on what they have memorised and practised, and Umar says he would have made an example of them if the people of Madinah had known.

n03246.summary: Ubaadah bin Saamit says that a migrant he had taught the Qur'aan gave him a bow as a gift, and the Prophet called it a burning ember hung between his shoulders.

n03247.summary: Ubay bin Ka'b, having taught a Surah to a man who gave him a garment, is told by the Prophet that wearing it would be wearing a garment of fire.

n03248.summary: Another narration says that when Ubay bin Ka'b taught the Qur'aan to a man, he received a bow as a gift.

n03250.summary: Awf bin Maalik reports that a man he had taught the Qur'aan gave him a bow, and the Prophet asked whether he wanted to meet Allaah carrying an ember of Jahannam on his back.

n03251.summary: Muthanna bin Waa'il recounts Abdullaah bin Busr's report of a man who was given a bow for teaching a child the Qur'aan, and the Prophet told him to return it, asking whether he wanted a bow of fire around his neck.

n03252.summary: Umar objects when he hears that Sa'd plans to pay Qur'aan teachers an allowance, later tells a governor to give allowances by merit of family and companionship with the Prophet instead, and warns that those who take pay for teaching will see even adulterers enter Jannah before them.

n03253.summary: Ibn Abbaas warns Umar that the spread of the Qur'aan among the people will lead to disputes, and after Umar's anger he recites verses to explain his view, and Umar agrees that he is right.

n03254.summary: Abdullaah bin Ubayd bin Umayr relates that Ibn Abbaas warned Umar that the spread of the Qur'aan would cause disputes and then killing, and that Umar admitted he had understood the same but had been concealing it.

n03255.summary: Kinaanah Adawi relates that Umar asked his commanders for lists of the Huffaadh so he could send them out to teach, that Abu Moosa replied there were just over three hundred, and that Umar wrote to them on honouring and following the Qur'aan.

n03256.summary: Abu Kinaanah and Abul Aswad Daly each relate Abu Moosa's addresses to his Huffaadh and Qurraa, urging them to follow the Qur'aan and not let time harden their hearts, and reminding them they will be questioned about what they do.

n03257.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood tells the people of Kufa not to dispute about the Qur'aan, since it contains no contradictions, and recalls that the Prophet approved his recitation; other reports add his advice on the qualities of a man of the Qur'aan and on listening carefully.

n03259.summary: Abu Hurayrah relates that when a Bedouin asked the Prophet, in the middle of his narrating, when the Qiyaamah would come, the Prophet said it would come when trusts are misappropriated and authority is given to unworthy people.

n03260.summary: Waabisah recalls the Prophet's address on the Farewell Hajj, that the month, city, and the blood, wealth and honour of the Muslims are sacred until the Day they meet their Rabb, and that those present must convey it to those absent.

n03261.summary: Makhool relates that Abu Umaamah told him and his companions that their sitting was a means for the Deen to reach them and that they must propagate it, and Saleem bin Aamir relates that Abu Ubaadah asked his listeners after each session to pass on what they had heard.

n03262.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas relates the Prophet's du'aa for mercy on his successors, those who will narrate his Ahadeeth and teach them to the people.

n03263.summary: Aasim bin Muhammad relates from his father that he saw Abu Hurayrah on a Jumu'ah standing at the pulpit narrating Ahadeeth until the Imaam emerged, and then sit down.

n03264.summary: Aslam relates that Umar refused to narrate Ahadeeth when asked for fear of adding or omitting a word, and Abdur Rahmaan bin Haatib says that Uthmaan narrated more thoroughly than any Sahabi but was very reluctant to do so.

n03266.summary: Uthmaan explains that his reluctance to narrate Ahadeeth is not weak memory but fear of the Prophet's warning against those who attribute falsehoods to him, and another narration gives that warning in different words.

n03267.summary: Ali says that when narrating Ahadeeth he would rather fall from the sky than say what the Prophet did not say, but that in matters of war strategy such strictness need not apply.

n03268.summary: Amr bin Maymoon and Masrooq each relate that Abdullaah bin Mas'ood sometimes went a whole year without narrating a Hadith, and that when he did he trembled and sweated, adding a qualification to what he attributed to the Prophet.

n03270.summary: Abu Dardaa and Anas bin Maalik closed their hadith reports with a qualifying phrase, so as not to claim more than the Prophet's exact words.

n03271.summary: Anas bin Maalik narrated few hadith and always added the qualifying phrase. Abu Ja'far Muhammad bin Ali says no Companion was more careful in narrating than Abdullaah bin Umar.

n03273.summary: Sha'bi says he sat with Abdullaah bin Umar for a full year and never heard him narrate a hadith from the Prophet.

n03274.summary: Imraan bin Husayn says he has memorised many hadith but holds back from narrating them, because some of his companions may differ with him over the wording.

n03275.summary: Mutarraf reports that Imraan bin Husayn could narrate hadith for two days without repeating one, but refrained because companions confuse the sequence of words. He was exact when quoting the Prophet.

n03276.summary: Suhayb tells Sulaymaan bin Abu Abdullaah that he will never say 'Rasulullaah said' for a hadith, though he will relate what he experienced on the expeditions.

n03277.summary: Makhool and Abul Azhar asked Waathila bin Asqa for a hadith in exact words. He replied that they had not mastered the Qur'aan, and that narrators should relate only the meaning.

n03278.summary: Before his death Umar summoned Companions from distant lands, asked what hadith they were spreading, and kept them in Madinah. He also confined Abdullaah bin Mas'ood, Abu Mas'ood and Abu Dardaa there.

n03279.summary: Ibn Abu Awfa reports that when asked to narrate hadith, Zaid bin Arqam said he had grown old and forgetful, and that narrating the Prophet's hadith was a serious matter.

n03280.summary: Mu'aadh bin Jabal and Abu Dardaa both said that knowledge brings no benefit until it is practised. Anas bin Maalik said the same, that there is no reward for knowledge until it is put into practice.

n03281.summary: Abdur Rahmaan bin Ghanam reports that ten Companions were learning in the Masjid of Quba when the Prophet came and told them to learn.

n03282.summary: Ali reports that a man asked the Prophet what would be the proof against him for ignorance and what would be the proof against him for knowledge. The Prophet answered knowledge, and then action.

n03283.summary: Umar tells people to study the Book of Allaah and practise its teachings, so that they become among its worthy bearers.

n03284.summary: Ali tells people to study and practise, warning that a time will come when most of the truth is rejected. Only the anonymous, aloof people who are the lanterns of knowledge will be saved, and they are not hasty and do not spread immoral behaviour or speech.

n03285.summary: Ali warns of people of knowledge whose private lives contradict their public teaching, who boast in their gatherings, and whose actions will not rise to Allaah.

n03286.summary: Ibn Mas'ood urges people to practise what they learn. Abdullaah bin Ukaym and Adi bin Adi relate his warnings that Allaah will question each person about whether they practised their knowledge.

n03289.summary: Abu Dardaa said he feared being asked on the Day of Judgement whether he practised his knowledge. He also said that the worst person before Allaah is one whose knowledge does not benefit him.

n03290.summary: Mu'aadh bin Jabal said that no one will be able to move on the Day of Judgement until he is questioned about four things, including how he practised his knowledge.

n03291.summary: Mu'aadh bin Jabal says no reward is given for knowledge until it is practised. Anas bin Maalik adds that true scholars aim to remember and practise, while foolish people aim only to pass knowledge on.

n03293.summary: Ubay bin Ka'b urges holding fast to the straight path and the Sunnah. He says that moderate deeds done for Allaah's pleasure are better than exertion that goes against the Sunnah, and that deeds should be checked against the way of the Prophets.

n03294.summary: Sa'eed bin Musayyib reports Umar's address after returning to Madinah, that the Sunan have been shown and the Faraa'idh ordained. Ibn Mas'ood then taught that every new introduction in the Deen is a bid'ah, and warned against distant hopes that make one forget the Aakhirah.

n03295.summary: Ibn Mas'ood says that moderation in the Sunnah is better than striving in bid'ah.

n03296.summary: Imraan bin Husayn says the Qur'aan was revealed and the Prophet showed how to live by it, and that people must follow the Companions or they will go astray.

n03297.summary: Imraan bin Husayn rebukes a man who would follow only the Qur'aan. He shows that the details of prayer, zakaah and other rules come from the Sunnah, which explains what the Qur'aan states only briefly.

n03298.summary: Ibn Mas'ood urges people to follow the Companions of the Prophet, who had the most righteous hearts, the deepest knowledge and the most upright example in the Ummah.

n03299.summary: Hudhayfah urges the Qurraa to fear Allaah and follow those who came before them, warning that whoever turns from their path goes far astray.

n03300.summary: Mus'ab bin Sa'd reports that his father, Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas, kept congregational prayer brief but prolonged it when praying alone. He told his son that the Companions are the leaders to be followed.

n03301.summary: Ibn Mas'ood says to follow and not introduce new ways, because the Prophet and the Companions have already laid the path.

n03302.summary: Ibn Mas'ood says that loving Abu Bakr and Umar and acknowledging their worth is an integral part of the Sunnah.

n03303.summary: Ali warns against imitating living people, since a person may change course for better or worse and die in that state. He says that if one must follow someone, it should be those who died as practising believers.

n03304.summary: When Ibn Mas'ood learned that a group in the Masjid was performing dhikr in set counts led by one man, he confronted them, called it a wrong bid'ah, and had them disperse.

n03305.summary: Ibn Mas'ood confronts groups in the Masjid of Kufa and between Maghrib and Isha, saying they have strayed very quickly while the Companions are still alive. Abu Moosa Ash'ari brings him word of the dhikr group.

n03306.summary: Abdullaah bin Zubayr finds his son Aamir sitting with people who fall unconscious in dhikr, and tells him never to sit with them again, since the Companions did not behave like this.

n03307.summary: Sila bin Haarith Ghifaari rebukes Anz Nujaybi, who was telling stories in the Masjid, saying the Companions had scarcely left the Prophet's time and that such innovations should not appear among them yet.

n03308.summary: Amr bin Zuraarah says that while he was relating stories in the Masjid, Ibn Mas'ood called it a misleading bid'ah, and everyone around him dispersed.

n03309.summary: Ibn Shihaab reports Umar's sermon that accurate opinions came only from the Prophet, whom Allaah guided. Sadaqah bin Abu Abdullaah reports Umar's warning that those who follow personal opinion are enemies of the Sunnah.

n03311.summary: Sha'bi relates Ibn Mas'ood's warning against asking for opinions and judging one matter by another, and his saying that 'Allaah knows best' is a third of knowledge. Ibn Mas'ood also foresaw that after the Ulema die, people would destroy Islaam by personal opinion.

n03312.summary: Ibn Abbaas says the basis of Islaam is the Book of Allaah and the Sunnah. A Companion, reported through Ataa from his father, says he is too shy before his Rabb to give a personal opinion on matters affecting the Ummah.

n03313.summary: Mu'aadh bin Jabal tells how the Prophet, sending him to Yemen, asked how he would judge. He answered by the Book of Allaah, then the Sunnah, then ijtihaad without neglecting diligence, and the Prophet approved.

n03314.summary: Muhammad bin Seereen reports that Abu Bakr was the most careful of all not to pass a verdict without knowledge, and that when no verse or Hadith applied he practised ijtihaad, asking Allaah's forgiveness if he was wrong.

n03315.summary: Shurayh reports Umar's letter to him: judge by the Book of Allaah, then by the Prophet's directives, then by the unanimous view of the scholars, and if none of these applies, either practise ijtihaad or refrain, with Umar advising refraining.

n03316.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood says a judge should rule by the Qur'aan, then by the Prophet's practice, then by the verdicts of the righteous scholars, and otherwise practise ijtihaad firmly, never speaking in doubt, since the clearly lawful and the clearly unlawful are plain and doubtful matters should be avoided.

n03317.summary: Abdullaah bin Abu Yazeed reports that Ibn Abbaas gave his answers in order: from the Qur'aan first, then from the Prophet's sayings, then from the statements of Abu Bakr or Umar, and only then by ijtihaad.

n03318.summary: Ibn Abbaas says that when a command was confirmed by corroborating evidence they would not place anything else on a par with it and would readily practise it.

n03319.summary: Masrooq reports that when he asked Ubay bin Ka'b about a matter that had not yet happened, Ubay asked for respite until it happened so that they could then practise ijtihaad.

n03320.summary: Abdur Rahmaan bin Abu Layla says he met 120 Sahabah in the Masjid, and each one, whether narrating a Hadith or giving a Fatwa, wished that a fellow Sahabi had done it instead.

n03321.summary: Ibn Mas'ood and Ibn Abbaas say that only a madman would issue a Fatwa on everything he is asked, and Hudhayfah says only three kinds of people should issue Fataawaa: one who knows which verses abrogate and which are abrogated, a leader with no alternative, and a pretentious fool.

n03322.summary: Muhammad bin Seereen reports that Umar told Abu Mas'ood Uqba that he had heard he was issuing Fataawaa to people, and warned him of the burden that goes with it.

n03323.summary: Umar adds that Abu Mas'ood is not a governor, so he need not issue Fataawaa.

n03324.summary: Abu Minhaal reports that Zaid bin Arqam and Baraa each sent him to ask the other about selling gold and silver, and Abu Husayn says that people now issue Fataawaa on matters which, had they been put to Umar, he would have taken to the veterans of Badr.

n03326.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar names Abu Bakr and Umar as the only ones who issued Fataawaa in the Prophet's time, while Qaasim bin Muhammad names Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthmaan and Ali, and Fudhayl bin Abu Abdullaah bin Dinaar names Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf, Abu Bakr, Umar and Uthmaan.
