n03327.summary: Abu Attiyya Hamdaani reports that when a man had already asked Abu Moosa, Ibn Mas'ood gave a contrary answer and left, and Abu Moosa then told people not to ask him anything while this great scholar was present.

n03328.summary: Sahl bin Abu Khaythamah reports that in the Prophet's time three Muhaajir Sahabah (Umar, Uthmaan and Ali) and three Ansaar Sahabah (Ubay bin Ka'b, Mu'aadh bin Jabal and Zaid bin Thaabit) were authorised to issue Fataawaa.

n03329.summary: Masrooq reports that the Sahabah who issued Fataawaa were Umar, Ali, Ibn Mas'ood, Zaid bin Thaabit, Ubay bin Ka'b and Abu Moosa Ash'ari.

n03330.summary: Qabeesah reports that Zaid bin Thaabit held the posts of judge, Fatwa, Qiraa'ah and inheritance in Madinah under Umar, Uthmaan and Ali, and after them until his death in 45 AH; Ataa bin Yasaar reports that Umar and Uthmaan consulted Ibn Abbaas, who issued Fataawaa until he died; Ziyaad bin Meenaa lists the Madinah Fatwa-givers; and Qaasim reports that his aunt Aa'isha issued Fataawaa after Abu Bakr's time.

n03331.summary: Abu Dharr says the Prophet left the Sahabah with so much knowledge that even the flutter of a bird's wings in the sky would remind them of something he had taught.

n03332.summary: Another narration quotes the Prophet saying that everything which brings a person closer to Jannah and further from Jahannam has been explained to the Sahabah.

n03333.summary: Amr bin Al Aas says he learnt a thousand similitudes from the Prophet, and Aa'isha reports that when the Sahabah disagreed her father Abu Bakr settled the matter with Hadiths on where a Nabi is buried and on the inheritance of the Prophets.

n03334.summary: Abu Waa'il reports that Ibn Mas'ood said Umar's knowledge would outweigh all the knowledge on earth, and Ibraheem reports Ibn Mas'ood saying that nine-tenths of knowledge left the world with Umar's death, and Ibn Mas'ood described Umar as the one who knew Allaah best and understood the Deen most deeply.

n03335.summary: Hudhayfah says the knowledge of everyone else is, compared with Umar's, like what could be buried in a small hole, and a man from Madinah says that learned scholars seemed like children before Umar.

n03336.summary: Abu Is'haaq reports that when the Prophet married Faatima to Ali, she objected that he had weak eyesight and a large stomach, and the Prophet replied that Ali was the first of his companions to accept Islaam, the most knowledgeable and the most tolerant.

n03338.summary: Ali says he knows precisely about which occasion, place and person every verse of the Qur'aan was revealed for, because his Rabb gave him a perceptive heart and an eloquent tongue.

n03339.summary: Sa'eed bin Musayyab reports that Umar used to seek Allaah's protection against any intricate problem that had to be resolved without Ali's help.

n03340.summary: Masrooq reports Ibn Mas'ood's claim to know the occasion of revelation of every chapter of the Qur'aan and Masrooq's own comparison of the Sahabah to dams and Ibn Mas'ood to an ocean; Zaid bin Wahab and Asad bin Wadaa'ah report that Umar called Ibn Mas'ood a coffer filled with knowledge of the Deen and preferred sending him to the people of Qaadisiyyah over keeping him in Madinah.

n03341.summary: Abul Bakhtari reports that some men asked Ali about the Sahabah, and Ali described the knowledge of Ibn Mas'ood, Abu Moosa, Ammaar, Hudhayfah, Abu Dharr and Salmaan, and then described his own: whenever he asked the Prophet he received an answer, and when he was silent the Prophet informed him.

n03342.summary: Ibn Mas'ood says Mu'aadh bin Jabal was an Ummah, Qaanit and Haneef, and not one of the Mushrikeen; when the narrator doubted this against the Qur'aan's description of Ibraheem, Ibn Mas'ood explained that Ummah means one who teaches good and Qaanit one who obeys Allaah and His Rasool, and that this described Mu'aadh.

n03343.summary: Masrooq says that after examining the Sahabah he found all their knowledge in six of them, and then found that all of it could be found in Ali and Ibn Mas'ood alone.

n03344.summary: Masrooq says that on arriving in Madinah and asking about the Sahabah, he found that Zaid bin Thaabit was among those with the most profound knowledge.

n03345.summary: Masrooq reports that Ibn Mas'ood said that if Ibn Abbaas were their age none of them could equal a tenth of his knowledge, and Mujaahid reports that Ibn Abbaas was called an ocean because of how much he knew.

n03346.summary: Layth bin Abu Sulaym asks Tawoos why he follows Ibn Abbaas, and Tawoos says seventy Sahabah preferred Ibn Abbaas's opinion; Aamir reports his father Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas praising Ibn Abbaas and Umar deferring to him; Abu Zinaad reports Umar's visit during Ibn Abbaas's fever; Talha praises his understanding; and Ubay bin Ka'b predicts he will become the most learned of the Ummah.

n03349.summary: Tawoos says Ibn Abbaas towered above others in knowledge as a tall palm tree towers above shorter ones.

n03350.summary: Abu Waa'il reports that when Ibn Abbaas was Ameer of Hajj and recited and commented on Surah Noor, his companion said even the Turks would accept Islaam; Umar praised Ibn Abbaas's answer to a question sent by Ya'la bin Umayyah from Yemen; and Ataa reports that Ibn Abbaas gave each group of questioners - on poetry, ancestry, Arab battles and history - a full answer.

n03353.summary: Ubaydullaah bin Abdullaah bin Utba describes the breadth of Ibn Abbaas's knowledge, including the verdicts of Abu Bakr, Umar and Uthmaan, and Ibn Abbaas himself says he questioned senior Muhaajir and Ansaar Sahabah about the Prophet's battles, and that Ubay bin Ka'b told him which Surahs were revealed in Madinah.

n03355.summary: Ikrimah reports that Amr bin Al Aas said Ibn Abbaas had the most knowledge of the earlier scriptures and of what the Qur'aan and Hadith left unclear, and Ibn Abbaas replied that he had that knowledge because he used to ask the Prophet about what was Halaal and Haraam.

n03356.summary: Aa'isha says Ibn Abbaas knew the rites of Hajj best of the Sahabah still living, and Jaabir, Raafi bin Khudayj and Ibn Hanafiyyah each lament his death, Ibn Hanafiyyah calling him the sage of this Ummah; Abu Kulthoom reports the last remark.

n03357.summary: Amr bin Dinaar says Abdullaah bin Umar was regarded as one of the young Fuqahaa.

n03358.summary: Khaalid bin Ma'daan says that in Shaam there remained no Sahabi whose knowledge was more reliable, whose understanding was deeper and who was more beloved to the people than Ubaadah bin Saamit and Shaddaad bin Aws.

n03359.summary: Handhla bin Sufyaan reports from his teachers that none had a better understanding of the Deen than Abu Sa'eed Khudri.

n03360.summary: Abu Za'eeza'a, Marwaan bin Hakam's scribe, reports that Marwaan questioned Abu Hurayrah on the same matters a year apart, seating him behind a screen the second time, and that Abu Hurayrah repeated his answers word for word both times.

n03361.summary: Abu Moosa Ash'ari reports that whenever the Sahabah had doubts they referred them to Aa'isha and always found the answer with her, and Qabeesah bin Dhuwayb says she was among the most knowledgeable.

n03362.summary: Abu Salamah says no one knew the Sunnah better than Aa'isha or gave better opinions, and Masrooq affirms she knew the laws of inheritance, as senior Sahabah consulted her on it.

n03363.summary: Mahmood bin Labeed says that Aa'isha and Umm Salamah knew the most Ahadeeth of the Prophet's wives, that Aa'isha issued fatwas through the caliphates of Umar and Uthmaan, and that they sent to her to ask about Sunnah practices.

n03364.summary: Mu'aawiya praises Aa'isha's eloquence, and Urwa says she was the most proficient in jurisprudence, poetry, Arab history and medicine, having learnt medicine while treating the Prophet in his illness.

n03368.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood tells his students to be fountainheads of knowledge and lanterns of the night who stay unknown on earth but known in the heavens, and a similar report from Ali is given.

n03369.summary: Wahab bin Munabbih reports that Ibn Abbaas, on hearing a group debating predestination, went to them and described the scholars who are devoted to Allaah and fear Him.

n03372.summary: Ibn Mas'ood warns of a time when fabricated Sunnahs become the norm and resisting change is treated as heresy, when the trustworthy and the Fuqahaa become few, and when knowledge is sought for worldly motives.

n03373.summary: Abu Dharr says Ahadeeth must be learnt only for Allaah's pleasure; Ka'b says greed and begging remove knowledge from scholars' hearts, and Ali names seeking the Deen for worldly motives as a sign of the end of time, in answer to Umar.

n03374.summary: Umar tells the people he fears two kinds of person for the Ummah: one who misinterprets the Qur'aan, and one who vies with his brother for kingship.

n03375.summary: Hasan narrates that Umar kept Ahnaf bin Qais back for a year when a delegation from Basrah came to him, then explained that he had feared the eloquent hypocrite and was now confident Ahnaf was not one.

n03376.summary: Abu Uthmaan Nahdi reports that Umar warned from the pulpit against the hypocritical Aalim, defined as one who speaks what is right but does what is wrong.

n03377.summary: Umar says he always maintained that the one who will destroy this Ummah is a hypocrite with an educated tongue.

n03378.summary: Abu Uthmaan Nahdi reports Umar's sermon that what he fears most for the Ummah is the hypocritical Aalim, whose tongue is educated but whose heart and actions are ignorant.

n03379.summary: Hudhayfah warns against the places of tribulation, and Ibn Mas'ood identifies them as the doors of rulers, where a scholar confirms the rulers' lies and praises them, losing his Deen for their wealth.

n03381.summary: Awf bin Maalik reports that the Prophet said Deeni knowledge will be lifted, and when Labeed and Ziyaad bin Labeed ask how, Shaddaad bin Aws explains that devotion will be the first thing to go.

n03382.summary: Abu Dardaa reports the Prophet asking what benefit the Torah and Injeel were to the Jews and Christians.

n03383.summary: Wahshi reports the Prophet saying the Jews and Christians paid no attention to their scriptures, and Ibn Labeed reports him saying they gained no benefit from them.

n03384.summary: Ibn Mas'ood says that the most serious cause of Islaam dwindling will be the death of the Ulema.

n03385.summary: Sa'eed bin Musayyib reports that after Zaid bin Thaabit was buried, Ibn Abbaas said that a great deal of knowledge had just left them.

n03386.summary: Ammaar bin Abu Ammaar reports that Ibn Abbaas, sitting by Zaid bin Thaabit's grave, pointed to it and said knowledge leaves when its bearers die, and gives variant wordings of this.

n03387.summary: Ibn Mas'ood says that a man forgets the knowledge he once learnt because of the sins he commits.

n03388.summary: Qaasim reports that Ibn Mas'ood said the problem with knowledge is forgetting it.

n03389.summary: Jaabir bin Abdullaah reports Hudhayfah saying that they were given this knowledge to bear and pass on, even though they do not practise it.

n03390.summary: Abu Hurayrah reports the Prophet's du'aa seeking refuge from knowledge that does not benefit, a heart that does not submit, a soul never satiated, and a du'aa that is not answered.

n03391.summary: Thowbaan reports that when the Muhaajireen asked which wealth is best, Umar offered to ask the Prophet, who said the best is a tongue that engages in dhikr, a grateful heart and a believing wife.

n03392.summary: Ali reports the Prophet repeating a warning against hoarding gold and silver after the verse on them was revealed, which prompted the Sahabah to ask what wealth to keep and led Umar to offer to ask.

n03393.summary: Abu Hurayrah reports that the Prophet, passing Humdaan on the road to Makkah, said the Mufarriddoon are in the lead, and explained that they are those who engage abundantly in dhikr.

n03394.summary: Another narration has the Prophet describing the Mufarriddoon as those intoxicated with Allaah's dhikr, which unburdens them of sins so they meet Allaah without a burden on the Day of Qiyaamah.

n03395.summary: Mu'aadh bin Jabal reports that the Prophet asked where those in the lead are, and said they are those intoxicated with Allaah's dhikr, and that whoever wishes to eat from the gardens of Jannah should engage in dhikr abundantly.

n03396.summary: Several reports say the Prophet named those who engage most in dhikr as the highest in rank, the most rewarded and the most saved from Jahannam, above jihaad, and Abu Bakr told Umar that the people of dhikr had taken all the good, which the Prophet confirmed.

n03398.summary: Mu'aadh bin Jabal recounts that the last advice the Prophet gave him when he left for Yemen was that the most beloved deed to Allaah is to die with the tongue moist with dhikr.

n03399.summary: Mu'aadh asks the Prophet which deed is best and closest to Allaah, and the narration is cut off before the answer.

n03400.summary: Umar advises against discussing people and urges constant dhikr of Allaah as a cure, and Uthmaan says that if their hearts were pure they would never tire of dhikr.

n03403.summary: Ibn Mas'ood urges abundant dhikr of Allaah, saying it does not matter if one keeps company only with those who can help in dhikr.

n03404.summary: Salmaan says that a man who spends the night reciting the Book of Allaah and engaging in dhikr is better than one who spends it giving away fair-complexioned slave women.

n03405.summary: Ahmad bin Habeeb reports that Abu Dardaa advised a man to remember Allaah in ease so that Allaah remembers him in hardship, and to consider how soon worldly things pass.

n03406.summary: Abu Dardaa says the best deed is the dhikr of Allaah, better than jihaad or giving gold and silver in charity, and that those whose tongues are moist with dhikr will enter Jannah laughing.

n03407.summary: Mu'aadh bin Jabal says dhikr saves a person from Allaah's punishment more than any deed, even jihaad unless the sword breaks, and Abdullaah bin Amr says dhikr morning and evening is better than breaking swords or giving large sums in charity.

n03408.summary: Anas reports the Prophet preferring to sit with people engaged in Allaah's dhikr between Fajr and sunrise, and between Asr and sunset, over freeing four slaves each time.

n03409.summary: Anas reports that the Prophet said sitting in dhikr from Asr until evening is better than freeing eight slaves from the progeny of Ismaa'eel.

n03410.summary: The Prophet said he prefers sitting with people engaged in Allaah's dhikr between Fajr and sunrise to everything the sun rises upon.

n03411.summary: Sahal bin Sa'd reports that the Prophet said he would rather attend Fajr and then sit in dhikr until sunrise than provide thoroughbred horses for the path of Allaah.

n03412.summary: Abbaas bin Abdul Muttalib reports that the Prophet said sitting in dhikr from Fajr until sunrise is preferred to freeing four slaves.

n03413.summary: The Prophet said he prefers praying Fajr and then sitting in Allaah's dhikr until sunrise over racing a horse in the path of Allaah until sunrise.

n03414.summary: Abu Hurayrah reports that the Prophet said he prefers reciting Subhaanallaah, Al Hamdulillaah, Laa Ilaaha Illallaah and Allaahu Akbar over everything the sun rises upon.

n03415.summary: Abu Umaamah reports two versions of the Prophet preferring the reciting of the four phrases of dhikr to freeing slaves from the progeny of Ismaa'eel, one version counting two slaves and the other four.

n03416.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood says he prefers engaging in Allaah's dhikr from morning to night over providing thoroughbred horses for jihaad from morning to night.

n03417.summary: Abu Ubaydah bin Abdullaah bin Mas'ood says it was difficult for Abdullaah bin Mas'ood to say anything other than the dhikr of Allaah.

n03418.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood disliked talk between dawn and Fajr and, after Fajr, told people chatting in the masjid either to pray or to stay silent.

n03419.summary: Abu Dardaa says he loves saying Allaahu Akbar a hundred times more than giving a hundred gold coins in charity, and Mu'aadh bin Jabal says he prefers dhikr from morning to night over providing horses for jihaad.

n03421.summary: Anas bin Maalik reports that Abu Moosa, hearing people talk eloquently, asked why people neglect the Aakhirah, and answered that the world is before them while the Aakhirah is still to come.

n03422.summary: Mu'aadh bin Abdullaah bin Raafi reports a gathering where Abdullaah bin Abu Umayrah relayed Mu'aadh bin Jabal's report that the Prophet said one of two phrases rises to the Throne and the other fills the space between heaven and earth, and Abdullaah bin Umar wept on hearing it.

n03423.summary: Jareeri reports that when Anas entered Ihraam from Dhaatul Irq he spoke nothing but the dhikr of Allaah until he came out of Ihraam.

n03424.summary: Abu Sa'eed Khudri narrates that on the Day of Qiyaamah Allaah will say the people of this assembly will soon learn who the people of honour are, and the Prophet said they are those who take part in gatherings of dhikr.

n03425.summary: Umar narrates that the Prophet said people who attend Fajr and then stay in dhikr until sunrise return sooner, with greater reward, than an expedition that had just come back from Najd with booty.

n03426.summary: Abdur Rahmaan bin Sahl bin Hunayf narrates that when the verse of Surah Kahf 28 was revealed the Prophet went out to find people engaged in dhikr, sat with them, and praised Allaah for placing such people among his Ummah.

n03427.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas narrates that the Prophet passed Abdullaah bin Rawaaha while he was advising companions, recited Surah Kahf 28 to them, and said that angels say the same dhikr as those gathered and that Allaah forgives them.

n03428.summary: Thaabit Bunaani narrates that when the Prophet passed a group engaged in dhikr that included Salmaan, he told them to continue and said Allaah's mercy was descending on them so he wished to join them.

n03429.summary: Jaabir reports that the Prophet said angels attend gatherings of dhikr, that such gatherings are the gardens of Jannah, and that Allaah treats a servant according to the esteem in which the servant holds Him.

n03430.summary: Jaabir bin Samurah reports that after the Fajr salaah the Prophet used to sit engaged in dhikr until sunrise.

n03431.summary: Abdullaah bin Amr asked the Prophet what the reward for gatherings of dhikr would be, and he replied that it is Jannah.

n03432.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood says gatherings of dhikr are the life of knowledge and create humility in the heart.

n03433.summary: Aa'isha asked the Prophet what he said after every gathering and salaah, and he explained that the words seal the good that was said and expiate the bad; Abu Barzah reports that the Prophet recited them at the end of every gathering.

n03435.summary: A longer version of the du'aa said at the end of a gathering, adding a request for forgiveness for having sinned and wronged oneself, because none but Allaah forgives sins.

n03436.summary: Zubayr bin Awwaam reports that the Companions said they fall into talk of the Period of Ignorance after gatherings, and the Prophet advised reciting the du'aa at the end of a gathering to atone for what was said in it.

n03437.summary: Abdullaah bin Amr says that certain words, recited three times after any gathering, atone for wrong said in it and seal it, as a letter is sealed.

n03438.summary: Abu Dharr asked the Prophet for advice and was told to hold fast to taqwa, and then to be particular about reciting the Qur'aan, which is a light for him on earth and a treasure in the heavens.

n03439.summary: Aws bin Hudhayfah describes the Thaqeef delegation's stay in Madinah, when the Prophet came to them late one night because he had not finished his daily portion of the Qur'aan, and his companions explained how he divided the Qur'aan into seven portions.

n03440.summary: Mughiera bin Shu'ba narrates that when a man asked to see the Prophet between Makkah and Madinah, the Prophet delayed granting permission because he had not finished his daily portion of the Qur'aan.

n03441.summary: Abu Salamah reports that when Umar asked Abu Moosa Ash'ari to remind them of their Rabb, Abu Moosa would begin reciting the Qur'aan.

n03442.summary: Reports of Umar's love for Qur'aan recitation: Abu Moosa Ash'ari recited beautifully when Umar asked him to remind them of their Rabb, and when told it was time for salaah Umar said they were already in salaah; Abdullaah bin Abbaas reports that Umar would open the Qur'aan and recite when he entered his house.

n03443.summary: Uthmaan says he does not like a single day or night to pass without looking into the Qur'aan and reciting it.

n03444.summary: Uthmaan says that had our hearts been pure we would never get enough of the speech of Allaah.

n03445.summary: Hasan reports Uthmaan's saying that had hearts been pure they would never tire of Allaah's speech, that he never let a day pass without looking into the Qur'aan, and that the pages of his Qur'aan were worn out by the time of his death.

n03446.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood says to always look into the Qur'aan while reciting, because it makes contemplation easier.

n03447.summary: Habeeb bin Shaheed narrates, through Naafi, that Abdullaah bin Umar made wudu for every salaah and recited Qur'aan between salaahs; Ibn Abu Mulaykah reports that Ikrama bin Abu Jahal placed the Qur'aan on his face and wept.

n03448.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar says that each letter of the Qur'aan recited brings ten good deeds, and that each salutation sent upon the Prophet also brings ten rewards; a second version explains that Alif, Laam and Meem each count for ten rather than the three letters together.

n03449.summary: Uqba bin Aamir narrates that the Prophet advised him to keep ties with those who sever them, give to those who deprive him and forgive those who wrong him, and then taught him to recite Surahs Ikhlaas, Falaq and Naas every night.

n03450.summary: Aa'isha reports that when the Prophet lay down to sleep he blew into his palms after reciting Surahs Ikhlaas and Falaq, then wiped over his body, and that when his illness intensified he asked her to do this for him.

n03451.summary: Jaabir, Irbaadh and Aa'isha report that the Prophet did not sleep until he had recited particular Surahs, and Tawoos comments on the virtue of those Surahs.

n03453.summary: Farwah bin Naufal asks the Prophet for something to recite on going to sleep, and the Prophet names Surah Kaafiroon as an exoneration from Shirk.

n03454.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood says that Surah Mulk protects its reciter from punishment in the grave and that reciting it at night is a great virtue.

n03455.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood repeats that Surah Mulk protects from the punishment of the grave, and Umar says that whoever recites Baqarah, Aal Imraan and Nisaa in one night is counted among the obedient.

n03458.summary: Abdullaah bin Khubayb says that on a dark rainy night, when the Companions went out to find the Prophet to lead salaah, the Prophet told him to recite Surah Ikhlaas and the Mu'awwadhatayn three times each morning and evening for protection.

n03459.summary: Ali says that whoever recites Surah Ikhlaas ten times after Fajr salaah will commit no sin that day, even if Shaytaan tries hard to make him sin.

n03460.summary: Ali reports the Prophet saying that reciting Aayatul Kursi after every salaah leaves nothing but death between a person and Jannah, and that reciting it at bedtime protects his house and those around it.

n03461.summary: Ali says that no person with understanding should spend the night without reciting Aayatul Kursi, which was given to the Prophet from the treasures beneath the Throne, and that he himself recites it three times each night.

n03462.summary: Ali says that no person with understanding should spend the night without reciting the final verses of Surah Baqarah, which come from the treasures beneath the Throne.

n03463.summary: Uthmaan says that whoever recites the final verses of Surah Aal Imraan at night receives the reward of spending the night in worship.

n03464.summary: Ibn Mas'ood says that reciting ten verses of Surah Baqarah at home keeps Shaytaan from entering that home all night.

n03465.summary: Ubay bin Ka'b catches a jinn stealing from his dates, and the jinn tells him that Aayatul Kursi protects people from jinn from evening until morning and from morning until evening; Ubay reports this to the Prophet, who confirms the jinn spoke the truth.

n03466.summary: Abdullaah bin Busr says that when jinn came to him at night near Hims, he recited a verse of Surah A'raaf, and they kept watch over him until morning.

n03467.summary: Alaa bin Jalaaj asks his sons to recite the beginning and end of Surah Baqarah at his grave, as he saw Abdullaah bin Umar do; and Ali says that reciting Surah Saaffaat verses 180 to 182 three times weighs one's deeds on a large scale.

n03468.summary: Abdullaah bin Ubayd bin Umayr reports that whenever Abdur Rahmaan bin Awf entered his house, he recited Aayatul Kursi in every corner of it.

n03469.summary: Abu Hurayrah asks the Prophet who will be most fortunate to receive his intercession, and the Prophet answers whoever says Laa Ilaaha Illallaah with complete sincerity; Zaid bin Arqam and Abu Sa'eed Khudri add reports on the same Kalimah, and Abu Sa'eed also reports Moosa's request to Allaah.

n03471.summary: Another narration quotes Allaah saying that Laa Ilaaha Illallaah placed on one side of a scale would outweigh the seven heavens, their inhabitants and the seven earths on the other.

n03472.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports the Prophet's account of the advice Nooh gave his sons, to affirm Laa Ilaaha Illallaah and the tasbeeh of Azeem wa Bihamdihi and to avoid Shirk and pride, and the Prophet explains that pride is looking down on others.

n03474.summary: Ya'la bin Shaddaad reports, confirmed by Ubaadah bin Saamit, that his father Shaddaad bin Aws reported the Prophet having the Companions raise their hands and recite Laa Ilaaha Illallaah, and then giving them glad tidings that Allaah had forgiven them all.

n03475.summary: Abu Dharr asks the Prophet for advice and is told to follow a sin with a good deed to erase it; when Abu Dharr asks whether a particular recitation is a good deed, the Prophet calls it the best of all good deeds.

n03476.summary: Umar says that when he saw people reciting Allaahu Akbar, it was the word of Taqwa that the Sahabah deserved most.

n03477.summary: Ali says that the word of Taqwa mentioned in Surah Fath verse 26 is the Kalimah.

n03478.summary: A further narration says that Allaahu Akbar is also part of the word of Taqwa, and lists other formulas of dhikr that go with it.

n03479.summary: Abu Sa'eed Khudri reports that the Prophet called Allaahu Akbar, Laa Ilaaha Illallaah, Al Hamdulillaah and Laa Howla wa Laa Quwwata Ilia Billaah the everlasting good deeds.

n03480.summary: Abu Hurayrah reports that the Prophet told the Companions to take up their shields, meaning Al Hamdulillaah and Allaahu Akbar, which protect against Jahannam and go before and behind them on the Day of Qiyaamah.

n03481.summary: Another narration quotes the Prophet calling the same formulas the saviours, and adds Laa Howla wa Laa Quwwata Ilia Billaah.

n03482.summary: Anas reports that the Prophet described the same formulas as going before and behind people, as saviours, and as everlasting good deeds.

n03483.summary: Imraan bin Husayn reports that the Prophet asked whether anyone could do deeds as large as Mount Uhud every day, and then said that Subhaanallaah, Al Hamdulillaah, Laa Ilaaha Illallaah and Allaahu Akbar each weigh more than Mount Uhud.

n03484.summary: Abu Hurayrah says that when the Prophet passed him while he was planting, the Prophet told him that Al Hamdulillaah, Laa Ilaaha Illallaah and Allaahu Akbar are better plants, and that a tree is planted in Jannah for each one said.

n03485.summary: Abu Hurayrah reports the Prophet saying that the gardens of Jannah are the masjids, and that one eats one's fill there by reciting Al Hamdulillaah, Laa Ilaaha Illallaah and Allaahu Akbar.

n03486.summary: Anas reports that the Prophet shook a branch three times, its leaves falling only on the third, and then said that Al Hamdulillaah, Laa Ilaaha Illallaah and Allaahu Akbar shake off sins as leaves fall from a tree.

n03487.summary: Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas reports that a Bedouin asked the Prophet to teach him something to recite, and the Prophet taught him a prayer for forgiveness, mercy, guidance, provision and safety, and said that the Bedouin left with his hands full of good.

n03488.summary: Abu Dharr reports that the Prophet named Subhaanallaahi wa Bihamdihi as the words most loved by Allaah, and other narrations give variant wordings of the same answer.

n03489.summary: Abu Talha reports that the Prophet said whoever says Laa Ilaaha Illallaah enters Jannah, and that reciting Subhaanallaahi wa Bihamdihi a hundred times earns a great number of good deeds, though the Companions' deeds still need Allaah's mercy.

n03490.summary: Sa'd (RA) reports that the Prophet asked whether anyone could not earn a thousand good deeds each day, and said that reciting a formula a hundred times earns a thousand good deeds or erases a thousand sins.

n03491.summary: Qais bin Sa'd bin Ubaadah says that after he had prayed two rakaahs, the Prophet nudged him with his foot and told him that reciting Laa Howla wa Laa Quwwata Ilia Billaah is a door of Jannah.

n03492.summary: Abu Dharr reports that while he was walking behind the Prophet, the Prophet told him that reciting Laa Howla wa Laa Quwwata Ilia Billaah is a treasure of Jannah.

n03493.summary: Abdullaah bin Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas reports that Abu Ayyoob Ansaari told him the Prophet had named abundant recitation of Laa Howla wa Laa Quwwata Ilia Billaah as a treasure of Jannah.

n03494.summary: Abu Ayyoob Ansaari reports that on the Mi'raaj the Prophet passed Ibraheem, who told him to urge his Ummah to plant plenty of the plants of Jannah, which are the words Laa Howla wa Laa Quwwata Ilia Billaah.

n03495.summary: Hadhrat Ibraheem (RA) greeted the Prophet before addressing him and welcomed him.

n03496.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas explains the reward of saying Subhaanallaah, Al Hamdulillaah, Allaahu Akbar, Laa Ilaaha Illallaah and Laa Howla wa Laa Quwwata Illa Billaah, which become an adornment and treasure for the speaker in Jannah.

n03497.summary: Mutarraf reports that Imraan bin Husayn told him that the best of Allaah's bondsmen on the Day of Qiyaamah will be those who praised Him most excessively.

n03498.summary: Umar asked what is meant by the phrases Subhaanallaah, Al Hamdulillaah and Laa Ilaaha Illallaah, and Ali replied that Allaah chose them for Himself and loves them to be said; a second report has Ibn Kawwaa asking Ali about Subhaanallaah, and Ali said it proclaims Allaah's purity from all evil.

n03502.summary: The Prophet told Juwayriyyah that four phrases he recited three times after leaving her would outweigh all the dhikr she had done since morning, and gave the wording of the dhikr in its variant forms.

n03503.summary: Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas reports that when he went with the Prophet to see a woman, they found her counting tasbeeh on date seeds or pebbles, and the Prophet taught her easier phrases to say instead.

n03504.summary: The Prophet taught Abu Umaamah a long dhikr praising and glorifying Allaah in measures covering all He has created, all that fills the earth and heavens, and all that His Book counts, and told him to teach it to everyone.

n03505.summary: The Prophet taught Abu Dardaa a comprehensive dhikr of glorifying and praising Allaah in measures covering all He has created, all that is on earth and all that His Book counts.

n03506.summary: Anas reports that a Sahabi greeted the Prophet and praised Allaah in a gathering, and the Prophet said ten angels raced to record the words, and Allaah ordered them to be recorded exactly as His servant said them.

n03507.summary: Abu Ayyoob Ansaari reports that the Prophet praised a man's words of praise; the man said he had spoken them hoping for reward, and the Prophet said thirteen angels raced to present them to Allaah.

n03508.summary: Sa'eed bin Jubayr reports that Umar saw a man counting tasbeeh on a rosary and advised him to say instead that he glorifies and praises Allaah and magnifies Him as much as fills the heavens, the earth and all that Allaah wills.

n03509.summary: The poor Muhaajireen complained that the wealthy had taken the rewards through charity and freeing slaves, and the Prophet taught them to glorify, praise and magnify Allaah after every salaah; Sumay recounts a dispute with his family about the counts, and Abu Hurayrah reports a similar account from Abu Dharr.

n03510.summary: Ummu Dardaa reports that Abu Dardaa told a traveller of his own conversation with the Prophet about the wealthy taking the rewards, and that the Prophet taught him to glorify, praise and magnify Allaah thirty-three, thirty-three and thirty-four times after every salaah.

n03511.summary: Qataadah reports that some poor believers complained that the wealthy had all the rewards, and the Prophet taught them a dhikr whose roots are on earth and whose branches are in heaven, to be recited ten times after every salaah.

n03512.summary: Ali says that he and Faatima asked the Prophet for a servant because of their hardships, and the Prophet taught them to recite three phrases ten times after every salaah and thirty-three, thirty-three and thirty-four times at bedtime, as better than a servant.

n03513.summary: In another narration the Prophet tells Ali and Faatima that the dhikr to be recited after every salaah and at bedtime is better for them than a servant.

n03514.summary: Ummu Salamah reports that Faatima complained to the Prophet about the callouses on her hands from grinding and making dough, and he taught her the dhikr to say at bedtime and after Fajr and Maghrib, which he said is better for her than a servant and brings protection.

n03515.summary: The Prophet used to recite after salaah that there is none worthy of worship but Allaah, to Him belong all kingdom and praise, and that none can prevent what He gives or give what He prevents.

n03516.summary: Abdul Hameed reports a morning du'aa that the Prophet taught a daughter of his, which protects until evening; Abu Dardaa reports that a dhikr said seven times morning and evening relieves all worries, though the dhikr itself is not legible in the text.

n03517.summary: Ismah reports that the Prophet called dhikr in the marketplace, when people are negligent of Allaah, the action Allaah loves most, and explained the two terms used for it, Subhatul Hadith and Tahreef.

n03518.summary: Abu Idrees Khowlaani reports Mu'aadh's advice to give full attention to Allaah when people are negligent of Him, which the chain says is the sign of an accepted du'aa; Abu Qilaabah reports that two men in a marketplace asked Allaah's forgiveness together, and one later saw the other forgiven in a dream.

n03520.summary: Abu Laas Khuzaa'ee says the Prophet gave them a Zakaah camel to use for Hajj and told them to mention Allaah whenever they mount, because a shaytaan sits in the hump of every camel, and that they could ride them as Allaah permits.

n03521.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas says the Prophet let him ride behind him and recited a set of glorifying phrases while mounting, then leaned on him and smiled, saying that Allaah smiles on a person who mounts and does the same.

n03522.summary: Usaamah reports that when the camel tripped with him behind the Prophet, he said may Shaytaan be destroyed, and the Prophet told him to say Bismillaah instead, since Shaytaan then shrinks to the size of a fly; Abu Tameemah Hujaymi relays a similar incident with another rider.

n03524.summary: Anas reports that when the Prophet mounted a high place while travelling, he said a du'aa that all prominence belongs to Allaah on every high place and all praise belongs to Him in every condition.

n03526.summary: Awf reports the du'aa Ibn Mas'ood recited when leaving home, trusting only in Allaah and affirming that there is no power or might except with Allaah; Ka'b Qurazi cites the travel du'aa in the Qur'aan from Surah Hood.

n03527.summary: Ubay bin Ka'b tells the Prophet that he wants to give all his time to sending salutations on him, after the Prophet warned the people to remember Allaah as the great events of the Last Day were near; the Prophet said his worries would be taken care of and he would be forgiven.

n03528.summary: Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf reports that the Prophet prostrated for so long in a date orchard that he feared the Prophet had died, and the Prophet said he prostrated in gratitude that whoever sends one salutation on him earns ten good deeds and has ten sins removed.

n03529.summary: The Prophet tells his Companions that Jibra'eel brought the good news that Allaah sends salutations on whoever sends salutations on the Prophet and greets of peace whoever greets him, and that this was why he prostrated.

n03530.summary: Abu Talha Ansaari reports that the Prophet was joyful because a messenger from his Lord said that whoever sends one salutation on him earns ten good deeds, has ten sins removed and ten stages raised; Ka'b bin Ujrah reports that on three steps of the pulpit the Prophet said Aameen after Jibra'eel named three people who are far from Allaah's mercy: one who does not get forgiven in Ramadhaan, one who does not send salutations when the Prophet is mentioned, and one whose parents grow old and do not get him into Jannah.

n03532.summary: Abu Dharr reports that the Prophet asked whether he should tell them who the most miserly person is, and said it is the one in whose presence his name is mentioned and who does not send salutations on him.

n03533.summary: Abu Mas'ood reports that Basheer bin Sa'd asked the Prophet how the Companions should send salutations on him, and the Prophet taught them a salutation asking Allaah to shower mercies on Muhammad and his family as He did on Ibraheem, then said that the greeting of peace is already taught in the Tashahhud.

n03534.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood tells the people to send salutations on the Prophet properly, since they do not know whether their salutations will be presented to him, and teaches them a form of salutation.

n03535.summary: Abu Bakr said that sending salutations on the Prophet removes sins more effectively than water extinguishes fire, that greeting him is more rewarding than freeing slaves, and that love for him is more rewarding than both freeing slaves and wielding a sword in Allaah's path.

n03536.summary: Umar bin Khattaab said that du'aas remain suspended between heaven and earth and do not rise until salutations are sent on the Prophet.

n03537.summary: Umar said that all du'aas stop just short of the heavens until salutations are sent on the Prophet, and only then is the du'aa raised.

n03538.summary: Ali said that every du'aa is held back until salutations are sent on the Prophet.

n03539.summary: Ali said that whoever sends a hundred salutations on the Prophet on a Friday will have so much light on his face on the Day of Qiyaamah that people will wonder what great deed he did; Abdullaah bin Abbaas said it is not appropriate to send salutations on anyone other than the Prophets.

n03541.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas states that sending salutations to anyone else is inappropriate, and the text breaks off in the middle of his exception.

n03542.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports that in a single sitting the Prophet recited a hundred times the istighfaar, 'O my Rabbi, forgive me and accept my repentance.'

n03543.summary: Hudhayfah complains to the Prophet that his sharp tongue towards his family may lead him to Jahannam, and the Prophet tells him to seek forgiveness a hundred times daily.

n03544.summary: Anas says that on a journey the Prophet had them all seek forgiveness seventy times, and taught that Allaah forgives seven hundred sins of a servant who does so each day; the text breaks off mid-sentence.

n03545.summary: Ali bin Rabee'ah relates that while he rode behind Ali he saw him ask Allaah for forgiveness and then smile, and that the Prophet had done the same and explained that Allaah laughs at a servant who knows none but Him forgives sins; the text breaks off.

n03546.summary: Abu Hurayrah says he has never seen anyone after the Prophet recite istighfaar more often than him; the quotation breaks off.

n03547.summary: Jaabir bin Abdillaah reports that a man with many sins came to the Prophet, who taught him a du'aa asking for forgiveness greater than his sins, and then told him Allaah had forgiven him.

n03548.summary: Hannaad reports that Umar corrected a man who said only 'I seek forgiveness from Allaah and repent to Him', telling him to add the words asking Allaah to forgive him and accept his repentance.

n03549.summary: Sha'bi reports that Ali said he is surprised at someone who destroys himself when salvation is at hand, and that the salvation is istighfaar.

n03550.summary: Abu Dardaa says there are glad tidings for the person who finds even a little istighfaar in his record of deeds.

n03551.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood says that a person who recites a particular istighfaar three times will be forgiven even for fleeing from the battlefield.

n03552.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood says that if people knew his sins not even two of them would walk behind him, and he would be glad if Allaah forgave even one of them.

n03553.summary: Abu Hurayrah says that every day he seeks Allaah's forgiveness and repents twelve thousand times, in proportion to the debt he owes Allaah.

n03554.summary: Abu Hurayrah is quoted in another version as saying the figure is in proportion to his sins, and Baraa bin Aazib explains that the verse 'do not throw yourselves into destruction' refers to one who sins and then despairs of Allaah's forgiveness, not to one who dies fighting.

n03555.summary: Abu Dardaa relates that the Prophet described people whom Allaah will raise on the Day of Qiyaamah on thrones of pearls, neither prophets nor martyrs, who love one another for Allaah's pleasure and gather to remember Him.

n03556.summary: Amr bin Abasa reports the Prophet said there are people on the right of Ar-Rahmaan who are neither prophets nor martyrs, whose faces shine, who gather for Allaah's dhikr and choose the best words as one chooses the best dates.

n03557.summary: Anas bin Maalik reports that the Prophet came upon Companions discussing their former ignorance and how Allaah guided them, and praised them, telling them to continue as they were.

n03558.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas says to speak often of Umar bin Khattaab, since speaking of him is speaking of justice and speaking of justice is speaking of Allaah.

n03559.summary: Aa'isha says to adorn gatherings with sending salutations upon the Prophet and with speaking of Umar bin Khattaab.

n03560.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas relates that when asked who the friends of Allaah are, the Prophet said they are the people whose sight reminds you of Allaah.

n03561.summary: Handhala, a scribe of the Prophet, reports that he felt himself a hypocrite when his heart's state from the Prophet's gatherings faded at home with his family, and the Prophet told him that if he stayed as he was in his company the angels would shake hands with him, with a second version adding Abu Hurayrah's similar complaint.

n03562.summary: Urwa bin Zubayr relates that when he proposed to Abdullaah bin Umar's daughter during Tawaaf, Ibn Umar stayed silent because they were remembering Allaah, and later in Madinah accepted the proposal and married him to her.

n03563.summary: Aa'isha relates that the Prophet said prayer after brushing the teeth with a miswaak is seventy times better than without it, and that silent dhikr is seventy times better than audible dhikr and will be rewarded by Allaah on the Day of Qiyaamah.

n03564.summary: Jaabir relates that at Baqee the Prophet asked for a body to be lifted from its grave and handed to him, and they found it was the man who used to raise his voice in dhikr.

n03565.summary: Muhammad bin Ibraaheem Taymi relates the story of Abdullaah Dhul Bijaadayn, an orphan who after accepting Islaam was stripped of his uncle's goods, was told by the Prophet to stay at his door, and was buried at Tabook by Abu Bakr and Umar while the Prophet prayed for his pleasure.

n03566.summary: Uqba bin Aamir reports that the Prophet said of Abdullaah Dhul Bijaadayn that he is one who sighs deeply, because he remembered Allaah aloud through Qur'aan and du'aa.

n03567.summary: Safiyya relates that the Prophet came to her while she was counting her tasbeehaat with four thousand date seeds and taught her to glorify Allaah as much as all of His creation.

n03568.summary: Another narration gives the dhikr as 'as much as everything He has created', and reports that Abu Safiyya, Abu Hurayrah and Sa'd counted their tasbeeh with stones or a knotted string.

n03569.summary: Abu Nadhra relays an old man's account of being Abu Hurayrah's guest in Madinah, where he saw him count his tasbeeh with stones or date seeds while his slave woman refilled the bag for him, and was struck by his care for guests.

n03570.summary: Hakeem bin Daylami reports that Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas used stones to count his tasbeeh.

n03571.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar advises making dhikr only in a state of purity, and Abu Hurayrah relates that the Prophet said Allaah multiplies the reward of a good deed to a very great number, citing Qur'aan 4:40.

n03572.summary: Mu'aadh bin Jabal relates that the Prophet corrected several people's du'aas: he told one who asked for patience to ask for safety, explained that the perfect bounty is Jannah and rescue from Jahannam, and said that the du'aa of one who called on Dhul Jalaali wal Ikraam had been accepted.

n03573.summary: Anas bin Maalik relates that the Prophet visited a very weak man who had asked Allaah to bring his punishment forward, taught him the Qur'aanic du'aa for good in this world and the Hereafter, and the man was cured.

n03574.summary: Basheer bin Khasaasiyah relates that the Prophet thanked Allaah for guiding him to Islaam, and that when Basheer asked him to pray that he die before him, the Prophet refused to make that du'aa for anyone.

n03575.summary: Ubay bin Ka'b says the Prophet always began his du'aa for anyone with himself, and remarked that Moosa would have seen stranger things had he been more patient with his companion.

n03576.summary: Abu Ayyoob Ansaari reports that the Prophet always began his du'aa with himself, and Aa'isha told Ibn Abu Saa'ib, a lecturer in Madinah, not to contrive rhymed du'aas since the Prophet and Companions did not.

n03577.summary: Umar corrects a man who prays for protection from trials by asking whether he wants his Lord to withhold family and wealth from him, and Muhaarib bin Dithaar reports his uncle's account of Ibn Mas'ood's pre-dawn du'aa for forgiveness, which Ibn Mas'ood linked to Ya'qoob's pre-dawn du'aa for his sons.

n03578.summary: Umar relates that whenever the Prophet made du'aa he raised his hands and passed them over his face on finishing.

n03579.summary: Another narration says the Prophet would not lower his hands from a du'aa until he had passed them over his face on completing it.

n03580.summary: Umar says he saw the Prophet make du'aa at Ahjaaruz Zayt with his palms towards his face and pass them over his face afterwards, and Aa'isha says he raised his hands for so long in du'aa that she grew tired.

n03582.summary: Rasulullaah ﷺ made du'aa asking Allaah not to punish him for any verbal abuse or hurt he had caused a Mu'min, saying he is only a human.

n03583.summary: Rasulullaah ﷺ raised his hands and cursed the coalition of armies that had destroyed a Bedouin tribe's settlement, and Abdullaah bin Umar and Abdullaah bin Zubayr were seen wiping their faces after du'aa.

n03584.summary: Zaid bin Thaabit tells a man to go to Abu Hurayrah, because Rasulullaah ﷺ said Aameen to his du'aa and Abu Hurayrah's, and Abu Hurayrah's request for knowledge he would never forget was granted first.

n03585.summary: Umar asked the people to say Aameen to three du'aas he made, asking Allaah to strengthen his weakness, soften his sternness and make him generous.

n03586.summary: In the Year of Ashes, Saa'ib bin Yazeed saw Umar weeping and seeking forgiveness in du'aa, then asking Allaah to accept the intercession of the Prophet's uncle Abbaas, who wept as he prayed beside him.

n03587.summary: Abu Sa'eed, a freed slave of Usayd, recounts how Umar patrolled the masjid at night, sat with a group making Dhikr and du'aa, and asked each to pray in turn, weeping himself when it came to Abu Sa'eed.

n03588.summary: Abu Hurayrah reports that Habeeb bin Maslamah, whose du'aas were always accepted, asked his army to say Aameen and prayed for protection of their blood and the reward of martyrs while facing the Roman army.

n03589.summary: Uqba bin Aamir reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ said Abdullaah Dhul Bijaadayn sighs very deeply, because he made Dhikr and du'aa aloud, reciting the Qur'aan.

n03590.summary: Umar asked Rasulullaah ﷺ for permission to perform Umrah and was asked not to forget them in his du'aas; Abu Umaama reports the comprehensive du'aa Rasulullaah ﷺ made for the people when they wished for more.

n03592.summary: Talha reports a Companion who, while rolling in hot sand and chiding his nafs, was told by Rasulullaah ﷺ to ask his brothers to include them in their du'aas; Buraydah reports the same incident and the du'aa that followed.

n03593.summary: Aseer bin Jaabir reports that Umar asked Uwais Qarni to pray for his forgiveness, citing the Prophet's words that the best of the Taabi'een is a man called Uwais, and that whoever meets him should ask for his du'aa.

n03595.summary: Abdullaah bin Roomi reports that when people from Basrah asked Anas bin Maalik for du'aa, he prayed for forgiveness, mercy, the best of this world and the Aakhirah, and salvation from Jahannam.

n03596.summary: Yazeed bin Asam reports that when a fierce warrior from Shaam took to drink, Umar wrote him a letter reminding him of Allaah's forgiveness and punishment, and asked the people to pray that the man's heart turn to Allaah.

n03597.summary: The man stopped drinking after reading Umar's letter, and Umar told the people to correct a brother who slips, encourage him, pray for his forgiveness, and not help Shaytaan against him.

n03598.summary: A fragment in which someone is said to have called on Allaah by His Ismul A'zam, too damaged by OCR to say more.

n03599.summary: Buraydah reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ overheard a Companion's du'aa that called on Allaah's Oneness and His Ismul A'zam, and told him he had asked by the name through which requests are granted.

n03600.summary: Mu'aadh bin Jabal reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ overheard a Companion making du'aa and told him that his du'aa had been accepted, so he should ask for what he wants.

n03601.summary: Anas bin Maalik reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ passed Abu Ayaash Zaid bin Saamit Zuraqi while he prayed, praising Allaah and calling on Him by His Ismul A'zam, and told him that with this name any du'aa is accepted.

n03603.summary: Anas bin Maalik reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ gave gold to a Bedouin who praised Allaah beautifully in salaah, and explained that he gave it for the manner of his praise rather than for family ties.

n03604.summary: Aa'isha reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ made du'aa using Allaah's most beloved name, refused to teach her the Ismul A'zam, and she then made du'aa calling on Allaah by His names.

n03606.summary: Fudhaala bin Ubayd reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ told a man who prayed and made du'aa too hastily to first praise Allaah and send salutations on him, and a later Companion who did so had his du'aa accepted.

n03607.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood advises that anyone making du'aa should begin by praising Allaah and sending salutations on the Prophet before asking for his need.

n03608.summary: Abbaas bin Mirdaas reports that at Arafaat Rasulullaah ﷺ prayed at length for his Ummah, and Allaah forgave all but wrongs between people, forgave those too at Muzdalifah, and Iblees fell to the ground in grief.

n03609.summary: Abdullaah bin Amr reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ recited the words of Ibraheem and Isa, then wept calling for his Ummah, and Allaah sent Jibraeel to tell him that his Ummah would please him.

n03610.summary: Anas bin Maalik reports the Prophet's du'aa that Allaah turn the hearts of his Ummah to obedience, and Aa'isha reports that when she asked for du'aa he prayed for forgiveness of all her sins, which he said he prays for his Ummah in every salaah.

n03611.summary: Anas bin Maalik reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ asked Allaah to include Abu Bakr in his own rank on the Day of Qiyaamah.

n03612.summary: Khabbaab reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ prayed that Islaam be strengthened through whichever of Umar bin Khattaab and Abu Jahal bin Hishaam Allaah loves more.

n03613.summary: Aa'isha and Abdullaah bin Mas'ood each report that Rasulullaah ﷺ prayed for Islaam to be strengthened through Umar.

n03615.summary: Zaid bin Aslam reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ asked Allaah to let Uthmaan pass speedily over the Siraat, Abu Sa'eed Khudri reports the Prophet's thrice-repeated words that he is pleased with Uthmaan, and Abdullaah bin Mas'ood reports a du'aa for the forgiveness of Uthmaan's sins.

n03618.summary: Ali reports that when he had severe pain Rasulullaah ﷺ covered him with his shawl and prayed, and he was cured, and the Prophet said that whatever he asked for himself he had asked for Ali, and that there would be no prophet after him.

n03619.summary: Zaid bin Yuthay, Sa'eed bin Wahab and Amr bin Dhi Murr report that Ali called on those who heard the Prophet at Ghadeer Khum to stand, thirteen Companions testified that they heard him say he is closer to the believers than they are to themselves, and the Prophet then prayed for whoever befriends Ali.

n03620.summary: Ibn Abbaas reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ prayed for Ali to be helped, for others to be helped through him, for mercy on him, and for Allaah to befriend Ali's friends and oppose his enemies.

n03621.summary: Ali reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ prayed that Allaah keep his tongue firm on the truth and guide his heart, and Ibn Abbaas reports a du'aa asking Allaah to guide Ali in passing judgement.

n03623.summary: Abu Bakr reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ prayed for Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas that his arrows travel straight, that his du'aas be accepted, and that Allaah love him.

n03624.summary: Sa'd reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ prayed that his du'aas be accepted, and Zubayr bin Awwaam reports that the Prophet made du'aa for him, his children and his progeny.

n03625.summary: Umm Salamah reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ gathered Faatima, her husband and her two sons under a blanket and prayed that Allaah send mercy and blessings on the family of Muhammad as He did on the family of Ibraheem.

n03626.summary: Abu Ammaar reports that Waathila bin Asqa told him how Rasulullaah ﷺ covered Ali, Faatima, Hasan and Husayn with a blanket and prayed for their purity, and Ali reports the Prophet tying a shawl over them and praying that Allaah be pleased with them.

n03628.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ prayed for Hasan and Husayn, saying that whoever loves them loves him too.

n03629.summary: Abu Hurayrah and other narrators report that the Prophet ﷺ made du'aa for Hasan and Husayn, asking Allaah to love them and those who love them.

n03633.summary: Ibn Abbaas reports that the Prophet ﷺ prayed for forgiveness of the open and secret sins of Abbaas and his children, and that Allaah be their guardian after his death.

n03634.summary: Abu Hurayrah reports that the Prophet ﷺ prayed for forgiveness of Abbaas's sins, both public and private, and of any sins he or his descendants might commit until the Day of Qiyaamah.

n03635.summary: Aasim reports the Prophet ﷺ's words about Abbaas, Abu Usayd Saa'idi describes the Prophet gathering Abbaas and his household under his shawl to pray for them, and Ibn Abbaas is prayed for deep understanding of the Deen.

n03637.summary: A variant wording of the Prophet's du'aa asks Allaah to teach him the Qur'aan and grant him deep understanding of the Deen, and another wording asks for wisdom and the interpretation of the Qur'aan.

n03639.summary: Abdullaah bin Ja'far reports that the Prophet ﷺ prayed that Allaah be the successor to Ja'far in caring for his children.

n03640.summary: Another report gives the Prophet ﷺ's du'aa that Allaah care for Ja'far's family and bless his son Abdullaah in trade, repeated three times.

n03641.summary: Sha'bi reports that after Ja'far was martyred at Balqaa in the Battle of Mu'ta, the Prophet ﷺ prayed that Allaah be a better successor to Ja'far's family than to any of His righteous servants.

n03642.summary: Abu Maysara reports that on hearing of the martyrdom of Zaid bin Haaritha, Ja'far and Abdullaah bin Rawaaha, the Prophet ﷺ spoke of them and prayed for their forgiveness.

n03643.summary: Uthmaan bin Affaan reports that the Prophet ﷺ prayed that Allaah forgive the family of Yaasir.

n03644.summary: Aa'isha reports a du'aa for Ammaar bin Yaasir, and Umm Salamah reports the Prophet ﷺ's du'aa for the forgiveness of Abu Salamah, the raising of his rank, Allaah being his successor among those left behind, and his grave being filled with light.

n03645.summary: Usaama bin Zaid says the Prophet ﷺ placed him and Hasan bin Ali on his thighs, embraced them, and prayed that Allaah show mercy and love to both of them.

n03646.summary: Usaama bin Zaid relates that when the Prophet's illness grew severe and he could no longer speak, the Prophet repeatedly placed his hand on him and lifted it, and Usaama understood that the Prophet was making du'aa for him.

n03647.summary: Jaabir reports the Prophet ﷺ prayed for Amr bin al-Aas's forgiveness because he always gave charity when asked; Hakeem bin Hizaam reports a du'aa for blessing in his trade; Jareer reports the Prophet ﷺ prayed that he would sit steady on a horse, and he never fell off again.

n03651.summary: Nadhla bin Amr al-Ghifaari reports that the Prophet ﷺ renamed a man of the Ghifaar tribe from 'Muhaan' to 'Mukrim', and that when he led the janazah of Baraa bin Ma'roor he prayed for Allaah's special mercy and for Baraa's entry into Jannah.

n03652.summary: Ibn Abu Qataadah reports that when the Prophet ﷺ led the janazah of Baraa bin Ma'roor on arrival in Madinah, he prayed for Allaah's forgiveness, mercy and pleasure with him.

n03653.summary: Qais bin Sa'd reports that the Prophet ﷺ prayed that Allaah shower His special mercy on the family of Sa'd bin Ubaadah and forgive them.

n03654.summary: Abu Qataadah relates that on a journey he held up the Prophet ﷺ when he leaned from exhaustion on his animal, and the Prophet prayed that Allaah look after Abu Qataadah as he had looked after him.

n03655.summary: Anas bin Maalik reports that when Umm Sulaym asked the Prophet ﷺ to pray for him, the Prophet prayed that Allaah grant him plenty of wealth and children and bless him in them.

n03656.summary: Abu Dardaa reports that a man named Harmala said his faith was on his tongue while hypocrisy lurked in his heart, and the Prophet ﷺ prayed for him to have a tongue that makes dhikr, a grateful heart and a good ending to his affairs.

n03657.summary: Talib reports that when he asked the Prophet ﷺ to pray for him, the Prophet waited for permission and then prayed three times for Allaah's forgiveness and mercy on him.

n03658.summary: Abu Moosa reports that the Prophet ﷺ prayed that Allaah elevate his little servant Abu Aamir above most people on the Day of Qiyaamah; Hassaan bin Shaddaad reports that his mother brought him to the Prophet for a du'aa that he become big and good, and the Prophet prayed for her and the child.

n03659.summary: Abu Hurayrah reports that the Prophet ﷺ prayed in salaah for Salamah bin Hishaam, Ayaash bin Abu Rabee'ah, Waleed bin Waleed and other oppressed Muslims in Makkah to be rescued, and cursed the Mudhar tribe with drought.

n03661.summary: Qaz'ah reports that Abdullaah bin Umar, bidding him farewell, recited the Prophet ﷺ's words placing his Deen, his trustworthiness and the results of his deeds in Allaah's custody.

n03662.summary: Another narration says that Abdullaah bin Umar would call anyone setting out on a journey close to him and recite that same farewell du'aa.

n03663.summary: Anas reports that a Companion asked the Prophet ﷺ for a provision of du'aa before a journey, and the Prophet prayed that Allaah make Taqwa his provision, forgive his sins and make good easy for him wherever he went.

n03664.summary: Qataadah Rahaawi says that the Prophet ﷺ appointed him leader of his people and bade him farewell; Abu Hurayrah reports that the Prophet ﷺ advised a man to keep Taqwa and say Allaahu Akbar when climbing a slope, and prayed that his journey be shortened and made easy.

n03665.summary: Abu Umaamah reports that when the Prophet ﷺ finished eating and lifted the tablecloth, he would praise Allaah with abundant, pure and blessed praise.

n03666.summary: Abu Sa'eed Khudri reports that whenever the Prophet ﷺ ate or drank, he praised Allaah for providing food and drink and for making him one of the Muslims.

n03667.summary: Abu Sa'eed Khudri reports that whenever the Prophet ﷺ wore a new garment he named it and recited a du'aa praising Allaah and asking for the good of the garment and protection from its evil.

n03668.summary: Talha reports that when the Prophet ﷺ sighted the new moon he asked Allaah to let it rise over them with good fortune, Imaan, safety and Islaam.

n03669.summary: Ibn Umar quotes a different wording of the new moon du'aa, asking Allaah to let the moon rise over them with peace, security, serenity and Islaam.

n03670.summary: Raafi bin Khadeej reports that when the Prophet ﷺ saw the new moon he called it the moon of good and virtue, and recited a du'aa three times for the good of that month and protection from its evil.

n03671.summary: Ibn Umar reports that when the Prophet ﷺ heard thunderclaps he asked Allaah not to let His wrath kill them or His punishment destroy them, but to grant them safety before that.

n03672.summary: Aa'isha reports that whenever the wind blew violently the Prophet ﷺ asked Allaah for its good, the good in it and the good it was sent for, and sought protection from its evil.

n03673.summary: Aa'isha reports that when the Prophet ﷺ noticed a cloud forming on the horizon he would leave what he was doing, even shorten his salaah, seek protection from its evil, and ask Allaah for a pleasant downpour if it rained.

n03674.summary: Aa'isha reports that when the Prophet ﷺ noticed a dense cloud he would leave what he was doing, even salaah, seek Allaah's protection from the punishment it was sent with, and ask for a beneficial downpour if it rained.

n03675.summary: Salama bin Akwa reports that when the wind blew fiercely the Prophet ﷺ asked Allaah to make it a fruitful wind and not a destructive one.

n03676.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood reports that the Prophet ﷺ used to ask Allaah for guidance, Taqwa, chastity and independence.

n03677.summary: Abu Moosa Ash'ari reports one of the Prophet's ﷺ frequent du'aas asking Allaah to forgive his sins, known and unknown.

n03678.summary: Three Companions each report a du'aa the Prophet ﷺ made: Abu Hurayrah on setting right the affairs of the Deen and the Aakhirah, Ibn Abbaas on submission and trust in Allaah, and Umm Salamah on steadfastness in the Deen.

n03679.summary: Two Companions report du'aas of the Prophet ﷺ: Aa'isha on well-being in body and sight, and Ibn Abbaas asking for help, guidance and a steadfast heart.

n03680.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood reports a du'aa of the Prophet ﷺ asking for Allaah's mercy, forgiveness, safety from sin, Jannah and protection from Jahannam.

n03681.summary: Three narrators report du'aas of the Prophet ﷺ asking forgiveness for sins committed in jest, earnestness, error or intent, and asking Allaah to make his character beautiful.

n03682.summary: Umm Salamah reports the Prophet ﷺ asking Allaah to forgive him, have mercy on him and guide him to the most upright path.

n03683.summary: Anas bin Maalik reports the Prophet ﷺ asking Allaah to keep him steadfast on Islaam until he meets Him.

n03684.summary: Busr bin Abi Artaat reports hearing the Prophet ﷺ ask Allaah to conclude all affairs well and to save from disgrace in this world and punishment in the Aakhirah.

n03685.summary: The Prophet ﷺ said that whoever recites the preceding du'aa will die before being put through tribulations.

n03686.summary: Abu Sirma reports the Prophet ﷺ asking Allaah to grant independence to him and to those associated with him.

n03687.summary: Thowbaan reports the Prophet ﷺ asking Allaah for what is lawful, for resolve to avoid evil, for love of the poor, for acceptance of repentance, and to be taken before any trial.

n03688.summary: Aa'isha reports a du'aa of the Prophet ﷺ asking Allaah to give the greatest share of provision in his old age and in the period just before death.

n03689.summary: Aa'isha reports that the Prophet ﷺ loved comprehensive du'aas and preferred them to any other kind.

n03690.summary: While Aa'isha was praying, the Prophet ﷺ told her to make comprehensive du'aas, and afterwards taught her a du'aa asking for all good and protection from all evil in this world and the next.

n03691.summary: In another narration of the same event, Aa'isha describes how the Prophet ﷺ asked her to make a concise and comprehensive du'aa and then taught her one.

n03692.summary: Abu Umaama reports that the Prophet ﷺ taught the Companions one comprehensive du'aa that covers all the du'aas he had been making, asking for all good he asked for and protection from all he sought protection from.

n03693.summary: Anas reports the Prophet ﷺ asking Allaah for protection from helplessness, laziness, cowardice, old age, miserliness, punishment in the grave and the trials of life and death, and another narration adds protection from debt and oppression.

n03694.summary: Aa'isha reports that the Prophet ﷺ included in his du'aa a request for protection from the evil of what he did and of what he did not do.

n03695.summary: Three narrators report du'aas of the Prophet ﷺ: Abdullaah bin Umar on protection from losing blessings and from Allaah's wrath; Zaid bin Arqam teaching a du'aa for protection from helplessness, grave punishment and useless knowledge, asking Allaah to grant taqwa to the self; and Aa'isha on protection from the trial of Jahannam and the evils of wealth and poverty.

n03696.summary: Qutba bin Maalik reports the Prophet ﷺ asking Allaah for protection from evil character, actions and desires.

n03697.summary: Anas reports the Prophet ﷺ asking Allaah for protection from leprosy, insanity and all debilitating diseases.

n03698.summary: Abu Yasar reports the Prophet ﷺ asking Allaah for protection from being crushed, falling, drowning, burning, extreme old age, Shaytaan's madness at death, dying while fleeing a battle, and dying from a poisonous bite.

n03699.summary: Abu Hurayrah reports the Prophet ﷺ asking Allaah for protection from starvation, the worst companion, and from treachery, the worst confidant.

n03700.summary: The Prophet ﷺ used to ask Allaah for protection from disputes, hypocrisy and bad character.

n03701.summary: Several narrations of the Prophet's ﷺ du'aas: Anas on protection from helplessness, poverty, sinfulness, hypocrisy, deafness, insanity and leprosy; Uqba bin Aamir on protection from a terrible day, night, companion and neighbour; Umar on protection from miserliness, cowardice and punishment in the grave; and Umar on a protective du'aa for Hasan and Husayn.

n03703.summary: Abu Tayyaah asks Abdur Rahmaan, who met the Prophet ﷺ, what happened the night the jinn plotted against him; he describes how Jibra'eel taught the Prophet ﷺ a protective du'aa and the jinn's flame was put out.

n03704.summary: Ubay bin Ka'b reports that a Bedouin came to the Prophet ﷺ about his brother afflicted by jinn, and the Prophet ﷺ recited protective verses and surahs over him, after which the man was cured.

n03705.summary: Abu Umaama reports that Khaalid bin Waleed told the Prophet ﷺ about frightening dreams that kept him from night prayer, and the Prophet ﷺ taught him a du'aa to recite to dispel them.

n03706.summary: Abdullaah bin Amr taught the du'aa for dreams that frighten a person to children old enough to learn it, and wrote it on paper tied around the necks of younger ones. Khaalid bin Waleed, who often woke frightened, was told by the Prophet to recite Bismillaah and the du'aa on waking. Waleed bin Waleed, who often felt fearful, was told to recite it on going to bed.

n03709.summary: Ali says the Prophet instructed him to recite a du'aa whenever he faced difficulty, praising Allaah as the Most Forbearing and Most Magnanimous, the Lord of the Glorious Throne and the Lord of the universe.

n03710.summary: Anas reports that whenever the Prophet ﷺ faced difficulty he would say that he sought help through Allaah's mercy, the Ever Living and Controller.

n03711.summary: Asmaa bint Umays reports that whenever the Prophet ﷺ was troubled or faced difficulty he would say that Allaah is his Rabb and he would not associate any partner with Him.

n03712.summary: In another narration, Asmaa says the Prophet ﷺ taught her the above du'aa to say when in difficulty.

n03713.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas reports that the Prophet ﷺ, holding the door-frame, told those in the room, the family of Abdul Muttalib, to say that Allaah is their Rabb and they would not associate any partner with Him when they face difficulties.

n03714.summary: A variant of the previous narration gives the words as 'Allaah! Allaah has no partner'.

n03715.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas reports the du'aa the Prophet ﷺ recited in times of difficulty, affirming that there is none worthy of worship but Allaah, the Rabb of the Throne, the heavens and the earth.

n03716.summary: Thowbaan reports that whenever something alarmed the Prophet ﷺ he would say that Allaah is his Rabb and he would not associate any partner with Him.

n03717.summary: Abu Dardaa says that reciting a particular du'aa seven times will relieve all worries, and Ibn Abbaas recited another du'aa for any anxiety or fear of a ruler, asking Allaah on the strength of his belief in Him.

n03718.summary: Ali reports that the Prophet ﷺ taught him a du'aa to recite before a tyrannical ruler; Abu Raafi reports that Abdullaah bin Ja'far advised his daughter to recite a du'aa when Hajjaaj came to her, and she was protected from him.

n03720.summary: Ibn Abbaas teaches that when a person faces a fearsome ruler who may oppress him, he should recite a du'aa three times seeking Allaah's protection from the ruler, his army and his partisans among jinn and mankind.

n03721.summary: Ibn Mas'ood teaches that a person who fears a tyrannical ruler should recite a du'aa seeking protection from him, his armies and partisans among jinn and mankind; in another version the tyrant's name is said as well, and Ibn Mas'ood says the tyrant will then be unable to harm him.

n03723.summary: The Prophet ﷺ's first sermon in Madinah urged people to send good deeds ahead for the Aakhirah, and he gave a second sermon praising the Qur'aan and calling to the worship of Allah alone.

n03724.summary: Sa'eed bin Abdur Rahmaan Jumhi reports the Prophet's sermon at the first Jumu'ah in Madinah, calling people to taqwa, the Aakhirah and the worship of Allah alone.

n03725.summary: Hiraar reports the Prophet's address before a battle, reminding the Sahabah of the reward of the one who is martyred in the path of Allah.

n03726.summary: Jaabir reports that at Hijr on the Tabook expedition the Prophet warned the Sahabah not to ask for miracles, recounting how the people of Saalih were destroyed, and named the one man who was saved.

n03727.summary: Hasan bin Ali reports the Prophet's sermon on the Tabook expedition, telling people to seek a moderate livelihood and to look for sustenance through obedience to Allah.

n03728.summary: Abdullaah bin Amr reports the Prophet's address after the conquest of Makkah, condemning unlawful killing, rejecting claims to a child that is not one's own, and giving rulings on adultery, prayer times and marrying an aunt and niece together.

n03729.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports the Prophet's address at the conquest of Makkah, setting the blood money for manslaughter and abolishing the killings and pride of the Period of Ignorance.

n03730.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports the Prophet's address from his camel during the conquest of Makkah, teaching that taqwa, not lineage or pride, is what makes a person honoured before Allah.

n03731.summary: Salmaan reports the Prophet's sermon on the last day of Sha'baan about the coming of Ramadhaan, its virtues, the reward for feeding a fasting person, and the four things to be done abundantly in it.

n03732.summary: Anas reports that as Ramadhaan drew near, the Prophet ﷺ told people that on its first night every believer of the Qiblah is forgiven.

n03733.summary: Ali reports the Prophet's first-night Ramadhaan sermon that the Shayaateen are restrained and du'aas are accepted, and then reports that the Prophet ﷺ devoted the last ten nights of Ramadhaan to worship and seclusion.

n03735.summary: Jaabir bin Abdullaah reports the Prophet's warning that whoever lives one, two or three miles from Madinah and misses Jumu'ah will have his heart sealed.

n03736.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas reports the Prophet's Farewell Hajj address: Shaytaan has despaired of being worshipped in the land but still works through lesser sins, the Book and Sunnah are left behind, Muslims are brothers, and they must not kill one another.

n03737.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas reports the Prophet's sermon at Masjidul Khayf in Mina: whoever makes the Aakhirah his main concern will have his affairs set right and be made self-sufficient, while whoever makes this world his main concern will be scattered and poor.

n03738.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports the Prophet's Mina sermon on three things a Muslim's heart never betrays, and Jaabir reports the Prophet's Farewell Hajj address on the sanctity of life and wealth, the abolition of Period of Ignorance debts and blood money, and the rights of women.

n03739.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas reports the Prophet's sermon on the day of Nahr, establishing the sanctity of the day, city and month, and charging those present to convey it to the absent and not to kill one another after him.

n03740.summary: Jareer reports that at the Farewell Hajj, after asking for silence, the Prophet warned the people not to become disbelievers after him by killing one another.

n03741.summary: Ummul Husayn reports seeing Usaamah and Bilaal with the Prophet ﷺ at the Farewell Hajj and hearing him tell the people to obey a leader who rules by the Book of Allaah; Abu Umaamah reports his further rulings on bequests, adultery, lending, debts, guarantees and a wife's spending.

n03742.summary: Abu Umaamah reports the Prophet's call from his camel to worship the Rabb, offer the five daily salaahs, fast Ramadhaan, obey the leader and so enter the Jannah of the Rabb.

n03743.summary: Abdur Rahmaan Taymi reports the Prophet teaching the rites of Hajj at Mina and placing the Muhaajireen and the Ansaar in separate camps, and Raafi bin Amr Muzani reports seeing him preach on a mule while Ali repeated his words.

n03746.summary: Jaabir bin Abdullaah reports the Prophet's farewell sermon in the days of Tashreeq, saying no Arab is superior to a non-Arab, nor a white person to a black person, except by taqwa.

n03747.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood reports the Prophet's address at Arafaat on the sanctity of the day, month and city, his going ahead to the pond, and his warning about innovations introduced after him.

n03748.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports that during the Farewell Hajj the Prophet ﷺ spoke at length about Maseeh Dajjaal, noting that every Prophet including Nooh warned his people of him, and that the Rabb is not one-eyed.

n03749.summary: Safeenah reports the Prophet's description of Maseeh Dajjaal: his missing left eye, the word Kaafir between his eyes, his deceptive Jannah and Jahannam, and his destruction at Afeeq in Shaam.

n03750.summary: Junaadah bin Abu Umayyah Azdi reports a Companion's narration of the Prophet's warning about Maseeh Dajjaal, describing his signs, his power to bring rain and his inability to enter the four Masaajid.

n03751.summary: Abu Umaamah Baahili reports the Prophet's long sermon on Maseeh Dajjaal: his trials, his forty days on earth, and how believers should estimate the prayer times in those short days.

n03752.summary: Jaabir reports the Prophet's sermon on the spy sent to investigate Maseeh Dajjaal and his statement that Maseeh Dajjaal cannot enter Madinah or Makkah, which are guarded by angels.

n03753.summary: Tha'laba bin Abbaad reports Samurah bin Jundub's account of the eclipse sermon, in which the Prophet ﷺ said eclipses are signs for people to repent, and warned that Qiyaamah comes after thirty liars and the one-eyed Maseeh Dajjaal.

n03754.summary: Another report has the Prophet say that whoever holds fast to Allaah, saying 'Allaah is my Rabb, Ever Living, who never dies', will suffer no punishment, while whoever tells the Dajjaal 'You are my Rabb' will be punished.

n03755.summary: Abu Bakrah says that people had been talking a lot about Musaylama before the Prophet spoke about him. The Prophet said Musaylama was one of thirty great liars who would appear before the Last Day, and that the awe of the Dajjaal would sweep up every town.

n03756.summary: Another report adds that the Prophet said the awe would not enter Madinah, which has two angels at each of its entrances repelling it.

n03757.summary: Khaalid bin Abdullaah bin Harmala reports from his aunt that the Prophet, with his head bandaged after a scorpion bite, said that fighting would continue until Ya'jooj and Ma'jooj emerge, with broad faces, tiny eyes, reddish hair, scrambling down every hill.

n03758.summary: Baqeera, wife of Qa'qaa, reports the Prophet's warning that when the earth is heard to sink in the west, Qiyaamah has arrived.

n03759.summary: Baraa reports the Prophet's loud lecture condemning backbiting and the searching out of Muslims' faults, warning that Allah exposes the faults of one who searches for them.

n03760.summary: Another narration adds the Prophet's words that one should not harm the Mu'mineen or search out their faults, because Allah exposes the faults of one who searches for his brother's faults.

n03761.summary: Aa'isha reports the Prophet's sermon on enjoining good and forbidding evil, warning that prayers and requests will go unanswered if this duty is neglected.

n03762.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports the Prophet's warning against oppression, lewdness and greed, followed by his answers on the best act of Islaam and the best Hijrah, and a further command about keeping trusts.

n03763.summary: Ayman bin Khuraym reports the Prophet's warning that false testimony is equated with shirk, Anas bin Maalik reports his warning against interest, and Abu Moosa Ash'ari reports his warning against the subtle shirk.
