n03765.summary: Nu'maan bin Basheer reports the Prophet's saying that ingratitude for little leads to ingratitude for much and that unity is a mercy while disunity is a punishment; Abu Umaamah Baahili then advises sticking to the larger group.

n03766.summary: Abu Dharr reports the Prophet's recitation of the Surah Saba verse about Dawood's thankfulness, and his teaching that fearing Allah in private and public, being just in anger and contentment, and spending moderately in poverty and wealth are gifts given to Dawood.

n03767.summary: Ali reports the Prophet's lecture that the only good in life lies with the listener and the truthful scholar, and his praise of the Qur'aan in reply to Miqdaad bin Amr's question about the period of truce.

n03768.summary: Husayn bin Ali reports the Prophet's lecture on abstinence from the world, reminding people of death and giving glad tidings to those who avoid searching for faults, earn purely, give Sadaqah from their excess and keep to the Sunnah.

n03769.summary: Anas and Aaisha report the Prophet's counsel to follow the Sunnah without innovation, to be shy before Allaah, and to remember death and leave the pleasures of this world.

n03770.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas reports the Prophet's lecture that people will be resurrected barefoot and uncircumcised, with Ibraheem clothed first and some of his Ummah taken to the left for their innovations.

n03771.summary: Ali reports the Prophet's lecture that the register of who is destined for Jannah or Jahannam is already fixed, and that actions are judged by how they end.

n03772.summary: Abu Sa'eed Khudri reports the Prophet saying that his kin are attached to him in both worlds, but that people who introduced innovations and turned back will be turned away from his pond of Kowthar on the Day of Qiyaamah.

n03773.summary: Abu Sa'eed Khudri and Abu Humayd Saa'idi report the Prophet's warnings to rulers and collectors: obey what is good, and do not keep gifts from office, since embezzled property will be carried on the Day of Qiyaamah.

n03774.summary: Abu Qataadah and Ka'b bin Maalik report the Prophet's words that the Ansaar are his inner garments and must be honoured, and his instruction to the Muhaajireen to honour the righteous Ansaar and overlook the sinful among them.

n03775.summary: Ka'b bin Maalik reports the Prophet's last sermon, in which he asked forgiveness for the martyrs of Uhud and advised the Muhaajireen to honour the honourable Ansaar and overlook the sinful among them.

n03776.summary: Abu Bakr reports the Prophet urging people to save themselves from Jahannam even with a piece of a date given in charity, because sadaqah straightens crookedness and repels a bad death.

n03777.summary: Aamir bin Rabee'ah reports the Prophet saying that the angels keep praying for forgiveness for as long as a person keeps sending salutations on him.

n03778.summary: Abdullaah bin Amr, Anas, Abu Sa'eed Khudri and Abu Hurayrah report the Prophet's lectures on Jannah and Jahannam, including his wish that people would weep more if they knew what he knew, and his counsel to think well of Allaah.

n03780.summary: Abu Zuhayr Thaqafi reports the Prophet saying that people will be told apart by the praise and criticism they receive after death, and Tha'laba reports his instruction to give a saa of dates or barley as Sadaqatul Fitr for every person.

n03782.summary: Uqba bin Aamir reports that after the Muslims slept past Fajr near Tabook, the Prophet led the qadhaa salaah and gave a long lecture on the best speech, guidance and dangers of sin, while Bilaal said the same sleep had overtaken him.

n03783.summary: Ayaadh bin Himaar reports the Prophet's lecture quoting Allaah: the Shayaateen led people into shirk, the Prophet was commissioned to call the Quraysh, and the traits of the people of Jannah and Jahannam are described.

n03784.summary: Abu Sa'eed Khudri reports the Prophet's comprehensive lecture after Asr, warning against the world and women, describing how people's faith at birth and at death differs, urging control of anger, honest settlement of debts, and speaking the truth to a tyrant.

n03785.summary: Saa'ib bin Mahjaan reports that Umar, while in Shaam, repeated a lecture of the Prophet on staying united, avoiding seclusion with a non-mahram woman, the signs of a believer and a hypocrite, moderation in seeking livelihood, and qadr.

n03786.summary: Mu'aawiya bin Abu Sufyaan reports the Prophet's final sermon, in which a servant was given the choice between this world and what is with Allaah, and that Abu Bakr alone understood and wept, so the Prophet praised him and asked that only his door stay open to the Masjid.

n03787.summary: Ayyoob bin Basheer reports the same final sermon, beginning with prayers for the martyrs of Uhud, and that only Abu Bakr understood it and wept.

n03788.summary: Abu Sa'eed Khudri reports that Abu Bakr alone wept at the Prophet's final sermon and was praised as the one who did him the most favours, and Abdullaah bin Abbaas reports the Prophet's advice about the Ansaar from the same sermon.

n03790.summary: Ka'b bin Maalik reports the Prophet's last sermon, in which he asked forgiveness for the martyrs of Uhud and advised the Muhaajireen to honour the honourable Ansaar and overlook the sinful among them.

n03792.summary: Abu Salmah bin Abdur Rahmaan reports, from Abu Hurayrah and Abdullaah bin Abbaas, the Prophet's final sermon: whoever guards the five fardh salaahs in congregation will cross the Siraat first and receive the reward of a thousand martyrs for each day and night he guarded them.

n03793.summary: Abu Zaid Ansaari reports that the Prophet led them in prayer and then lectured them from Fajr until Maghrib, telling them everything that was still to happen.

n03794.summary: Jaabir reports the Prophet's manner while lecturing, his eyes reddening and voice rising, his words that the Hour is as near as his two fingers, that the best guidance is Muhammad's and every bid'ah misleads, and that the debts and children left behind are his responsibility.

n03795.summary: Urwa reports Abu Bakr's first address as Khalifah: he is not the best of them, the Qur'aan and the Prophet's ways are settled, the strong and the weak must each have their rights restored, and he asks to be assisted when right and corrected when wrong.

n03796.summary: Abdullaah bin Ukaym reports Abu Bakr's first address as Khalifah, with variant versions recorded by Hasan, in which he says he is not the best of them, asks to be watched over, and says a Shaytaan comes to him.

n03798.summary: Qais bin Abi Haazim and Aasim bin Adi report Abu Bakr's later addresses, in which he asks to be corrected if he strays, sends Usaamah's army forward, and urges people to do good before their lives end.

n03799.summary: Sa'eed bin Abu Maryam reports Abu Bakr's address on becoming Khalifah: he would rather the burden had fallen on someone he detested, kings are the most ill-fated, and only the poor will be forgiven.

n03800.summary: Abdullaah bin Ukaym reports the Prophet's lecture urging taqwa, hope and fear of Allaah, quoting the praise of Zakariyya's family in the Qur'aan, and telling people to compete in good deeds before their lives end.

n03801.summary: Amr bin Dinaar reports Abu Bakr's counsel in hardship: fear Allaah, be sincere, send good deeds ahead, and reflect on those who have passed and on the kings whose cities are now in ruins.

n03802.summary: Nu'aym bin Namha reports a variant of Abu Bakr's address with additions: speech is good only when it pleases Allaah, wealth is good only when spent in His path, and a person should not fear a critic when carrying out Allaah's command.

n03803.summary: Aasim bin Adi reports Abu Bakr's address on sincerity and on learning from the dead, including that the sins of earlier kings remain theirs while their possessions pass to others.

n03804.summary: Moosa bin Uqba reports the comprehensive address Abu Bakr gave: testimony of faith, taqwa, obedience to leaders who enjoin good, guarding against desires and pride, and sincerity for the sake of the Aakhirah.

n03805.summary: Yazeed bin Haaroon reports Abu Bakr's warning about the ungrateful person who is humiliated on the Day of Qiyaamah for having sent no good deeds ahead, quoting Surah Taubah verse 63.

n03806.summary: Muhammad bin Ibraheem bin Haarith reports Abu Bakr's promise that if people have taqwa and do good, the time will come when they eat bread and butter until they are full.

n03807.summary: Zubayr reports Abu Bakr telling people to be modest before Allaah, saying he always covers his head when he goes out to relieve himself, out of shame before his Rabb.

n03808.summary: Ibn Shihaab reports Abu Bakr's sermon on shame before Allaah, and Abu Bakr himself reports that the Prophet once wept on the pulpit and asked for forgiveness and well-being, the best gift after conviction.

n03809.summary: Aws reports Abu Bakr's sermon quoting the Prophet's advice to ask Allaah for forgiveness and well-being, to hold to truthfulness and avoid lying, to avoid envy and hatred, and to be brothers.

n03810.summary: Abu Bakr bin Muhammad bin Amr bin Hazm reports that Abu Bakr told people the Prophet taught them to seek refuge from hypocritical humility, which is humility of the body with hypocrisy in the heart.

n03811.summary: Abul Aaliya reports Abu Bakr quoting the Prophet: a traveller prays two rak'ahs while a resident prays four, and on his own journey from Dhul Hulayfah towards Makkah he would pray two rak'ahs until he returned to Madinah.

n03812.summary: Abu Dhamra reports Abu Bakr's warning that the Muslims will conquer Shaam and that the masjids there must be built for Allaah's remembrance alone, and Anas reports Abu Bakr explaining how man is created, to remove pride.

n03813.summary: Humayd bin Hilaal reports, from someone present, that after Abu Bakr's burial Umar vowed to settle matters with integrity, to treat well those who behave well, and to punish those who do evil.

n03814.summary: Sha'bi reports Umar's first address as Khalifah, in which he says he will not presume to sit where Abu Bakr sat, urges reciting and practising the Qur'aan, and regards himself as a guardian of public funds in the way a guardian of an orphan is.

n03815.summary: Umar bin Khattaab tells the people in his first sermon as Khalifah to take account of themselves before Allaah takes account of them.

n03816.summary: Abul Firaas reports that Umar told the people he now judges them only by their outward conduct, warned against reciting the Qur'aan for worldly show, and instructed his governors to teach rather than oppress.

n03817.summary: Ibnul Ajfaa reports that Umar warned against inflated dowries and against calling every slain man a martyr, since he may have carried trade goods.

n03818.summary: Masrooq reports that Umar, from the pulpit, asked why dowries were inflated when those of the Prophet and his Companions were modest.

n03819.summary: At Jaabiya, Umar rebukes a priest who denied that Allaah misleads anyone, and explains that the dispute about predestination arose after the people were created and their destinies recorded.

n03820.summary: Abdur Rahmaan bin Abzah reports that Umar threatened to execute any two people he heard disputing predestination, and the dispute only resurfaced in Shaam under Hajjaaj.

n03821.summary: Baahili reports Umar's long lecture at Jaabiya urging people to learn and act on the Qur'aan, to be patient in seeking sustenance, to avoid wine, tyrants and prohibited dealings, and to refrain from abusing or cutting off fellow Muslims.

n03822.summary: Moosa bin Uqba reports Umar's comprehensive Jaabiya lecture on fearing Allaah, the times of salaah, fasting, zakaah, true jihaad and hijrah, and the duties of rulers to their subjects.

n03823.summary: Umar, at Jaabiya, urges people to put their private lives in order, stay with the united body of Muslims, and never be alone with a non-Mahram woman.

n03824.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports Umar's Jaabiya lecture quoting the Prophet on honouring the Sahabah and on unity, and Suwayd bin Ghafala reports Umar's ban on men wearing silk beyond a trivial amount.

n03825.summary: Sayf reports that just before returning to Madinah, Umar told the people in Shaam that he had been just in sharing the booty, camps and borders, and invited them to point out anything else worth doing.

n03826.summary: Urwa bin Zubayr reports Umar's first address as Khalifah on accountability, Taqwa and fair treatment of the people; a second address, from an anonymous transmitter, covers the same ground.

n03827.summary: Umar bin Khattaab tells the people in his first sermon as Khalifah to take account of themselves before Allaah takes account of them.

n03828.summary: Umar warns against greed and miserliness, urges generous sadaqah and earning only halaal wealth, forbids women from wearing sheer Egyptian cloth, and gives advice on buying a camel.

n03829.summary: Urwa and others report Umar's sermon on Allaah's countless bounties to the Ummah and the duty to be grateful, quoting the Qur'aan on how Allaah addressed Musa and the Prophet.

n03830.summary: Ibn Kulayb reports that Umar, reciting Surah Aal Imraan from the pulpit on a Friday, recounted how he ran up Uhud and threatened to kill anyone who said the Prophet had been martyred.

n03831.summary: Ibn Kulayb reports Umar's account, given while reciting Surah Aal Imraan, of seeing the Prophet alive after the rumour of his death at Uhud and of the verse revealed then.

n03832.summary: Abdullaah bin Adi bin Khiyaar reports Umar's lecture that Allaah raises the one who humbles himself for Him and humbles the one who is proud.

n03833.summary: Abu Sa'eed Khudri reports Umar telling people to avoid any transaction that raises doubt about interest, since the Prophet died before explaining its details.

n03834.summary: Aswad bin Yazeed reports Umar's list of the Miqaat places for Hajj, and Abdullaah bin Abbaas reports Umar's lecture that the Prophet had adulterers stoned and that this penalty must not be doubted.

n03836.summary: Sa'eed bin Musayyib reports Umar's du'aa at Abtah, his Madinah speech on the ordained duties and on stoning for adultery, and that he was stabbed within the month of Dhul Hijjah.

n03837.summary: Ma'daan bin Abu Talha reports Umar's last Friday sermon: his dream of his death, the six-man consultation to choose a successor, his concern about the law of kalaalah inheritance, and the rule that garlic and onions must be cooked before entering the Masjid.

n03838.summary: Yasaar bin Maroor reports Umar saying that the Prophet built the Masjid for the Muhaajireen and Ansaar, so that when crowds grew, people should make sajdah on each other's backs and pray inside rather than in the streets.

n03839.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports Umar's statement that the Prophet permitted Mut'ah for three days before it was forbidden, and Abdullaah bin Sa'eed reports Umar's warning about children born to non-Arab slave women.

n03840.summary: Ma'roor Tameemi reports hearing Umar urge people from the pulpit to adopt Taqwa and to obey those entrusted with their affairs.

n03841.summary: Abu Hurayrah, Qabeesah, Urwa and Abdullaah bin Khiraash each report short sayings of Umar on truthfulness, mercy, greed and independence, and a du'aa asking Allaah to keep them on His Deen.

n03844.summary: Another narration adds Umar's du'aa phrase 'and provide for us from Your grace'.

n03845.summary: Abu Sa'eed, Abdullaah bin Zubayr, Abu Ubayd, Alqama and Sulaymaan bin Yasaar each report Umar's sayings on Hajj and Umrah, silk, the prohibition of fasting on the two Eids, intention, and his du'aa for rain during a drought.

n03848.summary: Abu Uthmaan Nahdi heard Umar say in a sermon that the Prophet had said what he feared most for this Ummah was the hypocrite with an eloquent tongue.

n03849.summary: Ibraheem bin Abdur Rahmaan Makhzoomi reports that after the people pledged allegiance to Uthmaan, Uthmaan gave a sermon saying the first rung of the ladder is the hardest and promising more carefully prepared lectures in future.

n03850.summary: Badr bin Uthmaan reports from his uncle that after the consultative assembly pledged allegiance, the uncle went to the Prophet's pulpit and warned that the world is deception and death comes without warning, quoting Surah Luqmaan and Surah Kahf on the passing nature of this world and the lasting value of good deeds. The people then pledged allegiance.

n03851.summary: Utba reports Uthmaan's first address as Khalifah: he will follow the Book, the Sunnah and what the people agree on, and he warns against being drawn to the world.

n03852.summary: Mujaahid reports Uthmaan's address warning that the angel of death is closing in and that each person must prepare for death and take charge of his own soul.

n03853.summary: Hasan reports Uthmaan's address urging Taqwa, control of the soul for the life after death, and trust in Allaah above all else.

n03854.summary: Several reports are strung together: Uthmaan's advice to fear Allaah in private, his account of serving the Prophet on journeys and at home, his orders against child labour, slave-girl earning and backgammon, his full prayer at Mina, and a Hajjaaj report on the grave.

n03856.summary: Sa'eed bin Musayyib reports Uthmaan's account of buying dates from the Banu Qaynuqaa and the Prophet's advice to weigh them when buying and again when selling; Hasan reports Uthmaan ordering that dangerous dogs be killed and sporting pigeons slaughtered.

n03858.summary: Badr bin Uthmaan reports Uthmaan's final public address: the world is given to be used for the Aakhirah, not to be clung to; people should fear Allaah, avoid splintering, and stay united.

n03859.summary: A cross-reference: Uthmaan's praise of guarding in the path of Allaah was already narrated earlier in the chapter on Jihaad.

n03860.summary: Ali bin Husayn reports that when Ali became Khalifah, his first address urged obedience to Allaah, avoiding harm to Muslims, and readiness for death and the Aakhirah.

n03861.summary: Ali says that a man's tribe is more valuable to him than he is to them, citing the Qur'aanic accounts of Loot and Shu'ayb and their tribes.

n03862.summary: Sha'bi reports that at the start of each Ramadhaan, Ali reminded people that fasting means abstaining from lies and falsehood as well as food, and that the month must be fixed by sighting the moon.

n03863.summary: Ali speaks about death and the grave, warning that the grave is either a pit of Jahannam or a garden of Jannah, and describes the coming Day of Resurrection; Asbagh bin Nabaatah reports the same sermon with additions, and Ali weeps.

n03865.summary: Saalih Ijli reports Ali's address on the transience of the world, the lonely graves of those who have passed away, and the Day of Judgement when every deed is laid open.

n03866.summary: Ali (RA) opens a lecture praising Allaah, reminding people of death, resurrection and accountability, and warning them not to be deceived by this world.

n03867.summary: At a funeral, Ali (RA) tells the mourners what the dead man has witnessed and urges them to fear Allaah and prepare for the Aakhirah.

n03868.summary: Ali (RA) urges people to act for the Aakhirah, warning that this world is departing and the Aakhirah is arriving, and that they should be neither deceived nor heedless.

n03869.summary: Ziyaad A'raabi reports that Ali (RA) wept in the pulpit at Kufa after the battle of Nahrwaan and then warned against people who speak like the righteous but act like lovers of the world.

n03870.summary: Yahya bin Yamur reports Ali (RA) teaching that Allaah's decisions come down like rain, so adversity should be met with humility and du'aa, and that enjoining good neither cuts off sustenance nor brings death closer.

n03871.summary: A variant of the same lecture on Allaah's decisions adds that a believer who makes du'aa gets either what he asks or a reward in the Aakhirah, and that the harvest of this world is wealth and Taqwa.

n03872.summary: Abu Waa'il reports Ali's warnings in Kufa about pretending to poverty, long life, authority and consultation, and Ali's answer that Qiyaamah is near when the knowledge of Deen rests with the downtrodden.

n03873.summary: In a long sermon Ali (RA) advises taqwa, the Qur'aan, following the Sunnah and sincerity, and reminds people that this world is ending while the Aakhirah is arriving.

n03874.summary: Abu Khayrah reports Ali (RA) warning the people of Kufa that they would attack the Prophet's descendants among them, and reciting verses about Husayn being brought to Kufa by deception and pressed to pledge to Yazeed.

n03875.summary: Ibraheem Taymi reports that Ali (RA) denied the family had any secret writings beyond the Qur'aan and a note with camel ages for zakaah, injury laws and the Prophet's ruling that Madinah is sacred, with curses for fabrication and false claims of parentage.

n03876.summary: Ibraheem Nakha'ee reports Alqama bin Qais repeating from the same pulpit Ali's words that the best after the Prophet were Abu Bakr and Umar, and that later innovations are for Allaah to judge.

n03877.summary: Abu Juhayfah reports Ali (RA) saying from the pulpit that the best person of this Ummah after the Prophet was Abu Bakr, and then Umar.

n03878.summary: A variant report in which Ali (RA) says it never seemed far-fetched that an angel spoke through the tongue of Umar.

n03879.summary: Alqama bin Qais reports Ali (RA) rebuking those who rank him above Abu Bakr and Umar, announcing that anyone who says so after this will be punished as a slanderer, and stating the order of the best after the Prophet.

n03880.summary: Zaid bin Wahab reports that Suwayd bin Ghafalah, visiting Ali, led the salaah without adhaan or iqaamah and then gave the Prophet's ruling on eating sacrificial meat after three days, noting that the prohibition was later lifted.

n03881.summary: A scholar of Banu Tameem reports Ali warning that a time will come when people hold on to their wealth and the wicked are honoured, and that the Prophet forbade buying from the desperate and sales involving deception. Abu Ubayd, freed slave of Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf, reports Ali leading the Eid salaah without adhaan or iqaamah and telling people not to eat their sacrifice after three days, a ruling since lifted.

n03882.summary: Ribee bin Hiraash reports Ali (RA) saying in a lecture not to lie about him, because whoever lies about him will enter Jahannam.

n03883.summary: Abu Abdur Rahmaan Sulami reports Ali (RA) saying that the Shari'ah penalties must be enforced on slaves and recounting the Prophet's approval of his delayed sentence on a slave woman; Abdullaah bin Sabt reports Ali foretelling his own assassination and forbidding the people to kill anyone but the killer.

n03885.summary: Umayr bin Abdul Malik reports Ali (RA) telling the people he had taken nothing from their wealth except a perfume vial given to him as a gift, and then relaying the Prophet's report of Allaah's mercy and wrath towards those who obey or disobey.

n03887.summary: Hubayrah reports Hasan bin Ali (RA) addressing the people after his father Ali's death, praising Ali's merits and the night of his martyrdom, and Abu Tufayl reports Hasan reciting his lineage to the Prophet's household.

n03889.summary: Abu Jameela reports that after Ali's death and after Hasan was stabbed in the buttock, Hasan addressed the people of Iraq about fearing Allaah and about the Prophet's household, until everyone in the Masjid was weeping.

n03890.summary: Sha'bi reports that at Nakheelah, after making peace with Mu'aawiya, Hasan told the people he had relinquished the Khilaafah to Mu'aawiya to save the blood of the Ummah.

n03891.summary: In a second report from Sha'bi, Hasan at Nakheelah says the Khilaafah is temporary, that the Prophet's family guided the people while his own peace saved their blood, and concludes by asking Allaah's forgiveness.

n03892.summary: Muhammad bin Ka'b Qurazi reports Mu'aawiya's sermon in Madinah that Allaah grants understanding of the Deen to whoever He wishes good, and that Mu'aawiya heard this from the Prophet.

n03893.summary: Several chains report Mu'aawiya's sermon: the Prophet said that Allaah grants understanding of the Deen to whoever He wishes good, and that a group of this Ummah will stay upon the truth until Qiyaamah; Maalik bin Yakhaamir adds that Mu'aadh bin Jabal identified them as the people of Shaam.

n03895.summary: Yunus bin Halbas Janadi reports Mu'aawiya's sermon, in which he recites a verse about Isa's elevation and the Ummah prevailing until Qiyaamah, and Makhool reports the Prophet's words that a group of the Ummah will prevail until Qiyaamah.

n03896.summary: Muhammad bin Abdullaah reports Ibn Zubayr's Hajj lecture in Makkah just before the Day of Tarwiyah, covering the verses on the months of Hajj, Arafaat, Muzdalifah, the Talbiyah, the miqaats and Tamattu, with much dhikr and du'aa.

n03897.summary: Hishaam bin Urwa reports Ibn Zubayr teaching that pilgrims may stay at any part of Arafah except Batn Urna, and at any part of Muzdalifah except Batn Muhassar.

n03898.summary: Abbaas bin Sahl reports Ibn Zubayr quoting the Prophet that a person given a valley of gold would want a second, and that only the grave's sand fills the belly; Ataa bin Abi Rabaah reports Ibn Zubayr relating the Prophet's ruling on the reward of salaah in Madinah's Masjid and the Masjidul Haraam, and that the whole Haram is a Masjid.

n03900.summary: Wahab bin Kaysaan, a freed slave of Ibn Zubayr, reports that Ibn Zubayr led the Eid salaah before the lecture, saying this is the way shown by Allaah and His Rasool.

n03901.summary: Thaabit reports Ibn Zubayr relating the Prophet's ruling against men wearing silk in this world, and the Prophet's dhikr after salaah; Abu Zubayr reports Ibn Zubayr narrating the same from the same pulpit.

n03902.summary: Thuwayr reports Ibn Zubayr telling the people from the pulpit to fast on the Day of Aashura because the Prophet gave the instruction to fast.

n03903.summary: Kulthoom bin Hibr reports Ibn Zubayr warning the people of Makkah about a gambling game called Nardsheer, quoting Surah Maa'idah verse 90, and vowing severe punishment for anyone caught playing it.

n03904.summary: Abu Dardaa reports that the Prophet asked Abu Bakr, Umar and then Ibn Mas'ood to speak, and praised Ibn Mas'ood's short address on Allaah as Rabb, Islaam as Deen, the Qur'aan as Imaam and the Prophet as the one they follow, while warning against bombastic speech.

n03905.summary: A similar report of the Prophet asking Ibn Mas'ood to speak, in which Ibn Mas'ood says he is pleased with Allaah as Rabb and Islaam as his religion, and the Prophet says he is pleased with what Ibn Ummi Abd likes for them.

n03906.summary: Abul Ahwas Jushami reports Ibn Mas'ood killing a snake during his lecture on the Prophet's ruling that killing a snake is like killing a mushrik; Abu Waa'il reports Ibn Mas'ood's address in Kufa after Uthmaan became Khalifah, urging the people to pledge allegiance to him.

n03908.summary: Khaalid bin Umayr Adawi reports Utba bin Ghazwaan's sermon as governor of Basrah, on the world's ending, the stones of Jahannam, the gates of Jannah, his memory of living on tree leaves with the Prophet, and his fear of being esteemed by himself while humbled before Allaah.

n03909.summary: A variant of Utba bin Ghazwaan's address in which leadership after the Prophethood degenerates into kingship and many leaders and governors will test the people.

n03910.summary: Abu Abdur Rahmaan Sulami reports Hudhayfah bin Yamaan's Jumu'ah lectures at Madaa'in on Qiyaamah drawing near and the race towards Jannah through good deeds.

n03911.summary: Kurdoos reports Hudhayfah bin Yamaan at Madaa'in telling the people to check what their slaves earn, because the Prophet said no flesh nourished with haraam will enter Jannah.

n03912.summary: A variant of Hudhayfah bin Yamaan's Madaa'in lecture, warning the people to watch their slaves' sources of income and saying the seller, buyer and maker of wine are like the one who drinks it.

n03913.summary: Abu Moosa Ash'ari told the people of Basrah to weep over their sins and fear of Jahannam, since the people of Jahannam will weep until they cry blood.

n03914.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas, as Ameer of Hajj, lectured on Surah Baqarah verse by verse, and Shaqeeq said it was so impressive that the Romans and Persians would accept Islaam if they heard it.

n03915.summary: Abu Hurayrah praised Allaah from the Prophet's pulpit, foretelling the ruin of the Arabs at the hands of child rulers and that a group from the non-Arabs would reach the Deen.

n03916.summary: During the siege of Uthmaan, Abu Hurayrah quoted the Prophet's advice to stay with the Ameer during tribulation and pointed to Uthmaan as that Ameer.

n03917.summary: Hajjaaj asks Muhammad bin Yusuf about the narration of Abdullaah bin Salaam, who went to the besieged Uthmaan and addressed the rebels, and the item then passes to lectures of Husayn bin Ali.

n03919.summary: Mujaahid reports Yazeed bin Shajarah urging the people to engage the enemy in full combat and describing the rewards of martyrdom in Jannah.

n03920.summary: Mujaahid reports Yazeed bin Shajarah Rahaawi, a governor of Shaam, exhorting the people to combat and describing the recording of deeds, the shore of Jahannam and the punishment there.

n03921.summary: Sa'eed bin Suwayd reports that Umayr bin Sa'd, governor of Hims, taught from the pulpit that justice is the wall and truth the door that protect Islaam.

n03922.summary: Sa'd bin Ubayd told the people they would meet the enemy and be martyred the next day, and instructed that they not be washed or shrouded in anything other than the clothes they wore.

n03923.summary: Salamah bin Sabarah reports that in Shaam Mu'aadh bin Jabal told the Muslims that Allaah would admit into Jannah the prisoners from Rome and Persia who serve them, because the Muslims thank them for their service.

n03924.summary: Howshab Fazaari reports that Abu Dardaa feared being asked on the Day of Judgement how he acted on his knowledge, when the verses of Allaah's Book would testify against him.

n03925.summary: Abu Dharr asked the Prophet what the scriptures of Ibraheem and Moosa contained, and received lessons and advice on taqwa, the Qur'aan and dhikr, truthfulness, silence and good character.

n03926.summary: Aa'isha narrates the Prophet's parable of a dying man's three brothers, representing his family, his wealth and his deeds, and Abdullaah bin Kurz then recited verses on the same theme.

n03927.summary: Umar advised a man not to let others distract him from himself, not to waste his days, and to follow each sin with a good deed.

n03928.summary: Umar advised staying away from what harms you, keeping righteous friends even though they are scarce, and consulting those who fear Allaah in all matters.

n03929.summary: Sa'eed bin Musayyib reports that Umar gave eighteen guidelines, of which only a fragment survives: a principle on responding to someone who disobeys Allaah in matters affecting you, and a verse that only the knowledgeable fear Allaah.

n03930.summary: Ibn Shihaab reports Umar's advice to avoid meddling in others' affairs, to be wary of enemies and of friends who are not trustworthy, to avoid sinners, and to consult those who fear Allaah.

n03931.summary: Samurah bin Jundub reports Umar's description of three categories of women and three categories of men, contrasting the chaste, gentle and wise with the demanding and the bewildered.

n03932.summary: Umar told Ahnaf bin Qais that laughing, joking and talking too much cost a person respect, make him prone to error, and erode modesty, piety and eventually the heart.

n03933.summary: Another narration gives Umar's similar advice on laughing, joking and talking too much, and refers back to the previous narration for the rest.

n03934.summary: Umar described servants of Allaah who shun falsehood, speak the truth, fear Allaah, and prefer the rewards of the Aakhirah to the pleasures of this world.

n03935.summary: Umar advised becoming storehouses of the Qur'aan and fountains of knowledge, asking Allaah for daily sustenance, and keeping company with those who repent often.

n03936.summary: Umar said that one who fears Allaah does not vent anger or follow his whims, that justice to people brings success, and that humility in obedience is nearer to righteousness than seeking honour.

n03937.summary: Maalik reports Umar's teaching that a man's respect lies in taqwa, his honour in his Deen and his manhood in his character, and Sufyaan Thowri reports Umar's letter to Abu Moosa that wisdom is a gift and that one should avoid shameful acts.

n03939.summary: Umar wrote to his son Abdullaah advising him to hold to taqwa, which Allaah protects, and warned that deeds without intention and wealth without compassion carry no benefit.

n03940.summary: Ja'far bin Zabrqaan reports Umar's letters to a governor and to Mu'aawiya bin Abi Sufyaan urging self-reckoning and judgement by the truth, and Ibn Abbaas reports Ali's advice to Umar to curb his hopes and live simply.

n03942.summary: Ali said that true goodness is not in wealth or children but in growing knowledge and forbearance and in excelling in worship, and that a deed done with taqwa is never small.

n03943.summary: Uqba bin Abu Sahbaa reports that after Ali was stabbed by Ibn Muljim, he advised his son Hasan that intelligence is the greatest wealth and foolishness the worst poverty, and to avoid fools, liars, misers and sinners.

n03944.summary: Ali said that inspiration is the best guide, good character the best companion, intelligence the best friend and sound education the best legacy, and that only friendship not built on greed endures.

n03945.summary: Nimraan bin Makhmar reports that Abu Ubaydah bin Jarraah warned his troops against outward show without sincere Deen and urged them to erase old sins with fresh good deeds.

n03946.summary: Sa'eed bin Abu Sa'eed Maqbari reports that Abu Ubaydah, struck by plague in Shaam, advised the Muslims on salaah, zakaah and death, and Mu'aadh bin Jabal then urged sincere repentance and reconciliation with brothers.

n03947.summary: Abu Ubaydah said that the heart of a believer changes many times a day, which is why a person should consult others.

n03948.summary: Muhammad bin Seereen reports Mu'aadh bin Jabal's advice to give precedence to the share of the Aakhirah over the share of this world, and Amr bin Maymoon Awdi reports Mu'aadh's warning to Banu Awd that all return to Allaah and remain forever in Jannah or Jahannam.

n03950.summary: Mu'aawiya bin Qurra reports Mu'aadh bin Jabal's advice to his son to pray as one bidding farewell, and Abdullaah bin Salamah reports Mu'aadh's advice to a man to balance fasting and night prayer, earn without sin, die as a Muslim and beware the curse of the oppressed.

n03952.summary: Mu'aadh bin Jabal said that laughing without amusement, sleeping through the night without salaah and eating without hunger expose a person to resentment, and warned that prosperity and women's gold, silver and finery would test the believers.

n03953.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood said it angers him to see a man idle, doing nothing for this world or for the Aakhirah.

n03954.summary: Ibn Mas'ood said he would not find anyone lying like a corpse at night and restless all day like the Qutrub insect, and that the cream of this world has passed, making death a gift for every Muslim; Ibn Uyaynah explains the Qutrub image.

n03956.summary: Ibn Mas'ood compared the world to a drying lake, called death and poverty things people dislike but which a believer can benefit from, and taught that perfect Imaan means preferring halaal poverty and submission to Allaah over worldly honour.

n03957.summary: Ibn Mas'ood swore that a person who passes his mornings and evenings as a Muslim will not be harmed by the adversities of this world.

n03958.summary: Abdur Rahmaan bin Hujayrah reports that Ibn Mas'ood reminded those sitting with him that lives are shortening, deeds are recorded and death is near, and that each person is a guest whose wealth is borrowed.

n03960.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood advised a man to worship Allaah alone and to accept what is true from anyone, while rejecting falsehood even when it comes from someone close.

n03961.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood gave several sayings: the truth is hard and falsehood pleasant, the heart can be zealous or lethargic, outward health means little if the heart is sick, and one should not follow others blindly.

n03963.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood gave a long series of sayings on the Aakhirah, the Qur'aan, the Sunnah and the harm of worldly desire.

n03965.summary: Salmaan Faarsi said that three things make him laugh and three make him weep: the one who hopes at length while death searches for him, separation from the Prophet and his party, the scene of death's pangs, and standing before Allaah.

n03966.summary: Salmaan said that when Allaah intends a person's ruin, He removes modesty, then mercy, then trustworthiness, and finally the bond of Islaam.

n03967.summary: Salmaan compared the believer in this world to a sick person whose physician forbids harmful things, showing that Allaah withholds many comforts from the believer until Jannah.

n03968.summary: Abu Dardaa invited Salmaan to Shaam, and Salmaan replied that knowledge, not land, makes a person blessed, and warned Abu Dardaa as a judge not to be a quack who wrongly condemns people.

n03969.summary: Abu Dardaa said the people stay in good standing while they love their righteous ones and recognise the truth when it is spoken.

n03970.summary: Abu Dardaa gave several pieces of advice: do not compel or blame people beyond what Allaah requires, worship as if you can see Allaah, goodness lies in knowledge and patience rather than wealth, and seek forgiveness after sin.

n03972.summary: Abu Dardaa warned that secret disobedience brings hatred in the hearts of believers, described the apex of Imaan, warned against greed for wealth, and rebuked the people of Damascus for hoarding and building.

n03974.summary: Abu Dardaa called the people of Damascus to the Masjid and began to rebuke them for their building and planting, but the text gives only the opening and refers back to the previous narration.

n03975.summary: Abu Dardaa urged the wealthy to give in sadaqah before death, warned against seeking bounty while starving oneself of knowledge, praised those who fast, and spoke to builders and to ruins about the transience of the world.

n03976.summary: Abu Dardaa said he loved death, poverty and illness for the reasons they bring him closer to his Rabb and cleanse his sins, and Shurahbeel reports his reflection at every funeral.

n03978.summary: Aun bin Abdullaah reports Abu Dardaa's advice that searching hard for others' faults makes a person lose sight of his own, and that one should lend to the one who will repay on the Day of Qiyaamah.

n03980.summary: Abu Dardaa rebuked those who are greedy for provision already guaranteed while neglecting their duties, advised pure sustenance and remembrance of death, and urged seeking Allaah's mercy and forgiveness.

n03983.summary: Abu Dardaa warned against the curse of the oppressed and of the orphan, and said the person he most hates to oppress is one who has none but Allaah to turn to for help.

n03984.summary: Abu Dardaa wrote letters to Salmaan, an unnamed companion and Maslamah bin Mukhallad, passing on the Prophet's counsel about the Masjid, orphans, wealth, servants and pleasing Allaah.

n03986.summary: Abu Dardaa said there is no Islaam without obedience to Allaah, no good without staying with the Muslim community, and sincere goodwill toward Allaah's Deen, His Khalifah and the believers.

n03987.summary: Abu Dharr Ghifaari stood by the Kabah and advised the people to prepare provisions for the journey to Qiyaamah through Hajj, fasting, night prayer, sadaqah and good speech, and to avoid greed.

n03988.summary: Two reports give advice from Abu Dharr on the Aakhirah, night prayer, fasting, sadaqah, and the dislike people have for death and poverty, and in the second report Abu Dardaa joins him.

n03991.summary: Hudhayfah told the people to ask him about the living dead, who are those who oppose despotic rule neither with heart, tongue nor hand.

n03992.summary: Hudhayfah said hearts come in four kinds: the veiled heart of the disbeliever, the two-faced heart of the hypocrite, the clear heart of the believer, and the heart that holds both hypocrisy and Imaan.

n03993.summary: Hudhayfah warned that trials of temptation sweep away anyone who faces them alone, that each accepted temptation leaves a black spot on the heart, and advised staying at home and dying in times of peace if given the choice.

n03996.summary: Hudhayfah listed three sources of corruption, said trials wear down the senses more than wine, said a time will come when only one who makes du'aa like a drowning person is safe, and said the best person takes from both worlds.

n03998.summary: Abul Aaliya reports that Ubay bin Ka'b advised a man to make the Qur'aan his guide, his judge and his intercessor.

n03999.summary: Ubay bin Ka'b said that whoever gives something up for Allaah's pleasure is given something better from unexpected sources, and whoever wrongly takes what he looks down on will meet something worse.

n04000.summary: Ubay bin Ka'b said a believer has four qualities of patience, gratitude, truthfulness and justice, and that the believer and the disbeliever each pass through five places of light or darkness.

n04001.summary: Jabar or Juwaybir reports that when he belittled the world before Umar, Ubay bin Ka'b, who was sitting beside Umar, corrected him that the world is the means to the Aakhirah, and Ubay later gave advice about minding one's own affairs.

n04002.summary: Zaid bin Thaabit wrote to Ubay bin Ka'b that the tongue should follow the heart, that speech without matching action is empty, and that one should not look at others' faults while ignoring one's own.

n04003.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas warned a sinner that several things are worse than the sin itself, such as feeling safe, laughing at it or being pleased with it, and related how Ayyoob was tested for failing to help a poor man against an oppressor.

n04004.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas advised fulfilling the obligations Allaah has set with sincere intention, and taught that every person's lawful provision is decreed, that patience brings it, and that taking the unlawful reduces it.

n04005.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar said that receiving anything of this world lowers a servant's status before Allaah, even for someone who is honoured by Him.

n04006.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar said a man cannot reach the apex of Imaan until he counts people foolish for preferring this world, and then with Mujaahid he spoke to some ruins, saying that only their deeds remain.

n04008.summary: Hasan bin Ali said that craving the world makes a person its slave, that one who does not aspire to it has enough, and that a person who makes no spiritual progress is deceived.

n04009.summary: Hasan bin Ali said that tolerance adds beauty to character, keeping promises shows manliness, and haste, excessive travel, wicked company and sinful company are faults.

n04010.summary: Hasan bin Ali divided people into four kinds: those with goodness but no good character, those with good character but no goodness, those with neither, and the best, who have both.

n04011.summary: Ziyaad bin Maahak reports Shaddaad bin Aws saying that goodness and evil lie in Jannah and Jahannam and that people should belong to the Aakhirah rather than this world, and Abu Dardaa then praised Shaddaad for combining knowledge with forbearance.

n04012.summary: Jundub Bajali advises fearing Allaah, reciting the Qur'aan, valuing the Deen above wealth and health, and avoiding the shedding of a Muslim's blood.

n04013.summary: At a funeral near Damascus, Abu Umaamah Baahili warns that the grave is a house of loneliness and darkness and describes how the hypocrites will be left without light on the Day of Qiyaamah.

n04014.summary: Abu Umaamah Baahili tells a group that Allaah guarantees Jannah or reward for three kinds of people, warns of the debts settled on the bridge of Jahannam, and urges truthfulness and spending in the path of Allaah.

n04016.summary: Sahl bin Sa'd reports that Abu Usayd, after losing his eyesight, said he had seen the angels come down into the valley at Badr to assist the Muslims.

n04017.summary: Several reports describe angels taking the form of Companions at Badr, the angels wearing turbans, and Abu Raafi's account of Abu Lahab, Ummu Fadhl and the news of the Quraysh defeat at Badr.

n04019.summary: An unnamed Sahabi who fought against the Muslims at Hunayn says the enemy could not stand before the Muslims until strikingly handsome men appeared to the Prophet's side and told them to turn back, which led to their defeat.

n04020.summary: Auf A'raabi reports from Abdur Rahmaan that a fighter at Hunayn saw the Prophet with strikingly handsome men who told them to turn back, which led to their defeat.

n04021.summary: Jubayr bin Mut'im says that during Hunayn he saw what looked like a black blanket of ants come down between the two armies, and he was sure these were angels that decided the defeat.

n04022.summary: Abdullaah bin Fadhl reports that at Uhud an angel in the form of Mus'ab bin Umayr took the flag after Mus'ab was martyred, and the Prophet realised it was an angel sent to help him.

n04023.summary: Anas says he could see the dust rising from the street of Banu Ghanam as Jibra'eel rode past while the Prophet marched against Banu Quraizah.

n04024.summary: Another narration says that after the Battle of Khandaq Jibra'eel came to the Prophet and ordered the march against Banu Qurayzah, and the angels left in clouds of dust.

n04025.summary: Suhayl bin Amr says that at Badr he saw brilliant men on spotted horses killing the Mushrikeen and taking them prisoner.

n04026.summary: Baraa and other Companions report that when an Ansaari took Abbaas prisoner at Badr, Abbaas said that man had not captured him, and the Prophet told the Ansaari that Allaah had sent a noble angel to help him.

n04027.summary: A similar report from Ali says Abbaas described his captor as a handsome, bald-at-the-temples man on a spotted horse, and the Prophet told the Ansaari that a noble angel had helped him.

n04028.summary: Ibn Abbaas reports that Abbaas's captor at Badr was Abu Yasar Ka'b bin Amr, who said a man he had never seen helped him, and the Prophet said it was one of the noble angels.

n04029.summary: Ibn Abbaas reports that a Muslim pursuing a Mushrik heard a whiplash and a horseman calling his horse Hayzoom, and the Prophet confirmed it was an angel; a Sahabi of Banu Ghifaar adds how his cousin died of fear while watching Badr from a mountain.

n04030.summary: Abu Talha says that in a battle, when the Prophet recited 'Only You do we worship and only from You do we seek help', he saw the angels strike the enemy from front and back.

n04031.summary: Abu Umaamah reports that his father Sahl bin Hunayf said that at Badr a Mushrik's head fell from his body as soon as a Muslim pointed a sword at it.

n04032.summary: Abu Waaqid Laythi says that at Badr a Mushrik's head rolled off before his sword could reach him, so he realised an angel had killed him, and Abu Dawood Maazini reports the same.

n04033.summary: Sahl bin Abu Hathma reports that Abu Barzah brought three Mushrik heads to the Prophet at Badr and said an angel killed one of them, and Haarith bin Simma reports that the Prophet said angels fought beside Abdur Rahmaan bin Awf, who had killed seven Mushrikeen.

n04035.summary: Ibn Abbaas reports that Jibra'eel pointed at those who ridiculed the Prophet, and the Prophet named them, after which each of them met a painful end.

n04036.summary: Anas narrates how Abu Mu'liq, threatened with death by a robber, prayed and made du'aa three times, and a rider with a spear, an angel from the fourth heaven, killed the robber.

n04037.summary: Layth bin Sa'd reports that Zaid bin Haaritha, led to ruins by a Taa'if man who meant to kill him, called out 'Yaa Arhamar Raahimeen' and a horseman sent from above killed the attacker.

n04038.summary: Aa'isha says the Prophet went out to a man on a Turkish horse whom she took to be Dihya Kalbi and told her it was Jibra'eel sent to order the march against Banu Qurayzah; Sa'eed bin Musayyib adds that the Prophet said the rider others saw was Jibra'eel shaking that fortress.

n04039.summary: Ibn Abbaas reports that when the Prophet visited a sick Ansaari, he heard the Ansaari speaking to someone unseen, and the Prophet said it was Jibra'eel.

n04040.summary: Ibn Abbaas says he was with his father Abbaas when a man whispered to the Prophet, and the Prophet later said it was Jibra'eel, whom he had been too busy with to attend to them.

n04041.summary: Another narration says Abbaas sent his son Abdullaah to the Prophet, that the man with him was Jibra'eel, and that the Prophet foretold Abdullaah would have great knowledge but go blind before he died.

n04042.summary: Urwa bin Ruwaym reports that the very old Irbaadh bin Saariyah, who prayed to die, met a young man in the Damascus Masjid who taught him a du'aa and said he was the angel Roobaa'eel.

n04043.summary: Mutarrif bin Abdullaah reports that Imraan bin Husayn said the angels had greeted him during his illness until he had himself branded, and Qataadah adds that the angels used to shake his hand until then.

n04044.summary: Salam bin Atiyya Asadi reports that when Salmaan was dying he asked an angel to be gentle with him, and the angel replied that it is gentle with every Mu'min.

n04046.summary: Abu Sa'eed Khudri reports that the Prophet said whoever dislikes Umar dislikes him, that Allaah boasts of Umar, and that a Muhaddath, one on whose tongue the angels speak, would be Umar if there is one in this Ummah.

n04047.summary: Anas bin Hulays reports that after the siege of Buharseer, Aswad bin Qutba (Abu Mufazzir) answered the Persian emissary with words he did not know he was saying, and the enemy fled, which the Persians took as the speech of angels.

n04048.summary: Abu Sa'eed Khudri reports that Usayd bin Hudhayr saw a cloud of lights while reciting in his silo and the Prophet said they were listening angels; a second report says an angel announced the death of Sa'd bin Muaadh, and the Prophet hurried to his funeral.

n04049.summary: Usayd (RA) reports seeing lantern-like lights between the sky and the ground while reciting the Qur'aan; the Prophet ﷺ explains they were angels who had come down to listen, and a second report says they had drawn close because of his voice.

n04050.summary: Mahmood bin Labeed reports that Handhala bin Abu Aamir was struck down by Shaddaad bin Aswad at Uhud, and the Prophet ﷺ told the Companions that the angels were bathing him because he had left for battle without taking his ritual bath.

n04051.summary: Mahmood bin Labeed and Aasim bin Umar bin Qataadah report that the angels washed the body of Sa'd bin Mu'aadh after his death from an arrow wound at Khandaq, and the Prophet ﷺ hurried to the funeral, saying he feared the angels would reach Sa'd first as they had reached Handhala.

n04052.summary: Jaabir reports that when his father died he uncovered his face and wept, and the Prophet remarked that the angels would keep shading his father with their wings until the body was carried.

n04053.summary: Salamah bin Aslam says the room where Sa'd bin Muaadh's body lay was full of angels, and other reports say seventy thousand angels attended his funeral while hypocrites mocked how light the bier was.

n04056.summary: Hasan reports that hypocrites mocked how light Sa'd bin Mu'aadh's bier was, and the Prophet said it was light because angels were carrying it.

n04057.summary: Mu'aawiya bin Hayda reports that after the Prophet had prayed for drought or fear to be sent on his people, the drought kept uprooting him and fear of the Muslims filled his heart, so he came to accept Islaam.

n04058.summary: Saa'ib bin Yasaar reports that he asked Yazeed bin Aamir Suwaa'ee, who had fought with the Mushrikeen at Hunayn, to describe the fear Allaah cast into their hearts, and Yazeed imitated it by rattling pebbles on a platter.

n04059.summary: Suraaqa bin Maalik, still a non-Muslim at the time, pursued the Prophet during the Hijrah, and his horse's legs sank into the sand after the Prophet made du'aa.

n04060.summary: Suraaqa pleads for his horse to be freed, the Prophet and Abu Bakr make du'aa, and Suraaqa then turns back the pursuers and becomes a defender of the Prophet.

n04061.summary: Arbad bin Qais and Aamir bin Tufayl plot to kill the Prophet, Arbad is struck by lightning, and Aamir dies after developing a swelling on his throat.

n04062.summary: At the Battle of Hunayn the Prophet threw earth or pebbles at the enemy, and they were defeated as if every tree and stone were chasing them.

n04063.summary: Hakeem bin Hizaam relates that at Badr, after hearing a sound like stones falling on a platter, the Mushrikeen were defeated when the Prophet threw pebbles at them.

n04064.summary: Hakeem bin Hizaam relates that the Prophet was instructed to throw a handful of pebbles at the Mushrikeen at Badr, and that Allaah then revealed Surah Anfaal verse 17.

n04065.summary: Ibn Abbaas reports that at Badr the Prophet took pebbles from Ali and threw them into the enemy's faces, and that Allaah then revealed Surah Anfaal verse 17.

n04066.summary: Yazeed bin Aamir Suwaa'ee reports that the Prophet threw a handful of soil at the enemy at Badr, after which the Mushrikeen complained of dust in their eyes.

n04067.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood recalls that the enemy looked very few in number at Badr, until a captured man revealed they were a thousand strong.

n04068.summary: Sa'eed bin Jubayr describes the combined forces that marched on Madinah at Khandaq, and how Allaah sent a wind and angels against them so that they fled.

n04069.summary: Humayd bin Hilaal reports that Banu Qurayzah broke their pact by joining the Mushrikeen, and that Allaah sent an army and wind that routed the Mushrikeen while Qurayzah stayed in their fortress.

n04070.summary: Ibn Abbaas reports that during the Battle of Ahzaab the east wind was sent to assist the Prophet, because the north wind refused to travel by night.

n04071.summary: Buraydah reports that a Mushrik who prayed for Muhammad's falsehood to be shown sank into the ground at Uhud, and Naafi bin Aasim reports that the man who wounded the Prophet's face was gored to death by a ram.

n04073.summary: Abdullaah bin Mughaffal recounts that at Hudaybiyyah thirty armed Quraysh youths were blinded by the Prophet's curse, were then released, and Surah Fath verse 24 was revealed.

n04074.summary: Zaadhaan reports that when Ali was accused of lying, he challenged the accuser to a curse, and the man lost his sight before leaving the gathering.

n04075.summary: Ammaar reports the same incident, in which the man who accused Ali of lying was blinded by Ali's curse, and a second Zaadhaan account is included.

n04076.summary: Sa'eed bin Zaid prays that Arwa bint Uwais, who falsely claimed his land, be blinded if she is lying, and she falls into her well and dies; a flood then proves his claim.

n04078.summary: Abu Utaaridi warns against reviling Ali or the Prophet's family, reporting that a man from Balhujaym who scoffed at Husayn bin Ali lost his sight.

n04079.summary: Ibn Abbaas recounts that Quraysh men who tried to seize the Prophet in the Masjidul Haraam were blinded, then had their sight restored by his du'aa after pleading by family ties, and that Surah Yaaseen verses were revealed.

n04080.summary: Qataadah bin Nu'maan recounts losing his eye while shielding the Prophet at Uhud, and the Prophet restored it so that it became the better and sharper of his two eyes.

n04082.summary: Another narration confirms that the eye became the better and sharper of the two.

n04083.summary: Aasim bin Umar bin Qataadah reports that the Companions wanted to cut off Qataadah's dislodged eye, and the Prophet reset it with his palm so that Qataadah could no longer tell which eye had been wounded.

n04084.summary: Ubaydah reports that the Prophet applied his saliva to Abu Dharr's injured eye at Uhud, and it became the better of his two eyes.

n04085.summary: Rifaa'ah bin Raafi reports that the Prophet's saliva and du'aa removed the pain of an arrow in his eye at Badr, and Habeeb bin Fuwayk reports that the Prophet restored his father's sight with saliva.

n04087.summary: Sa'eed bin Ibraheem reports that the freed Roman woman Zinneera regained her sight after she rejected Laat and Uzza, and Anas reports from Ummu Haani that Abu Bakr had freed her and that her sight was restored.

n04088.summary: Hishaam bin Aas recounts his mission, sent by Abu Bakr, to invite Heraclius to Islaam, the palace shaking at the takbeer, and Heraclius showing them pictures of the prophets and then of the Prophet.

n04089.summary: Jubayr bin Mut'im recounts that Christians in a church showed him pictures of the Prophet and of Abu Bakr, and said that Abu Bakr would be the Khalifah after him.

n04090.summary: Jubayr bin Mut'im relates that a Christian told him there is no Nabi after the Prophet, and that the man following the Prophet in the picture is his Khalifah, which Jubayr confirmed was Abu Bakr.

n04091.summary: Scholars from the Ghassaan and Banu Qayn report that, as a reward for patience at Hims, Allaah shook the city with an earthquake when the Muslims called out Allaahu Akbar, and the Romans were humbled.

n04092.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports that Umar called out 'The mountain, O Saariyah, the mountain!' during a sermon, and Saariyah's army heard it, turned to the mountain and were granted victory.

n04093.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar gives further accounts of Umar's call to Saariyah, including Umar's explanation of the vision behind it and Ali's defence of Umar.

n04095.summary: Amr bin Haarith reports that Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf asked Umar why he made the call, Umar explained the danger his army faced near a mountain, and Saariyah's letter confirmed the Muslims' victory after they turned to it.

n04096.summary: Asked why he made the call, Umar replied that he said only what Allaah placed on his tongue.

n04097.summary: Izzah bint Aas reports that Abu Qirsaafah, whose son had been taken captive by the Romans, would climb a wall at each prayer time and call 'Salaah', and his son heard him from Roman territory.

n04098.summary: Ibn Abbaas and Aa'isha report that after the Prophet's death, an unidentified voice told the people to bathe his body in his garments, and they did so.

n04099.summary: Ibn Abbaas reports that during a naval expedition led by Abu Moosa Ash'ari, under the Prophet's appointment, a voice from above promised that whoever stays thirsty for Allaah on a hot day will be given drink on the Day of Qiyaamah.

n04100.summary: Abu Burdah reports Abu Moosa Ash'ari's account of hearing a voice at sea promise that whoever fasts on a hot day solely for Allaah's pleasure will be given drink on Qiyaamah, and that Abu Moosa afterwards sought out the hottest days to fast.

n04101.summary: Sa'eed bin Jubayr reports that at the funeral of Ibn Abbaas in Taa'if a white bird entered his shroud, and that unseen voices recited Surah Fajr beside the grave.

n04102.summary: Maymoon bin Mahraan reports that after the sand was levelled over the grave, an unidentified voice was heard.

n04103.summary: Another account adds that a white bird entered Ibn Abbaas's shroud, and Ikrimah explained it as the eyesight the Prophet had promised would return to him at death, and that the verses recited at the grave were heard by all present.

n04104.summary: Khuraym bin Faatik tells Umar how a Jinn called him to Islaam and guided him to Madinah, where Umar accepted Uthmaan's testimony to a hadith Khuraym had quoted.

n04105.summary: Khuraym bin Faatik recites the Jinn's verses of guidance again, and Ibn Abbaas later tells Umar the story.

n04106.summary: Umar questions the former fortune-teller Sawaad bin Qaarib, who relates how his Jinn told him of a Nabi from Luway bin Ghaalib, and how he came to the Prophet and accepted Islaam.

n04108.summary: Abbaas bin Mirdaas hears a voice from his idol Dimaad announcing the Prophet's coming, destroys the idol, and with his tribe goes to the Prophet and accepts Islaam.

n04109.summary: Jaabir and Ali bin Husayn report that a Jinn serving a woman in Madinah brought news of the Prophet's coming and his prohibition of adultery.

n04110.summary: Uthmaan recounts that a fortune-teller in Shaam said his Jinn could not enter because Ahmed had appeared, and that when he returned to Makkah the Prophet had already announced his Nabuwwaat.

n04111.summary: Mujaahid reports an old man's account of hearing a voice from a cow's belly call people to say that there is none worthy of worship but Allaah, during the Period of Ignorance.

n04112.summary: Ibn Abbaas reports how a Shaytaan named Mis'ar stirred the Quraysh against the Muslims through an idol, and how a Jinn named Samhaj, whom the Prophet named Abdullaah after he believed, killed him; Ali then prayed for the Jinn.

n04113.summary: Abdullaah bin Mahmood reports that men of the Khath'am tribe accepted Islaam after a Jinn's call, heard while they stood by their idol, announced the Prophet's Nabuwwaat.

n04114.summary: Tameem Daari recounts hearing a Jinn in Shaam announce the Prophet's coming, then consulting a monk who confirmed it, and then accepting Islaam.

n04115.summary: Waathila bin Asqa reports that Hajaaj bin Ilaat, frightened in a valley at night, heard a Jinn recite a verse of Surah Rahmaan, then went to the Prophet and accepted Islaam, while Aas bin Waail dismissed the story among the Quraysh.

n04116.summary: Ubay bin Ka'b reports that a Jinn who had heard the Prophet guided a group of lost travellers, who were close to death, to water and the road.

n04117.summary: Sa'eed bin Shuyaym reports that his father heard an unseen voice in Uyaynah's army warning that their families were under attack, so they all turned back during the Battle of Khaybar.

n04118.summary: Abu Hurayrah reports the Prophet's account of seizing a Shaytaan at night and releasing him after recalling the du'aa of Sulaymaan, and Abu Dardaa gives a similar account.

n04119.summary: Buraydah reports that Mu'aadh bin Jabal caught a Shaytaan stealing Sadaqah dates, and the Shaytaan taught him Aayatul Kursi and the end of Surah Baqarah.

n04120.summary: Abu Hurayrah catches a Shaytaan taking from the zakaah of Ramadhaan, who teaches him Aayatul Kursi, and Abu Ayyoob Ansaari tells of a Jinn stealing his dates.

n04121.summary: Cross-reference only: it notes that a similar narration about Ubay bin Ka'b has already been quoted in the chapter on Dhikr.

n04122.summary: Abu Waa'il reports Ibn Mas'ood's account of a Companion who wrestled a Shaytaan three times and learned a verse of Surah Baqarah from him, and Ibn Mas'ood names that Companion as Umar.

n04123.summary: Ibn Mas'ood tells of a Companion who floored a Jinn three times, learned Aayatul Kursi from him, and whom he identifies as Umar.

n04124.summary: Mujaahid says the Shaytaans were chained during Umar's khilaafah and were released only after his martyrdom.

n04125.summary: Aamir bin Abdullaah reports that Abdullaah bin Zubayr rebuked a Jinn he met at Yanaasib, and that his companions then fell from their animals.

n04126.summary: Abu Sulaymaan Daaraani reports that Abdullaah bin Zubayr, camped at Tabook, lunged at an old man on his animal, who then warned him, and Ibn Zubayr rebuked him in return.

n04127.summary: Suwayd bin Zaid reports Abu Dharr's account of pebbles in the Prophet's hands glorifying Allaah in the hands of Abu Bakr, Umar and Uthmaan, and the Prophet said this denotes the successors of Nubuwwah.

n04128.summary: Abu Dharr adds that the pebbles also glorified Allaah in Ali's hand, and in the hands of the other Companions they stayed silent.

n04129.summary: Ibn Mas'ood recounts the Prophet's miracles: water gushing from between his fingers, and food glorifying Allaah as it was eaten.

n04130.summary: Jaabir reports that the palm trunk the Prophet used to lean on wept like a child when he left it for the new pulpit.

n04131.summary: Further reports describe the palm trunk moaning like a camel until the Prophet came back and embraced it, and Hasan used to tell this to remind people of their longing for the Prophet.

n04132.summary: Abul Bakhtari reports that Salmaan and Abu Dardaa saw a plate and the food on it glorify Allaah while they ate, and Qais adds that they often reminded each other of it.

n04133.summary: Ja'far bin Abu Imraan reports that Abdullaah bin Amr heard a fire say it too seeks Allaah's protection from the immense Fire.

n04134.summary: Yahya bin Ayyoob reports that a devoted youth who fell unconscious on remembering Allaah when tempted by a woman later died, and that when Umar recited a verse at his grave, the youth answered that he had been given both gardens of Jannah.

n04135.summary: A variant says the youth asked Umar to pass on his greetings and to ask about the reward for fearing standing before one's Rabb, and Umar then told the grave it would have two gardens.

n04136.summary: Muhammad bin Himyar reports that Umar greeted the dead at Baqee Gharqad, and a voice replied that the deeds sent ahead were found and the wealth left behind was lost.

n04137.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports seeing Abu Jahal in a pit near Badr being punished, which the Prophet confirmed would last until the Day of Qiyaamah.

n04138.summary: Sa'eed bin Musayyib reports that Zaid bin Khaarija spoke after death, naming the Prophet and the first three Khalifas and foretelling the trials to come, and that a man of Banu Khatmah did the same.

n04139.summary: Nu'maan bin Basheer reports that Zaid bin Khaarija spoke from beneath his covering, affirming the Prophet's prophethood and praising Abu Bakr, Umar and Uthmaan, and foretelling trials.

n04140.summary: Nu'maan bin Basheer says that while waiting for Uthmaan to lead the prayer, Zaid bin Khaarija raised his shroud, greeted them and spoke, asking about Abdullaah bin Rawaaha and his fathers; a variant adds more of his speech and a verse about Jahannam.

n04142.summary: Nu'maan bin Basheer reports Zaid bin Khaarija's corpse speaking about the strength of the Khulafaa, Uthmaan's forgiveness and the coming trials, and greeting the Prophet and Abdullaah bin Rawaaha while asking after his father Khaarija bin Zaid.

n04143.summary: Anas bin Maalik recounts how a Muhaajir mother's du'aa over her dead son brought him back to life, and he ate with them; a variant identifies her as Ummu Saa'ib.

n04145.summary: Abdullaah bin Aun reports Anas bin Maalik's account that when the Prophet sent him to tell a Muhaajir woman her son had died, her du'aa brought the boy back to life, and he lived until the Prophet died.

n04146.summary: Abu Nadhra reports Jaabir bin Abdullaah's account that his father, the first to be martyred at Uhud, asked him to settle his debts and treat his sisters well, and that his body was found unchanged six months later.

n04147.summary: Jaabir bin Abdullaah reports that the Uhud martyrs, exhumed about forty years later during Mu'aawiya's canal digging, were still fresh, including his father Abdullaah bin Amr and Amr bin Jamooh who shared one grave.

n04148.summary: Jaabir reports that when the canal was dug near the Uhud martyrs, a spade struck Hamzah's foot and it bled after forty years.

n04149.summary: Muhammad bin Shurahbeel narrates that a Companion took sand from the grave of Sa'd bin Mu'aadh, found it to be musk, and the Prophet exclaimed Subhaanallaah.

n04150.summary: Another report says that someone took sand from the grave of Sa'd bin Mu'aadh and found it had become musk.

n04151.summary: Abu Sa'eed Khudri says that while digging Sa'd bin Mu'aadh's grave, the fragrance of musk rose with each shovelful of sand.

n04152.summary: Urwa reports that after the Bir Ma'oonah massacre, Aamir bin Tufayl saw the martyr Aamir bin Fuhayrah lifted to the sky, and the Prophet told the Sahabah the martyrs were pleased with their Rabb.

n04153.summary: Another report says that the man who killed Aamir bin Fuhayrah, Jabbaar bin Sulma, asked what success Aamir had meant and then accepted Islaam.

n04154.summary: Urwa reports that because Aamir bin Fuhayrah's body could not be found, the Sahabah believed the angels had buried him.

n04155.summary: The Prophet says the angels buried Aamir bin Fuhayrah and his soul was taken to 'Illiyyeen, and Aamir bin Tufayl describes seeing that Sahabi lifted between earth and sky.

n04156.summary: Amr bin Umayyah reports untying Khubayb's body from the cross and finding it gone into the earth, and Dahhaak reports the Prophet sending Miqdaad and Zubayr who found the body fresh and the ground then took it.

n04158.summary: Anas and Abu Hurayrah report that the grave of Alaa bin Hadhrami was found empty after burial, filled with light, or could not be located again.

n04160.summary: Abu Hurayrah reports that the Prophet sent Aasim bin Thaabit on an expedition, and Allaah protected his body from the Quraysh with a swarm of wasps.

n04161.summary: Urwa reports that when the Mushrikeen tried to cut off Aasim bin Thaabit's head, Allaah sent wasps that stung them and stopped them.

n04162.summary: Hamzah bin Abu Usayd reports that the Prophet, going to a funeral at Baqee, told a wolf blocking the path to take its share, and advised a fixed one goat per year from each flock of forty or more.

n04163.summary: Mutallib bin Abdullaah reports a wolf coming to the Prophet in Madinah with a proposal for a share of the flocks, and a Juhaynah man reports a delegation of about a hundred wolves that the Prophet sent away.

n04164.summary: Safeenah, the Prophet's freed slave, reports that a lion guided him out of the forest after a shipwreck, and in another account the lion led him when he lost his way.

n04166.summary: Ibn Munkadir reports that Safeenah, lost in Roman territory, met a lion that accepted his claim to be the Prophet's freed slave, then walked beside him and led him to the army.

n04167.summary: Wahab bin Abaan reports that Abdullaah bin Umar moved a lion off the road, and then quoted the Prophet that whoever fears and hopes in none but Allaah will not be overpowered by anything else.

n04168.summary: Auf bin Maalik reports that a lion in a church in Areeha told him that Mu'aawiya, son of Abu Sufyaan, would be among the people of Jannah.

n04169.summary: Abu Sa'eed Khudri reports that a wolf spoke to a shepherd about the Prophet, and the Prophet confirmed it; a similar wolf spoke to Abu Sufyaan and Safwaan bin Umayyah about the Prophet's call.

n04170.summary: Qais bin Hajjaaj reports that Amr bin al-Aas refused the Egyptians' ritual of throwing a girl into the Nile, Umar's letter had a note cast into the river, and the Nile then rose.

n04171.summary: Urwa A'ma reports that Abu Rayhaana's needle fell into the sea and, after he prayed for it, surfaced in his hand.

n04172.summary: Abu Hurayrah reports that Alaa bin Hadhrami, sent by the Prophet to Bahrain, crossed the sea by reciting Bismillaah, brought rain after a prayer and du'aa, and that his grave was later found empty.

n04173.summary: Abu Hurayrah adds that the Persian governor Ibn Muka'bir, on seeing the Muslims, said they could never be fought and sailed back to Persia.

n04174.summary: Anas reports that Umar appointed Alaa bin Hadhrami to lead an army, and that Alaa's du'aa brought rain and a crossing of the gulf without the animals' hooves getting wet.

n04175.summary: Several accounts describe Alaa bin Hadhrami's du'aa for rain, his crossing of the sea with his men at Daareen, and Abu Bakr's dispatch of him to fight the Murtaddeen in Bahrain.

n04177.summary: Ibn Rufayl reports that Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas, unable to find boats, led the army across the Tigris after Aasim bin Amr and sixty men went ahead, and the Persians fled the town of Bahurseer.

n04178.summary: Several narrators describe the Muslim army crossing the Tigris at Madaa'in: Sa'd and Salmaan were assured the waters were subject, the rising mounds were seen, and the Persians fled, calling them madmen.

n04182.summary: A'mash reports that a Muslim plunged into the Tigris saying Bismillaah, his horse rode over the water, and the other Muslims followed, which made the Persians flee.

n04183.summary: Mu'aawiya bin Harmal reports that Tameem Daari, when Umar sent him, pushed back a fire that came from Harra with his bare hands, and Umar said such a witness cannot be like one who has not seen it.

n04184.summary: Mu'aawiya bin Harmal reports that after repenting of fighting for Musaylama, Umar sent him to Tameem Daari, who pushed a fire from Harra back through its door and came out unharmed.

n04185.summary: Another narration has Umar telling Tameem Daari that they keep him hidden for emergencies like this, but the text breaks off.

n04186.summary: Abu Hurayrah reports that during Isha, Hasan and Husayn climbed on the Prophet's back in sajdah, and a flash of lightning lit their way home; another account has Hasan walking home by lightning.

n04187.summary: Abu Sa'eed Khudri reports that on a stormy night the Prophet saw Qataadah bin Nu'maan in lightning and gave him a date-palm branch that lit the way and was to be used against a Shaytaan.

n04188.summary: Qataadah bin Nu'maan says that the Prophet's branch lit his way home and he struck a hedgehog in his house, which he took for a Shaytaan.

n04189.summary: Anas reports that two Companions leaving the Prophet at night had lights shine before them, and each kept a light until they reached home.

n04190.summary: Anas reports that Usayd bin Hudhayr and another Ansaari, leaving the Prophet on a dark night, each had their staff light up, and the second report names the other man as Abbaad bin Bishr.

n04191.summary: Hamzah bin Amr Aslami reports that his fingers shone on a dark night so the Companions could gather their mounts, and at Tabook his fingers gave light to recover the Prophet's fallen luggage.

n04193.summary: Zaid bin Abu Abs reports that his father, Abu Abs, after praying behind the Prophet, had his staff light up on a dark rainy night so he could reach his locality.

n04194.summary: Another account says that the Prophet gave Abu Abs bin Jabr a staff when his eyesight became weak, and it lit up a wide area for him.

n04195.summary: Tufayl bin Amr Dowsi's whip shone with light after a du'aa of the Prophet, Abbaas advised treating people well, and a cloud shaded Amr bin Abasa.

n04196.summary: This is a broken fragment ('and the Sahabah') from the section on rain sent through the Prophet's du'aa, and it does not say who did what.

n04197.summary: The Prophet ﷺ asked for rain during a Friday sermon, then asked for it to stop, and rain fell until Abu Lubaabah plugged his granary gutter with his loincloth.

n04198.summary: When the Sahabah had no water, the Prophet ﷺ made du'aa and Allaah sent a cloud that rained enough for all their needs.

n04199.summary: Khawwaat bin Jubayr prayed for rain during Umar's caliphate and rain fell at once, and in a dream the Prophet ﷺ sent Umar word that rain was coming.

n04201.summary: In the Year of Ashes Umar asked other provinces for food, led prayer for rain, and a Bedouin was told in a dream that rain would come and Umar should keep applying his intelligence.

n04202.summary: During a drought Mu'aawiya had Yazeed bin Aswad raise his hands in du'aa, and a cloud came with rain straight after.

n04203.summary: Anas's orchard keeper asked for rain in summer and rain fell only on Anas's land after Anas prayed, and Hujr bin Adi asked for water while held by Mu'aawiya's forces and a cloud rained on him.

n04204.summary: A tribe of the Ansaar had rain fall on the grave of each member through an earlier du'aa of the Prophet, including on a freed slave who was counted as one of them.

n04205.summary: Ummu Ayman, thirsty while fasting on her migration to Madinah, was given water from a bucket let down from the sky, and after that she never felt thirst on hot fasting days.

n04206.summary: At Asr time with no water for wudhu, the Prophet ﷺ placed his hand in a vessel and water gushed from under his fingers so that everyone could make wudhu.

n04207.summary: Water flowed from the Prophet's fingers at a basin and at Zowraa, and at Hudaybiyyah he made du'aa and spat into the well, which then gave enough water for everyone.

n04210.summary: On a journey, when there was little water for salaah, the Prophet ﷺ poured it into a dish and water gushed from his fingers, and Ibn Mas'ood drank some of it.

n04211.summary: On a journey the Prophet ﷺ made wudhu from a small container of water, and once the container was opened it gave seven hundred people enough to drink with some left over.

n04212.summary: On the way to Tabook the Prophet ﷺ washed his hands and face in a thin spring, after which the water gushed out for everyone, and he told Mu'aadh that the area would one day be full of gardens.

n04213.summary: On a journey with no water, the Prophet ﷺ passed his hand over a woman's two waterskins so that forty thirsty men drank and filled their vessels, and her tribe then became Muslims.

n04214.summary: Ziyaad bin Haarith Sudaa'ee saw water gush from the Prophet's fingers, and after his tribe became Muslims the Prophet ﷺ had seven stones thrown into their well so that it gave abundant water.

n04215.summary: Husayn bin Ali gargled with water from Ibn Mutee's well and returned it to the well, and afterwards the water increased and became sweeter.

n04216.summary: On an expedition the army was starving until Umar suggested pooling the remaining food, the Prophet ﷺ made du'aa over it, and everyone ate their fill with food still left over.

n04217.summary: At Usfaan the army drank rainwater after the Prophet ﷺ ordered them to leave, and on the Tabook expedition the Sahabah asked to slaughter their water camels for food until Umar intervened.

n04219.summary: At Khaybar the Prophet ﷺ had the Sahabah's dates gathered on a leather cloth, and after about 1,400 people had eaten, the pile was still the size of a sitting goat.

n04220.summary: Salamah says that after they had eaten to their fill they also filled their satchels.

n04221.summary: While the trench was being dug, the Prophet ﷺ made one goat and a little bread enough for the whole group, and at a boulder he promised the palaces of Shaam and Persia while the hypocrites scoffed.

n04222.summary: A plate of Thareed was served to the Prophet ﷺ and the Sahabah, and they kept eating until near Zuhr, and Samurah said the extra food came from the heavens.

n04223.summary: Waathila bin Asqa and the men of Suffa were fed bread and Thareed that the Prophet ﷺ made with his own hands, which kept increasing until the plate was full and each group had eaten its fill.

n04225.summary: Faatima kept the bread and meat a neighbour gave her for the Prophet ﷺ, and when he had eaten it with his household the platter stayed full and he told her to give it to the neighbours.

n04226.summary: Ummu Shareek Dowsiyyah was given a drink in a dream when thirsty on her migration, the Prophet ﷺ married her to Zaid with thirty Saa of barley, and her butter kept coming until the bag was tied shut.
