n04228.summary: A man asked the Prophet ﷺ for food and received half a Wasaq of barley, which lasted until they weighed it, after which it ran out.

n04229.summary: Naufal bin Haarith asked the Prophet ﷺ for help with marriage, and barley pawned for thirty Saa lasted half a year without decreasing until they weighed it.

n04230.summary: After the Prophet ﷺ passed away, Aa'isha had barley on a shelf that lasted for a very long time until she weighed it.

n04231.summary: Jaabir's father left debts, and when the Prophet ﷺ walked around the heaps of dates and made du'aa, Jaabir's creditors were paid in full with dates left over.

n04232.summary: Jaabir says the Prophet ﷺ sat on the heap of dates and had the creditors called, and although the debts were paid, the heap looked untouched.

n04233.summary: A girl carrying her mother's dates to her father was stopped by the Prophet ﷺ, who spread them on a cloth and called the trench-diggers to eat, and the dates kept multiplying.

n04234.summary: On the Tabook expedition seven dates fed three hungry men and then ten people without ever decreasing, and the Prophet ﷺ later gave the dates to a child in Madinah.

n04235.summary: Abu Hurayrah's bag of dates was blessed by the Prophet ﷺ's du'aa to feed the whole army, and it stayed full through the lifetimes of Abu Bakr, Umar and Uthmaan until it was stolen after Uthmaan's martyrdom.

n04236.summary: Anas's mother asked the Prophet ﷺ to pray for her son, and Anas reports that his wealth, children and orchards were blessed, so that his orchards bear fruit twice a year.

n04238.summary: Ummu Maalik Bahziyyah's bag of butter kept giving butter after she gave it to the Prophet ﷺ, and when she brought him a gift the bag stayed full, after which he taught her tasbeeh to recite after each salaah.

n04239.summary: Ummu Aws Bahziyyah's gift of butter stayed full after the Prophet ﷺ took some from it, and she went on eating from the bag until the dispute between Ali and Mu'aawiya.

n04240.summary: Ummu Sulaym's bag of butter stayed full after the Prophet ﷺ took from it, he told her to eat from it and feed others, and it lasted her household a month or two.

n04241.summary: Ummu Shareek reports that the butter in her small bag kept replenishing until she emptied it out, and the Prophet remarked that it would have lasted much longer had she left it alone.

n04242.summary: Ummu Shareek lent her bag out to people, and it refilled with butter even after it seemed empty, which people took as one of the signs of Allaah.

n04243.summary: Hamzah bin Amr relates that when the butter bag spilled while he was preparing the Prophet's food, it later filled to its chest, and the Prophet said it would have filled to its mouth had he left it alone.

n04244.summary: Hamzah bin Amr relates that while the Prophet was away on the Tabook expedition, the butter bag refilled after he dozed beside it, and the Prophet said the whole valley would have flowed with butter had he left it.

n04245.summary: Khabbaab bin Arat's daughter relates that the Prophet milked their goat into the family's largest vessel until it overflowed, and her father then said the Prophet's hands were far more blessed than his own.

n04246.summary: Mas'ood bin Khaalid relates that the meat the Prophet sent back from the goat he had given him was still left over after his family had eaten, which surprised him since one or two goats were usually not enough for them.

n04247.summary: Khaalid bin Abdul Uzza sends a goat to the Prophet, who and his Companions eat it and return the leftovers, which still feed Khaalid's very large family with some to spare.

n04248.summary: Salamah bin Nufayl reports that food is brought to the Prophet from the heavens and lifted back after it is left over, and the Prophet foretells a time of strife and many deaths before Qiyaamah.

n04250.summary: Jaabir bin Abdullaah relates that when the men were starving, the sea cast up a huge creature which fed them, and five of them went into its eye socket and then stood one of its ribs up like a bow.

n04251.summary: Jaabir bin Abdullaah relates that when Abu Ubaydah's army ran out of provisions, the sea washed up a fish the size of a hill that fed them for eighteen days, and a camel and carriage passed under its ribs without touching them.

n04252.summary: Jaabir bin Abdullaah gives several accounts of Abu Ubaydah's army, which ate a fish the sea threw up for a month, and reports that the Prophet called it the sustenance Allaah had brought out for them.

n04253.summary: Abu Hurayrah reports that when a Sahabi's wife prayed for provision in her family's hunger, the grindstone and oven kept producing until the husband lifted the grindstone, and the Prophet said it would have continued until the Day of Qiyaamah.

n04256.summary: Abu Bakr relates how a Bedouin woman hosted the Prophet and himself, how the Prophet milked her goat for them and her flock grew, and how she accepted Islaam when she recognised him.

n04257.summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood relates that the Prophet drew milk from a goat that had not yet mated, then told her teat to contract and it did, and afterwards Ibn Mas'ood asked to be taught and the Prophet prayed that he be well taught.

n04258.summary: Another account says Abdullaah bin Mas'ood brought the Prophet a young goat, who prayed over her and milked her into a dish that Abu Bakr brought, then gave Abu Bakr to drink before drinking himself.

n04259.summary: Khabbaab bin Arat relates that on a campaign sent out by the Prophet the Muslims became very thirsty, and a companion's camel sat down with udders so full of milk that they all drank from her.

n04260.summary: Maawiyya, a slave of Hujayr bin Abi Ihaab, reports that while Khubayb was held prisoner in their house in Makkah she peeped in and saw him eating a huge bunch of grapes, when grapes could not be had anywhere.

n04261.summary: Saalim bin Abul Ja'd relates that when the Prophet sent two men out with no provisions, he told them to fill a water bag and go to a place where Allaah would provide, and there they found goat's milk and cream inside it.

n04262.summary: Abdullaah bin Salaam relates that while Uthmaan was besieged, the Prophet appeared to him in a dream, offered him water, and then offered to help him against his attackers or to break his fast with the Prophet, and Uthmaan chose the latter and was martyred that day.

n04263.summary: Dubaa'ah bint Zubayr relates that her husband Miqdaad found seventeen dinars that a rat had carried out of a hole, and when he told the Prophet, the Prophet said no khumus was due from him and prayed for blessing, after which their wealth grew greatly.

n04264.summary: Saa'ib bin Aqra relates that while governor of Madaa'in he found a huge treasure under a figurine that pointed to the spot, and Umar wrote back instructing him to distribute it among the Muslims.

n04265.summary: Sha'bi reports that during the Conquest of Mihrijaan Saa'ib bin Aqra noticed a lime figurine of a deer pointing its foreleg, investigated, and discovered the treasure of Hurmuzaan, which included several bags of gems.

n04266.summary: Abdur Rahmaan bin Yazeed bin Jaabir relays how Abu Umaamah gave away his last dinars in charity and then found three hundred gold coins left in his bed, after which his Christian slave woman accepted Islaam.

n04267.summary: Salmaan relates that when he still owed money for his freedom, the Prophet gave him a gold nugget that weighed forty awqiya, enough to pay off the debt in full.

n04268.summary: Urwa Baariqi relates that the Prophet prayed for blessing in his trade after he bought two goats for one dinar and sold one, and he later made large profits in the Kunaasah marketplace.

n04269.summary: Abu Aqeel relates that his grandfather Abdullaah bin Hishaam bought grain to resell and earned a camel's worth of profit, because the Prophet had prayed for blessing on him, and Abdullaah bin Zubayr and Abdullaah bin Umar asked to be partners.

n04270.summary: Abdullaah bin Unays relates that after the Jew Mustaneer bin Rizaam struck him with a staff and fractured his skull, the Prophet opened the wound, applied his saliva to it, and it healed without a trace.

n04271.summary: Mukhallad bin Uqba relates that a boil on his palm hindered him from holding his sword and reins, so the Prophet opened his palm, applied his saliva, and rubbed the boil until no trace of it remained.

n04272.summary: Abyadh bin Hammaal relates that he had a ringworm infection covering his face and nose, and after the Prophet passed his blessed hand over it, no trace of it remained.

n04273.summary: Raafi bin Khudayj relates that after he ate a piece of fat from a pot of meat and was ill for a year, the Prophet passed his hand over his stomach, he vomited a green lump, and he never had stomach pain again.

n04274.summary: Ali relates that the Prophet prayed for him when he was ill and then cured him, and Abdullaah bin Ateek describes how the Prophet healed his broken leg by passing his hand over it after he was injured going to kill Abu Raafi.

n04275.summary: Handhala bin Hadheem relates that the Prophet passed his hand over his head and prayed for blessing when he came with his grandfather's delegation, and Dhayyaal relates that Handhala cured a swollen face and inflamed teats by touching them with the blessing of the Prophet's palm.

n04276.summary: Dhayyaal relates that a man with a swollen face was brought to Handhala, who applied saliva to his hand, recited Bismillaah, touched the swelling and said it was done with the blessing of the place where the Prophet placed his palm, and it disappeared instantly.

n04277.summary: Abdullaah bin Qurt relates that when his camel grew exhausted while he rode with Khaalid bin Waleed, he made du'aa to Allaah, and the camel stood up straight so he could ride it again.

n04278.summary: Abu Safar, Dhul Jowshan and others relate that Khaalid bin Waleed swallowed poison in the name of Allaah without harm, and that Amr bin Buqayla, who carried poison, said the Arabs would conquer any land while the Sahabah lived among them.

n04280.summary: Abdur Rahmaan bin Abi Layla relates that his father asked Ali why he wore light clothes in winter and heavy ones in summer, and Ali explained that the Prophet's saliva and du'aa for protection against heat and cold had kept him from feeling either.

n04282.summary: Bilaal relates that on an icy winter morning the people did not come out for Fajr after the Adhaan, so the Prophet prayed that Allaah remove the cold from them, and then they came for Fajr and Duha with ease.

n04283.summary: A one-line cross-reference notes that a narration from Hudhayfah about the Battle of the Trench makes the same point about cold.

n04284.summary: Imraan bin Husayn relates that the Prophet placed his hand on Faatima's chest and prayed that she not suffer hunger, after which the paleness from her hunger left her face and she never went hungry again.

n04285.summary: Abu Zaid Ansaari relates that the Prophet prayed for his good looks and that he lived past a hundred with only a few white hairs, and a second report says he had none at ninety-four.

n04286.summary: Abul A'laa reports that after the Prophet passed his hand over Qataadah bin Milhaan's face, the signs of age were removed from it, so that his face kept looking oiled and reflected passers-by.

n04287.summary: Hayyaan bin Umayr reports that the Prophet's touch on Qataadah bin Milhaan's face kept every part of his body ageing except his face, which still reflected a woman passing behind him when he died.

n04288.summary: Naabigha Ja'di recites couplets before the Prophet, who asks where the greater heights lead and is told Jannah, and the Prophet then prays that Naabigha's teeth never fall out, and they stayed intact even past a hundred years of age.

n04289.summary: A further narration reports that Naabigha Ja'di always had a perfect set of teeth, and each one that fell out was replaced by another so that he lived to a very old age.

n04290.summary: Ummu Is'haaq relates that, after arriving in Madinah and learning her brother Is'haaq had been killed, the Prophet sprinkled water from his wudhu on her face, and her tears never ran down her cheeks in calamity afterwards.

n04291.summary: Ummu Is'haaq says she kept weeping over her brother's murder until the Prophet sprinkled water on her face, and Ummu Hakeem testifies that even in great tragedy her tears welled up but never fell.

n04293.summary: Zaid bin Aslam and others narrate that when Ukaasha bin Mihsin's sword broke at Badr, the Prophet gave him a branch which became a sturdy, sparkling sword in his hand.

n04294.summary: Khaythama reports several versions of Khaalid bin Waleed's du'aa turning a casket of wine into honey or vinegar after its bearer lied about what it was.

n04295.summary: Muhammad bin Is'haaq reports that Maalik Ashja'ee told the Prophet his son Awf had been taken captive, the Prophet told Awf to recite 'Laa Howla wa Laa Quwwata illaa Billaah', and Awf escaped and brought back his captors' camels.

n04296.summary: Awf's father complained to the Prophet about his captive son's suffering, and the Prophet advised him to be patient, saying Allaah would soon create an escape for him.

n04297.summary: Abbaas bin Sahl reports that when the Prophet forbade drinking the water at Hijr or leaving camp alone at night, two men who disobeyed were punished, one by a jinn and the other by a tempest, and the Prophet prayed for the one who was throttled and he was cured.

n04298.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports that Jahjaa Ghifaari struck Uthmaan's knee with his staff during a sermon, and within the year Jahjaa was afflicted with a disease that ate his arm and killed him.

n04299.summary: Another narration says Jahjaa snatched Uthmaan's stick and struck his knee so that it broke, Uthmaan went home without retaliating, and Jahjaa died of a disease in his knee before the year was out.

n04300.summary: Abdul Malik bin Umayr reports that after a man mocked Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas in verse at Qaadisiyyah, Sa'd prayed against him, and the man was struck by an arrow, lost his tongue and hand, and was killed.

n04301.summary: Another narration says that Sa'd's curse left the man's tongue and hand paralysed, an arrow struck his mouth and his hand was cut off in the battle, and when Sa'd was carried to the city gate with his wounds visible, people knew he was truly excused from fighting.

n04302.summary: Several narrations describe how Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas cursed a man who reviled Ali, Talha and Zubayr, and the curse was fulfilled when a camel or the ground killed him.

n04303.summary: Ibn Showdhab reports that when Abdullaah bin Umar heard Ziyaad son of Sumayya wanted the governorship of Hijaaz, he prayed that Ziyaad be granted death without being killed, and a painful infection on his thumb killed him before the next Friday.

n04304.summary: Abu Waa'il, present at Karbala, reports that a man threatened Husayn with Jahannam, and Husayn prayed that he be taken in pieces to Jahannam, after which the man's animal threw him, his foot caught in the stirrup, and only his leg was left.

n04305.summary: Kalbi reports that Husayn cursed the man who shot an arrow that paralysed his jaw so that he could not quench his thirst, and the man drank until his stomach burst; other reports describe punishments on the men who killed Husayn and on a man who defiled his grave.

n04307.summary: Rabee'ah bin Qusayt reports that during the Year of Jamaa'ah, when Ali's and Mu'aawiya's armies had clashed, a downpour of blood fell on the returning army, and Amr bin Al-Aas warned the people to mend their relationship with Allaah.

n04308.summary: Zuhri reports that Abdul Malik asked him for the sign of Husayn's martyrdom, and he answered that fresh blood was found beneath every stone lifted in Baytul Maqdas.

n04309.summary: Zuhri reports that on the day Husayn was martyred, every stone lifted in Shaam gave way to blood.

n04310.summary: Ummu Hakeem says that for a few days after Husayn was martyred, the sky stayed the colour of a blood clot.

n04311.summary: Abu Qubayl reports that when Husayn was martyred the sun eclipsed so much that stars were visible at noon, and people thought the Last Day had come.

n04312.summary: Maalik bin Dinaar, Ma'roof Mowsili and Aa'isha report that when Umar was martyred, an unseen voice of a jinn lamented him in couplets, and Aa'isha heard one lament recited at night.

n04315.summary: Sulaymaan bin Yasaar reports that the jinn mourned Umar's death with a set of couplets, which he quotes in full.

n04316.summary: Aa'isha quotes the couplets of the jinn mourning Umar in a different order and adds a final couplet wishing Umar a meeting with his Rabb in Jannah.

n04317.summary: Ummu Salamah says the jinn were heard bewailing the death of Husayn bin Ali.

n04318.summary: Ummu Salamah says that after hearing the jinn lamenting one night, her maid learnt that Husayn had been martyred and a jinn woman recited couplets of mourning, and Maymoona reports that the jinn were also heard lamenting Husayn bin Ali.

n04319.summary: Abu Moosa Ash'ari dreamt that the Prophet beckoned Umar up a mountain, which he took to mean Umar would die, and when Anas advised him to write to Umar, Abu Moosa said he could not inform Umar of his own death.

n04320.summary: Katheer bin Silt reports that Uthmaan, after a nap on the day he was martyred, said he had dreamt the Prophet told him, 'You will be with us this Friday'.

n04321.summary: Another narration adds that the day on which Uthmaan was martyred was a Friday.

n04322.summary: Uthmaan told his companions one morning that the Prophet had told him in a dream to break his fast with them, so he fasted that day and was martyred on it.

n04323.summary: Muslim Abu Sa'eed, a freed slave of Uthmaan, reports that Uthmaan freed twenty slaves and put on trousers for the first time, then said he had dreamt of the Prophet, Abu Bakr and Umar promising he would break his fast with them the next evening, and he was martyred while reading the Qur'aan.

n04324.summary: Hasan or Husayn, the sons of Ali, report that their father Ali said he had complained in a dream to the Prophet about the people of Iraq, and the Prophet promised deliverance soon, and Ali passed away barely three days later.

n04325.summary: Abu Saalih reports that Ali dreamt the Prophet told him to turn round and see two men in fetters whose heads were crushed by boulders and restored each time, and the next day Ali was assassinated.

n04326.summary: Filfila Ju'fi reports that Hasan bin Ali said he saw in a dream the Prophet holding the Arsh, with Abu Bakr, Umar and Uthmaan each holding the one before him and blood flowing from the sky to the earth, and that when Shia present asked about Ali, Hasan said he would have loved Ali to be in that position.

n04327.summary: Hasan bin Ali relates a dream in which the Rabb was on the Arsh, the Prophet, Abu Bakr, Umar and Uthmaan stood in order, and blood poured from the sky, and when told of it Ali replied that Hasan was only relating what he saw.

n04328.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas reports that in a dream the Prophet appeared dishevelled with a glass, saying it held the blood of Husayn and his companions which he had been collecting all day, and Ibn Abbaas found that day was the day Husayn was martyred.

n04329.summary: Abbaas (RA) reports that Umar (RA) appeared to him in a dream after his death and said his reckoning was over and that only Allaah's mercy saved him.

n04330.summary: Abbaas (RA) reports that after a year of du'aa he saw Umar (RA) in a dream, and Umar said his reckoning was over and that he was saved by a Forgiving and Merciful Rabb.

n04331.summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) reports that after a year of du'aa he saw Umar (RA) in a dream, and Umar said he had found a Most Forgiving and Merciful Rabb.

n04332.summary: Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) reports that in a dream he saw a palace belonging to his father Umar (RA), who said he had been saved by a Forgiving Rabb and had just come back from his reckoning.

n04333.summary: Saalim bin Abdullaah reports an Ansaari's account of seeing Umar (RA) in a dream after ten years, when Umar said his reckoning was complete and he was saved only by his Rabb's mercy.

n04334.summary: Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf (RA) reports that in a dream Umar (RA) nudged his sleeping wife awake, and that he chased Umar and caught up only after exhausting himself, which Umar said was not due to his speed.

n04336.summary: A second report has Abdullaah bin Salaam (RA) asking Salmaan (RA) in a dream which deed he found most virtuous, and Salmaan answering Tawakkul.

n04337.summary: Auf bin Maalik (RA) reports seeing in a dream a tent belonging to Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf, who said it was given for the Qur'aan and that Allaah had prepared a reward for Abu Dardaa because he pushed the world away.

n04338.summary: Abdullaah bin Amr bin Haraam (RA) reports that Mubashir bin Abdul Mundhir told him in a dream that the martyrs of Badr live in Jannah, and the Prophet ﷺ remarked that this is the reality of martyrdom.

n04339.summary: Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf (RA) says that the Sahabah found good in hardships, such as leaving Makkah with the Prophet ﷺ and the march to Badr, and cites the Qur'aan's account of Badr.

n04340.summary: Ibn Ishaq narrates Abu Bakr's letter to Khaalid bin Waleed after Yamaamah, ordering him to march to Iraq and urging the Muslims to fight in Allaah's path with patience and sincerity.

n04341.summary: Utba bin Abd (RA) reports that the Sahabah pledged to fight with the Prophet ﷺ, and Ali (RA) rebuked an astrologer (Musaafir) for claiming to foresee harm on a journey, then marched at the hour he forbade and won at Nahrwaan.

n04342.summary: Abdullaah bin Auf bin Ahmar reports that when Ali (RA) was leaving for Nahrwaan, the fortune-teller Musaafir urged him to delay; Ali refused, rebuked him for claiming knowledge of the unseen, and said trust should be placed in Allaah alone, then marched and won.

n04343.summary: Taariq bin Ziyaad reports that Umar (RA) waded across water in humility, and when Abu Ubaydah objected, Umar said honour comes only through Islaam.

n04344.summary: Qais and Abul Aaliya Shaami report that Umar (RA) entering Shaam declined a Turkish horse and fine clothing, keeping his own camel and simple dress because Islaam gave him honour.

n04345.summary: Abu Nuhayk and Abdullaah bin Handhala report that they beat a man who reviled Maryam and Isa while they recited Surah Maryam, and Salmaan (RA) rebuked them and taught respect for others' beliefs and nafl salaah.

n04346.summary: Jubayr bin Nufayr (RA) reports seeing Abu Dardaa (RA) weeping after Cyprus was conquered, saying that the people were degraded because they forsook Allaah's commands and became obsessed with enslaving others.

n04347.summary: Ibn Abu Maryam reports that Mu'aadh bin Jabal (RA) told Umar (RA) that sincerity, salaah and obedience to the leader keep the Ummah steady, and later foretold that Umar would live only a short while.

n04348.summary: Abu Abdah Ambari reports that after Madaa'in was conquered a man brought a dish of jewels to the booty, refusing praise out of fear of Allaah, and was identified as Aamir bin Abd Qays.

n04349.summary: Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas (RA) and Jaabir bin Abdullaah (RA) vouch for the integrity of the army at Qaadisiyyah, and Jaabir names three men they had doubted, Tulayha, Amr bin Ma'dikarib and Qais bin Makshooh, who proved trustworthy and abstinent.

n04351.summary: Qais Ijli reports that when the Persian emperor's sword, belt and jewels were brought to Umar (RA), Umar praised the trustworthiness of those who brought them, and Ali (RA) replied that the subjects are trustworthy because the ruler is.

n04352.summary: Zaid bin Aslam reports Umar's letter to Amr bin al-Aas urging him to seek Allaah's help with sincere intentions and prayer, and a later letter sending four thousand reinforcements under commanders including Zubayr, Miqdaad, Ubaadah and Maslamah.

n04353.summary: Iyaadh Ash'ari reports that at Yarmook five commanders shared the army with Abu Ubaydah as commander-in-chief, and the army wrote to Umar (RA) that the enemy outnumbered them and asked for reinforcements.

n04354.summary: Umar (RA) replies to the army's request for reinforcements by directing them to Allaah, who helped Muhammad ﷺ at Badr when his forces were fewer than theirs.

n04355.summary: Umar (RA) adds that the army should fight without writing back, and after victory Iyaadh (RA) proposed exchanging ten prisoners for each Muslim, while Abu Ubaydah (RA) raced a youngster who beat him.

n04356.summary: After Zuhr, Sa'd (RA) had a young Qaari recite Surah Anfaal to the army at Qaadisiyyah, and the whole army learned it and drew tranquillity from it; another report says he ordered them to recite it to one another.

n04357.summary: Ibraheem bin Haarith Tameemi (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ sent a force with instructions to recite Surah Mu'minoon verse 115 every morning and evening, and they gained booty and remained safe.

n04358.summary: Sa'd (RA) commands the Muslims to hold position until after Zuhr, call Allaahu Akbar with each of his calls, and finally charge while reciting 'Laa Howla wa Laa Quwwata Illaa Billaah'.

n04359.summary: Sa'd (RA) calls the Takbeer three times while the Qurraa finish reciting the verses of Jihaad, the army mobilises, and the most courageous go forward; the narration is cut off.

n04360.summary: Ja'far bin Abdullaah bin Hakam reports that Khaalid bin Waleed (RA) kept a hat containing hairs of the Prophet ﷺ taken at Umrah, and was granted victory whenever he wore it into battle.

n04362.summary: Shaqeeq reports that at Qaadisiyyah, when the muadhin was injured, the Sahabah eagerly competed to call the adhaan, and Sa'd (RA) settled it by drawing lots.

n04363.summary: Ma'qal bin Yasaar (RA) reports the conquest of Isfahaan, where Mughiera bin Shu'ba (RA) went as envoy to the Persian ruler Dhul Haajibayn, and Mughiera contrasted the Arabs' former poverty and the Prophet's message with the Persian splendour.

n04364.summary: Rib'ee bin Aamir, Hudhayfah bin Mihsin and Mughiera bin Shu'ba (RA) each go before Rustam at Qaadisiyyah in turn; they reject the Persian display of wealth and call the Persians to Islaam, Jizya or battle.

n04365.summary: Abu Hurayrah (RA) reports that at Mu'ta, daunted by the enemy's numbers, he was reminded by Thaabit bin Aqram (RA) that victory comes through Allaah, not through large numbers.

n04366.summary: Abdullaah bin Amr bin Al Aas reports Abu Bakr's letter to Amr bin Al Aas that victory never depended on numbers, recalling Uhud and the scarce horses and camels of the Prophet's time, and urging obedience to Allaah.

n04367.summary: Ubaadah (RA) and Khaalid bin Waleed (RA) report that Khaalid answered a man who feared the Romans' numbers by saying Muslims win through Allaah's help, not numbers, and wished the Romans were double.

n04368.summary: Zuhri reports that after some Arabs apostatised, Abu Bakr sent Khaalid bin Waleed, who defeated the false prophet Tulayha, and one of Tulayha's own men said his side fought people who wanted to die before their companions.

n04369.summary: Amr bin Al Aas (RA) reports his conversation with the king of Alexandria, in which he described the Arabs' former state and the Prophet's message, and the king advised that they would prevail only while they followed their prophet's teachings.

n04370.summary: Abu Is'haaq reports that Heraclius asked why his defeated Roman army lost to Muslims who pray at night, fast by day and keep promises, and an elderly leader replied that the Romans drank, fornicated and oppressed.

n04371.summary: Yahya bin Yahya Ghassaani reports that two Arab Christians spied on the Muslims at Damascus and described them as monks by night, horsemen by day, always reciting the Qur'aan and making dhikr, and the Damascus commander said they could not be resisted.

n04372.summary: Qubuqalaar, the Roman general at Yarmook, sends a spy into the Muslim army, who reports that they are devout by night, brave horsemen by day and strict in applying justice.

n04373.summary: Rustam's spy reports on the Muslims' worship at Qaadisiyyah, and Rustam, watching them prepare for salaah, remarks on how Umar has shaped them.

n04374.summary: A Roman who had been held captive by the Muslims and then escaped describes them to Heraclius, who concludes they will inherit the land under his feet.

n04375.summary: After Yazdgird asks China for reinforcements, the Chinese Emperor questions the Persian envoy about the Sahabah and advises a treaty with them rather than war.
